docs.title: F&O Studio for VS Code
docs.text:
F&O Studio brings Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (X++) development to VS Code, without Visual Studio, with Copilot built in. It uses Microsoft's own metadata API, compiler (xppc, LabelC, reportsc), best-practice checker (xppbp), packaging script and debugger proxy, so projects and models move between F&O Studio and Visual Studio unchanged.

  • Install: Visual Studio Marketplace, MNazmi.xpp-vscode
  • Source and issues: nazmolla/xpp-vscode
  • What's new: Changelog

docs.title: ALM Overview
docs.text: Application lifecycle management (ALM) for Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations covers how X++ changes move from a developer's machine to production: source control, work items, reviews, builds, deployable packages and environments. This page maps that lifecycle and shows, step by step, which parts F&O Studio covers and which parts stay with your existing tools (Git, Azure DevOps or GitHub, Lifecycle Services, the Power Platform admin center). Read it before the other ALM pages: they go deeper into each step.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You set up a new team or project and want to know where F&O Studio fits in your ALM.
  • You come from Visual Studio and want to know which ALM commands have an equivalent in VS Code.
  • You need to explain to a project lead what the extension does and does not automate.

docs.title: The lifecycle at a glance
docs.text:
Stage General D365FO practice What F&O Studio does Plan Work items in Azure Boards (or GitHub issues) Link Work Itemâ€¦ puts the work item in the commit message, Open Work Itemâ€¦ opens it in Azure Boards Code Models and projects in a Git (or TFVC) repository, one developer environment per developer Element designers, code view, project view with Git change marks, Open Team Repositoryâ€¦ links a repository's packages Review Pull requests in Azure Repos or GitHub Review My Changes, Show Changed Elements, View History, the F&O Code Reviewer agent Build Developer builds; an automated build pipeline produces the deployable package Build Project, Build Model, build tasks for tasks.json; Open Pipelines opens your pipelines in the browser Package Deployable package (zip) from the build pipeline or from Visual Studio Create Deployment Packageâ€¦ runs the same script Visual Studio runs Deploy to dev Visual Studio deploys to the unified developer environment Deploy Models to Environment and Synchronize Database, through the environment's Dataverse Test SysTest in Visual Studio or in the pipeline Run Tests, Test Explorer, Pre-Deploy Checklist Promote Sandbox and production through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center Nothing: F&O Studio never deploys to sandbox or production

The last column is the complete list. F&O Studio has no pipeline definitions, no pipeline runner, no branch policies and no release management of its own. Everything in the "General D365FO practice" column that is not repeated in the last column is done with Microsoft's or your hosting provider's tools.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO development environment configured on the machine: a unified developer environment (UDE) connected with Connect to Environmentâ€¦, or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (see Connect to Environment and Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments).
  • Git installed and on the PATH. Every Git feature of F&O Studio calls git directly.
  • Your models in a Git repository. Azure DevOps (Azure Repos) and GitHub are recognized for the work item and pipeline links; any Git host works for change marks, history and review.

docs.title: How the pieces fit together
docs.text:
1. Repository layout. The team keeps each custom package (its models' metadata and the Descriptor folder) and the .rnrproj projects in one repository. See Source Control for X++.
  2. Getting the code onto a machine. A developer clones the repository and links its packages into the custom metadata folder of the active configuration. Open Team Repositoryâ€¦ does this and builds the packages in dependency order. See Open Team Repository.
  3. Working on a change. The developer creates a branch, opens the project (Open D365FO Projectâ€¦) and edits. The project view marks every changed element with Git's letter (M, A, D, R). See Git Changes in the Project View.
  4. Linking the work item. Link Work Itemâ€¦ adds #123 (Azure Repos) or AB#123 (GitHub repositories connected to Azure Boards) to the commit message in VS Code's Source Control view. See Work Items and Pipelines.
  5. Reviewing. Review My Changes lists the changed elements since the base branch, with a pull request summary, work items found in the commits, Chain of Command, best practice and performance findings. See Review My Changes.
  6. Deploying to the developer's own environment. Deploy Models to Environment uploads the packages as built on this machine. See Deploy to Environment.
  7. Pull request and pipeline. The developer pushes and creates the pull request with VS Code's Git tools or the hosting site. The team's build pipeline (general practice, not part of F&O Studio) compiles the models and produces the deployable package. Open Pipelines opens the pipeline list. See Build Automation and Pipelines.
  8. Promotion. The package from the pipeline goes to sandbox and then production through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center. See Environments and Promotion.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect on ALM features xpp.git.baseBranch empty Branch your work is compared with (for example main). Show Changed Elements, Review My Changes and the change marks in the project view include what the current branch changed since it left this branch. Empty: only uncommitted changes. xpp.project empty The D365FO project of the workspace, written by Open D365FO Projectâ€¦ into the project's own workspace. xpp.build.crossReference true Updates the cross-reference database while building. xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild used for the C# projects the X++ project references, before X++ is compiled and before a deploy.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Git features run the git command line from the extension (src/changes.ts, src/devops.ts, src/history.ts) and, for the agent tool xpp_diff_changes, from the metadata server (server/Ported/Tools/ChangedElementsReport.cs).
  • Model folders are often junctions from the custom metadata folder into the repository. F&O Studio resolves the real path of each of your models before it asks Git, so the repository is found even when the workspace is not inside it.
  • Azure DevOps and GitHub are recognized from the origin remote URL only. F&O Studio calls no Azure DevOps or GitHub API: it builds browser URLs and edits the commit message box.
  • Deploy goes through the environment's Dataverse (core/src/deploy.ts); the deployable package is made by Microsoft's RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin (src/d365Tools.ts).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No build or release pipeline is created, run or monitored by F&O Studio. Open Pipelines only opens a web page.
  • No Azure DevOps or GitHub sign-in, API call, pull request creation or work item query. Use VS Code's Git features, the GitHub Pull Requests extension, or the hosting site.
  • TFVC is not supported; every source control feature needs Git.
  • Deploy works only on unified developer environments. Sandbox and production deployments are out of scope.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: F&O Studio is built on VS Code's own user interface wherever it can: tree views, quick picks, notifications, the Problems view, Test Explorer, the debugger and text editors. These parts work with the keyboard, screen readers, high contrast themes and zoom the way the rest of VS Code does. Where F&O Studio draws its own panels (webviews such as the element designer, the data panel and the trace analyzer), it follows VS Code's theme, shows a visible keyboard focus, draws borders in high contrast themes, stops animations when you ask for reduced motion, and labels its controls for screen readers. This page describes what you can expect, panel by panel, and how to report a barrier.

docs.title: What uses VS Code's own UI
docs.text:
These parts of F&O Studio are standard VS Code components, so VS Code's accessibility features apply to them unchanged (screen reader announcements, keyboard navigation, accessible view, high contrast, zoom):

Part of F&O Studio VS Code component Application Explorer, D365FO Project, Security, Dynamics 365, Results, Infolog and Copilot Activity views Tree views Open Element…, Select Environment…, New Element…, the Database and Environment menus, every picker Quick picks Prompts for names, URLs and filters Input boxes Messages, progress and confirmations Notifications and modal dialogs X++ code views, the debug source, compare views, usage statistics and reports in Markdown Text editors and diff editors Build errors, best practice and performance findings Problems view SysTest classes Test Explorer Breakpoints, stepping, variables Run and Debug Status bar items (environment, database, project, X++ server, Copilot checkpoint) Status bar items, each with a name

Every F&O Studio command is in the Command Palette unless it needs a clicked element (see Command-Reference), so you can reach the features without a mouse. Three commands have keybindings: Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O), Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view or .rnrproj file) and Search Code in All Packages (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F). You can bind any other command ID yourself.

The images in the Get started with F&O Studio walkthrough have alternative text.

docs.title: Shared behaviour
docs.text:
Six panels load a shared stylesheet, media/a11y.css:

  • the element designer,
  • the form designer (Form Layout),
  • the label editor,
  • the data panel (Browse Table Data and New SQL Query),
  • the trace analyzer (Analyze Trace),
  • the report designer.

The stylesheet gives them:

Feature What it does Visible keyboard focus Buttons, inputs, selects, text areas and every focusable element show an outline in VS Code's focus border colour when you reach them with the keyboard High contrast In the High Contrast and High Contrast Light themes, buttons and inputs get a border in the theme's contrast border colour, and the selected item gets a dashed outline Reduced motion When Windows (or VS Code) asks for reduced motion, all animations and transitions in the panel stop

These panels take their colours from VS Code's theme (--vscode-* theme variables), so they follow your light, dark or high contrast theme. Two parts keep fixed colours on purpose: the form preview, which is drawn with the web client's colours and sizes so it looks like the form your users see, and parts of the report designer and trace analyzer that draw the report page and the timeline.

docs.title: Element designer
docs.text:
• The node tree is an ARIA tree: nodes are tree items with their level, expanded state and selection announced.
  • Keyboard in the tree: Up and Down move between visible nodes; Right expands and Left collapses; Enter on a method opens its code, and on a precision design opens the Report Designer; F12 goes to the element the node refers to.
  • The Properties grid is an ARIA grid. In a property that has a picker, Alt+Down opens the picker.
  • Buttons that switch on and off (for example categories or "modified only") announce their pressed state.
  • Status messages at the bottom are announced politely (live region).
  • Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) undo and redo property changes, except while you type in a field.

See Element-Designer and Properties-Grid-and-Pickers.

docs.title: Form designer and form preview
docs.text:
• The page has three labelled regions: Controls (the outline), Form preview and Properties.
  • In the preview, menu buttons are marked as having a popup and announce whether they are open; their lists are ARIA menus with menu items.

See Form-Designer-and-Preview.

docs.title: Label editor
docs.text:
• The search box is labelled "Search labels".
  • When you edit a row, every input is labelled: "Label ID", "Text" plus the language, and "Comment".
  • Enter saves the row; Escape cancels the edit.

See Label-Editor.

docs.title: Data panel (Browse Table Data, New SQL Query)
docs.text:
• The toolbar is an ARIA toolbar. Its controls are labelled: "Maximum rows", "Company (DataAreaId)", "As-of date", "Filter column", "Filter operator", "Filter value", and "Remove filter" plus the column name.
  • Column headers announce their sort order. Enter or Space on a header sorts by that column.
  • In the result grid, Up and Down move between rows and Enter opens the selected row in the inspector.
  • The record inspector is labelled "Selected row", with "Filter fields", "Previous row" and "Next row".
  • The SQL text area is labelled "SQL query"; Ctrl+Enter runs the query.
  • Status messages are announced politely (status region), and errors are announced right away (alert).

See Browse-Table-Data and SQL-Query-Panel.

docs.title: Trace analyzer (Analyze Trace)
docs.text:
• The views are ARIA tabs; Left and Right switch between them, Home and End go to the first and last.
  • The request list is an ARIA list box labelled "Requests"; Up, Down, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down move through it, and Enter or Right moves into the call tree.
  • The call tree is an ARIA tree grid with levels, position in set, expanded state and column headers; Up, Down, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, Right (expand), Left (collapse), Enter and Space work in it.
  • The tables (for example hot methods and SQL) move by row with the same keys, and Enter runs the row's action where it has one.
  • The summary and the timeline are labelled regions. The filter box is labelled "Filter methods and SQL"; Escape clears it.

See Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: Report designer
docs.text:
• The design surface is labelled: "Design surface. Arrow keys move the selection, Shift+arrows resize, Ctrl+arrows move by 0.1 mm."
  • Keyboard: arrow keys move the selected items by the grid, Ctrl+arrows by 0.1 mm, Shift+arrows resize; Delete removes; Escape clears the selection; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo; Ctrl+A selects all items in the body; Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste; Ctrl+D duplicates; Ctrl+S saves.
  • The toolbars are ARIA toolbars; toggle buttons announce their pressed state; the warnings list is a log region.

The report designer is a visual layout tool: placing items to the millimetre on a page is easiest with a mouse. The keyboard commands above let you move, resize and edit items without one, and the report's structure (datasets, designs, parameters) is also available in the element designer's tree. See Report-Designer.

docs.title: Other panels
docs.text: The hierarchy, references and dependencies diagrams, the entity relationship diagram and the Security panel are drawn as webviews too. They use VS Code's theme colours but do not load the shared stylesheet. Their content is also available in text form: diagrams export as Mermaid text, the Security-Report writes Markdown or CSV, and Find-All-References and Call-and-Type-Hierarchy give the same relations in VS Code's standard views.

docs.title: Copilot
docs.text: Copilot Chat is VS Code's own chat view, with its accessibility features. F&O Studio's agents answer in text; the Copilot Activity view lists every tool call as a tree. See Copilot-Agents and Copilot-Activity.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O) and Go to Symbol in Workspace (Ctrl+T) instead of browsing the Application Explorer tree; both are quick picks you can type into.
  • For results of checks (Review My Changes, Pre-Deploy Checklist, Upgrade Readiness), Copy Report as Markdown or Export Report… in the Results view gives you the whole report as text. See Results-View.
  • F8 and Shift+F8 step through the problems of a build in the editor.
  • To go from a code view to the element's designer, use Open Designer on the editor's right-click menu.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The diagrams, the entity relationship diagram and the Security panel do not load the shared accessibility stylesheet.
  • The form preview uses the web client's fixed colours, not your theme's.
  • Not every panel has been tested with a screen reader end to end.

docs.title: Reporting an accessibility problem
docs.text: Use Report a Problem… (see Report-a-Problem) or open an issue on GitHub. Say which panel or view, which assistive technology and theme you use, and what you expected to happen.

docs.title: Add to Privilege
docs.text: Add to Privilege puts a menu item into a security privilege of your model, as an entry point with the access you choose. You can create a new View or Maintain privilege for it in the same step. Every new menu item needs this before users without the System administrator role can open it. In Visual Studio you open or create the privilege and drag the menu item onto its Entry Points node, then set the Grant properties.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You created a display, output or action menu item and users must get access to it.
  • You follow the usual pattern of one View privilege (read access) and one Maintain privilege (full access) per menu item.
  • You want to add a menu item to a privilege that already exists in your model.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The menu item exists (in any model, standard or yours).
  • The privilege must be in one of your models. Standard privileges cannot be changed; to change access to standard objects, create your own privilege, or a role or duty extension.
  • The new privilege is created in your project's model, or a model you pick.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the command:
  2. Right-click a menu item in Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view and choose Add to Privilege….
  3. Right-click the root node of a menu item in the Element Designer and choose Add to Privilege….
  4. Run F&O Studio: Add to Privilege… from the Command Palette, type part of the menu item's name (at least 3 characters) and pick it.
  5. Choose where it goes:
  6. New privilege…
  7. Existing privilege of your models…
  8. For a new privilege:
  9. Pick the kind: View or Maintain.
  10. Confirm or change the name. The default is the menu item's name followed by the kind, for example ContosoOrderStatusView or ContosoOrderStatusMaintain. Names use letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
  11. If a privilege with that name already exists in your models, the menu item is added to it. If it exists in a standard model, the command stops.
  12. For an existing privilege:
  13. Type part of its name (at least 3 characters).
  14. Pick it from the privileges of your models that match. Standard privileges are not listed.
  15. Choose the access the privilege grants. The list is Read, Update, Create, Correct, Delete and Invoke; you can pick several. The defaults:
Menu item Privilege name Preselected Display ends with Maintain Read, Update, Create, Delete Display anything else Read Output or action any Invoke
  1. F&O Studio creates or updates the privilege and adds it to the active project. A message confirms, for example Display Menu Items ContosoOrderStatus is in privilege ContosoOrderStatusMaintain (Read,Update,Create,Delete).
  2. Click Open Privilege to open it in the Element Designer.

docs.title: What is written
docs.text:
The privilege gets one entry point:

Property Value Name The menu item's name Object Type MenuItemDisplay, MenuItemOutput or MenuItemAction Object Name The menu item's name Grant The access you picked

If the privilege already has an entry point with that name, it is updated with the new grant instead of being added twice.

A new privilege contains only this entry point. Set its label and description in the Element Designer.

docs.title: After adding the privilege
docs.text:
A privilege gives access only when it reaches a user through a duty or a role. Add the new privilege to a duty or role of your model (or to an extension of a standard duty or role). Then check the result:

  • Security View shows roles, duties and privileges of your models.
  • Who Can Access shows the privileges, duties and roles that reach the menu item.
  • Find Security Gaps reports menu items that no privilege grants.
  • Analyze License shows the license the new access needs.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings. The model is the active project's model; without a project you pick one of your models.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/addToPrivilege.ts gets the menu item from the tree node or a picker and asks the questions.
  2. It looks up privileges with the bridge action find_object (exact match for a new name, partial match for an existing one) and keeps only privileges of your models.
  3. It sends create_object (new privilege, type AxSecurityPrivilege, with the entry point) or update_object (existing privilege, entry point added or updated) to the metadata server, which saves the privilege through the metadata API (MetaModelBridge.Security.cs).
  4. It calls add_to_project when a project is active and refreshes the trees.

You can get the same result with Drag and Drop: drop a menu item onto a privilege of your model.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Menu items only. Service operations and other entry point types are not handled by this command.
  • It does not add the privilege to a duty or a role.
  • It does not change standard privileges.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Only menu items can be added to a privilege. The element is not a menu item. Run it on a display, output or action menu item. Privilege <name> exists in <model>, which is not one of your models. The name of the new privilege is taken by a standard privilege. Choose another name, for example with your prefix. None of your models has a privilege matching '<text>'. No privilege of your models matches. Create a new privilege instead, or check the name. Users still cannot open the menu item The privilege is not in a duty or role assigned to them. Add it to a duty or role, deploy, and assign the role.

docs.title: Agent Tools: Analysis
docs.text:
These agent tools answer questions about existing code and metadata: who uses an element, which standard code to follow, where a message comes from, what a role costs in licenses, where code is slow, what a trace shows, what an upgrade breaks, and what Microsoft's documentation says. They don't change anything. For the overview and the guarantees, see MCP-Agent-Tools.

Most of them have a command in F&O Studio that shows the same analysis in VS Code; the "UI equivalent" line of each section links to it.

docs.title: When the agent uses them
docs.text: Question Tool Who calls this method, uses this table, extends this class? xpp_find_references How does standard code do this? Which class should I copy or extend? xpp_find_examples, xpp_search_code Where does this error message come from? xpp_find_message_source Which license does this role need? Who can open this form? Which roles should get my new duty? Are there security gaps or SoD conflicts? xpp_analyze_security Is this code slow? Is this data entity ready for OData and data management? xpp_analyze_performance What happened in this trace? xpp_analyze_trace What breaks when we take the next version? xpp_find_deprecations How does this X++ feature or API work? xpp_search_docs, xpp_get_guide

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk.
  • The cross-reference database of the configuration (named in the configuration, usually on (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB) for xpp_find_references, the usages in xpp_find_message_source, xpp_find_examples and the obsolete-API part of xpp_find_deprecations. Your own code is in it after a build with cross-references (xpp.build.crossReference, default true).
  • Internet access to learn.microsoft.com for xpp_search_docs.
  • A .etl file and the trace event manifests for xpp_analyze_trace.

docs.title: xpp_find_references
docs.text:
Where-used: every element and member that uses or references an element, or one method or field of it. It queries the cross-reference database (indexed, milliseconds). If the database is missing or incomplete, the result says exactly why; agents are told to report that and never fall back to searching XML files.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType (required) string Type of the target: AxClass, AxTable, AxForm, AxEnum, AxEdt, AxView, AxQuery, AxDataEntityView, AxMap, AxMenuItemDisplay, AxMenuItemAction, AxMenuItemOutput, AxTableExtension, AxEnumExtension, AxReport, AxSecurityRole, AxSecurityPrivilege, AxSecurityDuty objectName (required) string Exact name of the target memberName string A method or field of the target: only who uses that member referenceKind string Any (default), MethodCall, TypeReference, InterfaceImplementation, ClassExtended, TestCall, Property, Attribute, TestHelperCall, Tag, MethodOverride maxResults integer Default 25, max 100 includeCode boolean Also show the code line of each reference (max 25 references) 
{ "objectType": "AxClass", "objectName": "SalesFormLetter", "memberName": "construct", "includeCode": true }

A typical use: the API you need is internal or private. The agent finds the public entry points (controllers, services, forms) that call it, and calls or wraps those instead.

UI equivalent: Find-All-References.

docs.title: xpp_find_examples
docs.text:
Finds standard (Microsoft) implementations to learn from, reuse or copy. Give a task in words, an element to resemble, or both. Output: ranked examples with the reason; small, focused examples come first for framework patterns.

Parameter Type Meaning query string The task in words, for example "batch job with a data contract", "number sequence for a new table", "custom lookup", "business event", "report data provider", "service operation", "workflow", "form with the SimpleList pattern" objectType string With objectName: find elements similar to this one (AxClass, AxTable, AxForm...) objectName string The element to resemble maxResults integer Default 15, max 50 
{ "query": "batch job with a data contract" }

{ "objectType": "AxClass", "objectName": "SalesFormLetter", "maxResults": 10 }

Similar elements are those that share the most distinctive references with the given one (base class, interfaces, attributes, called APIs, tables; rare targets count most). A task in words maps to the framework classes such implementations extend, call or carry as attributes. Your own models are left out of the examples.

UI equivalent: Find-Similar-Implementations.

docs.title: xpp_search_code
docs.text:
Searches the X++ source of every package, standard and custom: method code and declarations of classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, queries and maps. Literal text by default, case-insensitive; regex=true for a .NET regular expression. Output: element, method, line and the matching line.

Parameter Type Meaning pattern (required) string Text or regex, at least 3 characters, for example NumberSeq::newGetNum( regex boolean Treat pattern as a .NET regular expression caseSensitive boolean Case-sensitive match objectTypes string[] Limit to these types, for example ["AxClass"]. Default: all code types model string One model or package (a package such as ApplicationSuite covers all its models) maxResults integer Default 50, max 200 
{ "pattern": "SysOperationServiceController", "objectTypes": ["AxClass"], "maxResults": 20 }

The files are scanned in parallel from the metadata folders. Until they are in the operating system's file cache, a search over everything reads them from disk (30 to 60 seconds); limiting to AxClass or one model is much faster.

UI equivalent: Search-Code.

docs.title: xpp_find_message_source
docs.text:
Finds the X++ code that raises a message. Paste the message as the user saw it, values included. It is matched against every label text (placeholders %1..%9 match any value), and the label's usages come from the cross-reference database with the code line: raising code first, tests last. Messages written as literal strings are found by a code search.

For the platform's "Field '%1' must be filled in." it first lists the table fields with that label whose Mandatory property is Yes (on the table or a table extension), and separates code that raises it for one of those fields from code that reuses the text for other fields.

Parameter Type Meaning message (required) string The message text as shown, for example "Customer 1001 is on hold. Cannot post the order." language string Language of the message. Default en-US maxLabels integer Labels to report. Default 5 maxResults integer Usages per label. Default 15 
{ "message": "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." }

UI equivalent: Find-Message-Source. Scenario: Scenario-From-Error-Message-to-Fix.

docs.title: xpp_analyze_security
docs.text:
Security and license analysis of the metadata of all packages. No environment is needed. One tool, six operations chosen with op.

Parameter Type Used by Meaning op (required) string all license, access, placement, gaps, sod or report objectType string license, access license: AxSecurityRole, AxSecurityDuty or AxSecurityPrivilege. access: AxMenuItemDisplay, AxMenuItemOutput, AxMenuItemAction, AxForm, AxTable or AxDataEntityView objectName string license, access The element duty string placement Your new duty objects string[] placement Standard elements of the same job as Type:Name, for example ["AxForm:CustTable", "AxMenuItemDisplay:SalesTableListPage"] role string sod, placement sod: one role (default: the roles of your models and the roles they extend). placement: the requirement's role wording, for example "Accounts receivable clerk" models string[] gaps Models to check (default: your custom models) rulesJson string sod Optional rules: [{"Name":...,"First":duty,"Second":duty,"Severity":"High","Reason":...}] roles string[] report Roles to report model string report All roles of this model and the roles it extends format string report markdown or csv

What each operation returns:

op Result license The user license the object needs (Team Members, Activity, Operations), the menu items and grants that drive it, and which grants Read would lower access Who reaches a menu item, form, table or data entity: privileges, duties and roles with their grants placement Standard roles to give a new duty, ranked by whether they already reach the same standard objects (the forms the duty's menu items open, plus objects) and by label similarity to the role wording gaps Menu items no privilege grants, privileges in no duty, duties in no role, over-granting, missing objects, data entities without permissions sod Segregation-of-duties conflicts in your roles (or one role) against standard rules or rulesJson report A Markdown or CSV security report for roles or a model, for sign-off 
{ "op": "license", "objectType": "AxSecurityRole", "objectName": "TradeSalesClerk" }

{ "op": "access", "objectType": "AxMenuItemDisplay", "objectName": "CustGroup" }

{ "op": "sod", "role": "TradeSalesClerk" }

UI equivalents: Analyze-License, Who-Can-Access, Find-Security-Gaps, Segregation-of-Duties, Security-Report, Security-View.

docs.title: xpp_analyze_performance
docs.text:
Static performance review of the X++ methods of a class, table, form or data entity. No environment is needed. Each finding gives the method, line, why it is slow and the fix. Findings are heuristics: the agent should confirm before changing code.

What it checks:

  • Queries and row-by-row insert, update or delete inside loops.
  • select firstonly inside while select (use a join or exists join).
  • while select of every field.
  • select forupdate without a write.
  • Unbalanced ttsbegin/ttscommit.
  • crossCompany queries.
  • insert_recordset, update_recordset and delete_from that quietly run row by row because the table overrides insert, update or delete, has delete actions or is date-effective.
  • Forms: display methods in grids without cacheAddMethod; data sources that fetch every field but show a few in a grid (OnlyFetchActive); data sources shown in a parent's grid with link type Delayed or Active instead of a join.
  • Data entities: readiness for OData and data management (public entity and collection names, an entity key, staging table fields missing for entity fields, mandatory fields of the root table that are not mapped) and set-based processing over views, entities or temporary tables.

Database log and alerts, which also force row-by-row operations, are environment setup and are not checked.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType (required) string AxClass, AxTable, AxForm or AxDataEntityView objectName (required) string The element 
{ "objectType": "AxClass", "objectName": "CustCollectionLetterCreate" }

Output: <name>: N performance finding(s) in M method(s). then up to 100 lines - [severity] rule in method line N: message Fix: fix.

UI equivalent: Analyze-Performance; rules: Performance-Rules-Reference.

docs.title: xpp_analyze_trace
docs.text:
Analyzes a trace (.etl) taken in the web client (Settings > Trace) or with the trace tools, with F&O Studio's own trace parser. A trace covers every AOS and session that ran while it was recorded: other users, dual-write and OData integrations, batch.

The report lists:

  • the AOS instances and the sessions with their user, UTC time range and errors;
  • errors and exceptions with the full X++ call stack (calls to Global::error, checkFailed, warning, and frames unwound by an exception with the method that caught it);
  • platform messages;
  • the slowest requests with their hot call path;
  • methods by exclusive time; SQL by total time; pauses.

To look at one scenario, the agent calls it again with filters taken from the session list, then reads the methods it names.

Parameter Type Meaning path (required) string Full path of the .etl file minRequestMs number Ignore requests shorter than this when nothing is filtered. Default 50 aos string Only this AOS (machine name or part of it) session string Only this X++ session ID user string Only sessions of this user (user ID or GUID, or part of it) method string Only requests whose call tree has a method containing this text; shows the path to it from string Requests running at or after this time: UTC time (20:05:50), UTC date and time, or seconds from the start of the trace to string Requests that started at or before this time (same formats) manifestFolder string Folder with DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man, only when the tool reports none were found 
{ "path": "C:\\Traces\\SalesOrderPosting.etl", "method": "SalesFormLetter", "from": "20:05:50", "to": "20:06:30" }

The manifests are found in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring, AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring or the registered trace providers' folder. The tool runs in parallel with other calls and never uses the metadata lock.

UI equivalent: Analyze-Trace. Scenario: Scenario-Performance-Tuning-a-Slow-Process.

docs.title: xpp_find_deprecations
docs.text:
Upgrade readiness of one model, in three or four parts:

  1. Every place its code uses a class, table or method marked [SysObsolete], with the attribute's message (often the replacement) and whether it is marked as an error (it will stop compiling). Read from the cross-reference database.
  2. Extension compatibility against the installed application: Chain of Command wrappers whose target method is gone, changed its signature (static, return type, parameters) or is no longer wrappable (private, final, Wrappable(false)/Hookable(false), internal); event handlers whose class, method, delegate or table is gone; table, form and enum extensions whose base element, fields, field groups or controls are gone.
  3. Collisions with other models: your extensions compared with the other installed models' extensions of the same elements.
  4. With previousPackagesFolder: wrapped standard methods whose code changed since the earlier version (number of changed lines, no code), so behaviour around next may differ.
Parameter Type Meaning modelName (required) string The model to check (its package's code is read) previousPackagesFolder string PackagesLocalDirectory of the earlier application version (under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>) 
{ "modelName": "ContosoExtensions", "previousPackagesFolder": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Microsoft\\Dynamics365\\<previous version>\\PackagesLocalDirectory" }

Run it after installing a new version (or on the version you upgrade to) and before building. Environment variables in previousPackagesFolder are expanded.

UI equivalents: Upgrade-Readiness, Standard-Code-Drift. Scenario: Scenario-Upgrade-to-a-New-Version.

docs.title: xpp_search_docs
docs.text:
Searches Microsoft Learn for D365FO, X++, extensibility and technical references, or fetches one Learn page. Output: Source: <url>, other matches the agent can pass as url, and the page text.

Parameter Type Meaning query (required) string What to search for url string A Microsoft Learn URL to fetch instead maxLength integer Maximum characters returned. Default 12000 (accepted range 1000 to 50000) 
{ "query": "Chain of Command wrapping rules" }

How it searches: Microsoft Learn's public MCP endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp, microsoft_docs_search) first, then Learn's keyword search API. Questions about code get developer pages (/dev-itpro/) first. Only learn.microsoft.com and docs.microsoft.com URLs are fetched; AX 2012 pages are refused with the advice to read the D365FO element with xpp_read_object.

docs.title: xpp_get_guide
docs.text:
Returns the full F&O Studio development guide by topic. The instructions the agent always has are its summary; the guide adds rules with examples and code templates. Without topic it lists the topics.

Parameter Type Meaning topic string Words of a topic title, for example ssrs, chain of command, event handlers, display methods, language reference 
{ "topic": "acceptance test library" }

Topics include: the tool-first directive, query size limits, what to do when the API you need is internal or not extensible, JSON only, environment, workflow, critical rules, models and packages, ownership, the five extensibility mechanisms, the X++ language reference, object types and properties, display and edit methods, the full decision tree, naming conventions, best practices, tests with the Acceptance Test Library (ATL), and SSRS report patterns. One topic is returned at a time, capped in size.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Tool Implementation xpp_find_references XRefQuery (XRefQuery.cs): SQL against the cross-reference database of the active configuration xpp_find_examples CodeExamples (CodeExamples.cs) over the cross-reference database xpp_search_code CodeSearch (CodeSearch.cs): parallel scan of the metadata files, parsing only files with a match xpp_find_message_source MessageTrace (MessageTrace.cs): label texts of all packages (built once per server), then label usages from the cross-reference database xpp_analyze_security SecurityAnalysis (SecurityAnalysis.cs) xpp_analyze_performance Bridge action analyze_performance (PerformanceAnalysisService) xpp_analyze_trace TraceService in server/Tracing, F&O Studio's own .etl parser xpp_find_deprecations DeprecationReport plus bridge actions extension_compatibility, extension_collisions and wrapper_drift xpp_search_docs DocSearchHandler (DocSearchHandler.cs) xpp_get_guide AgentGuide over the embedded XppCopilotGuide.txt

All of these tools are registered as ParallelRead: they run in parallel with other calls. Those that need the metadata API still wait for its lock.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Where-used, examples, message usages and obsolete-API usages depend on the cross-reference database. Your own code is only in it after a build with cross-references; a deleted element's own entries are removed by F&O Studio.
  • Performance findings are static heuristics, not measurements. Use traces for measurements.
  • Security analysis works on metadata, not on the user-role assignments of an environment.
  • xpp_search_docs needs internet access to Microsoft Learn.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix xpp_find_references explains that the cross-reference database is missing or unusable No XRef database for the configuration, or LocalDB not running Restore it (Connect-to-Environment) or start LocalDB Your own code is missing from where-used The model was built without cross-references Build with xpp.build.crossReference on (Build-Project-and-Model) xpp_search_code takes close to a minute The files are not in the file cache yet Limit with objectTypes or model; later searches are faster xpp_analyze_trace reports no manifests found The event manifests are not in the usual folders Pass manifestFolder (or set xpp.trace.manifestFolder for the panel) Pass modelName. from xpp_find_deprecations modelName missing Pass the model Only Microsoft Learn URLs are allowed url is not on learn.microsoft.com Use query or a Learn URL

docs.title: Agent Tools: Build and Data
docs.text:
These agent tools close the loop after the agent changes code: build the model, run the best-practice checks, run the unit tests on the environment, list what changed in Git, create a deployable package, look at business data, and show the user an element in the editor. For the overview and the guarantees, see MCP-Agent-Tools.

Tool Purpose Where it runs xpp_build Build a custom model like Dynamics 365 > Build: LabelC, xppc with cross-references, reportsc MCP server xpp_check_best_practice Run the X++ best-practice rules (xppbp) on a custom model MCP server xpp_package Create a deployable package (.zip) of custom models from their last build MCP server xpp_diff_changes List the elements of your models that changed in Git MCP server xpp_run_tests Run SysTest classes on the environment's cloud runtime VS Code extension xpp_query_data Run one read-only SELECT on the environment's business database VS Code extension xpp_open_element Show an element in the X++ code editor or designer VS Code extension

The last three are VS Code language model tools: they are registered by the extension and don't exist when the server runs in another MCP host (MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code). You can reference them in a chat prompt as #xppRunTests, #xppQueryData and #xppOpenElement.

docs.title: When the agent uses them
docs.text:
• After every code change: xpp_build, then fix every error. A build is only successful when the result says BUILD SUCCEEDED.
  • Next to the build: xpp_check_best_practice, then fix what it reports or say why a warning stays.
  • After deploying: xpp_run_tests to run the tests against the deployed code.
  • For a code review or a pull request description: xpp_diff_changes, then xpp_read_object on each element.
  • Only when you ask for a package: xpp_package. It does not deploy anything.
  • While investigating behaviour: xpp_query_data, after you confirm the query.
  • When you ask to see code: xpp_open_element, never the metadata .xml file.

The agent does not deploy or synchronize a UDE database with these tools. You deploy with Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its compiler tools in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin (xppc, LabelC, xppbp, reportsc, SyncEngine).
  • A custom model; builds, best practice and packages refuse other models.
  • Git for xpp_diff_changes: your models must be in a Git repository.
  • For xpp_run_tests: signed in to the unified developer environment and the code deployed (Run-Tests).
  • For xpp_query_data: database credentials (F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials on a UDE, or the local AxDB on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment; see Database-Access).

docs.title: xpp_build
docs.text:
Builds a custom model exactly like Dynamics 365 > Build: compiles label files (LabelC), then X++ (xppc) with cross-references, then the reports (reportsc), and returns every error, fatal error and warning with element, method, line and message.

Parameter Type Meaning modelName string Model to build. Default: the active project's model scope string model (default) or project: report only the diagnostics of elements in the active project (xppc still compiles the whole package) syncDatabase boolean Synchronize the database after a successful build where a local database exists. Default false 
{ "modelName": "ContosoExtensions", "scope": "project" }

Steps, as Visual Studio does them:

  1. When the active project belongs to the package: build the C# projects and copy the assemblies the X++ project references into <package>\bin (Solution-View-and-CSharp-References).
  2. LabelC for every label file of the model, into <package>\Resources.
  3. xppc with -metadata, -compilermetadata, -modelmodule, -output=<package>\bin, -xmllog, -log, -appBase, -refPath, one -referenceFolder per reference folder plus the custom folder, and -xref with the configuration's cross-reference server and database.
  4. After a successful X++ build: reportsc compiles the reports to <package>\Reports.
  5. With syncDatabase=true: SyncEngine on cloud-hosted and VHD environments. On a UDE the result says the database is synchronized by deployment instead.

Output:

BUILD SUCCEEDED: ContosoExtensions in 41s - 0 error(s), 2 warning(s).
<one line per diagnostic, errors first>
Reports compiled to <custom folder>\ContosoExtensions\Reports.

Identical diagnostics are listed once with a count ((x12)). At most 80 lines are listed; the rest are counted with the path of the xppc XML log (<package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppc.xml). A build also fails when xppc exits with an error or no assembly was written, and then the end of the log is shown.

Builds take minutes. Logs are kept in <package>\BuildLogs.

UI equivalent: Build-Project-and-Model, Compiler-Diagnostics.

docs.title: xpp_check_best_practice
docs.text:
Runs the X++ best-practice rules (xppbp, the checks Visual Studio runs and partner code reviews use) on a custom model and returns every warning and error with element, member, line, rule moniker and message. Takes a minute or more.

Parameter Type Meaning modelName string Model to check. Default: the active project's model scope string model (default) or project: only the active project's elements 
{ "modelName": "ContosoExtensions", "scope": "project" }

Output: errors first, at most 80 lines, then ... N more.. The XML log is <package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppbp.xml.

UI equivalent: Best-Practice-Checks.

docs.title: xpp_package
docs.text:
Creates a deployable package (.zip) of custom models with the script Visual Studio's Create Deployment Package runs (RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin), from their last build. It does not build and does not deploy.

Parameter Type Meaning modelNames string[] Custom models to package. Default: the active project's model version string Package version in the form 1.0.0.0 (default) 
{ "modelNames": ["ContosoExtensions"], "version": "1.0.3.0" }

Output: PACKAGE CREATED: <path of the zip> or PACKAGE FAILED (exit N)., then the packages and version, the reminder that the package contains the last build, and the end of the script's log. Packages are written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\packages\<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.

UI equivalent: Create-Deployment-Package.

docs.title: xpp_diff_changes
docs.text:
Lists the elements of your models that changed in Git: uncommitted changes, and with baseBranch also what the current branch changed since it left that branch (added, modified, deleted, renamed).

Parameter Type Meaning baseBranch string Branch to compare with, for example main. Omit for uncommitted changes only 
{ "baseBranch": "main" }

Output:

3 changed element(s) (uncommitted and since main):
- ContosoExtensions AxClass/ContosoOrderStatusService: modified (uncommitted)
- ContosoExtensions AxTableExtension/CustGroup.ContosoExtensions: added (on the branch)
- ...

For every model folder under the custom metadata folder it runs git status --porcelain and, with a base branch, git merge-base HEAD <branch> and git diff --name-status on the model's path. Only Ax<Type>/<Name>.xml files count as elements. At most 500 are listed. If none of your models is in a Git repository, it says so.

UI equivalent: Show-Changed-Elements, Review-My-Changes. Scenario: Scenario-Review-a-Pull-Request.

docs.title: xpp_run_tests
docs.text:
Runs X++ unit tests (SysTestCase classes) on the connected unified developer environment's cloud runtime, the same way Visual Studio's Test Explorer does, and returns pass or fail per test with assertion messages and infolog.

Parameter Type Meaning classes string[] Test class names. Omit to run every test class of the active project methods string[] Only these test methods of the given classes timeoutMinutes number How long to wait for results. Default 30 
{ "classes": ["ContosoOrderStatusServiceTest"] }

Before it runs, VS Code asks you to confirm: "Run X++ tests on the environment. The tests run on the connected environment against the deployed code and may create test data there." The run's lines go to the X++ Tests output channel.

Tests run against the code deployed to the environment. If the build is newer than the last deploy from this machine, the result starts with WARNING: and says to deploy and run the tests again. If the run fails, the result starts with TEST RUN FAILED: and the last lines of the log.

The tool uses the same runner as the Run Tests command, in @fno-studio/core (runTests), with your Dataverse sign-in. See Run-Tests and Test-Explorer.

docs.title: xpp_query_data
docs.text:
Runs one read-only T-SQL SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) against the business database (AxDB) of the active environment and returns tab-separated rows.

Parameter Type Meaning sql (required) string One SELECT statement maxRows number Rows to return, 1 to 500. Default 50 
{ "sql": "SELECT TOP 10 ACCOUNTNUM, CUSTGROUP FROM CUSTTABLE WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf'", "maxRows": 10 }

Rules the agent is given: SELECT only (no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, EXEC, INTO); one statement; SQL names are the table and field names (for example CUSTTABLE.ACCOUNTNUM); filter per company with DATAAREAID in lower case; always add TOP or WHERE and select only the columns needed. Enum fields hold integers; RecId values come back as text.

Every query needs your confirmation: VS Code shows "Run a read-only query on the environment database" with the SQL.

Output:

QUERY OK on <database> (35 ms, read-only).
10 row(s)
ACCOUNTNUM  CUSTGROUP
...

(limit reached) marks a truncated result. Output over 20,000 characters is cut with a note to select fewer columns or rows. Errors come back as QUERY FAILED: .... Without credentials the answer is NO DATABASE ACCESS with the advice to run F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials.

How it stays read-only: the extension's own server process refuses statements that are not a single read-only query, and runs it in a transaction that is always rolled back. That process is started with --allow-data; the MCP server Copilot starts can't reach business data, and the agent never sees the connection or credentials. See Database-Access and SQL-Query-Panel.

docs.title: xpp_open_element
docs.text:
Shows an element to the user in F&O Studio's editor: classes, and the code of tables, forms, views, entities, queries and maps, in the X++ code editor (optionally at a method, with a line of code selected); other elements in their designer.

Parameter Type Meaning objectName (required) string Element name, for example SalesFormLetter objectType string AxClass, AxTable, AxForm... Optional when the name is unique method string Method to scroll to (code editor) text string Code to select, for example the line with the bug; searched from the method on 
{ "objectName": "CustGroup", "objectType": "AxTable", "method": "find" }

Answers: Opened <name> in the X++ code editor at line N. (with method ... not found or text not found notes), Opened <type> <name> in the designer., NOT FOUND: no element named <name>., or AMBIGUOUS: <name> exists as AxTable, AxForm; pass objectType. Without a method or text, non-class elements open in their designer. See Open-Element and X++-Code-View.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice and xpp_package pass their arguments to the bridge actions build, best_practice and create_package, implemented in BuildService (server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs). They run Microsoft's command-line tools from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin. C# references are prepared by ProjectReferences (server/Host/ProjectReferences.cs), which follows the same rules as the extension's src/dotnetReferences.ts.
  • xpp_diff_changes is ChangedElementsReport (ChangedElementsReport.cs), which runs git. The base branch name is validated before it is used.
  • xpp_run_tests is registered in src/tests.ts, xpp_query_data in src/database/queryTool.ts (readOnlyQuery in core/src/data/client.ts, server side DataQueryService), and xpp_open_element in src/goTo.ts. Their definitions are in contributes.languageModelTools of package.json.
  • These server tools run in order with other non-read tools; they are not ParallelRead.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only custom models can be built, checked or packaged.
  • scope=project filters the diagnostics; xppc still compiles the whole package.
  • No database sync on a UDE from xpp_build: deploy the package instead (Synchronize-Database).
  • xpp_package packages the last build; it does not build first.
  • xpp_run_tests tests the deployed code, not your local build.
  • xpp_query_data is read-only and row-limited; it can't change data.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Pass modelName, or select a project with xpp_select_project. No model given and no active project Pass modelName or select a project Model '...' is not one of your custom models; only your own models can be built. The model is a reference model Build your own model scope 'project' needs an active project (xpp_select_project). No active project Select a project or use scope=model BUILD FAILED: building or copying the projects and assemblies ... references. A referenced C# project failed to build Fix the C# project; check xpp.build.msbuildPath BUILD FAILED: label compilation (LabelC) exited with N. A label file is invalid Open it in the Label-Editor version must look like 1.0.0.0. Wrong package version format Use four numbers Your models are not in a Git repository, so changes can't be listed. No Git repository Put your models under Git (Source-Control-for-X++) NO DATABASE ACCESS: ... No credentials for the environment's database Run F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials Test results don't reflect your change The build is not deployed Deploy, then run again (Deploy-to-Environment)

docs.title: Agent Tools: Metadata
docs.text:
These are the agent tools that read and change D365FO elements, find them, describe models and the environment, work with labels and manage the D365FO project. They all go through Microsoft's metadata API in F&O Studio's server, so an agent never reads or writes AOT XML files. For the overview, the guarantees and how the tools are registered, see MCP-Agent-Tools.

Each section gives the tool's purpose, every input parameter, the output and an example of the arguments object of a tools/call request. Examples use standard objects and a custom model named ContosoExtensions.

docs.title: When the agent uses them
docs.text: Task Tools, in the usual order Understand an element xpp_find_object, xpp_read_object Create something new xpp_find_examples (see Agent-Tools-Analysis), xpp_get_object_type_schema, xpp_create_object, xpp_validate_object Extend a standard table or form xpp_read_object / xpp_get_form_layout on the base, xpp_create_object with AxTableExtension / AxFormExtension Change an element of your model xpp_read_object, xpp_update_object Clean up xpp_delete_object or xpp_remove_from_project Labels xpp_read_label, xpp_create_object (AxLabelFile), xpp_create_label Project xpp_select_project, xpp_list_project_items, xpp_add_to_project

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk.
  • A custom model in the custom metadata folder for every write (Models-and-Model-Dependencies).
  • An active project if new elements should be added to it. Without one, xpp_get_environment says ActiveProject: none and new elements are not added to a project.

docs.title: xpp_read_object
docs.text:
Reads any element by type and name: the declaration, every method's signature (with internal, private, public) and full source, and the strongly typed metadata (typedMetadata plus properties, enum values, fields, indexes, field groups, relations, data sources), the model and whether you can edit it. Large objects return a summary first.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType string Any metadata type: AxClass, AxTable, AxForm, AxEnum, AxEdt, AxView, AxQuery, AxMap, AxReport, AxDataEntityView, AxTableExtension, AxFormExtension... objectName string The element name methodNames string[] Return the full source of only these methods (after a read that listed signatures only) sections string[] Only these sections, for example properties, dataSources, entityFields, fields, relations, indexes, fieldGroups, methods, declaration, controls, typedMetadata. ["summary"] lists the sections with their sizes; ["all"] returns everything filePath string Absolute path of the metadata file, if you have it; objectType + objectName is preferred

Output: a header (ObjectType, Name, Model, Editable: YES/NO), then === Declaration ===, the methods and the metadata. Without sections, objects over 25,000 characters return their small sections plus a list of the large ones.

{ "objectType": "AxClass", "objectName": "SalesFormLetter", "methodNames": ["construct"] }

docs.title: xpp_create_object
docs.text:
Creates a new element, all or nothing, and adds it to the active project. The response ends with a Validation: line; check it.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType (required) string One of: AxClass, AxTable, AxView, AxDataEntityView, AxEdt, AxEnum, AxForm, AxTile, AxMenu, AxMenuItemDisplay, AxMenuItemOutput, AxMenuItemAction, AxQuery, AxSecurityPrivilege, AxSecurityDuty, AxSecurityRole, AxService, AxServiceGroup, AxConfigurationKey, AxTableExtension, AxEnumExtension, AxEdtExtension, AxFormExtension, AxDataEntityViewExtension, AxSecurityDutyExtension, AxSecurityRoleExtension, AxLabelFile, AxMenuExtension, AxCompositeDataEntityView, AxWorkflowCategory, AxWorkflowTemplate, AxWorkflowApproval, AxReport objectName (required) string Name, with the model's naming prefix. Extensions are named <Base>.<Suffix> modelName string Target model; default the active project's model typedMetadata object Full typed metadata graph of the type (see xpp_get_object_type_schema) declaration string Plain X++ class or table declaration; no XML, no CDATA methods string[] Complete X++ method sources; XML is rejected properties object Scalar properties as strings (Label, IsExtensible, TableGroup, EdtType, Extends, StringSize, Languages...); bool, int and enum values are converted enumValues object[] AxEnum: { name, value, label } (name, value required) fields object[] Tables: { name, fieldType, extendedDataType, enumType, label }; fieldType is String, Int, Real, Date, DateTime, Enum, Int64, Container, Guid or Time indexes object[] { name, allowDuplicates, alternateKey, fields[] } fieldGroups object[] { name, label, fields[] } relations object[] { name, relatedTable, constraints: [{ field, relatedField }] }; every relation is checked before saving dataSources object[] AxQuery: { name, table, parentDataSource, joinMode, linkType, dynamicFields, fields[], relations, firstOnly, ranges: [{ name, field, value }] }. AxFormExtension: data sources to add (name, table, parentDataSource, linkType) controls object[] AxFormExtension: controls to add: { name, controlType, parent, position (end, begin, after), previousSibling, dataSource, dataField, dataGroup, label, properties, controls[] } controlModifications object[] AxFormExtension: { name, properties } on base-form controls. Allowed properties: Text, Label, HelpText, Caption, Visible, Enabled, EnableFormRef, CountryRegionCodes, Pattern, PatternVersion, NeedsRecord, SaveRecord, AllowEdit, NeededPermission, Style, DataGroup entryPoints object[] Privileges: { name, objectType, objectName, grant }; objectType MenuItemDisplay, MenuItemOutput or MenuItemAction; grant such as Read or Read,Update,Create,Delete or Invoke dataEntityPermissions object[] Privileges: { name, grant, integrationMode (All, DataServices, DataManagement) } privileges string[] Duties, roles and their extensions: privileges to add duties string[] Roles and role extensions: duties to add entityFields object[] AxDataEntityViewExtension: { name, dataSource, dataField, label, mandatory }; the staging table extension gets the same fields skipStagingTable boolean AxDataEntityViewExtension: don't extend the staging table. Default false rootDataEntities object[] AxCompositeDataEntityView: one root { name, dataEntity, embeddedDataEntities: [{ name, dataEntity, relation, embeddedDataEntities }] } menuElements object[] AxMenuExtension: { name, menuItemName, menuItemType (Display, Output, Action), parent, position, previousSibling }

Rules the tool applies:

  • Extensions. To change a standard table, enum or EDT, create AxTableExtension, AxEnumExtension or AxEdtExtension named <Base>.<Suffix> in your model. Fields, indexes, field groups, relations and enum values are added to the base; properties become property modifications of the base.
  • Form extensions. Call xpp_get_form_layout first. Placement is validated against the base form plus all its existing extensions before saving and verified after saving. Other control properties in controlModifications are rejected (they fail the build with UnsupportedPropertyForModification).
  • Security. Standard privileges can't be extended: create your own privilege and add it to a standard duty or role with AxSecurityDutyExtension / AxSecurityRoleExtension.
  • Label files. objectName is the label file ID, properties.Languages such as en-US,fr-CA; one label file per language is created.

Example, a table extension with one field:

{
  "objectType": "AxTableExtension",
  "objectName": "CustGroup.ContosoExtensions",
  "modelName": "ContosoExtensions",
  "fields": [ { "name": "ContosoPriority", "fieldType": "Int", "extendedDataType": "Integer", "label": "@ContosoLabels:Priority" } ]
}

Example, a form extension that places a field after an existing control:

{
  "objectType": "AxFormExtension",
  "objectName": "CustGroup.ContosoExtensions",
  "controls": [ { "name": "ContosoPriority", "parent": "<group from xpp_get_form_layout>", "position": "after",
                  "previousSibling": "<control from xpp_get_form_layout>", "dataSource": "CustGroup", "dataField": "ContosoPriority" } ]
}

docs.title: xpp_update_object
docs.text:
Changes an element of your own model: declaration, methods, properties, structure, form extension controls, security content. Only custom-model elements; read the element first.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType, objectName (required) string The element. For extensions, properties are written as property modifications of the base typedMetadata object Full typed metadata graph declaration string Replaces the declaration methods string[] Methods to add or replace (matched by name) removeMethodNames string[] Methods to remove properties object Scalar properties to set enumValues object[] Values to add; existing names are skipped fields object[] New fields. An existing name is refused; the EDT's base type must match fieldType; a removed field name can't come back with another base type updateFields object[] Change fields this object defines: { name, extendedDataType, enumType, label, helpText, properties }. The base type never changes removeFields, removeIndexes, removeFieldGroups, removeRelations string[] Names to remove (removed fields also leave their field groups) indexes, fieldGroups, relations object[] Add; an existing one of this object with the same name is replaced dataSources object[] AxQuery data sources, or data sources to add to an AxFormExtension controls object[] AxFormExtension: controls to add (same shape as in create) controlModifications object[] AxFormExtension: allowed property changes on base controls updateControls object[] AxFormExtension: change controls this extension added: { name, properties, label, dataSource, dataField, dataGroup, parent, position, previousSibling }; moves are verified removeControls string[] Controls this extension added (with their children). Base controls can't be removed: hide them with Visible=No removeControlModifications string[] "Control" or "Control.Property" entryPoints object[] Privileges: add or update by name; grant Read, Update, Create, Correct, Delete, Invoke or All privileges, duties string[] Add to duties and roles (and their extensions) dataEntityPermissions object[] Add or update removeSecurityItems string[] Entry points, data entity permissions, privileges or duties to remove entityFields, skipStagingTable object[], boolean Data entity extensions, as in create menuElements object[] AxMenuExtension: add or replace by name rootDataEntities object[] AxCompositeDataEntityView: the full reference tree (replaces the current one) 
{
  "objectType": "AxClass",
  "objectName": "ContosoOrderStatusService",
  "methods": [ "public static void main(Args _args)\n{\n    info(\"Done\");\n}" ]
}

To change a field's type, add a new field with another name and remove the old one: an Int field can't become a String field, because the database sync can't convert the column (Visual Studio behaves the same).

docs.title: xpp_delete_object
docs.text:
Deletes an element of your own model completely (the metadata file and the project entry), like Visual Studio's Delete. Ownership is checked first. Then where-used: when other elements reference it, the delete is refused and the referencing elements are listed, unless force is true. If where-used can't be checked, the result says so.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType (required) string Metadata type. Label files are deleted per language: <Id>_<lang> objectName (required) string The element force boolean Delete even when referenced (the referencing elements stop compiling). Default false 
{ "objectType": "AxClass", "objectName": "ContosoOrderStatusService" }

docs.title: xpp_validate_object
docs.text:
Checks that an element exists, is in the active project and has the expected metadata, with a deep comparison of each section you pass. Returns valid=true only when every check passes; otherwise a list of mismatches with expected and actual values. Create and update run it automatically.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType, objectName (required) string The element typedMetadata object Graph compared recursively (form controls, design, query data sources, role privileges...) properties object Expected key-value pairs, compared case-insensitively fields object[] Name, fieldType, extendedDataType, enumType, label enumValues object[] Name, value, label indexes object[] Name, allowDuplicates, fields relations object[] Name, relatedTable, constraints fieldGroups object[] Name, label, fields entryPoints object[] Name, objectType, objectName, grant dataSources object[] Table, joinMode, linkType, ranges, child data sources 
{ "objectType": "AxEnum", "objectName": "ContosoOrderStatus", "enumValues": [ { "name": "Open", "value": 0 } ] }

docs.title: xpp_get_object_type_schema
docs.text:
Returns a JSON schema for an element type, generated by reflection over Microsoft's metadata classes. Agents use it to learn the full typedMetadata shape for create, update and validate.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType (required) string For example AxClass, AxTable, AxForm, AxEnum, AxQuery, AxView 
{ "objectType": "AxEnum" }

docs.title: xpp_get_form_layout
docs.text:
Shows the effective layout of a form: the base form with all its extensions applied by D365FO's own extension applier. Lists the data sources and the control tree with each control's type, binding and the extension that added it. Required before creating or updating an AxFormExtension.

Parameter Type Meaning formName (required) string The base form (for example CustTable), not the extension rootControl string Show only the subtree under this control maxDepth integer Tree depth. Default 4, max 12. Containers with hidden children show (+N children) 
{ "formName": "CustGroup", "maxDepth": 3 }

docs.title: xpp_find_object
docs.text:
Searches the loaded metadata for elements by name, across all models and packages. Best for one exact name. Roles, duties and privileges (with a partial name) are also found by label text, such as "Sales manager"; each match shows its label. Output: matches with type, model and whether they are yours; exact matches come first.

Parameter Type Meaning objectName (required) string Full or partial name, case-insensitive; partial names need at least 3 characters objectType string Limit to one type (much faster). An unknown type is reported as an error, never as "not found" exactMatch boolean Only exact name matches. Default false maxResults integer Default 10, max 50 
{ "objectName": "CustGroup", "objectType": "AxTable", "exactMatch": true }

A no-match means nothing matched in the loaded metadata. Scans stop after a few seconds and return partial results with a message; the agent should narrow the search, not repeat it.

docs.title: xpp_list_objects
docs.text:
Lists a handful of elements whose name contains a text. Only for substring discovery.

Parameter Type Meaning nameFilter (required) string At least 3 characters, specific (for example SalesOrder) objectType string Strongly recommended; required with modelName modelName string Model filter maxResults integer Default 10, max 50 
{ "nameFilter": "CustGroup", "objectType": "AxForm", "maxResults": 5 }

docs.title: xpp_list_model_objects
docs.text:
Lists what one model contains, reading the model's index on disk without loading metadata. Without objectType it returns counts per type; with it, sorted names, paged. Names only; reflects saved elements only.

Parameter Type Meaning modelName (required) string Model, for example ApplicationPlatform or your model objectType string Type to list; omit for counts per type nameFilter string Case-insensitive substring offset integer Default 0 limit integer Default 200, max 1000 
{ "modelName": "ContosoExtensions", "objectType": "AxClass" }

docs.title: xpp_list_models
docs.text:
Lists all models of the environment with their display name and editability (your own models are marked). No parameters.

{}

docs.title: xpp_get_model_info
docs.text:
Returns a model's name, display name, publisher, version, layer, model ID, package and dependencies.

Parameter Type Meaning modelName (required) string The model 
{ "modelName": "ContosoExtensions" }

docs.title: xpp_get_environment
docs.text: Returns CustomMetadataFolder, each ReferenceMetadataFolder, ActiveProject, ActiveModel and Layer. Agents are told to call it only when the task needs this context, not to check whether an element exists. No parameters.

docs.title: xpp_read_label
docs.text:
Reads labels by ID or searches them by text. A full reference such as @SYS7149 or @SCM:SalesStatusLabel can be passed as labelId without labelFileId.

Parameter Type Meaning labelFileId string Label file ID; optional with a full @ reference language string Default en-US labelId string Label ID or full reference searchText string Find labels containing this text maxResults integer Default 25, max 100 
{ "labelId": "@SYS7149" }

docs.title: xpp_create_label
docs.text:
Creates labels in a label file of your model: one (labelId + text) or many (labels), each in the given language and optionally in other languages. Each label file is written once per call. The result lists every label and language as created, unchanged (same text already there) or FAILED, and the reference to use in properties: @<labelFileId>:<labelId>. The label file must exist (create it with xpp_create_object, type AxLabelFile).

Parameter Type Meaning labelFileId (required) string The label file ID language string Language of text. Default en-US labelId string Letters and digits; omit when using labels text string The text translations object Texts in other languages of the same file, keyed by language code comment string Optional comment labels object[] { labelId, text, comment, translations } (labelId, text required) 
{
  "labelFileId": "ContosoLabels",
  "labels": [
    { "labelId": "Priority", "text": "Priority", "translations": { "fr-CA": "Priorité" } },
    { "labelId": "PriorityHelp", "text": "Priority of the customer group" }
  ]
}

Label text files are not AOT metadata: the server writes <Id>.<lang>.label.txt under your model's AxLabelFile\LabelResources\<lang> folder directly, sorted by ID, and only under the custom metadata folder. See Label-Editor.

docs.title: xpp_select_project
docs.text:
Without projectFile, lists the .rnrproj projects that can be opened (the active one marked *), from searchFolder, the current project's repos folder and %USERPROFILE%\source\repos. With projectFile, makes it the active project for all tools: new elements are added to it and scope=project builds use it. The VS Code project view follows the selection.

Parameter Type Meaning projectFile string Full path of the .rnrproj to activate; omit to list searchFolder string Extra folder to search, 3 levels deep

docs.title: xpp_add_to_project
docs.text:
Adds an existing element to the active project, the way Visual Studio saves it (<Content Include="AxClass\Name">).

Parameter Type Meaning objectType, objectName (required) string The element 
{ "objectType": "AxTable", "objectName": "CustGroup" }

docs.title: xpp_list_project_items
docs.text: Lists the items of the active project with their file paths. Says The active project is empty. or No active project. Select one with xpp_select_project. No parameters.

docs.title: xpp_remove_from_project
docs.text:
Excludes an element from the active project and keeps it in the model, like Visual Studio's Exclude From Project.

Parameter Type Meaning objectType, objectName (required) string The element

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• xpp_create_object, xpp_update_object, xpp_list_models, xpp_get_environment, xpp_list_project_items, xpp_remove_from_project and xpp_select_project pass their arguments to the bridge action of the same name (create_object, update_object, ...) in MetaModelBridgeServer.cs. Element types and what each supports are in MetaModelBridge.ElementTypes.cs.
  • xpp_delete_object first calls delete_object with checkOnly (ownership and existence), then queries the cross-reference database for users of the element, then deletes.
  • xpp_list_model_objects is served by ModelObjectLister (ModelObjectLister.cs), which reads the model folder on disk.
  • Labels are handled by LabelStore in server/Host; .rnrproj edits by XppProject.
  • After a write the metadata host reloads what changed, so the next read sees it.
  • Write tools are checked against your models, the Copilot scope and the open checkpoint (see MCP-Agent-Tools).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Writes only in your own models. Standard reports and standard privileges can't be extended; copy the report (Agent-Tools-Reports) or create your own privilege.
  • xpp_list_model_objects reflects saved elements only.
  • Name searches are bounded in time and results; they are not a full inventory.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Validation: FAILED after a create or update The saved element doesn't contain everything requested Read the mismatches; fix with xpp_update_object or delete with xpp_delete_object ... is still referenced by N object(s): ... Not deleted. Other elements use it Remove the references first, or pass force=true Model '...' is not one of your custom models. modelName points to a reference model Use your own model A form extension control is refused The parent or previous sibling doesn't exist in the effective layout, or a modification uses a property outside the allowed list Call xpp_get_form_layout and pick placement from its output Partial results with a message from xpp_find_object The scan hit its time limit Pass objectType and exactMatch=true

docs.text:

  • Scenario-Extend-a-Standard-Form-and-Table
