docs.title: Agent Tools: Reports
docs.text:
These agent tools let an agent work on SSRS reports the way a report developer does in Visual Studio's report designer, and add what Visual Studio doesn't have: rendering a precision design with Microsoft's report engine and seeing the pages, measuring a scanned form in millimetres, and laying the rendered page over the scan to see how far each field is off. Together they let an agent build a report for preprinted stationery (a cheque, an invoice form) and check every field's position. For the overview and the guarantees, see MCP-Agent-Tools.

Tool Purpose Changes metadata xpp_get_report_design Read a report: designs, datasets, parameters, page geometry, items in mm, warnings, RDL No xpp_set_report_design Save a precision design's RDL, generate one from an auto design, or copy a standard report into your model Yes, your model only xpp_render_report Render a precision design with sample or given data; pages as images, item positions, optional PDF No xpp_measure_image Measure a scanned form: scale, deskew, boxes, rules, text with positions, a picture with a mm grid No xpp_compare_layout Overlay a rendered page on the scan and report each text box's offset in mm No

docs.title: When the agent uses them
docs.text:
• To learn how a standard report builds its layout (for example SalesInvoice, PurchPurchaseOrder, Cheque_US) before designing one.
  • To change the layout of a standard report: copy it into your model and change the copy (reports have no extensions).
  • To place fields on preprinted stationery from a scan, then iterate until every field is within tolerance.

The Report Builder agent (Agents-for-Developers) follows this loop from a scanned or sample document. Scenario: Scenario-Report-from-a-Scanned-Document.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk.
  • A custom model for xpp_set_report_design.
  • For xpp_render_report and xpp_compare_layout: the report preview runtime. Install it in VS Code with F&O Studio: Install Report Preview Runtime (Report-Preview).
  • For xpp_measure_image and xpp_compare_layout: a scan as PNG, JPEG, TIFF or BMP (export a PDF page as a 300 dpi image first). Text reading uses Windows' built-in OCR on your machine; nothing is uploaded. The OCR language must be installed in Windows.

docs.title: The loop the agent follows
docs.text:
1. xpp_measure_image on the scan: calibrate the scale, read the boxes, rules and printed text with their positions in mm.
  2. xpp_get_report_design on the report to change (or a standard one to learn from): datasets, fields, page geometry.
  3. Create or copy the report and its precision design with xpp_set_report_design (duplicateOf, fromAutoDesign or rdl).
  4. Write the RDL with items at the measured positions; save it with xpp_set_report_design.
  5. xpp_render_report with data that shows the values printed on the sample, to see real widths.
  6. xpp_compare_layout against the scan; move each item by its reported offset; repeat steps 4 to 6 until every item is within toleranceMm.
  7. Build the model with xpp_build (Agent-Tools-Build-and-Data); the build compiles the report for deployment.

docs.title: xpp_get_report_design
docs.text:
Reads an SSRS report: its designs, datasets with fields and types, parameters, and for a precision design the page geometry, every report item with its position in mm on the page (as designed, before growth), layout warnings (body wider than the page, fonts the cloud doesn't have, items outside the body) and the RDL text to edit.

Parameter Type Meaning reportName (required) string The report (AxReport) designName string The design. Default: the first design includeRdl boolean Include the RDL text. Default true; false for the summary only 
{ "reportName": "SalesInvoice", "includeRdl": false }

Output, in order:

  • Report <name> (model <model>, yours) or ..., standard: copy it into your model before changing it.
  • Designs: each design with its kind.
  • One Dataset line per dataset: data source type, query, fields with types.
  • Parameters: (the AX_ parameters are left out; hidden ones marked).
  • Page W x H mm, margins L R T B, body W x H mm, header H mm, footer H mm.
  • WARNING: lines.
  • Items: type, name, section/container, x, y, w, h, font and size, grow (CanGrow), hidden-if, value. Up to 400 items.
  • The RDL, truncated when very long.

docs.title: xpp_set_report_design
docs.text:
Saves the RDL of a precision design (AxReportPrecisionDesign.Text) of a report in your model through the metadata API, as Visual Studio's report designer does, and creates the design when it doesn't exist. Images embedded in the RDL become the report's embedded images. Positions and sizes take units (mm, cm, in, pt). Returns layout warnings.

Parameter Type Meaning reportName (required) string The report in your model (or the name of the copy, with duplicateOf) designName string The precision design to save or create rdl string The complete RDL document (<Report xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/reporting/2016/01/reportdefinition">...). Keep the namespace of the design you read duplicateOf string Copy this report (for example SalesInvoice or Cheque_US) into your model as reportName first; its datasets keep using the standard data provider modelName string Your model for the copy; required with duplicateOf fromAutoDesign string Instead of rdl: create designName as a precision design from this auto design, with Microsoft's report generator (Visual Studio's Create Precision Design). The auto design stays

Three ways to call it:

{ "reportName": "ContosoSalesInvoice", "duplicateOf": "SalesInvoice", "modelName": "ContosoExtensions" }

{ "reportName": "ContosoOrderStatusReport", "fromAutoDesign": "AutoDesign1", "designName": "Report" }

{ "reportName": "ContosoSalesInvoice", "designName": "Report", "rdl": "<Report xmlns=\"http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/reporting/2016/01/reportdefinition\">...</Report>" }

What it tells the agent next:

  • After a copy: add it to the project with xpp_add_to_project, and route printing to it through print management (PrintMgmtDocType.getDefaultReportFormatDelegate, PrintMgmtReportFormatPopulator.addDocuments) or the controller (parmReportName).
  • After generating from an auto design: read the generated layout with xpp_get_report_design, adjust it, check it with xpp_render_report.
  • After saving RDL: check the layout with xpp_render_report; xpp_build compiles the report (reportsc) into the package for deployment.

When the report is standard, the save is refused with the ownership message plus: "Reports have no extensions: copy it into your model with duplicateOf (the standard report), reportName (the copy) and modelName, then change the copy." Without rdl, fromAutoDesign or duplicateOf, it answers Pass designName and rdl (or fromAutoDesign to generate it from an auto design, or duplicateOf to copy a report).

docs.title: xpp_render_report
docs.text:
Renders a precision design with Microsoft's SSRS report engine (the engine behind the Report Viewer, with the same hard page layout as PDF and print), using sample or given data. Returns the pages as images, the item positions in mm and warnings. Labels resolve in the chosen language; D365FO report functions that need the environment are shown empty and named. Optionally writes a PDF.

Parameter Type Meaning reportName (required) string The report designName string The precision design. Default: the first design rdl string Render this RDL instead of the saved design (to try a change before saving) data object Rows per dataset: {"DatasetName": [{"Field": value, ...}, ...]}. Datasets left out get generated rows sampleRows number Generated rows for datasets without data (field names as text, 12345.67 for amounts). Default 1 parameters object Report parameter values by name language string Label and format language. Default en-US company string AX_CompanyName for the preview. Default USMF firstPage number First page to return. Default 1 maxPages number Pages to return as images, 1 to 4. Default 1 dpi number Image resolution, 48 to 300. Default 96 pdfPath string Also write the whole report as PDF to this path (.pdf, in an existing folder) overwrite boolean Replace pdfPath when the file exists. Default false includeItems boolean List the items with their positions. Default true 
{
  "reportName": "ContosoSalesInvoice",
  "designName": "Report",
  "data": { "<dataset name>": [ { "<field>": "CIV-000123" } ] },
  "maxPages": 2,
  "pdfPath": "C:\\Temp\\ContosoSalesInvoice.pdf"
}

Output: <report>.<design>: pages a-b of N at D dpi, rendered by Microsoft's report engine as PDF and print render (hard page breaks)., one Data line per dataset with its row count, the PDF path, the layout (as in xpp_get_report_design), and the pages as PNG images.

docs.title: xpp_measure_image
docs.text:
Measures a scanned or photographed form for a precision design. All positions are in mm from the sheet's top-left corner.

What it does:

  1. Calibrates the scale: whole sheet of a paper size, the scan's dpi, or two reference points.
  2. Straightens a skewed scan (up to 3 degrees).
  3. Finds ruled lines and boxes.
  4. Reads the text with Windows' built-in OCR, with each line's position and height and an estimated font size in points.
  5. Returns a picture of the image, or of a cropped area, with rulers and a millimetre grid (red lines every 10 or 50 mm, blue every grid step).
Parameter Type Meaning imagePath (required) string Full path of the image paper string The scan shows the whole sheet of this size: Letter, Legal, A4, A5, Executive, or WIDTHxHEIGHT with mm, cm or in (for example 8.5x3.5in for a cheque). Default: from the image's dpi, else the paper size closest to the image's proportions dpi number The scan's resolution, when the image is not the whole sheet and has no dpi of its own referencePoints object { x1, y1, x2, y2, distanceMm }: two points on the image (pixels) and their real distance. Most precise for partial scans deskew boolean Straighten a skewed scan. Default true language string OCR language, for example en-US. Default: the user's languages crop object { x, y, width, height } in mm: only this area; the picture zooms in with a finer grid gridMm number Grid step in mm. Default by zoom (1, 2 or 5) imageWidth number Picture width in pixels, 600 to 2000. Default 1400 minLineMm number Shortest ruled line to report, in mm. Default 10 ocr boolean Read the text. Default true 
{ "imagePath": "C:\\Scans\\cheque-sample.png", "paper": "8.5x3.5in" }

{ "imagePath": "C:\\Scans\\cheque-sample.png", "paper": "8.5x3.5in", "crop": { "x": 150, "y": 10, "width": 60, "height": 20 } }

docs.title: xpp_compare_layout
docs.text:
Compares a rendered report page with a scanned sample: places the calibrated scan on the report's page, renders the design with Microsoft's report engine, and returns an overlay (scan ink red, report ink blue, both black). For the words that read the same on both, it reports the overall shift and each report text box's offset in mm, marked within or outside the tolerance.

Parameter Type Meaning imagePath (required) string Full path of the scanned sample (whole sheet) reportName (required) string The report designName string The precision design. Default: the first design rdl string Render this RDL instead of the saved design data, sampleRows, parameters, company As in xpp_render_report language string Label language of the render and OCR language of both images page number Report page to compare. Default 1 dpi number Comparison resolution, 72 to 200. Default 120 paper string Sheet size of the scan, as in xpp_measure_image scanDpi number The scan's own resolution, when the image doesn't record it. Not needed with paper or referencePoints referencePoints object { x1, y1, x2, y2, distanceMm } deskew boolean Straighten a skewed scan. Default true toleranceMm number Offsets up to this are reported as ok. Default 0.5 scanOffsetMm object { x, y }: where the scan's top-left corner sits on the page, when the scan doesn't start at the sheet's corner 
{
  "imagePath": "C:\\Scans\\cheque-sample.png",
  "paper": "8.5x3.5in",
  "reportName": "ContosoCheque",
  "data": { "<dataset name>": [ { "<field>": "000123" } ] },
  "toleranceMm": 0.5
}

When OCR is not available, the overlay is still returned and the text says why positions were not compared.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The handlers are in ReportTools (server/Ported/Tools/ReportTools.cs). They call the bridge actions report_info, get_report_design, set_report_design, create_precision_design, duplicate_object and render_report.
  • set_report_design and create_precision_design are registered as Edit actions with object type AxReport, so the write policy checks that the report belongs to your model, and the Copilot scope and checkpoint apply. duplicate_object is a Copy action: the target model must be yours.
  • Rendering uses Microsoft's report engine from the report preview runtime; the PNG pages travel back to the agent as MCP image content.
  • Measuring and the overlay use ImageMeasure (calibration, deskew, line and box detection, grid picture) and Windows' OCR. Everything runs on your machine.
  • xpp_get_report_design, xpp_render_report, xpp_measure_image and xpp_compare_layout are registered as ParallelRead.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Reports have no extensions. To change a standard report's layout, copy it into your model and route printing to the copy.
  • The preview shows D365FO report functions that need the environment as empty, named placeholders; real values come only from a deployed report.
  • Fonts the cloud doesn't have are flagged as warnings by xpp_get_report_design; check them before you deploy.
  • xpp_render_report returns at most 4 pages as images per call.
  • OCR needs the language installed in Windows.

docs.title: Agents for Developers
docs.text:
F&O Studio's developer agents are Copilot personas for X++ work: building features, reviewing changes, tracking down errors, tuning performance, preparing upgrades, writing tests and reports, and releasing. Each one follows its own working method, uses the F&O Studio agent tools on the real metadata, and hands off to the next agent when its step is done. Four more agents (Solution Designer, Architect, Security & License, Integration) serve developers and functional consultants alike and are described here too.

For how agents are picked, routed and kept under control, see Copilot Agents.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• GitHub Copilot chat in agent mode, and F&O Studio connected to an environment so the xpp_* tools are available (Connect to Environment).
  • A D365FO project for agents that create elements: new elements are added to the active project (D365FO Projects).
  • For xppRunTests: a unified developer environment with your code deployed (Run Tests, Deploy to Environment).
  • For xppQueryData: database access (Database Access).
  • Recommended before an agent changes code: start a Copilot checkpoint and, for a narrow task, set a Copilot scope.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Agent Changes things? Use it to Hands off to F&O Developer Yes, with permission Build or change a feature Code Reviewer, Test Engineer F&O Code Reviewer No Review a branch, change or element Developer, Release Manager F&O Support No Find the cause of an error, stack, batch failure or trace Developer F&O Performance No Find why something is slow and how to fix it Developer F&O Upgrade Reviewer No Check models before a version update Developer F&O Test Engineer Yes, with permission Write and run SysTest unit tests Code Reviewer F&O Report Developer Yes, with permission Build or change SSRS reports, ER, print management Code Reviewer, Report Builder F&O Report Builder Yes, with permission Build a report from a scanned or sample document Code Reviewer, Release Manager F&O Workflow & Events Yes, with permission Build approval workflows and business events Code Reviewer F&O Release Manager Yes, with permission Checks, package, deploy and release summary Release Notes F&O Code Archaeologist No Explain unfamiliar custom code Developer F&O Solution Designer No Turn one requirement into a design Developer, Test Scenarios F&O Architect No Decisions across models, integrations, ALM Solution Designer F&O Security & License No Access, roles, license cost, SoD, gaps Developer F&O Integration Yes, with permission Entities, services, business events, integration errors Data Migration

"Yes, with permission" means the agent changes things only after you explicitly allow it, and only in a development, sandbox or build environment, never in production. If it doesn't know the environment type, it asks and treats it as production until you answer. "No" agents are read-only: they recommend changes and offer the next agent.

docs.title: F&O Developer
docs.text:
Builds and changes X++ features in your own models, the way an experienced D365FO developer would.

How it works:

  1. Understands before writing. Reads the standard elements involved (xpp_find_object, xpp_read_object, xpp_get_form_layout) and finds a standard precedent with xpp_find_examples. Reads the xpp_get_guide topic for any kind of code it hasn't written in the session.
  2. Extends, doesn't copy. Prefers metadata extensions, Chain of Command, event handlers and extension methods. It copies standard code only when nothing is extensible, and says why.
  3. Plans first for anything beyond a small change: elements to create or extend, names with the model's prefix, labels, security. It confirms the plan with you when it creates several elements.
  4. Creates through the tools (xpp_create_object, xpp_update_object, xpp_create_label) and adds elements to the project. It never writes AOT XML by hand.
  5. Proves it works: xpp_build until there are no errors or warnings in its elements, xpp_check_best_practice, and xppRunTests when tests exist. It opens what it changed with xppOpenElement.

Output: what it changed (element, member, why), the build and best-practice result, and what is left for you (deploy, database sync, security assignment).

Example prompts:

Add a field CreditHoldReason (string, 60) to CustGroup through a table extension in model ContosoExtensions,
and show it on the CustGroup form after the Description field.

Wrap SalesFormLetter.run with Chain of Command: after next, write an info message with the number of
journals posted. This is a development environment; you may create the class.

Create a SysOperation batch job ContosoPurgeOldLogs that deletes ContosoLog records older than 90 days.
Plan it first and wait for my OK.

docs.title: F&O Code Reviewer
docs.text:
Read-only reviewer for X++ changes before a pull request is merged.

How it works:

  1. Lists the changes with xpp_diff_changes (base branch main unless you name another) and reads each changed element.
  2. Runs xpp_check_best_practice and xpp_analyze_performance on the changed elements, xpp_find_deprecations when the model calls obsolete APIs, and xpp_analyze_security (op=gaps) for new menu items, forms and services.
  3. Checks by hand what the tools miss: CoC wrappers that don't call next, logic in the wrong layer, set-based operations that fall back to row by row, missing ttsbegin/ttscommit, hard-coded text instead of labels, missing find/exist, and your Team Rules in .xpp/agent-rules.md.

Output: findings ordered by severity (Blocker, Major, Minor) with element and method, problem, impact and fix; then what is good and what it couldn't verify. No style nitpicks.

Example prompts:

Review this branch against main.

Review the class SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension only.

Review my changes against the develop branch and focus on performance and security.

docs.title: F&O Support
docs.text:
Read-only troubleshooter for errors, call stacks, batch failures and traces.

How it works:

  1. For a message, runs xpp_find_message_source with the text exactly as shown. For "Field '...' must be filled in." it lists the mandatory fields first: the platform raises that message, so it looks at the field and its data, not only code.
  2. Reads the raising method (xpp_read_object with methodNames) and its callers (xpp_find_references) to state the exact condition.
  3. For a trace, uses xpp_analyze_trace (errors with call stacks, slow requests). For a batch job, reads its history and the job's class.
  4. Checks the data or setup behind the condition: in the live environment through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, or with xppQueryData on a development environment.

Output: the cause (condition and where it is), evidence, the fix (setup, data or code) and how to verify it. If the cause is setup or data, it says so plainly.

Example prompts:

Users get "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." when they create a customer from the sales order.
Where does it come from?

Here is the call stack of a batch job that fails in SalesFormLetter: <paste the stack>. Why does it fail?

Analyze C:\Traces\posting.etl and tell me which errors occur and where.

See also Scenario: From Error Message to Fix.

docs.title: F&O Performance
docs.text:
Read-only analyst that finds why something is slow and how to make it fast.

How it works:

  1. For a trace (.etl), runs xpp_analyze_trace: slowest requests, hot methods, repeated queries, call tree.
  2. Runs xpp_analyze_performance on the classes, tables and forms involved and reads the flagged methods.
  3. Looks at the queries: indexes on the tables (xpp_read_object), row counts and plans (xppQueryData on a development environment).
  4. Proposes typical fixes: set-based operations, joins instead of nested loops, firstOnly, field lists, caching, OnlyFetchActive, batch parallelism, indexes.

Output: findings ranked by expected gain: where, why it's slow (evidence), the fix, and how to measure it.

Example prompts:

Posting customer collection letters is slow. Analyze CustCollectionLetterCreate and the tables it reads.

Here is a trace of the slow form opening: C:\Traces\custtable-open.etl. What takes the time?

See also Analyze Performance, Analyze Trace and Scenario: Performance Tuning a Slow Process.

docs.title: F&O Upgrade Reviewer
docs.text:
Read-only reviewer that checks whether custom models and ISV solutions survive a version update.

How it works:

  1. Runs xpp_find_deprecations on each custom model: obsolete APIs used, CoC wrappers of changed or removed methods, extension collisions.
  2. Reads the affected standard elements to see what changed and what replaces the obsolete API (the SysObsolete message).
  3. Checks the model's dependencies (xpp_get_model_info) and ISV models for the same issues.
  4. Searches the release notes and deprecated-features lists with xpp_search_docs for the target version.

Output: a readiness report per model: blockers, required changes, recommended changes, the replacement for each obsolete call, and the test focus for the update.

Example prompts:

We move to the next service update. Check model ContosoExtensions for deprecated APIs and broken wrappers.

Which of our Chain of Command wrappers wrap methods that changed in standard?

See also Upgrade Readiness and Scenario: Upgrade to a New Version.

docs.title: F&O Test Engineer
docs.text:
Writes automated tests for X++ code and makes them pass.

How it works:

  1. Reads the code under test and its dependencies, and the xpp_get_guide topic on the Acceptance Test Library (ATL).
  2. Creates test classes (SysTestCase, ATL entities and data) in a test model or the project's model, one test per behaviour, with clear arrange, act and assert.
  3. Builds (xpp_build) and runs them with xppRunTests; fixes failing tests or reports the bug they reveal.

xppRunTests runs the tests on the environment against the deployed code, so deploy first.

Output: the tests created, what each covers, the run result, and any bug found.

Example prompts:

Write SysTest tests for ContosoCreditHoldService.validate: a customer group with and without a hold reason.

Run the tests of the project and fix the failing ones.

See also Generate SysTest Class and Test Explorer.

docs.title: F&O Report Developer
docs.text:
Builds and changes reports: SSRS (data provider, contract, controller, temporary table, design), Electronic Reporting and print management.

How it works:

  1. Finds a similar standard report (xpp_find_examples) and reads its data provider, contract and controller (xpp_get_report_design for its datasets and layout). Reads the xpp_get_guide topic "ssrs".
  2. Decides between a new report and extending a standard one. Standard reports can't be changed in place: it duplicates the report, extends its temporary table and data provider, and routes through print management or the controller. It lists the elements it will create with why each is needed, and creates no extras (setup fields, label files, menu items, privileges) unless you ask or the report can't work without them.
  3. For SSRS, creates the temporary table, contract, data provider and controller when the report needs them (a Query dataset needs none), writes the precision design with xpp_set_report_design, checks it with xpp_render_report, adds the output menu item and privilege when users run it from a menu, and builds with xpp_build.
  4. For Electronic Reporting, explains the data model, model mapping and format to configure, and X++ only when ER can't reach the data.
  5. For print management, covers the document type, setup and code hooks when the report is a business document.

Output: elements created, remaining steps (deploy reports, security, menu, print management setup), and how to test.

Example prompts:

Create a report ContosoCustGroupList that lists customer groups with their payment terms, run from a menu item.

Add the customer's VAT number to the sales invoice without changing the standard report.

See also Report Designer, Report Preview and Wizard: Report.

docs.title: F&O Report Builder
docs.text:
Turns a scanned or sample document (cheque, purchase order, invoice, preprinted stationery) into a working SSRS report: the data chain and a precision design that matches the sample to the millimetre.

How it works:

  1. Asks first what it can't see: preprinted stock or plain paper, paper size, whether it replaces a standard business document or is a new report, which data each field shows, the target model, and one or two ruler measurements of the real form to verify the scan's scale.
  2. Lists only the elements the report needs, each with a one-line reason. For a standard document: the copy of the standard report and one hook that routes to it (for cheques, a copy of the matching Cheque_XX report and a Chain of Command of ChequeController.determineReportMenuOutput; for invoices, purchase orders and confirmations, the print management registration). Anything more it proposes instead of creating.
  3. Measures the sample with xpp_measure_image: boxes, rules and text lines in mm from the sheet's top-left corner, with estimated font sizes.
  4. Builds the data side: copies the standard report into your model (xpp_set_report_design with duplicateOf) and extends its temporary table and data provider, or creates a Query or data provider data source for a new report.
  5. Writes the precision design with xpp_set_report_design: fixed textboxes at the measured positions, a tablix for line items, fonts that D365FO renders with, labels for captions. On preprinted stock it leaves out everything already printed.
  6. Renders and compares with xpp_render_report and xpp_compare_layout, moving items until each is within 0.5 mm (or your tolerance), then builds with xpp_build.

Output: elements created or changed (and the ones it proposed but didn't create), the comparison result per field, and what you still do: deploy, print a test on plain paper held over the preprinted form, confirm on the real printer at actual size, print management setup, fonts this machine doesn't have.

Example prompts:

Build our cheque layout from C:\Scans\cheque.png. It is preprinted cheque stock, 8.5 x 11 in, cheque at the top.
Model ContosoReports. It replaces the standard cheque.

Here is a scan of our purchase order form (A4, plain paper): C:\Scans\po.png. Make PurchPurchaseOrder print like it.

See also Scan Overlay and Measure and Scenario: Report from a Scanned Document.

docs.title: F&O Workflow & Events
docs.text:
Builds approval workflows and business events.

How it works:

  • Workflow: finds a similar standard workflow (xpp_find_examples), then creates the status field, workflow category, type, approval, the submit and event handler classes, menu items and the form changes (WorkflowEnabled, data source, type). The Wizard: Approval Workflow in F&O Studio does most of this.
  • Business event: the event class, its contract, where to send it from, the category, and how consumers (Power Automate, Azure Service Bus, Event Grid) subscribe.

Output: elements created, the remaining setup in the client (workflow configuration, business event catalog and endpoints), and how to test.

Example prompts:

Add an approval workflow to ContosoPriceChangeRequest: submit, approve, reject, with a status field on the table.

Send a business event when a customer is put on credit hold, with the account number and the reason.

See also Wizard: Business Event.

docs.title: F&O Release Manager
docs.text:
Gets a change ready for deployment and deploys it where allowed.

How it works:

  1. Runs the checks: xpp_build of every model to release, xpp_check_best_practice, xppRunTests, xpp_analyze_security (op=gaps), labels.
  2. Summarizes the changes (xpp_diff_changes) with their risk: data model changes needing database sync, security changes, integrations, upgrade risks.
  3. Creates the deployable package with xpp_package (the tool asks you first).
  4. Deploys and syncs only to development, sandbox or build environments and only with your permission. Production goes through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center by your organization's process.

Output: a release summary: checks with results, changes and risk, package path, deployment steps and rollback notes.

Example prompts:

Prepare model ContosoExtensions for release: run all checks and create the deployable package.

What in this branch needs a database sync, and what is the risk of deploying it?

See also Pre-Deploy Checklist, Create Deployment Package and Scenario: Prepare and Ship a Release.

docs.title: F&O Code Archaeologist
docs.text:
Read-only agent that makes unfamiliar custom code understandable.

How it works:

  1. Maps the model (xpp_list_model_objects, xpp_get_model_info): what it adds and what it extends.
  2. Follows the entry points (menu items, CoC wrappers, event handlers, batch jobs), reads the code and traces callers with xpp_find_references.
  3. Finds dead code: elements and methods nothing references, obsolete calls (xpp_find_deprecations), copies of standard code that a newer extension point would replace.

Output: what it does in plain words, how it hooks into standard, a Mermaid diagram of the main flow, risks, and clean-up candidates with evidence.

Example prompts:

Explain what model ContosoLegacy does and how it hooks into sales order posting.

Which classes in ContosoExtensions are never referenced?

See also Scenario: Onboard to an Existing Codebase.

docs.title: F&O Solution Designer
docs.text:
Read-only agent that turns one requirement into a functional and technical design a developer can build and a consultant can test. It writes no code.

How it works:

  1. Restates the requirement and the open questions; asks only what blocks the design.
  2. Looks for standard functionality first (xpp_search_docs, xpp_find_examples, the live environment): configuration beats code.
  3. For the gap, finds the extension points: the standard elements and methods (xpp_read_object, xpp_find_references, xpp_get_form_layout) and how standard solves similar cases.

Output: a design document with Summary, Functional design, Technical design (elements with names, extension mechanism per change, data model, labels), Security (privileges, duties, license impact via xpp_analyze_security), Data migration and integrations, Test scenarios, Risks and open questions.

Example prompts:

Requirement: sales clerks must enter a reason when they change the customer group of a customer. Design it.

Design a credit hold flag on customer groups that blocks sales order confirmation.

See also Scenario: Build a Feature End to End.

docs.title: F&O Architect
docs.text:
Read-only agent for decisions that span many requirements.

It covers:

  • Models and packages: inspects the landscape (xpp_list_models, xpp_get_model_info) and recommends the split, dependencies and naming.
  • Build or buy: standard feature, configuration, ISV solution or custom extension, with the trade-offs.
  • Integrations: OData, data management, custom services, business events, dual-write; volumes, error handling and monitoring.
  • ALM and environments: branches, builds, deployable packages, environment types (UDE, sandbox, production) and how changes flow between them.
  • Quality attributes: performance at volume, security and licensing, upgradeability (xpp_find_deprecations).

Output: context, options with trade-offs, the recommendation and why, risks, and the decisions the customer must make, with a Mermaid diagram when it helps.

Example prompts:

We have three custom models with circular dependencies. Propose a new model split.

Should we integrate orders from our web shop through OData, data management or a custom service? About 20,000 orders a day.

docs.title: F&O Security & License
docs.text:
Read-only analyst for security and licensing, from the metadata and, when available, the live environment.

It uses xpp_analyze_security:

op Answers access Which privileges, duties and roles reach a menu item, form or table license The license a role or menu item requires and what drives it placement Which standard roles a new duty or privilege belongs in gaps Menu items, forms and services of a model that no privilege covers sod Segregation-of-duties conflicts

It reads users' actual role assignments in the live environment when needed.

Output: the answer with the chain (role, duty, privilege, entry point, access level) and license impact; the cheapest license that still works.

Example prompts:

Who can open the CustGroup menu item, and with which access level?

What license does TradeSalesClerk need, and what drives it?

Find menu items in ContosoExtensions that no privilege covers.

See also Security View, Analyze License and Find Security Gaps.

docs.title: F&O Integration
docs.text:
Designs, builds and troubleshoots integrations.

How it works:

  • Picks the entity: finds standard entities for the data (xpp_find_object, xpp_list_objects on AxDataEntityView), reads their fields, keys and whether they are public (OData) and enabled for data management. Prefers a standard entity, then an extension, then a new entity.
  • Builds: entity extensions or new entities with staging tables through the F&O Studio tools; custom services and business events when entities don't fit.
  • Troubleshoots: reads the import or OData error, finds its source (xpp_find_message_source), and checks the staging data and mappings in the live environment.

Output: for design, the entity or service per data flow, keys, direction, volume, error handling; for errors, cause and fix.

Example prompts:

Which standard entity exposes customer groups over OData, and is it enabled for data management?

Add our field CreditHoldReason to the customer group entity and its staging table.

See also Try Data Entity (OData) and Scenario: Expose Data to an Integration.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Name the environment type. "This is a development environment; you may create the elements." Without it, agents that change things ask, and treat the environment as production meanwhile.
  • Ask for the plan first on larger changes. The F&O Developer confirms its plan when it creates several elements.
  • Use the handoffs. Developer, then Code Reviewer, then Release Manager is the usual path.
  • Watch the work. Copilot Activity shows each tool call; a notification offers a diff after each element change.
  • Be able to undo. Start a checkpoint before the agent writes.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Read-only agents are read-only by instruction. To make the server refuse changes outside a set of elements, set a Copilot scope.
  • The F&O Studio tools write only to your own (custom) models; standard elements are changed through extensions.
  • xppRunTests tests the code deployed to the environment, not your local build.

docs.title: Agents for Functional Consultants
docs.text:
F&O Studio includes nine Copilot agents written for functional consultants and key users. They answer in business terms (menu paths, fields as labelled in the client, setup and data) and show X++ only when you ask. They read the application's metadata with the F&O Studio tools when a development environment is connected, and look at the running environment through Microsoft's Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server. Four shared agents (Solution Designer, Architect, Security & License, Integration) also serve consultants; they are described on Agents for Developers.

For how agents are picked and routed, see Copilot Agents.

docs.title: When to use them
docs.text:
• You need to know what a field, parameter or process does and which setup drives it.
  • A user reports an error or an unexpected result, and you want the setup or data cause and the fix.
  • You need to explain why a sales order, invoice, voucher or item looks the way it does.
  • You are designing roles, writing test scenarios, running a fit-gap, planning a data migration or writing release notes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Need Why VS Code with GitHub Copilot, chat in agent mode The agents are Copilot custom agents. F&O Studio installed It contributes the agents. Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server connected (recommended) Lets the agents read setup, open forms and read data in the running environment. Microsoft's setup page: Use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in VS Code. A development environment connected in F&O Studio (optional) Makes the F&O Studio tools (xpp_*) available: the agents can then read forms, tables, labels and the code behind a behaviour. See Connect to Environment. Database access (optional) On a development environment, xppQueryData reads the business database with one read-only SELECT. See Database Access.

docs.title: Working without a development environment
docs.text: You can use most functional agents without a development environment. Explainer, Setup Advisor, Data Investigator, Functional Triage, Test Scenarios, Fit-Gap Analyst and Data Migration then work from the live environment and documentation (xpp_search_docs when available, otherwise Microsoft Learn on the web), and say that metadata-based checks were skipped. Role Designer and Release Notes rely on the F&O Studio tools (xpp_analyze_security, xpp_diff_changes), so they need a development environment for a full answer.

docs.title: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server
docs.text:
The ERP MCP server is Microsoft's MCP server for Finance & Operations. F&O Studio does not install or configure it. When it is connected, the agents use its tools to see the environment as users see it:

Tools Used for data_* Find and read records through data entities (and, when allowed, create, update or delete them) form_* Open menu items and forms, read controls, filter grids, open lookups api_* Find and invoke actions

When it is not connected, the agent suggests connecting it, or opens the environment with the browser tools.

docs.title: The rule about changes
docs.text:
Only two functional agents may change anything: F&O Setup Advisor and F&O Data Migration. They follow this rule:

  • They create, change or delete data, setup, security or metadata only after you explicitly allow that change.
  • Only in a development, sandbox or build environment, never in production.
  • If they don't know which kind of environment it is, they ask, and treat it as production until you answer.
  • Where they may not change something, they describe the change: the menu path and the values to enter.

All other functional agents are read-only. They recommend changes and offer the next agent.

Always tell the agent which environment you are connected to, for example "This is the UAT sandbox" or "This is production; read only".

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Agent Changes things? Use it to Hands off to F&O Functional Explainer No Explain a form, field, parameter or process Setup Advisor F&O Setup Advisor Yes, with permission Check configuration and say what to fix Data Investigator F&O Data Investigator No Explain why a record looks the way it does Setup Advisor F&O Functional Triage No Turn a user's error into a cause and a fix F&O Support F&O Role Designer No Design roles for a job, with license and SoD Developer, Security & License F&O Test Scenarios No Write functional test cases (none) F&O Fit-Gap Analyst No Classify requirements against standard Solution Designer F&O Data Migration Yes, with permission Plan loads and fix import errors Integration F&O Release Notes No Write user-facing release notes (none)

docs.title: F&O Functional Explainer
docs.text:
Explains the system to a functional consultant or key user.

How it works:

  1. Finds the form, field or process (xpp_find_object, xpp_get_form_layout for what the form shows, xpp_read_label).
  2. Reads the logic behind it (xpp_read_object, xpp_find_references) to know which parameters and setup it uses and when, and translates that into business rules.
  3. Confirms with Microsoft Learn (xpp_search_docs) and, when connected, the actual setup in the live environment.

Output: a short explanation: what it does, the setup that drives it (menu path, field, values), examples and exceptions.

Example prompts:

What does the "Credit limit type" parameter in Accounts receivable parameters do?

On the customer group form, what is the "Terms of payment" field used for when a sales order is created?

When does a sales order line get its warehouse from the item and when from the customer?

docs.title: F&O Setup Advisor
docs.text:
Reviews configuration and says what to fix. It may change setup only with your permission and never in production.

How it works:

  1. Reads the setup in the live environment: parameters forms, number sequences, posting profiles, groups, defaults, per legal entity.
  2. Knows what each setting does (xpp_read_object on the parameters table and the code that reads it, xpp_search_docs) to judge its impact.
  3. Compares against what the process needs, or against another legal entity or environment when you ask.

Output: a checklist: setting (menu path), current value, expected value, impact, fix.

Example prompts:

Check the Accounts receivable setup in legal entity USMF for invoicing sales orders. This is a sandbox; read only.

Compare the number sequences of USMF and DEMF for sales orders and invoices.

docs.title: F&O Data Investigator
docs.text:
Investigates data, one record at a time.

How it works:

  1. Finds the record and its related records (lines, transactions, vouchers, inventory dimensions, settlements) in the live environment, or with xppQueryData on a development environment. It uses the table relations (xpp_read_object) to join correctly and filters by company (DataAreaId).
  2. Finds the setup and code that produced the values (defaults, posting, price and discount logic) with the F&O Studio tools.
  3. Keeps queries narrow: specific records, few columns, row limits.

Output: what happened to the record, step by step, with the evidence (records, fields, values) and the setup or action that caused it; how to correct it, if needed.

Example prompts:

Sales order SO-000123 in USMF has a line discount of 10% that nobody entered. Why?

Why did invoice CIV-000045 post to main account 130100 instead of 130200?

See also Scenario: Investigate Why a Record Looks Wrong.

docs.title: F&O Functional Triage
docs.text:
First line for a user's error or unexpected result.

How it works:

  1. Gets the exact message and context (form, action, company, record).
  2. Runs xpp_find_message_source. For "Field '...' must be filled in." the platform checks a mandatory field: the agent finds which field on the form or entity is empty. Otherwise it reads the condition in the raising code and translates it into setup and data.
  3. Checks that setup or data in the live environment.
  4. If the cause is a code defect, says so and hands off to F&O Support.

Output: the cause in one sentence, evidence, the fix (menu path and values), and how to avoid it next time.

Example prompts:

A user gets "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." when creating a customer in USMF. What's missing?

Posting a vendor invoice fails with "The posting profile is not set up". The vendor is in group 10.

See also Find Message Source and Scenario: From Error Message to Fix.

docs.title: F&O Role Designer
docs.text:
Designs security roles from job descriptions.

How it works:

  1. Lists the tasks the job needs (menu items, view or maintain) and the ones it must not have.
  2. Finds standard roles and duties that cover them (xpp_analyze_security with op=access and op=placement), preferring reuse over new privileges.
  3. Checks the license (op=license) and conflicts (op=sod), and proposes read-only access where it lowers the license.

Output: the role design: roles and duties to assign, duties or privileges to add or remove, license per role, conflicts and mitigations. Building new security elements goes to the F&O Developer.

Example prompts:

Design a role for a sales clerk who enters and confirms sales orders but must not post invoices or change prices.

Can a user with TradeSalesClerk get by with a cheaper license if we remove maintain access on customer groups?

See also Scenario: Design a Security Role and Reduce License Cost.

docs.title: F&O Test Scenarios
docs.text:
Writes test cases a key user can run.

How it works:

  1. Identifies the process and the changed behaviour (from the requirement, the design, or xpp_diff_changes).
  2. Finds the forms and fields involved (xpp_get_form_layout) so steps use the client's labels and menu paths.
  3. Covers the happy path, variations (setup, legal entity, dimensions), negative cases (validations) and regression of the standard process.

Output: a table per scenario with ID, title, preconditions and test data, steps (menu path, action, values) and expected result; optionally a Task Recorder outline.

Example prompts:

Write test scenarios for the new credit hold reason on customer groups, including negative cases.

Write regression scenarios for sales order confirmation after the changes in this branch.

docs.title: F&O Fit-Gap Analyst
docs.text:
Classifies requirements against standard D365FO.

How it works: for each requirement, it searches Microsoft Learn (xpp_search_docs) and the standard application (xpp_find_examples, xpp_find_object) for the feature, checks feature management and parameters, and estimates the gap.

Output: a table with ID, requirement, fit (Standard, Configuration, Extension, ISV, Process change), how it's met (feature, menu path, or the gap), evidence (doc link or element), complexity (Low, Medium, High) and notes; then a summary and the gaps to design next.

Example prompts:

Fit-gap these requirements:
1. Block sales orders for customers over their credit limit.
2. Print the customer's VAT number on the invoice.
3. Approve purchase requisitions above 10,000 by two managers.

docs.title: F&O Data Migration
docs.text:
Plans and troubleshoots data migration with data management. It may change data only with your permission and never in production.

How it works:

  1. Finds the entities per data area (xpp_list_objects on AxDataEntityView, or the entity list in the environment) and reads their fields, mandatory fields, natural keys and staging (xpp_read_object).
  2. Orders the loads by dependency (setup before masters before open transactions), per legal entity.
  3. For import errors, reads the error, finds its source (xpp_find_message_source; for "must be filled in" it lists the mandatory fields) and the staging record.

Output: a migration plan (entity per data area, keys, required fields, sequence, templates and validation steps), or for errors, the cause and the corrected data.

Example prompts:

Plan the migration of customers: groups, customers, addresses, contacts and open balances for USMF.

The customer import fails with "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." for 30 rows. What's wrong with the file?

See also Scenario: Expose Data to an Integration.

docs.title: F&O Release Notes
docs.text:
Explains a release to the people who use the system.

How it works:

  1. Lists the changes (xpp_diff_changes, commit messages and linked work items) and reads enough of each to know the user-visible effect (forms, fields, validations, reports, security).
  2. Groups them by business process and audience.

Output: release notes per process: what changed and why, who is affected, new or changed setup (menu path), and training or communication notes. No technical jargon.

Example prompts:

Write release notes for this branch for the accounts receivable team.

docs.title: A typical consultant flow
docs.text:
F&O Functional Triage    "Users in USMF get 'Field 'Customer group' must be filled in.' when they create customers."
   -> (setup cause found)
F&O Setup Advisor        "Check the setup described above in the environment."
   -> Explain a record
F&O Data Investigator    "Investigate a record affected by the setup above."

If Triage finds a code defect, it hands off to F&O Support (a developer agent) with Investigate in code.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Live checks need the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, which you set up separately. Without it, the agents fall back to the browser tools or describe what to check.
  • Without a development environment, metadata-based checks (forms, fields, code behind a behaviour) are skipped; the agent says so.
  • Read-only agents are read-only by instruction. Tell agents the environment type, and never give production write permission you don't intend.

docs.title: Analyze License
docs.text: Analyze License tells you which user license a security role, duty or privilege needs, which menu items and grants drive that license, and where granting Read only would lower it. It works on the metadata of all packages, with no environment, so you see the license effect of a security change before you deploy it. Visual Studio has no equivalent: there you read the ViewUserLicense and MaintainUserLicense properties of each menu item by hand.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you add a duty or privilege to a role: check that the role's license does not go up.
  • When a role needs a higher license than expected and you want to know exactly which menu item and grant cause it.
  • When you design a role for a Team Members or Activity user and look for grants you can reduce to Read.
  • To compare standard roles before you extend one (see Scenario: Design a security role and reduce license cost).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). No sign-in or database.
  • The role, duty or privilege can be in any model, standard or yours.

docs.title: The license model, as F&O Studio applies it
docs.text:
In D365FO the license a user needs is decided by the entry points (menu items) their roles reach and by the access they get on them. Every menu item has two properties:

Property Used when the grant is ViewUserLicense Read only MaintainUserLicense anything more than Read: Update, Create, Correct, Delete or Invoke

F&O Studio applies these rules:

  1. It expands the object: a role into its sub-roles (recursively), duties and privileges, including everything that role extensions and duty extensions add; a duty into its privileges; a privilege into its entry points.
  2. For every menu item entry point it merges the grants of all paths that reach it, and takes the license of each grant: Read only uses ViewUserLicense, any other grant uses MaintainUserLicense. A missing property counts as None.
  3. The highest license wins. The object's license is the highest license of all its entry points.

Licenses are ranked from lowest to highest, and shown with these names:

Metadata value Shown as Rank None (or not set) None 1 (lowest) Server None (server) 2 SelfServe Self-serve 3 Universal Team Members 4 Activity Activity 5 Enterprise Operations 6 (highest)

Only menu item entry points (display, output and action) count. Data entity permissions and table permissions of a privilege are part of its access but do not change the license in this analysis.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A privilege ContosoCustGroupMaintain grants the display menu item CustGroup with Read, Update, Create and Delete. Because the grant is more than Read, the privilege needs the menu item's MaintainUserLicense. A privilege ContosoCustGroupView that grants Read only on the same menu item needs its ViewUserLicense instead. A role with both privileges gets the merged grant (Read, Update, Create, Delete), so the maintain license applies.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
From How Security View Right-click a role, duty or privilege > Analyze License, or the inline credit card button on the node. Application Explorer or the D365FO project view Right-click a role, duty or privilege (or an extension of one) > Analyze License. Element Designer Title bar menu of a role, duty or privilege > Analyze License. Dynamics 365 view Security > Analyze License… Command Palette F&O Studio: Analyze License

Run on an extension (for example a role extension), it analyzes the base element, which includes every extension.

Run without an element (Dynamics 365 view or Command Palette):

  1. Pick Role, Duty or Privilege.
  2. For a role, type part of a role name or label (leave it empty for the roles of your models), then pick the role. For a duty or privilege, pick it from the element picker.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
The result opens in the security panel (one panel for all security results; a new result replaces the previous one).

  • Title: <Role|Duty|Privilege> <name>: <license>.
  • Summary: the number of entry points, duties and privileges reached.
  • Roles: the roles included (the role itself and its sub-roles). Click one to analyze it.
  • Entry points by license: how many entry points need each license, highest first.
  • What drives the license: listed only when the license is Activity or Operations. One row per entry point that needs the top license (up to 60, the heading says "first 60 of N" when there are more):
Column Meaning Menu item The menu item; click it to open it. Type MenuItemDisplay, MenuItemOutput or MenuItemAction. Grant The merged grant, for example Read,Update,Create,Delete. License The license this grant needs. View license / Maintain license The menu item's two properties. Via Up to three paths that grant it, for example Role X > Duty Y > Privilege Z [Read,Update].
  • Read-only alternatives: drivers granted more than Read whose view license is lower than the top license. Each line reads <menu item>: <grant> needs Operations; Read only would need Team Members. Up to 25 lines. Changing those grants to Read (in a separate View privilege, for example) lowers the license, provided no other driver remains.
  • Missing objects: privileges, duties or sub-roles that are referenced but not in the metadata, with the path that references them (up to 20).

In the panel header, Copy as Markdown copies the result and Export… saves it as a .md file (default name license-<name>.md in the first workspace folder).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: None. The analysis always uses the metadata of every package of the active configuration.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Command: xpp.security.analyzeLicense in src/security/index.ts (analyzeLicense, showLicense); the panel is src/security/securityPanel.ts.
  • The extension calls the server's security language action with op: 'license'.
  • server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs: Expand walks the role, duty or privilege over the cached security index; LicenseOf picks the view or maintain license per entry point; License ranks them, lists the drivers and computes the read-only alternatives.
  • The same analysis is available to Copilot as the agent tool xpp_analyze_security with op=license (see Agent Tools: Analysis). The F&O Security & License and F&O Role Designer agents use it.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The result comes from metadata. It does not read user role assignments or license usage in an environment, and it is not a licensing statement: check Microsoft's licensing guide for contract decisions.
  • Only menu item entry points decide the license. Data entity and table permissions, and entry points of other types, are not counted.
  • The drivers list and read-only alternatives are shown only for Activity and Operations licenses.
  • Changes to security files may need Refresh Security in the Security View before the analysis sees them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "... have no license of their own. Analyze a role, duty or privilege." The command was run on another element type. Run it on a role, duty or privilege, or use Who Can Access for menu items, forms and tables. "Role '' not found." (or Duty, Privilege) The name is not in the metadata, or the index is stale. Check the name; click Refresh Security. License shows None for a role with access Its entry points are not menu items, or the menu items have no license properties. Check Entry points by license and the menu items' properties. Missing objects lists entries A role or duty refers to a privilege, duty or sub-role that is not installed. Fix the reference; Find Security Gaps reports missing duties and privileges in your models. The license did not change after you edited a privilege Cached index. Click Refresh Security in the Security view and run the analysis again.

docs.title: Analyze Performance
docs.text: Analyze Performance is a static performance review of the X++ code and metadata of a class, table, form or data entity. It reads the element from your local metadata, runs a set of rules over every method and over the element's properties, and puts each finding in the Problems view on the element's code, with the reason and the fix. No environment, database or trace is needed. Visual Studio has no equivalent command.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you commit or open a pull request, to catch queries in loops and row-by-row writes in your own code.
  • When a process is slow and you want a quick list of suspects in the classes, tables and forms it runs, before or after you take a trace (see Analyze Trace).
  • When you review a standard or ISV element you are about to extend, to know which of its methods are expensive.
  • On a form that opens slowly: display methods in grids, data sources that fetch every field, and joined data sources that query again for every record.
  • On a data entity before you expose it to OData or data management: public names, keys, staging fields, mandatory fields and set-based processing.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration (any environment type: unified developer environment, cloud-hosted or VHD). The analysis reads metadata from the local PackagesLocalDirectory and your custom metadata folder, so standard, ISV and custom elements can all be analyzed.
  • The element must be a class (AxClass), table (AxTable), form (AxForm) or data entity (AxDataEntityView). Other element types have no code to analyze; the server answers "Performance analysis covers classes, tables, forms and data entities".
  • No build, no database access and no sign-in are needed.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
You can start the command, F&O Studio: Analyze Performance, from five places:

Where How Application Explorer or the project view Right-click a class, table, form or data entity > Analyze Performance. X++ code view Right-click in the code of an element > Analyze Performance. Dynamics 365 view Analyze > Analyze Performance… Command Palette F&O Studio: Analyze Performance, then pick the element (classes, tables, forms and data entities are offered). Hover Hover the name of a class, table or form in X++ code and click the Analyze performance link.

Then:

  1. F&O Studio shows "Analyzing ElementName" in the status bar while the server reads the element.
  2. When it finishes, a notification reports the totals, for example CustCollectionLetterCreate: 18 performance finding(s), 5 warning(s), in 42 method(s).
  3. If there are findings, click Show Problems in the notification (or open the Problems view yourself).
  4. The findings are listed under the element's code view document (for example CustGroup.xpp). Each one shows:
  5. the message and the fix in one line, for example select inside a loop: one query per row of the loop. Move the query out of the loop, or join it into the outer while select.
  6. the source X++ performance and the rule id in parentheses, for example X++ performance(QueryInLoop);
  7. the severity: Warning for problems that are slow in most cases, Information for problems that depend on data volume or context.
  8. Click a finding to open the code view at the method and line. Findings about the element as a whole (table cache, form data sources and display methods, data entity readiness) have no method and point to the first line of the code view.
  9. Fix the code, save, and run Analyze Performance again. A new run replaces the findings of that element; the findings are not refreshed while you type.

The full list of rules, with examples of slow code and the fix, is in the Performance Rules Reference.

docs.title: What it checks, by element type
docs.text: Element Checks Class Every method (and member variables from the class declaration): queries and set-based statements in loops, row operations in loops, crossCompany, while select of every field, forupdate without a write, unbalanced transactions, set-based statements that fall back to row by row, == filters that no index starts with. Table The table's methods (same rules as a class) plus the table's CacheLookup against its TableGroup. Form The form's methods (same rules) plus display methods shown in grids without cacheAddMethod, data sources that should use OnlyFetchActive, and joined data sources with LinkType Delayed or Active shown in the parent's grid. Data entity The entity's methods (same rules) plus readiness for OData and data management: public names, entity key, staging table and staging fields, unmapped mandatory fields, set-based processing.

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
The findings are heuristics. They read the source text and the metadata; they do not run the code and do not know how many rows a table has. Treat each finding as a question:

  • A select firstOnly inside a while select over 10 setup rows is fine. The same lookup inside a loop over 100,000 sales lines is the reason the job runs for an hour.
  • An Information finding such as NoMatchingIndex matters on a large transaction table and not on a small parameter table.
  • A RowByRowFallback warning tells you a set-based statement will not be set-based. Whether you can skip the table's insert() or delete actions is a functional decision.

When you want evidence, take a trace of the slow scenario and open it in Analyze Trace: the hot methods and SQL tabs show which of the findings cost time.

docs.title: Where else the analysis runs
docs.text:
The same server analysis (bridge action analyze_performance) is used by:

  • Review My Changes: for every changed class, table, form or data entity, the Warning findings are listed with the element, method and line, and added to the pull request summary.
  • Pre-Deploy Checklist: the Performance step counts the warnings in the project's elements. It reports them but does not fail the checklist.
  • Copilot agents, through the MCP tool xpp_analyze_performance (see Agent Tools: Analysis). The F&O Performance agent runs it on the classes, tables and forms involved in a slow process, and the review steps of the developer agents run it on changed elements. The default team rules file asks agents to run it on changed classes and fix every Warning.

docs.title: The agent tool
docs.text:
xpp_analyze_performance takes objectType (AxClass, AxTable, AxForm or AxDataEntityView) and objectName. It returns text, at most 100 findings:

ContosoOrderGroup: 2 performance finding(s) in 6 method(s).
- [Warning] QueryInLoop in recalculate line 9: select inside a loop: one query per row of the loop. Fix: Move the query out of the loop, or join it into the outer while select.
- [Info] TableCache in (table) line 0: ContosoOrderGroup (TableGroup Group) has CacheLookup None: setup data is read far more than written. Fix: Use Found, or EntireTable when the table is small.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Analyze Performance has no settings. The rules and their thresholds are fixed in the server.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The command (src/performance.ts) resolves the element from the tree item, the code view URI or a picker, and calls the bridge action analyze_performance on the F&O Studio server.
  2. The server's PerformanceAnalysisService (server/Ported/MetaModel/PerformanceAnalysisService.cs) reads the element through Microsoft's metadata API (GetClass, GetTable, GetForm, GetDataEntityView) and passes each method's source, with the class declaration, to PerformanceRules.Analyze.
  3. PerformanceRules (server/Analysis/PerformanceRules.cs) first blanks comments, strings and labels (keeping line breaks), so text inside them never matches. It then scans the method token by token:
  4. while, for, do and while select open a loop when they are followed by a { block;
  5. select, while select, insert_recordset, update_recordset, delete_from and calls such as buffer.insert() are checked against the loop depth;
  6. variable types come from declarations in the method and the class declaration, so the rules know which variables are table buffers.
  7. Table facts come from the metadata and are cached for the run: whether the table overrides insert, update or delete, has delete actions, is date-effective (ValidTimeStateFieldType), and the fields of every index, including indexes added by table extensions.
  8. For tables, forms and data entities the service adds element-level checks (cache lookup, form display methods and data sources, entity readiness).
  9. The result is JSON: rule, severity, method, line within the method, message and fix. The extension maps the method line to the code view line (methodSpans in src/xppSource.ts) and sets the diagnostics in its own collection, xpp-performance.

Nothing is written. The analysis reads metadata only and runs under the server's metadata lock like other read actions.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Static and text-based. It does not follow calls: a CustTable::find() call inside a loop is not reported, because the query is in another method. Only select statements written in the analyzed method count.
  • A loop is only recognized when its body is a { } block. A single-statement loop without braces is not tracked.
  • Table buffers are recognized from declarations such as CustTable custTable;. Buffers declared with var, or reached through a method call, are not recognized as tables, so row-operation and index rules skip them.
  • NoMatchingIndex only looks at == comparisons on fields of a declared buffer; it does not consider ranges, joins, the clustered index choice or the data. Tables without any index are not reported.
  • Database log and alerts also force set-based statements to run row by row. They are environment setup, so they are not checked; the fix text reminds you of skipDatabaseLog and skipEvents.
  • Data entity readiness checks the root data source for mandatory fields and the mapped fields for staging; computed and unmapped fields are not staged and are not reported.
  • For live data (missing indexes reported by SQL Server, expensive queries, batch history), use Database Performance Insights. For runtime evidence, use Analyze Trace.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Nothing happens after you pick the command on an element. The element is not a class, table, form or data entity. Run it on one of those types. For a form extension or class extension, run it on the extension class or the base element. Error "Performance analysis covers classes, tables, forms and data entities; ... has no code to analyze." The agent tool or bridge was called with another element type. Use AxClass, AxTable, AxForm or AxDataEntityView. Error "Type Name not found." The element does not exist in the active configuration's metadata. Check the name and the selected environment (Select Environment). Old findings still show after you fixed the code. Findings are refreshed only when the command runs. Run Analyze Performance again on the element. A finding points to the first line of the code view. It is an element-level finding (table cache, form data source, display method, entity). Read the message: it names the property, data source or control to change in the designer. A query in a loop is not reported. The query is in a called method, or the loop has no braces, or the buffer is declared with var. See Limitations. Use Analyze Trace to find repeated queries at run time.
