docs.title: Analyze Trace
docs.text: Analyze Trace opens a Dynamics 365 performance trace (.etl) in a panel inside VS Code and shows where the time went: requests on a timeline, call trees, hot spots, hot methods, SQL statements, pauses, errors and exceptions with their X++ call stacks, and every AOS, session and user in the trace. It reads the file with F&O Studio's own parser, so you need neither Trace Parser nor an import database. Every method links to its code. The Visual Studio side equivalent is Microsoft's Trace Parser desktop tool.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• A user reports that a form, a button or a posting is slow, and you want the method and the SQL that cost the time.
  • A batch job or a dual-write/OData integration fails or is slow on an environment you can trace, and you need the X++ call stack of the error.
  • You fixed a performance problem and want to compare the new trace with the old one.
  • You want Copilot to read the trace for you (xpp_analyze_trace) and point to the methods to look at.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A trace file (.etl) taken in the web client (see below) or with the Dynamics 365 trace tools.
  • The trace event manifests of the platform (DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man and the other *.man files). F&O Studio finds them in your installation:
  • unified developer environment: PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring;
  • cloud-hosted or VHD: AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring, or the folder of the registered Dynamics 365 trace providers;
  • anywhere else: set xpp.trace.manifestFolder to a folder that contains them.
  • An active D365FO configuration (the manifests are found from it). No database access, sign-in or build is needed.
  • Windows (the parser uses the Windows event tracing API) and the 64-bit server that F&O Studio ships.

docs.title: Capture a trace in the web client
docs.text:
Tracing is a feature of Finance and Operations, not of F&O Studio. The steps below follow Microsoft's documentation (Capture a trace).

  1. Make sure your user has the System tracing user role (System administration > Users > Users), or is an administrator.
  2. In the web client, open Help (the ? icon on the navigation bar) and select Trace.
  3. Enter a Trace name that describes the scenario, for example Confirm sales order 000123.
  4. Set Include SQL parameter value to Yes only when you need the values; they can contain business data.
  5. Select Start trace.
  6. Reproduce the scenario. Keep it short: Microsoft recommends traces of 30 seconds to a couple of minutes. Client traces are capped at 1 GB.
  7. Select Stop trace, then Download trace. The browser saves an .etl file.
  8. Copy the file to the machine where VS Code runs.

A trace records every session that runs on the AOS while it is on: other users, batch tasks, dual-write and OData calls. The Sessions tab and the agent filters let you narrow it to your scenario.

docs.title: Open a trace
docs.text:
Use one of these:

Where How Explorer Right-click an .etl file > Analyze Trace… Dynamics 365 view Analyze > Analyze Trace… Command Palette F&O Studio: Analyze Trace…, then choose the file (the dialog filters on Event traces .etl).

A notification shows "Reading file.etl…" while the server reads the trace. Large traces take a while (the request times out after 10 minutes). The panel opens with the title <file>.etl [Trace]. You can open several traces, one panel each. Panels come back after a restart of VS Code: the trace is read again.

docs.title: The panel
docs.text: From top to bottom:

docs.title: Summary tiles
docs.text: Tile Shows Duration The time from the first to the last event, and the number of events. Requests Requests shown (by default the ones over 50 ms), and the number of batch tasks. Slowest request (or Slowest task) Its duration and method, with "unfinished" when it was still running when the trace stopped. Click it to select that request. X++ calls Number of X++ method calls in the trace, and how many hot methods are listed. SQL Number of SQL statements and their total time in the database. Pauses Number of pauses of 500 ms or more, and the longest one.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
• One lane per thread (T1688). When the trace has several AOS instances, each lane also names the AOS, because thread ids are per AOS.
  • Each request is a bar from its start to its end, with the method name when it fits. The legend shows the colours for Request, Batch task, Pause and Selected.
  • Thin marks at the bottom of a lane are pauses on that thread; hatched areas across all lanes are periods where the whole process logged nothing.
  • Hover a bar for the method, duration, start time, thread, session, user, SQL count and errors. Click it to select the request.
  • Show batch tasks adds batch work (hidden by default, so the timeline shows what users did).
  • Click Timeline to collapse or expand it.
  • The axis is seconds from the start of the trace. Elsewhere, times are UTC times of day (20:05:53.120), so you can match them with integration logs.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: Six tabs, each with a count: Requests, Errors, Sessions, Hot methods, SQL and Pauses. Use the arrow keys, Home and End to move between tabs.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
The box Filter methods and SQL filters the current tab as you type (press Ctrl+F in the panel to focus it, Escape to clear it). What it matches:

Tab Matches on Requests AOS, session, user and every method in the request's call tree. Non-matching requests are dimmed in the timeline; in the call tree the matching methods are expanded and highlighted. Errors The method, the catching method, AOS, session, user, request method and every frame of the stack. Sessions AOS, session id, user id and user GUID. Hot methods Method name. SQL Statement text and the methods that ran it. Pauses The last method, the thread (T1688) or "whole process".

docs.title: Requests tab
docs.text:
A request is one outermost X++ call on a thread: a button click, a form opening, a service call, a batch task. The list on the left shows each request with its method, duration, a bar, the thread, start time and SQL count, and badges for errors, unfinished and batch. Sort it with Slowest first or In time order. When batch tasks are hidden, the footer says how many and offers Show. Use the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End to move in the list; Enter or the right arrow moves to the call tree.

The detail on the right has three parts:

  1. Facts: Duration (with ≥ when unfinished), Started (time and thread), Session (user and session), SQL (time, statements and share of the request), and either Waiting (time in methods that wait for another session) or Busy (time in X++ and the kernel).
  2. Hot spots: up to 8 methods with the most self time in this request, with their share. Methods that wait for another session (methods ending in ::wait or WaitForCompletion, such as the operation sandbox) are marked waiting: that time is not work done here.
  3. Call tree, with columns Method, Total (inclusive time: the method and everything it called), Self (exclusive time), Calls and SQL (statements and time run by the method itself).
  4. At first, calls that take 15% or more of the request are expanded.
  5. Hot path expands the heaviest child at each level down to the call where the time is spent.
  6. Collapse collapses everything.
  7. The server sends only the heaviest part of each tree. A row Show N calls (or Show N more calls) loads the calls it left out, up to 500 at a time. Expanding a call whose children were left out loads them too.
  8. Keyboard: arrows to move, right/left to expand/collapse, Space to toggle, Enter to open the method's code.

docs.title: Errors tab
docs.text:
One card per distinct error, warning or exception:

  • error: a call to Global::error, Global::checkFailed or Global::exceptionTextFallThrough;
  • warning: a call to Global::warning;
  • exception: X++ frames that never logged their exit because an exception unwound them. The card says "Exception in method, caught by method": the catching method is the first frame that logged its exit.

Each card shows the UTC time, a count when the same stack repeats in the request, the AOS, thread, session, user and request method, and the full call stack, outermost first. Show request selects the request in the Requests tab. Very deep stacks keep the first 5 and the last 54 frames.

The trace has no message text for these calls. To find the label behind a message a user saw, use Find Message Source.

docs.title: Sessions tab
docs.text: Every session in the trace: AOS, session id, user, start time, span, requests, X++ calls, errors and exceptions. Sessions with errors are highlighted. Click a session id (or press Enter on its row) to put it in the filter and switch to the Requests tab, which then lists only that session's requests. Columns with a sort button can be sorted.

docs.title: Hot methods tab
docs.text: Methods summed over the whole trace: Self, Total, Calls, Average (total per call), Longest call, SQL and SQL time (statements run by the method itself). Recursive calls count once in the total. Methods that wait for another session are left out; Include waits (N) shows them. Click a column header to sort, click a method (or press Enter) to open its code.

docs.title: SQL tab
docs.text: Statements grouped by text (whitespace normalized), with Total, Count, Longest, Statement and Run by (the X++ methods that ran it, with counts). Expand a statement to see it formatted on several lines and all its callers; the copy button copies the SQL. Statements whose text was scrubbed from the trace show as "Direct SQL (the text was scrubbed from the trace)". A statement run thousands of times with a small total is a query in a loop; a statement with a large Longest is a slow query to check with Explain Plan.

docs.title: Pauses tab
docs.text: Periods of 500 ms or more where nothing was logged: At, Duration, Where (a thread, or the whole process / whole AOS) and Last method. Show request selects the request the pause belongs to. A pause on a thread means the request waited (locks, another session, the client) or the runtime was busy (for example JIT compilation). A pause of the whole process usually means garbage collection or a busy machine.

docs.title: Open the code
docs.text: Click any method name (or press Enter on it) to open it in the X++ code view at that method. Trace names such as Forms.SalesTable+SalesLine::linkActive open the form SalesTable. Classes and tables are looked up in the metadata (class, table, view, data entity, map, query). Kernel classes have no X++ code; F&O Studio says so.

docs.title: Analyze a trace with Copilot
docs.text:
The MCP tool xpp_analyze_trace gives agents the same analysis as text. The F&O Performance agent starts with it for any .etl file, and F&O Support uses it for error traces (see Copilot Agents). Example prompts:

  • "Analyze C:\Traces\confirm-order.etl. Which method costs the most in the slowest request, and why?"
  • "In this trace, find the error the user contoso.user got around 20:05 and show the call stack."
  • "Only the dual-write session in this trace: which entity method is slow?"

docs.title: Tool parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Meaning path (required) Full path of the .etl file. Other file types are refused. minRequestMs Without filters, ignore requests shorter than this. Default 50. aos Only this AOS: machine name, or part of it (case-insensitive). session Only this X++ session id (exact). user Only sessions of this user: user id or user GUID, or part of it. method Only requests whose call tree has a method containing this text (for example SalesFormLetter or PriceDisc). The output adds the path from the request to that method. from Only requests running at or after this time: a UTC time (20:05:50), a UTC date and time, or seconds from the start of the trace. to Only requests that started at or before this time (same formats). manifestFolder Folder with the event manifests, only when the tool reports none were found.

When aos, session or user is given, the server reads the trace twice: first to find the matching sessions, then to analyze only their events. If nothing matches, the error lists up to 20 sessions to pick from. The AOS and session lists in the output always cover the whole trace, so the agent can pick another session next.

docs.title: Tool output
docs.text:
Plain text, bounded so it fits in the agent's context:

  1. The trace's UTC start and end, duration, events, X++ calls and SQL statements, and the filter.
  2. AOS instances with their event and session counts.
  3. Sessions (up to 40): AOS, session, user, UTC time range, requests, X++ calls, errors and exceptions.
  4. Errors and exceptions (up to 25) with the call stack (up to 18 frames, outermost first).
  5. Platform messages (up to 25): the first time, count, event, session and user of each distinct message the platform logged.
  6. Slowest requests (the 10 slowest over minRequestMs), or with a filter the Requests matching the filter (first 30, in time order). For each: start, thread, session, user, duration, batch/unfinished/error marks, SQL, the hot path (up to 10 calls with inclusive/exclusive time and calls) and the methods with the most exclusive time.
  7. Methods by exclusive time (top 15, waits left out).
  8. SQL by total time (top 10) with the main caller.
  9. Pauses (up to 8).

A typical agent flow: analyze the whole trace, pick the session and time window of the scenario from the session list, call the tool again with session and from/to, then read the named methods with xpp_read_object and run xpp_analyze_performance on them (Analyze Performance).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.trace.manifestFolder empty Folder with the Dynamics 365 trace event manifests (DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man). Empty: F&O Studio looks in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring, AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring and the registered trace providers' folder. Machine scope.

The panel remembers the selected tab, Show batch tasks, Include waits, the timeline state and the request order.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Analyze Trace… (src/traceAnalyzer.ts) sends xpp/trace with action analyze, the file path and xpp.trace.manifestFolder to the F&O Studio server (src/serverClient.ts). Trace requests run in parallel with other requests, outside the metadata lock.
  2. The server's TraceService (server/Host/TraceService.cs) loads the event manifests (EventManifest, server/Tracing/EventManifest.cs): every *.man file of the first folder that has any, mapping provider and event id to the event name and its fields. The search order is xpp.trace.manifestFolder; then, for the framework and reference folders of the active configuration, <folder>\bin\Monitoring and <parent>\WebRoot\Monitoring; then the folders of the registered Dynamics 365 trace providers in the Windows event log registry.
  3. EtwFileReader (server/Tracing/EtwFileReader.cs) reads the .etl with the Windows ETW consumer API (OpenTrace/ProcessTrace in advapi32), no other library. Events without a manifest are skipped.
  4. Each event is decoded with its manifest layout. The fields used are machineName (AOS), sessionId, userId, userGuid, requestId and message, and:
  5. XppMethodEnter / XppMethodExit with methodName (the Dynamics.AX.Application. prefix is removed);
  6. AosSqlStatementExecutionLatency with sqlStatement, preparationTimeSeconds and executionTimeSeconds (SQL time is preparation plus execution).
  7. TraceAnalyzer (server/Analysis/TraceAnalyzer.cs) keeps a call stack per AOS and thread:
  8. the first call on an empty stack starts a request; the call tree merges repeated calls of the same method under the same parent;
  9. SQL statements are attributed to the method on top of the stack;
  10. an exit that skips frames records an exception caught by the exiting method; calls to Global::error, checkFailed, exceptionTextFallThrough and warning record errors and warnings with the stack (up to 500 distinct ones);
  11. 500 ms without any event on a running thread, or on the whole AOS, records a pause;
  12. at the end, requests still on the stack are unfinished, and every request on a thread where a request's outermost method starts with Batch is marked batch.
  13. The report is bounded: without filters only requests of 50 ms or more (or with errors), at most 150 requests (those with errors first, then the slowest), and per request up to 400 call tree nodes of at least 5 ms (or 0.2% of the request). Hot methods: top 300; SQL: top 200; pauses: top 50; sessions: top 300. Call trees are sent as flat lists of nodes with a parent id, so very deep stacks do not hit JSON nesting limits.
  14. The server keeps the 2 most recent traces in memory (TraceSession) so the panel can load left-out calls (action children, 500 per page). Closing a panel sends close. When a panel's trace was dropped, F&O Studio asks "... is no longer loaded, so its other calls can't be shown. Read the trace again?" with Reload Trace.
  15. The panel (media/trace.js) renders the report; all text from the trace is shown as text, never as HTML.

The agent tool xpp_analyze_trace runs the same analysis (TraceService.AnalyzeText) and formats text instead of JSON. node scripts/trace-test.js <exe> <config> <file.etl> (scripts/trace-test.js) checks both against a real trace.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The panel has no server-side filters: it always reads the whole trace and filters what it shows. The AOS, session, user, method and time filters that reduce the analysis itself are in xpp_analyze_trace.
  • Only X++ method and SQL events are analyzed. Platform messages are collected for the agent tool but are not shown in the panel.
  • Without filters, requests under 50 ms are left out (unless they have errors).
  • Errors are found from calls to the error methods and from unwound frames, not from message text; the infolog text is not in the trace.
  • Statements whose text the platform scrubbed cannot be shown.
  • Calls entered before the trace started have no enter event; their exits are ignored.
  • The trace is read into memory; very large traces take time and memory. Take short traces.
  • Windows only, 64-bit server.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No event manifests (*.man) found. Searched: ..." The manifests are not in the searched folders (for example a machine without the platform installed). Copy the *.man files from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring of a development environment to a folder, and set xpp.trace.manifestFolder (or pass manifestFolder to the tool). "No event manifests (*.man) in folder." xpp.trace.manifestFolder points to a folder without .man files. Point it to the folder that contains DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man, or clear the setting. "Pass the full path of a trace file (.etl)." The path is empty or not an .etl file. Pick the .etl file. "Trace file not found: ..." The path does not exist on the machine where the server runs. Copy the trace locally and use its full path. "Can't open the trace ..." / "Can't read the trace ..." Windows could not open or read the file (locked, corrupt, incomplete download). Download the trace again; make sure tracing was stopped before downloading. "No session matches ... Sessions in the trace: ..." (agent tool) The aos, session or user filter matches no session. Use a session id or user from the list in the message. "Can't read the time '...'" (agent tool) from/to is not seconds, a UTC time or a UTC date and time. Use 20:05:53, 2026-11-25 20:05:53 or a number of seconds. "Name is not in the metadata (a kernel class); it has no X++ code to open." The method belongs to a kernel class. Look at its caller in the call tree instead. "file is no longer loaded, so its other calls can't be shown." The server keeps only the 2 most recent traces. Click Reload Trace. The timeline is empty: "No requests to show. Turn on batch tasks to see background work." The trace only has batch work. Check Show batch tasks. Few requests in the list. Requests under 50 ms are left out. Use the agent tool with minRequestMs, or with a filter (filters show requests of any length).

docs.title: Application Explorer
docs.text: The Application Explorer lists every element of every model in the active D365FO configuration, standard and your own, grouped the way Visual Studio's Application Explorer groups them. It is the starting point for browsing standard code, opening designers, creating extensions and running most element commands from the right-click menu. It has the same two layouts as Visual Studio: the classic view (elements by type across all models) and the model view (elements by model).

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Browse what exists: all tables of a module, all extensions of a form, all security privileges of a model.
  • Find an element when you know part of its name (filter), then open its designer or code.
  • Start an action on an element: create an extension or a Chain of Command class, find references, view the ERD, browse table data, compare, copy its name.
  • Look at one model only (model view), for example your own model, to see what it contains.
  • Run model-level actions: update a model's parameters, view its dependencies, run upgrade readiness.

If you already know the element name, Open Element (Ctrl+Alt+O) is faster.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio needs D365FO metadata on this machine: a unified developer environment (UDE) that you connected with Connect to Environment, or a cloud-hosted / VHD environment (Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments).
  • Without metadata the view shows No D365FO metadata found on this machine. with a Connect to Environment link.
  • A D365FO project is not required. The Application Explorer works without one. Commands that add elements to a project (Add to Project, Create Extension, Duplicate…) use the project when one is open (D365FO Projects).

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Open the F&O Studio icon in the activity bar. The side bar has four views: Application Explorer, D365FO Project, Security (collapsed) and Dynamics 365. The Application Explorer is the first one.

The title bar of the view has these buttons:

Button Command What it does Filter Filter Application Explorer… Asks for part of an element name and filters the tree. Shown when no filter is active. Clear filter Clear Filter Removes the filter. Shown instead of Filter while a filter is active. Model view Switch to Model View (Elements by Model) Switches to the model view. Shown in the classic view. Classic view Switch to Classic View (Elements by Type) Switches back. Shown in the model view. Open element Open Element… Opens the Open Element picker. Search code Search Code in All Packages See Search Code. Build Build Model See Build Project and Model. Refresh Refresh Application Explorer Reads the models and element lists from disk again. Collapse all (VS Code) Collapses the whole tree.

The view's description, next to its title, shows the current layout and filter, for example Classic view · filter: CustGroup.

docs.title: Classic view (elements by type)
docs.text:
The classic view is Visual Studio's default layout. The top level is a list of categories. Each category holds element types, and each type lists the elements of all models:

Data Types
  Base Enums
  Base Enum Extensions
  Extended Data Types
  Extended Data Type Extensions
Data Model
  Tables
    CustGroup            Application Suite
    CustTable            Application Suite
    ...
  Table Extensions
    CustTable.ContosoExtensions   Contoso Extensions
Code
  Classes
  Macros
User Interface
  Forms
  ...

Next to each element, the description shows the display names of the models that contain it. An element that exists in two models (for example a custom model that holds a copy) shows both.

docs.title: Model view (elements by model)
docs.text:
The model view lists the models first, by display name, then the same categories and types inside each model. Only categories and types that the model has are shown.

  • Your own (custom) models come first, with a package icon. Standard models have a library icon.
  • When the display name differs from the model name, the model name is shown next to it. For example the model Foundation is listed as Application Suite with Foundation as its description.
  • The tooltip of a model shows its display name, model name, package, folder and whether it is a custom model.

docs.title: Categories and element types
docs.text:
The categories and their element types follow Visual Studio's order:

Category Element types Data Types Base Enums, Base Enum Extensions, Extended Data Types, Extended Data Type Extensions Data Model Tables, Table Extensions, Views, View Extensions, Queries, Query Extensions, Data Entities, Data Entity Extensions, Composite Data Entities, Aggregate Data Entities, Maps, Map Extensions, Table Collections Code Classes, Macros User Interface Forms, Form Extensions, Tiles, Tile Extensions, Menus, Menu Extensions, Display / Action / Output Menu Items and their extensions, Form Parts, Info Parts, Cues, Cue Groups AI Skills Analytics Aggregate Dimensions, Aggregate Measurements, KPIs, Calculated Measure Templates, Calculated Measure Templates (Other Period) Reports Reports, Report Embedded Images, Report Data Sources, Report Layout Templates, and the list, matrix, pie/doughnut chart, table and XY chart style templates Business Process and Workflow Workflow Categories, Workflow Approvals and extensions, Workflow Tasks and extensions, Workflow Automated Tasks, Workflow Types and extensions, and the due date calculation, hierarchy, participant and queue assignment providers Label Files Label Files Resources Resources Configuration Configuration Keys, Configuration Key Groups, License Codes Security Security Roles and extensions, Security Duties and extensions, Security Privileges, Security Policies, Direct Access Permissions References References Services Services, Service Groups

A category that holds only its own type (Label Files, Resources, References) is shown as that type directly, as in Visual Studio. Element type folders that F&O Studio does not know yet still appear, under a category named Other.

docs.title: Open an element
docs.text:
Click an element:

  • A class opens in the X++ Code View.
  • A label file opens in the Label Editor.
  • Any other element opens in the Element Designer.

This matches Visual Studio, where classes open in the code editor and other elements in their designer. Elements with code (tables, forms, views, data entities, queries, maps) also have an inline View Code button.

docs.title: Filter the tree
docs.text:
1. Click the filter button, or run F&O Studio: Filter Application Explorer….
  2. Type part of an element name, for example CustGroup, and press Enter.
  3. The tree shows only categories, types (and, in the model view, models) with at least one matching element, expanded.

Details:

  • The match is a case-insensitive "contains" match on the element name. custgroup finds CustGroup, CustGroupCategory and CredManCreditLimitCustGroupLine.
  • Each type node lists at most 2,000 matching elements; the rest are summarized as N more… refine the filter.
  • The filter applies to both views. Switching views keeps it.
  • Clear Filter shows everything again. An empty filter also clears it.

docs.title: Locate an element
docs.text:
Locate in Application Explorer selects an element in the tree, like Visual Studio's command of the same name. It is on:

  • the right-click menu of an element in the D365FO Project view;
  • the right-click menu of the root node in the Element Designer;
  • the right-click menu of an X++ code view editor.

If a filter would hide the element, the filter is cleared first. If the element is not found you get is not in the Application Explorer.

docs.title: Select several elements
docs.text: The tree supports multi-select (Ctrl+click, Shift+click). Multi-selection is used for drag and drop into the project view; see Drag and Drop.

docs.title: Right-click actions on elements
docs.text: What the menu offers depends on the element type and on whether the element belongs to one of your models. The same actions (except Add to Project) are on the element nodes of the D365FO Project view.

docs.text: Action Shown for Details Rename… Elements of your own models, except extensions Rename and Refactoring Delete Elements of your own models See below

docs.title: Add to Project
docs.text:
Add to Project adds the element to the open D365FO project, as Visual Studio does when you drag an element into Solution Explorer.

  1. Right-click an element of your model and choose Add to Project (or click the + inline button).
  2. If no project is open, F&O Studio runs Open D365FO Project… first.
  3. The element is added to the .rnrproj and the project view refreshes: Added to the project.

    A D365FO project belongs to one model. Adding an element of another model fails with a message that the element belongs to model X while the project targets model Y. To change a standard element, create an extension instead.

docs.title: Duplicate…
docs.text:
Duplicate… is Visual Studio's Duplicate: a copy of the element in your model.

  1. Right-click the element and choose Duplicate….
  2. The target model is the open project's model. Without a project you pick one of your models.
  3. Enter the name. The default is <Name>Copy. For an extension the name must be <Base>.<Suffix> with a new suffix (default <Base>.<Model>).
  4. The copy is created, added to the project (when one is open) and opened.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
Delete removes the element's metadata from its model. It is only shown for elements of your own models.

  1. Right-click the element and choose Delete.
  2. Confirm Delete '' from its model? The metadata file is removed.
  3. If the element is still referenced by other elements, F&O Studio shows the server's message about those references and offers Delete Anyway.
  4. The element is also removed from the project, and both trees refresh.

    5. To take an element out of the project but keep it in the model, use Exclude from Project in the project view.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl empty Web client URL for Open in Browser and Open Table Browser when the environment's configuration has none xpp.git.baseBranch empty Used by the change marks in the project view, not by the Application Explorer

The Application Explorer has no settings of its own. The view (classic or model) and the filter are kept while the window is open; a new window starts in the classic view without a filter.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The tree is built by AotTreeProvider in src/aot.ts. It does not call the metadata server: it reads the folders of the active configuration directly, which makes it fast and keeps it working while the server starts.
  • Models. The active configuration (registry CurrentMetadataConfig and its XPPConfig JSON, see Select Environment) gives the custom metadata folder (ModelStoreFolder) and the reference package folders. For each package folder, each Descriptor\<Model>.xml is a model; its DisplayName gives the display name. Models in the custom folder are custom. Custom roots are read first, so a custom model wins over a same-named reference copy.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD environments keep all packages in one folder. There, a package is standard when every model in it has a Publisher that starts with Microsoft; the others are your models.
  • Elements. Each element is a file <package>\<model>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml. A type node lists the .xml file names of that type folder, per model (model view) or merged across all models (classic view), sorted by name.
  • Caching. The model list and each type's element list are read once and cached. Refresh Application Explorer (also Refresh Models in the Dynamics 365 view) clears the cache. Creating, duplicating, importing or deleting elements through F&O Studio refreshes it, and so does switching environment.
  • Context menus. Each element node carries a context value with flags such as code, form, extensible, coc, browser, table, refs, hier, class, menuitem, ext, xstr and custom. The view/item/context menus in package.json show each action when its flag is present.
  • Clicking runs vscode.open on the code view URI xpp:/AxClass/<Name>.xpp for classes and Open Designer for everything else.
  • Actions that change metadata (Add to Project, Duplicate…, Delete, Create Extension) go to the F&O Studio metadata server through bridge actions such as add_to_project, duplicate_object and the agent tool xpp_delete_object; the server uses Microsoft's metadata API. See Metadata Server and Bridge Protocol.
  • The action handlers are in src/d365Tools.ts and src/extension.ts.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Elements are listed from the files on disk. An element that another tool writes while the view is open shows up after Refresh Application Explorer.
  • The filter matches element names only, not labels or properties. Use Search Code for code and Open Element for ranked name search.
  • There are no element sub-nodes (fields, methods) in the tree. Open the element in the Element Designer to see them.
  • Write actions (Rename…, Delete, View History) are offered only on your own models. Standard elements are read-only; extend them instead.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No D365FO metadata found on this machine. No active configuration, or its folders are missing Run Connect to Environment or Select Environment A new element is missing The element lists are cached Click Refresh Application Explorer Your model is listed as standard (library icon) on a VHD Every model in its package has a publisher starting with Microsoft Set your own publisher with Update Model Parameters… or Visual Studio's model management N more… refine the filter More than 2,000 matches in one type Type a longer filter Add to Project fails: belongs to model …, but the active project targets model … Projects hold elements of one model Create an extension in your model, or open a project for that model is not in the Application Explorer. after Locate in Application Explorer The element's file is not in any model folder of the active configuration Check the environment; refresh the view

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
F&O Studio has three parts: a TypeScript VS Code extension, a Node library for the cloud operations (@fno-studio/core), and a .NET Framework metadata server (XppVsCode.Server.exe). The extension owns the UI. The server works on Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations metadata with Microsoft's own metadata API, loaded from your installation. The core library talks to Dataverse and the unified developer environment (UDE).

This page shows how the parts fit together. The pages under Related go deeper into each part.

docs.title: The three parts
docs.text:
Part Folder Language and runtime What it does Extension src/ TypeScript, VS Code extension host Views, designers (webviews), code view, language features, commands, build with xppc and LabelC, debugger, database UI, sign-in, settings and state Core library core/ TypeScript, Node 20+, no VS Code Dataverse client, deploy and database sync, SysTest runs, just-in-time SQL credentials, the data client, environment discovery, UDE connection check and setup, deployed-versus-built staleness Metadata server server/ C#, .NET Framework 4.8, x64 Reads and writes metadata through Microsoft's metadata API, labels, .rnrproj projects, cross-reference queries, code intelligence, analysis, report designs and preview, trace parsing, business data queries, and the MCP agent tools

There is no other runtime dependency: package.json has no dependencies, only development tools.

docs.title: How they connect
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph VSCode["VS Code"]
        EXT["Extension (src/)"]
        CORE["@fno-studio/core (core/dist)"]
        COP["GitHub Copilot (agent mode)"]
    end
    subgraph Servers["XppVsCode.Server.exe processes"]
        S1["Extension server<br/>--allow-data"]
        S2["Language server<br/>--allow-data"]
        S3["MCP server<br/>--activity-log [--rules]"]
    end
    D365["PackagesLocalDirectory\\bin<br/>(Microsoft assemblies, xppc, LabelC)"]
    META["Metadata folders<br/>(reference + custom)"]
    XREF["Cross-reference DB<br/>(SQL LocalDB)"]
    DV["Dataverse / UDE"]
    SQL["Business database<br/>(AxDB or UDE Azure SQL)"]

    EXT -- "JSON-RPC over stdio<br/>xpp/bridge, xpp/lang, xpp/data, xpp/trace" --> S1
    EXT -- "xpp/lang" --> S2
    COP -- "MCP over stdio<br/>tools/list, tools/call" --> S3
    EXT --> CORE
    CORE -- "HTTPS" --> DV
    S1 --> D365
    S2 --> D365
    S3 --> D365
    S1 --> META
    S3 --> META
    S1 --> XREF
    S2 --> XREF
    S3 --> XREF
    S1 --> SQL
    EXT -- "spawns" --> D365
  • The extension starts two server processes of its own (see Extension-Internals): one for designers, the code view and explorers, and one for language features, "so index builds never block the designers". Both get --allow-data.
  • VS Code starts a third process for Copilot, from the MCP server definition the extension registers. It gets --activity-log and, when the workspace has .xpp/agent-rules.md, --rules. It never gets --allow-data, so Copilot's process cannot reach business data through the server.
  • The core library runs inside the extension host. It never shows UI and never reads settings: the extension passes sign-in, logging, progress, cancellation and options in. See Core-Library.

docs.title: What each process is started with
docs.text:
Process Started by Arguments Source Extension server XppServerClient --config <json> --allow-data [--project <rnrproj>] src/serverClient.ts Language server a second XppServerClient same src/extension.ts MCP server VS Code, from registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider('xpp.mcp', ...) --config <json> --activity-log [--project <rnrproj>] [--rules <file>] src/mcpProvider.ts

--config is the active environment's XPPConfig JSON file. --project is the active D365FO project. When the environment, the project or the team rules file changes, the MCP definition gets a new version string (a hash of config, project and rules timestamp), and VS Code restarts the MCP server with the new arguments. The extension restarts its own two servers when the environment or the xpp.project setting changes.

The server also has two command-line modes the extension uses during environment setup: --sql-check and --restore-xref (server/Host/SqlSetup.cs). In those modes it does not load metadata.

docs.title: Where the environment comes from
docs.text:
All parts read the same D365FO development configuration Visual Studio uses:

  1. The registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations, value CurrentMetadataConfig, points at the active JSON configuration under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig.
  2. The JSON gives ModelStoreFolder (your custom metadata), ReferencePackagesPaths (standard packages), FrameworkDirectory (PackagesLocalDirectory, whose bin folder holds xppc, LabelC and Microsoft's assemblies), the cross-reference database and more.

Each VS Code window can select its own environment (Select-Environment); the extension then passes that configuration file to the servers with --config. Reading the configuration is in core (core/src/environment/discovery.ts) for the extension, and in server/Ported/DynamicsConfigurationReader.cs for the server.

docs.title: Microsoft components, loaded not shipped
docs.text:
F&O Studio never redistributes Microsoft's D365FO assemblies or tools.

  • The server compiles against PackagesLocalDirectory\bin with <Private>false</Private> references, so the assemblies are not copied to its output.
  • At run time, Program.Main registers an AssemblyResolve handler that loads them from <FrameworkDirectory>\bin of your configuration. This happens before any D365FO type is touched: Program.Run is marked NoInlining so the runtime does not resolve those types early.
  • The extension runs xppc.exe, LabelC.exe, xppbp, reportsc and the deployment package script from the same bin folder.
  • The release build fails when server/bin or the VSIX contains a Microsoft assembly (see Release-Process).
  • The report preview uses Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime, which the extension downloads from nuget.org only after you accept Microsoft's licence.

docs.title: Opening a table in the designer
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as You
    participant E as Extension (elementDesigner.ts)
    participant S as Extension server
    participant M as Metadata API
    U->>E: Open Designer on CustGroup
    E->>S: xpp/bridge get_element_tree {objectType: AxTable, objectName: CustGroup}
    S->>M: read AxTable CustGroup (disk provider)
    M-->>S: typed metadata object
    S-->>E: node tree JSON
    E-->>U: webview with nodes and Properties grid

docs.title: Copilot changing a class
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Copilot
    participant S as MCP server
    participant P as Write policy and agent scope
    participant M as Metadata API
    C->>S: tools/call xpp_update_object
    S->>S: ActivityLog snapshot of the element
    S->>P: is the element in a custom model and in scope?
    P-->>S: allowed (checkpoint copy taken)
    S->>M: update through the metadata API
    S-->>C: result text (with best-practice warnings)
    S->>S: activity.jsonl entry for Copilot Activity

docs.title: Deploying to a UDE
docs.text: The extension builds locally (xppc, LabelC, reportsc, PDB conversion), then calls core's deployPackages. Core zips each package, creates an msprov_fnopackages row in Dataverse, uploads the zip and starts msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync, then polls the async operation. The server is not involved. See Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: State and files on disk
docs.text:
What Where Written by Copilot tool calls and element snapshots %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activity.jsonl, snapshots\ MCP server (ActivityLog) Copilot scope and open checkpoint %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\agentSession.json extension; read by the MCP server before each write Checkpoint copies of elements %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\checkpoints\<id>\ MCP server Project an agent selected %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activeProject.txt MCP server; the extension asks you before opening it Bridge errors %TEMP%\XppVsCodeBridge.log any server process Database credentials VS Code secret storage (Windows Credential Manager) extension Built-versus-deployed state, usage counts VS Code global state extension

Server logs go to stderr; the extension shows them in the X++ output channel. Stdout is reserved for protocol messages.

docs.title: Design rules
docs.text:
These rules come from the project's contributor instructions and are enforced by tests where possible:

  • Metadata changes go through the metadata API. The server never writes AOT XML by hand. .rnrproj files and label text files are not AOT metadata and are edited directly, the way Visual Studio saves them.
  • Only your own models are writable. The bridge dispatcher checks every write action centrally (see Bridge-Protocol and Security-Model).
  • No Visual Studio dependency. The server references only DLLs from the packages bin folder; no EnvDTE or Microsoft.VisualStudio.*.
  • Bounded output. Agent tool results are kept short, because the agent's context is the budget.
  • The core has no VS Code. node scripts/check-core.js fails when anything in core/ imports vscode.
  • Metadata loads once, under a lock. Microsoft's descriptor reader is not safe for two loads at once.

docs.title: Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration
docs.text: F&O Studio recognizes repositories hosted on Azure DevOps (Azure Repos) and GitHub from the origin remote of your Git repository, and uses that to link your work to Azure Boards work items and to open the repository's pipelines. The integration is deliberately light: it reads the remote URL, writes to VS Code's commit message box and opens web pages. It calls no Azure DevOps or GitHub API and needs no token. This page describes what is recognized, what each host supports and how it combines with the general Azure DevOps and GitHub setup of a D365FO team.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Your team tracks work in Azure Boards and wants commits and pull requests linked to work items.
  • Your code is on GitHub but your work items are in Azure Boards.
  • You want one click from VS Code to the team's build pipelines or GitHub Actions runs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Git on the PATH, and the repository cloned on the machine.
  • The repository's origin remote pointing to Azure DevOps or GitHub (see the URL forms below).
  • Either the workspace folder or one of your custom models inside that repository (see How the repository is found).
  • For GitHub repositories with Azure Boards: the Azure Boards app for GitHub installed and the repository connected to the Azure DevOps project (general Azure DevOps setup, done by a project administrator, not by F&O Studio).

docs.title: What each host supports
docs.text:
Feature Azure Repos GitHub Link Work Item… Adds #123 to the commit message Adds AB#123 (the Azure Boards mention for GitHub) Open Work Item… Opens https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_workitems/edit/<id> Not available: shows "The repository is on GitHub: open the work item from Azure Boards (AB# mentions link there)." Open Pipelines Opens https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_build Opens https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions, filtered on the current branch Work items in Review My Changes #123 and AB#123 mentions in the branch's commit messages Same Change marks, Show Changed Elements, View History, xpp_diff_changes Any Git repository Any Git repository

The last row does not depend on the host at all: every Git repository, wherever it is hosted, gets change marks, history and review.

docs.title: Recognized remote URLs
docs.text:
F&O Studio reads git remote get-url origin and recognizes these forms (a trailing .git is ignored):

Form Example Azure DevOps HTTPS https://dev.azure.com/contoso/FinOps/_git/ContosoFinOps Azure DevOps HTTPS with user name https://contoso@dev.azure.com/contoso/FinOps/_git/ContosoFinOps Azure DevOps SSH git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/contoso/FinOps/ContosoFinOps Older visualstudio.com HTTPS https://contoso.visualstudio.com/FinOps/_git/ContosoFinOps (also with DefaultCollection/) GitHub HTTPS https://github.com/contoso/contoso-finops GitHub SSH git@github.com:contoso/contoso-finops

visualstudio.com URLs are turned into https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project> for the links. Encoded repository names (for example %20 for a space) are decoded.

Not recognized:

  • remotes other than origin (an upstream remote is ignored);
  • Azure DevOps Server (on-premises) and GitHub Enterprise Server host names;
  • ssh:// URLs.

For those, the commands show "The workspace is not in a Git repository with an Azure DevOps or GitHub origin." The host-independent Git features keep working.

docs.title: How the repository is found
docs.text:
The work item and pipeline commands look for a Git repository in this order and use the first one found:

  1. each folder of the current VS Code workspace (when a project is open: the project folder, the model folder and the C# project folders of its workspace);
  2. the real folder of each of your custom models (junctions resolved), so a model linked from the custom metadata folder into a repository is found even when the workspace is elsewhere.

In each candidate F&O Studio runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel. Then it reads the origin remote of that repository. If your models live in several repositories, the first match wins; open the project whose folder is in the repository you want, so the workspace folder is found first.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository (VS Code's Git: Clone, or Open Team Repository… which also links and builds the packages; see Open Team Repository).
  2. Open your D365FO project. Make your change.
  3. Before you commit, run Link Work Item… from the command palette or the Dynamics 365 view (Deploy). Enter the work item number. The mention is added to the commit message and the Source Control view opens.
  4. Commit and push with VS Code's Source Control view.
  5. Create the pull request on the hosting site (or with an extension such as GitHub Pull Requests). Azure Repos and Azure Boards link the commits, and the pull request, to the work item from the mention.
  6. Run Open Pipelines to watch the team's build.

Details and every prompt: Work Items and Pipelines.

docs.title: General Azure DevOps and GitHub practice for D365FO
docs.text:
The following is common D365FO practice. F&O Studio neither sets it up nor needs it, but it works alongside it:

  • Branch policies on main (Azure Repos) or branch protection rules (GitHub): required reviewers, a successful build, linked work items. Azure Repos can require a linked work item on every pull request; the #123 mention from Link Work Item… links the commit to the work item. If the pull request does not show the work item, add it on the pull request page.
  • A build pipeline that compiles the models with the X++ compiler from Microsoft's NuGet packages and produces the deployable package; see Build Automation and Pipelines.
  • Release to sandbox and production through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center; see Environments and Promotion.
  • Azure Boards for GitHub: connects a GitHub repository to an Azure DevOps project so AB#123 mentions link.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for the integration itself: the host is read from the remote each time a command runs. Review My Changes reads work item mentions from the commits between the base branch you enter (proposed from xpp.git.baseBranch, else main) and HEAD; with an empty base branch it lists no work items.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
All of it is in src/devops.ts:

  • parseRemote(url) matches the remote against the forms above and returns the host kind (azure or github), the base URL and the repository name.
  • linkWorkItem() uses the API of VS Code's built-in Git extension (vscode.git) to find the repository whose root is the one found above (or the first repository) and appends the mention to its commit message box (inputBox). If the Git extension has no repository open, the mention is copied to the clipboard instead.
  • openWorkItem() and openPipelines() build a URL and open it with the system browser.
  • branchWorkItems(base) runs git log --format=%B <base>..HEAD and collects every #<number> and AB#<number> (up to nine digits, not preceded by a letter, digit, _ or &). src/review.ts uses it for the Work items line of the review.

No credentials are read or stored. Browser pages use your normal browser sign-in.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No API access: F&O Studio cannot list, create or update work items, read their titles, create pull requests, or start or watch pipeline runs.
  • Work item links on GitHub depend on the Azure Boards app; F&O Studio cannot check that the connection exists.
  • Only the origin remote, and only dev.azure.com, *.visualstudio.com and github.com hosts.
  • Azure Pipelines opens the pipeline list of the project, not filtered on the branch.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The workspace is not in a Git repository with an Azure DevOps or GitHub origin." No workspace folder or model folder is in a Git repository, or its origin is not a recognized URL. Run git remote get-url origin in the repository. Add or fix the origin remote, or open the project whose folder is in the repository. The mention lands in the clipboard, not in the commit box VS Code's Git extension has no repository open (for example Git is disabled in VS Code). Paste the mention into your commit message, or enable git.enabled and open the repository folder. The mention lands in another repository's commit box The Git extension has several repositories and none has the root found by F&O Studio; the first one is used. Open the workspace on the right repository, or copy the mention by hand. AB#123 does not link on GitHub The repository is not connected to Azure Boards. Ask an Azure DevOps project administrator to connect it (Project settings > GitHub connections). The wrong Azure DevOps project opens The origin remote points to another project. Check git remote -v.

docs.title: Best Practice Checks
docs.text: Run Best Practice Checks on Project runs Microsoft's best practice checker (xppbp), the same checker Visual Studio runs for Dynamics 365 > Run best practice checks, on your project's model and puts the findings for the project's elements in the Problems view. Copilot agents run the same checks with the xpp_check_best_practice tool. Use it to catch best practice violations before a code review or a deploy.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you ask for a code review or open a pull request.
  • After Copilot created or changed elements, to check them against the rules partner code reviews use.
  • As part of the Pre-Deploy Checklist and Review My Changes, which run it for you.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An open D365FO project whose model is one of your own models (see D365FO Projects). The command fails with "Open a D365FO project first." without one.
  • An active environment configuration: xppbp.exe is read from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin of the active configuration.
  • Build the model first if you changed code: the checker reads the metadata and code on disk, and compile errors make its findings less useful. See Build Project and Model.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the checks in one of these ways:
  2. Dynamics 365 view: Build and check > Best Practice Checks;
  3. D365FO Project view title bar: Check menu > Run Best Practice Checks on Project;
  4. command palette: F&O Studio: Run Best Practice Checks on Project.
  5. A notification shows "Best practice checks: …". Click Cancel to stop the checker.
  6. When it finishes, the status bar shows "Best practice: N error(s), M warning(s)" for 10 seconds.
  7. Open the Problems view (Ctrl+Shift+M). Each finding is on the element's code view:
  8. the problem code is the rule's moniker (its identifier);
  9. findings on code have a line; findings on metadata (line 0) are shown on the first line of the code view;
  10. errors and fatal findings show as errors, warnings as warnings, others as information.
  11. Click a finding to open the element. Fix it, or decide that the warning stays and say why in your review.
  12. The X++ Build output has the full log, starting with "=== Best practice checks () ===" and ending with the counts.

    Each run replaces the previous run's best practice findings. Compiler diagnostics from a build are kept separately and are not cleared by a best practice run.

docs.title: Project scope
docs.text: The checker always checks the whole model (-all); F&O Studio then keeps only the findings of elements in the project (and findings that do not name an element). The counts in the status bar and the output are those of the project's elements.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Agents call xpp_check_best_practice after they create or change code, next to xpp_build. Its inputs:

Input Values Default modelName a custom model the active project's model scope model or project model

The result is text, errors first, at most 80 findings:

BEST PRACTICE: ContosoExtensions (project XvsDemo only) in 63s - 0 error(s), 4 warning(s).
  WARNING AxClass ContosoOrderStatusHelper.run line 22:9 [<moniker>] <message>
  WARNING AxTable ContosoOrderStatusTable [<moniker>] <message>

Example prompt in agent mode with the F&O Developer or F&O Code Reviewer agent:

Run the best practice checks on my project and fix the warnings in ContosoOrderStatusHelper.

See Agent Tools: Analysis and Agents for Developers.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
There are no settings for the best practice run itself. Related:

Setting Default Effect xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules false Runs AppChecker rules as part of the build (xppc -RunAppcheckerRules), not of the best practice run.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
XppBuilder.bestPractice in src/build.ts runs:

xppbp.exe -metadata=<custom metadata folder>
          -packagesRoot=<FrameworkDirectory (PackagesLocalDirectory)>
          -module=<package> -model=<model> -all
          -xmlLog=<package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppbp.xml
  • The custom metadata folder is the source; the reference packages under -packagesRoot provide everything the model uses.
  • The package is found from the model name (a package can hold a model with another name).
  • The XML log has the same <Diagnostic> format as the compiler's, so it is parsed and mapped to code view lines the same way (see Compiler Diagnostics), into a separate diagnostic collection.
  • If the checker writes no XML log (for example when you cancel), nothing is reported.

The agent tool runs the same command line in the metadata server, BuildService.BestPracticeJson in server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs.

Other features that run the checker:

  • Pre-Deploy Checklist: the "Best practice" step fails when the project's elements have best practice errors.
  • Review My Changes: checks the changed elements of each model.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The command checks the open project only; to check a whole model from the UI, ask an agent to run xpp_check_best_practice with scope: model.
  • Only your own models can be checked.
  • The checker takes a minute or more because it checks the whole model.
  • Findings are not updated while you type; run the checks again after changes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Open a D365FO project first." No project is open. Open your project. No status bar message and no findings The checker wrote no XML log (cancelled, or xppbp failed to start). Read the X++ Build output. Agent tool: "Model '...' is not one of your custom models." The model is a standard model. Pass one of your own models. Agent tool: "scope 'project' needs an active project" No project selected for the MCP server. Select a project (xpp_select_project) or use scope: model. Agent tool: "The best-practice checker wrote no results" xppbp failed. The tool result shows the end of its output.

docs.title: Branching and Team Workflow
docs.text: This page describes a branching model and a day-to-day workflow for a D365FO team that develops with F&O Studio, and which F&O Studio features support each step. The branching model itself is general D365FO and Git practice: F&O Studio does not create branches, enforce policies or merge. What it adds is branch-aware tooling: change marks and reviews against a base branch, element history, a shared repository setup and shared Copilot rules.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You agree on a branching model for a new D365FO team.
  • You move a team from Visual Studio and TFVC or Git to VS Code and want to keep the same workflow.
  • You want every developer's F&O Studio set up the same way.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A Git repository with your packages and projects (see Source Control for X++).
  • One development environment per developer: a unified developer environment (UDE) or a cloud-hosted / VHD environment. D365FO developers do not share a development environment, because each one builds and deploys its own packages.

docs.title: A branching model that works for D365FO (general practice)
docs.text:
D365FO code ships as whole packages: a deployable package carries the full compiled package, not a diff. That favours a simple model with short-lived branches:

Branch Purpose Built by main Integrated code that builds and passes tests. Source of the deployable package for sandbox. The team's build pipeline feature/<work item>-<short name> One work item or a small set; merged by pull request. The developer (F&O Studio build), optionally a pull request build release/<version> or tags Optional: what went to production, for hotfixes. Many teams tag main instead. The build pipeline hotfix/<work item> Optional: fix on top of the production release, merged back to main. The build pipeline

Rules most teams keep:

  • Small branches, merged often. X++ elements are XML files; long branches produce merge conflicts in large XML files (forms, tables) that are hard to resolve.
  • One model per concern. Changes in different models conflict less; models also define what deploys together (see Models, Packages and Versioning).
  • Pull requests with a build. The pull request build compiles the whole package, so a change that compiles only on one developer's machine is caught.
  • Production comes from the pipeline, never from a developer machine.

docs.title: Daily workflow with F&O Studio
docs.text:
1. Start from the latest base. Pull main and create your branch with VS Code's Source Control view or git switch -c feature/4711-order-status.
  2. Build after switching branches. A branch switch changes element files on disk. Run Build Model (or Build Project) so the package's assemblies match the branch. On a UDE, the status bar then shows that the build is newer than the last deploy, and Run Tests and the debugger offer Deploy First. If designers still show content from the other branch, restart the X++ server from its status bar item.
  3. Work. Create and change elements. The project view marks them M, A, D or R (see Git Changes in the Project View).
  4. Commit with the work item. Run Link Work Item… before each commit, so the commit links to Azure Boards (see Work Items and Pipelines).
  5. Review before the pull request. Run Review My Changes with base branch main. Fix Chain of Command wrappers that skip next, best practice errors and performance warnings. Copy the report into the pull request (see Review My Changes).
  6. Deploy to your own environment and test. On a UDE, Deploy Models to Environment, then Run Tests (see Deploy to Environment, Run Tests). Or run Pre-Deploy Checklist to do the checks in one report.
  7. Push and open the pull request on Azure Repos or GitHub. Run Open Pipelines to watch the pull request build.
  8. Review a colleague's pull request: check out their branch, build, and run Review My Changes against main, or ask the F&O Code Reviewer agent (see Scenario: Review a Pull Request).
  9. After the merge, switch back to main, pull, delete the feature branch and build again.

docs.title: Settings and files to agree on in the team
docs.text:
Item Where Effect xpp.git.baseBranch = main Each developer's user settings, or the workspace settings of the open project Change marks and Show Changed Elements include everything the branch changed since main. .xpp/workspace.json Repository The packages Open Team Repository… links for every developer. Written the first time a developer runs it on the repository; commit it. .xpp/agent-rules.md The first workspace folder (the project folder when a project is open); commit it with the project Team rules for Copilot: naming prefix, model, patterns, review steps. Created by Create Team Rules for Copilot (see Team Rules). .gitignore Repository Keeps build output out of commits (see Source Control for X++).

Opening a project writes its VS Code workspace file into F&O Studio's own storage, not into the repository, so per-developer project workspaces never show up as changes. The workspace file keeps settings you add to it.

docs.title: Merge conflicts in X++ metadata
docs.text:
Conflicts happen in the element XML files. General guidance:

  • Methods are in <Method> nodes with the source in CDATA. Conflicts between different methods usually merge cleanly; conflicts in the same method are resolved like any code conflict.
  • Forms and tables have long lists of controls or fields. Keep both sides' new nodes; avoid reordering nodes by hand.
  • After resolving, build the model; the compiler reports errors in the merged elements. Then commit.
  • Use View History on the element to compare versions as X++ code rather than XML (see Element History), and Compare Code… / Compare Metadata… to compare two elements (see Compare Code and Metadata).

F&O Studio has no merge tool of its own. VS Code's merge editor works on the XML files.

docs.title: Working with Visual Studio users on the same repository
docs.text:
The repository layout, the .rnrproj format and the metadata are the same in Visual Studio and F&O Studio, so a team can mix both:

  • Projects created in either tool open in the other.
  • F&O Studio saves elements through the same metadata API as Visual Studio, so files written by one are read by the other.
  • Both use the same configuration of the machine (see Visual Studio Side by Side).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Base branch for change marks, Show Changed Elements and the proposed value in Review My Changes.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• F&O Studio does not create, switch, merge or delete branches; use VS Code's Git features or git.
  • No branch policy or pull request integration: policies are set in Azure Repos or GitHub.
  • The deployed-or-not state is per machine and per environment: it only knows deploys run from this machine.

docs.title: Breakpoints and Source Mapping
docs.text: You set X++ breakpoints in the element's code view, the same view you edit in. The debugger, however, binds breakpoints to the source documents recorded in the compiled symbols (PDBs), and those documents are numbered the way the X++ compiler sees the element, not the way the code view shows it. F&O Studio bridges the two: it writes a debug source file per element, copies each code view breakpoint to the matching line of that file, sends it to the debugger under the document name the symbols use, and shows every stop back in the code view. Visual Studio does the same internally with its xppSource: protocol.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Read this page when a breakpoint does not bind, stops on an unexpected line, or when you want to understand what the files in %TEMP%\XppDebugSource are.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A debug session as described on Debugger.
  • The element's code view: click a class in the Application Explorer, or use View Code on a table, form, view, query, map or data entity. See X++ Code View.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the element's code view and set a breakpoint: click in the gutter or press F9 on the line.
  2. Optional: right-click the breakpoint to add a condition, a hit count or a log message (logpoint). They are copied with the breakpoint.
  3. Start the debugger (F&O Studio: Launch Debugger) or, if it is running, keep going: breakpoints you add, change, disable or remove during the session are copied right away.
  4. Hover the breakpoint to see its state:
Breakpoint Meaning Solid red dot Bound: the debugger will stop here Hollow, "Waiting for the symbols to load." Copied, but the module holding the element has no symbols loaded yet. Run the code once (open the form) Hollow, "This element was not prepared for debugging when the session started; restart the debugger." The breakpoint is in a standard element that had no breakpoint when the session started. Restart the debugger Hollow, another message The debugger's own reason (for example no code on that line)
  1. When the debugger stops, VS Code shows the line in the element's code view, the same document you set the breakpoint in (for example PurchTable.xpp), not the debug source copy.

The X++ output channel logs each change of a copy's state, for example Breakpoint axclass_contosoorderservice.xpp:57: bound (the line of the debug source).

docs.title: Element types that can be debugged
docs.text:
Debug sources are written for these element types, the ones the compiler emits as their own source file in the symbols:

Element type Debug source text Class (AxClass) Complete source as the compiler builds it Form (AxForm) Complete source: form methods, then data source classes and control classes Query (AxQuery) Complete source Data entity (AxDataEntityView) Complete source Table (AxTable), view (AxView), map (AxMap) Declaration and methods in the compiler's layout

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Where Key Effect launch.json sourceFileMap Extra path mappings, added to F&O Studio's (yours win on the same key)

There is no setting to change the debug source folder.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The code is in src/debug.ts.

docs.title: Three views of the same element
docs.text:
View Where Used for Code view xpp: document in the editor Editing and setting breakpoints Debug source %TEMP%\XppDebugSource\<model folder>\<axtype>_<name>.xpp (lower case) The text whose line numbers the symbols record Document in the symbols xppSource://Source/<model folder>\<AxType>_<Name>.xpp What the debugger binds breakpoints to

The model folder is the folder name the symbols record: for your model, its folder under the custom metadata folder; for Microsoft's elements, the model's folder in PackagesLocalDirectory (for example Foundation for Application Suite elements). Example: the PurchTable form's document is xppSource://Source/Foundation\AxForm_PurchTable.xpp and its debug source is %TEMP%\XppDebugSource\foundation\axform_purchtable.xpp.

docs.title: Writing debug sources (complete_source)
docs.text:
When a session starts, F&O Studio writes a debug source for every element of the types above in every custom model on the machine, and for each standard element that has a breakpoint (Debugging Standard Code). The text comes from the metadata server's bridge action complete_source, which calls the metadata API's GetCompleteSource() for classes, forms, queries and data entities. That is what the compiler parses: for a form it includes the data source and control classes, which the code view does not show, and methods are separated by a blank line. The PDB line numbers refer to this text, so breakpoints land on the right line. For other types (tables, views, maps) the text is built from the element's declaration and methods in the compiler's layout (compilerView in src/xppSource.ts).

The server side is CompleteSourceJson in MetaModelBridge.ElementDump.cs.

docs.title: Copying breakpoints
docs.text:
For each breakpoint in a code view, F&O Studio:

  1. Finds the element's model folder (from the element's model, or from the standard element's package).
  2. Finds the line of the debug source that holds the same code: the same non-blank text (whitespace normalised) at the same occurrence. The code view adds blank lines and its own layout around the same method bodies, so text matching is more reliable than arithmetic. If the text is not found, it falls back to converting the code view line to the compiler's line numbering (documentLineToCompilerLine).
  3. Adds a breakpoint at that line of the debug source with the same enabled state, condition, hit condition and log message. If a copy with different settings exists, it is replaced. Disabling the code view breakpoint disables the copy, so it does not stop.
  4. Removes copies whose code view breakpoint moved or was removed. F&O Studio remembers which debug source breakpoints are copies (in the workspace state); breakpoints you set on a debug source file yourself are left alone.

Copy passes run one after another, so a change made during a pass is handled by the next one.

code view (xpp:)                 debug source (%TEMP%\XppDebugSource)        symbols
ContosoOrderService.xpp:42  -->  contosoextensions\axclass_contosoorderservice.xpp:57  -->  xppSource://Source/<folder>\AxClass_ContosoOrderService.xpp:57
        ^                                                                               |
        +-------------------- stack frame shown at line 42 of the code view <----------+

docs.title: Sending breakpoints to the debugger
docs.text:
The code view is not a document the debugger knows, so F&O Studio answers setBreakpoints for the code view itself: each code view breakpoint gets the state of its copy (bound or not, and the message). When the debugger later reports that a copy became bound, the code view breakpoint is updated too.

The copies on debug source files go to the debugger. On a UDE the adapter replaces the debug source path with the symbols' document name (xppSource://Source/...) in setBreakpoints, breakpointLocations and source requests; a local path mapped with sourceFileMap does not bind to those documents. The debugger answers with the document name either as is or under its local cache (...\VSDbg\xppSource:\Source\<folder>\<AxType>_<Name>.xpp); both are mapped back to the debug source file.

On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the clr debugger gets a sourceFileMap that maps xppSource:\\Source\ to the debug source folder instead.

On both, the source root that compiled packages can record (e:\source\) also maps to the debug source folder.

docs.title: Showing stops in the code view
docs.text: When the debugger returns a stack trace, each frame in a debug source file is moved to the same line of the element's code view. F&O Studio maps every line of the debug source to the code view line with the same text, in order. Lines the code view does not show (for example a form's data source and control methods) keep pointing at the debug source file, so VS Code opens that file instead. Debug source files are the compiler's view, not code to edit; F&O Studio does not check them.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Debug sources are written when the session starts. Changing code during a session does not update them; build, deploy (on a UDE) and restart the debugger.
  • A breakpoint on a line that has no code in the compiler's view (a blank line, a comment) does not bind.
  • When the same line text appears in a method the code view does not show (forms), the occurrence count can differ; the fallback numbering is used when the text is not found.
  • Writing debug sources for every element of every custom model takes longer for large models.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Breakpoint hollow, "Waiting for the symbols to load." The module that holds the element has not loaded yet, or its symbols are not included Run the code once; for standard code see Debugging Standard Code; check additionalModules "This element was not prepared for debugging when the session started; restart the debugger." Breakpoint added during the session in a standard element Restart the debugger Breakpoint binds but stops one method off or never The environment runs a different build than the code you see Build and deploy, then restart the debugger VS Code opens axform_<name>.xpp instead of the code view The stop is in code the code view does not show (data source or control method) Expected; step on in that file A breakpoint appears in %TEMP%\XppDebugSource you did not set It is the copy of a code view breakpoint Leave it; it is removed with the code view breakpoint
