docs.title: Bridge Protocol
docs.text:
The bridge is how the F&O Studio extension talks to its metadata server. It is JSON-RPC 2.0 over the server's stdin and stdout, one message per line, with F&O Studio's own methods (xpp/bridge, xpp/lang, xpp/data, xpp/trace) next to the MCP methods Copilot uses (initialize, tools/list, tools/call). The xpp/bridge method calls a named action, such as read_object or set_element_property, and returns its JSON result.

This page is for contributors and for people who script the server. Most users never see it.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• Framing: one JSON object per line, UTF-8 without BOM, \n line ends. The server strips \r and \n from every response, so a response is always one line.
  • Direction: the client writes requests to the server's stdin; the server writes responses to stdout. Stderr carries logs (timestamped lines), never protocol.
  • Ids: every request with an id gets exactly one response with the same id. Requests without an id (notifications such as notifications/initialized) get none.
  • Order: responses can arrive out of order. Read-only tool calls, xpp/data and xpp/trace run in parallel; match responses by id.
  • Timeouts: the extension waits 180 seconds per request by default (600 for trace analysis). The server itself does not time out requests.

The extension's client is src/serverClient.ts; the server side is server/McpStdioServer.cs.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as XppVsCode.Server.exe
    C->>S: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}}
    S-->>C: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{...},"instructions":"..."}}
    C->>S: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"xpp/bridge","params":{"action":"find_object","body":{...}}}
    S-->>C: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"success":true,...}}

initialize answers with the protocol version the client asked for (default 2025-06-18), capabilities: { tools: {} }, serverInfo (name: "xpp-vscode") and the agent instructions.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Params Result Notes initialize protocolVersion, clientInfo server info and instructions ping none {} tools/list none { "tools": [ ... ] } definitions from server/Resources/Tools.json tools/call name, arguments { "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": ... }], "isError": bool } some report tools add image content (PNG, base64) xpp/bridge action, body the action's JSON metadata actions, below xpp/lang action, body JSON language features (CodeIntel) xpp/data action, body JSON only with --allow-data; actions test, browse, query, plan, cancel xpp/trace action, body JSON analyze, children, close

Errors use JSON-RPC error objects: -32601 "Method not found" for unknown methods (and for xpp/data without --allow-data), -32602 "Unknown tool", -32603 "Internal error" with the exception message.

docs.title: Request and result
docs.text:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"xpp/bridge","params":{"action":"get_element_properties","body":{"objectType":"AxTable","objectName":"CustGroup","path":["Fields","CustGroup"]}}}

Every action returns an object with at least success (boolean) and, when it fails, message. The other members depend on the action. In TypeScript this is BridgeResult:

export interface BridgeResult {
    success: boolean;
    message?: string;
    [member: string]: any;
}

A failed action is a normal result, not a JSON-RPC error:

{"success":false,"message":"AxClass 'Global' belongs to <model>, which you can't change. Create an extension in your model instead."}

An unknown action returns {"success":false,"message":"Unknown action: <name>"}.

Common body members: objectType (an Ax type such as AxTable, AxClass, AxForm), objectName, modelName, path (designer node path as an array of names), checkOnly.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
src/bridgeContract.ts lists every action as a TypeScript union (BridgeAction, 80 names today). XppServerClient.bridge(action, body) only accepts those names, so a typo fails to compile.

Two checks keep the contract and the server in step:

  • node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js reads the contract, the registrations in MetaModelBridgeServer.RegisterActions and the new MetaModel.BridgeAction(...) registrations in ToolRouter.cs, and every bridge call in src/. It reports actions listed but not served, served but not listed, and used by the extension but not served. npm run test:server and the release build run it.
  • A unit test in test/server checks the same against the running registry.

docs.title: Actions by area
docs.text: Area Actions Elements create_object, read_object, read_object_by_path, update_object, delete_object, duplicate_object, validate_object Discovery find_object, list_objects, find_references, get_model_info, list_models, get_environment, get_object_type_schema, get_form_layout, type_members, dump_element, complete_source Labels read_label, create_label, label_file_entries, save_label, delete_label Project add_to_project, list_project_items, remove_from_project, select_project, project_references, add_reference, remove_reference Tables table_erd, incoming_relations, table_data_shape Build build, best_practice, create_package, sync_tables Analysis analyze_performance, extension_compatibility, wrapper_drift, extension_collisions Reports report_info, get_report_design, set_report_design, render_report, create_precision_design, add_report_data_region, report_datasource_schema, set_report_dataset_query Copilot checkpoints checkpoint_entries, revert_checkpoint Element designer get_form_tree, get_table_fields, get_element_tree, get_element_properties, set_element_property, get_node_types, add_element_node, delete_element_node, rename_element_node, duplicate_element_node, move_element_node, replace_references, drop_on_node, drop_on_property, get_element_method, set_element_method, get_overrides Models get_model, create_model, update_model, list_packages Project packages (.axpp) export_project, inspect_project_package, import_project Cross-reference (no metadata lock) where_used, list_tags, tag_references, label_usage, element_dependencies

docs.title: Registration and dispatch
docs.text:
Each action is registered once in MetaModelBridgeServer.RegisterActions (server/Ported/MetaModel/MetaModelBridgeServer.cs) as a BridgeAction (BridgeActions.cs):

Member Meaning Name the action name in the contract Write WriteKind: Read, Edit, Create or Copy Handler takes the body JSON, returns the result JSON UsesMetadata true by default; false for cross-reference actions, which run without the lock

Registering a name twice throws at startup.

Dispatch(action, body):

flowchart TD
    A["Dispatch(action, body)"] --> B{"registered?"}
    B -- "no" --> U["success:false, Unknown action"]
    B -- "yes" --> L{"UsesMetadata?"}
    L -- "yes" --> K["take the metadata lock"]
    L -- "no" --> R
    K --> R["WriteDenial(kind, body)"]
    R -- "denied" --> D["success:false, message"]
    R -- "allowed" --> H["Handler(body)"]
    H -- "exception" --> E["success:false, message = cause"]
    H --> OK["result JSON"]

docs.title: Write kinds and checks
docs.text:
WriteKind Check before the handler Read none Edit EditDenial(objectType, objectName): an existing element must belong to a custom model. Skipped when checkOnly is true Create TargetModelDenial(modelName): the target model must be a custom model Copy same as Create

In the MCP server process (started with --activity-log), Edit and Create actions also go through the Copilot session: AgentScopeDenial refuses elements outside the scope you set, and BeforeAgentWrite keeps the element's state in the open checkpoint. See Security-Model and Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

Some actions are registered as Read but write non-AOT files (labels, models, project items, .axpp import). They apply their own checks: label writes go only under the custom metadata folder, and label file IDs and languages are validated before any path is built.

Errors are unwrapped (MetaModelBridge.Cause) so messages show the real cause instead of "Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation". The full exception goes to %TEMP%\XppVsCodeBridge.log.

docs.title: Agent tools over the same pipe
docs.text:
tools/call goes to ToolRouter. Many tools delegate to bridge actions (for example xpp_create_object to create_object, xpp_build to build), so the same write checks apply to Copilot. With --activity-log, HandleToolCall snapshots the element before a WritesElement tool runs and appends an entry to activity.jsonl afterwards.

The extension can call agent tools itself with XppServerClient.tool(name, args).

docs.title: Calling the server by hand
docs.text:
Scripts in scripts/ start the server with a configuration and send one request. Always use them with a timeout; never leave a stdio session waiting.

node scripts/bridge-call.js <exe> <config.json> find_object "{\"objectName\":\"CustGroup\",\"objectType\":\"AxTable\",\"exactMatch\":true}"
node scripts/tool-call.js <exe> <config.json> xpp_read_object "{\"objectType\":\"AxClass\",\"objectName\":\"SalesFormLetter\",\"methodNames\":[\"construct\"]}"

<exe> is server\bin\XppVsCode.Server.exe; <config.json> is an XPPConfig file. bridge-call.js takes an optional maxChars; tool-call.js takes outBase (where images are saved) and maxChars.

docs.title: Adding an action
docs.text:
1. Add the handler to the right service (see the roles in Metadata-Server).
  2. Register it in RegisterActions with the correct WriteKind. A write action registered as Read would skip the ownership check.
  3. Add the name to BridgeActions in src/bridgeContract.ts.
  4. Run node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js and npm run test:server.
  5. If behaviour of existing actions must not change, run the golden master before and after (see Testing-the-Extension).

docs.title: Browse Table Data
docs.text: Browse Table Data shows the rows of one table in an editor tab, the way a developer needs them: field labels, enum names next to their numbers, a company filter, an as-of date for date-effective tables, column filters, sorting, CSV export, and a record inspector that follows the table's relations to related rows. It is the F&O Studio counterpart of Visual Studio's "Open table browser", but it reads the database directly and needs no web client.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Check the setup a company has (for example CustGroup or VendGroup rows in usmf).
  • Confirm what your code wrote after a test run.
  • Follow a record to its related records: a CustTable row to its CustGroup, a SalesTable row to its customer.
  • Grab a row as JSON, or a WHERE clause for a query, while you investigate.

To open the web client's table browser instead, use Open Table Browser (see Copy Name and Open in Browser).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Database access for the active environment: the local AxDB on a cloud-hosted or VHD machine, or JIT credentials on a unified developer environment. See Database Access. If a UDE has no credentials yet, the tab asks in a modal dialog when it opens.
  • The table must be in the metadata (F&O Studio reads labels, enums and relations from it) and in the database (synchronized). Temporary tables (TempDB, InMemory) have no rows to browse.

docs.title: Open a table
docs.text:
Any of these opens a tab named <Table> [Data]:

  • Application Explorer or the project view: right-click a table and choose Browse Table Data.
  • Element designer: right-click in the designer of a table and choose Browse Table Data.
  • Code view hover: hover a table name in X++ code and click Browse data. See Hover.
  • Dynamics 365 view: Data > Browse Table Data…, then pick the table.
  • Command Palette: F&O Studio: Browse Table Data, then pick the table.
  • Database menu (status bar): Browse Table Data….

If you run it on a table extension (for example CustTable.ContosoExtension), the base table opens.

The first 200 rows load immediately. The panel's tabs come back after a window reload.

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text: Control What it does Title The table name, and its label when it differs, for example CustGroup (Customer group) Company Shown for tables saved per company. Type a company ID (for example usmf) and press Enter or leave the box; empty (placeholder all) means all companies. The value is compared lower case against DATAAREAID. As of Shown for date-effective tables (valid time state other than None). Pick a date to see only the rows valid on that date; clear it to see all rows. Rows 100, 200 (default), 500, 1000 or 5000 rows. Applies on the next refresh. Filter editor A column, an operator and a value, then Add filter (or Enter in the value box) Refresh Loads the rows again with the current filters Cancel Stops a running load Open as SQL Opens the current view as an editable query in a new SQL Query Panel Target (right) The database and server, and the credential role on a UDE, for example AxDB on localhost

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The column list holds the table's fields from the metadata (including fields added by table extensions). Operators: =, <>, <, <=, >, >=, contains and startsWith. Each filter shows as a chip under the toolbar, for example CustGroup = 10; click its × to remove it. All filters are combined with AND. Every change reloads the rows.

Values are compared as SQL sees them: enum fields hold integers (filter SalesStatus = 3, not the name), dates compare as SQL dates.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: Click a column header (or focus it and press Enter or Space) to sort by it. Click again to switch between ascending and descending. The sorted column shows an arrow. Sorting runs in the database, so it covers all rows, not only the loaded ones.

docs.title: Reading the grid
docs.text:
• Enum fields show the value's name followed by the number in brackets, for example Invoiced (3). The tooltip shows SalesStatus::Invoiced. The enum is found directly on the field or through its extended data type chain.
  • Values added by enum extensions stay as numbers. Their tooltip explains that the number is assigned per environment, so F&O Studio does not guess the name.
  • Column header tooltips show the field's label and its enum type or SQL type.
  • NULL is shown for missing values; numbers are right-aligned.
  • Double-click a cell to copy its value.
  • RecId and other 64-bit values come back as text, so they are exact.
  • The result header shows the row count, with + and "(limit reached)" when there are more rows than the limit. Export CSV saves the loaded rows.

Columns come from the database (SELECT *), labels from your local metadata. A field you added but have not deployed and synchronized yet has no column in the grid.

docs.title: The record inspector
docs.text:
Click a row (or select it and press Enter) to show all of its fields in the panel next to the grid.

  • Row n of m with previous and next buttons; the Up and Down arrow keys in the grid move the selection too.
  • A Field search box filters the list by field name or label.
  • Each field shows its value, with the enum name in brackets for enum fields, for example 3 (Invoiced).
  • Relation links. For each relation of the table that uses the field, a link → <RelatedTable> opens a new Browse tab on the related table, filtered on the relation's fields and on the row's company. On a CustTable row, for example, the customer group field links to CustGroup. Links are left out when the value is empty or 0.
  • Copy as JSON copies the row as a JSON object (column name to value).
  • Copy WHERE clause copies a clause on the row's keys, for example WHERE RECID = '5637144576' AND DATAAREAID = 'usmf'.

Only relations with field constraints are followed (the same relations the Entity Relationship Diagram shows). Fixed-value constraints do not become filters.

docs.title: Export CSV
docs.text: Export CSV asks where to save and proposes <Table>.csv. The file holds the loaded rows (not the whole table), RFC 4180 quoted, with the column names as the header row.

docs.title: Open as SQL
docs.text:
Open as SQL writes the current view as SQL and opens it in a new query tab, for example:

SELECT TOP (200) *
FROM [CustGroup]
WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
  AND [PaymTermId] = 'Net30'
ORDER BY [CUSTGROUP]

From there you can change the column list, add joins or run Explain Plan.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Browse Table Data has no settings of its own. Database access settings are on Database Access.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The extension opens a webview tab (src/database/dataPanel.ts, media/dataPanel.js).
  2. It asks the metadata server for the table's shape with the bridge action table_data_shape (TableDataShapeService.cs): label, table type, whether data is saved per company, the valid time state, the effective fields (table extensions included) with labels and enum types, and each enum's values and whether it is extensible.
  3. If the table type is TempDB or InMemory, the tab stops with a message.
  4. It reads the table's relations with the bridge action table_erd and keeps those with field constraints for the inspector.
  5. It sends a browse request to the data service (xpp/data) with the table, filters, company, as-of date, sort and row limit, and the connection.
  6. The server (DataQueryService.cs) reads the table's columns from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS and builds the statement itself:
  7. column names are checked against that list and quoted; an unknown column fails with "Table X has no column Y.";
  8. every value is a SQL parameter; contains and startsWith become LIKE with %, _ and [ escaped;
  9. the company filter applies only when the table has a DATAAREAID column;
  10. the as-of date applies only when the table has VALIDFROM and VALIDTO, as VALIDFROM <= @date AND VALIDTO >= @date, the rows X++ validtimestate(date) selects;
  11. SELECT TOP (limit + 1) tells whether there are more rows.
  12. The statement runs in a transaction that is rolled back, like every read. See Database Access.

Business data never passes through the MCP server; the tab uses the extension's own server process.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One table per tab, no joins. Use Open as SQL for joins and computed columns.
  • Read-only. Changing rows needs the SQL Query Panel with Allow changes.
  • Filters on enum fields take the number, not the name.
  • Rows beyond the limit are not loaded; raise the limit or add filters. Export CSV writes the loaded rows only.
  • Labels and relations come from your local metadata; if it differs from the environment's application, they can differ from what the database holds.
  • Values added by enum extensions show as numbers.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Table X not found." The table is not in your metadata Check the name; open it from Application Explorer "X is a temporary table (TempDB); its rows exist only while code runs." Temporary tables have no stored rows Debug the code that fills it instead "Table X is not in the database. Is it synchronized (or a temporary table)?" The table was never synchronized on this environment Deploy and run Synchronize Database "Table X has no column Y." A filter or sort column exists in metadata but not in the database Deploy and synchronize your changes "No database access. Request credentials with F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials, then run again." You declined the credentials dialog on a UDE Run Request Database Credentials Company box missing The table is not saved per company Nothing to do No rows for a company that has data Company IDs are compared lower case against DATAAREAID Check the company ID

docs.title: Build Automation and Pipelines
docs.text: D365FO teams build their code twice: on each developer's machine while they work, and in an automated pipeline that produces the deployable package for sandbox and production. F&O Studio covers the first part completely (build, label and report compilation, best practice checks, build tasks you can chain). It does not define or run pipelines: the automated build is general D365FO practice with Azure Pipelines and Microsoft's X++ build NuGet packages. This page explains both, how they fit together, and what you can automate inside VS Code.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You set up the team's build pipeline and want to know what F&O Studio projects need in it.
  • You want to automate the local build-deploy-test loop with VS Code tasks.
  • You want to know why a change builds on your machine but fails in the pipeline (or the other way round).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• For local builds: an active D365FO configuration and your models in its custom metadata folder (see Build Project and Model).
  • For a pipeline (general practice): an Azure DevOps organization with the Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations Tools extension, an Azure Artifacts feed with Microsoft's X++ build NuGet packages, and the repository holding your Metadata folder and a Visual Studio solution or projects.

docs.title: Part 1: what F&O Studio builds on the developer machine
docs.text:
Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view or on a .rnrproj) and Build Model build one package with Microsoft's command-line tools from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin, the same tools Visual Studio's build calls:

Step Tool Output C# projects and assemblies the X++ project references MSBuild (xpp.build.msbuildPath, or Visual Studio's / Build Tools' MSBuild, else dotnet msbuild) Copied into the package bin folder Labels LabelC.exe <Package>\Resources X++ xppc.exe <Package>\bin\Dynamics.AX.<Package>.dll, netmodules, PDBs; log in <Package>\BuildLogs Reports reportsc.exe <Package>\Reports Portable PDBs (for the UDE debugger) Pdb2Pdb In <Package>\bin

With xpp.build.crossReference on (the default) xppc also updates the cross-reference database. With xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules it runs AppChecker rules. Errors go to the Problems view. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, xpp.build.restartLocalAos restarts the running AOS hosts after a successful build.

Run Best Practice Checks on Project runs xppbp.exe. Both are described in Build Project and Model and Best Practice Checks.

docs.title: Automating the local loop with tasks
docs.text:
F&O Studio provides VS Code tasks of type xpp, so you can chain build, deploy and database sync, or bind them to keys. They run the same code as the commands:

action Other properties What it does buildProject Builds the open project's model and reports only the project's problems. buildModel model (default: the project's model) Builds the whole model. deploy dbSync: None, Module or Full (any other value, such as Incremental, means Module) Deploys the package of the project's model to the selected UDE, without prompts. syncDatabase mode: Full or Module; modules: comma-separated (default: the project's model) Database sync on the UDE (on cloud-hosted/VHD: a full local sync).

Example tasks.json that builds and then deploys with a module sync:

{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "Build ContosoExtensions",
      "type": "xpp",
      "action": "buildModel",
      "model": "ContosoExtensions"
    },
    {
      "label": "Build and deploy",
      "type": "xpp",
      "action": "deploy",
      "dbSync": "Module",
      "dependsOn": "Build ContosoExtensions"
    }
  ]
}

A failed build ends the task with exit code 1, so dependent tasks do not run. More in Build Tasks.

docs.title: Part 2: the automated build pipeline (general D365FO practice)
docs.text:
Microsoft documents two ways to build X++ in Azure Pipelines: a build VM, or Microsoft-hosted agents with NuGet packages. The hosted approach needs these packages, downloaded from the Shared Asset Library in Lifecycle Services and published to your Azure Artifacts feed:

NuGet package Contents Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Platform.CompilerPackage The X++ compiler and build tools Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Platform.DevALM.BuildXpp Platform reference binaries Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Application1.DevALM.BuildXpp Application references, part 1 Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Application2.DevALM.BuildXpp Application references, part 2 Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.DevALM.BuildXpp Application Suite references

A typical pipeline:

  1. Restore the NuGet packages (a packages.config and nuget.config in the repository, -ExcludeVersion so paths stay stable).
  2. Optionally update the model versions (task Update Model Version).
  3. Build the solution or projects with MSBuild, pointing /p:BuildTasksDirectory, /p:MetadataDirectory, /p:FrameworkDirectory, /p:ReferenceFolder, /p:OutputDirectory and related arguments at the restored packages and the repository's Metadata folder.
  4. Install NuGet 3.3.0 or earlier (required by the packaging task).
  5. Create the deployable package (task Create Deployable Package, version 3 can also create a Power Platform unified package for unified environments).
  6. Publish the package as a pipeline artifact for release.

Microsoft's documentation, which is the reference for this part:

  • Build automation that uses Microsoft-hosted agents and Azure Pipelines
  • Create deployable packages in Azure Pipelines
  • Tutorial: Set up a nightly build pipeline for finance and operations apps
  • Continuous integration and deployment for the unified developer experience

docs.title: What the pipeline needs from an F&O Studio project
docs.text:
• The projects. A project created with Create D365FO Project… is the same MSBuild file Visual Studio writes: it sets <Model>, imports Microsoft.Dynamics.Framework.Tools.BuildTasks.17.0.targets from $(BuildTasksDirectory), and writes a .slnx solution next to it. The pipeline overrides BuildTasksDirectory with the NuGet package path, as it does for Visual Studio projects.
  • Every element in the repository. The pipeline compiles what is committed. An element created on your machine but not committed builds locally and fails in the pipeline. Show Changed Elements lists uncommitted elements.
  • Matching versions. The NuGet packages must match the application version your developers build against. F&O Studio's version drift guard warns when the environment runs a newer application version than the metadata on the machine (see Version Drift Guard); update the pipeline's packages at the same time.
  • Referenced C# projects in the solution, so MSBuild builds them before the X++ projects.

docs.title: What F&O Studio does and does not do for the pipeline
docs.text: Pipeline step F&O Studio Define, edit or run a pipeline No Restore the X++ NuGet packages No Build in the pipeline No; the pipeline uses MSBuild and Microsoft's targets Show pipeline runs Open Pipelines opens the Azure Pipelines list or the GitHub Actions page in the browser Same compiler as the pipeline Yes: xppc from your environment's PackagesLocalDirectory\bin (the pipeline's comes from the NuGet package; keep versions aligned) Deployable package without a pipeline Create Deployment Package… runs Microsoft's RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 locally (see Create Deployment Package)

docs.title: An example of a CI build that uses the compiler package
docs.text: F&O Studio's own release workflow, .github/workflows/release.yml, restores Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Platform.CompilerPackage from a private GitHub Packages feed with nuget install ... -ExcludeVersion and compiles F&O Studio's server against it on a windows-latest runner. It builds the extension, not X++ models, but it shows the pattern: the Microsoft package comes from a private feed at build time and is never committed or shipped.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Update the cross-reference database while building. xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules false Run AppChecker rules during the build. xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Save unsaved X++ code views before a build. xpp.build.restartLocalAos true Cloud-hosted and VHD: restart the running AOS hosts after a successful build. xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild for the C# projects the X++ project references.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Local build: src/build.ts runs LabelC, xppc and reportsc with the paths of the active configuration; diagnostics are read from the tools' XML logs in BuildLogs.
  • Tasks: src/tasks.ts registers the xpp task type with custom executions that call the builder and the deploy code.
  • Pipelines link: src/devops.ts (openPipelines).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No pipeline templates, YAML generation or pipeline runs.
  • F&O Studio's build does not call MSBuild on the .rnrproj for X++; it calls xppc directly. Pipeline-only MSBuild properties in the project are not used by the local build.
  • xppc always compiles the whole package; Build Project only limits which problems are reported.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Builds locally, fails in the pipeline with a missing element The element is not committed. Run Show Changed Elements, commit the added elements. Fails in the pipeline with an unknown standard method or field The pipeline's NuGet packages are older than your environment's application version. Update the packages in the feed and in packages.config. Builds in the pipeline, fails locally The machine's metadata is older than the pipeline's packages. Update the environment's metadata (see Version Drift Guard). xpp task fails with "Open a D365FO project or set "model" in the task." No project is open and the task has no model. Open the project or add "model".

docs.title: Build Project and Model
docs.text: F&O Studio compiles your X++ models with the same Microsoft tools Visual Studio uses: LabelC for label files, xppc for X++ code and reportsc for SSRS reports. Build Project reports only the problems of the elements in your D365FO project; Build Model reports the problems of the whole model. Errors and warnings go to the Problems view at the right line of the element's code view. This is the equivalent of Visual Studio's Build and Dynamics 365 > Build models.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After you change code or metadata, to check that the model compiles before you test, debug or deploy.
  • Before you deploy to a unified developer environment (UDE): deploy uploads the package as built on this machine, so an old build means old code on the environment.
  • On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, to get the new code into the local AOS (the build restarts the running AOS hosts).
  • To refresh the cross-reference database so that Find All References includes your code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active environment configuration (see Select Environment or Connect to Environment). The build reads the compiler, the reference packages and the custom metadata folder from it.
  • The model must be one of your own models, in the custom metadata folder of the configuration. Standard models cannot be built: the build stops with "Model '...' is not in your custom metadata folder (...). Only your own models can be built."
  • For Build Project, an open D365FO project (.rnrproj); see D365FO Projects.
  • Cloud-hosted or VHD environment: run VS Code as administrator, as you would run Visual Studio, because the build writes into PackagesLocalDirectory. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.
  • If your X++ project references C# projects or assemblies, MSBuild must be available (Visual Studio, the Build Tools, or the .NET SDK). See Solution View and C# References.

docs.title: Build Project
docs.text:
1. Open your D365FO project.
  2. Start the build in one of these ways:
  3. press Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view or with a .rnrproj file active;
  4. click the project item in the status bar (see Status Bar);
  5. click Build Project (wrench icon) in the title bar of the D365FO Project view;
  6. click Build and check > Build Project in the Dynamics 365 view;
  7. run F&O Studio: Build Project from the command palette.
  8. A notification shows "Building project …". Click Cancel on it to stop the compiler.
  9. When the build succeeds, the status bar shows "Build succeeded" with the number of warnings for 10 seconds.
  10. When it fails, a message says "Build failed: N error(s), M warning(s) in ." with two buttons:
  11. Show Problems opens the Problems view;
  12. Show Output opens the X++ Build output with the full compiler log.

    13. If no project is open, Build Project builds a model instead (see below).

docs.title: Build Model
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Build Model from the command palette, click Build and check > Build Models… in the Dynamics 365 view, or use the build icon in the title bar of the Application Explorer view.
  2. With a project open, F&O Studio builds the project's model. Without a project, a picker titled Model to build lists the packages in your custom metadata folder; pick one.
  3. The progress, result message and Problems view work as for Build Project, but every diagnostic of the model is reported.

docs.title: Project build versus model build
docs.text:
Build Project Build Model What xppc compiles The whole package of the project's model The whole package What reaches the Problems view Diagnostics of the project's elements (and fatal errors) Every diagnostic of the package Count in the result message Errors and warnings of the project's elements All errors and warnings Success Only when the whole package compiles without errors Same

xppc always compiles the whole package. A project build only filters what it reports. If an element outside your project has an error, Build Project fails even though the Problems view shows nothing for your project; run Build Model to see that error.

docs.title: What you see in the X++ Build output
docs.text:
Every step writes the command line it runs and the tool's output to the X++ Build output channel, for example:

=== Build ContosoExtensions (10:42:13) ===
> LabelC.exe -metadata=... -output=...\ContosoExtensions\Resources -modelmodule=ContosoExtensions -names=ContosoLabels_en-US
> xppc.exe -metadata=... -compilermetadata=... -modelmodule=ContosoExtensions -output=...\ContosoExtensions\bin ...
Warning: dynamics://Class/ContosoOrderStatusHelper/Method/run(12,9): ...
Converted 1 PDB(s) to portable PDBs for debugging in VS Code.
=== ContosoExtensions (project items): BUILD SUCCEEDED - 0 error(s), 3 warning(s) ===

docs.title: Save before build
docs.text: By default, unsaved X++ code views are saved before the build starts, so the compiler sees your latest code (xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild). Unsaved code would otherwise be compiled from the metadata on disk.

docs.title: Build after every save
docs.text: The setting xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave (off by default, marked "Slow") runs Build Project after you save X++ code, so semantic errors reach the Problems view without a manual build. It costs about 10 seconds per save.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Save unsaved X++ code views before a build. xpp.build.crossReference true Pass -xref to xppc so the cross-reference database is updated and where-used includes your code. Only used when the configuration names a cross-reference server and database. xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules false Pass -RunAppcheckerRules to xppc. xpp.build.restartLocalAos true Cloud-hosted and VHD: restart the running AOS hosts after a successful build. Not used on UDEs. xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild.exe for the C# projects and assemblies your X++ project references. Empty: Visual Studio's or the Build Tools' MSBuild, else the .NET SDK's (dotnet msbuild). xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave false Build the project after each save of X++ code.

See Settings Reference for all settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The build is implemented in src/build.ts (XppBuilder.build). The commands are registered in src/extension.ts. Every step runs on your machine; nothing is sent to the environment.

docs.title: 1. Find the package
docs.text: A model lives in a package (a folder in the custom metadata folder). The package can have a different name than the model: F&O Studio looks for <package>\Descriptor\<model>.xml to find it. Build logs go to <package>\BuildLogs.

docs.title: 2. C# references
docs.text:
If the open project belongs to the package being built and the .rnrproj has project references, assembly references or files marked Copy to Output Directory, F&O Studio runs MSBuild on the .rnrproj first, as Visual Studio does (src/dotnetReferences.ts):

  • Visual Studio's build tasks (imported through $(BuildTasksDirectory)) are replaced by empty stand-ins, and a target that only resolves the references is added.
  • The referenced C# projects are built; their assemblies, dependencies, PDB and XML files, satellite assemblies and Copy to Output Directory files are copied into <package>\bin.
  • Finance and Operations' own assemblies (anything in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin, or named Dynamics.AX.*) are never copied; the output says "reference it with Copy Local = False".

If this step fails, the build stops with "BUILD FAILED (the projects and assemblies the X++ project references)".

docs.title: 3. Labels (LabelC)
docs.text:
If any model of the package has label files, LabelC compiles them into <package>\Resources:

LabelC.exe -metadata=<custom metadata folder> -output=<package>\Resources -modelmodule=<package> -names=<Id_language,...>

The names carry their language suffix (for example ContosoLabels_en-US,ContosoLabels_de), as LabelC expects.

docs.title: 4. X++ (xppc)
docs.text:
xppc.exe -metadata=<custom metadata folder>
         -compilermetadata=<RuntimePackagesDirectory, else FrameworkDirectory>
         -modelmodule=<package>
         -output=<package>\bin
         -xmllog=<package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppc.xml
         -log=<package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppc.log
         -appBase=<PackagesLocalDirectory>\bin -refPath=<PackagesLocalDirectory>\bin
         -referenceFolder=<each reference package path> -referenceFolder=<custom metadata folder>
         [-xref -xrefSqlServer=<server> -xrefDbName=<database>]
         [-RunAppcheckerRules]

A build counts as successful only when xppc exits with 0, the XML log has no error or fatal diagnostic, and Dynamics.AX.<package>.dll was written by this build. Otherwise the result line says why, for example "(xppc exited with an error)" or "(no assembly was produced)". The XML log is turned into Problems entries; see Compiler Diagnostics.

docs.title: 5. Reports (reportsc)
docs.text:
After a successful X++ compile, the package's reports are compiled to <package>\Reports\*.rdl, which the AOS reads at run time (src/reports/reportCompiler.ts):

reportsc.exe -metadata=<root> -modelmodule=<package> -name=<Report1,Report2,...> -output=<package>\Reports
             -LabelsPath=<root> -log=...\Dynamics.AX.<package>.reportsc.log -xmllog=...\Dynamics.AX.<package>.reportsc.xml
  • reportsc reads one metadata root, so standard and custom packages must sit side by side. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments (one shared folder) that is the custom metadata folder itself. Otherwise F&O Studio keeps a folder of junctions to every package under %LOCALAPPDATA%\FOStudio\ReportMetadata\<configuration>.
  • Reports are always passed by name; without -name reportsc would first delete every .rdl in the output folder.
  • Compiled .rdl files of reports that are no longer in the package are removed.
  • Report errors make the build fail ("(report compilation)"). Packages without reports skip this step.

See Report Build.

docs.title: 6. Portable PDBs
docs.text: xppc writes Windows PDBs; the VS Code debugger reads only portable PDBs. After a successful build, every Windows PDB in <package>\bin is converted in place with Microsoft's Pdb2Pdb, which ships with the extension. A conversion problem does not fail the build; it writes a warning to the output. See Debugger.

docs.title: 7. Cloud-hosted and VHD: restart the AOS
docs.text:
On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the AOS keeps running the old assemblies. After a successful build, as Visual Studio does, F&O Studio restarts the hosts that are running: IIS Express (stopped and started with its own command line), the AOS application pool in IIS (recycled) and the batch service (DynamicsAxBatch). Hosts that are not running are left alone. If a debug session is attached, it is detached first; start debugging again once the AOS is back. Batch tasks running at that moment are cut off. Turn this off with xpp.build.restartLocalAos.

UDEs run the code that was last deployed, so nothing restarts; deploy instead (see Deploy to Environment).

docs.title: 8. After the build
docs.text: The result (model, success, errors, warnings, project or model scope, time) updates the project item in the status bar and the built-versus-deployed state used by Status Bar, Run Tests and the debugger.

docs.title: Builds by Copilot
docs.text:
The agent tool xpp_build runs the same steps in the metadata server (server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs, C# references in server/Host/ProjectReferences.cs). It accepts modelName, scope (model or project) and syncDatabase, and returns "BUILD SUCCEEDED" or "BUILD FAILED" with up to 80 diagnostics. Differences from the commands:

  • it does not pass -RunAppcheckerRules and always adds -xref when the configuration names a cross-reference database;
  • it does not convert PDBs or restart the AOS;
  • its result goes to the agent, not to the Problems view, and it does not update the status bar or the deploy state.

See Agent Tools: Build and Data.

docs.title: Other places that build
docs.text:
• Build Tasks (tasks.json).
  • Pre-Deploy Checklist builds the project first.
  • Open Team Repository builds linked packages in dependency order.
  • Run Snippet builds the project before it runs.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only models in the custom metadata folder can be built.
  • xppc always compiles the whole package, so a project build takes as long as a model build.
  • Builds are one model at a time. There is no "build all models with dependencies" command; build models in dependency order yourself (or use Open Team Repository for linked packages).
  • On a UDE, a build does not change what runs on the environment until you deploy.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Model '...' is not in your custom metadata folder" The model is a standard model or lives in another configuration. Select the right environment, or create your own model. "Build failed: 0 error(s)" after Build Project An element outside the project has an error; the project build hides it. Run Build Model to see all errors. "BUILD FAILED (xppc exited with an error)" with no diagnostics xppc crashed or could not start. Open Show Output and read the xppc log in <package>\BuildLogs. "(no assembly was produced)" xppc wrote no new Dynamics.AX.<package>.dll, often because the file is locked. On cloud-hosted/VHD, check that VS Code runs as administrator and the AOS is not locking the file. "Label compilation failed." LabelC returned an error. Read the LabelC output in X++ Build; check the label files of the model. "BUILD FAILED (the projects and assemblies the X++ project references)" MSBuild failed on a referenced C# project. Read the MSBuild output; set xpp.build.msbuildPath if the .NET SDK's MSBuild cannot build the project. "BUILD FAILED (report compilation)" reportsc reported errors. The errors are listed in X++ Build; see Report Build. "Warning: ... was not converted to a portable PDB" Pdb2Pdb could not convert a file. The build still succeeded; the VS Code debugger cannot use that PDB. "Warning: the AOS may still run the previous build until it is restarted." One restart step failed (cloud-hosted/VHD). Restart IIS or IIS Express and the batch service yourself.

docs.title: Build Tasks
docs.text: F&O Studio contributes a task type xpp for VS Code's tasks.json. Its four actions build the project, build a model, deploy to a unified developer environment and synchronize the database. Tasks run the same code as the commands, so you can chain them with your own tasks (dependsOn), run them with Tasks: Run Build Task, and bind them to keys. Visual Studio has no direct equivalent; this is how you automate the build-deploy-sync loop inside VS Code.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want one key or one command that builds, then deploys, then synchronizes.
  • You want to run a script (for example a data reset or a test run) after a successful build.
  • You want Run Build Task (Ctrl+Shift+B outside X++ editors) to build your X++ project.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An open D365FO project for buildProject and deploy, and for syncDatabase with mode: Module when the task sets no modules. buildModel needs either a project or a model in the task.
  • deploy and the Dataverse syncDatabase need a unified developer environment that you selected and signed in to (see Connect to Environment and Sign In and Authentication).
  • On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, syncDatabase runs SyncEngine locally and needs VS Code running as administrator.

docs.title: Run a contributed task without tasks.json
docs.text:
1. Run Tasks: Run Task from the command palette.
  2. Pick F&O Studio. Four tasks are listed:
  3. Build project (action: buildProject)
  4. Build model (action: buildModel)
  5. Deploy models (action: deploy, dbSync: Incremental, which runs a Module sync)
  6. Synchronize database (action: syncDatabase, mode: Module)
  7. The task opens a terminal that shows short status lines. The compiler output still goes to the X++ Build output, deploy and sync output to X++ Deploy.

The two build tasks are in the Build group, so Tasks: Run Build Task lists them.

docs.title: Define tasks in tasks.json
docs.text:
Add tasks of type xpp to .vscode/tasks.json. Every task needs type, action and a label:

{
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "tasks": [
        {
            "label": "X++: build project",
            "type": "xpp",
            "action": "buildProject",
            "group": { "kind": "build", "isDefault": true },
            "problemMatcher": []
        },
        {
            "label": "X++: build ContosoExtensions",
            "type": "xpp",
            "action": "buildModel",
            "model": "ContosoExtensions",
            "problemMatcher": []
        },
        {
            "label": "X++: deploy with module sync",
            "type": "xpp",
            "action": "deploy",
            "dbSync": "Module",
            "problemMatcher": []
        },
        {
            "label": "X++: sync module",
            "type": "xpp",
            "action": "syncDatabase",
            "mode": "Module",
            "modules": "ContosoExtensions",
            "problemMatcher": []
        }
    ]
}

No problem matcher is needed: build errors go to the Problems view directly (see Compiler Diagnostics).

docs.title: Chain build and deploy
docs.text:
{
    "label": "X++: build and deploy",
    "dependsOn": ["X++: build project", "X++: deploy with module sync"],
    "dependsOrder": "sequence",
    "problemMatcher": []
}

A failed build ends its task with exit code 1, so VS Code does not start the next task in the sequence.

docs.title: Bind a task to a key
docs.text:
In keybindings.json:

{
    "key": "ctrl+alt+d",
    "command": "workbench.action.tasks.runTask",
    "args": "X++: build and deploy"
}

Note: Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view (or with a .rnrproj file active) is bound to F&O Studio's Build Project command, not to the default build task. Elsewhere it runs VS Code's Run Build Task.

docs.title: Task properties
docs.text:
Property Used by Values Default Effect action all buildProject, buildModel, deploy, syncDatabase required What the task does. model buildProject, buildModel model name the active project's model Model to build. dbSync deploy None, Module, Full None Database sync after the deploy. Module synchronizes the deployed package. mode syncDatabase Full, Module Full Sync kind on a unified environment. modules syncDatabase with mode: Module comma-separated module names the active project's model Modules to synchronize.

Notes:

  • dbSync: "Incremental" is still accepted and runs a Module sync. (It needed an argument file when deploy went through pac.) Any value other than None and Full is treated as Module.
  • The contributed Deploy models task uses Incremental, so it runs a Module sync.

docs.title: buildProject
docs.text: Builds the active project's model and reports only the problems of the project's elements, exactly as Build Project (see Build Project and Model). Without a project it fails with "Open a D365FO project or set "model" in the task." (no model set) or "Open a D365FO project first." (model set). The terminal says "Building project … (compiler output: X++ Build)", then "Build succeeded." or "Build failed; see the Problems view." Closing the terminal cancels the build.

docs.title: buildModel
docs.text: Builds model (or the project's model) and reports every problem of the package. Fails with "Open a D365FO project or set "model" in the task." when neither is available.

docs.title: deploy
docs.text:
Deploys the package of the active project's model, as built on this machine, to the selected unified environment, without the package and sync pickers that Deploy Models to Environment shows. See Deploy to Environment.

  • The project's package must have been built: otherwise "The package of has not been built."
  • Without a project: "Open a D365FO project first: the task deploys the package of its model."
  • On success the terminal says "Deployed ." and the deploy is recorded, so the status bar no longer shows the build as newer than the deploy.
  • On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment nothing is deployed: an information message explains that the models run on the local AOS once built, and the terminal says "Nothing was deployed."

docs.title: syncDatabase
docs.text:
• Unified environment: starts a Full or Module database sync through Dataverse, as Synchronize Database does. See Synchronize Database.
  • Cloud-hosted or VHD: runs SyncEngine with a full sync of the local business database in a separate task terminal named "Synchronize database". mode and modules are not used there.

The terminal ends with "Database synchronization finished." or "Failed: ".

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/tasks.ts registers a TaskProvider for type xpp (the schema is contributes.taskDefinitions in package.json). Each task is a CustomExecution with a pseudo-terminal:

  • BuildTerminal calls the same XppBuilder.build as the commands (src/build.ts), passing the project's items for buildProject, and exits with 0 or 1.
  • DeployTerminal calls the same deploy and sync code as the commands (src/pac.ts, which uses core/src/deploy.ts). Passing dbSync, mode or modules skips the questions the commands ask.

Because the tasks run inside the extension, they need the VS Code window: they cannot run on a build server. For pipelines, see Build Automation and Pipelines.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• deploy deploys only the active project's package. To deploy several packages, use Deploy Models to Environment.
  • Closing a deploy or sync task's terminal does not stop the job on the environment.
  • Tasks run in VS Code only; they are not a command-line build.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Open a D365FO project first." or "Open a D365FO project or set "model" in the task." buildProject and deploy need the active project; buildModel needs a project or model. Open the project, or set model. "The package of has not been built." deploy found no bin\Dynamics.AX.<package>.dll. Run the build task first (dependsOn). "Nothing was deployed." Cloud-hosted or VHD environment. Nothing to do: the build already updated the local AOS. syncDatabase fails on a VM with SyncEngine exit code SyncEngine needs administrator rights. Run VS Code as administrator. The task is not listed under Run Build Task Only the two build actions are in the Build group. Add "group": "build" to your own task definition.

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
This page explains how to build F&O Studio from its GitHub repository, run it in a development host, and package a local VSIX for testing. It is for contributors and for anyone who wants to check what the extension does by building it themselves.

You do not need this to use F&O Studio: install it from the Visual Studio Marketplace (see Getting-Started).

docs.title: What gets built
docs.text:
Output From Tool core/dist/ core/src (@fno-studio/core) tsc -p core out/ src/ (the extension) tsc -p . server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe (+ .config) server/ (.NET Framework 4.8, x64) dotnet build through scripts/build-server.ps1 tools/pdb2pdb/ Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Pdb2Pdb (MIT), downloaded scripts/fetch-pdb2pdb.ps1 xpp-vscode-<version>.vsix all of the above vsce package

All of these are in .gitignore; the repository holds only sources.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Windows. The server targets .NET Framework 4.8 x64 and the extension only runs on Windows.
  • Node.js 20 or later (core requires >=20; the release workflow uses Node 22) and npm.
  • .NET SDK with dotnet build and dotnet test. The server project uses Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies, so you do not need a .NET Framework developer pack.
  • A Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations installation whose PackagesLocalDirectory\bin contains xppc.exe and Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Metadata.dll. Any of these works:
  • a unified developer environment connected with Connect to Environment… (installed F&O Studio, or Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools);
  • a cloud-hosted or VHD environment;
  • any folder with those files, given in the environment variable XPP_BIN.
  • Git to clone https://github.com/nazmolla/xpp-vscode.git.
  • Optional: MSBuild (Visual Studio or Build Tools) for the C# reference tests.

The server compiles against Microsoft's assemblies but never copies them: every reference to them has <Private>false</Private>. At run time the server loads them from the installation of whoever runs it.

docs.title: How to build
docs.text:
1. Clone and install the development dependencies:
git clone https://github.com/nazmolla/xpp-vscode.git
cd xpp-vscode
npm install

The extension has no runtime npm dependencies; npm install gets TypeScript, @types/*, @vscode/test-electron and @vscode/vsce.

  1. Build everything:
npm run build

This runs, in order:

Script Does npm run build:server scripts/build-server.ps1 npm run build:tools scripts/fetch-pdb2pdb.ps1 npm run compile tsc -p core && tsc -p .
  1. Check the output: server\bin\XppVsCode.Server.exe, tools\pdb2pdb\Pdb2Pdb.exe, core\dist\index.js and out\extension.js exist.

docs.title: How build-server.ps1 finds the D365FO binaries
docs.text:
The script takes the first candidate folder that contains xppc.exe:

  1. XPP_BIN;
  2. FrameworkDirectory of the active configuration (registry HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations, value CurrentMetadataConfig);
  3. the registry's FrameworkDirectory;
  4. every configuration in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig, newest first;
  5. on cloud-hosted and VHD environments, the local AOS's Aos.PackageDirectory (from the batch service's web.config) and Visual Studio's machine default configuration.

Each candidate gets \bin appended. When nothing matches, the script stops with "D365FO compiler (PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\xppc.exe) not found".

It then runs:

dotnet build server\XppVsCode.Server.csproj -c Release -o server\bin -p:D365BinPath=<bin> -p:Version=<package.json version>

-p:Version puts the extension's version into the exe's file metadata (Product "F&O Studio for VS Code"); the release build checks it. The project also stops with a clear error when D365BinPath has no Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Metadata.dll.

Options: -Configuration Debug for a debug build, -Test to run the server unit tests after the build (npm run test:server does that and also runs the bridge contract check).

docs.title: Pdb2Pdb
docs.text: xppc writes Windows PDBs; the VS Code debugger (vsdbg) reads only portable ones, so builds convert them, and the VSIX must carry Pdb2Pdb. fetch-pdb2pdb.ps1 downloads a pinned version from the public .NET tools feed, checks its SHA-256 and extracts it into tools\pdb2pdb. It does nothing when that version is already there.

docs.title: Run the extension from source
docs.text:
The repository has a launch configuration Run Extension (.vscode/launch.json) that starts an Extension Development Host with --extensionDevelopmentPath=${workspaceFolder} and runs the npm: compile task first.

  1. Build the server once (npm run build:server), because launching does not build it.
  2. Open the repository folder in VS Code.
  3. Press F5 (Run and Debug > Run Extension).
  4. In the new window, open a D365FO workspace or project and use F&O Studio as usual.

For continuous TypeScript builds use npm run watch (extension only; rebuild core with tsc -p core when you change it).

After a server change, rebuild the server and run F&O Studio: Restart X++ Server in the development host. Copilot's MCP server restarts when VS Code restarts it; reload the window if it still uses the old exe.

docs.title: Package a VSIX for testing
docs.text:
npm run package

This fetches Pdb2Pdb, regenerates CHANGELOG.md from docs/FEATURES.md, and runs vsce package with docs/FEATURES.md as the Marketplace overview. Install the result with Extensions: Install from VSIX….

.vscodeignore keeps sources, scripts, tests, docs and server/ out of the package, except server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe and its .config.

A local build's server is unsigned. npm run publish refuses on purpose: releases are built, signed and published by the release workflow. See Release-Process.

docs.title: Other generated files
docs.text:
Command Writes Check npm run agents agents/*.agent.md, agents/fno-agents.instructions.md, chatAgents and chatInstructions in package.json, from scripts/agent-definitions.js node scripts/build-agents.js --check npm run changelog CHANGELOG.md from the "What's new" sections of docs/FEATURES.md node scripts/changelog.js --check

Never edit the generated files by hand; the release build fails when they are out of date.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text: Folder Contents src/ extension (TypeScript) core/ @fno-studio/core (TypeScript, Node, no VS Code) server/ metadata and MCP server (C#) server/Resources/ embedded agent instructions, agent guide, Tools.json, report resources media/ webview scripts, styles and icons syntaxes/ X++ TextMate grammar agents/ generated Copilot agents scripts/ build, check and test scripts test/ extension-host smoke tests (*.js) and the server unit tests (test/server) docs/ Marketplace overview (FEATURES.md), roadmap, review findings, images .github/workflows/release.yml release build

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "D365FO compiler (PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\xppc.exe) not found" No configuration with a usable FrameworkDirectory on this machine Connect to a UDE, build on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, or set XPP_BIN to a folder with xppc.exe "Set D365BinPath (or XPP_BIN) to PackagesLocalDirectory\bin" dotnet build ran without the script, or the folder lacks Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Metadata.dll Use npm run build:server, or pass -p:D365BinPath=... "Pdb2Pdb ... has hash ..., expected ..." The download was changed or corrupted Delete tools\pdb2pdb and run npm run build:tools again The development host says the X++ server could not run server\bin\XppVsCode.Server.exe is missing npm run build:server check-core.js fails after your change Something in core/ imports vscode or reaches into src/ Move the VS Code part to the extension and pass it in (see Core-Library) MSBuild skips a rebuild after you restored files with Copy-Item Old timestamps Touch the files

docs.title: Call and Type Hierarchy
docs.text: The call hierarchy shows who calls a method (incoming calls) and what a method calls (outgoing calls), as a tree you can expand level by level. The type hierarchy shows the base classes and the subclasses of a class. Both read the cross-reference database, so they cover all models, not just the files you have open. Visual Studio offers Find References and the class hierarchy in Application Explorer; F&O Studio puts both into VS Code's hierarchy views.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Trace how a method is reached: from CustGroup::find up through its callers to a form or a batch job.
  • See what a method depends on before you wrap or replace it.
  • See every subclass of SalesFormLetter and pick the one that handles invoices.
  • Walk up from a class to its base classes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The cross-reference database, with your own code built with cross references (xpp.build.crossReference, on by default). See Find All References.
  • xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation on (the default).
  • The code in a code view.

docs.title: Call hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Put the cursor on a method: on its name in the signature, on a call such as CustGroup::find(, or anywhere inside the method's body.
  2. Right-click and choose Show Call Hierarchy (or run it from the command palette).
  3. The Call Hierarchy view opens on incoming calls: each caller method, grouped by method, with its element in the description. Expand a caller to see its callers.
  4. Use the button in the view title to switch to outgoing calls: the methods this method calls. Expand them to go deeper.
  5. Click an entry to open the code view at the call. With several calls in the same method, each call site is listed.

Callers and callees without code (for example kernel methods) are left out. Each level shows up to 200 calls; outgoing calls are grouped by target, up to 100 targets.

Use Peek Call Hierarchy to see the same tree in a peek window.

docs.title: Type hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Put the cursor on a class name (in code or on the class declaration line), or anywhere in a class's code view.
  2. Right-click and choose Show Type Hierarchy.
  3. The Type Hierarchy view shows the class. Switch between supertypes (the base class, then its base class...) and subtypes (classes that extend it, then theirs).
  4. Click an entry to open its code view.

Only classes have a type hierarchy. For tables, and for a diagram of a class hierarchy you can export, use View Hierarchy (Hierarchy and Reference Diagrams).

docs.title: Related views
docs.text:
• The code lens counts (Code Lens) show how many callers a method has.
  • Find All References lists every kind of reference, not only calls.
  • Implementations and Chain of Command lists overrides and Chain of Command wrappers, which the call hierarchy doesn't show.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation true Call hierarchy, type hierarchy and Go to Implementations xpp.build.crossReference true Keep your code's calls in the cross-reference database when you build

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The providers are in src/codeIntel/providers.ts; they ask the code intelligence server process (xpp/lang).

Call hierarchy

  1. prepareCallHierarchy resolves the method at the cursor (Go to Definition rules) or takes the method that encloses the cursor.
  2. Incoming and outgoing calls send calls with direction: in or out. Calls in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs runs one SQL query on the cross-reference tables Names and References for the method's path (for example /Tables/CustGroup/Methods/find), with reference kinds MethodCall, TestCall and TestHelperCall.
  3. Each call has the source or target path and the compiler line; compilerLineToDocumentLine in src/xppSource.ts maps it to the code view line.

Type hierarchy

  1. prepareTypeHierarchy takes the class at the cursor, or the class of the code view.
  2. Supertypes come from the extends clause in the class's code view.
  3. Subtypes send subtypes; the server returns the classes with a ClassExtended reference to the class (up to 500).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Calls are as of the last build with cross references.
  • Event handlers and delegate subscribers are not called by the code they handle, and dynamic calls (DictClass, callStatic) are not recorded, so they are not edges in the call tree; see Implementations and Chain of Command.
  • Up to 200 calls per level (100 call targets for outgoing calls).
  • The type hierarchy covers classes only; interfaces they implement are not shown.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No incoming calls for your new method Not built with cross references yet Build the project Show Call Hierarchy does nothing The cursor is not in or on a method, or navigation is off Put the cursor on a method name; turn the setting on Show Type Hierarchy does nothing on a table Only classes are supported Use View Hierarchy The hierarchy is always empty The cross-reference database is not usable (the server returns no calls) Check it with Find References; see Find All References troubleshooting

docs.title: Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments
docs.text: On a cloud-hosted environment (a VM deployed from Lifecycle Services into your Azure subscription) or a VHD environment (the downloadable virtual machine), Finance and Operations runs on the same machine as VS Code: PackagesLocalDirectory, the AOS (IIS or IIS Express), the batch service and the AxDB database are all local. F&O Studio finds them on its own. There is no connection step, no download and no sign-in for the metadata. This is the setup Visual Studio has always used on these machines.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You develop on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment and want to use VS Code (with or next to Visual Studio).
  • You want to build into PackagesLocalDirectory, synchronize the local AxDB and debug the local AOS from VS Code.

For unified developer environments (UDE), use Connect to Environment instead.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Requirement Why A machine with PackagesLocalDirectory and the AOS, as set up by Microsoft F&O Studio finds them from Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options, the batch service and the AOS web.config. VS Code running as administrator As with Visual Studio on these machines: building writes into PackagesLocalDirectory, and Synchronize Database and the AOS restart need administrator rights. The C# extension (for debugging only) The debugger attaches to the local AOS with its .NET debugger. F&O Studio offers to install it.

No xpp.environmentUrl is needed. Leave it empty on these machines unless you also work with a UDE.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code as administrator on the VM.
  2. Open a folder (for example the folder of your .rnrproj project), or just open the Dynamics 365 view.
  3. F&O Studio finds the local AOS. The status bar shows the machine name as the environment name, and its tooltip says "Cloud-hosted or VHD environment (local AOS and PackagesLocalDirectory)".
  4. Work as usual: Application Explorer, D365FO Projects, designers and code, Build Project and Model.
  5. After a successful build, the running AOS hosts are restarted so they load the new build (see Restart after build).
  6. Synchronize the database with F&O Studio: Synchronize Database (or Synchronize Table(s) with the Database for your tables). See Synchronize Database.
  7. Debug with Launch Debugger: it attaches to the local AOS. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: What differs from a unified developer environment
docs.text: Area Cloud-hosted and VHD Unified developer environment Setup None; found automatically Connect to Environment Custom metadata folder PackagesLocalDirectory itself (your models sit next to Microsoft's) A separate C:\CustomXppMetadata... folder Build Into PackagesLocalDirectory; running AOS hosts are restarted Into the custom folder; then deploy Deploy Models to Environment Not needed: "your models run on the local AOS once they are built, so there is nothing to deploy." Through Dataverse (Deploy to Environment) Synchronize Database SyncEngine.exe full sync of the local AxDB Through Dataverse Run Tests Not available ("Tests run through Dataverse, which only unified developer environments have. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, run them from Visual Studio on the VM.") Run Tests Database access Local AxDB with Windows authentication Temporary credentials (Database Access) Debugger Attaches to the local AOS (preview, C# extension) DebuggerProxy to the cloud AOS Version Drift Guard, Clean Up Old Application Versions…, (pac) commands Hidden Available

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.restartLocalAos true After a successful build, restart the AOS hosts that are running (IIS Express or the AOS application pool in IIS, and the batch service) so they load the new build. Not used on UDEs. xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl empty Web client URL for Open in Browser and Open Table Browser when the configuration has none. xpp.trace.manifestFolder empty Folder with the trace event manifests for Analyze Trace; empty searches PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring, AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring and the registered trace providers.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Discovery is in the core library: core/src/environment/localAos.ts and core/src/environment/discovery.ts.

docs.title: When the local AOS is used
docs.text: F&O Studio first looks for the selected UDE's configuration, then for the machine-wide configuration in the registry (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations, value CurrentMetadataConfig). On cloud-hosted environments that value may name Visual Studio's DefaultConfig.xml rather than an XPPConfig JSON file; only an existing .json file is used. If neither gives a configuration, the local AOS is used.

docs.title: Finding PackagesLocalDirectory and the AOS
docs.text:
Nothing assumes a drive letter. F&O Studio reads, in this order:

  1. Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options: Documents\Visual Studio Dynamics 365\DynamicsDevConfig.xml (the Documents folder is read from the user's shell folders), then the machine default named in HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX\Development, value DefaultConfig. From these it takes WebRoleDeploymentFolder, RuntimeHostType (default IIS) and AosWebsiteName (default AOSService).
  2. The AOS web.config: next to the web role folder, or the configuration the batch service runs with (the -service argument of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DynamicsAxBatch, value ImagePath).
  3. PackagesLocalDirectory: the first of the web.config settings Aos.PackageDirectory and Common.BinDir, or the folder two levels above DefaultConfig, that contains bin\xppc.exe.

If no folder with bin\xppc.exe is found, the machine has no local AOS (for example a workstation used with a UDE).

docs.title: The configuration F&O Studio writes
docs.text:
Cloud-hosted and VHD machines have no XPPConfig file, so F&O Studio writes one into its own extension storage, named <machine name>.json:

{
    "FrameworkDirectory": "K:\\AosService\\PackagesLocalDirectory",
    "ModelStoreFolder": "K:\\AosService\\PackagesLocalDirectory",
    "ReferencePackagesPaths": [ "K:\\AosService\\PackagesLocalDirectory" ],
    "DatabaseServer": "<DataAccess.DbServer, else localhost>",
    "BusinessDatabaseName": "<DataAccess.Database, else AxDB>",
    "CrossReferencesDbServerName": "<same as DatabaseServer>",
    "CrossReferencesDatabaseName": "DYNAMICSXREFDB",
    "CloudInstanceURL": "<Infrastructure.HostUrl>"
}

The values in angle brackets come from the AOS web.config. The drive in the example is only an example. The file is rewritten only when its content changes. Because it has no RuntimePackagesDirectory and no RuntimeHostType 4, F&O Studio and its metadata server treat it as a local environment. This file is not registered in the registry, so Visual Studio's own configuration is not touched.

docs.title: Restart after build
docs.text:
After a successful build, F&O Studio does what Visual Studio does, so the AOS loads the new assemblies:

  1. If the debugger is attached to the AOS, it detaches first (the build output says so; start debugging again when the AOS is back).
  2. Each running iisexpress.exe is stopped and started again with its own command line.
  3. The AOS site's application pool in IIS is recycled (found with appcmd.exe), when it has worker processes.
  4. If the batch service DynamicsAxBatch is running, its process is ended and the service is started again. Batch tasks that were running are cut off.

Hosts that are not running are left alone. A failed step does not stop the others; the build output shows "Run VS Code as administrator, as Visual Studio must be on this environment." when access was denied, and "Warning: the AOS may still run the previous build until it is restarted." when a step failed. Turn this off with xpp.build.restartLocalAos.

docs.title: Synchronize Database
docs.text:
On a local environment, Synchronize Database runs a full synchronization as a visible task:

SyncEngine.exe -syncmode=fullall -metadatabinaries=<PackagesLocalDirectory>
  -connect="Data Source=<server>;Initial Catalog=<AxDB>;Integrated Security=True;Enlist=True;Application Name=SyncEngine"
  -fallbacktonative=False

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Cloud-hosted environments use the same code path as VHD environments but have not been tested yet (see FEATURES).
  • The debugger on these environments is a preview and needs the C# extension.
  • Tests (SysTest) do not run from F&O Studio here; use Visual Studio on the VM.
  • Your models are in PackagesLocalDirectory together with Microsoft's, as on any cloud-hosted or VHD environment.
  • The (pac) commands, deploy, version drift and version clean-up are UDE features and are hidden.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No active D365FO configuration found. Connect to a unified developer environment first, or work on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (AosService\PackagesLocalDirectory)." No PackagesLocalDirectory with bin\xppc.exe was found from Visual Studio's options, the batch service or the web.config Check that the AOS is installed and that Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options or the batch service point to it. The status bar shows a UDE name instead of the machine xpp.environmentUrl or the registry names a UDE configuration that exists on this VM Clear xpp.environmentUrl; use Select Environment… > Use the Default Environment. Build output: "...FAILED. ... Run VS Code as administrator..." Restarting IIS or the batch service needs administrator rights Start VS Code as administrator. "SyncEngine failed (exit n). It needs VS Code running as administrator; see the terminal output." Synchronization needs administrator rights, or a sync error Run VS Code as administrator; read the task's terminal output. "IIS is not installed on this machine (appcmd.exe not found)..." when debugging The AOS runs in IIS Express but Visual Studio's option says IIS Set Runtime host type to IISExpress in Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options. Tests are not offered Tests need Dataverse, which only UDEs have Run them from Visual Studio on the VM.
