docs.title: Code Intelligence Settings
docs.text: Every code intelligence feature of F&O Studio can be switched on or off: outline, implementations and hierarchies, workspace symbols, completion, hover details, code lens, live syntax check, obsolete API warnings, formatting, the form and data event handler index, semantic highlighting and compile on save. You switch them in one picker, Configure Code Intelligence…, or with the xpp.codeIntelligence.* settings. The Dynamics 365 view shows how many are on and the state of the extension index.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Turn off a feature you don't use, or one that is slow on your machine.
  • Turn on the slower features that are off by default: semantic highlighting and compile on save.
  • Turn off the form and data event handler scan when you don't need those handlers and want the index to build faster.
  • Check whether the extension index is ready and rebuild it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Nothing; the settings work without an environment. Most features need an active D365FO configuration and some need the cross-reference database to do anything (see the table below).

docs.title: Configure Code Intelligence…
docs.text:
1. Run Configure Code Intelligence… from the command palette, or click it under Code Intelligence in the Dynamics 365 view.
  2. A picker titled "Code intelligence features" lists every feature with a checkbox and a description. Slow features are marked slow.
  3. Check the ones you want, uncheck the others, and press Enter (or OK).
  4. The settings are saved in your user settings and take effect right away: code lenses, semantic tokens and diagnostics refresh. Turning off the syntax check clears its problems; turning on the event handler index starts the scan.

docs.title: The Code Intelligence node
docs.text:
The Dynamics 365 view has a Code Intelligence node. Its description shows N of 12 features on, or indexing… while the extension index builds. Hover it to see each feature with a check mark. Under it:

Item What it does Configure Code Intelligence… Opens the picker above Rebuild Extension Index Rebuilds the Chain of Command and event handler index; its description shows the index status Show Extensions and Handlers… Lists what extends an element (Implementations and Chain of Command)

docs.title: Settings editor and settings.json
docs.text:
The same switches are in the Settings editor under F&O Studio (search for xpp.codeIntelligence), or in settings.json:

{
    "xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting": true,
    "xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave": false,
    "xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex": true
}

You can set them per workspace too, for example to turn on compile on save for one project only. The picker always writes the user settings; a workspace value still overrides it.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Picker label Effect Needs xpp.codeIntelligence.outline true Outline and breadcrumbs Methods and members of the open element in Outline, breadcrumbs and Go to Symbol in Editor - xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation true Implementations, call and type hierarchy Go to Implementations (overrides, Chain of Command, event handlers, subclasses), call hierarchy and type hierarchy Cross-reference database, extension index xpp.codeIntelligence.workspaceSymbols true Go to Symbol in Workspace Ctrl+T over elements and methods of all models Cross-reference database xpp.codeIntelligence.completion true Completion and signature help Members after . and ::, label references in strings, keywords; parameter hints Metadata xpp.codeIntelligence.hover true Hover details Label texts, EDT and enum details on hover Metadata xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens true Code lens Reference, override, Chain of Command and handler counts above methods; what a Chain of Command or handler method wraps Cross-reference database, extension index xpp.codeIntelligence.syntaxCheck true Live syntax check Syntax errors while you type, with the X++ compiler's parser Compiler assemblies xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings true Obsolete API warnings Warnings (or errors) where code uses methods, classes and tables marked [SysObsolete] Cross-reference database xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting true Format document 4-space Allman layout (Format Document / Format Selection) - xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex true Form and data event handlers (marked slow) Include [FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler] and similar handlers. The first scan of all packages takes about a minute; it is cached afterwards Reference packages on disk xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting false Semantic highlighting (marked slow) Colour classes, tables, enums, EDTs, methods and fields by what they are; looks up every identifier of the open document Metadata xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave false Compile on save (marked slow) Build the project with the X++ compiler after saving code, so semantic errors reach Problems (about 10 s per save) A D365FO project

Features that are always on, with no setting: Go to Definition, Find All References, the element and method hover, Ctrl+click links, folding, syntax colouring and snippets.

Related settings outside this group:

Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Update the cross-reference database while building, so references, call hierarchy, code lens and symbols include your code xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Save unsaved X++ code views before a build

All F&O Studio settings: Settings Reference.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The feature list (key, label, description, slow flag, default) is in src/codeIntel/settings.ts; the matching settings are declared in package.json.
  • Every provider in src/codeIntel/providers.ts and src/productivity/obsolete.ts checks its setting each time it runs, so changes apply without a reload.
  • A configuration change under xpp.codeIntelligence refreshes the code lenses, semantic tokens and the Dynamics 365 view. It clears the syntax diagnostics when the syntax check is turned off and starts the index scan when the event handler index is turned on.
  • The picker writes with ConfigurationTarget.Global (user settings).
  • The code intelligence features run in a second server process, separate from the designers' server, so a slow index build doesn't block the designers. Restart X++ Server restarts both.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The picker can't write workspace settings; edit .vscode/settings.json for that.
  • Turning a feature off doesn't stop the extension index; the index builds when an X++ document opens, for implementations, code lens and completion alike.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A feature stays off after you checked it A workspace setting overrides the user setting Remove the value from .vscode/settings.json The Code Intelligence node says indexing… for a long time The first form and data event handler scan (about a minute) or a large cross-reference database Wait; or turn off Form and data event handlers Rebuild Extension Index shows failed: ... The cross-reference database is not usable See Find All References troubleshooting Every save takes about 10 seconds Compile on save is on Uncheck Compile on save

docs.title: Code Lens
docs.text: Code lens puts small, clickable counts above the code of an element: how many places reference each method, how many Chain of Command wrappers, overrides and event handlers it has, and how many Chain of Command classes, handlers and subclasses the element has. In an extension or handler class it shows what each method wraps or handles. Visual Studio's X++ editor has no code lens; you would run Find References or search for extensions by hand.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• See at a glance which methods are used, and how often, before you change them.
  • See which standard methods are wrapped or handled, so you know where extra code runs.
  • In your own Chain of Command class, jump from each wrapper to the method it wraps.
  • In a handler class, see which event each handler method subscribes to.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The element must be open in a code view of the whole element (not a single nested method such as a form data source method).
  • Counts come from the cross-reference database and the extension index; see Implementations and Chain of Command.
  • xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens must be on (the default), and VS Code's own editor.codeLens setting must be on.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Open a class, table or form in the code view. The lenses appear above the first line and above each method signature.

docs.title: On the first line (the element)
docs.text: Lens Shown when Click N Chain of Command classes · N event handlers · N subclasses The element has any of them (parts with 0 are left out) Opens Show Extensions and Handlers… for the element extends X (Chain of Command) The element is a Chain of Command class ([ExtensionOf(...)]) Opens the extended element extension index building… (with a spinning icon) The extension index is not ready yet Runs Rebuild Extension Index

docs.title: Above each method
docs.text:
Lens Meaning Click N references Calls of the method from the cross-reference database (method calls, test calls and test helper calls) Peeks the references N Chain of Command Chain of Command methods that wrap this method Peeks the wrappers N overrides Methods in subclasses that override it Peeks the overrides N handlers Pre/post, delegate and form/data event handlers of the method Peeks the handlers wraps X.method This method is a Chain of Command wrapper Opens the wrapped method Post handler of X.method (or another handler kind) This method is an event handler Opens the handled method or element

The reference lens shows for every method that has an entry in the cross-reference database or a Chain of Command wrapper; it can read 0 references when the method is only overridden or wrapped. The other counts show only when they are above zero. A method that nothing references, overrides or wraps shows no lens.

Example: in the code view of SalesFormLetter, the run method shows 49 references | 2 Chain of Command | 2 overrides | 1 handler. Clicking 2 Chain of Command peeks the two wrappers. In your own extension class, the method run shows wraps SalesFormLetter.run.

The lenses refresh when you save a code view, when you change a code intelligence setting and when the extension index finishes building.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens true Show the code lens xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex true Count form and data event handlers too xpp.build.crossReference true Keep the reference counts of your code current when you build

You can also switch the code lens in Configure Code Intelligence… (see Code Intelligence Settings).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. codeLenses in src/codeIntel/providers.ts sends one code_lens request for the open element to the code intelligence server process.
  2. CodeLens in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs answers with:
  3. one SQL query over the cross-reference database that counts, for every method path under the element (/Classes/SalesFormLetter/Methods/%), the references of kinds MethodCall, TestCall and TestHelperCall, and the MethodOverride references;
  4. the number of subclasses (kind ClassExtended);
  5. from the extension index: the Chain of Command classes of the element, its handlers, and per method the wrappers and handlers;
  6. for a class that is itself an extension or handler class: what it extends, what each method wraps and what each handler handles.
  7. The extension finds each method's signature line with methodSpans from src/xppSource.ts and places the lenses there.
  8. Clicking a count runs the internal command xpp.codeIntel.peek, which asks for the references or for the implementations of that kind and shows them in a peek window. wraps and handler lenses run xpp.codeIntel.goto.

The server waits up to 15 seconds for the extension index; if it is not ready the counts from the database still show and the "building" lens is added.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No lenses in nested method documents (data source, field and control methods).
  • Reference counts are as of the last build with cross references.
  • Only calls (method calls, test calls and test helper calls) are counted as references; the References view (Find All References) shows every kind.
  • The lens counts Chain of Command classes of the element itself; those on its data sources or controls appear in Show Extensions and Handlers….

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No lenses at all xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens or editor.codeLens is off, or the document is a nested method Turn the settings on; open the element's code view No reference lenses, but the extension lenses show The cross-reference database is not usable See Find All References extension index building… stays The index is still building or failed Look at the status on the Code Intelligence node in the Dynamics 365 view; run Rebuild Extension Index A count is lower than expected Your latest code is not built with cross references Build the project

docs.title: Compare Code and Metadata
docs.text: Compare Code… shows the X++ code of two elements side by side in VS Code's diff editor. Compare Metadata… does the same with the whole element as readable text: its nodes, every property that has a value, and the code of its methods. They replace Visual Studio's Compare command; the content is the same, the view is VS Code's diff editor.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Compare two similar elements before you copy a pattern: CustGroup and VendGroup, SalesFormLetter_Invoice and PurchFormLetter_Invoice.
  • Check what differs between your duplicate and its original after Duplicate….
  • Compare two table extensions, two menu items or two security privileges property by property.
  • Find the property that makes one form behave differently from another.

To compare one element with its own earlier versions, use Element History. To compare the standard methods you wrap between two application versions, use Standard Code Drift.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An environment with metadata on this machine (Connect to Environment).
  • No project is needed. Both commands work on standard elements and on your own.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Place Compare Code… Compare Metadata… Application Explorer, right-click an element Elements with code All elements D365FO Project view, right-click an element Elements with code All elements Element Designer, right-click the root node Elements with code All elements Dynamics 365 view View and run > Compare Code… View and run > Compare Metadata… Command Palette F&O Studio: Compare Code… F&O Studio: Compare Metadata…

Elements with code are classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, queries and maps.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click the first element, for example table CustGroup, and choose Compare Code… or Compare Metadata…. From the Command Palette or the Dynamics 365 view, you are first asked for the first element: type at least 3 characters (Compare code: first element / Compare metadata: first element) and pick it.
  2. Compare CustGroup with: type at least 3 characters of the second element's name, for example VendGroup, and pick it. Only elements of the same type are offered.
  3. The diff editor opens:
  4. Compare Code…: the two code views, titled CustGroup ↔ VendGroup;
  5. Compare Metadata…: the two metadata texts, titled CustGroup ↔ VendGroup (metadata).

Use the diff editor as usual: next/previous change, inline or side-by-side view, collapse unchanged regions.

When you run Compare Code… on an element without code (for example from the Command Palette on an EDT), the metadata texts are compared instead.

docs.title: The metadata text
docs.text:
Compare Metadata… turns each element into an indented text, one line per node and property. For a table of your model it looks like this (shortened, values are illustrative):

// AxTable ContosoOrderStatusTable  [ContosoExtensions]
ContosoOrderStatusTable (Table)
    Label = @ContosoLabels:OrderStatus
    PrimaryIndex = StatusIdx
    ...
    [Fields]
        StatusId (TableFieldString)
            ExtendedDataType = ContosoOrderStatusId
            ...
    [Indexes]
        StatusIdx (TableIndex)
            ...
    [Methods]
        find()
        | public static ContosoOrderStatusTable find(ContosoOrderStatusId _statusId, boolean _forUpdate = false)
        | {
        |     ...
        | }
- The first line names the type, the element and its model. - Each node shows its name and its type (without the Ax prefix). - Properties with a value are listed, sorted by name. Empty and default-object values are left out. Multi-line values are shown on one line with \n. - Child collections appear as [Fields], [Field Groups], [Indexes], [Relations], [Data Sources], [Controls] and so on, with their items below. - Methods are listed with () and their code, each line prefixed with |. A class declaration is shown under Declaration the same way.

Because properties are sorted and laid out the same for both elements, the diff lines up nodes and properties that match.

docs.title: Typical comparisons
docs.text:
Goal Command Example Copy a pattern from a similar standard table Compare Metadata… CustGroup with VendGroup: fields, indexes, relations, delete actions, find and exist methods See how two posting classes differ Compare Code… SalesFormLetter_Invoice with PurchFormLetter_Invoice Check a duplicate against its original Compare Metadata… ContosoCustGroupCopy with CustGroup after Duplicate… Compare two of your table extensions Compare Metadata… CustTable.ContosoExtensions with VendTable.ContosoExtensions Compare two security privileges Compare Metadata… Entry points, grants and data entity permissions side by side

Tips:

  • Start with Compare Metadata… when you do not know where the difference is: it includes the code too.
  • In the metadata diff, differences inside methods appear as | lines, property differences as Name = value lines.
  • Select text in either pane of the diff editor to copy it.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Compare has no settings. The diff editor follows VS Code's own diff settings (for example diffEditor.renderSideBySide and diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The command is compareElements in src/d365Tools.ts. It picks the elements, then runs VS Code's vscode.diff on two URIs.
  • Compare Code… uses the code view URIs xpp:/<AxType>/<Name>.xpp, the same documents the X++ Code View shows (declaration, methods inside the class body, closing brace).
  • Compare Metadata… uses read-only documents with the scheme xppmeta (xppmeta:/<AxType>/<Name>.xppmeta), provided by MetadataDocuments in src/diagrams.ts. Their text comes from the bridge action dump_element, implemented in MetaModelBridge.ElementDump.cs: the server reads the element through Microsoft's metadata provider and walks it by reflection, using the same property and collection attributes as the Element Designer.
  • The second element is found with find_object, limited to the first element's type.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The two elements are found by type and name. Two versions of the same element (for example the same name in two models, or two application versions) cannot be compared this way. Use Element History for versions in Git and Standard Code Drift for application versions.
  • Both elements must be of the same type. Comparing a table with its table extension is not offered.
  • The metadata texts of Compare Metadata… are read-only. Change the elements in the code view or the designer.
  • The metadata text leaves out properties without a value.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Nothing happens after typing the name Fewer than 3 characters Type at least 3 characters No element matching '…'. Wrong name, or no element of the first element's type matches Check the name; only the first element's type is offered One side shows // <type> '<name>' not found. The element is not in the active configuration Select the right environment

docs.title: Compared with Visual Studio
docs.text:
F&O Studio covers what the Visual Studio Dynamics 365 tools do for X++ development, in VS Code. Where it can, it uses the same compiler, scripts, file formats and metadata API as Visual Studio, so results are the same and the two can be used on the same machine. This page maps Visual Studio features to F&O Studio and says where they are the same, different or more.

If you come from Visual Studio, read this page with Getting-Started and Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: How to read the table
docs.text:
• Same means the same compiler, script, file format or metadata API.
  • Different means another way to get the same result.
  • More means F&O Studio adds to what Visual Studio does.

docs.title: Feature map
docs.text: Visual Studio F&O Studio Application Explorer (classic and model view) Application-Explorer Same Solution Explorer: X++ and C# projects, references Project view with References, the solution's C# projects and their files; Add Reference, New C# Project (Solution-View-and-CSharp-References) Same .rnrproj items and AxReference elements; C# editing through the C# extension Solution Explorer: Add > New Item New Element… and the wizards (New-Element) Same element types, plus batch job, report, workflow, service, business event, number sequence and feature wizards Element designers and the Properties window Element-Designer with a filterable, categorized Properties grid and pickers Same metadata classes Form designer Form layout preview, form extensions, element designer for the nodes (Form-Designer-and-Preview) Same: a preview where clicking a section selects its control Code editor XPP-Code-View with completion, definitions, references, Chain of Command implementations, code lens, folding and formatting Same code layout Build models, build project Build Model, Build Project; errors in Problems (Build-Project-and-Model) Same (xppc, LabelC) Best practice checks Run Best Practice Checks on Project (Best-Practice-Checks) Same (xppbp) Synchronize database Synchronize Database (Dataverse on UDE, SyncEngine on cloud-hosted and VHD), Synchronize Table(s) with the Database (Synchronize-Database) Same Create deployment package, deploy Create Deployment Package…, Deploy Models to Environment (Deploy-to-Environment) Same: the locally built packages go up through Dataverse Model management Create Model…, Update Model Parameters…, View Model Dependencies… (Models-and-Model-Dependencies) Same Import/Export project (.axpp) Import Project…, Export Project… (Export-and-Import-Projects) Same file format Find references, metadata search, find labels, tag references Find References, Open Element…, Find Labels…, Find Tag References… Same cross-reference database Compare Compare Code…, Compare Metadata… in VS Code's diff editor (Compare-Code-and-Metadata) Different view, same content Launch debugger Launch Debugger (DebuggerProxy with vsdbg on UDE; the C# extension's debugger on the local AOS) (Debugger) Same debugger proxy on UDE Infolog Infolog in the F&O Studio panel Same messages Test Explorer (SysTest) Test Explorer and Run Tests (Test-Explorer, Run-Tests) Same runner on the environment DGML diagrams Hierarchy, references, dependencies and entity relationship diagrams, exportable as Mermaid (Hierarchy-and-Reference-Diagrams, Entity-Relationship-Diagram) Different Trace Parser Analyze Trace… (own .etl reader, no import database) (Analyze-Trace) Different Open in browser, table browser Open in Browser, Open Table Browser, Browse Table Data, SQL queries (Browse-Table-Data, SQL-Query-Panel) More Report designer (.rdl) Report-Designer for precision designs, with a preview by Microsoft's report engine and a scan overlay; New Report… wizard Same RDL; Visual Studio has no local preview. Charts, gauges, maps and subreports are kept but edited in the RDL Data entity wizard New Data Entity… (entity, staging table, privileges) and New Table with Form… (Wizard-Data-Entity, Wizard-Table-with-Form) Same result, more elements

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
F&O Studio reads and writes the same development configuration Visual Studio uses: the registry value CurrentMetadataConfig under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations, and the JSON files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig. Connect to Environment… performs the same client setup as Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools for a UDE: download the metadata, restore the cross-reference database, link the runtime packages, write the configuration and make it active.

Visual Studio reads configurations with a strict parser and silently leaves out a file that lacks a required member. F&O Studio writes every member of Power Platform Tools' template and repairs files written by older versions, so Visual Studio can list and load them. See Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: The metadata server uses Microsoft's metadata API (MetadataProviderFactory().CreateDiskProvider, MetaModelServiceFactory().Create) from your PackagesLocalDirectory\bin. The element designer is generated from the same metadata classes Visual Studio's designer uses, so node order and properties match. Labels are stored in the same label text files, sorted by ID as Visual Studio's label editor does. Projects are .rnrproj files saved the way Visual Studio saves them. See Metadata-Server.

docs.title: Build
docs.text: Build Project and Build Model run LabelC and then xppc with the same arguments Visual Studio passes, and reportsc for reports. Before compiling, referenced C# projects are built and their files copied into the package's bin folder, as Visual Studio's build tasks do. Best practice uses xppbp. Create Deployment Package… runs RunPackageCreationAll.ps1, the script Visual Studio runs.

docs.title: Deploy and tests on a UDE
docs.text: Deploy zips the locally built package folders, as Visual Studio does, and sends them through the environment's Dataverse (msprov_fnopackages, msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync). Nothing is recompiled in the cloud, so your build and its debug symbols reach the environment. Tests run through the same Dataverse test runner Visual Studio's Test Explorer uses, against the deployed code. See Core-Library.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: On a UDE, Visual Studio's default debugging uses the FinOps tools' DebuggerProxy.exe in vsdbg mode. F&O Studio runs the same proxy as its debug adapter and attaches to AXHost.exe. Just My Code, symbols on demand and exception logging stay at Visual Studio's defaults unless you change them in launch.json (Debugger-Options).

docs.title: What is different
docs.text: Area Visual Studio F&O Studio Editor Visual Studio editor VS Code; X++ language features come from F&O Studio's own server and the cross-reference database, with a TextMate grammar Code layout Code editor per element The same layout (declaration, then methods inside the class body) as a virtual xpp: document; methods of data sources, fields and controls open in their own editor Diagrams DGML Webview diagrams, exportable as Mermaid or SVG Traces Trace Parser with an import database F&O Studio's own .etl reader Workspaces One solution per Visual Studio instance Each project opens in its own VS Code workspace; each workspace remembers its own environment Projects Required Optional: you can browse, open and build models without one

docs.title: What F&O Studio adds
docs.text:
• Copilot agents and agent tools on the real metadata API, with checkpoints, scope and an activity view (Copilot-Agents, MCP-Agent-Tools).
  • Data: Browse Table Data, the SQL panel with Explain Plan, and Database-Performance-Insights.
  • Analysis: Analyze-Performance, Upgrade-Readiness, Standard-Code-Drift, security and license analysis (Security-View).
  • Review and release: Review-My-Changes, Pre-Deploy-Checklist.
  • Productivity: Search-Code, Find-Similar-Implementations, Find-Message-Source, Quick-Fixes, Run-Snippet, Generate-SysTest-Class.
  • Report preview with Microsoft's report engine and a scan overlay for preprinted stationery (Report-Preview, Scan-Overlay-and-Measure).
  • Environment tools: Version-Drift-Guard (preview), Open-Team-Repository (preview).

docs.title: Environment differences
docs.text: Environment Visual Studio F&O Studio Unified developer environment Power Platform Tools connect, build, deploy, test and debug Connect to Environment…; build, deploy, sync, tests and debugging Cloud-hosted or VHD Runs on the VM against the local AOS Works without a connection step; uses the local PackagesLocalDirectory, AOS and AxDB. Deploy and Run Tests are UDE-only and hidden. Run VS Code as administrator to build into PackagesLocalDirectory, as with Visual Studio. The debugger attaches to the local AOS (preview, needs the C# extension)

docs.title: Using both
docs.text: You can keep Visual Studio on the same machine. Both read the same active configuration, so switching environments in one shows in the other's configuration list. Visual Studio's FinOps tools must match the environment's metadata version, or its Application Explorer does not open; Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version installs the matching tools when they differ. F&O Studio never depends on Visual Studio. See Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is a preview. Some features have not been verified end to end on a live environment: the version drift guard, Open Team Repository on a real team repository, Try Data Entity and Try Service Operation, and Verify Changes in the Running App.
  • In the Report Designer, charts, gauges, maps and subreports are kept but edited in the RDL.
  • Windows only, as Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 tools.

docs.title: Compiler Diagnostics
docs.text: When you build, the X++ compiler (xppc) writes every error and warning to an XML log. F&O Studio reads that log and shows each diagnostic in VS Code's Problems view, on the element's code view, at the line where the problem is. Click a problem to open the code view at that line. This replaces Visual Studio's Error List after a build.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After a build, to go from each error to the code that causes it.
  • To check the warnings of your project's elements before a review or a deploy.
  • With xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave, to see compiler errors after every save.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A build must have run: diagnostics come from the compiler, not from a live language server. For errors while you type, see Syntax Check and Obsolete Warnings.
  • The code view of an element is a virtual document (scheme xpp:); see X++ Code View.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Build with Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ editor) or Build Model.
  2. If the build fails, click Show Problems in the error message, or open the Problems view (Ctrl+Shift+M).
  3. Problems are grouped by element. Each entry shows:
  4. the severity icon (error, warning or information);
  5. the message from the compiler;
  6. the diagnostic's moniker (the compiler's rule or error code) as the problem code;
  7. the diagnostic type reported by the compiler as the source.
  8. Click a problem. F&O Studio opens the element's code view (for example xpp:/AxClass/ContosoOrderStatusHelper.xpp) and selects the reported line and columns.
  9. Fix the code, save, and build again. Each build replaces the previous build's diagnostics.

docs.title: Severities
docs.text:
Compiler severity Problems view Error Error Fatal (compiler crash) Error Warning Warning Anything else (for example Informational) Information

Fatal diagnostics count as errors and are shown even in a project build when they belong to elements outside the project.

docs.title: Diagnostics without a line
docs.text:
Some diagnostics are about metadata, not code (a property, a field, a relation). They have no line, or line 0, which means the element as a whole. They are shown on the first line of the element's code view, and when no line is reported, the compiler's path is added to the message, for example:

<message> (<path of the element node>)

docs.title: Project build or model build
docs.text:
• Build Project shows only the diagnostics of elements that are in the project, plus fatal errors and diagnostics that do not name an element.
  • Build Model shows every diagnostic of the package.

The compiler compiles the whole package in both cases. If the result says the build failed but the Problems view has no error, the error is in an element outside the project: run Build Model.

docs.title: The X++ Build output
docs.text:
Every diagnostic is also written to the X++ Build output, one per line, with its path and position:

Error: dynamics://Class/ContosoOrderStatusHelper/Method/run(14,13): <message>
Warning: dynamics://Class/ContosoOrderStatusHelper/Method/main(31,9): <message>

The line numbers in the output are the compiler's own numbers (see below). The Problems view shows the converted line.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave false Runs Build Project after you save X++ code, so compiler errors reach the Problems view without a manual build (about 10 seconds per save). xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Saves unsaved code views before a build, so the diagnostics match what you see. xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules false Adds AppChecker rules to the build; their findings appear as diagnostics too.

docs.title: Reading the XML log
docs.text:
xppc is started with -xmllog=<package>\BuildLogs\Dynamics.AX.<package>.xppc.xml. Each <Diagnostic> element has a DiagnosticType, Severity, Path, Moniker, Message, Line, Column, EndLine and EndColumn. src/diagnostics.ts parses them (parseDiagnostics) and finds the element each one belongs to (diagnosticTarget):

  • code diagnostics use paths such as dynamics://Class/<name>/Method/<method>;
  • the first segment is the element type (for example Class becomes AxClass), the second the element name;
  • diagnostics whose path does not name an element are not attached to a code view; they still appear in the X++ Build output.

src/build.ts (XppBuilder.publish) then creates one VS Code diagnostic per entry on the element's code view URI, sets the moniker as the code and the diagnostic type as the source, and replaces the contents of the diagnostic collection. Compiler diagnostics and best practice diagnostics are kept in two separate collections, so a best practice run does not clear build errors and the other way round.

docs.title: Converting compiler lines to code view lines
docs.text:
xppc does not count lines the way the code view shows them. It counts as if the element's text were the class declaration without its closing brace, followed by each method back to back. The code view shows the declaration, then the methods inside the class body (indented, with blank lines between them), then the closing brace, the way Visual Studio shows it.

compilerLineToDocumentLine in src/xppSource.ts converts one to the other:

  1. It finds the class layout in the code view text: the declaration and the start and end of every method.
  2. Compiler lines up to the end of the declaration map one to one.
  3. For later lines, it walks the methods in order, adding each method's line count, until it finds the method that contains the compiler line, and returns the same offset inside that method in the code view.
  4. For elements whose code view is a list of method blocks without a class body (for example a form's classDeclaration followed by methods), each block is counted on its own.

The conversion reads the current text of the code view. If the text cannot be read, the compiler line is used as is. The end line of a range keeps the same distance from the start line as the compiler reported. The repository's scripts/diag-test.js checks this conversion.

docs.title: Builds by Copilot
docs.text:
The agent tool xpp_build reads the same XML log in the metadata server (server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs) and returns the diagnostics as text, errors first, at most 80 lines, with identical lines listed once with a count:

BUILD FAILED: ContosoExtensions in 41s - 1 error(s), 2 warning(s).
  ERROR AxClass ContosoOrderStatusHelper.run line 14:13 [<moniker>] <message>
  WARNING AxTable ContosoOrderStatusTable [<moniker>] <message> (x2)

These line numbers are the compiler's own. The agent's diagnostics do not go to the Problems view.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Diagnostics come only from a build; there is no incremental compile while you type. Syntax errors and obsolete API warnings while you type come from Syntax Check and Obsolete Warnings.
  • Each build replaces all compiler diagnostics; a project build does not keep diagnostics from an earlier model build.
  • Diagnostics on metadata (no line) point at the first line of the code view, not at the property in the Element Designer.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The build failed but the Problems view is empty The error is in an element outside the project (project build), or xppc failed without writing diagnostics. Run Build Model; if still empty, open X++ Build and read the xppc log. A problem points at the wrong line The code view changed after the build (unsaved edits, or edits after the build). Save and build again; keep xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild on. Old problems stay after fixing the code Diagnostics only change when you build. Build again, or turn on xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave. A problem shows the compiler path in its text The diagnostic has no line (metadata finding). Open the element in the Element Designer and fix the node named in the path.

docs.title: Completion and Signature Help
docs.text: Completion suggests what you can type next in X++ code: the methods and fields of a type after . or ::, enum values, label references inside strings, and keywords. Signature help shows the parameters of the method you are calling and highlights the one you are typing. This is the counterpart of IntelliSense in Visual Studio's X++ editor. F&O Studio reads the members from the metadata, so methods that Chain of Command classes add to a type are listed too.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Find a static method such as CustGroup::find or SalesTable::exist without opening the table.
  • See the fields and methods of a record variable after custTable..
  • Pick an enum value after SalesStatus::.
  • Find a label of your model while writing info("@...").
  • Check the parameter order of a call while you type it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration; members are read from the metadata of all models.
  • For methods added by Chain of Command classes: the extension index (see Implementations and Chain of Command).
  • xpp.codeIntelligence.completion must be on (the default). It switches completion and signature help together.

docs.title: Members after . and ::
docs.text:
Completion opens on its own when you type ., :: or @, or when you press Ctrl+Space.

You type You get CustGroup:: Static methods of CustGroup and its base types SalesStatus:: The values of the enum, including values added by enum extensions custGroup. (a variable) Instance methods and fields of the variable's declared type this. or element. Instance members of the current element, including its private members super. Instance members of the base class Namespace.Type:: or Namespace. .NET types and members from the C# projects of your solution

Each entry shows:

  • the name, with () for methods;
  • on the right, the type that declares it, with "(extension)" when a Chain of Command class adds it;
  • in the details, the full signature (methods) or the field type.

Private members are hidden unless you are inside the element that declares them. Members are listed from the type itself and its base types: classes through extends, tables and views through their Extends property. Tables also list the fields of their table extensions and the system fields and methods every table has (RecId, DataAreaId, insert, update, validateWrite, initValue and so on).

When you accept a method, F&O Studio inserts name() with the cursor between the parentheses and opens signature help.

The type of a variable comes from the nearest declaration above the cursor (CustGroup custGroup; or a parameter CustGroup _custGroup), else from a field of the class. A plain name before :: or . that is not a variable is taken as a type name.

docs.title: Label references in strings
docs.text:
1. Inside a string, type "@.
  2. Keep typing part of a label ID or of its text, for example "@Contoso or "@order status.
  3. The list shows up to 100 matches as @File:Id with the label text. The label comment, if any, shows in the details.
  4. Accept one; the reference replaces what you typed after the quote.

Only label files of your own models are searched, in en-US. For standard labels use Find Labels… (Label Tools).

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text: Anywhere else, typing a word offers the X++ keywords (select, firstonly, forupdate, ttsbegin, changecompany, crosscompany, validtimestate and others) together with the Snippets.

docs.title: Signature help
docs.text:
1. Type the name of a method and (, or a , inside a call.
  2. A popup shows the method's signature with the current parameter in bold.
  3. As you type commas, the bold parameter moves. Nested parentheses and brackets and commas inside strings are skipped.

Signature help works on calls F&O Studio can resolve: Type::method(, this.method(, super.method(, variable.method(, unqualified calls of methods of the current element or its base classes, and global functions of class Global. It looks back up to 10 lines for the open parenthesis, so it also works when a call spans several lines. The signature comes from the member list (methods on several lines, kernel methods and Chain of Command methods included), else from the method's signature line in code.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.completion true Completion after . and ::, label references in strings, keywords, and signature help

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. completion in src/codeIntel/providers.ts looks at the text before the cursor:
  2. "@... inside a string: sends labels to the code intelligence server;
  3. a dotted qualifier (A.B:: or A.B.): asks the C# index (clrNavigation.ts);
  4. qualifier. or qualifier::: finds the owner type (current element, base class, declared type or type name) and sends members;
  5. otherwise: the keyword list.
  6. Members in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs calls the bridge action type_members, which reads the type through the metadata provider and walks up to 12 base types, collecting methods (signature, static, access, doc), fields and enum values (MetaModelBridge.Members.cs). Then it adds the non-private methods of every Chain of Command class of each type in the chain, from the extension index, marked as extension members.
  7. Member lists are cached for 60 seconds, both in the server and in the extension. Saving an X++ document clears the extension's cache.
  8. Labels reads the *.en-US.label.txt files of your custom packages, cached by file time, and matches the search text against the reference and the label text.
  9. signatureHelp finds the open ( of the call, resolves the name before it with the same logic as Go to Definition, and splits the signature's parameters on top-level commas.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Type inference is textual: chained calls (CustTable::find(x).), method return values and var variables don't give a type, so you get no member list there.
  • Label completion covers only your models' labels and only en-US.
  • Signature help shows one signature (X++ has no overloads) and only for calls it can resolve.
  • Members are read once a minute at most; a method you just added to another element appears after you save it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No list after variable. The variable's declaration was not found above the cursor, or its type is var Declare the variable with its type Chain of Command methods are missing The extension index is not ready Wait for ready on the Code Intelligence node in the Dynamics 365 view "@ offers no labels No label file in your models has a matching label, or the files are not en-US Create the label (Label Editor) or use Find Labels… Nothing at all xpp.codeIntelligence.completion is off Turn it on in Configure Code Intelligence…

docs.title: Connect to Environment
docs.text: Connect to Environment… prepares this machine for X++ development against a unified developer environment (UDE). It downloads the environment's system metadata (PackagesLocalDirectory), cross-reference database and FinOps tools, extracts and restores them, links the runtime packages, writes the metadata configuration and makes it the active one. It is the same client setup that Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools perform when you connect Visual Studio to a Dataverse environment, and the configuration it writes is the one Visual Studio reads.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• The first time you work with a unified developer environment on this machine.
  • When Microsoft has updated the environment to a new application version and the Version Drift Guard offers Update Metadata. The new version gets its own folder and configuration.
  • When a previous setup failed or was cancelled, to finish it. Steps that are already done are skipped.
  • When you want the same environment's configuration rewritten (for example after you deleted the runtime links folder).

You do not need it on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment. Those already have PackagesLocalDirectory, an AOS and AxDB on the machine; see Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Requirement Why A unified developer environment (Dataverse environment with finance and operations, deployment type OnlineDev) Setup stops with "Not a unified developer environment" for any other type, such as a sandbox. The environment's Dataverse URL, for example https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com Copy the Environment URL from the Power Platform admin center. The finance and operations URL (https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com) also works; see below. A Microsoft account with access to the environment You sign in through VS Code's Microsoft account. See Sign-In and Authentication. SQL Server Express LocalDB with the instance MSSQLLocalDB The cross-reference database is restored into (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB with Windows authentication. At least 16 GB free on the drive of %LOCALAPPDATA% Checked before the download when the version's PackagesLocalDirectory is not there yet. Windows F&O Studio runs on Windows only. Extraction uses the Windows tar.exe.

If LocalDB is missing or its instance is not created, setup stops at the second step with a message that tells you to install it or run:

sqllocaldb create MSSQLLocalDB -s

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the setup in one of these ways:
  2. Dynamics 365 view: Environment group > Connect to Environment….
  3. Status bar: click the environment item (it shows the environment name), then Connect to Environment….
  4. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Connect to Environment….
  5. The Get started walkthrough: step Connect to your environment.
  6. F&O Studio: Select Environment… > Connect to Another Environment….
  7. Enter the Dataverse URL in the input box Connect to a unified developer environment. The box is filled with the environment this window already uses, if any.
  8. The box rejects Power Platform portal pages (powerplatform.microsoft.com, powerapps.com) and tells you to copy the environment's Environment URL instead.
  9. You can enter a URL without https://; it is added.
  10. You can enter the finance and operations URL (https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com). A UDE's finance and operations host starts with the same org name as its Dataverse host, so F&O Studio looks up <org>.crm.dynamics.com, <org>.crm2.dynamics.com and the other regional Dataverse hosts and uses the one that exists. If none exists, you get "No Dataverse environment found for ..." and should enter the Dataverse URL.
  11. Sign in when VS Code asks (a browser window opens if you have no session for that org yet).
  12. Follow the progress:
  13. A notification X++ environment setup shows Step n/6: <message>. It has a Cancel button.
  14. The X++ output channel opens and logs every message with a time stamp.
  15. The Dynamics 365 view gets focus. Its Environment group lists the six phases with an icon each: pending, running (spinning), done or failed. The running phase shows its current message, such as Downloading PackagesLocalDirectory.zip: 42%.
  16. When setup succeeds you see Environment connected. The Application Explorer, designers and code views now use it. Click Done in the Environment group to return it to the normal environment menu.

docs.title: The six phases
docs.text: # Phase (as shown in the view) What happens 1 Sign in to Dataverse Interactive sign-in, then two Dataverse calls read the environment details. Setup checks that the deployment type is OnlineDev and that an application version is returned. The log shows Environment <finance and operations URL>, application <version>. 2 Check SQL Server LocalDB F&O Studio's server (XppVsCode.Server.exe --sql-check) connects to (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB with Windows authentication. Then the free disk space is checked (16 GB) if PackagesLocalDirectory is not there yet. 3 Download metadata and tools Downloads what is missing: PackagesLocalDirectory.zip, DYNAMICSXREFDB.bak and Microsoft.Dynamics.FinOps.ToolsVS2022.vsix. Progress is reported every 5 seconds. 4 Extract PackagesLocalDirectory Extracts the zip (this takes several minutes) and deletes it, then extracts the FinOps tools VSIX into a FinOpsTools folder. 5 Restore cross-reference database Restores the .bak into LocalDB and deletes it. Skipped when the database of the existing configuration is already there. 6 Configure this machine Creates the runtime package links, writes the configuration file and sets it as the active configuration in the registry.

docs.title: When it fails: retry
docs.text:
If a step fails, the phase gets a red icon with the error, the view shows Retry and Done, and an error notification Environment setup failed: ... offers:

  • Retry: runs Connect to Environment again for the same URL without asking for it.
  • Show Log: opens the X++ output channel.
  • Report Problem: opens Report a Problem for this command.

Retrying is cheap because every step checks what is already on the machine (see What is reused on a second run). A download that failed or was cancelled leaves no partial file: it is written to <file>.partial and renamed only when complete, so a retry starts that file again.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.environmentUrl empty Dataverse URL of your default environment. Connect to Environment sets it when it is empty, or when no folder is open. See Select Environment. xpp.auth.clientId empty Optional Microsoft Entra app (client) ID for the sign-in, when your tenant does not allow VS Code's default sign-in for Dataverse. See Sign-In and Authentication.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The command is registered in src/extension.ts and implemented in src/setup.ts (input, progress, status in the view, retry). The setup itself is runUdeSetup in the VS Code-free core library: core/src/environment/setup.ts, with the Dataverse and download-service calls in core/src/environment/ude.ts. The VS Code side passes in the sign-in (dataverseTokens in src/ude.ts), the progress reporter and a cancellation signal. See Core Library.

docs.title: 1. Reading the environment from Dataverse
docs.text:
With the Dataverse token, setup calls two unbound Dataverse messages on https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2:

Message Values used RetrieveFinanceAndOperationsIntegrationDetails Url (finance and operations URL), TenantId msprov_getfinopsapplicationdetails applicationdeploymenttype (must be OnlineDev), applicationversion, platformversion, finopsenvironmentid

Each message is called as an action (POST) first, and as a function (GET with ()) if the org returns 404 or 405.

docs.title: 2. Downloads
docs.text:
For each asset, setup asks Microsoft's developer tools service for a time-limited download link:

GET https://developertools.powerplatform.microsoft.com/api/clientmetadata/<resource>?version=<application version with dashes>
Authorization: Bearer <Dataverse token>
dataverseEnvironmentUri: https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com/
Resource File systemmetadata PackagesLocalDirectory.zip crossreference DYNAMICSXREFDB.bak finopsvsix22 Microsoft.Dynamics.FinOps.ToolsVS2022.vsix

The service answers with a blob storage link, which is downloaded into the version folder %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<application version>\. If the server reports a content length and fewer bytes arrive, the download fails as incomplete. This service is not documented by Microsoft; F&O Studio calls it the same way Power Platform Tools does.

docs.title: 3. Extraction
docs.text: PackagesLocalDirectory.zip is extracted with %SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe into <version folder>\PackagesLocalDirectory, then the zip is deleted. The FinOps tools VSIX is extracted into <version folder>\FinOpsTools (it contains the debugger proxy used by the Debugger and Microsoft's configuration template). The VSIX file itself is kept, so Visual Studio Side by Side can install it into Visual Studio.

docs.title: 4. Cross-reference database
docs.text:
• The database name is XRef_<org><application version without dots>, for example XRef_yourorg10024701234. If that name already exists in LocalDB, _1 to _5 is appended.
  • The data and log files go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig\<configuration name>\ as DYNAMICSXREFDB1.mdf and DYNAMICSXREFDB1_log.ldf.
  • Before the restore, NETWORK SERVICE gets full control of the Dynamics365 folder, the version folder and the data folder (icacls), because a full SQL Server instance reads the files as that account. Failures of this step are ignored.
  • The restore runs in F&O Studio's server (--restore-xref), the same restore Visual Studio performs:
RESTORE DATABASE [XRef_...] FROM DISK = @bak WITH REPLACE,
  MOVE 'DYNAMICSXREFDB' TO @mdf, MOVE 'DYNAMICSXREFDB_log' TO @ldf, RECOVERY
  • The .bak is deleted after a successful restore.

docs.title: 5. Custom metadata folder
docs.text: Your own models live in the custom metadata folder (ModelStoreFolder). Setup keeps the folder of the active configuration when it is a UDE configuration and the folder exists, so every environment and version builds the same models. Otherwise it creates C:\CustomXppMetadata<random> (on the drive of your user profile).

docs.title: 6. Runtime package links
docs.text:
Setup creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\RuntimeSymLinks\<org> and fills it with directory junctions:

Junction Points to bin <version folder>\PackagesLocalDirectory\bin PackagesLocalDirectory <version folder>\PackagesLocalDirectory ZZZZ__<custom folder name> the custom metadata folder

An existing folder of that name is deleted first; if it cannot be deleted, <org>1, <org>2 and so on is used. This folder becomes RuntimePackagesDirectory, which the compiler and runtime see as one package folder.

docs.title: 7. Configuration file and registry
docs.text:
The configuration is written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig\<org>___<application version>.json. It starts from every member of Microsoft's Template_xppconfig.json (read from FinOpsTools\Resources when present, otherwise built-in values), keeps the values of an existing file for this org and version, and sets:

{
    "Description": "Unified development environment yourorg. FinOps application version 10.0.x. Configuration generated on <date> by X++ for VS Code.",
    "CloudInstanceURL": "https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com",
    "ReferencePackagesPaths": [ "...\\Dynamics365\\<version>\\PackagesLocalDirectory" ],
    "FrameworkDirectory": "...\\Dynamics365\\<version>\\PackagesLocalDirectory",
    "ModelStoreFolder": "C:\\CustomXppMetadata...",
    "DebugSourceFolder": "C:\\CustomXppMetadata...",
    "RuntimePackagesDirectory": "...\\Dynamics365\\RuntimeSymLinks\\yourorg",
    "CrossReferencesDbServerName": "(LocalDB)\\MSSQLLocalDB",
    "CrossReferencesDatabaseName": "XRef_..."
}

Then two values are written under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations:

  • CurrentMetadataConfig = the configuration file
  • FrameworkDirectory = the PackagesLocalDirectory folder

This registry key is where Visual Studio reads its active configuration too, so after a connect Visual Studio uses the same environment. See Visual Studio Side by Side.

docs.title: 8. Switching the window to the environment
docs.text: After setup, the window works with the new environment (Select Environment explains how this is stored per workspace). The metadata servers restart, and the Application Explorer, project view, open designers and unchanged code views reload. No window reload is needed. The MCP server for Copilot is restarted with the new configuration as well.

docs.title: What is reused on a second run
docs.text:
Item Considered done when PackagesLocalDirectory download and extraction <version folder>\PackagesLocalDirectory exists Cross-reference download and restore the existing configuration names a database and that database exists in LocalDB FinOps tools download <version folder>\FinOpsTools exists Any download the downloaded file is already in the version folder FinOps tools extraction FinOpsTools\extension.vsixmanifest exists

The configure phase always runs again: links are recreated, and the configuration and registry are rewritten.

docs.title: Disk space
docs.text: Each application version takes its own folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365. PackagesLocalDirectory is about 16 GB. After an update, remove versions you no longer need with Clean Up Old Application Versions… (Version Drift Guard).

docs.title: Check Environment Connection
docs.text:
F&O Studio: Check Environment Connection (also in the Environment group and the status bar menu) runs every read-only step of the setup without downloading anything:

  1. Signs in.
  2. Reads the environment (type, application, platform, finance and operations URL).
  3. Asks for each asset's download link and reports its size.

The output goes to the X++ channel:

--- Checking https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com
1. Signed in.
2. Environment: type OnlineDev, application 10.0.x, platform 7.0.x, F&O https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com
3. PackagesLocalDirectory.zip: download link OK, ...
3. DYNAMICSXREFDB.bak: download link OK, ...
3. Microsoft.Dynamics.FinOps.ToolsVS2022.vsix: download link OK, ...
All read-only setup steps succeeded.

If the environment is not OnlineDev, the log says setup would stop there. If no environment is selected yet, a successful check selects it. If this window works with another environment, you are offered Use This Environment.

docs.title: Show Active Environment
docs.text: F&O Studio: Show Active Environment (Show Active Configuration in the view and status bar menu) writes the active configuration as JSON to the X++ output channel: name, configuration file, framework and bin folders, reference package paths, custom metadata folder, runtime packages folder, cross-reference server and database, business database, application version, web client URL, Dataverse URL and whether it is a local (cloud-hosted or VHD) environment.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Unified developer environments only. Sandboxes and other environment types are refused.
  • The developer tools download service is undocumented; if Microsoft changes it, setup can fail at the download phase. The manual steps Microsoft documents for Visual Studio (connect with Power Platform Tools) produce a configuration F&O Studio also reads.
  • The cross-reference database always goes to (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB.
  • Interrupted extraction is not detected: if the PackagesLocalDirectory folder exists, extraction is treated as done.
  • Old cross-reference databases are not removed when you clean up versions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "That is a portal page..." in the URL box You pasted a Power Platform admin center or maker portal link Copy the environment's Environment URL (https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com). "No Dataverse environment found for ..." A finance and operations URL whose org has no regional Dataverse host that resolves Enter the Dataverse URL directly. "Not signed in to ..." The sign-in was cancelled Run the command again and complete the sign-in. If your tenant blocks VS Code's sign-in, set xpp.auth.clientId. "Not a unified developer environment (type ...)" The environment is not OnlineDev (for example a sandbox) Use a unified developer environment. "SQL Server Express LocalDB is not reachable with Windows authentication" LocalDB not installed or instance missing Install SQL Server Express LocalDB or run sqllocaldb create MSSQLLocalDB -s, then Retry. "At least 16 GB free disk space is needed on C:\ ..." Not enough space on the drive of %LOCALAPPDATA% Free space (for example with Clean Up Old Application Versions…) and retry. "DevTools service returned 4xx for systemmetadata" The download service refused the request Check access to the environment with Check Environment Connection; retry later. "Download of ... was incomplete" or failed Network interruption Retry; finished downloads are kept. "Extracting PackagesLocalDirectory.zip failed" Disk full or files locked Free space, then retry. Build or Application Explorer misses standard packages after a cancelled extraction PackagesLocalDirectory exists but is incomplete; setup treats it as done Delete <version folder>\PackagesLocalDirectory. If the zip is still there, Connect to Environment… extracts it again; otherwise it downloads it. "Cross-reference restore failed: ..." LocalDB could not read or write the files, or the name exists Check the message in the log; free space; retry.

docs.title: Copilot Activity
docs.text: The Copilot Activity view lists every F&O Studio agent tool Copilot calls, newest first: the tool, the element it worked on, the time and how long it took. When Copilot creates, changes or deletes one of your elements, a notification tells you right away and offers the change as a diff. It is the audit trail of what the agent did with your metadata. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Follow what an agent is doing while it works: which elements it reads, which searches it runs, how long each takes.
  • Review every element change the agent made, as a diff against the state before the change.
  • Find a failed tool call and see the arguments the agent sent.
  • Check that a read-only agent really only read.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• GitHub Copilot in agent mode, using the F&O Studio MCP server (registered automatically when an environment is selected; see MCP Agent Tools).
  • Nothing to switch on: F&O Studio starts Copilot's MCP server with activity logging.

docs.title: Open the view
docs.text:
The view is in the F&O Studio panel (next to Results and Infolog). You can also open it from:

  • the Dynamics 365 view: Copilot > Copilot Activity;
  • the empty view's Open Chat link, which opens the Chat view.

When there is no activity yet, the view says: "The F&O Studio tools Copilot calls, and the elements it creates or changes, appear here."

docs.title: Read the entries
docs.text:
Each entry shows:

Part Content Icon A magnifier for reads, a pencil for element writes, an error icon for failed calls Label The tool name without the xpp_ prefix, then the element name when the call had one, e.g. read_object PurchReqTable, analyze_performance CustCollectionLetterCreate, search_code Description The local time of the call and its duration in milliseconds Tooltip The full tool name, "succeeded" or "failed", the duration and the call's arguments as JSON

The view shows the 200 most recent calls. It updates on its own while Copilot works (it checks the log every two seconds).

docs.title: Review a change
docs.text:
After the agent creates, changes or deletes one of your elements successfully, a notification appears, for example:

Copilot changed CustGroup.ContosoExtension (TableExtension).

with up to two buttons:

Button What it does View Changes Opens a diff: the element file before the change on the left, the current file on the right, titled <name> (before Copilot ↔ now). For a new element it opens the new file; for a deleted element, the file as it was. Open Opens the element in its designer (not offered after a delete).

In the view, click a write entry (pencil icon) to open the same diff, or use the View Changes icon that appears on the entry when you hover over it.

The diff compares the element's metadata XML. It is read-only review; to undo a change use a Copilot checkpoint or source control.

docs.title: Clear the view
docs.text: Click Clear Copilot Activity in the view's title bar (or run F&O Studio: Clear Copilot Activity from the Command Palette). It empties the log file; the element snapshots stay on disk until newer ones replace them.

docs.title: What counts as a write
docs.text:
The tools that create, change or delete elements are logged as writes and get the before/after snapshot:

Tool Write xpp_create_object Yes (no "before" file) xpp_update_object Yes xpp_delete_object Yes (no "after" file) Every other tool, including xpp_create_label, xpp_add_to_project, xpp_set_report_design, xpp_build Logged as a call, without a diff

Label, project and report design changes are still listed as calls. A checkpoint covers them on revert: label files and the project file are copied when the checkpoint starts, and report design changes go through the same element snapshot as other element edits.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. F&O Studio registers Copilot's MCP server (src/mcpProvider.ts) with the argument --activity-log. Only that server process logs; the extension's own server processes don't.
  2. For each tools/call, the server's ToolRouter reads objectType and objectName from the arguments. For tools with the WritesElement trait it first copies the element's XML file from your custom metadata folder to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\snapshots\ (the "before" file).
  3. After the call, server/Host/ActivityLog.cs appends one JSON line to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activity.jsonl: time, tool, duration, success, arguments (cut at 400 characters), object type and name, whether it was a write, and the paths of the before and after files.
  4. The extension's src/activity.ts watches the file, shows the last 200 entries, and raises the notification for each new successful write.
  5. View Changes opens only absolute paths to .xml files, using VS Code's diff editor.

Example log line (shortened):

{"time":"2026-11-25T14:51:01.000Z","tool":"xpp_update_object","ms":812,"ok":true,
 "arguments":"{\"objectType\":\"AxClass\",\"objectName\":\"ContosoCreditHoldService\",...}",
 "objectType":"AxClass","objectName":"ContosoCreditHoldService","write":true,
 "before":"C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\XppVsCode\\snapshots\\20261125145100123_AxClass_ContosoCreditHoldService.xml",
 "after":"C:\\CustomMetadata\\ContosoExtensions\\ContosoExtensions\\AxClass\\ContosoCreditHoldService.xml"}

Limits that keep the files small:

Limit Value Entries shown in the view 200 Log size before it is trimmed 2 MB (the older half is dropped) Arguments kept per call 400 characters Snapshot files kept 200 (oldest deleted)

The log is per Windows user (%LOCALAPPDATA%), so every VS Code window shows the same activity.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only calls to the F&O Studio MCP server are logged. Calls to other MCP servers (for example the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server), files Copilot edits directly, and terminal commands are not in this view; VS Code's chat shows those.
  • The language model tools xppOpenElement, xppRunTests and xppQueryData run in the extension, not the MCP server, and are not listed.
  • Snapshots exist only for elements in your custom metadata folder. A diff can't be shown when the before file was removed by the 200-snapshot limit.
  • A snapshot shows the file before the call, not before the first change of the session: for the whole session's changes use a checkpoint or Git (Show Changed Elements).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The view stays empty while Copilot works Copilot is not using the F&O Studio MCP server, or it was started without activity logging (for example a server configured by hand) Use the server F&O Studio registers (MCP server "F&O Studio"); check the X++ output channel for "X++ MCP server: config ...". No notification after a change The call failed, or the tool is not an element write (labels, project, report design, build) Check the entry's icon and tooltip. View Changes opens only one file The element was created (no before file) or deleted (no after file), or the snapshot was trimmed Use Git or a checkpoint for older changes.
