docs.title: Copilot Agents
docs.text:
F&O Studio adds 24 GitHub Copilot agents for Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations work. Each agent is a persona with its own instructions, its own way of working and the next agent to hand off to: an X++ developer, a code reviewer, a troubleshooter, a security analyst, a functional explainer, a data investigator and so on. The agents work on the real metadata through the F&O Studio agent tools (xpp_*), and the functional agents also look at the live environment through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

This page explains what the agents are, how you pick one, how Copilot routes requests to them, and the rules every agent follows. The agents themselves are described on Agents for Developers and Agents for Functional Consultants.

docs.title: When to use them
docs.text:
• You want Copilot to do D365FO work the way an experienced developer or consultant would: read standard code first, extend instead of copy, build and check, answer with evidence.
  • You want a specific kind of answer: a review ordered by severity, a design document, a fit-gap table, test scenarios with menu paths, a role design with license cost.
  • You are a functional consultant and want answers in business terms (menu paths, field labels, setup), not X++.

For a quick question you can also stay in the default Copilot agent mode: the routing instructions (see below) make Copilot suggest the right F&O agent when one fits.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Need Why GitHub Copilot in VS Code, chat in agent mode The agents are VS Code custom agents (contributes.chatAgents). F&O Studio connected to an environment The F&O Studio MCP server (the xpp_* tools) starts only when the active D365FO configuration can be read. See Connect to Environment. A D365FO project (optional) Tools that add elements to a project or build scope=project need an active project. See D365FO Projects. Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server (optional) Lets agents see forms, setup and data in the running environment. Needed for the functional agents' live checks and for Verify Changes in the Running App. Database access (optional) xppQueryData reads the business database on a development environment. See Database Access.

docs.title: The agents
docs.text:
Agent For Changes things? Hands off to F&O Developer Developer Yes, with permission Code Reviewer, Test Engineer F&O Code Reviewer Developer No (read-only) Developer, Release Manager F&O Support Developer No Developer F&O Solution Designer Both No Developer, Test Scenarios F&O Architect Both No Solution Designer F&O Security & License Both No Developer F&O Performance Developer No Developer F&O Upgrade Reviewer Developer No Developer F&O Integration Both Yes, with permission Data Migration F&O Test Engineer Developer Yes, with permission Code Reviewer F&O Report Developer Developer Yes, with permission Code Reviewer, Report Builder F&O Report Builder Developer Yes, with permission Code Reviewer, Release Manager F&O Workflow & Events Developer Yes, with permission Code Reviewer F&O Release Manager Developer Yes, with permission Release Notes F&O Code Archaeologist Developer No Developer F&O Functional Explainer Functional No Setup Advisor F&O Setup Advisor Functional Yes, with permission Data Investigator F&O Data Investigator Functional No Setup Advisor F&O Functional Triage Functional No Support F&O Role Designer Functional No Developer, Security & License F&O Test Scenarios Functional No (none) F&O Fit-Gap Analyst Functional No Solution Designer F&O Data Migration Functional Yes, with permission Integration F&O Release Notes Functional No (none)

"For" is the audience the agent writes for. "Both" agents serve developers and consultants alike.

docs.title: How to use them
docs.text:
1. Open the Chat view and switch it to agent mode.
  2. Open the agent picker and choose an F&O agent, for example F&O Developer or F&O Functional Explainer. Each agent shows a hint of what to type (for example "The error message, call stack, batch job or trace").
  3. Describe the task. Name objects exactly when you know them (CustGroup, SalesFormLetter.run), paste error messages as shown, and say which environment you are working on.
  4. Read the answer. Agents name their evidence: elements, methods, fields, labels, records and menu paths, and say what they could not check.
  5. When the agent finishes, the chat shows handoff buttons such as Review the changes or Write tests. A handoff switches to the next agent and fills in its prompt ("Review the changes made above."); you send it yourself.

Example flow for a small feature:

F&O Solution Designer  "Add a 'Credit hold reason' to customer groups and show it on the customer group form."
   -> Build it
F&O Developer          "Implement the design above."
   -> Review the changes
F&O Code Reviewer      "Review the changes made above."
   -> Prepare the release
F&O Release Manager    "The review is done. Prepare this change for deployment."
   -> Write release notes
F&O Release Notes      "Write release notes for the release above."

docs.title: Coming from @fno
docs.text:
The @fno chat participant was removed because VS Code retires chat participants. Its commands map to agents:

@fno command Agent /design F&O Solution Designer /extend F&O Developer /explain F&O Code Archaeologist (code) or F&O Functional Explainer (business) /review F&O Code Reviewer /support F&O Support /performance F&O Performance

docs.title: Routing: when you haven't picked an agent
docs.text:
F&O Studio also contributes routing instructions (agents/fno-agents.instructions.md, contributed as chatInstructions). They describe every agent in one table and tell Copilot what to do with a D365FO request when you have not selected an F&O agent:

  • If one agent clearly fits, Copilot says which one in one line and offers to switch to it.
  • If a self-contained part of the task clearly fits an agent (for example a review after a change, or triage of a pasted error), Copilot may run that agent as a subagent and use its result. It does not do this for small questions it can answer directly.
  • Agents started this way follow the same change rules as when you pick them yourself.

Each agent also carries the Right agent rule: if your request fits another F&O agent better, it says which one in one line and offers to switch, and for a self-contained part of the task it may run that agent as a subagent.

docs.title: Rules every agent follows
docs.text: All agents share a small set of rules, written once in scripts/agent-definitions.js and added to each agent's instructions. Which rules an agent gets depends on its role.

docs.title: Changes need permission and a non-production environment
docs.text:
Agents that may change things (Developer, Integration, Test Engineer, Report Developer, Report Builder, Workflow & Events, Release Manager, Setup Advisor, Data Migration) carry this rule:

  • They create, change or delete data, setup, security or metadata only after you explicitly allow that change.
  • They do so only in a development, sandbox or build environment, never in production.
  • If they don't know which kind of environment it is, they ask. An unknown environment is treated as production.
  • Where they may not change something, they describe the change instead: the menu path and values, or the code.

The same rule is in the routing instructions, so it also applies when Copilot runs an agent as a subagent.

docs.title: Read-only role
docs.text: The other agents are read-only: they don't create, change or delete elements, files, data or setup, and they don't build, package or deploy. They recommend the change and offer the next agent through their handoffs.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Every agent bases its answer on what the tools return and names it. It says what it could not check. For one exact metadata object name it uses xpp_find_object with the object type and exactMatch=true; xpp_list_objects is for substring searches. A "no match" only means no match in the loaded metadata, not that the object does not exist anywhere. It calls xpp_get_environment only when the request needs environment, project or model context.

docs.title: Live environment (Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server)
docs.text:
Agents that need to see setup, forms or data as users see them use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server's tools when they are available:

Tool group What it does data_* Find, read, create, update and delete records through data entities form_* Open menu items and forms, read and set controls, filter and sort grids, open lookups, save api_* Find and invoke actions

The ERP MCP server is Microsoft's, not part of F&O Studio; you connect it to VS Code yourself. Microsoft's setup page: Use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in VS Code. When it is missing, the agent suggests connecting it, or opens the environment with the browser tools. On a development environment, xppQueryData reads the database (SELECT only).

Note that the ERP MCP server can change data and save forms. The change rule above is what keeps agents from doing that without your permission or in production.

docs.title: Without a development environment
docs.text: The functional agents (except Role Designer and Release Notes) also carry this rule: without a development environment the F&O Studio tools (xpp_*) are not available, so the agent works from the live environment and documentation (xpp_search_docs when available, otherwise Microsoft Learn on the web) and says that metadata-based checks were skipped.

docs.title: Business language
docs.text: The functional agents answer for a functional consultant: menu paths, fields as labelled in the client, setup and data. They show X++ only when you ask.

docs.title: Tools the agents use
docs.text:
Source Tools F&O Studio MCP server xpp_find_object, xpp_read_object, xpp_create_object, xpp_update_object, xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice, xpp_find_message_source, xpp_analyze_security, xpp_analyze_performance, xpp_analyze_trace, xpp_diff_changes, xpp_package, report tools and more. See MCP Agent Tools. F&O Studio language model tools xppOpenElement (show an element in the editor or designer), xppRunTests (run SysTest classes on the environment), xppQueryData (one read-only SELECT on the business database) Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server data_*, form_*, api_* VS Code Browser, files, terminal, as your Copilot setup allows

The agent files do not restrict the tool list. Read-only agents stay read-only because of their instructions; the F&O Studio server itself enforces that writes go only to your own models, and the Copilot scope if you set one.

docs.title: Keeping control
docs.text:
• Copilot Activity lists every F&O Studio tool call and lets you see each element change as a diff.
  • Copilot Checkpoints and Scope lets you revert everything Copilot changed since a checkpoint, and limit which elements it may change.
  • Team Rules adds your team's naming and coding rules to the agent instructions.
  • Verify Changes in the Running App has Copilot check your deployed changes through the ERP MCP server.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• scripts/agent-definitions.js defines every agent once: id, name, audience, description, argument hint, rules, instructions body and handoffs.
  • scripts/build-agents.js (npm run agents) writes agents/<id>.agent.md for each agent, the routing file agents/fno-agents.instructions.md, and the chatAgents / chatInstructions contributions in package.json. node scripts/build-agents.js --check fails when a generated file is out of date, and checks that read-only agents never carry the change rule and that every handoff points to a known agent.
  • Each .agent.md file has front matter (name, description, argument-hint, handoffs with send: false), then the instructions, a Rules section and a Next steps section that lists the handoffs.
  • The F&O Studio MCP server returns its own system prompt as MCP instructions on initialize, plus your Team Rules when the repository has them. The agent instructions come on top of that.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The agents need GitHub Copilot's agent mode and custom agent support in VS Code.
  • Read-only is an instruction, not a tool restriction. Use Copilot scope when you want the server to refuse changes outside a set of elements.
  • The non-production rule depends on the agent knowing the environment type. Tell it, or it treats the environment as production and describes changes instead of making them.
  • Live checks need the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, which you set up separately.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The F&O agents are not in the agent picker Copilot chat is not in agent mode, or custom agents are not available in your VS Code / Copilot version Switch the chat to agent mode; update VS Code and the Copilot extension. The agent says the xpp_* tools are not available The F&O Studio MCP server did not start (no active D365FO configuration) Select an environment (Select Environment); check the X++ output channel for "MCP server not started". A functional agent says it can't see the environment The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server is not connected Connect it as described on Microsoft Learn (link above). The agent describes a change instead of making it It does not know the environment is non-production, or you have not allowed the change Say which environment it is (development, sandbox, build) and allow the change explicitly. A write is refused with "outside the elements the user allows Copilot to change" A Copilot scope is set Add the element to the scope or remove the limit: Set Copilot Scope…

docs.title: Copilot Checkpoints and Scope
docs.text: Checkpoints and scope keep Copilot's changes to your metadata under your control. A checkpoint records the state of every element before Copilot first changes it, so you can revert everything Copilot did since the checkpoint in one step: changed elements go back to their earlier state, new elements are deleted, and the project file and label files are restored. A scope limits which existing elements Copilot may change; the F&O Studio server refuses any other write. Both are enforced by the server Copilot uses, not by the agent's instructions. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Checkpoint: before you let an agent build or change something, so you can undo the whole session without Git gymnastics. Especially for exploratory prompts ("try a Chain of Command approach and build it").
  • Scope: when the task is narrow ("fix the validation in these three classes") and you don't want the agent to touch anything else in your models, even by mistake.
  • Both together for the safest setup: scope to the project's elements, then start a checkpoint.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio connected to an environment, and Copilot using the F&O Studio MCP server (registered automatically; see MCP Agent Tools).
  • For The Project's Elements and Pick Elements... scopes: an open D365FO project (D365FO Projects).
  • Copilot can only change elements in your own (custom) models anyway: standard elements are always refused and are changed through extensions. Checkpoints and scope work within your models.

docs.title: Where to find the commands
docs.text: Command (Command Palette, category F&O Studio) Also in Start Copilot Checkpoint Dynamics 365 view > Copilot > Start Checkpoint Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… Dynamics 365 view > Copilot > Revert Copilot Changes…; the checkpoint menu End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes) The checkpoint menu Set Copilot Scope… Dynamics 365 view > Copilot > Set Copilot Scope… Checkpoint menu (Copilot Checkpoint…, not in the Command Palette) The status bar item (click it)

docs.title: The status bar item
docs.text:
While a checkpoint is open or a scope is set, a status bar item appears on the left:

Shows Meaning History icon and a number, e.g. 3 A checkpoint is open; Copilot has changed 3 elements since it started (refreshed every 10 seconds) Lock icon A scope is set Both Both are active

The tooltip says, for example, "Copilot checkpoint: 3 element(s) changed. Click to review or revert." and "Copilot may change 12 element(s) and the ones it creates (F&O Studio: Set Copilot Scope)." Clicking it opens the checkpoint menu. With neither active, the item is hidden.

docs.title: Start a checkpoint
docs.text:
1. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint.
  2. F&O Studio copies the active project file (.rnrproj) and every label text file of your custom models, and records that a checkpoint is open.
  3. A message confirms: "Copilot checkpoint started: every element Copilot changes from now on can be reverted."

If a checkpoint is already open, you are asked "A Copilot checkpoint is already open." with Keep Its Changes and Start a New One (ends the old checkpoint, keeping its changes) or Cancel.

docs.title: Work with Copilot
docs.text:
Use any agent as usual. Before Copilot's first change to an element, the server saves that element's state (or notes that it is new). Later changes to the same element don't overwrite the saved state, so revert always goes back to the state at the checkpoint.

The element writes covered are the bridge actions that create or edit elements: xpp_create_object, xpp_update_object, xpp_delete_object and report design changes (xpp_set_report_design).

docs.title: Review the checkpoint
docs.text:
Click the status bar item. A list titled "Copilot checkpoint: N element(s) changed" shows:

  • each element Copilot touched, with an edit icon for changed elements and an add icon and "(new)" for new ones; pick one to open it in its designer;
  • Revert Everything Copilot Changed…;
  • Keep the Changes (End Checkpoint).

If no checkpoint is open, clicking the status bar item starts one.

docs.title: Revert
docs.text:
1. Run Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… (or pick Revert Everything Copilot Changed… in the menu).
  2. A confirmation lists up to 15 elements as "Restore " or "Delete ", and warns: "The project file and label files go back to their state at the checkpoint, including your own changes to them since."
  3. Choose Revert. A progress notification "Reverting Copilot's changes…" appears.
  4. The server restores every element:
  5. elements that existed: saved back through the metadata API to their state at the checkpoint (an element Copilot deleted is created again);
  6. elements Copilot created: deleted.
  7. The project file and label files are copied back from the checkpoint.
  8. Application Explorer and the project view refresh.
  9. On success the checkpoint ends and a message says, for example, "Restored 4 element(s)." If some elements fail, an error lists them, and the checkpoint stays open so you can fix the cause and revert again.

docs.title: End a checkpoint (keep the changes)
docs.text: Run End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes) or pick Keep the Changes (End Checkpoint). You are asked: "Keep Copilot's changes and end the checkpoint? They can no longer be reverted here (only through Git)." Choose End Checkpoint. The saved states are deleted.

docs.title: Set a scope
docs.text:
1. Run Set Copilot Scope…. The picker title shows the current state, e.g. "Elements Copilot may change (now: no limit)".
  2. Choose one option:
Option Effect The Project's Elements Copilot may change the elements in the open project, plus new elements it creates Pick Elements… A multi-select list of the project's elements; Copilot may change the ones you tick, plus new elements it creates No Limit Copilot may change any element of your models (the default)
  1. A status bar message confirms, for example "Copilot may change 12 element(s) and the ones it creates", and the lock icon appears in the status bar.

The scope is a fixed list taken when you set it. Elements you add to the project later are not in the scope until you set it again.

docs.title: What happens when Copilot goes outside the scope
docs.text:
Before every create, edit or delete from Copilot, the server checks the scope:

  • The element is in the scope: the write goes ahead.
  • The element doesn't exist yet (Copilot creates it): the write goes ahead, and the new element joins the scope, so Copilot can keep working on what it created.
  • The element exists and is not in the scope: the write is refused. The agent receives:
AxClass 'SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension' is outside the elements the user allows Copilot to change
(F&O Studio: Set Copilot Scope). Ask the user to add it to the scope; the allowed elements are:
AxTable/ContosoCreditHold, AxClass/ContosoCreditHoldService, ...

The agent then asks you. To allow it, run Set Copilot Scope… again and include the element, or choose No Limit.

Scope applies only to Copilot. Your own edits in the designers and the code editor are never limited.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The extension and Copilot's MCP server are separate processes. They share one small state file:

%LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\agentSession.json
{"checkpoint":"2026-11-25T14-51-01-123Z","scope":["AxTable/ContosoCreditHold","AxClass/ContosoCreditHoldService"]}
  1. src/agentSession.ts writes the file when you start or end a checkpoint or set a scope. At checkpoint start it also creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\checkpoints\<id>\files\ with copies of the project file and label text files, listed in files.json.txt.
  2. Copilot's MCP server is started by F&O Studio with --activity-log; only that process gets the agent write checks. In the bridge dispatcher (MetaModelBridgeServer.cs), every action registered as WriteKind.Edit or WriteKind.Create first passes the custom-model check, then AgentScopeDenial and, when allowed, BeforeAgentWrite (MetaModelBridge.AgentSession.cs). Check-only calls (checkOnly) are not affected.
  3. BeforeAgentWrite reads the element through the metadata provider and serializes it into checkpoints\<id>\<type>__<name>.json, with its model, its CLR type and whether it existed. A file that already exists is kept, so only the state before the first change is saved. If the element can't be serialized, the entry records why, and the change itself still goes ahead.
  4. The checkpoint menu and status bar call the bridge action checkpoint_entries; revert calls revert_checkpoint on the extension's own server. It deserializes each saved element and saves it with the provider's Update (or Create if it no longer exists) into its model, deletes elements that didn't exist, then reloads the metadata.
  5. The extension copies the project and label files back, refreshes the trees, and ends the checkpoint on success.

Because the state lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%, one checkpoint and one scope apply to every VS Code window and Copilot session of the same Windows user.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only writes through the F&O Studio MCP server are covered. Files Copilot edits directly, terminal commands, and changes made through other MCP servers (such as data or setup changed through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server) are not part of the checkpoint or the scope.
  • Labels and the project file are restored as whole files: revert also undoes your own changes to them since the checkpoint. Labels and project membership are not limited by the scope.
  • Revert works only for elements in your custom models. An element whose state couldn't be saved is reported ("its state before the change could not be saved ... restore it from source control").
  • Builds, packages and deployments are not undone by a revert. Build again after reverting.
  • One checkpoint at a time. Ending a checkpoint deletes its saved states; use Git for anything older.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No Copilot checkpoint is open." You ran revert without starting a checkpoint Start one before the next Copilot session; use Git (Show Changed Elements) for this one. "Open a D365FO project first." when setting the scope No active project Open a project, or choose No Limit. Revert reports "not in one of your models" The saved element belongs to a model that is not a custom model Restore it from source control. Revert reports "cannot be saved through the metadata API" or "unknown element type" The element type can't be restored that way Restore it from source control. Revert failed for some elements and "The checkpoint stays open." At least one element could not be restored Fix the cause (for example a locked file), then revert again; or restore those from Git and end the checkpoint. The agent says an element is outside the allowed elements A scope is set and the element is not in it Add it with Set Copilot Scope… or choose No Limit. The status bar count stays at 0 while Copilot changes elements Copilot isn't using the F&O Studio MCP server registered by F&O Studio Check the X++ output channel for the MCP server line; see Copilot Activity.

docs.title: Copy Name and Open in Browser
docs.text: Small commands that save typing and switching windows. Copy Name and Copy X++ Reference put an element's name, or the X++ that names it (tableStr(CustTable), fieldStr(CustTable, AccountNum)), on the clipboard. Open in Browser opens a menu item, form or class in the Finance and Operations web client, and Open Table Browser opens a table in the table browser, like Visual Studio's startup object and its Open table browser command.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You write X++ and need an element or field name spelled exactly: copy it from the tree or the designer.
  • You write tableStr, formStr, fieldStr or formControlStr calls and want them right the first time.
  • You changed a form or a class and want to try it in the web client without typing a URL.
  • You want to look at a table's rows in the web client's table browser.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Copy commands: nothing beyond the metadata on this machine.
  • Open in Browser and Open Table Browser: the web client URL of your environment. F&O Studio takes it from the active configuration when it has one; otherwise from the setting xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl, and if that is empty it asks once and saves your answer.
  • Open in Browser on a form needs the cross-reference database, to find the display menu item that opens the form.
  • To see your latest changes in the browser, build and deploy them first (Build Project and Model, Deploy to Environment).

docs.title: Copy Name
docs.text:
1. Right-click an element in the Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view, or a node in the Element Designer.
  2. Choose Copy Name.
  3. The name is on the clipboard; the status bar shows Copied for a few seconds.

    In the designer, Copy Name copies the name of the right-clicked node: a field (AccountNum), a method (validateWrite), a data source, a control. It is not offered on folder nodes and event nodes.

docs.title: Copy X++ Reference
docs.text:
1. Right-click an element (or a designer node) and choose Copy X++ Reference.
  2. The X++ expression is on the clipboard; the status bar shows Copied .

docs.title: Elements
docs.text:
Element type Copied Table, view, data entity tableStr(CustTable) Class classStr(SalesFormLetter) Form formStr(CustTable) Base enum enumStr(SalesStatus) Extended data type extendedTypeStr(CustGroupId) Query queryStr(<Name>) Display, action, output menu item menuItemDisplayStr(CustTable), menuItemActionStr(<Name>), menuItemOutputStr(<Name>) Configuration key, license code configurationKeyStr(<Name>), licenseCodeStr(<Name>) Menu, tile menuStr(<Name>), tileStr(<Name>) Workflow approval, task, type workflowApprovalStr(<Name>), workflowTaskStr(<Name>), workflowTypeStr(<Name>)

In the Application Explorer and the project view, the command is shown for the element types in this table. In the designer of an extension, the root node copies the reference of the element it extends: the designer of CustTable.ContosoExtensions (table extension) copies tableStr(CustTable).

docs.title: Designer nodes
docs.text:
On nodes inside an element (the Element Designer), Copy X++ Reference copies the intrinsic for that member:

Node Copied Field of a table, view, data entity or map fieldStr(CustTable, AccountNum) Index of a table, view, data entity or map indexStr(CustTable, AccountIdx) Value of a base enum SalesStatus::Invoiced Data source of a form formDataSourceStr(CustTable, CustTable) Field of a form data source formDataFieldStr(CustTable, CustTable, AccountNum) Control of a form formControlStr(CustTable, <Control>)

In an extension's designer, these use the base element's name, so a field of CustTable.ContosoExtensions copies fieldStr(CustTable, <Field>).

Paste the result into code, for example:

FormDataSource ds = _formRun.dataSource(formDataSourceStr(CustTable, CustTable));
str fieldName = fieldStr(CustTable, AccountNum);

docs.title: Open in Browser
docs.text:
Open in Browser opens an element in the web client of the active environment, in your default browser.

Element URL opened (after the web client address) Display menu item /?mi=<Name> Output menu item /?mi=output:<Name> Action menu item /?mi=action:<Name> Class /?mi=SysClassRunner&cls=<Name> (the class runner, as Visual Studio's startup object does) Form The display menu item that opens it (see below)

Steps:

  1. Right-click a menu item, class or form in the Application Explorer, the project view or the designer root, and choose Open in Browser.
  2. For a form, F&O Studio looks in the cross-reference database for display menu items that open it. One is used directly; with several, you pick one (Display menu items that open ). With none: No display menu item opens . Create one, then open it in the browser.
  3. The browser opens the URL, for example https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com/?mi=CustTable.

    4. To add a company to the URL (&cmp=USMF) or open another page, edit the URL in the browser.

    From the Command Palette or the Dynamics 365 view (View and run > Open in Browser…) there is no element to open; you get Right-click a form, menu item, class or table in Application Explorer and choose Open in Browser.

docs.title: Open Table Browser
docs.text:
Open Table Browser opens a table in the web client's table browser: /?mi=SysTableBrowser&tableName=<Name>.

  • Right-click a table (Application Explorer, project view or designer root) and choose Open Table Browser.
  • From the Command Palette or the Dynamics 365 view (View and run > Open Table Browser…), enter the table name in Open table browser.

On tables, Open Table Browser replaces Open in Browser.

To look at rows inside VS Code instead, with enum names and a company filter, use Browse Table Data.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl empty Web client URL (for example https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com) for Open in Browser and Open Table Browser, used when the selected environment's configuration has none. Filled in the user settings the first time F&O Studio asks for it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Copy Name and Copy X++ Reference are registered in src/d365Tools.ts and write to the clipboard through vscode.env.clipboard. The expressions come from intrinsicReference in src/aot.ts; the designer computes them for each node and passes them with the right-click context.
  • Open in Browser and Open Table Browser: openInBrowser in src/d365Tools.ts. The web client address is:
  • the web client URL of the active configuration, unless you selected a unified environment whose metadata is not on this machine (its configuration would name another environment's web client);
  • else xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl;
  • else a prompt (Finance and operations URL, an https URL), saved to xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl in your user settings.
  • For a form, the display menu item is found with the bridge action where_used on the form (cross-reference database), keeping references from display menu items.
  • The URL is opened with vscode.env.openExternal, so your default browser and its sign-in are used.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Open in Browser does not add a company (cmp) or other parameters.
  • Classes open through SysClassRunner, which starts the class through its main method; a class without one does not run.
  • Forms need a display menu item that references them and an up-to-date cross-reference database.
  • Elements you changed run in the browser only after they are built and deployed to that environment.
  • Copy X++ Reference has no intrinsic for some element types (for example security privileges and duties, and extension elements in the trees); the command is not shown for them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No display menu item opens . Create one, then open it in the browser. No display menu item references the form, or the cross-reference database is out of date Create a menu item, or build with cross references (xpp.build.crossReference) The browser opens another environment xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl points elsewhere, or the configuration's web client is another environment Fix the setting; Select Environment can't be opened in the browser. The element type has no web client URL Use a menu item that opens it Copy X++ Reference is missing The element type has no naming intrinsic Use Copy Name The page says the menu item does not exist It is not deployed to that environment yet Build and deploy

docs.title: Core Library
docs.text:
@fno-studio/core is F&O Studio's library for cloud operations on Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations unified developer environments (UDE), without VS Code. It holds the Dataverse client, deploy and database sync, SysTest runs, just-in-time SQL credentials, the data client, environment discovery, the UDE connection check and setup, and deployed-versus-built staleness. The F&O Studio extension uses it, and so can other hosts such as a command-line plugin.

It lives in the core/ folder of the repository and builds to core/dist (JavaScript and .d.ts). It runs on Windows with Node 20 or later.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You work on F&O Studio and change deploy, sync, tests, database credentials or environment setup. That code belongs in core, not in src/.
  • You build another host (a CLI, an agent plugin) that needs the same cloud operations and wants to reuse them.

If you only use the extension, you do not need this page. See Deploy-to-Environment, Run-Tests and Database-Access instead.

docs.title: Design: the host supplies everything interactive
docs.text:
The core never signs in, shows UI or reads settings. The host passes these in (core/src/host.ts):

Interface Shape VS Code host implementation TokenProvider getToken(resource, { interactive }): Promise<string \| undefined>; scope <resource>/.default dataverseTokens in src/ude.ts: VS Code's Microsoft account, interactive or silent Log line(text) an output channel Progress report(message) a progress notification AbortSignal standard abortSignalOf / withAbortSignal in src/coreHost.ts turn a CancellationToken into one settings plain option objects read by the extension from xpp.* settings and passed in

OperationOptions (log, progress, signal) is the common option bag of long-running operations. onAbort(signal, listener) runs a listener when a signal aborts (on the next tick when it already has, as a VS Code cancellation token does).

The no-VS Code rule is enforced by node scripts/check-core.js. It fails when a file in core/src, core/dist or core/test imports vscode or @vscode/*, when a relative import reaches outside core/, when core/package.json has a VS Code dependency or engines.vscode, and when core/tsconfig.json does not limit compilerOptions.types to ["node"]. The compiler alone cannot catch it, because vscode resolves through the root node_modules/@types.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
core/src/index.ts re-exports every module:

Module Main exports What it does host.ts TokenProvider, Log, Progress, OperationOptions, onAbort Host contract http.ts httpFetch fetch wrapper used by every request dataverse.ts Dataverse, normalizeDataverseUrl, validateDataverseUrl, resolveDataverseUrl Dataverse Web API client (/api/data/v9.2) of one org packages.ts packageFolders Package folders of a metadata store deploy.ts deployPackages, syncDatabase, builtPackages, ensureErpLinked, waitForJob, zipPackage, moduleDefinition Deploy and database sync tests.ts runTests, discoverTests, buildTestSuite, parseTrx, summarizeTests SysTest runs on the cloud runtime data/credentials.ts requestSqlCredentials, isExpired, publicAddress, validateAddressRange Just-in-time SQL credentials data/client.ts DataClient, readOnlyQuery, formatResultSet, connectionOf Business data through F&O Studio's server data/insights.ts Insights Queries behind Database-Performance-Insights environment/discovery.ts loadEnvironment, listEnvironments, findEnvironment, dynamics365Folder, orgName XPPConfig and registry discovery environment/config.ts templateConfiguration, completeConfiguration, repairGeneratedConfiguration(s) Writing configurations Visual Studio can read environment/ude.ts checkUdeConnection, readUdeEnvironment, getAssetDownloadUrl, ClientAssets UDE details and download URLs environment/setup.ts runUdeSetup, SetupPhases Full Connect to Environment setup environment/localAos.ts discoverLocalAos, restartLocalAos, aosHostProcesses The local AOS on cloud-hosted and VHD environments environment/deployState.ts deployStaleness, staleDeployMessage, deployStateKey Built versus deployed

docs.title: Dataverse client
docs.text:
Dataverse.connect(environmentUrl, tokens) accepts a Dataverse URL or a UDE's Finance and Operations URL. For an *.operations.dynamics.com host, resolveDataverseUrl looks up the same org name in the regional Dataverse hosts (crm, crm2 and so on) with DNS. It then asks the TokenProvider for a token for the org URL, interactively.

validateDataverseUrl refuses portal URLs (powerplatform.microsoft.com, powerapps.com) with a message telling you to copy the environment URL from the Power Platform admin center.

The client has send, json and action(name, parameters) (an unbound Dataverse action). Errors carry the Dataverse error message.

const { Dataverse } = require('@fno-studio/core');
const dv = await Dataverse.connect('https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com', tokens);
const details = await dv.action('RetrieveFinanceAndOperationsIntegrationDetails', {});

docs.title: Deploy and database sync
docs.text:
core/src/deploy.ts deploys locally built packages the way Visual Studio does. Nothing is recompiled: the package folder from your custom metadata store goes up as built, with the PDBs the build converted to portable ones.

sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Host
    participant C as core deploy.ts
    participant D as Dataverse
    H->>C: deployPackages(dv, builtPackages(store), 'Module')
    C->>D: ensureErpLinked
    loop each package
        C->>C: zip <package>/... + fnomoduledefinition.json
        C->>D: POST msprov_fnopackages
        C->>D: PATCH msprov_packagepayload (zip)
    end
    C->>D: msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync
    C->>D: poll asyncoperations (waitForJob)
    D-->>H: done or failure message
  • DbSync is None, Module or Full. Module sync passes the deployed modules in msprov_dbsyncvalue.
  • syncDatabase(dv, 'Full' | 'Module', modules) runs msprov_dbsynctofinopsasync without a deploy.
  • waitForJob polls the system job (15 seconds by default, pollIntervalMs) and throws with the server's message when the job fails.
  • ensureErpLinked fails early when the org cannot take Finance and Operations packages (not a UDE).

The extension never uses pac package compile for deploy, because it recompiles a scaffolded copy with pac's own SDK; your local build and its portable PDBs would never reach the environment.

docs.title: SysTest runs
docs.text:
runTests(request, options) in core/src/tests.ts works like Visual Studio's Test Explorer on a UDE:

  1. discoverTests reads the test classes through an ObjectReader (anything that answers the bridge action read_object, normally F&O Studio's server). Test classes must extend SysTestCase and test methods must be public and start with test or carry [SysTestMethod].
  2. buildTestSuite writes a test suite (.tsx) pointing at <runtime root>\<model>\bin\Dynamics.AX.<model>.dll.
  3. The suite goes to Dataverse (msprov_unittestsuites, config uploaded with PATCH) and runs with msprov_unittestexecutiononfinopsasync.
  4. The .trx result is downloaded, unzipped and parsed (parseTrx); summarizeTests writes a summary with one line per test and, for failures, its Infolog.

Tests run the code last deployed to the environment, not your local build. The host can use deployStaleness to warn when the build is newer.

docs.title: Database credentials and queries
docs.text:
requestSqlCredentials(dataverse, { addresses, reason, role }) calls the Dataverse action msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync with sqljitclientipaddress, sqljitreason and sqljitrole. The role is Reader unless Writer is asked for explicitly. The result has user, password, role and expiration; isExpired checks it. publicAddress finds this machine's public address and validateAddressRange checks what you type.

The core never stores credentials. The VS Code host keeps them in secret storage per environment.

DataClient sends business data requests through a DataTransport (data(action, body, timeoutMs)), which in VS Code is the extension's server process (xpp/data). connectionOf(target) builds the connection that travels with each request: SQL credentials for a UDE, Windows authentication for a local AxDB. The server never stores or logs it.

readOnlyQuery(client, target, { sql, maxRows }, { noAccessMessage }) is the agent's query path: 50 rows by default, 500 at most, output capped at 20,000 characters, tab-separated rows (RecIds arrive as text, so they stay exact).

Never start the server used as an MCP server with --allow-data. Business data is only for the host's own server process.

docs.title: Environment discovery and setup
docs.text:
loadEnvironment(dataverseUrl?, options) returns an XppEnvironment: the configuration file, frameworkDirectory, binDirectory, referencePackagesPaths, modelStoreFolder, runtime packages folder, cross-reference database, business database, application version, web client URL and Dataverse URL. Without a URL it reads the registry's CurrentMetadataConfig. Cloud-hosted and VHD environments have no XPPConfig; pass localConfigFolder to find them.

listEnvironments() returns the newest configuration of each environment in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig (an application update leaves the old one).

checkUdeConnection(dataverseUrl, tokens, log) checks the connection and logs what it finds.

runUdeSetup(dataverseUrl, options) is Connect to Environment. Its phases (SetupPhases):

Phase Label signIn Sign in to Dataverse sql Check SQL Server LocalDB download Download metadata and tools extract Extract PackagesLocalDirectory restore Restore cross-reference database configure Configure this machine

It needs tokens, serverExe (F&O Studio's server, which checks LocalDB and restores the cross-reference database with --sql-check and --restore-xref), a SetupProgress that receives the phase with each message, an optional signal, and optionally the active environment so the new configuration keeps the same custom metadata folder. It returns the new configuration file. See Connect-to-Environment.

config.ts writes every member of Power Platform Tools' configuration template. Visual Studio reads configurations with a strict serializer and silently drops a file that lacks a required member; repairGeneratedConfigurations fixes files written by older versions.

docs.title: Build, test and pack
docs.text:
From core/:

npm run build        # tsc: dist/*.js and dist/*.d.ts
npm test             # node --test: fake TokenProvider, recorded HTTP responses (test/fixtures)
npm pack             # fno-studio-core-<version>.tgz, for a consumer outside this repository

From the repository root, npm run compile builds core before the extension, and npm run test:core runs check-core.js and then core's tests. The release build runs npm run test:core.

The tests in core/test use a fake TokenProvider (helpers.js) and recorded HTTP responses in core/test/fixtures (deploy, failed database sync, test run, SQL credentials, UDE check). They make no network calls.

docs.title: Using it from another host
docs.text:
const { Dataverse, builtPackages, deployPackages } = require('@fno-studio/core');

const tokens = {
    async getToken(resource, { interactive }) {
        // Return an access token for `${resource}/.default`, from your own sign-in.
    },
};
const dv = await Dataverse.connect('https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com', tokens);
await deployPackages(dv, await builtPackages(modelStoreFolder), 'Module', { log: { line: console.log } });

Database queries need F&O Studio's server (XppVsCode.Server.exe), started by your host with --allow-data. The release publishes the server on its own as fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip for this purpose (see Release-Process and MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Windows only ("os": ["win32"] in core/package.json).
  • The UDE setup service is undocumented by Microsoft; F&O Studio ships it as experimental, with the manual steps as fallback.
  • The debugger's source mapping is still in the extension (src/debug.ts), not in core.

docs.title: Create Code Extension
docs.text: Create Code Extension creates a Chain of Command (CoC) class for a class, table, form, data entity, view or map: a final class with the [ExtensionOf(...)] attribute, in your model, ready for wrapper methods. It matches Visual Studio's Create code extension command. A related quick fix, Create Chain of Command wrapper for method, creates the class and the wrapper method in one step from the code view.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need to run code before or after a standard method, for example SalesFormLetter.run or CustTable.validateWrite.
  • You want to add new methods to a standard table or form (methods on an extension class are available on the base element).
  • You want a single extension class per element and model, named by convention.

For metadata changes (fields, controls, enum values), use Create Extension. For event handlers, see Event Handlers.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (Connect to Environment).
  • A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects); otherwise you pick one of your custom models and the class is not added to a project.
  • Your model references the package of the element you extend.

docs.title: Element types
docs.text:
Element type Attribute in the generated class Class [ExtensionOf(classStr(<Name>))] Table [ExtensionOf(tableStr(<Name>))] Form [ExtensionOf(formStr(<Name>))] Data Entity [ExtensionOf(tableStr(<Name>))] View [ExtensionOf(tableStr(<Name>))] Map [ExtensionOf(mapStr(<Name>))]

For other types you get a message such as Queries can't have a code extension.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Application Explorer Right-click a class, table, form, data entity, view or map > Create Code Extension Project view Same context menu entry Element Designer Right-click the root node > Create Code Extension New Element Pick Code extension (Chain of Command) in the Code group Command Palette F&O Studio: Create Code Extension X++ code view (quick fix) On the header of a method of a read-only element: light bulb > Create Chain of Command wrapper for method

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click the element, for example class SalesFormLetter, and choose Create Code Extension. From the Command Palette, type at least three characters of the name and pick the element.
  2. The Create code extension input box suggests <Element>_<Model>_Extension, for example SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension.
  3. Keep or change the name. It must be a valid class name ending with _Extension; otherwise the box shows Use a valid class name ending with _Extension.
  4. Press Enter. The class is created in your model, added to the project and opened in the X++ code view.

docs.title: The generated class
docs.text:
For table CustTable in model ContosoExtensions:

[ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustTable))]
final class CustTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
}

You then add wrapper methods. A wrapper has the same signature as the method it wraps and must call next:

[ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustTable))]
final class CustTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    public boolean validateWrite()
    {
        boolean result = next validateWrite();

        if (result && !this.CustGroup)
        {
            result = checkFailed("Customer group is required.");
        }

        return result;
    }

}

Use Implementations and Chain of Command to see the wrappers other models already have on the same method.

docs.title: The Chain of Command wrapper quick fix
docs.text:
When you read the code of a standard element in the code view, you cannot edit it. The quick fix creates the wrapper for you:

  1. Open the code of a standard class, table, form, data entity, view or map, for example SalesFormLetter.
  2. Put the cursor on the header of a method that is not private, for example run.
  3. Open the light bulb (Ctrl+. in VS Code's default keymap) and choose Create Chain of Command wrapper for run.
  4. The input box (title Chain of Command wrapper for SalesFormLetter.run) suggests SalesFormLetter_<Model>_Extension. The class is created if it does not exist.
  5. F&O Studio:
  6. creates the class with the [ExtensionOf(...)] attribute and the wrapper method, or
  7. adds the wrapper to the existing class when it is already an extension of the same element in your model, or
  8. tells you SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension already wraps run. when the method is already there.
  9. The class opens with the cursor on the wrapper.

The wrapper copies the method's modifiers (without abstract, final, server and client), its return type and its parameters (type and name; default values are not copied). For a void method it calls next and nothing else; otherwise it keeps the result and returns it:

public void run()
{
    next run();
}

public boolean validateWrite()
{
    boolean result = next validateWrite();

    return result;
}

The quick fix stops with an error when:

  • the class name exists in a model that is not yours (... exists in ..., which is not one of your models.);
  • the class exists but is not an extension of the element (... exists but is not an extension of SalesFormLetter.);
  • F&O Studio cannot read the method header (Could not read the header of run.).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.project (empty) The D365FO project of the workspace. Its model receives the class; without a project you pick one of your custom models.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Create Code Extension is createCodeExtension in src/d365Tools.ts. The supported types and their intrinsic functions are the CodeExtensionFunctions table in src/aot.ts; tree nodes of those types get the coc context value that shows the menu entry.
  2. The class is created by the create_object bridge action with the declaration above and formatCode: false, so the server stores the source as written. The server refuses names that already exist.
  3. add_to_project adds the class to the .rnrproj, the trees refresh and the class opens in the code view.
  4. The quick fix is in src/productivity/quickFixes.ts. It parses the method header from the code view, checks whether the class exists with find_object and read_object, then calls create_object (new class with the method) or update_object (method added to the existing class).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The command creates an empty class; you write the wrappers (or use the quick fix for one method at a time).
  • The quick fix is offered on read-only elements (outside your models) and not on private methods, which cannot be wrapped.
  • The quick fix copies parameters as type and name only. Check the wrapper before you build; the compiler reports signature mismatches (Compiler Diagnostics).
  • Classes go only to your own models.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Create Code Extension is not in the context menu The element type does not support Chain of Command Use a class, table, form, data entity, view or map Use a valid class name ending with _Extension. The name does not end with _Extension or has invalid characters Fix the name ... already exists (model ...). Nothing was changed A class with that name exists Use another name, or open the existing class and add methods The quick fix is missing on a method The element is in your model (editable), the method is private, or the cursor is not on the method header Put the cursor on the header of a non-private method of a standard element Build error on the wrapper Signature differs from the base method, or next is missing Copy the exact signature; every wrapper must call next

docs.title: Create Deployment Package
docs.text: Create Deployment Package… makes a deployable package (a .zip) of your models' last build with the same Microsoft script Visual Studio runs for Dynamics 365 > Deploy > Create Deployment Package: RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin. Copilot agents can create the same package with the xpp_package tool. Use the package to move your code to sandbox and production environments the way your project does.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• When a release is ready and you need a deployable package for the next environment (test, sandbox, production).
  • On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, where there is no Deploy to Environment: the package is how your code leaves the VM.
  • After a passed Pre-Deploy Checklist, which offers Create Deployment Package directly.

Note: to put your code on your own unified developer environment, use Deploy to Environment instead; it does not need a deployable package.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Build the models first. The script packages what is in the package folders now; it does not compile. See Build Project and Model. If your models reference C# projects, the build copies their assemblies into the package's bin folder, so they are part of the package.
  • The models must be your own models (in the custom metadata folder).
  • An active environment configuration: the script and the tools it uses come from its PackagesLocalDirectory\bin.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Click Deploy > Create Deployment Package… in the Dynamics 365 view, or run F&O Studio: Create Deployment Package… from the command palette.
  2. In Create deployment package: packages, select one or more packages. The list shows your custom models by package name, with the model's display name as description.
  3. In Package version, enter a four-part version. The default is 1.0.0.0; anything else must look like 1.2.3.4 ("Use a version like 1.0.0.0").
  4. Pick the Output folder for the deployable package and click Create package here.
  5. A task terminal named Create deployment package runs the script and shows its output. The deployable package is written to the folder you picked.

Cancel any of the prompts to stop without creating anything.

docs.title: With the Pre-Deploy Checklist
docs.text: Pre-Deploy Checklist builds the project, runs best practice, performance and security checks, and looks for leftover Run Snippet scratch code. When every step passes, it asks "The checklist passed." with Create Deployment Package (and Deploy on a UDE). The checklist fails while Run Snippet's scratch class is still in the model, so it does not end up in the package.

docs.title: With Copilot
docs.text:
The agent tool xpp_package creates the package without prompts:

Input Effect Default modelNames Custom models to package; each one's package is included once. The active project's model version Package version, n.n.n.n. 1.0.0.0

The package goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\packages\<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>. The result starts with "PACKAGE CREATED:" and the path of the zip, or "PACKAGE FAILED (exit N)." with the end of the script's output. The tool is meant to be called only when you ask for a package; it deploys nothing. The F&O Release Manager agent uses it in its release checklist. See Agent Tools: Build and Data.

Example prompt:

Build ContosoExtensions, check best practice, and create a deployable package version 1.4.0.0.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for packaging.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The command is createDeploymentPackage in src/d365Tools.ts. It runs Windows PowerShell as a VS Code task:

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command
  & '<PackagesLocalDirectory>\bin\RunPackageCreationAll.ps1'
    -packageNames @('ContosoExtensions')
    -metadataDir '<custom metadata folder>'
    -modelDir '<custom metadata folder>'
    -binDir '<PackagesLocalDirectory>\bin'
    -packageVersion '1.0.0.0'
    -outputDir '<the folder you picked>'
  • The script is Microsoft's, from your installation; F&O Studio only passes the arguments Visual Studio passes. What goes into the zip is decided by the script.
  • Package names and paths are quoted for PowerShell; the version is validated before it is used.

The agent tool runs the same command line in the metadata server (BuildService.PackageJson in server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs), with the output folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\packages, and reports success only when the script exits with 0 and a .zip exists in the output folder.

docs.title: Where the package goes next
docs.text: Deploying a deployable package to sandbox or production is not done by F&O Studio. In general D365FO practice, you upload it to the project's asset library in Lifecycle Services, or deploy it through the Power Platform admin center or a release pipeline, depending on how your environments are managed. See Environments and Promotion and Build Automation and Pipelines.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No build is run: the package holds whatever the package folders contain now, normally the last build. Build every selected model first.
  • Only custom models can be packaged.
  • The command packages the selected packages only; it does not add packages they depend on.
  • F&O Studio does not upload or deploy the package anywhere.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Use a version like 1.0.0.0" The version is not four numbers. Enter for example 1.0.0.0. The terminal shows a PowerShell error from the script The script failed. Read the error; check that every selected package was built, then create the package again. Agent tool: "Model '...' is not one of your custom models." A standard model was passed. Pass your own models. Agent tool: "version must look like 1.0.0.0." Invalid version. Pass a four-part version. Agent tool: "PACKAGE FAILED (exit N)." The script failed or wrote no zip. Read the output included in the result; build first.

docs.title: Create Extension
docs.text: Create Extension creates a metadata extension of an existing element in your model: a table, form, enum, EDT, data entity, security duty or security role extension. It is how you add fields, controls, enum values or duties to standard objects without overlayering. It matches Visual Studio's Create extension command in Application Explorer.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Add fields, field groups, indexes or relations to a standard table such as CustTable.
  • Add controls or data sources to a standard form such as SalesTable.
  • Add values to an extensible enum.
  • Change the label, help text or size of a standard EDT.
  • Add fields to a standard data entity and its staging table.
  • Add privileges to a standard duty, or duties to a standard role.

For X++ code (Chain of Command), use Create Code Extension instead.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (Connect to Environment).
  • A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects). Without a project, F&O Studio asks which of your custom models gets the extension and does not add it to a project.
  • Your model references the package of the element you extend. If not, add the reference first in Models and Model Dependencies; otherwise the build fails later.

docs.title: Element types you can extend
docs.text:
Element type Extension type created Table (AxTable) Table Extension (AxTableExtension) Form (AxForm) Form Extension (AxFormExtension) Base Enum (AxEnum) Base Enum Extension (AxEnumExtension) Extended Data Type (AxEdt) Extended Data Type Extension (AxEdtExtension) Data Entity (AxDataEntityView) Data Entity Extension (AxDataEntityViewExtension) Security Duty (AxSecurityDuty) Security Duty Extension (AxSecurityDutyExtension) Security Role (AxSecurityRole) Security Role Extension (AxSecurityRoleExtension)

Other types (views, maps, queries, menus, menu items, tiles, workflow elements) have extension types in Application Explorer, but Create Extension does not create them. For any other type you get a message such as Views can't be extended this way.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Application Explorer Right-click an element of a supported type > Create Extension Project view Right-click an element of a supported type > Create Extension Element Designer Right-click the root node > Create Extension Element Designer title bar Create Extension button, shown when the designer shows a read-only element (not in your models) of a supported type New Element Pick an extension type such as Table Extension, then the element to extend Command Palette F&O Studio: Create Extension

docs.title: Steps from the context menu
docs.text:
1. In Application Explorer, find the element, for example table CustTable.
  2. Right-click it and choose Create Extension.
  3. The Create extension input box suggests the name <Element>.<Model>, for example CustTable.ContosoExtensions. Change the part after the dot if your team uses another suffix.
  4. Press Enter. The extension is created in your model, added to the project, and opened in the Element Designer.

docs.title: Steps from the Command Palette
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Create Extension.
  2. Type at least three characters of the element name, for example CustGro, and press Enter.
  3. Pick the element from the list. Only elements of the supported types are shown; the line under each shows its model.
  4. Continue with the name as above.

docs.title: The name rule
docs.text: The name must start with the base element's name and a dot. The input box refuses anything else with The name must start with 'CustTable.'. The usual convention is <Element>.<Model> or <Element>.<Prefix>Extension. The name must also be unique: if an extension with the same name exists, the server answers ... already exists (model ...). Nothing was changed.

docs.title: After you create it
docs.text:
The extension opens in the Element Designer. The designer shows the base element's nodes together with the extension's own nodes; the extension's own nodes are shown in bold. Typical next steps:

  • Table extension: add fields, field groups, indexes and relations under the nodes. Set field properties in the Properties grid.
  • Form extension: add controls and data sources; use Form Layout and Form Extensions to place controls and check them against the form's patterns.
  • Enum extension: add values. The base enum must be extensible.
  • EDT extension: change label, help text or string size.
  • Data entity extension: add fields; F&O Studio handles the staging table as part of the entity extension.
  • Duty or role extension: add privileges or duties.

Then build (Build Project and Model) and synchronize the database for table changes (Synchronize Database).

docs.title: Example: add a field to CustGroup
docs.text:
1. In Application Explorer, filter on CustGroup, right-click the table, choose Create Extension.
  2. Accept CustGroup.ContosoExtensions.
  3. In the designer, add a field ContosoRegion of EDT Name under Fields.
  4. Add it to the Overview field group if it should show in the list.
  5. Build the project, then synchronize the table.

To show the field on the form, create a form extension of CustGroup the same way and add a control bound to the new field.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.project (empty) The D365FO project of the workspace. Its model receives the extension; without a project you pick one of your custom models.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The command is registered in src/d365Tools.ts (createExtension). The supported types and their extension types are the ExtensionTypes table in src/aot.ts.
  2. The context menu entry appears only on tree nodes whose context value contains extensible, which F&O Studio sets for the supported types.
  3. Without a tree node, pickElement asks for part of the name, runs the find_object bridge action (up to 50 matches) and filters the matches by type.
  4. The target model is the project's model, else a custom model you pick.
  5. create_object on the metadata server creates the extension through Microsoft's metadata API. The server checks that no element of that type and name exists and reloads metadata after the save.
  6. add_to_project writes the extension into the .rnrproj, the trees refresh, and xpp.openDesigner opens the extension.
  7. In the Element Designer, the title bar button runs xpp.designer.createExtension, which calls the same command for the element in the active designer tab. It is shown only when the element is not editable (not in your models) and its type is supported.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Seven element types are supported (see the table). Other extension types are not created by this command.
  • The extension starts empty; you add its content in the designer.
  • F&O Studio does not add the model reference for you. If the base element's package is not referenced by your model, fix the model's references.
  • Extensions go only to your own models.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Create Extension is not in the context menu The element's type is not one of the seven supported types Use the right element type, or Create Code Extension for code Views can't be extended this way. (or another type) You picked a type that is not supported (Command Palette flow) Pick a table, form, enum, EDT, data entity, duty or role The name must start with 'X.' You removed or changed the base name before the dot Keep <Element>. at the start ... already exists (model ...). Nothing was changed An extension with that name exists Use another suffix, or open the existing extension No element matching '...'. The search text matched nothing Check the spelling; type at least three characters Build errors about the base element after creating the extension Your model does not reference the base element's package Update the model's references in Models and Model Dependencies
