docs.title: D365FO Projects
docs.text: A D365FO project (.rnrproj) is the same project file Visual Studio uses: an MSBuild file that names one model and lists the elements you work on. F&O Studio opens, creates and edits these projects, shows them in the D365FO Project view (F&O Studio's Solution Explorer), and opens each project in its own VS Code workspace with the project folder and the model folder. Projects stay compatible with Visual Studio in both directions.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You work on a feature or fix: the project collects its elements, and Build Project compiles only those.
  • You want new elements (New Element, wizards, extensions, Copilot) to land in a known model and be listed in one place.
  • You want the change marks of Git on your elements, and Review My Changes and Best Practice Checks scoped to your work.
  • You share work with Visual Studio users: they open the same .rnrproj.

A project is optional. The Application Explorer, designers, code views and agent tools also work without one. Without a project, commands that create elements ask which of your models to use.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An environment with metadata on this machine (Connect to Environment).
  • A custom model for the project. Create one with Create Model… (Models and Model Dependencies) if you have none; Create D365FO Project… refuses to run without one.
  • For source control, put the project folder in your Git repository (see Source Control for X++).

docs.title: The project view
docs.text:
The D365FO Project view is the second view of the F&O Studio side bar.

Without a project it shows: No D365FO project open. Opening a project opens its workspace: the project folder and its model folder. The Application Explorer and agent tools also work without one. with links Open D365FO Project, Open Recent D365FO Project and Create D365FO Project.

With a project it shows the solution, like Visual Studio's Solution Explorer:

ContosoProject                     ContosoExtensions
  References
    ContosoLibrary                 C# project
  Classes                          3
    ContosoOrderStatusService
    CustTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension
    SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension
  Table Extensions                 1
    CustTable.ContosoExtensions
ContosoReports                     ContosoReporting · not open
ContosoLibrary                     C#
  Greeter.cs
  • The project node shows the project name and its model. It opens expanded.
  • References lists the C# projects and assemblies the X++ project references (Solution View and C# References).
  • Folders group the elements by the folder Visual Studio gives them (Classes, Tables, Table Extensions, Forms...). The number of elements is shown next to the folder.
  • Elements show their name and their type (Class, Table Extension...). A click opens them like in the Application Explorer.
  • Other X++ projects of the same solution appear as further project nodes, marked not open.
  • C# projects of the solution, or that the project references, appear with their files.
  • An empty project shows the hint No elements yet: New Element….

The view's description shows the solution name, <solution> (solution), or, without a solution, <project> (<model>).

docs.title: Git change marks
docs.text: Elements of your models that differ from Git carry Git's letter and colour: M modified, A added, D deleted, R renamed. The tooltip says whether the change is uncommitted or only on the current branch. With xpp.git.baseBranch set (for example main), elements changed since the branch left that base are marked too. The marks refresh when you save and every 30 seconds. See Git Changes in the Project View.

docs.title: Title bar
docs.text: Button / menu Shown Command + With a project New Element… (New Element) Build With a project Build Project (Build Project and Model) Open element Always Open Element… (Open Element) Open project Without a project Open D365FO Project… Create project Without a project Create D365FO Project… Project submenu (... menu) With a project Open D365FO Project…, Open Recent D365FO Project…, Create D365FO Project…, Close D365FO Project, Add Reference…, New C# Project… Check submenu (... menu) With a project Run Best Practice Checks on Project, Review My Changes, Pre-Deploy Checklist, Run Tests (unified developer environments only) ... menu Always Build Model, Refresh Project

docs.title: Right-click actions
docs.text:
On a folder of the open project: New Element… (also as an inline +). The element type of the folder is preselected, so + on Classes starts a new class.

On an element, the same actions as in the Application Explorer (see Application Explorer), except Add to Project, plus:

Action Details Locate in Application Explorer Selects the element in the Application Explorer, clearing a filter that hides it Exclude from Project Removes the element from the .rnrproj. The element stays in the model. Not offered on elements of the other X++ projects of the solution.

Project items always count as elements of your own model, so Rename…, Delete and View History are available on them.

On a project node: Add Reference… and New C# Project… on the open project; Open This Project on another X++ project of the solution. On References, Add Reference… and New C# Project…; on a reference, Remove Reference. On a C# project, Build C# Project and Open Project File. See Solution View and C# References.

The view supports multi-select, and elements dragged from the Application Explorer are added to the project when dropped on it (Drag and Drop).

docs.title: Open a project
docs.text:
1. Run Open D365FO Project… (project view, Dynamics 365 view > Model and project > Open Project…, Command Palette, or the Open or create a D365FO project walkthrough step).
  2. The picker titled Open D365FO project (.rnrproj) lists:
  3. projects you opened before (marked recently opened), newest first;
  4. .rnrproj files found in your source\repos folder (Visual Studio's default, up to four folders deep) and in the current workspace;
  5. Browse… to pick any .rnrproj.
  6. Pick a project. F&O Studio opens the project's workspace in the current window (the window reloads).

Open Recent D365FO Project… shows only the recent list (up to 10 projects that still exist). If it is empty you get No recent D365FO projects. Open one with Open D365FO Project.

docs.title: The project workspace
docs.text:
Opening a project opens a VS Code workspace file that F&O Studio writes for that project. It contains:

Folder Name in the Explorer The folder of the .rnrproj (with the .slnx and your source control) <Project> (project) The model's metadata folder, <package>\<model> <Model> (model) Each C# project of the solution, or that the project references <Folder> (C#)

and the setting xpp.project with the full path of the .rnrproj.

  • The workspace files live in F&O Studio's own storage (workspaces\<Project>-<hash>.code-workspace), so your repository stays clean.
  • Folders and settings you add to the workspace yourself are kept when F&O Studio rewrites it.
  • VS Code's File > Open Recent lists the workspaces too.
  • Each window has at most one project. Two windows can have two projects.

Close D365FO Project closes the workspace; the window stays open without a project.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
1. Run Create D365FO Project….
  2. Create D365FO project (1/3): model — pick one of your custom models. The project's elements belong to it.
  3. (2/3): name — the default is <Model>Project. Letters, digits, _, . and -, starting with a letter.
  4. (3/3): parent folder — your source\repos folder (Visual Studio's repos folder) or Browse…. The project goes to <parent>\<name>.
  5. F&O Studio writes <name>.rnrproj and <name>.slnx, shows Created D365FO project for model . and opens the project's workspace.

    If the .rnrproj already exists, it stops with an error and leaves the file alone.

docs.title: Add and remove elements
docs.text:
• New elements created by New Element, the wizards, Create Extension, Create Code Extension, Duplicate… and Copilot's tools are added to the open project automatically.
  • Existing elements of the project's model: Add to Project in the Application Explorer or Open Element, or drag them onto the project view.
  • Exclude from Project removes an element from the project only. Delete removes it from the model too.

A project holds elements of its own model only. Adding an element of another model fails; extend it instead.

docs.title: Build and check
docs.text:
• Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view or a .rnrproj editor) compiles the project's elements, after building the C# projects it references. See Build Project and Model.
  • The Check submenu runs Best Practice Checks, Review My Changes, the Pre-Deploy Checklist and Run Tests on the project.

docs.title: Projects selected by Copilot
docs.text: An agent can switch the project with the tool xpp_select_project. When it does, F&O Studio shows The agent selected project . with Open Project. The window only switches when you click it, because opening a project reloads the window and would interrupt the agent.

docs.title: The project file
docs.text:
F&O Studio writes .rnrproj files the way Visual Studio saves them. A new project looks like this (shortened):

<Project ToolsVersion="14.0" DefaultTargets="Build" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/developer/msbuild/2003">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Model>ContosoExtensions</Model>
    <TargetFrameworkVersion>v4.8</TargetFrameworkVersion>
    <OutputPath>bin</OutputPath>
    <GenerateCrossReferences>True</GenerateCrossReferences>
    <RunAppCheckerRules>False</RunAppCheckerRules>
    <DeployOnline>False</DeployOnline>
    <ProjectGuid>{...}</ProjectGuid>
    <Name>ContosoProject</Name>
    <StartupType>Class</StartupType>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)|$(Platform)' == 'Debug|AnyCPU'">
    <DBSyncInBuild>False</DBSyncInBuild>
    <Partition>initial</Partition>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <Import Project="$(MSBuildBinPath)\Microsoft.Common.targets" />
  <Import Project="$(BuildTasksDirectory)\Microsoft.Dynamics.Framework.Tools.BuildTasks.17.0.targets" />
</Project>

Elements are Content items. Adding CustTable.ContosoExtensions writes:

<ItemGroup>
  <Folder Include="Table Extensions\" />
</ItemGroup>
<ItemGroup>
  <Content Include="AxTableExtension\CustTable.ContosoExtensions">
    <SubType>Content</SubType>
    <Name>CustTable.ContosoExtensions</Name>
    <Link>Table Extensions\CustTable.ContosoExtensions</Link>
  </Content>
</ItemGroup>
  • Include is <AxType>\<Name>; the project view's folder is the first part of Link.
  • The folder names follow Visual Studio: Classes, Tables, Forms, Extended Data Types, Base Enums, Views, Queries, Maps, Data Entities, Menus, Tiles, Display Menu Items, Output Menu Items, Action Menu Items, Security Privileges, Security Duties, Security Roles, Services, Service Groups, Configuration Keys, Label Files, Reports, and the extension folders (Table Extensions, Form Extensions...).
  • Removing the last element of a type removes its Folder entry and empty item groups, as Visual Studio does.
  • References to C# projects and assemblies are ProjectReference and Reference items (Solution View and C# References).

The .slnx written next to it lists the project:

<Solution>
  <Configurations>
    <BuildType Name="Debug" />
  </Configurations>
  <Project Path="ContosoProject.rnrproj" Type="fc65038c-1b2f-41e1-a629-bed71d161fff" Id="..." />
</Solution>

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.project empty The .rnrproj of this workspace. Written by Open D365FO Project… into the project's workspace. A value in the user settings is not used. Changing it restarts the metadata server and refreshes the project view. xpp.git.baseBranch empty Branch the change marks compare with, in addition to uncommitted changes xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Save code views before Build Project xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild for the referenced C# projects

Earlier versions kept xpp.project in the user settings, so every window opened the same project. F&O Studio now moves such a value to the recent projects list and removes it from the user settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• src/project.ts: ProjectWorkspaces (open, recent, close, workspace files), createProject (the .rnrproj and .slnx templates) and ProjectTreeProvider (the view). The project of a window is the workspace value of xpp.project; a .rnrproj that happens to be in an open folder does not select a project.
  • The view reads the .rnrproj itself (model and Content items). It watches the project's folder and refreshes 0.4 seconds after the file changes, so elements added by Copilot, the MCP server, Visual Studio or a Git pull show up on their own. It also watches the C# project folders and the solution file.
  • Writes to the project go through the metadata server: bridge actions add_to_project and remove_from_project, implemented by XppProject in server/Host/XppProject.cs, which edits the MSBuild XML the way Visual Studio saves it. add_to_project checks that the element exists and belongs to the project's model.
  • The metadata server is started with --project <rnrproj>; agent tools such as xpp_list_project_items, xpp_add_to_project, xpp_remove_from_project and xpp_select_project work on the same file (Agent Tools: Metadata).
  • An agent's project choice is written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activeProject.txt; the extension checks it every 3 seconds and asks before opening the project. Choices written before the window started are ignored.
  • Git marks come from ChangeDecorations in src/changes.ts, which runs git status (and git diff against the merge base of xpp.git.baseBranch) on the real path of each custom model folder.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One model per project, as in Visual Studio.
  • One project per window. To work on two projects at once, open two windows.
  • The project view does not rename or move project folders; folders follow the element types.
  • Project properties other than the model (Company, Partition, DBSyncInBuild...) are kept but not edited by F&O Studio. Edit the .rnrproj as XML if you need to.

docs.title: Database Access
docs.text: F&O Studio reads (and, if you ask for it, changes) the business database of your active environment. All data features use this access: Browse Table Data, the SQL Query Panel, Explain Plan, Database Performance Insights, Open in SSMS and the agent tool xpp_query_data. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment it connects to the local AxDB with Windows authentication. On a unified developer environment (UDE) it requests temporary just-in-time (JIT) SQL credentials, the same request Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools make, and keeps them in VS Code's secret storage until they expire.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see the rows behind a form, check setup, or confirm what your code wrote.
  • You investigate a performance problem and need query plans or the database's own statistics.
  • A Copilot agent needs to look at real data (it asks you before each query).
  • You want to open the same database in SQL Server Management Studio without copying passwords around by hand.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Environment What F&O Studio connects to What you need Unified developer environment (UDE) The environment's Azure SQL database A selected environment (Select Environment or the xpp.environmentUrl setting), a Microsoft sign-in (Sign-In and Authentication), and the System administrator role in the environment Cloud-hosted or VHD environment The local business database (AxDB by default) on this machine A Windows account that can sign in to the local SQL Server

F&O Studio decides which case applies from the active configuration: a configuration without RuntimePackagesDirectory and with a host type other than 4 is treated as local (cloud-hosted or VHD). For a local environment the server and database come from the configuration's DatabaseServer and BusinessDatabaseName (defaults localhost and AxDB). On cloud-hosted and VHD machines F&O Studio writes that configuration itself from the AOS settings DataAccess.DbServer and DataAccess.Database. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
• Dynamics 365 view, Data group. The group shows the access state next to its name: no access, the database name (local), or the role and expiry time (for example Reader · until 14:30). It contains Browse Table Data…, New SQL Query, Performance Insights… and Database… (credentials, connection, SSMS).
  • Status bar. Once there is access, a $(database) item shows the database name (local) or the role and expiry (Reader until 14:30). Its tooltip names the database, server, user and expiry. Click it to open the Database menu. It stays hidden while a UDE has no credentials. See Status Bar.
  • Environment menu. The environment status bar menu has a Database… entry that opens the same menu.
  • Command Palette (category F&O Studio): Request Database Credentials, Forget Database Credentials, Test Database Connection, Copy Database Connection Detail, Open Database in SQL Server Management Studio, Browse Table Data, New SQL Query, Database Performance Insights.

docs.title: The Database menu
docs.text:
The menu title is Database of <environment>. It offers:

Entry What it does Browse Table Data… Opens Browse Table Data after you pick a table New SQL Query Opens an empty SQL Query Panel Performance Insights… Opens the Database Performance Insights picker Test Connection Connects and reports the database, server, signed-in SQL user and SQL Server version Open in SQL Server Management Studio See Open in SSMS Copy Connection Detail… Copies the server, database, user name or password to the clipboard Request Database Credentials… / Request New Credentials… UDE only (or when there is no access yet) Forget Credentials UDE only, when credentials are stored

docs.title: Request credentials on a UDE
docs.text:
You do not have to request credentials up front. The first data feature you use asks in a modal dialog: "The database of a unified environment needs temporary credentials." Choose Request Credentials. You can also run F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials directly.

  1. Reason (1/3). Describe why you need access, at least five characters, for example Investigate why sales order SO-001234 does not post. The reason is recorded with the request.
  2. Allowed IPv4 addresses (2/3). The database firewall refuses connections from other addresses. The box is prefilled with this machine's public address, as seen by https://checkip.amazonaws.com/ (the service Visual Studio uses). Enter a single address (203.0.113.10) or a range (203.0.113.1-203.0.113.50); the first address of a range must not be above the last. If you are offline the box starts empty.
  3. Access (3/3). Choose Reader (read data only, recommended) or Writer (read and change data; changes made in SQL skip X++ business logic). If you already have valid credentials, the prompt warns that new credentials replace them, including credentials Visual Studio requested.
  4. A progress notification shows while the request runs; you can cancel it.
  5. When it succeeds you see Database credentials (Reader) for <environment> until <date and time>. They are kept in VS Code's secret storage. The status bar item and the Data group update.

Azure SQL needs a few minutes to apply the new firewall rule and password. If a connection fails with a sign-in error in the first ten minutes after the request, F&O Studio tells you the credentials are not active yet and keeps them. Try again a minute later.

docs.title: Test and copy the connection
docs.text:
• Test Database Connection shows Connected to <database> on <server> as <user> (SQL Server <version>).
  • Copy Database Connection Detail lets you pick Server, Database, User name or Password (the last two only with JIT credentials). The value goes to the clipboard. Paste the password where you need it, then clear the clipboard.

docs.title: Forget credentials
docs.text: Forget Database Credentials deletes the stored credentials for the active environment. The next data feature asks again. On a local environment this command and Request Database Credentials report that the database uses Windows authentication and needs no credentials.

docs.title: Read-only by default
docs.text:
Every read goes through the same rules, whichever feature sends it:

  • One statement, SELECT only. A read-only batch must start with SELECT or WITH, contain a single statement (a trailing ; is fine) and use none of these keywords outside strings, quoted names and comments: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, TRUNCATE, DROP, ALTER, CREATE, EXEC, EXECUTE, SP_EXECUTESQL, GRANT, REVOKE, DENY, INTO, BACKUP, RESTORE, DBCC, KILL, SHUTDOWN, RECONFIGURE, BULK, OPENROWSET, OPENQUERY, OPENDATASOURCE, OPENXML, WRITETEXT, UPDATETEXT, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVE, BEGIN, USE, SET, DECLARE, WAITFOR, CHECKPOINT, SETUSER, REVERT.
  • Always rolled back. The batch runs inside a READ COMMITTED transaction that is rolled back afterwards, even when the keyword check passed. The keyword check is the first line of defence; the rollback is the second.
  • Bounded output. At most 5 result sets, a row limit per result set (the panel's choice, at most 10,000), cells longer than 4,000 characters cut, binary values shown as hex up to 64 bytes.
  • Time limit. 60 seconds by default (at most 600).

Changing data needs an explicit choice in the SQL Query Panel: the Allow changes check box, which is only enabled on a local database or with Writer credentials, and a confirmation for every run. Agents can never change data.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.environmentUrl empty Dataverse URL of your default unified developer environment. Credentials are requested from the selected environment; Select Environment chooses another one per workspace.

There are no settings for row limits or timeouts; they are chosen in the panels.

docs.title: Where each part runs
docs.text: Part Where Source Access state, status bar, Database menu Extension src/database/connection.ts, src/database/index.ts Credential prompts and secret storage Extension src/database/credentials.ts JIT credential request @fno-studio/core core/src/data/credentials.ts Data client, read-only agent query @fno-studio/core core/src/data/client.ts SQL execution Extension's own server process, JSON-RPC method xpp/data server/Host/DataQueryService.cs Read-only check Server server/Host/ReadOnlySql.cs

docs.title: Requesting JIT credentials
docs.text:
requestSqlCredentials calls the unbound Dataverse action msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync on the selected environment with three inputs:

{
  "sqljitclientipaddress": "203.0.113.10",
  "sqljitreason": "Investigate why sales order SO-001234 does not post",
  "sqljitrole": "Reader"
}

The output parameters servername, databasename, sqljitusername, sqljitpassword, sqljitrole, sqljitexpiration and ipaddress (names compared without case) become the stored credentials. If the server, database, user or password is missing, the request fails with "The environment did not return database credentials. Database access needs the System administrator role in a unified developer or sandbox environment." and the operationhistoryid, when the service returns one.

docs.title: Credential lifetime and storage
docs.text:
• The credentials are stored as JSON in VS Code's secret storage (Windows Credential Manager) under the key xpp.database.<environment name>. They are never written to settings, logs or files.
  • The expiry is the one the service returns (sqljitexpiration). When it parses as a date, F&O Studio drops expired credentials the next time it reads them, and a timer refreshes the status bar at the expiry time.
  • If the database refuses the sign-in (SQL errors 18456, 40615, 18487, 18488) more than ten minutes after the request, F&O Studio deletes the stored credentials so the next use asks again. The message says the credentials expired, were replaced, or this address is not allowed.

docs.title: The connection travels with each request
docs.text:
The extension starts its own server process with --allow-data (src/serverClient.ts). Only that process answers xpp/data. Each request carries the connection (server, database, and either Windows authentication or the user and password); the server opens a connection for the request and never stores or logs the credentials. SQL logins use an encrypted connection with certificate validation (Encrypt=true, TrustServerCertificate=false), a 20-second connect timeout and the application name F&O Studio, so the sessions are recognisable on the server.

Values come back in a form JSON keeps exactly: 64-bit integers (RecId, RefRecId) and decimals as text, dates as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fff, GUIDs as text.

Data requests run outside the metadata lock, so a long query does not block the designers or code navigation. Cancelling (closing the tab or pressing Cancel) sends cancel with the query's ID and the server cancels the running SQL command.

docs.title: Separation from the MCP server
docs.text:
The MCP server that Copilot starts (MCP Agent Tools) is launched without --allow-data. It answers xpp/data with "Method not found". Agents read data only through xpp_query_data, a VS Code language model tool the extension registers (src/database/queryTool.ts):

  • You confirm each query; the confirmation shows the SQL.
  • It runs read-only (never with changes allowed), 50 rows by default, at most 500.
  • The result is tab-separated text cut at 20,000 characters.
  • Without access it answers NO DATABASE ACCESS and tells the agent to ask you to run F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials.
  • The agent never sees the server name, user or password.

See Agent Tools: Build and Data and Security Model.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Windows only, like the rest of F&O Studio.
  • One database per window: the active environment's.
  • The firewall rule covers the addresses you entered. If your public address changes (VPN, another network), request new credentials.
  • Changes made with Allow changes skip X++ business logic. Use them only on development data.
  • F&O Studio does not show the request history; the reason is recorded by the environment.

Database access needs the System administrator role…" Your account lacks the role, or the environment is not a UDE Ask for the System administrator role in the environment "No environment selected. Run "F&O Studio: Connect to Environment" or "F&O Studio: Select Environment" first." No Dataverse environment selected Run Select Environment or set xpp.environmentUrl "The new database credentials are not active yet…" Azure SQL has not applied the firewall rule and password Wait a minute and run again "…The credentials expired, were replaced, or this address is not allowed. docs.title: Database Performance Insights
docs.text: Database Performance Insights runs four ready-made, read-only queries against the active environment's database: missing indexes, the most expensive queries of the last 24 hours, the slowest batch jobs of the last 7 days, and number sequences that serialize work. Each opens in the SQL Query Panel, runs right away, and stays editable. They complement the static Analyze Performance rules with what the database itself has seen. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Users say "it got slow" and you need a starting point on real data.
  • Before a release, to see which batch jobs take longest per company.
  • When posting is slow and you suspect a continuous number sequence.
  • To pick the query to look at with Explain Plan.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Database access for the active environment. See Database Access. The queries were verified on a unified developer environment with Reader credentials.
  • The results reflect the activity on that database. A fresh development environment with little use shows little.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the picker in one of these ways:
  2. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Database Performance Insights.
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Data > Performance Insights….
  4. Database menu (status bar): Performance Insights….
  5. The picker is titled Database performance insights (read-only). Choose one of the four insights below.
  6. A query tab opens with the insight's SQL and runs it at once with a limit of 500 rows.
  7. Read the result, sort or filter it by editing the SQL, export it with Export CSV, or select a query text and use Explain Plan.

docs.title: Missing indexes
docs.text:
"Indexes SQL Server would have used, by estimated benefit (add them as table indexes in your model, not in SQL)."

Reads sys.dm_db_missing_index_details, sys.dm_db_missing_index_groups and sys.dm_db_missing_index_group_stats for the current database. The top 25 rows, by benefit (avg_user_impact × (user_seeks + user_scans)).

Column Meaning Benefit Estimated impact times the number of seeks and scans that would have used the index TableName The SQL table EqualityColumns Columns compared with = InequalityColumns Columns compared with <, >, <>, ranges IncludedColumns Columns the query reads that the index could carry Seeks How often the index would have been sought ImpactPercent Estimated cost reduction for those queries LastSeek When it was last wanted

What to do: decide whether the index belongs in your model. Add it as a table index (in your table, or a table extension of a standard table), equality columns first, then the inequality columns. Weigh the write cost on tables with many inserts.

docs.title: Most expensive queries (last 24 hours)
docs.text:
"Query Store: total duration, executions and the slowest run; select a query and use Explain Plan."

Reads the Query Store views (sys.query_store_runtime_stats, …_runtime_stats_interval, …_plan, …_query, …_query_text) for intervals that started in the last day. The top 20 queries by total duration.

Column Meaning QueryId Query Store's ID of the query Executions Runs in the period TotalMs Average duration × executions, in milliseconds MaxMs The slowest single run LogicalReads Average logical reads × executions QueryText The SQL text (first 2,000 characters)

What to do: a query with a high TotalMs and many Executions usually comes from code that queries inside a loop (see the loop rules in Performance Rules Reference). A query with a high MaxMs and few executions is a candidate for Explain Plan. If the query text has parameters (@P1…), replace them with values before explaining it: Explain Plan does not accept DECLARE.

docs.title: Slowest batch jobs (last 7 days)
docs.text:
"Batch job history: runs, average and longest duration per job and company."

Reads BATCHJOBHISTORY for jobs started in the last 7 days that have an end time after their start. The top 25 by longest run.

Column Meaning Job The batch job's caption Company The company it ran in Runs Number of runs AvgSeconds Average duration in seconds MaxSeconds Longest duration in seconds

What to do: for a slow job of your own, record a trace of one run and open it with Analyze Trace, or run Analyze Performance on its classes. See Wizard: Batch Job for the recommended structure.

docs.title: Number sequences that serialize work
docs.text:
"Continuous sequences (a lock per number) and non-continuous ones without preallocation."

Reads NUMBERSEQUENCETABLE for sequences that are continuous, or have no preallocation (FETCHAHEAD = 0), with a review text per row:

Column Meaning NumberSequence The number sequence code Continuous 1 when continuous Preallocation 1 when preallocation is on PreallocationQty Numbers fetched ahead Review "Continuous: numbers are taken one at a time under a lock; keep it only where gaps are not allowed", or "No preallocation: each number is a database round trip; consider preallocating"

What to do: discuss with the functional consultant. Continuous sequences are needed where gaps are not allowed (often legal documents); elsewhere a non-continuous sequence with preallocation removes the lock and the round trips. The change is setup in Organization administration > Number sequences, not code.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
There are no settings. To change a query (another period, more rows, one company), edit the SQL in the tab and run it again; it stays read-only.

For example, the slowest batch jobs of one company over 30 days:

SELECT TOP 25 CAPTION AS Job, COUNT(*) AS Runs,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(second, STARTDATETIME, ENDDATETIME)) AS AvgSeconds,
  MAX(DATEDIFF(second, STARTDATETIME, ENDDATETIME)) AS MaxSeconds
FROM BATCHJOBHISTORY
WHERE STARTDATETIME > DATEADD(day, -30, GETUTCDATE()) AND ENDDATETIME > STARTDATETIME
  AND COMPANY = 'usmf'
GROUP BY CAPTION
ORDER BY MaxSeconds DESC

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The queries are defined once in core/src/data/insights.ts (part of @fno-studio/core, so other hosts can use them too).
  • The command (src/database/index.ts) shows the picker and opens a query panel with the chosen SQL and autoRun, which runs it with 500 rows.
  • They run like any query in the panel: read-only check, a transaction that is rolled back, 60-second limit. See SQL Query Panel and Database Access.
  • Nothing is cached; each run reads the database's current statistics.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The DMVs and Query Store hold what SQL Server collected; missing-index statistics are not kept forever, and Query Store must be on for the expensive-queries insight to return rows.
  • The insights look at the whole database, not your model. Map table names back to your tables yourself.
  • Batch job history only covers jobs whose history was kept.
  • They are pointers, not fixes. Verify each one with Explain Plan, a trace, or the code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The picker opens but the tab asks for credentials No access on a UDE Choose Request Credentials; see Database Access "Most expensive queries" returns no rows No Query Store data for the last day Use the environment first, or widen the period in the SQL "Slowest batch jobs" returns no rows No batch job with a start and end in the last 7 days Widen the period in the SQL A query is cut off after about a minute The 60-second time limit Narrow the period or add TOP

docs.title: Debugger Options
docs.text: The X++ debugger works without any configuration: F&O Studio: Launch Debugger builds the attach configuration for you. When you need something different (another process, more modules, quieter output), add an xpp configuration to .vscode/launch.json. This page lists every option, its default on a unified developer environment (UDE) and on cloud-hosted or VHD environments, and the one setting that affects the debugger proxy.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Debug the batch service on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (processName).
  • Step into standard code beyond the element you set a breakpoint in (additionalModules).
  • Stop the Debug Console from printing every exception (logging).
  • Use a debugger proxy from another folder (xpp.debuggerProxyPath).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A workspace folder (the configuration goes into its .vscode/launch.json).
  • Read Debugger first.

docs.title: Create the configuration
docs.text:
1. Open the Run and Debug view.
  2. Choose create a launch.json file and pick X++ (Dynamics 365 unified developer environment). VS Code writes the initial configuration:
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "xpp",
      "request": "attach",
      "name": "Attach to Dynamics 365 (unified developer environment)"
    }
  ]
}
  1. In an existing launch.json, choose Add Configuration… and pick the snippet X++: Attach to Dynamics 365.
  2. Add options from the table below. VS Code offers them with completion and descriptions.
  3. Start it from the Run and Debug view (select the configuration, press F5).

F&O Studio: Launch Debugger always uses the default configuration, not your launch.json. Start from the Run and Debug view to use your options.

A fuller example:

{
  "type": "xpp",
  "request": "attach",
  "name": "Attach to Dynamics 365",
  "justMyCode": true,
  "additionalModules": ["Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.*.netmodule"],
  "logging": { "exceptions": false }
}

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Type UDE default Cloud-hosted / VHD default Effect processName string AXHost.exe the runtime host type's AOS process Process to attach to justMyCode boolean on (debugger default) off when a standard element has a breakpoint, else on Step only through code with symbols loaded additionalModules string array [] [] More modules whose symbols load, wildcards allowed symbolOptions object F&O Studio's module filter not used Replaces the symbol options entirely logging object debugger default { "exceptions": false } vsdbg logging: exceptions, moduleLoad sourceFileMap object F&O Studio's mappings F&O Studio's mappings Extra source path mappings, merged over F&O Studio's

docs.title: processName
docs.text:
• UDE: the process in the environment that the debugger attaches to. Leave it at AXHost.exe, the process that runs the AOS in a UDE.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD: without it, F&O Studio attaches to the AOS of the runtime host type set in Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options (the IIS application pool workers, w3wp.exe, or iisexpress.exe). Any other name attaches to processes with that image name, for example "processName": "Batch.exe" for the batch service. AXHost.exe is ignored there. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: justMyCode
docs.text:
With Just My Code on, the debugger steps only through code whose symbols are loaded and stops only on exceptions in that code. Keep it on, on a UDE. Turning it off makes every exception the environment throws go through the debugger, and X++ throws many; the environment can stop responding for every user while you are attached. Visual Studio keeps it on too.

On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, F&O Studio turns it off by default only when you have a breakpoint in standard code, and on otherwise. Set it explicitly to override. See Debugging Standard Code.

docs.title: additionalModules
docs.text:
F&O Studio loads the symbols of only these modules (module filter loadOnlyIncluded):

  • your packages' modules: Dynamics.AX.<package>.*.netmodule and Dynamics.AX.<package>.*.dll for the package of each custom model;
  • the C# assemblies in your packages' bin folders that have a PDB (Debugging C# Code);
  • for each standard element with a breakpoint, the one module that holds it, for example Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.16.netmodule.

additionalModules adds names to that list. Wildcards are allowed, for example "Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.*.netmodule". Empty entries are ignored. Each extra module makes loading slower, and a broad wildcard over a standard package can make the environment slow to respond while symbols load. Prefer a breakpoint in the element you need (its module is picked automatically) over a wildcard.

docs.title: symbolOptions
docs.text: The debugger's own symbolOptions object (for example moduleFilter). On a UDE, when you set it, it replaces F&O Studio's symbol options completely: your packages, referenced assemblies and standard modules are then loaded only if your object says so. Use additionalModules to add modules instead. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments this option is not used; F&O Studio always builds the symbol options there.

docs.title: logging
docs.text: The debugger's logging options. { "exceptions": false } stops printing each exception in the Debug Console; moduleLoad controls the module load messages. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments F&O Studio sets { "exceptions": false } unless you give your own.

docs.title: sourceFileMap
docs.text:
Extra mappings from a path recorded in the symbols to a folder on this machine. F&O Studio already maps the compiler's source roots to its debug source folder (%TEMP%\XppDebugSource; see Breakpoints and Source Mapping); your entries are added and win on the same key. Use it, for example, when a C# assembly was built in another folder:

"sourceFileMap": { "C:\\agent\\_work\\1\\s\\": "${workspaceFolder}\\" }

docs.title: Attributes F&O Studio fills in
docs.text: On a UDE, F&O Studio also sets console: "internalConsole" and requireExactSource: false. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments it sets requireExactSource: false, the process ID, and the symbol search paths. You do not need to add these.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.debuggerProxyPath empty Path to Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe (UDE). Empty: the FinOps tools installed by F&O Studio: Connect to Environment…, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\FinOpsTools\DebuggerProxy. Machine scope: only your user settings can set it, not a workspace, because F&O Studio runs that file xpp.build.restartLocalAos true Cloud-hosted and VHD: restart the running AOS hosts after a successful build so they load it; the debugger detaches first

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The options are declared in the debuggers contribution of package.json (debug type xpp, request attach) and applied in resolveDebugConfiguration and attachLocal in src/debug.ts.

  • UDE: your configuration is passed on to the debugger with F&O Studio's values filled in where you gave none: processName, console, requireExactSource, sourceFileMap (merged) and symbolOptions (yours or F&O Studio's). justMyCode is only sent when you set it. The proxy path is resolved from xpp.debuggerProxyPath, else from the FinOps tools folder of the environment's application version, else of the active configuration's version.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD: F&O Studio builds a new clr configuration per AOS process and takes processName, justMyCode, logging, sourceFileMap and additionalModules from yours.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Launch Debugger ignores launch.json; start from Run and Debug to use your options.
  • There is no launch request; the debugger only attaches.
  • symbolOptions has no effect on cloud-hosted and VHD environments.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The environment stops responding while attached justMyCode: false, or a wide additionalModules wildcard Remove them and disconnect Your packages' breakpoints stay hollow after adding symbolOptions Your symbolOptions replaced F&O Studio's module filter Remove symbolOptions and use additionalModules "Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe was not found. …" Wrong or empty proxy path and no FinOps tools for this version Run F&O Studio: Connect to Environment… or fix xpp.debuggerProxyPath processName ignored on a VHD It is AXHost.exe Leave it out, or name the process you want (e.g. Batch.exe)

docs.title: Debugger
docs.text:
F&O Studio debugs X++ in VS Code's own debugger: breakpoints, stepping, variables, the call stack, the Debug Console and the Infolog. On a unified developer environment (UDE) it attaches to AXHost.exe in the cloud through Microsoft's debugger proxy, exactly the way Visual Studio's Launch Debugger does. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments it attaches to the local AOS with the C# extension's .NET debugger, the way Visual Studio's F5 does. You set breakpoints in the X++ code view of your own elements and of standard elements, and in the C# code your project references.

This page is the overview. The details are on separate pages:

Page What it covers Breakpoints and Source Mapping How a breakpoint in the code view reaches the compiled code, debug source files, PDB document names Debugging Standard Code Breakpoints in Microsoft's elements (for example PurchTable.init), module loading, Just My Code Debugging C# Code Breakpoints in the C# assemblies your X++ project references Debugging on Cloud-Hosted Cloud-hosted and VHD environments: local AOS, IIS or IIS Express, Batch.exe, portable PDBs Infolog The Infolog view: messages raised by the code you debug Debugger Options launch.json options and the xpp.debuggerProxyPath setting

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see why a class, table method or form method behaves the way it does on a running environment.
  • You want to stop in standard code (for example the init method of the PurchTable form) to understand what it does before you extend it.
  • You need the Infolog messages that the code raises while you step through it.
  • Your X++ project calls a C# library and you want to step into it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An environment selected. Run F&O Studio: Select Environment… (or F&O Studio: Connect to Environment… for a new UDE). See Select Environment and Connect to Environment.
  • A UDE: the FinOps tools that Connect to Environment… downloads contain the debugger proxy (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\FinOpsTools\DebuggerProxy\Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe). You sign in with your Microsoft account; F&O Studio uses the Dataverse token of that sign-in (Sign-In and Authentication).
  • A cloud-hosted or VHD environment: the C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp) is needed; F&O Studio offers to install it. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.
  • Built code. Build your model first (Build Project and Model). On a UDE the environment runs the deployed code, so deploy what you built (Deploy to Environment). On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the build restarts the AOS so it loads the new build.

docs.title: Start the debugger
docs.text:
Start it in any of these ways:

  • Command Palette: F&O Studio: Launch Debugger.
  • Dynamics 365 view: the Debug group has Launch Debugger (and Infolog). The view's title bar also has the Launch Debugger button.
  • Infolog view (in the F&O Studio panel): the Launch Debugger button in its title bar.
  • Run and Debug view: with no launch.json, press F5 (Run > Start Debugging) and pick the X++ debugger, or add a configuration to .vscode/launch.json (see Debugger Options). The configuration snippet is X++: Attach to Dynamics 365, and the configuration it creates is:
{
  "type": "xpp",
  "request": "attach",
  "name": "Attach to Dynamics 365 (unified developer environment)"
}

The debugger always attaches. There is no launch request: the environment is already running.

docs.title: What happens on a UDE
docs.text:
1. When your project's model was built after its last deploy from this machine, a warning says so and adds "The debugger uses the deployed code." Choose Deploy First to run Deploy Models to Environment (the debugger does not start), or Continue to debug the code that is deployed.
  2. A notification Preparing X++ debugging… shows the steps: signing in, then writing debug sources.
  3. F&O Studio starts the debugger proxy and attaches to AXHost.exe. The Debug toolbar appears.
  4. Use the environment in the browser (open the form, run the class). When the code reaches a breakpoint, VS Code stops and shows the line in the element's X++ code view.
  5. Step (F10, F11, Shift+F11), look at Variables, Watch and Call Stack, and evaluate expressions in the Debug Console as with any VS Code debugger.
  6. Press Continue (F5) or Disconnect when you are done.

docs.title: What happens on cloud-hosted and VHD environments
docs.text: F&O Studio recognises the local environment and attaches to the AOS process on this machine with the C# extension's clr debugger, one debug session per process. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: Set breakpoints
docs.text: Open the element's code view (click a class in the Application Explorer, or View Code on a table or form) and click in the gutter, or press F9. That is all: F&O Studio copies each code view breakpoint to the compiled view of the element and reports the copy's state on your breakpoint. A solid red dot means it is bound; a hollow one shows a message when you hover it, for example "Waiting for the symbols to load.". Conditions, hit counts and logpoints work. See Breakpoints and Source Mapping.

docs.title: The environment pauses for every user
docs.text:
On a UDE, the debugger stops the server process (AXHost.exe), not just your session. While VS Code is stopped at a breakpoint, or after you press Pause, the environment's server is paused for every user of that environment: pages stop responding until you continue. Continue or disconnect promptly, and do not leave a session stopped.

F&O Studio protects the environment in several ways:

  • Disconnect resumes first. When you disconnect (or stop) while the server is stopped, F&O Studio sends continue first and only then detaches. The X++ output says "Resuming the environment before the debugger detaches.".
  • It never ends the process. An attached debugger only detaches: terminateDebuggee is always sent as false, on a UDE and on the local AOS. Stopping the debugger never takes the AOS down.
  • Closing or reloading the window resumes and detaches every session, then stops the proxy (after at most about three seconds).
  • A crashed window can leave a debugger proxy running. F&O Studio remembers the proxies it started; when it starts again it stops proxies whose window is gone and logs "Stopped a debugger left attached by a closed window (DebuggerProxy ).". Proxies of other open windows are left alone.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Where Key Default Effect Setting xpp.debuggerProxyPath empty Path to Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe. Empty uses the FinOps tools installed by Connect to Environment. Machine scope (a workspace cannot set it) Setting xpp.build.restartLocalAos true Cloud-hosted and VHD only: a successful build restarts the running AOS hosts (and detaches the debugger first) launch.json justMyCode on (UDE) Keep it on. See Debugger Options launch.json additionalModules [] More modules whose symbols load launch.json symbolOptions F&O Studio's Replaces the symbol options entirely (UDE) launch.json logging vsdbg logging, e.g. { "exceptions": false } launch.json processName AXHost.exe Process to attach to; on cloud-hosted and VHD e.g. Batch.exe launch.json sourceFileMap Extra source path mappings

Full details: Debugger Options.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The code is in src/debug.ts. F&O Studio registers the debug type xpp ("X++ (Dynamics 365 unified developer environment)") with a configuration provider and a debug adapter factory, plus a tracker on the clr debug type for the local AOS.

docs.title: UDE: the debugger proxy is the debug adapter
docs.text:
Visual Studio debugs a UDE through Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe (part of the FinOps tools). The proxy has a mode for Visual Studio Code's .NET debugger, vsdbg: it speaks the Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) on stdin/stdout and tunnels to vsdbg running next to AXHost.exe in the environment, over wss://<environment>/___sidecar/AOS1/remote-debugger/connect.

  1. Sign-in and environment. F&O Studio reads the selected environment's Dataverse URL, gets a Dataverse token and asks the environment for its finance and operations URL and application version.
  2. Find the proxy. xpp.debuggerProxyPath if set; else %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<application version>\FinOpsTools\DebuggerProxy\, then the same folder for the version of the active configuration.
  3. Write debug sources for your models and for standard elements with breakpoints, and copy the code view breakpoints onto them (Breakpoints and Source Mapping).
  4. Build the attach configuration: processName AXHost.exe, requireExactSource: false, a sourceFileMap that maps the compiler's source root (e:\source\) to the debug source folder, and symbolOptions with a module filter (loadOnlyIncluded) listing your packages' modules (Dynamics.AX.<package>.*.netmodule and .*.dll), the C# assemblies your projects reference, and the one module of each standard element with a breakpoint. Just My Code is left at the debugger's default (on), as Visual Studio does.
  5. Start the proxy inline. The arguments are the ones Visual Studio passes in its VSDbgLaunch.json:
Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe --port <free local port> --remoteProxyHost <environment host>
    --VSVersion vsdbg --accessToken <Dataverse token>

F&O Studio picks a free port instead of the default 5119, so a Visual Studio session or a leftover proxy on that port does not stop it. It runs the proxy itself (a ProxyDebugAdapter) rather than as a plain executable, so the proxy's error output goes to the X++ output channel (prefixed [DebuggerProxy]) and its exit code is reported, instead of VS Code's bare "read error".

The adapter changes a few messages on the way:

Message Change Why initialize adapterID is set to clr vsdbg rejects VS Code's debug type xpp; clr is .NET Framework, as in Visual Studio's launch file setBreakpoints on a code view (xpp:) Answered by F&O Studio with the state of the breakpoint's copy vsdbg does not know the code view; the copy on the debug source binds setBreakpoints, breakpointLocations, source Debug source paths are replaced by the symbols' document names (xppSource://Source/<model folder>\<AxType>_<Name>.xpp) A local path mapped with sourceFileMap does not bind to those documents Messages from vsdbg xppSource names are turned back into the debug source files So VS Code can open them stackTrace response Frames in a debug source file point at the same line of the element's code view You see the stop where you set the breakpoint disconnect continue first if stopped; terminateDebuggee: false The environment serves every user

docs.title: Cloud-hosted and VHD
docs.text: When the active environment is local, the configuration provider does not start the xpp adapter. It converts the packages' PDBs to portable PDBs, writes the debug sources and starts one clr attach session per AOS process. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: Infolog
docs.text: A debug adapter tracker on both xpp and clr sessions reads output events. Infolog messages arrive there as <InfologMessage> XML, as in Visual Studio's Infolog window; F&O Studio parses them into the Infolog view.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview. The debugger is part of a preview extension. It was verified on a UDE (10.0.2790.108) and on a VHD (10.0.46, IIS and IIS Express). Cloud-hosted environments use the VHD code path but have not been tested.
  • The debugger only attaches. It cannot start the environment or a process.
  • On a UDE you debug the deployed code. Breakpoints in code you changed but did not deploy bind to the old lines, or not at all.
  • Breakpoints in an element only bind if the element was prepared when the session started. A breakpoint in a standard element you add during the session says "This element was not prepared for debugging when the session started; restart the debugger."
  • Stopping pauses the environment for everyone (see above).
  • There is no process list to pick from. On a UDE the process is AXHost.exe unless you set processName.

docs.title: Debugging C# Code
docs.text: When your X++ project references a C# library (a C# project in the solution or an assembly), you can set breakpoints in its .cs files and the debugger stops there next to your X++ breakpoints. F&O Studio loads the symbols of the assemblies your projects reference, the way Visual Studio's debugger does for referenced assemblies, so you can follow a call from X++ into C# in one session.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• X++ code calls a .NET helper (for example a parser, a file format library or an HTTP client wrapper you wrote in C#) and you want to step into it.
  • A C# class calls back into X++ (Dynamics.AX.Application) and you want to stop on both sides.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A C# reference in your X++ project. Add it in the project view with Add Reference…, or create one with New C# Project…. See Solution View and C# References.
  • A build. Build builds the referenced C# projects first with MSBuild and copies their assemblies, PDB files and dependencies into your package's bin folder before X++ is compiled. Finance and Operations' own assemblies are never copied. See Build Project and Model.
  • On a UDE: a deploy. Deploy Models to Environment refreshes the referenced assemblies first, so the deployed package carries them. See Deploy to Environment.
  • On cloud-hosted and VHD environments: the build restarts the AOS so it loads the new assemblies (Debugging on Cloud-Hosted).
  • Breakpoints in .cs files. VS Code lets you set breakpoints in C# files when an extension that debugs C# is installed, such as the C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp). That extension also gives you IntelliSense in the C# projects of your solution.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Build your project (and on a UDE, deploy it).
  2. Open the .cs file from the project view (the C# projects of the solution are listed with their files) and set a breakpoint.
  3. Set X++ breakpoints where you want them too, for example on the X++ line that calls the C# method.
  4. Start the debugger: F&O Studio: Launch Debugger.
  5. Run the code in the environment. The debugger stops on the X++ breakpoint; Step Into (F11) on the call to the C# method, or let it run to the C# breakpoint.

Example X++ calling a C# library:

using Contoso.Integration;

internal final class ContosoOrderExport
{
    public static void main(Args _args)
    {
        OrderSerializer serializer = new OrderSerializer();
        str json = serializer.Serialize(SalesTable::find('000123').SalesId);
        info(json);
    }
}

With a breakpoint on the serializer.Serialize(...) line and one in OrderSerializer.Serialize in the C# project, the debugger stops on both.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Where Key Effect launch.json additionalModules Add assemblies whose symbols should load that F&O Studio does not pick up (for example an assembly without a PDB in your package's bin) launch.json symbolOptions UDE only: replaces the module filter entirely; referenced assemblies are then only loaded if you list them Setting xpp.build.msbuildPath The MSBuild that builds the referenced C# projects

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The code is in src/debug.ts (referencedAssemblies, includedModules) and src/dotnetReferences.ts (referencedModules).

  1. Which assemblies. When a session starts, F&O Studio looks in the bin folder of the package of each of your custom models and takes every .dll that has a .pdb with the same name next to it and whose name does not start with Dynamics.AX.. These are the assemblies the build copied there from your C# references.
  2. Module filter. Those assembly names are added to the debugger's module filter (loadOnlyIncluded), next to your X++ packages' modules (Dynamics.AX.<package>.*.netmodule and .*.dll) and the modules of standard elements with breakpoints. Without them, the debugger would not load the C# symbols and the C# breakpoints would stay hollow.
  3. Portable PDBs. The VS Code .NET debugger reads only portable PDBs. A successful build converts every Windows PDB in the package's bin folder that has a matching .dll or .netmodule to a portable PDB with Microsoft's Pdb2Pdb (shipped with F&O Studio). That includes the PDBs of referenced assemblies built with Windows PDBs. See Debugging on Cloud-Hosted.
  4. Source files. The C# breakpoints are sent to the debugger on the .cs paths as they are; the PDB records the path the project was built from. requireExactSource is off, so a source that changed slightly since the build is still shown.

The same assemblies are included on a UDE (through the debugger proxy) and on the local AOS (through the C# extension's debugger).

docs.title: Going to definition across X++ and C
docs.text: Not part of the debugger, but useful while debugging: Go to Definition in X++ code on a .NET type of the solution's C# projects opens the C# source, and in C# code on an X++ type (Dynamics.AX.Application.CustTable) opens the X++ code view. Hover and completion also show .NET types in X++. The code is in src/clrNavigation.ts. See Go to Definition.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Not tested yet: stopping at a C# breakpoint on a UDE or a VHD has not been verified end to end. X++ calling C# and C# calling X++ build and run together; the debugging part is untested.
  • Only assemblies in your packages' bin folders with a PDB next to them are included. Any other assembly needs additionalModules and its symbols.
  • If you set symbolOptions in launch.json (UDE), F&O Studio's module list, including the referenced assemblies, is replaced by yours.
  • On a UDE, the C# code runs as deployed: rebuild and deploy after changing it.
  • Source paths are the ones recorded at build time. If you build on another machine or move the project, VS Code may not find the .cs file; add a sourceFileMap entry.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix C# breakpoint hollow The assembly's PDB is not in your package's bin, or was not converted Build again; check the X++ Build output for "was not converted to a portable PDB" C# breakpoint hollow on a UDE after a code change The environment runs the previously deployed assembly Build and deploy, then restart the debugger You cannot set a breakpoint in a .cs file No installed extension declares C# breakpoints Install the C# extension Stops show "source not found" The PDB records a path that does not exist on this machine Add a sourceFileMap entry from the recorded folder to your project folder

docs.title: Debugging Standard Code
docs.text: You can stop in Microsoft's own X++ code, for example the init method of the PurchTable form or SalesFormLetter.run, on a unified developer environment and on cloud-hosted or VHD environments. Set the breakpoint in the standard element's code view and start the debugger; F&O Studio loads the symbols of only the module that holds that element, the way Visual Studio does, so the environment keeps responding. This is how you learn what standard code does before you extend it with Chain of Command or an event handler.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see which branch standard code takes with your data (for example why PurchTable initialises a field).
  • You are choosing where to hook in: which method runs, in which order, with which values.
  • You want to confirm that your Chain of Command wrapper runs around the standard method (set breakpoints in both).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Everything on Debugger: a selected environment, and on a UDE the FinOps tools from F&O Studio: Connect to Environment….
  • The standard element's package must be on this machine with its symbols (the .pdb files in PackagesLocalDirectory\<package>\bin). Connect to Environment downloads them for a UDE; cloud-hosted and VHD environments have them.
  • Run the code once before you start the debugger (open the form, run the process). The module that holds the element is then already loaded in the server, and the breakpoint binds right away.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the standard element's code view. For example, find PurchTable with Open Element (Open Element) and choose View Code on the form, or click SalesFormLetter in the Application Explorer.
  2. Set a breakpoint on a line inside the method you want (click in the gutter or press F9).
  3. Start the debugger: F&O Studio: Launch Debugger. The X++ output lists the standard elements prepared for this session, for example:
Debugging standard code too: PurchTable (Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.16, xppSource://Source/Foundation\AxForm_PurchTable.xpp).

The module name in the parentheses is the one whose symbols load. When F&O Studio cannot find the module, the line says all of <package> instead and the symbols of all the package's modules load (slower). 4. Do what runs the code in the browser. The debugger stops in the code view of the standard element; step, inspect variables and continue. 5. Continue or disconnect promptly. While stopped, the environment's server is paused for every user.

docs.title: Adding breakpoints during a session
docs.text: Breakpoints in your own models can be added at any time. A breakpoint in a standard element that had no breakpoint when the session started cannot bind: its module was not included. It shows "This element was not prepared for debugging when the session started; restart the debugger." Disconnect and start the debugger again. More breakpoints in an element that was already prepared bind normally.

docs.title: Which element types
docs.text: Breakpoints in standard classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, queries and maps are supported, the element types the compiler emits as their own source file. See Breakpoints and Source Mapping.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
launch.json option Effect on standard code additionalModules More modules to load symbols for, with wildcards, for example "Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.*.netmodule". Use it to step into other standard code that is not in the prepared module. Each extra module makes loading slower justMyCode Leave it at the default. See below symbolOptions UDE only: replaces F&O Studio's module filter entirely, including the standard modules it picks

Details: Debugger Options.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The code is in src/debug.ts (standardBreakpointElements, moduleOfElement, includedModules).

docs.title: Finding the standard elements
docs.text: When the session starts, F&O Studio looks at every breakpoint in a code view. For each element of a debuggable type it asks the metadata server for the element's model (read_object). If that model is not one of your custom models, the element is standard: F&O Studio records its package, the model's folder name (for example Foundation for Application Suite) and looks for the module that holds it.

docs.title: One module, not the whole package
docs.text:
A standard package is compiled into hundreds of modules (.netmodule files with their .pdb). Loading the symbols of all of them takes minutes, and on a UDE, loading them while attached made the environment stop responding. F&O Studio reads the PDBs in <PackagesLocalDirectory>\<package>\bin and finds the one whose document list contains <model folder>\<AxType>_<Name>.xpp, for example Foundation\AxForm_PurchTable.xpp. That PDB's module (for example Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.16) is the only standard module added to the debugger's module filter, as <module>.netmodule. The exact document name, with its case as written in the PDB, becomes the name F&O Studio sends breakpoints to. The result is cached for the rest of the VS Code session.

Never the package's main Dynamics.AX.<package>.dll: Visual Studio includes only the element's netmodule, and including the main assembly was one of the causes of an unresponsive environment found in testing.

docs.title: Debug sources for standard elements
docs.text: Only standard elements with a breakpoint get a debug source file (a standard package has tens of thousands of elements). The file is written under the model folder the symbols record, for example %TEMP%\XppDebugSource\foundation\axform_purchtable.xpp, with the text the compiler numbered (complete_source). See Breakpoints and Source Mapping.

docs.title: Just My Code
docs.text:
Just My Code tells the debugger to step only through code that has symbols loaded and to stop only on exceptions in that code.

  • UDE: F&O Studio leaves Just My Code at the debugger's default, on, as Visual Studio's own launch file does. With it off, every exception AXHost.exe throws (X++ throws many) goes through the debugger and the environment hardly responds while attached. It also does not change symbols-on-demand or exception logging on a UDE. Only set justMyCode in launch.json if you know why.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD: unless you set justMyCode, F&O Studio turns Just My Code off when there is a standard-code breakpoint (and on otherwise), turns off exception logging (logging.exceptions: false), and lets the debugger load symbols on demand and from next to the modules. This configuration was verified on a VHD with a breakpoint in PurchTable.init.

docs.title: Why the environment could hang, and what changed
docs.text: An earlier version turned Just My Code off on a UDE, loaded symbols on demand, and included the package's main assembly. Every hang happened when the element's module loaded while the debugger was attached. The current settings match Visual Studio's (its CloudRuntimeHostSupplier and debugger symbol options) and were verified on a UDE: the breakpoint in PurchTable.init bound at attach, stopped and stepped.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• A breakpoint added during a session in a standard element that was not prepared does not bind until you restart the debugger.
  • Only the module that holds the element loads symbols. Stepping into other standard code (another class) shows no source unless you add its module with additionalModules.
  • On a UDE, a module that loads after you attach was not retested with these settings. Run the code once before attaching, as advised.
  • The module lookup reads PDB files from PackagesLocalDirectory; it needs the symbols that match the environment's version. If your local metadata is a different version from the environment, lines may not match (Version Drift Guard).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The X++ output says all of <package> for the element No PDB in the package's bin names the element Check that the package's symbols are present; loading will be slower "This element was not prepared for debugging when the session started; restart the debugger." The element got its first breakpoint during the session Restart the debugger Breakpoint hollow, "Waiting for the symbols to load." The module has not loaded in the server yet Run the code once (open the form), or restart the debugger after running it The environment stops responding while attached Just My Code turned off, or many modules added Remove justMyCode: false and large additionalModules wildcards; disconnect Stepping into another standard method shows no source Its module is not loaded Add it with additionalModules, or set a breakpoint in that element too and restart
