docs.title: Debugging on Cloud-Hosted
docs.text: On cloud-hosted and VHD (downloadable virtual machine) environments, the AOS runs on the same machine as VS Code. F&O Studio debugs it the way Visual Studio's F5 does: it attaches to the AOS process of the runtime host type you chose in Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options (the AOS site's application pool in IIS, or IIS Express), with no process list to pick from. It uses the C# extension's .NET debugger (clr), converts the compiler's PDBs so that debugger can read them, and restarts the AOS after each build so it runs what you built. This is a preview.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You develop on a cloud-hosted environment or a VHD and want to debug X++ without Visual Studio.
  • You want to debug the batch service (Batch.exe) on such an environment.

For a unified developer environment (UDE), see Debugger; the start is the same, the mechanism differs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The active configuration is a local environment (cloud-hosted or VHD). F&O Studio uses the local PackagesLocalDirectory, AOS and AxDB; there is no connection step. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.
  • The C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp). F&O Studio uses its .NET debugger. When it is missing, F&O Studio offers to install it; when it is installed but disabled, F&O Studio says so and opens its page so you can enable it. The C# extension downloads its debugger on its first activation; F&O Studio waits for that download (a cancellable notification "Waiting for the C# extension to install its debugger…").
  • The AOS is running. Open the web client once so IIS or IIS Express starts the AOS process.
  • Run VS Code as administrator if restarting the AOS after a build fails with "access denied", as Visual Studio must be run on these environments.
  • Your code is built. The build converts the PDBs and restarts the AOS (Build Project and Model).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Build your project or model. On success, the X++ Build output shows the conversion and the restart, for example:
Converted 3 PDB(s) to portable PDBs for debugging in VS Code.
Restarting the local AOS so it loads the new build:
  Recycling application pool AOSService (IIS site AOSService): done.
  Restarting the batch service (DynamicsAxBatch): done.
  1. Set breakpoints in the code view of your elements or of standard elements.
  2. Run F&O Studio: Launch Debugger (or press F5 in Run and Debug with an xpp configuration).
  3. A notification Preparing X++ debugging… shows converting symbols to portable PDBs, then writing debug sources.
  4. F&O Studio starts one debug session per AOS process, named for example Attach to the local AOS (w3wp.exe 9172, IIS site AOSService, application pool AOSService). The Call Stack view shows each session.
  5. Use the web client. The debugger stops in the code view; step, inspect and continue.
  6. Press Stop or Disconnect: the debugger detaches and the AOS keeps running.

docs.title: Debugging the batch service
docs.text:
Add a configuration to .vscode/launch.json with processName:

{
  "type": "xpp",
  "request": "attach",
  "name": "Attach to the batch service",
  "processName": "Batch.exe"
}

Any process name other than AXHost.exe attaches by name (.exe is added if you leave it out). AXHost.exe (the default, meant for a UDE) is ignored here and the runtime host type decides.

docs.title: Which process
docs.text:
Runtime host type (Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options) Process attached IIS (default) The w3wp.exe worker processes of the application pool of the AOS site (AosWebsiteName, AOSService by default), found with appcmd IISExpress The iisexpress.exe processes processName set in launch.json Processes with that image name

Visual Studio attaches to every process of the host; the .NET debugger takes one process per session, so F&O Studio starts one session per process.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Where Key Default Effect Setting xpp.build.restartLocalAos true After a successful build, restart the AOS hosts that are running (IIS Express, the AOS application pool in IIS, the batch service). The debugger detaches first launch.json processName Attach to this process instead, e.g. Batch.exe launch.json justMyCode on, or off when there is a standard-code breakpoint See Debugger Options launch.json logging { "exceptions": false } vsdbg logging launch.json additionalModules [] More modules whose symbols load launch.json sourceFileMap Extra source path mappings

symbolOptions in launch.json is not used on the local AOS: F&O Studio always builds its own symbol options there (use additionalModules).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The code is attachLocal in src/debug.ts, the AOS discovery in core/src/environment/localAos.ts and the PDB conversion in src/portablePdb.ts.

docs.title: Finding the AOS
docs.text:
F&O Studio reads the same places the environment's own tools record:

  1. Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options: Documents\Visual Studio Dynamics 365\DynamicsDevConfig.xml, falling back to the machine default (DefaultConfig under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX\Development). From there: RuntimeHostType (IIS by default), AosWebsiteName (AOSService by default) and WebRoleDeploymentFolder.
  2. The AOS web.config: in the web role folder, or the one the batch service (DynamicsAxBatch) runs with.
  3. PackagesLocalDirectory: aos.packagedirectory or common.bindir from the web.config, or the folder of DefaultConfig; the first one that contains bin\xppc.exe.

No drive is assumed, so PackagesLocalDirectory on K: or C: both work.

docs.title: Portable PDBs
docs.text: The X++ compiler writes Windows PDBs; the C# extension's debugger reads only portable PDBs. Before attaching (and after every successful build), F&O Studio converts every Windows PDB in your packages' bin folders that has a matching .netmodule or .dll, in place, with Microsoft's Pdb2Pdb (shipped in the extension under tools\pdb2pdb), four at a time. A PDB the AOS has open cannot be overwritten but can be renamed: it is moved aside to <package>\BuildLogs\ReplacedPdbs and deleted on a later conversion. Microsoft's own packages already ship portable PDBs. Visual Studio's debugger reads both formats, so it debugs the converted PDBs too.

docs.title: The attach configuration
docs.text:
For each process F&O Studio starts a clr attach session with:

  • processId of the process;
  • justMyCode: your value, else off when a standard element has a breakpoint and on otherwise;
  • logging: your value, else { "exceptions": false };
  • requireExactSource: false;
  • sourceFileMap: xppSource:\\Source\ and the compiler's source root (e:\source\) to the debug source folder %TEMP%\XppDebugSource, plus yours;
  • symbolOptions: search paths = your packages' bin folders and the bin folders of standard packages with breakpoints; no Microsoft symbol server; module filter loadOnlyIncluded with your packages' modules, referenced C# assemblies, the module of each standard element with a breakpoint and your additionalModules; symbols next to modules and on demand.

The debug sources and breakpoint copies are the same as on a UDE (Breakpoints and Source Mapping).

docs.title: Stop only detaches
docs.text: Stopping an attach session sends disconnect with terminateDebuggee: true, and the .NET debugger would then end w3wp.exe (or the batch service) for every user. F&O Studio's tracker on the clr sessions it started changes that to false, so stopping always detaches.

docs.title: Restart after build
docs.text:
After a successful build (unless xpp.build.restartLocalAos is off) F&O Studio detaches the local debug sessions first, then restarts the hosts that are running, as Visual Studio does:

Host Action IIS Express Stopped and started again with its own command line IIS The AOS site's application pool is recycled (appcmd recycle apppool) Batch service DynamicsAxBatch The process is ended and the service started again right away. Batch tasks that were running are cut off

Hosts that are not running are left alone. The build output says how many sessions were detached; start debugging again when the AOS is back.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview. Verified on a VHD (10.0.46) on IIS and on IIS Express: build converts the PDBs and restarts the AOS, attach without a process list, breakpoints in your own and in standard code stop, step, continue, Infolog; stopping leaves the AOS running. Cloud-hosted environments use the same code path but have not been tested. The current way of restarting the batch service has not been run on a VHD yet.
  • Deploy and Run Tests are UDE-only; on these environments the build itself updates the running AOS.
  • The restart cuts off running batch tasks.
  • One session per process: with several worker processes you see several sessions.
  • When stopped, the AOS process is paused for every user of the environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The local AOS was not found: neither Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options nor the batch service name its web.config and PackagesLocalDirectory." None of the sources above lead to a PackagesLocalDirectory with bin\xppc.exe Check Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options and the batch service "No IIS site AOSService (w3wp.exe) process is running. Open the web client once to start the AOS, then try again. …" The AOS has not started since the last restart Open the web client, then start the debugger again "IIS is not installed on this machine (appcmd.exe not found). …" Runtime host type is IIS but IIS is missing Set Runtime host type to IISExpress in Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options "The C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp) is installed but disabled. …" The C# extension is disabled Enable it (Show C# Extension), then start again "The C# extension's debugger is not installed yet. Check the C# output, then start debugging again." The C# extension's debugger download did not finish Check the C# output; try again " was not converted to a portable PDB, so its breakpoints will not bind: …" in the X++ output Pdb2Pdb failed for that PDB Rebuild; check that the file is not locked by another tool Restart step "FAILED … Run VS Code as administrator, as Visual Studio must be on this environment." Restarting IIS or the service needs elevation Run VS Code as administrator "Warning: the AOS may still run the previous build until it is restarted." A restart step failed Restart the AOS yourself "read error" in the Debug Console after disconnect The C# extension reports it when its debugger exits Harmless

docs.title: Deploy to Environment
docs.text: Deploy Models to Environment uploads your packages, exactly as you built them on this machine, to your unified developer environment (UDE) and waits until the environment has applied them, optionally with a database sync. It is the equivalent of Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 > Deploy > Deploy Models to Online Environment and uses the same Dataverse API. Nothing is recompiled on the way, so the environment runs the build you debug. The Power Platform CLI (pac) is not needed.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After a successful build, so that the environment, the debugger, Run Tests, Run Snippet and the web client run your latest code.
  • When the project item in the Status Bar shows the cloud-upload icon (built after the last deploy).
  • After you changed tables or other synchronized elements, with a Module or Full database sync.

Cloud-hosted and VHD environments do not need a deploy: their local AOS runs what you build. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A unified developer environment, connected on this machine and selected in this window (Connect to Environment, Select Environment).
  • Signed in with VS Code's Microsoft account to the environment's Dataverse (Sign In and Authentication). Your account needs the rights to deploy to the environment.
  • A built package. Only packages in your custom metadata folder with bin\Dynamics.AX.<package>.dll are offered. Build first (Build Project and Model). Packages linked into the metadata folder with a junction or symbolic link (for example by Open Team Repository) are offered too.
  • If your X++ project references C# projects or assemblies, MSBuild must be available; the deploy refreshes them in the package first.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the deploy in one of these ways:
  2. Dynamics 365 view: Deploy > Deploy Models to Online Environment…;
  3. command palette: F&O Studio: Deploy Models to Environment;
  4. the Deploy now link in the tooltip of the project item in the status bar;
  5. Deploy First in the warning that Run Tests, the Debugger or Verify Changes in the Running App show when the build is newer than the deploy;
  6. Deploy after a passed Pre-Deploy Checklist.
  7. Pick the packages in Packages to deploy (as built on this machine). The list shows every built package with its folder; your project's package is preselected. You can select several.
  8. Pick the Database sync after deploy: | Option | Effect | |---|---| | None | No database sync. | | Module | Synchronize the tables of the deployed packages. | | Full | Synchronize the whole database (slow). |
  9. The X++ Deploy output opens and a notification "Deploying " shows each step. Typical output: 
    Deploying ContosoExtensions to https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com (database sync: Module)…
Packaging ContosoExtensions from <custom metadata folder>\ContosoExtensions…
Uploading ContosoExtensions_1_0_0_1_managed.zip (5120 KB)…
Deployment started (system job <id>). This usually takes several minutes, longer with the database sync.
  deployment: <status>
  deployment: <status>
Deployed.

    The status lines are the formatted status of the environment's system job; a new line appears when it changes. 5. When the deploy ends, the message "Deployed ." appears. The deploy is recorded for the models in those packages, so the status bar shows that the environment runs the latest build.

    Click Cancel on the notification to stop waiting. The message then says that the deployment keeps running on the environment, with its system job id.

docs.title: Deploy as a task
docs.text: The task { "type": "xpp", "action": "deploy", "dbSync": "Module" } deploys the active project's package without the pickers. See Build Tasks.

docs.title: Optional pac commands
docs.text:
Deploy does not use pac. Two commands remain for teams that deploy with the Power Platform CLI themselves:

  • Sign In to Environment (pac) creates (or selects) a pac auth profile named after the environment's org.
  • Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) runs pac package init --package-type erp --model <models> in the workspace folder.

Both are hidden on cloud-hosted and VHD environments. xpp.pacPath points at pac when it is not on PATH. See Power Platform CLI.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild used to refresh the C# projects and assemblies the X++ project references before the deploy. xpp.pacPath empty Path to pac, for the optional pac commands only.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The command is in src/pac.ts (PacCommands.deploy); the transport is in the core library, core/src/deploy.ts, reached through src/udeDeploy.ts. The flow was taken from what Power Platform Tools and pac do for Visual Studio's deploy.

docs.title: 1. Refresh the project package
docs.text:
For the open project's package only:

  • the C# projects and assemblies the X++ project references are built with MSBuild and copied into <package>\bin, as the build does (src/dotnetReferences.ts);
  • Windows PDBs in <package>\bin are converted to portable PDBs (Pdb2Pdb), because the UDE debugger reads portable PDBs only.

If the references fail, the deploy stops before anything is uploaded.

docs.title: 2. Check the environment
docs.text: F&O Studio checks that the Dataverse org has the solution msprov_fnouploadersolution. Without it the deploy fails with " has no Finance and Operations deployment support (solution msprov_fnouploadersolution). Is it a unified developer environment?"

docs.title: 3. Zip each package
docs.text:
Each package folder is zipped as <package>_1_0_0_1_managed.zip in %TEMP%\xpp-vscode-deploy\<timestamp> (deleted afterwards), with .NET's ZipFile as Visual Studio does:

  • every file under the package folder goes in as <package>/<relative path>;
  • left out: the BuildLogs folder, *.delete files and the build result logs (buildprojectresult.*, buildmodelresult.*);
  • a fnomoduledefinition.json at the root identifies the package for the environment's apply step, in the same shape pac and Visual Studio write:
{
  "Module": { "Name": "ContosoExtensions", "properties": [{ "Item1": "packagingSource", "Item2": "Pipeline" }] },
  "BuildType": "Full",
  "PackageType": "Dev",
  "TimestampUtc": "<timestamp>",
  "CorrelationID": "<new GUID>",
  "ClientID": "<this machine's name>",
  "OrganizationID": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "DBSync": { "SyncKind": "Module", "Arguments": "" },
  "Versions": { "Platform": "0.0.0.0", "Application": "0.0.0.0", "Compiler": "0.0.0.0", "PackageVersion": "<from the current time>" },
  "AdditionalData": {}
}

docs.title: 4. Upload through Dataverse
docs.text:
For each package:

  1. POST msprov_fnopackages creates a package record: msprov_name (the zip name), msprov_buildtype 0 (Full), msprov_packagetype 0 (Dev), msprov_dbsyncoptions (None 0, Full 1, Module 2) and msprov_dbsyncvalue ({"Modules":["ContosoExtensions", ...]} for a Module sync, empty otherwise).
  2. PATCH msprov_fnopackages(<id>)/msprov_packagepayload uploads the zip. Files up to 100 MB go in one request; larger files use Dataverse's chunked upload in blocks of the size Dataverse returns.

docs.title: 5. Start and wait
docs.text: POST msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync with all package records starts the deployment as a Dataverse system job. F&O Studio reads the job (asyncoperations(<id>)) every 15 seconds and writes each new status to the output. The job succeeds when it is completed with status Succeeded; any other end fails the deploy with the environment's message. It waits at most 4 hours.

docs.title: 6. Record the deploy
docs.text: After a successful deploy the models of the deployed packages (from their Descriptor files) are recorded as deployed for this environment, at the current time. See Status Bar for how this is compared with the last build.

docs.title: Why not pac package compile
docs.text: pac's own deploy path recompiles a scaffolded copy of your source with pac's SDK. Then the local build, and its portable PDBs, never reach the environment, and the debugger cannot match the code. F&O Studio uploads the built package folder instead, as Visual Studio does.

docs.title: Cloud-hosted and VHD environments
docs.text: There is nothing to deploy: the build writes into the local PackagesLocalDirectory and restarts the AOS hosts. The deploy commands are hidden there; if you start one anyway, the message is "This is a cloud-hosted or VHD environment: your models run on the local AOS once they are built, so there is nothing to deploy." To move code to a sandbox or production environment, create a deployable package (Create Deployment Package) and deploy it the way your project does.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• UDEs only.
  • Deploys packages as last built on this machine; it never builds. A package that was never built is not offered.
  • Deploys made from Visual Studio, another machine or a pipeline are not recorded, so the status bar may still show the build as not deployed.
  • Cancelling only stops waiting; the deployment continues on the environment.
  • Not tested yet according to the release notes: several packages in one deploy and packages larger than 100 MB.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Nothing to deploy: no package in ... has been built. Build your model first." No built package in the custom metadata folder. Build the model. "No environment selected." No environment in this window. Run Connect to Environment or Select Environment. "Not signed in to ." No Dataverse token. Sign in when VS Code asks; see Sign In and Authentication. "... has no Finance and Operations deployment support (solution msprov_fnouploadersolution)" The selected Dataverse org is not a UDE. Select the right environment. "Deploy stopped: building or copying the projects and assemblies the X++ project references failed." MSBuild or a copy failed. Read X++ Deploy; fix the C# project or set xpp.build.msbuildPath. "The deployment ended with status : " The environment failed to apply the package. Read the message; check the environment's deployment history. "Stopped waiting. The deployment keeps running on the environment (system job )." You cancelled. Wait for the environment; the deploy is not recorded, deploy again later if needed. "The deployment did not finish within 4 hours" Very long deployment or sync. Check the system job on the environment. POST ... returned 4xx/5xx: ... Dataverse refused a request (rights, limits). Read the error text; check your role on the environment.

docs.title: Drag and Drop
docs.text: F&O Studio supports the drag and drop moves Visual Studio developers use every day: drag elements from the Application Explorer into the project, onto a node of the element designer, onto a property, or into X++ code. Inside the designer you can drag nodes onto other nodes, for example a field onto a field group. Drops into the designer follow Visual Studio's drop rules (an EDT dropped on a table becomes a field of that type, a menu item dropped on a privilege becomes an entry point).

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Collect existing elements of your model into the project.
  • Build a table quickly: drop EDTs and enums on it to create fields, another table to create a relation.
  • Build a form: drop a table to add a data source, drop data source fields on the design to add bound controls, drop menu items to add buttons.
  • Fill a privilege, duty or role: drop menu items, services, data entities, tables, privileges or duties on it.
  • Insert an element name into X++ code without typing it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An environment with metadata (Connect to Environment).
  • Dropping on the project view needs an open project (D365FO Projects) and elements of the project's model.
  • Dropping into a designer needs an element of one of your models open in the Element Designer; standard elements are read-only. In an extension's designer you can also drop on some of the base element's nodes (see below).

docs.title: What you can drag, and where
docs.text:
Drag from Drop on Result Application Explorer, project view (one or several elements) D365FO Project view Elements are added to the project Application Explorer, project view X++ code view or .xpp editor The element names are inserted at the drop position, separated by commas Application Explorer, project view A node of the Element Designer tree (hold Shift) The node gets the child that refers to the element (Visual Studio's drop rules) Application Explorer, project view A text property row of the designer's property grid (hold Shift) The property is set to the element's name, if the property refers to that kind of element A node of the designer tree Another node of the same designer Adds a reference (field to field group, index, key, range; data source field to form design) or moves the node

Both trees support multi-select: select several elements with Ctrl+click or Shift+click and drag them together.

docs.title: Add elements to the project
docs.text:
1. Select one or more elements in the Application Explorer, for example your class ContosoOrderStatusService and your enum ContosoOrderStatus.
  2. Drag them onto the D365FO Project view and release.
  3. The status bar shows Added ContosoOrderStatusService, ContosoOrderStatus to the project. and the project view refreshes.

Elements that cannot be added (wrong model, no project) are listed in a warning with the reason, for example CustGroup: AxTable 'CustGroup' belongs to model 'ApplicationSuite', but the active project targets model 'ContosoExtensions'. …

docs.title: Insert names into code
docs.text:
Drag elements from either tree into an open X++ code view. The names are inserted where you drop, for example CustTable, CustGroup.

To insert an intrinsic such as tableStr(CustTable) instead, right-click the element and use Copy X++ Reference (Copy Name and Open in Browser).

docs.title: Drop elements into the designer
docs.text:
VS Code's webviews only accept drops while you hold Shift. The designer's tree tooltip says so: Drag nodes onto other nodes, or Application Explorer elements onto this tree (hold Shift to drop into the designer).

  1. Open an element of your model in the Element Designer, for example your table ContosoOrderLine.
  2. Drag an element from the Application Explorer over the designer, then hold Shift.
  3. A node that accepts the element is highlighted while the pointer is over it. Drop on it (the root or a folder such as Fields).
  4. The designer refreshes and the status bar shows the result, for example Added ItemId to Fields.

If you prefer not to drag, right-click the node and choose Add from Application Explorer…: it asks for an element (at least 3 characters of the name), offers only the element types that node accepts, and applies the same rule.

docs.title: Drop rules for elements
docs.text:
These are the rules applied when an Application Explorer element is dropped on a designer node:

Target node Dropped element Creates Table, table extension Extended data type A field of that EDT (Fields) Table, table extension Base enum An enum field of that type (Fields) Table, table extension Table A relation to that table (Relations) Table Table A delete action (DeleteActions) Map Table A mapping (Mappings) Form, form extension Table, view, data entity, map, aggregate data entity A data source Form Query Data sources from the query Form design, group, tab page, button group Display, action or output menu item A menu item button Query, query data source Table, view, data entity, aggregate data entity A root or embedded data source Menu, submenu Menu item A menu item element Menu, submenu Menu A menu reference Menu, submenu Tile A tile element Security privilege Menu item An entry point (with the default grant) Security privilege Service Entry points for the service's operations Security privilege Data entity A data entity permission Security privilege, role, role extension Table A direct access permission Security privilege Form Form control overrides Duty, duty extension, role, role extension Privilege A privilege reference Role, role extension Duty A duty reference Role Role A sub-role Service Class Sets the service's Class Service group Service A service reference Configuration key group Configuration key A configuration key reference Composite data entity Data entity A root data entity Composite entity root or embedded entity Data entity An embedded data entity Report Query or class A data set Menu item Form, class, report or query Sets the menu item's object Tile KPI Sets KPI Tile Menu item Sets the menu item name and type Workflow type Workflow approval, task or automated task A supported element Aggregate measurement Table, view, data entity, aggregate data entity A measure group

A drop that matches no rule fails with a message such as Edt CustGroupId can't be dropped on Indexes.

Extensions. In a form or menu extension's designer, the base element's nodes are shown too. Dropping a menu item on a base form container adds a control to the extension, placed at the end of that container. Dropping a menu item, menu or tile on a base submenu adds an element to the menu extension. Other drops on base nodes fail with … can't be dropped here. Drop it on the extension's own nodes.

docs.title: Drop elements on a property
docs.text:
Drag an element onto a text property row in the property grid (holding Shift). F&O Studio sets the property when it refers to that kind of element, for example:

  • a menu item's Object to a form (the object type follows);
  • a menu item button's MenuItemName to a menu item (the menu item type follows);
  • a privilege entry point's ObjectName to a menu item (the object type follows).

Otherwise you get doesn't refer to a . The property is set on the node selected in the tree.

docs.title: Drag nodes inside the designer
docs.text:
Nodes of your own element (items and methods) can be dragged onto other nodes of the same element, without Shift:

Drag Onto Result A table field A field group, index, full-text index Adds the field to it A data entity field An entity key, or the entity's Ranges Adds a key field or a range A query data source field Its own data source (Ranges, Order By, Group By, Having) Adds a range, order by, group by or having field A query data source field The Fields of a data entity or view Adds a field mapped to it A form data source field The form design, a group, grid, tab page or table control Adds a control bound to the field A node Another node in the same folder Moves it before that node

See Element Designer for the other editing commands (Move Up, Move Down, Duplicate…).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Drag and drop has no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The trees' drag and drop controller is ElementDragAndDrop in src/dragAndDrop.ts. A drag from the Application Explorer or the project view carries the elements twice: as JSON in the MIME type application/vnd.xpp.elements, and as xpp-element:/<AxType>/<Name> URIs in text/uri-list.
  • The project view accepts application/vnd.xpp.elements and calls the bridge action add_to_project once per element.
  • X++ editors use a document drop edit provider (ElementDropIntoCode) that inserts the element names.
  • The designer is a webview: it receives the text/uri-list of the operating system drag. When a drop arrives without data, the designer uses the last drag from the trees, if it started less than a minute ago.
  • The designer (media/element.js, src/elementDesigner.ts) sends drop_on_node (element dropped on a node, or a node dragged inside the designer) and drop_on_property. The server applies the rules in MetaModelBridge.Drops.cs, modelled on Visual Studio's merge rules, and saves the element through the metadata API. Each node reports which element types it accepts, which drives the highlighting and Add from Application Explorer….
  • Both write actions are checked by the server's write policy: only elements of your own models change (Security Model).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Dropping into the designer and its property grid needs Shift, because VS Code only passes drops to webviews that way.
  • The project view only accepts elements dragged from the F&O Studio trees, not files from the VS Code Explorer.
  • Designer drops cover the rules listed above. Other Visual Studio drops are not implemented; use New… in the designer instead.
  • Dragging in the Report Designer (report data onto the page) is a separate feature.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Nothing happens when dropping on the designer Shift was not held Hold Shift while you drop No node is highlighted under the pointer The element is read-only, or no node accepts that element type Open an element of your model; check the rules above … can't be dropped on … No drop rule for that pair Drop on another node, or use New… … can't be dropped here. Drop it on the extension's own nodes. Drop on a base node of an extension that only accepts controls or menu elements Drop on the extension's own nodes Warning after dropping on the project view An element is in another model, or no project is open Open the right project; extend standard elements instead

docs.title: Element Designer
docs.text: The element designer shows any D365FO element as a node tree with a Properties grid next to it, like the designer and Properties window of Visual Studio. You use it to read standard elements and to change the elements of your own models: add nodes, write and override methods, rename, duplicate, reorder, delete, drag elements in from the Application Explorer and set properties. Every change goes through Microsoft's metadata API and is saved at once.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see how a standard element is built: its fields, field groups, indexes, relations, data sources, controls, methods and properties.
  • You want to change a table, form, EDT, enum, menu item, query, security object or any other element of your own model without opening Visual Studio.
  • You work on an extension (table extension, form extension and so on) and want to see the base element's nodes next to what your extension adds.
  • You want to add a method, override a kernel or base class method, or copy an event handler for one of the element's events (see Event Handlers).

For forms the designer also draws a preview of the form as the web client shows it; see Form Designer and Preview. For the Properties grid and its pickers in detail, see Properties Grid and Pickers. Classes open in the X++ Code View instead; label files open in the Label Editor.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (see Connect to Environment). This works on UDE, cloud-hosted and VHD environments, because the designer only reads and writes local metadata.
  • To change an element, it must belong to one of your own (custom) models. Standard elements open read-only. To change a standard element, create an extension (see Create Extension).
  • A D365FO project is not needed to open a designer. It is needed for commands that add elements to the project, such as Add to Project.

docs.title: Opening the designer
docs.text:
Place How Application Explorer or project view Click an element (any type except classes and label files). Or right-click > Open Designer. Application Explorer or project view Right-click > Open to the Side opens the designer in the editor group beside the current one (classes open their code there). X++ code view Right-click in the editor > Open Designer (for tables, forms, views, entities, queries and maps). Security view Right-click a role, duty, privilege or access entry > Open Designer. Diagrams, references, ERD, Copilot Activity Click an element link.

Each element has one designer tab, titled <Name> [<Type>], for example CustGroup [Table]. Opening the same element again brings its tab to the front. Designer tabs come back after a window reload.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Toolbar: the element name with its element type in brackets, and a badge. The badge shows the model name for your own elements, or <model> · read-only (standard · read-only when the model is unknown) for everything else.
  • Node tree (left): the element node (with its model in brackets), then its folders and items in Visual Studio's node order and with similar icons. Folders below the first level start collapsed, like Visual Studio. Form controls show their control type after the name, for example ActionPane (Action Pane). Hovering a folder shows how many items it has. An Events folder appears after Methods on tables, data entities, forms, form data sources, data source fields and form controls.
  • Properties (right): the properties of the selected node. Selecting a folder shows its item count, selecting a method or an event shows a short hint.
  • Preview (forms only): a drawing of the form; see Form Designer and Preview.

Very large elements are cut off after 20,000 nodes. The tree then ends with "This element is very large; some nodes are not shown."

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text:
Key Action Up / Down arrow Select the previous or next visible node Right / Left arrow Expand or collapse the selected node Enter Open the selected method in the code editor; open a report's precision design in the Report Designer F12 Open the first element the node refers to (for example the EDT of a field) Ctrl+Z Undo the last property change Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo Ctrl+F Focus the property filter Alt+Down (in a property value) Open the property's picker

Double-click opens a method in the code editor, copies the handler of an event (see Event Handlers), opens a precision design, or expands and collapses a folder.

docs.title: Editor title buttons
docs.text:
The buttons in the editor title act on the active designer tab:

Button Shown when What it does Create Extension The element is not in your model and its type can be extended (table, form, enum, EDT, data entity, security duty, security role) Runs Create Extension for the element View Code The element type has X++ code (table, form, view, data entity, query, map) Opens the X++ Code View Form Layout The element is a form or form extension Opens the form layout view of the base form (see Form Layout and Form Extensions) Refresh Designer Always Reloads the tree from the metadata

docs.title: Right-click menu on nodes
docs.text:
What the menu offers depends on the node and on whether you can change the element. All editing commands only appear on elements of your own models.

Command Where What it does New… A folder, or a node with folders Adds a node. When the folder accepts several types (for example the Fields folder of a table: String, Integer, Enum, ...), you pick the type first. Then you enter a name; the default is the type name plus 1. New Method… A Methods folder, or a node that has one Asks for a name (default method1), adds private void <name>() with an empty body and opens it in the code editor Override Method… Same Lists the methods you can still override (base class methods for classes; kernel methods for tables, views, data entities, maps, forms, form data sources, data source fields, buttons and other controls) with their signatures. The picked one is added with its super() call and opened in the code editor. "There are no more methods to override here." when all are already there. Add from Application Explorer… A node that accepts dropped elements Picks an element of the accepted types and adds it as if you dropped it (see Drag and drop below) View Code A method Opens the method in the code editor Copy Event Handler Method An event or a method See Event Handlers Find Event Handlers Events folder, an event, a method, the element See Event Handlers Rename… An item inside a folder (not a method) Renames the item and updates what refers to it inside the same element Duplicate… An item inside a folder (not a method) Copies the item under a new name (default <name>Copy) right after the original Move Up / Move Down An item or method inside a folder Moves it one place. The order is what forms, field groups and enums show. Delete An item or method inside a folder Asks for confirmation, then removes it Go to Referenced Element… A node that refers to other elements Opens the referenced element; with several references you pick one Find References A field or method of a table, class, form and other cross-referenced types Runs Find All References for that member (for extension members, under the base element) Copy Name Any item Copies the node name Copy X++ Reference The element, a field, index, enum value, form data source, data source field or control Copies the X++ that names it, for example tableStr(CustGroup), fieldStr(CustGroup, CustGroup), indexStr(CustGroup, <index>), formControlStr(CustGroup, <control>), NoYes::Yes

The element node (the root) has the same element actions as the Application Explorer: View Code, Open Form Layout…, Locate in Application Explorer, Add to Project, Duplicate…, Create Extension, Create Code Extension, Find References, View References, View Dependencies, View Hierarchy, View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), Compare Code…, Compare Metadata…, View History, Open Table Browser, Open in Browser, Find Similar Standard Implementations, Show Extensions and Handlers…, and the security and test commands that fit the element type. Delete on the element node removes one of your own elements from its model.

docs.title: Editing nodes in detail
docs.text:
Rename. Names must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits and underscores. Inside the same element, F&O Studio updates the properties that name the item:

  • a field: field group fields, index fields, key fields, relation constraints, map field mappings, and the table's TitleField1, TitleField2 and CountryRegionContextField;
  • an index: the table's PrimaryIndex, ClusteredIndex and ReplacementKey;
  • a relation: delete actions that use it;
  • a form, query or entity data source: DataSource, JoinSource, TitleDataSource and the other data source properties of the element;
  • a control of a form extension: Parent and PreviousSibling of the extension's controls.

X++ code is not changed by this rename. Before renaming a field, F&O Studio asks the cross-reference database how many references the field has and warns you: "They are not renamed." Exception: renaming a field of a table of your model (not a table extension) runs the full refactoring. It shows the code changes in the refactor preview and also updates the metadata of your other elements that use the field. See Rename and Refactoring.

Methods are renamed in their code, not with Rename… ("Rename a method by changing its name in the code.").

Duplicate. The copy is a deep copy of the node. Form control names are unique in the whole form, so when you duplicate a container its controls get new names too (a number is added).

Move. In an extension's designer you only move the extension's own items; the base element's items keep their place ("... is already first of this extension's items").

docs.title: Drag and drop
docs.text:
You can change your elements by dragging:

  • Inside the tree: drag an item or method onto another node. For example, drag a field onto a field group to add it there, or a data source field onto the form design to create a bound control, or move items.
  • From the Application Explorer or the project view: drag elements onto a node that accepts them. VS Code needs you to hold Shift while dropping into a webview. Use Add from Application Explorer… when you prefer a picker.
  • Onto a property row: drop an element on a string property to set it (for example a menu item on MenuItemName).

F&O Studio follows Visual Studio's drop rules. Examples:

Target Dropped element Result Table or table extension EDT A field of that type in Fields Table or table extension Enum An enum field Table or table extension Table A relation to that table Table Table A delete action Form or form extension Table, view, data entity, map A data source Form Query Data sources from the query Form design, group, tab page, button group Menu item A menu item button Menu or submenu Menu item, menu, tile A menu entry Security privilege Menu item, service, data entity, table, form An entry point, data entity permission, direct access permission or form control override Duty or role Privilege, duty, role A privilege, duty or sub-role reference Service Class Sets the service class Service group Service Adds the service Configuration key group Configuration key Adds the key Report Query or class A dataset Menu item Form, class, report, query Sets the menu item's object Workflow type Workflow approval, task or automated task A supported element

On the base nodes of an extension (see below), dropped elements become extension items.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
An extension's designer (for example CustTable.ContosoExtensions) shows the base element's nodes and the extension's own nodes merged into the same folders, as Visual Studio does:

  • The extension's own nodes are shown in bold.
  • Base element nodes are read-only. Their properties are read from the base element. Folders that only extensions have (field modifications, property modifications and so on) are at the end.
  • Go to Referenced Element… on the root offers the base object.

docs.title: Undo and redo
docs.text: Property changes are saved immediately. Ctrl+Z sets the previous value again (and saves it), Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z sets it back. The status bar shows "Undid " or "Nothing to undo". Undo works while the focus is not in a text box or drop-down. It only covers property changes made in this designer tab since it was opened; node operations (New, Rename, Duplicate, Move, Delete, drops, methods) are not undone. Use source control (see Source Control for X++) or Element History to go back further.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The element designer has no settings of its own. Find Event Handlers depends on xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex (see Event Handlers).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The panel is src/elementDesigner.ts with the webview media/element.js. Forms add media/formPreview.js.
  • The tree comes from the metadata server's bridge action get_element_tree, implemented in MetaModelBridge.ElementDesigner.cs. It is generated by reflection over Microsoft's metadata classes: members marked [AxCollectionProperty] become child nodes, members marked [AxProperty] are what the Properties window shows. A table of Visual Studio's node order per element type orders the folders; some collections are hidden or inlined as in Visual Studio. The element read is cached for 30 seconds.
  • For extensions, the server merges the base element's tree into the extension's tree and marks nodes as inherited or own.
  • The extension adds the Events folders (from src/events.ts) and, per node, the X++ reference and the cross-reference member used by Copy X++ Reference and Find References.
  • Properties: get_element_properties and set_element_property. Node edits: get_node_types, add_element_node, delete_element_node, rename_element_node, duplicate_element_node, move_element_node (MetaModelBridge.DesignerActions.cs, MetaModelBridge.NodeEdits.cs). Methods: set_element_method, get_overrides. Drops: drop_on_node, drop_on_property (MetaModelBridge.Drops.cs).
  • Every write reads the element fresh through the metadata provider, refuses elements outside your custom models, changes the object and saves it with the provider's Update method for the element's model. The server then reloads the metadata and clears its caches. All write actions are registered with write kind Edit, so the central write policy applies to them (see Security Model).
  • After a change the designer reloads its tree, keeps the selection, and tells open code views of the element to reload.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Classes open in the code view, not in a designer. Label files open in the label editor; its Properties button opens the label file's designer.
  • Undo and redo cover property changes only, and only in the current designer tab.
  • Rename and Duplicate are not available for methods.
  • Renaming an item updates only the same element (except table fields of your tables, see above).
  • Elements in standard models cannot be changed, not even temporarily. Create an extension.
  • Report designs are edited in the Report Designer (see Report Element Designer and Report Designer).

docs.title: Element History
docs.text: View History lists the Git commits that changed an element's metadata file and opens each change in VS Code's diff editor. For elements with code it shows the X++ code of each version laid out like the code view, so you compare code, not XML. It is the VS Code counterpart of Visual Studio's View History on an element under source control.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Find out when and why a method of your class changed, and who changed it.
  • Compare an element as it is now with how it was in a commit (before a regression).
  • Review your uncommitted changes to one element before you commit.
  • See metadata changes (properties, fields, controls) of an element without code, such as a table extension or a menu item.

For all changed elements of your models at once, use Show Changed Elements or Review My Changes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The element's model folder must be in a Git repository. Model folders are often junctions (or symbolic links) into the repository; F&O Studio follows them to the real path.
  • Git must be installed. F&O Studio uses the Git that VS Code uses (the git.path setting), or git on PATH.
  • View History is offered on elements of your own models. Standard elements are not under your source control.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Application Explorer Right-click an element of your model > View History D365FO Project view Right-click an element > View History Element Designer Right-click the root node of an element of your model > View History X++ code view Right-click in the editor > View History Command Palette F&O Studio: View History, then type at least 3 characters of the element name and pick it

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click the element, for example your class ContosoOrderStatusService, and choose View History.
  2. A picker titled History of ContosoOrderStatusService (Class) opens. It lists:
  3. Uncommitted changes (working tree) at the top, when the file has changes that are not committed;
  4. every commit that changed the file, newest first (up to 500): the commit subject, then the author and date, then the first 8 characters of the commit hash.
  5. Type to filter by subject, author, date or hash.
  6. Pick a commit to see what that commit changed: a diff between the parent commit and the commit, titled ContosoOrderStatusService (1a2b3c4d: Add status check).
  7. Pick Uncommitted changes to see a diff between HEAD and the file on disk, titled ContosoOrderStatusService (HEAD ↔ working tree).

docs.title: Buttons on each commit
docs.text: Button Shown for What it shows Compare with the current version Every commit The commit's version against the current file on disk: <name> (<hash> ↔ current) Show the metadata (XML) changes Elements with code, on commits and on Uncommitted changes The same change as XML instead of X++ code

docs.title: Code or XML
docs.text:
• Elements with code (classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, queries, maps) open as X++ code. Pick the commit for the code change, or use Show the metadata (XML) changes for the XML.
  • Other elements (EDTs, enums, extensions without code, menu items, security objects...) always open as XML.

docs.title: How a code version is laid out
docs.text:
Each version's code is rebuilt from that version's metadata file:

  1. The class declaration and the element's own methods, laid out like the X++ Code View (declaration, methods inside the class body, closing brace).
  2. Then the methods of nested nodes (form data sources, their fields, controls), grouped under a comment with the names of the nodes that contain them, for example a form data source ContosoOrderTable:
public class ContosoOrderForm extends FormRun
{
    public void init()
    {
        super();
    }

}
// ContosoOrderTable
    public void initValue()
    {
        super();
    }

Both sides of every diff are rebuilt the same way, including the current version, so only real changes show up.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect git.path (VS Code's Git setting) empty The Git executable View History runs; empty uses git on PATH

View History has no settings of its own.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• src/history.ts registers the command and a read-only document provider for the scheme xpphistory.
  • Finding the file. F&O Studio looks for <model folder>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml in your models first, then in the others. It resolves the real path (realpath) because model folders are often junctions into the repository, then asks Git for the repository root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel).
  • Commits. git log -n 500 --format=<hash, parents, author, date, subject> -- <file> lists the commits; git status --porcelain -- <file> tells whether there are uncommitted changes.
  • Versions. Each side of a diff is a URI xpphistory:/<ref>/<path in repository>?<repository root>#<code|xml>. <ref> is a commit hash, HEAD, working (the file on disk) or empty (before the first commit). Only these forms are accepted, and paths containing .. are refused. A commit version is read with git show <ref>:<path>.
  • Code view. For #code, the XML's <SourceCode> section is parsed: the <Declaration>, each <Method> with its <Name> and <Source>, grouped by the names of the nodes that contain them.
  • Everything runs locally with Git; the metadata server is not involved.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Git only. Elements under Team Foundation Version Control (TFVC) have no history in F&O Studio.
  • The last 500 commits of the file are listed.
  • History follows the file path; a renamed element's commits from before the rename are not listed under its new name.
  • The diffs are read-only. To restore an old version, use Git (for example the VS Code Source Control view or git checkout <commit> -- <file>), then refresh the designer.
  • The code view of a version shows declarations and methods only. Property changes appear in the XML view.
  • Standard elements have no View History in the tree menus.

docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix  has no Git history yet. The file has never been committed and has no changes Commit it first  is not under Git source control (). The model folder (or its junction target) is not in a Git repository Put the model in a repository; see Source Control for X++ No metadata file found for . The element is not in any model folder of the active configuration Check the environment (Select Environment) An empty side in the diff That version did not exist (first commit), or Git could not read it Expected for an added element View History is not in the menu The element is in a standard model Use it on elements of your models

docs.title: Entity Relationship Diagram
docs.text: View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) draws a table and its related tables as boxes with their key fields, connected by the table relations with their cardinality. You choose how many levels of related tables to follow, whether to follow the table's own relations, the relations of other tables to it, or both, and whether to show key fields or all fields. You can export the diagram as SVG or as a Mermaid ER diagram. Visual Studio has no ERD for F&O tables.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Understand the data model around a table before you write a query, a data entity or an integration, for example what CustTable refers to.
  • Find which tables refer to a table (incoming relations), for example everything that points at CustGroup.
  • Document a feature's data model: export the diagram to SVG for a design document or to Mermaid for a Markdown page or wiki.
  • Check the relations of your own new tables.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). The diagram is built from local metadata; it does not need the cross-reference database or the environment.
  • The first diagram with incoming relations scans all table and table extension files once (see How it works); later diagrams use the cached index.

docs.title: Opening the diagram
docs.text:
Place How Application Explorer or project view Right-click a table > View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) Element designer of a table Right-click the table node > View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) Command Palette F&O Studio: View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), then pick a table

The diagram opens in a tab titled ERD: <table>. Running the command again for the same table brings that tab to the front.

docs.title: Reading the diagram
docs.text:
• Tables are laid out in columns by level: the starting table in the middle, tables it refers to (outgoing) to the right, tables that refer to it (incoming) to the left. Each column is sorted by name and centred vertically.
  • The starting table has a highlighted header. Tables of your own models have a green border.
  • Each box lists fields with their type (EDT, enum or base type) on the right. Primary key fields are bold with a key symbol. The primary key is the fields of the table's primary index; a table without one (or with the surrogate key) shows RecId.
  • Each curve is a relation, drawn from the field it uses in one table to the related field in the other, with an arrow at the related table. The small labels at both ends show the cardinality (0..*, 1..*, 0..1, 1). Hover a curve to see the relation name and its field pairs, for example CustTable.CustGroup → CustGroup / CustGroup = CustGroup.CustGroup.
  • Hover a box to see the table name and its model.
  • The status line shows the number of tables and relations.

docs.title: Working with the diagram
docs.text:
• Click a table to open it in the Element Designer.
  • Double-click a table to make it the starting table: the diagram is rebuilt around it and the tab title changes.
  • Change the toolbar options; the diagram is rebuilt at once:
Option Values Levels 1 to 5 levels of related tables from the starting table Relations Outgoing (tables it refers to), Incoming (tables referring to it), Both Fields Keys and relation fields (primary key plus the fields the drawn relations use), All fields
  • Export SVG… saves the diagram as a standalone SVG (the current theme's colours are written into the file, on the editor background).
  • Export Mermaid… saves a Mermaid erDiagram as .mmd, or as .md wrapped in a ```mermaid block.
  • Copy Mermaid copies the Mermaid text to the clipboard.

docs.title: Mermaid output
docs.text:
The Mermaid text has one line per drawn relation and one block per table with the shown fields, marked PK and FK. A shortened example:

erDiagram
    CustTable }o--|| CustGroup : "CustGroup"
    CustTable {
        CustAccount AccountNum PK
        CustGroupId CustGroup FK
    }
    CustGroup {
        CustGroupId CustGroup PK
    }

The type of a field is its EDT, else its enum, else its base type (str, ...). The relation's cardinality and related table cardinality map to Mermaid's crow's foot symbols.

docs.title: Size limit
docs.text: A diagram shows at most 60 tables. When the levels and direction would reach more, the status line says "limited to 60 tables, lower the levels". Lower the levels, or switch from Both to one direction.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
The settings set the toolbar defaults for new diagrams:

Setting Default Effect xpp.erd.depth 1 Levels of related tables to follow (1 to 5) xpp.erd.direction outgoing outgoing: tables the table refers to (its relations); incoming: tables that refer to the table; both xpp.erd.fields keys keys: primary key and the fields of the drawn relations; all: all fields

Changes in the toolbar apply to the open diagram only.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The panel is src/erd.ts. It collects the tables level by level, then draws them in the webview as SVG.
  • Bridge action table_erd (TableRelationsService.cs) returns, for up to 40 tables per request: label, model, whether the model is yours, table group, primary index and key fields, all fields (including fields of table extensions) with their type, and all relations (including relations added by table extensions) with related table, cardinalities, relationship type and constraints.
  • Outgoing follows the relations of each table. Incoming asks bridge action incoming_relations for the tables whose relations name the table. That action uses an index built by scanning every AxTable and AxTableExtension XML file of the reference and custom metadata folders for <RelatedTable> inside <Relations>. The index is kept in memory and in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\cache\relations-<hash>.json, and is rebuilt when the folders change.
  • Only relations of tables whose relations were followed (outgoing) or into tables whose incoming relations were followed are drawn, so the diagram shows the paths it explored.
  • Table details are cached for the lifetime of the tab, so changing options or re-centring is fast.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Tables only. Views, data entities and maps are not drawn.
  • At most 60 tables and 5 levels.
  • Relations are drawn from the relation constraints with fields; fixed-value constraints are not shown on the curve.
  • The layout is by level, not optimized to avoid crossing lines.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Table '' not found." The table is not in the metadata of the active environment Check the name and the environment (Select Environment) The first diagram with Incoming or Both takes a while The relation index is being built from all table files Wait; later diagrams use the cache "limited to 60 tables, lower the levels" The diagram reached the limit Lower Levels or use one direction A new relation of your table is missing in Incoming of the other table The cached index is from before the change It is rebuilt when the table folders change; reopen the diagram

docs.title: Environments and Promotion
docs.text: A D365FO change passes through several environments: the developer's own development environment, then usually a build environment or pipeline, a sandbox (test, UAT), and finally production. Promotion between them is done with deployable packages through Lifecycle Services (LCS) or, for unified environments, the Power Platform admin center. F&O Studio works with development environments only: it builds, deploys and synchronizes on the environment you develop against, and helps you check a change before it leaves your machine. This page describes the environment types, what F&O Studio does in each, and where its job ends.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You plan the environments of a project and want to know which ones F&O Studio is used with.
  • You want to know how a change moves from your UDE to a sandbox.
  • You wonder why there is no "deploy to sandbox" command.

docs.title: Environment types and F&O Studio
docs.text:
Environment What it is F&O Studio Unified developer environment (UDE) A Power Platform hosted environment with Finance and Operations, one per developer. Code is built on the developer's machine and deployed to the environment. Full support: build locally, Deploy Models to Environment, Synchronize Database, Run Tests, debugger, database access. Cloud-hosted environment (CHE) An LCS-deployed VM in your Azure subscription with the AOS, database and Visual Studio on the same machine. Supported on the VM: build, local database sync (Synchronize Database runs SyncEngine; Synchronize Table(s) with the Database syncs only chosen tables), debugger (preview). Nothing to deploy: the local AOS runs what was built. VHD (local VM) The downloadable development VM. Same as cloud-hosted. Build environment / pipeline Builds the deployable package from the repository. Not used; see Build Automation and Pipelines. Sandbox (tier 2+) Test and UAT, Microsoft-managed. Not deployed to by F&O Studio. Functional agents can look at it through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server when you connect it; their rules allow changes only with your permission and never in production. Production Microsoft-managed. Never deployed to by F&O Studio.

See Connect to Environment, Select Environment and Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments for setting up development environments.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A development environment configured on the machine (UDE connected, or a cloud-hosted / VHD environment).
  • For deploying to a UDE: signed in with the Microsoft account that has access to the environment's Dataverse organization (see Sign-In and Authentication).

docs.title: Promotion path (general practice)
docs.text:
Developer machine ──build──> UDE (Deploy Models to Environment)            F&O Studio
        │
        └─commit/push──> Repository ──pipeline──> Deployable package        Azure Pipelines (general practice)
                                                     │
                                                     ├──> Sandbox (test, UAT)   LCS or Power Platform admin center
                                                     └──> Production            LCS or Power Platform admin center
  1. Develop and test on your own environment. Build with F&O Studio; on a UDE deploy with Deploy Models to Environment and test there. Run Pre-Deploy Checklist for build, best practice, performance, security and scratch code checks in one report.
  2. Commit and merge. The pull request build proves the change compiles from the repository alone.
  3. Build the release package. The pipeline builds main (or a release branch) and creates the deployable package. Microsoft's Create Deployable Package task can create the classic LCS package and the Power Platform unified package.
  4. Deploy to sandbox. Upload the package to the LCS Asset library and apply it to the sandbox, or, for environments managed in the Power Platform admin center, deploy the unified package there (for example with pac package deploy or the Power Platform Build Tools in a release pipeline).
  5. Test and sign off in the sandbox.
  6. Deploy to production with the same package, through the same channel, by your change process.

Steps 3 to 6 are not done by F&O Studio. The F&O Release Manager agent follows the same rule: it deploys and synchronizes only to development, sandbox or build environments with the user's permission, and says that production goes through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center by the customer's process.

docs.title: Deploying to your UDE
docs.text:
Deploy Models to Environment (command palette; in the Dynamics 365 view: Deploy > Deploy Models to Online Environment…) uploads your packages as built on this machine. It is hidden on cloud-hosted and VHD environments.

  1. Pick the packages. Every package in the custom metadata folder that has been built (bin\Dynamics.AX.<Package>.dll exists) is listed, including packages linked in with a junction; the open project's package is preselected.
  2. Pick the database sync: None, Module (the tables of the deployed packages) or Full (slow).
  3. Progress shows in a notification and in the X++ Deploy output.

Before the upload, F&O Studio builds and copies the C# projects and assemblies the X++ project references into the package, and converts the package's PDBs to portable PDBs for the UDE debugger. Nothing is recompiled: the environment runs the exact build you debug. Details: Deploy to Environment and Synchronize Database.

docs.title: How the deploy works
docs.text:
core/src/deploy.ts, the way Visual Studio and pac deploy:

  1. Check that the Dataverse organization has the Finance and Operations deployment solution (msprov_fnouploadersolution); otherwise it is not a UDE.
  2. For each package: zip the package folder as <Package>/... plus fnomoduledefinition.json into <Package>_1_0_0_1_managed.zip (skipping BuildLogs, build result logs and .delete files).
  3. Create an msprov_fnopackages row (build type Full, package type Dev, the sync option and, for a module sync, {"Modules":[...]}), and upload the zip to its msprov_packagepayload column (in blocks above 100 MB).
  4. Call msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync and poll the system job (asyncoperations) every 15 seconds until it ends, for at most 4 hours. Cancelling stops waiting; the deployment keeps running on the environment.

docs.title: Built versus deployed
docs.text:
On a UDE the environment runs the code last deployed to it, not what you built. F&O Studio records, per environment and model, when the model was last built and last deployed from this machine:

  • The project's status bar item shows a cloud-upload icon when the build is newer than the deploy; its tooltip has the times and a Deploy now link.
  • Run Tests, the debugger and Verify in the Running App warn first: "ContosoExtensions was built (...) after its last deploy (...)." with Deploy First and Continue.
  • Deploys from other machines or pipelines are not known.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild for the C# projects copied into the package before a deploy. xpp.build.restartLocalAos true Cloud-hosted / VHD: restart running AOS hosts after a build, so the environment runs the new build.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No deployment to sandbox or production, no LCS or Power Platform admin center integration, no package upload to the LCS Asset library.
  • Deploy is for unified developer environments only.
  • The deployed state only knows deploys run from this machine.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Nothing to deploy: no package in (folder) has been built. Build your model first." No package in the custom metadata folder has its Dynamics.AX.<Package>.dll. Build the model. "(URL) has no Finance and Operations deployment support (solution msprov_fnouploadersolution). Is it a unified developer environment?" The selected Dataverse organization is not a UDE. Select the right environment (see Select Environment). "This is a cloud-hosted or VHD environment: your models run on the local AOS once they are built, so there is nothing to deploy." Deploy on a local environment. Expected; build instead. "Stopped waiting. The deployment keeps running on the environment (system job ...)." You cancelled the progress. Wait, then check the environment. "The deployment ended with status ...: ..." The environment's apply step failed. Read the message; fix and deploy again.
