docs.title: Event Handlers
docs.text: In the Element Designer, tables, data entities, forms and their parts have an Events folder, as in Visual Studio. From an event, or from one of the element's own methods, you copy a ready-to-paste event handler method (Visual Studio's Copy event handler method) and you list the handlers that already exist (Find Event Handlers). This is how you hook into standard code without changing it: data events, form events, form data source and control events, pre- and post-event handlers on methods, and delegate subscribers.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need to react when a standard record is inserted, validated or deleted (onInserted, onValidatedWrite, ...), when a form is initialized, when a data source is written, when a field is modified or when a button is clicked.
  • You need a pre- or post-event handler on a method, or a subscriber to a delegate.
  • You want to know who already handles an event before you add your own handler, for example to find why a standard behaviour changed.

Chain of Command is often the better choice for methods; see Create Code Extension and Implementations and Chain of Command.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Open the element in the Element Designer. Events are available on standard elements too: you copy the handler, then paste it into a class of your own model.
  • Find Event Handlers uses F&O Studio's extension index. Form and data event handlers ([FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler] and similar attributes) are found only when xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex is on (default). The first scan of all packages takes about a minute and is cached.
  • Have a class to paste the handler into, for example a new class ContosoCustTableEventHandler (see New Element).

docs.title: Where the Events folders are
docs.text:
The designer adds an Events folder right after Methods:

Node Events Table (and table extension) onDeleted, onDeleting, onInitializedRecord, onInitializingRecord, onInserted, onInserting, onModifiedField, onModifiedFieldValue, onModifyingField, onModifyingFieldValue, onUpdated, onUpdating, onValidatedDelete, onValidatedField, onValidatedFieldValue, onValidatedWrite, onValidatingDelete, onValidatingField, onValidatingFieldValue, onValidatingWrite, onDefaultingField, onDefaultedField, onDefaultingRow, onDefaultedRow Data entity (and extension) The table events plus onPersistingEntity, onPersistedEntity, onInitializingEntityDataSource, onInitializedEntityDataSource, onMappingEntityToDataSource, onMappedEntityToDataSource, onMappingDataSourceToEntity, onMappedDataSourceToEntity, onFindingEntityDataSource, onFoundEntityDataSource, onInsertingEntityDataSource, onInsertedEntityDataSource, onUpdatingEntityDataSource, onUpdatedEntityDataSource, onDeletingEntityDataSource, onDeletedEntityDataSource, onPostingLoad, onPostedLoad Form (not on a form extension's root) OnActivated, OnClosing, OnInitialized, OnInitializing, OnPostRun Form data source OnActivated, OnCreated, OnCreating, OnDeleted, OnDeleting, OnDisplayOptionInitialize, OnInitialized, OnInitValue, OnLeavingRecord, OnLeftRecord, OnMarkChanged, OnPostLinkActive, OnQueryExecuted, OnQueryExecuting, OnRefreshed, OnReread, OnSelectionChanged, OnValidatedDelete, OnValidatedWrite, OnValidatingDelete, OnValidatingWrite, OnWriting, OnWritten Form data source field OnJumpRef, OnModified, OnValidated, OnValidating Button controls OnClicked plus the focus events Tab page OnAllowPageDeactivate, OnPageActivated plus the focus events Tab OnTabChanged plus the focus events Tree OnExpanded, OnExpanding, OnSelectionChanged, OnSelectionChanging plus the focus events Grid, list OnSelectionChanged, OnSelectionChanging plus the focus events Input controls (string, integer, real, date, time, GUID, combo box, check box, radio button, segmented entry, reference group, enum) OnJumpRef, OnLookup, OnModified, OnValidated, OnValidating plus the focus events Other controls The focus events: OnEnter, OnGotFocus, OnLeaving, OnLostFocus

docs.title: Copying a handler for an event
docs.text:
1. Expand the Events folder of the node.
  2. Double-click an event, or right-click it > Copy Event Handler Method.
  3. The status bar says "Event handler for copied".
  4. Paste the method into your event handler class.

    5. For the onInserted event of table CustTable you get:

    /// <summary>
///
/// </summary>
/// <param name="sender"></param>
/// <param name="e"></param>
[DataEventHandler(tableStr(CustTable), DataEventType::Inserted)]
public static void CustTable_onInserted(Common sender, DataEventArgs e)
{

}

    The other kinds follow Visual Studio's templates:

    Event kind Attribute Method name Parameters Table / entity data event DataEventHandler(tableStr(T), DataEventType::E) T_onE Common sender, DataEventArgs e Form event FormEventHandler(formStr(F), FormEventType::E) F_OnE xFormRun sender, FormEventArgs e Form data source FormDataSourceEventHandler(formDataSourceStr(F, DS), FormDataSourceEventType::E) DS_OnE FormDataSource sender, FormDataSourceEventArgs e Form data source field FormDataFieldEventHandler(formDataFieldStr(F, DS, Fld), FormDataFieldEventType::E) Fld_OnE FormDataObject sender, FormDataFieldEventArgs e Form control FormControlEventHandler(formControlStr(F, C), FormControlEventType::E) C_OnE FormControl sender, FormControlEventArgs e

    On a form extension's designer the handler names the base form, as handlers always do.

docs.title: Pre- and post-event handlers and delegate subscribers
docs.text:
1. Right-click one of the element's own methods (directly under Methods of a class, table, view, data entity or form) > Copy Event Handler Method.
  2. If the method is a delegate, F&O Studio copies a subscriber with the delegate's parameters:
[SubscribesTo(classStr(ContosoOrderService), delegateStr(ContosoOrderService, orderPosted))]
public static void ContosoOrderService_orderPosted(SalesTable _salesTable)
{

}
  1. Otherwise pick Post-event handler or Pre-event handler. For SalesFormLetter.run (post) you get:
[PostHandlerFor(classStr(SalesFormLetter), methodStr(SalesFormLetter, run))]
public static void SalesFormLetter_Post_run(XppPrePostArgs args)
{

}

Static methods use staticMethodStr (classes) or tableStaticMethodStr (tables, views, entities); table methods use tableMethodStr; form methods formMethodStr. F&O Studio reads the method header in the code view to tell static methods and delegates apart. Every copied method starts with the same empty /// <summary> header and <param> lines as the data event example above (left out here).

Methods of nested nodes (data sources, controls) and of extensions are not offered: "Event handlers can be written for methods of classes, tables, views, data entities and forms (not for methods of nested nodes or extensions)."

docs.title: Finding existing handlers
docs.text:
Right-click > Find Event Handlers on:

Node Lists An event The handlers of that event An Events folder All handlers of that node's events; on the element and on a form data source also those of their child nodes A method Its pre/post handlers and delegate subscribers A data source, data source field or control All handlers of that node The element node All handlers of the element

A picker shows each handler as <Class>.<method> with the event, for example ContosoCustTableEventHandler.CustTable_onInserted Inserted. Pick one to open it in the code view. When nothing is found, the message says why: the index is still building, or form and data handlers are off in the settings.

To see all extensions of an element together (Chain of Command classes, table and form extensions and handlers), use Show Extensions and Handlers… on the element node; see Implementations and Chain of Command.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex true Includes form and data event handlers ([FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler], ...), which the cross-reference database does not record, in the extension index. The first scan takes about a minute and is cached. Also switchable in the Dynamics 365 view under Code Intelligence.

See Code Intelligence Settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• src/events.ts adds the Events folders to the designer tree after the server returns it. The event lists are the platform's event enums (DataEventType, FormEventType, FormDataSourceEventType, FormDataFieldEventType, FormControlEventType).
  • handlerText builds the method text from the event and copies it to the clipboard. Nothing is written to metadata.
  • For methods, src/elementDesigner.ts opens the element's code view, finds the method header and checks for static and delegate.
  • Find Event Handlers turns the node into a path in the extension index (for example /Tables/CustTable, /Forms/CustTable/DataSources/CustTable, /Classes/SalesFormLetter/Methods/run) and an event filter, and runs xpp.codeIntel.eventHandlers, which asks the code intelligence index (src/codeIntel/providers.ts). Pre/post handlers and delegate subscribers come from the index of extensions; form and data event handlers come from the scan enabled by xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The handler is copied to the clipboard; F&O Studio does not create the handler class for you. Snippets for event handlers exist too (see Snippets).
  • Pre/post handlers are offered only for methods directly under the element's Methods folder, not for methods of data sources or controls and not on extensions.
  • A form extension's root has no form events folder; open the base form for those.
  • Handlers in packages that are not in your metadata are not found.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No event handlers for ... The extension index is still building; try again in a moment." The index is being built Wait for the Code Intelligence status in the Dynamics 365 view "No event handlers for ... Form and data event handlers are found only when "Form and data event handlers" is on (Code intelligence)." xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex is off Turn it on (first scan about a minute) "Event handlers can be written for methods of classes, tables, views, data entities and forms ..." The method is on a nested node or an extension Use the Events folder of the node, or Chain of Command A handler you just wrote is not found The index has not seen the change Run Rebuild Extension Index

docs.title: Explain Plan
docs.text: Explain Plan shows how SQL Server would run a SELECT on the active environment's database, without running it. It compiles the query with SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON, then summarizes the plan in plain language: where the cost goes, scans of large tables, the indexes SQL Server says are missing, and plan warnings such as implicit conversions. Use it to check the SQL behind a slow while select before you change indexes or code. Visual Studio has no equivalent; there you would use the estimated execution plan in SQL Server Management Studio.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• A form or batch job is slow and you suspect one query.
  • You found a heavy query with Database Performance Insights ("Most expensive queries") and want to see why it is expensive.
  • You want to know whether a new table index in your model would be used, before deploying it.
  • Analyze Performance or Analyze Trace pointed at a query and you want its plan on real data volumes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Database access for the active environment. See Database Access.
  • An open SQL Query Panel with the query. Explain Plan accepts the same statements as a read-only run: one SELECT or WITH … SELECT.
  • Write the query in SQL, with SQL names. X++ select statements are not translated. To see the SQL an X++ query produces, take it from a trace (Analyze Trace) or from Query Store (Database Performance Insights).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open a query tab: F&O Studio: New SQL Query, Open as SQL in a Browse tab, or a Performance Insights query.
  2. Type or paste the SELECT. For example, the customers of a customer group:
SELECT ACCOUNTNUM, PARTY, CUSTGROUP
FROM CUSTTABLE
WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf' AND CUSTGROUP = '10'
  1. Click Explain Plan on the toolbar.
  2. A progress indicator Getting the query plan shows in the status bar.
  3. A Markdown document opens beside the panel, as a preview tab. The query is not run.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
The document has four parts:

# Query plan (estimated; the query was not run)

    (the query)

Estimated cost 0.0328, 3 operator(s).

## Where the cost goes
- Clustered Index Scan on CUSTTABLE.I_10011RECID: 92% of the cost, about 1,240 row(s).
- Compute Scalar: 5% of the cost, about 1,240 row(s).
- Clustered Index Scan on CUSTTABLE.I_10011RECID reads about 1,240 rows: an index on the filtered columns may avoid it.

## Missing indexes
- Missing index on CUSTTABLE (impact 87%): equality [DATAAREAID, CUSTGROUP], inequality [], include [ACCOUNTNUM, PARTY]. In F&O, add it as a table index in your model, not in SQL.

## Warnings
None.

The numbers and index names above are illustrative; yours come from your database.

Part What it tells you Estimated cost, operators SQL Server's estimated subtree cost of the statement and the number of plan operators Where the cost goes The five operators with the highest own cost (their cost minus their children's), each with its physical operator, the logical one when different, the table and index, its share of the total cost and the estimated rows. Then every table scan, clustered index scan or index scan estimated to read more than 1,000 rows. Missing indexes Each index SQL Server's optimizer asked for: table, estimated impact, equality columns, inequality columns and included columns Warnings Plan warnings. Implicit conversions show the expression and a hint to compare with values of the column's type; a join without a join condition is called out as a cross join; other warnings show their name.

When a part is empty it says "Nothing stands out.", "None suggested." or "None.".

docs.title: Acting on the result
docs.text:
• Missing index. Do not create it in SQL: F&O Studio's insight text says the same, add it as a table index in your model. An index created directly in SQL is not part of your model and is not deployed with it. Add the index to the table in your model (or in a table extension), with the equality columns first, then build, deploy, synchronize and explain the query again.
  • Large scan. Look at the WHERE clause: is a filter missing in the X++ code, or does no index start with the filtered fields?
  • Implicit conversion. A value of another type is compared with the column, which can prevent an index seek. In SQL you wrote, quote strings and use numbers for numeric columns.
  • Cross join. A join condition is missing; in X++ check the exists join / join clauses and their where.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Explain Plan has no settings. It uses the Database Access of the active environment.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The panel sends a plan message with the editor's text (src/database/dataPanel.ts).
  2. DataClient.plan (core/src/data/client.ts) sends the plan action to the extension's server process (xpp/data) with the connection.
  3. The server (DataQueryService.cs) applies the read-only check (ReadOnlySql.cs), opens a connection, runs SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON, executes the query text (SQL Server returns the plan instead of running it) with a 60-second time limit, and turns SHOWPLAN_XML off again.
  4. QueryPlan.cs parses the showplan XML: StmtSimple/@StatementSubTreeCost for the total, each RelOp for operators (own cost = its EstimatedTotalSubtreeCost minus its child operators'), MissingIndexGroup for missing indexes and Warnings for warnings.
  5. The summary comes back; the raw XML is returned too when it is under 200,000 characters, but the document shows only the summary.
  6. The extension writes the Markdown document and opens it beside the panel.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Estimated plan only. Actual row counts, actual memory grants and runtime statistics are not shown, because the query is not run.
  • One SELECT at a time, with the same read-only rules as the query panel; no plans for UPDATE or DELETE.
  • No graphical plan. For the full plan, open the same query in SQL Server Management Studio (Open in SSMS).
  • The plan is the one SQL Server compiles for the literal values you wrote. X++ queries usually run with parameters, so the plan in production can differ.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Only SELECT queries run in read-only mode." The text is not a SELECT Explain only SELECT statements "Run one statement at a time." More than one statement in the editor Keep one statement "The server returned no plan." SQL Server returned no showplan for the text Check that the text is a complete query "No database access. Request credentials with F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials, then run again." No credentials on a UDE Run Request Database Credentials The document says "Nothing stands out." The plan has no costly operator or large scan The query is probably not the problem; look at how often it runs (Analyze Trace)

docs.text:

  • Analyze Performance
  • Analyze Trace
  • Performance Rules Reference
  • Scenario: Performance Tuning a Slow Process

Source: Explain-Plan on the wiki.

docs.title: Export and Import Projects
docs.text: Export Project… packs the open D365FO project and the metadata of its elements into an .axpp file. Import Project… unpacks an .axpp into your model and writes its project file. The format is the one Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 > Import/Export project uses, so .axpp files move freely between Visual Studio and VS Code.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Hand a set of elements to someone who has no access to your source control: a colleague, a partner, support.
  • Move a prototype from one development machine (or environment version) to another.
  • Bring in an .axpp that someone exported from Visual Studio.
  • Keep a snapshot of a project's elements outside Git.

For day-to-day teamwork, use source control instead (Source Control for X++); for deployment, build a deployable package (Create Deployment Package). An .axpp holds metadata (source), not compiled code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Export: an open D365FO project (D365FO Projects) whose elements are in your custom metadata folder.
  • Import: an environment with metadata on this machine. The model in the .axpp must be one of your models, or not exist yet (F&O Studio then creates it).
  • Both run in the F&O Studio metadata server.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Model and project > Export Project… / Import Project… Command Palette F&O Studio: Export Project… / F&O Studio: Import Project…

docs.title: Export a project
docs.text:
1. Open the project you want to export.
  2. Run Export Project…. Without an open project you get Select a D365FO project first (F&O Studio: Open D365FO Project).
  3. In the save dialog (Export project , file type Dynamics 365 project export), keep the default <project folder>\<project>.axpp or choose another place.
  4. F&O Studio writes the file and shows, for example, Exported 6 element(s) of model ContosoExtensions to C:\Exports\ContosoProject.axpp.
  5. Elements listed in the project whose metadata file is missing are skipped and named: Not found (skipped): AxClass\ContosoOldHelper.

docs.title: Import a project
docs.text:
1. Run Import Project… and pick an .axpp file.
  2. F&O Studio reads the file first and shows a summary, for example: ContosoProject: 6 element(s) for model ContosoExtensions (the model will be created). 2 already exist.
  3. Choose:
  4. Import — when none of the elements exist yet;
  5. Import and overwrite — replace the elements that already exist with the ones in the file;
  6. Import new only — import only the elements that do not exist; existing ones are kept.
  7. Pick the Folder for the project (button Import here). The project file goes to <folder>\<project name>\<project>.rnrproj.
  8. F&O Studio imports the elements, writes the project file, refreshes the Application Explorer and the project view, and shows Imported 6 element(s) into model ContosoExtensions. (plus Kept existing: … when you chose Import new only).
  9. Click Open This Project in the message to open the imported project's workspace.

Then build the project (Build Project and Model): an import writes metadata only.

docs.title: The .axpp format
docs.text:
An .axpp is a ZIP file. F&O Studio writes and reads the same entries as Visual Studio:

Entry Content Project\<Project>.rnrproj The project file, unchanged Model\<Model>.xml The model's ModelInfo (name, display name, publisher, layer, version, module references...), serialized with the .NET DataContractSerializer ProjectItem\<Model>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml One entry per project element: its metadata file ProjectItem\<Model>\AxLabelFile\LabelResources\<lang>\<Id>.<lang>.label.txt Label texts of an exported label file ProjectItem\<Model>\AxResource\ResourceContent\<Name>.* Content of an exported resource BA6BECB9-70B9-4E31-BD29-1A3725A0BA4F.xml The package descriptor: PackageVersion 1.1 and a ContentResourceDictionary that maps each label file or resource entry to its content entry

Example of the entries for a small project:

Project\ContosoProject.rnrproj
Model\ContosoExtensions.xml
ProjectItem\ContosoExtensions\AxClass\ContosoOrderStatusService.xml
ProjectItem\ContosoExtensions\AxEnum\ContosoOrderStatus.xml
ProjectItem\ContosoExtensions\AxTableExtension\CustTable.ContosoExtensions.xml
ProjectItem\ContosoExtensions\AxLabelFile\ContosoLabels_en-US.xml
ProjectItem\ContosoExtensions\AxLabelFile\LabelResources\en-US\ContosoLabels.en-US.label.txt
BA6BECB9-70B9-4E31-BD29-1A3725A0BA4F.xml

docs.title: What export includes
docs.text:
• Every Content item of the .rnrproj of the form <AxType>\<Name> (items with a DependentUpon are left out), read from <custom metadata folder>\<package>\<model>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml.
  • For a label file <Id>_<lang> (for example ContosoLabels_en-US), its .label.txt file for that language.
  • For a resource, its files in AxResource\ResourceContent.
  • The model's descriptor information (Model\<Model>.xml).

Not included: compiled binaries, referenced C# projects and assemblies (the .rnrproj keeps the reference items, but not the files), and elements that are not in the project.

docs.title: What import does
docs.text:
1. Reads Model\<Model>.xml. If no model of that name exists, it creates it with the archived ModelInfo (through the metadata API) and reloads the metadata.
  2. Stops with Model is not one of your models; importing into it is not allowed. if the model exists and is a standard model.
  3. Extracts each ProjectItem\<Model>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml to <custom metadata folder>\<package>\<model>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml, skipping existing files unless you chose to overwrite. Read-only flags on existing files are cleared first.
  4. Extracts the label and resource content that the descriptor maps to each element, into the target model's folder.
  5. Writes the .rnrproj to <folder>\<project name>\. An existing project file there is overwritten.
  6. Reloads the metadata and clears the caches.

    7. Every extracted path is checked to stay inside the target folder; an entry that would land outside it stops the import (Entry is outside the target folder: …).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Export and import have no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Commands: exportProject and importProject in src/d365Tools.ts.
  • Server: ProjectPackageService in server/Ported/MetaModel/ProjectPackageService.cs, bridge actions export_project (projectFile, outputFile), inspect_project_package (file: project, model, whether the model exists, and each element with whether it exists) and import_project (file, targetFolder, overwrite). The format follows Visual Studio's ProjectExporter / ProjectImporter (descriptor namespace Microsoft.Dynamics.Framework.Tools.ProjectSystem.ExportImport).
  • Element files are extracted as they are in the archive; F&O Studio does not convert them. A missing model is created with IMetaModelService.CreateModel of Microsoft's metadata API.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Export works on the open project only.
  • Import always targets the model named in the file. It cannot rename the model or import into a different model.
  • Import does not merge into an existing project file; it writes the project file from the archive.
  • Elements that are not in your custom metadata folder (for example standard elements listed by mistake in the project) are not exported.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Select a D365FO project first (F&O Studio: Open D365FO Project). No project open Open the project, then export The project's model '…' was not found. The <Model> of the .rnrproj is not in the active configuration Select the right environment, or fix the project's model Not found (skipped): … after export Project items without a metadata file in your model Remove them from the project, or restore the files Not a Dynamics 365 project export (.axpp). The ZIP has no Project\ or Model\ entry Use a file exported by Visual Studio or F&O Studio Can't read : … The file is damaged or not a ZIP Export it again Model … is not one of your models; importing into it is not allowed. The archive's model is a standard model on this machine Import on a machine where that model is yours, or move the elements into your model by hand Could not create model …. The metadata API refused the archived model Check the custom metadata folder and the server log (Troubleshooting)

docs.text:

  • Models and Model Dependencies
  • Create Deployment Package
  • Source Control for X++
  • Compared with Visual Studio

Source: Export-and-Import-Projects on the wiki.

docs.title: Extension Internals
docs.text:
This page describes the TypeScript extension in src/: how it activates, which server processes it runs, how commands, views, webviews and language features are wired, and where each feature lives. It is for contributors and for anyone who wants to understand what happens behind a command.

For the big picture, read Architecture first.

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
package.json declares:

Field Value main ./out/extension.js (TypeScript compiled by tsc from src/) engines.vscode ^1.101.0 activationEvents workspaceContains:**/*.rnrproj, onFileSystem:xpp, onStartupFinished capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.supported false (the extension runs the compiler, the debugger and the metadata server)

activate() in src/extension.ts runs these steps:

  1. Creates the output channels X++ (server logs, command errors) and X++ Build (compiler output).
  2. Restores this window's environment selection (initEnvironmentSelection) and repairs XPPConfig files written by older versions that lacked members Visual Studio requires (repairGeneratedConfigurations).
  3. Creates two XppServerClient instances: server and languageServer. Neither starts a process yet; each starts on its first request.
  4. Creates the builder (XppBuilder), the deploy state, the project and Application Explorer tree providers, the xpp: file system for the code view, navigation, pac commands, the version guard and the environment status.
  5. Registers webview panel serializers so the element designer, form designer and label editor tabs survive a window reload (src/webviewState.ts).
  6. Registers the MCP server definition provider for Copilot (registerMcpProvider).
  7. Registers the file system provider, the tree views xpp.project and xpp.aot (with drag and drop), and language providers for X++ documents: definition, references, hover, rename, document links and drop edits. It also registers a definition provider for C# documents that goes from C# to X++ code.
  8. Registers every command through one wrapper (see below), then the feature modules: database, Dynamics 365 tools, productivity, security, performance, upgrade readiness, integration, telemetry queries, Copilot Activity, trace analyzer, report designer, references, Go To, history, tests and Test Explorer.
  9. Starts watching for a project selected by an agent (activeProject.txt). When an agent selects a different project, the extension asks before it opens it, because opening reloads the window.

deactivate() releases running debugger proxies.

docs.title: The two server clients
docs.text:
src/serverClient.ts owns one XppVsCode.Server.exe process.

  • Start: on first use it reads the active environment, then spawns server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe --config <json> --allow-data [--project <rnrproj>] with a hidden window, and sends initialize.
  • Protocol: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin and stdout. Each request gets a numeric id and a timer. Stderr goes to the X++ output channel.
  • Timeouts: 180 seconds by default; trace analysis uses 600 seconds; data queries take a timeout from the caller.
  • Methods it exposes:
Client method JSON-RPC method Used for bridge(action, body) xpp/bridge metadata actions (designers, code view, explorers, projects, labels, models, reports) lang(action, body) xpp/lang language features (completion, symbols, code lens, implementations, syntax check, search) data(action, body) xpp/data business data (browse, query, explain plan, cancel, connection test) trace(body), traceAction(...) xpp/trace .etl trace analysis and loading call tree children tool(name, args) tools/call the same agent tools Copilot uses, called by the extension itself
  • State: onDidChangeState fires starting, ready or failed. ServerStatus (src/serverStatus.ts) shows it in the status bar; clicking restarts the server.
  • Restart: restart() kills the process and rejects pending requests with a message that points to F&O Studio: Restart X++ Server. The next request starts a new process. The extension restarts both clients when the environment or xpp.project changes.

server serves designers, the code view, explorers and most commands. languageServer serves code intelligence, so building an index never blocks a designer.

Bridge action names are typed: BridgeAction in src/bridgeContract.ts is a union of every action the server registers, and every result is a BridgeResult (success, optional message, other members per action). See Bridge-Protocol.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
All commands go through one command(id, handler) helper in extension.ts:

  • It counts the command in VS Code global state when xpp.usageStatistics is on (local only; see Usage-Statistics).
  • It catches errors, writes the stack to the X++ output channel, remembers the error for Report a Problem… (recordError), and shows the message with Show Log and Report Problem buttons.

Many commands take an element argument. elementFromArg accepts (type, name) strings, an Application Explorer or project tree node, or an xpp: code view URI (editor context menu), so the same command works from every menu.

package.json contributes 169 commands (category "F&O Studio"). See Command-Reference.

docs.title: Views and webviews
docs.text:
UI Implementation Application Explorer (xpp.aot) AotTreeProvider in src/aot.ts Project view (xpp.project) ProjectTreeProvider in src/project.ts, solution helpers in src/solution.ts and src/references.ts Copilot Activity (xpp.activity) src/activity.ts, reads the MCP server's activity.jsonl Results view src/results.ts Security view src/security/ Element designer src/elementDesigner.ts with media/element.* Form designer and preview src/designer.ts with media/formPreview.* Label editor src/labelEditor.ts Report designer src/reports/ ERD and diagrams src/erd.ts, src/diagrams.ts Data panel and SQL panel src/database/ Trace panel src/traceAnalyzer.ts

Webviews set a Content-Security-Policy with a nonce from crypto.randomBytes. Panel state is kept in the page (data-xpp-state on <body>), so registerPanelSerializer can reopen designer tabs after a reload.

docs.title: The code view (xpp: documents)
docs.text:
X++ code is not stored as files you edit directly. The code view is a virtual file system:

  • XppCodeFileSystem in src/codeView.ts serves xpp: URIs. readFile reads the element through the bridge; writeFile splits your text back into declaration and methods and saves them through the bridge.
  • src/xppSource.ts lays out the source like Visual Studio: the declaration without its closing brace, methods (stored indented by four spaces) inside the class body, then }. splitSource uses the original declaration to keep trailing comments and macros. It also maps compiler line numbers to document lines (compilerLineToDocumentLine).
  • When the environment changes, open xpp: documents that are not dirty refresh from the new environment.

See XPP-Code-View.

docs.title: Language features
docs.text:
src/codeIntel/providers.ts registers completion, signature help, document and workspace symbols, code lens, implementations, call and type hierarchy, hover, folding, syntax diagnostics, semantic tokens and formatting. Obsolete API warnings are in src/productivity/obsolete.ts. Each feature is a switch under xpp.codeIntelligence.* (src/codeIntel/settings.ts). They call languageServer.lang(...); the server's CodeIntel class answers actions such as symbols, members, implementations, code_lens, calls, subtypes, syntax, obsolete, labels and search_code.

Navigation (definition, references, hover) is XppNavigation in src/navigation.ts. The formatter and folding are pure TypeScript (src/codeIntel/formatter.ts, src/codeIntel/folding.ts).

Microsoft's X++ language server is not used: it only advertises document sync.

docs.title: Build, deploy, tests and debugging
docs.text: Feature Where Notes Build src/build.ts Runs LabelC, then xppc, then reportsc from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin; reads xppc's XML log into Problems (src/diagnostics.ts); converts PDBs to portable ones with the shipped Pdb2Pdb (src/portablePdb.ts) C# references src/dotnetReferences.ts Builds referenced C# projects with MSBuild and copies their output into the package bin folder, as Visual Studio does Best practice build.ts Runs xppbp.exe Build tasks src/tasks.ts Task type xpp, actions buildProject and buildModel Deploy and sync src/udeDeploy.ts, src/pac.ts The work is in core (deployPackages, syncDatabase) Deploy state src/deployState.ts Built versus deployed per environment and model Tests src/tests.ts, src/testExplorer.ts The runner is core's runTests Debugger src/debug.ts Debug type xpp; on a UDE, the FinOps tools' DebuggerProxy.exe (--VSVersion vsdbg) is the debug adapter; on a local AOS, the C# extension's debugger

docs.title: Cloud operations through core
docs.text:
The extension imports @fno-studio/core only through src/core.ts, which re-exports core/dist. Two small adapters connect core to VS Code:

  • Sign-in: dataverseTokens in src/ude.ts is a core TokenProvider over VS Code's Microsoft account (vscode.authentication.getSession('microsoft', ...)), interactive or silent. When xpp.auth.clientId is set, the scopes include that app ID.
  • Cancellation: src/coreHost.ts turns a CancellationToken into an AbortSignal (abortSignalOf, withAbortSignal).

Logs go to output channels through core's Log interface; progress goes to VS Code notifications through Progress. See Core-Library.

docs.title: Copilot integration
docs.text:
• MCP server: src/mcpProvider.ts registers the definition "F&O Studio" for provider id xpp.mcp. It watches **/.xpp/agent-rules.md, xpp.project and environment changes, and fires a change so VS Code restarts the server with the new arguments.
  • Language model tools contributed by the extension itself (not the MCP server): xpp_open_element, xpp_run_tests and xpp_query_data (src/database/queryTool.ts). xpp_query_data runs in the extension's process, which holds the database credentials; the agent never sees them.
  • Agents: generated from scripts/agent-definitions.js into agents/*.agent.md and the chatAgents and chatInstructions contributions. Never edit the generated files; run npm run agents.
  • Checkpoints and scope: src/agentSession.ts writes agentSession.json; the MCP server enforces it. See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

docs.title: Settings with machine scope
docs.text: Settings that point at programs the extension runs have machine scope, so a workspace cannot set them: xpp.pacPath, xpp.debuggerProxyPath, xpp.build.msbuildPath and xpp.trace.manifestFolder. xpp.project has window scope. See Settings-Reference.

docs.title: Adding something new
docs.text: You add Also do A bridge action Register it in the server's RegisterActions with the right WriteKind, add the name to src/bridgeContract.ts, run node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js An agent tool Register it in ToolRouter.RegisterTools and add its definition to server/Resources/Tools.json (the server refuses to start when they differ) A Copilot agent Edit scripts/agent-definitions.js, run npm run agents Something in core Keep vscode out; run npm run test:core A command Add it to contributes.commands and register it with the command() helper

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Answers to the questions D365FO developers ask most about F&O Studio. For error messages, see Troubleshooting; for terms, see the Glossary.

docs.title: What is F&O Studio?
docs.text: A VS Code extension, F&O Studio for VS Code (ID MNazmi.xpp-vscode), for Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations X++ development without Visual Studio. It has an Application Explorer, element, form and report designers, X++ code navigation, build, best practice checks, deployment packages, deploy, database sync, the debugger, data browsing, and agent tools and agents for GitHub Copilot. See Getting-Started.

docs.title: Is it from Microsoft?
docs.text: No. F&O Studio is an independent open-source project under the Apache License 2.0. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. It uses Microsoft's D365FO tools (metadata API, compiler, scripts) from your own installation.

docs.title: Is it finished?
docs.text: It is a preview. Some features are not yet verified end to end on a live environment: the version drift guard, Open Team Repository on a real team repository, Try Data Entity and Try Service Operation, and Verify Changes in the Running App. Cloud-hosted environments use the same code path as VHD environments but have not been tested yet.

docs.title: Does it cost anything?
docs.text: The extension is free. Copilot features need your own GitHub Copilot subscription.

docs.title: Do I need Visual Studio?
docs.text: No. F&O Studio builds with xppc and LabelC, deploys through the environment's Dataverse and debugs with Microsoft's debugger proxy, without Visual Studio. See Compared-with-Visual-Studio.

docs.title: Can I use Visual Studio and F&O Studio on the same machine?
docs.text: Yes. F&O Studio reads and writes the same configuration Visual Studio uses (the CurrentMetadataConfig registry value and the JSON files in XPPConfig), and the same project (.rnrproj) and export (.axpp) formats. Visual Studio's FinOps tools must match the metadata version; Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version installs the matching tools into Visual Studio when they differ. See Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: Will my projects open in Visual Studio?
docs.text: Yes. Create D365FO Project… writes a .rnrproj and a .slnx the way Visual Studio does, and the project view follows the .rnrproj, so elements added in Visual Studio show up in F&O Studio and the other way round. See D365FO-Projects.

docs.title: Is the build the same as Visual Studio's?
docs.text: It uses the same compilers: xppc for X++, LabelC for labels and reportsc for reports. Referenced C# projects are built and copied into the package first, as Visual Studio does. Errors go to VS Code's Problems view. See Build-Project-and-Model.

docs.title: Is the deploy the same as Visual Studio's?
docs.text: On a unified developer environment, Deploy Models to Environment uploads your packages as built on this machine through the environment's Dataverse, as Visual Studio's Deploy Models to Online Environment does. Nothing is recompiled, so the environment runs the build you debug. See Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: Which environments does it support?
docs.text: Unified developer environments (UDE), cloud-hosted environments (CHE) and VHD environments, on Windows. A UDE needs Connect to Environment… once; a cloud-hosted or VHD environment needs no setup. See Connect-to-Environment and Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments.

docs.title: Does it run on macOS or Linux?
docs.text: No. It needs Windows, because Microsoft's D365FO compiler and metadata API are Windows tools.

docs.title: What does Connect to Environment download, and where?
docs.text: The standard metadata (PackagesLocalDirectory), the cross-reference database backup and the FinOps tools for the environment's application version, from the same Microsoft service Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools use. They go into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<application version>\. You need about 16 GB of free disk space. The cross-reference database is restored into SQL Server LocalDB.

docs.title: Can I work with several environments?
docs.text: Yes. Connect each one, then switch with Select Environment… or the environment name in the status bar. Each workspace remembers its environment, so two VS Code windows can work with two environments. See Select-Environment.

docs.title: The UDE was updated. What do I do?
docs.text: F&O Studio warns you when the environment runs a newer application version than the metadata on your machine. Select Update Metadata to download the new version, and Clean Up Old Application Versions… to remove old ones. See Version-Drift-Guard.

docs.title: Why are Deploy and Run Tests missing?
docs.text: They are UDE-only: they run through the environment's Dataverse, which cloud-hosted and VHD environments do not have. F&O Studio hides them there. On those environments the build goes into the local PackagesLocalDirectory and the running AOS restarts after a successful build.

docs.title: Do I need the Power Platform CLI (pac)?
docs.text: No. Deploy and database sync run through Dataverse directly. Only Sign In to Environment (pac) and Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) use pac, for when you run your own pac commands. See Power-Platform-CLI.

docs.title: Do I need SQL Server LocalDB?
docs.text: Yes, for the cross-reference database. Find References, rename, the references diagrams and the report data provider list use it.

docs.title: Can I change standard code?
docs.text: No, the same as in Visual Studio. Standard elements are read-only; you extend them with Create Extension (metadata) or Create Code Extension (Chain of Command), or event handlers. Delete and rename work only on elements of your own models. See Create-Extension and Create-Code-Extension.

docs.title: Does F&O Studio write AOT XML files by hand?
docs.text: No. Metadata changes go through Microsoft's metadata API, as in Visual Studio. Only the project file (.rnrproj) and the label text files are edited directly, because they are not AOT metadata.

docs.title: Can I debug Microsoft's code?
docs.text: Yes, on unified developer environments: set a breakpoint in the code view of a standard element (for example the init method of the PurchTable form). Open the form or run the code once before you start the debugger, so the breakpoint binds right away. See Debugging-Standard-Code.

docs.title: Can I debug on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment?
docs.text: Yes. Launch Debugger attaches to the local AOS with the C# extension's .NET debugger; F&O Studio offers to install the C# extension. See Debugging-on-Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: Can I use C# projects with my X++ project?
docs.text: Yes. The project view shows the solution's C# projects; Add Reference… and New C# Project… add references and C# class libraries, and the build compiles them first. See Solution-View-and-CSharp-References.

docs.title: Can I build an LCS deployable package?
docs.text: Create Deployment Package… runs the same script Visual Studio runs (RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from PackagesLocalDirectory's bin folder). See Create-Deployment-Package.

docs.title: Does it have SSRS report design?
docs.text: Yes. The element designer shows reports as Visual Studio does, the Report Designer lays out precision designs, and the preview renders with Microsoft's report engine. The preview downloads Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime from nuget.org the first time, after you accept Microsoft's licence. See Report-Designer and Report-Preview.

docs.title: Can I look at table data?
docs.text: Yes. Browse Table Data and New SQL Query work against the environment's database. On a UDE, F&O Studio requests temporary SQL credentials (the same just-in-time request Visual Studio makes); on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment it uses the local AxDB with Windows authentication. See Database-Access.

docs.title: Why does the database request fail?
docs.text: Database access on a unified developer or sandbox environment needs the System administrator role. New credentials can take a minute before Azure SQL accepts them. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Can a query change data?
docs.text: New SQL Query is read-only by default: one SELECT, always rolled back. Allow changes commits after a confirmation each run, with a warning that X++ business logic is skipped. Copilot's xpp_query_data runs only a read-only, row-limited SELECT after your confirmation. See SQL-Query-Panel.

docs.title: Do I need GitHub Copilot?
docs.text: Only for the agents and the agent tools. Everything else works without it.

docs.title: What can Copilot do with F&O Studio?
docs.text: It gets agent tools to read, create, extend, validate and build elements through the metadata API, search code, find references and message sources, analyze security, performance and traces, run tests and, with your confirmation, read data. F&O agents (for developers and for functional consultants) appear in the chat's agent picker. See Copilot-Agents and MCP-Agent-Tools.

docs.title: Can Copilot break my model or change standard code?
docs.text: Agent tools write only to your own models, every write is all or nothing, and an existing name is never overwritten. Standard elements are extended, never changed. Start Copilot Checkpoint lets you revert everything Copilot changed afterwards, and Set Copilot Scope… limits which elements it may change; the server enforces both. See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope and Scenario-Work-Safely-with-Copilot.

docs.title: Does Copilot see my database credentials?
docs.text: No. xpp_query_data runs one read-only query after your confirmation, and the agent never sees the credentials.

docs.title: Where did @fno go?
docs.text: It was removed, because VS Code retires chat participants. Pick an F&O agent in the chat's agent picker instead: for example /extend became the F&O Developer agent and /review the Code Reviewer.

docs.title: Can I share rules with my team for Copilot?
docs.text: Yes. Create Team Rules for Copilot creates .xpp/agent-rules.md in your repository; it is added to the agent instructions of everyone working in the repository. See Team-Rules.

docs.title: Can I use the agent tools outside VS Code?
docs.text: Each GitHub release includes a standalone server package (fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip) with its SHA-256 checksum for MCP hosts outside VS Code. See MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code.

docs.title: Does F&O Studio collect telemetry?
docs.text: No. It talks to the Finance and Operations and Dataverse environments you connect it to, Microsoft's download service for that environment's tools, nuget.org for the report preview runtime (after you accept the licence), and GitHub only when you choose to report a problem. Optional command counts stay on your machine. See Usage-Statistics.

docs.title: Does it ship Microsoft's assemblies?
docs.text: No. The extension's server is compiled against Microsoft's D365FO assemblies but never includes them; it loads them at run time from your own installation.

docs.title: How do I sign in?
docs.text: With VS Code's Microsoft account sign-in. If your tenant does not allow VS Code's default sign-in for Dataverse, set xpp.auth.clientId to your own Entra application ID. See Sign-In-and-Authentication.

docs.title: Where are database credentials stored?
docs.text: In VS Code's secret storage, until they expire. Forget Database Credentials removes them.

docs.title: How do I report a problem?
docs.text: Use Report a Problem… (Command Palette, the bottom of the Dynamics 365 view, or the Report Problem button on an error). It shows you a redacted report first. See Report-a-Problem.

docs.title: Where are the logs?
docs.text: In the Output panel: X++ (server, setup, debugger, failed commands), X++ Build, X++ Deploy and X++ Tests.

docs.title: Where is the source code?
docs.text: On GitHub: nazmolla/xpp-vscode. See Building-from-Source and Architecture.

docs.title: Find All References
docs.text: Find All References lists the places that use an element or a method: X++ code in every model, and metadata such as form data sources, menu items, relations or security objects. It reads the cross-reference database that the X++ compiler fills during a build, the same database Visual Studio's Find References uses. In code you get VS Code's References view (Shift+F12); from the Application Explorer, the project view, a designer or a hover you get a picker with every reference and its kind.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you change the signature of a method, see who calls it.
  • Find the code that reads or writes a field of a table.
  • Find which forms, menu items, entities or security objects use an element.
  • Understand how standard code uses a class you want to extend.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Cross-reference database. Your D365FO configuration names it (on a unified developer environment usually (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB with a database XRef_<org><version>). Connect to Environment restores Microsoft's database for the standard application.
  • Your own code is in it only after a build with cross references. xpp.build.crossReference is on by default, so Build Project and Model updates it. References in code you changed since the last build are not there yet.
  • The element type must be one the database indexes: classes, tables, forms, enums, EDTs, views, queries, data entities, maps, menus, menu items, table and enum extensions, reports, security roles, privileges and duties, tiles and configuration keys.

docs.title: In code (References view)
docs.text:
1. In a code view, put the cursor on an element name or a method (CustGroup, CustGroup::find, this.validateWrite, custGroup.find).
  2. Press Shift+F12 to see the references in a peek window, or right-click and choose Find All References to see them in the References view.
  3. VS Code lists the code locations, grouped by file. Each entry opens the code view at the line of the reference. Methods of form data sources and controls open in their own editor.

The symbol is resolved the same way as for Go to Definition: a method found in code is searched as a member (/Tables/CustGroup/Methods/find), anything else as the element. For an element, references to its members count too (a call to CustGroup::find is a reference to CustGroup).

In the editor list you see only references from code (classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, queries, maps). Use the Find References command below to also see metadata references.

The Code Lens above each method shows the reference count; clicking it peeks the same list.

docs.title: From the trees, designers and hover (picker)
docs.text:
Run Find References from:

  • the context menu of an element in the Application Explorer or the project view;
  • the context menu of the Element Designer: on the root node, or on a member such as a method or a field;
  • the Find references link in the Hover over an element name;
  • the Find References… node in the Dynamics 365 view, or the command palette (F&O Studio: Find References), which ask for an element name (at least 3 characters) and let you pick the element.

A notification shows "Finding references to X…". Then a picker opens with the title "N reference(s) to X" (N+ when there are more than 1,000). Each row shows:

Part Content Label The referencing element, for example SalesTable Description The member (method or node) that holds the reference, line N, and the reference kind Detail The element type and the module (package)

You can type to filter on all three. Picking a row opens the code view at that line, the nested method's editor, or the designer for elements without code.

When nothing references the target you see "No references to X from other elements."

docs.title: Reference kinds
docs.text:
The kind tells you how the target is used. The values come from the cross-reference database:

Kind Meaning MethodCall A call of the method TypeReference The type is used: a declaration, tableStr(), a property value InterfaceImplementation A class implements the interface ClassExtended A class extends the class TestCall, TestHelperCall Calls from test code Property A metadata property names the target Attribute An attribute uses the class (for example [ExtensionOf(...)]) Tag A tag (see Find Tag References) MethodOverride A method overrides the target method

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Update the cross-reference database while building, so where-used includes your code

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Editor: provideReferences in src/navigation.ts resolves the symbol and calls the bridge action where_used with the element, the member (for methods) and at most 200 results.
  2. Command: findReferences in src/d365Tools.ts calls where_used with at most 1,000 results.
  3. Server: XRefQuery.QueryJson in server/Ported/Tools/XRefQuery.cs checks the database health (configured, online, initialized, not empty, a schema version it knows; cached for two minutes), then runs one SQL query on the Names, References and Modules tables:
  4. the target is the path /Tables/CustGroup, or /Tables/CustGroup/Methods/find or /Fields/<name> for a member; fields added by table extensions (/TableExtensions/CustGroup.<suffix>/Fields/<name>) count as fields of the table;
  5. for an element, references from the element itself are left out; for a member, references from the member itself are left out (other methods of the same element are kept);
  6. results are ordered by module, source and line.
  7. Each reference comes back with the source path, member path, line, kind and module. The line is counted the way the compiler counts it; compilerLineToDocumentLine in src/xppSource.ts maps it to the code view line.

The same query serves the agent tool xpp_find_references (see Agent Tools: Metadata) and the reference diagram (Hierarchy and Reference Diagrams).

When you delete an element, F&O Studio removes the cross-reference entries from it (xppc only drops them on a full model build), so where-used doesn't list deleted elements.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The results are as of the last build with cross references. New code is not found until you build.
  • Custom packages that were never built with cross references are missing; the server notes them as warnings.
  • Packages marked as not local (typically test packages) are indexed but their source is not installed, so you can't open their code.
  • The editor list shows at most 200 references and only code references; the picker shows at most 1,000.
  • References are found by element and member, not by text. Dynamic calls (for example through DictClass or method names in strings) are not found.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The server reports why the database can't be used. Typical messages:

Message Cause Fix "The active D365FO configuration does not define the cross-reference database ..." The configuration has no CrossReferencesDbServerName / CrossReferencesDatabaseName Re-run Connect to Environment or fix the configuration "Cross-reference database '...' is ... not ONLINE." The database is offline or restoring Bring it online in SQL Server / LocalDB "... exists but is not initialized ..." or "... is empty. Build the models with 'Build cross reference data' enabled." No build has filled the database Build with xpp.build.crossReference on "Where-used is not available for AxX." The type is not indexed by the database Use Search Code instead "No cross-reference entries for ..." Nothing references it, the name is wrong, or its package was not built with cross references Check the name; build the package $(warning) in the status bar after Shift+F12 The query failed; the message says why See the rows above Your newest call is missing It was written after the last build Build the project

docs.title: Find Message Source
docs.text: Find Message Source takes a message exactly as a user saw it, values included, and finds where it comes from: the labels whose text matches the message, the X++ code that uses those labels, and, for the platform's "Field '...' must be filled in." message, the table fields whose Mandatory property causes it. It turns the most common support request, "I get this error, why?", into a list of code lines you can open. In Visual Studio you would do this by hand: search the label files for the text, note the label ID, then run Find References on the label.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• A user reports an error, warning or info message and you need the code that raises it.
  • You debug and the Infolog view shows a message you do not recognize.
  • You need the standard validation that you must satisfy or extend (for example the check behind "Customer ... is on hold").
  • A "Field '...' must be filled in." message appears and you need to know which field is mandatory and where that is set.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration (Select Environment). Labels are read from the label files of every package of that configuration.
  • The cross-reference database of the configuration, to find where labels are used. On a UDE it is restored during Connect to Environment. Without it you still see the matching labels, but not the code.
  • For code in your own models to show up, build them with cross-reference data (setting xpp.build.crossReference, on by default). See Build Project and Model.
  • The command matches English (en-US) label texts. Copilot's xpp_find_message_source tool accepts another language.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the command in one of these ways:
  2. In the Infolog view, click the search icon on a message, or right-click it and choose Find Message Source. The message text is passed in.
  3. In the Dynamics 365 view, open Find and choose Find Message Source… ("error text to code").
  4. Run F&O Studio: Find Message Source from the Command Palette. Text selected in the editor (up to 400 characters) is filled in.
  5. In the input box, paste or type the message as shown in the infolog or the error dialog, with its values, for example Field 'Customer group' must be filled in. At least 4 characters are needed.
  6. Press Enter. A notification shows Finding where the message comes from….
  7. A pick list opens with the title Where "<message>" comes from. It is divided into sections by separators (see below). Type in the list to filter by object, code line or label ID.
  8. Select an entry:
  9. a code line opens the method in the X++ Code View at that line;
  10. a mandatory field opens its table (or the table extension that sets Mandatory) in the Element Designer;
  11. a metadata usage (for example a label on a menu item or a security object) is listed for information only.

If nothing matches you see No label text or code matches this message.

docs.title: Label sections
docs.text:
Each label text that matches the message gets a separator:

"Customer %1 is on hold." · @Contoso:CustOnHold
  • The label text, with its placeholders.
  • The label IDs that have this text, up to three, then +N for more. The same text often exists in several label files (copies per module); they are merged into one section and their usages are combined.
  • (part of the message) when the label explains only a part of the message, for example a sentence inside a longer error.

Under the separator, each code line that uses one of these labels:

Part Content Label Object.method:line Description The code line that contains the label Detail Element type, the path inside the element for nested methods, and the label ID used

If no code uses the label, the section shows Not used in X++ code with one of these explanations:

  • The platform (kernel) raises it, or its package was not built with cross-reference data.
  • Where-used is unavailable: <reason> when the cross-reference database could not be opened.

docs.title: Literal text section
docs.text: When no label with usages explains the message, F&O Studio searches the code itself for the message written as a literal string (code such as throw error("...") without a label). This section is titled Code with the message as literal text.

docs.title: Mandatory fields section
docs.text:
For the platform message "Field '...' must be filled in." the list starts with Mandatory fields · platform check (@SYS26332), then the code sections:

  1. Mandatory fields: every table field that carries the field label from the message and has Mandatory = Yes, shown as Table.Field, with Mandatory = Yes and where it is set (Table, Extension <name> or Field of extension <name>) and the model.
  2. Code that raises it for "": code that uses the same label text and names one of these fields.
  3. Same text, other fields (N): code that reuses the text for other fields. These are kept apart because they rarely explain the user's case.

    4. If no table field with that label is mandatory, the first entry is No table field with this label is mandatory, with the number of fields that carry the label and a hint to check Mandatory on form data source fields and controls, personalization, or the code below.

docs.title: Message to label
docs.text:
1. F&O Studio builds an index of every label text of the language from all packages: each line Id=Text of every <LabelFile>.<language>.label.txt file under AxLabelFile\LabelResources\<language>. Custom packages are read first; a label file that exists in more than one place is read once.
  2. Each label text is split at its placeholders %1 to %9 into literal pieces. Customer %1 is on hold. gives the pieces Customer and is on hold.. Labels whose literal text is shorter than 4 characters are not used for matching.
  3. A label matches when all its pieces occur in the message, in order, ignoring case and extra white space. The placeholders match any value, so Customer US-001 is on hold. matches.
  4. A label is a whole match when its first piece starts at the beginning of the message and its last piece ends at the end (2 characters of slack on each side). Otherwise it explains only a part of the message.

docs.title: Ranking labels
docs.text:
Many short labels ("Customer", "Canceled") occur inside almost any message. To keep the list useful:

  • Labels that are not whole matches must have at least min(12, max(4, 30% of the message length)) literal characters; shorter ones are dropped (unless nothing else matches).
  • Label sections are ordered: whole matches first, then labels that code uses, then longer texts.
  • When a whole match is used by code, only whole matches are shown: they explain the message on their own.
  • Up to 5 label texts are shown.

docs.title: Label to code
docs.text:
For each label ID, F&O Studio asks the cross-reference database for the places that use /Labels/@File:Id, with the method and line. It then reads the method's source and finds the exact line that contains the label ID, so the line number and the code line you see are the real ones.

Usages are ordered:

  1. Code related to the mandatory field (mandatory-field messages only).
  2. Code outside test classes (objects whose name ends with Test or contains Test_ go last).
  3. Lines that raise a message first: lines with throw, error, warning, checkFailed, info, Box::..., addMessage or Message::.

Up to 40 usages are shown per label text.

docs.title: Literal strings
docs.text: When no label explains the message through code, F&O Studio splits the message at numbers, quoted values and placeholders, takes the longest remaining piece, and, if it has at least 12 characters, runs a Search Code for it over all packages (60 second limit). Comment lines are skipped.

docs.title: The mandatory-field message
docs.text:
The platform raises @SYS26332 ("Field '%1' must be filled in.") when a record is saved with an empty field whose Mandatory property is Yes. The code that reuses this label for its own checks is usually not the cause, so F&O Studio does more for this message:

  1. It recognizes the message by matching it against the text of @SYS26332 and takes the value of %1, the field label, for example Customer group (quotes removed).
  2. It finds every label in every label file whose whole text is that field label.
  3. Through the cross-reference database it finds:
  4. table fields whose Label property is one of those labels (on the table or added by a table extension);
  5. EDTs with one of those labels, the EDTs that extend them (up to four levels) unless they set their own label, and the table fields that use any of these EDTs without a label of their own.
  6. It reads the table and table extension files of those fields and keeps the fields whose Mandatory property is Yes, either on the field itself or through a field modification in a table extension.
  7. It sorts them: tables users work in first (most referenced in the cross-reference database), staging tables and temporary tables (names ending in Staging, Tmp or Temp) last.
  8. It marks each code usage of the label as related when the statement around it (the line before and the two lines after) names one of the fields, one of the field label IDs, or the field label text in double quotes.

In the screenshot above, SalesTable.CustGroup, CustTable.CustGroup and CustGroup.CustGroup come first because they are the most used tables with a mandatory field labelled "Customer group".

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Builds update the cross-reference database, so usages in your own code are found.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/findMessageSource.ts asks for the message and sends the language action message_source (maxLabels: 5, maxResults: 40) to the language server process.
  2. CodeIntel.cs passes it to MessageTrace.cs, which matches labels, queries the cross-reference database (Names and References tables), reads method sources and table files from the metadata folders, and falls back to CodeSearch.cs for literal strings.
  3. The extension builds the sectioned pick list and opens what you select with the same code as Search Code.

What is cached:

  • The label index is built on the first search, once per language, and kept for the life of the server process.
  • The list of table and table extension files is kept for 5 minutes, so new tables in your model are picked up.

Copilot agents use the same trace through the xpp_find_message_source tool (parameters message, language, maxLabels, maxResults). See MCP Agent Tools.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The command matches en-US label texts. Messages in another language need the agent tool with language.
  • Labels added after the first search are not in the index until the server restarts (for example after Developer: Reload Window).
  • Messages raised by the platform kernel have a label but no X++ usage; the section then says so.
  • Usages come from the cross-reference database: code that was not built with cross-reference data is missing.
  • Mandatory detection covers table fields. Mandatory set on form data source fields or form controls is not checked.
  • A message built from several labels concatenated in code matches each label as a part, not as a whole.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Enter at least 4 characters. The message is too short. Paste the full message. No label text or code matches this message. The text differs from the label (another language, typed by hand) or is built in code. Copy the exact text from the Infolog view, or search a distinctive part with Search Code. Where-used is unavailable: ... The cross-reference database could not be opened. Check the configuration in Select Environment. Label found but Not used in X++ code The kernel raises it, or the code's package has no cross-reference data. Build your model with xpp.build.crossReference on; for kernel messages, look at the field or table properties. A label you just created is not found The label index was built before you created it. Reload the window. No table field with this label is mandatory The field is mandatory on the form, or the code checks it. Check the form's data source fields and controls, and the code sections below.

docs.title: Find Security Gaps
docs.text: Find Security Gaps checks the security of the models you pick and lists what is missing or too broad: menu items no privilege grants, privileges and duties nobody gets, over-granting, license upgrades hidden in View privileges, references to objects that do not exist, and data entities without permissions. It runs on the metadata, so you find these problems before a user reports "I cannot open this form" after a deployment. Visual Studio's best practice checks cover part of this per element; this check looks across the whole security chain.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After you add menu items, privileges, duties, role extensions or data entities to a model.
  • Before a deployment: the Pre-Deploy Checklist runs this check and treats errors as blocking.
  • When you review someone else's security changes (see Review My Changes).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). No sign-in or database.
  • The models you want to check. By default your models (the models in the custom metadata folder) are selected.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the check:
  2. Security View title bar: the checklist button (Find Security Gaps);
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Security > Find Security Gaps…;
  4. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Find Security Gaps.
  5. Pick the models to check. The list shows every model; your models are already selected. You can select several.
  6. The result opens in the security panel, titled Security gaps: <models>.

Findings are grouped by severity: Errors, Warnings and Information, each with its count. Each group is a table:

Column Meaning Object The element with the problem; click it to open it. Type Its element type. Check The finding kind (see below). Message What is wrong and what it means for users.

Rows have a red, yellow or blue bar for errors, warnings and information. When nothing is found the panel says "No gaps found."

Copy as Markdown and Export… in the panel header copy or save the result (default file name security-gaps.md).

docs.title: The checks
docs.text:
Only elements in the selected models are checked. References are resolved against every package, so a menu item of your model granted by a privilege in another model counts as granted.

Check Severity Object Finds Message UngrantedMenuItem Error Menu item A display, output or action menu item that no privilege (in any package) has as an entry point. No privilege grants this menu item: users without System administrator cannot open it. MissingEntryPoint Error Privilege A menu item entry point that names a menu item that does not exist. Entry point <type> <name> does not exist. MissingPrivilege Error Duty A duty that lists a privilege that does not exist. Privilege <name> does not exist. MissingDuty Error Role A role of the selected models, or a role extension of the selected models, that adds a duty that does not exist. Standard roles are checked only for duties your role extensions add. Duty <name> does not exist (added by <extension>). OrphanPrivilege Warning Privilege A privilege that is in no duty and no role (duty and role extensions count). The privilege is in no duty or role, so nobody gets it. EmptyPrivilege Warning Privilege A privilege with no entry points, no data entity permissions and no table permissions. The privilege grants nothing. OverGrant Warning Privilege A privilege whose name ends with View and grants Create or Delete on a display menu item. A View privilege grants <grant> on <menu item>; View privileges should grant Read only. LicenseUpgrade Warning Privilege A privilege whose name ends with View and grants more than Read on a menu item whose maintain license is higher than its view license. Granting <grant> on <menu item> needs <maintain license> instead of <view license>. OrphanDuty Warning Duty A duty that is in no role (role extensions count). The duty is in no role. The message suggests finding the standard roles that do this job and adding the duty with a role extension. UnsecuredEntity Warning Data entity A data entity of the selected models that no privilege (in any package) has a data entity permission on. No privilege has permissions on this data entity: only System administrator can use it in data management, OData or Excel. OverGrant Information Privilege An action menu item entry point granted Create, Update or Delete. Action menu item <name> is granted <grant>; actions need Invoke (or Delete for delete actions) only.

Within a severity, findings are sorted by object name.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Your model ContosoExtensions has a display menu item ContosoOrderStatus and a privilege ContosoOrderStatusView that grants it with Read, Update, Create and Delete, and the privilege is in no duty. The check reports:

  • Warning OrphanPrivilege on ContosoOrderStatusView: nobody gets the privilege.
  • Warning OverGrant on ContosoOrderStatusView: a View privilege grants Create and Delete.
  • Warning LicenseUpgrade on ContosoOrderStatusView, if the menu item's maintain license is higher than its view license.

The menu item itself is not reported as ungranted, because a privilege grants it. Fix it by setting the View privilege to Read, creating a ContosoOrderStatusMaintain privilege for the other grants, and adding both to duties that roles have.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: None. The models are picked each time.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Command xpp.security.findGaps in src/security/index.ts (findGaps). It calls the server's security language action with op: 'gaps' and the picked models.
  • server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs (Gaps) runs the rules above over the cached security index of all packages. Models are matched by model folder name.
  • The Pre-Deploy Checklist calls the agent tool xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps on the project's model and fails its Security step when there is at least one Error.
  • Copilot agents run the same check with xpp_analyze_security op=gaps; without models the tool checks your custom models (see Agent Tools: Analysis).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The OverGrant (display) and LicenseUpgrade rules rely on the naming convention: they look only at privileges whose name ends with View.
  • Not checked: privileges or sub-roles added directly to a role that do not exist (Analyze License lists them under Missing objects), tables or data entities named in permissions that do not exist, and forms or services without a menu item.
  • Duties added to standard roles are found through role extensions, but a duty that only a role in another, unselected model contains still counts as placed.
  • Metadata only; security configured in the environment (for example roles built in the security configuration form) is not seen.
  • Recent edits may need Refresh Security in the Security View.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix UngrantedMenuItem on a menu item you granted The privilege was saved after the index was built. Click Refresh Security and run the check again. MissingDuty naming a standard duty The duty does not exist in this application version (renamed or removed). Check the name with Open Element; see Upgrade Readiness after a version update. UnsecuredEntity on an entity used only by batch code No privilege grants it; at runtime only System administrator can use it in data management, OData or Excel. Add a privilege with data entity permissions if users or integrations need it. Pre-Deploy Checklist fails on Security At least one Error finding in the model. Run Find Security Gaps on the model and fix the errors.
