docs.title: Find Similar Implementations
docs.text: Find Similar Standard Implementations lists standard Microsoft elements to learn from or reuse. You either point it at an element ("show me standard classes like this one") or describe a task in words ("batch job with contract", "number sequence", "form with the ListPage pattern"). It answers the question every X++ developer asks before writing new code: how does the standard application already do this? Visual Studio has no equivalent; there you would search the Application Explorer by name and read code until you find a good example.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you write a new batch job, report data provider, service, lookup, business event or workflow: find a small standard example of the same framework pattern and follow its structure.
  • When you inherit a custom class and want to see standard classes built the same way (same base class, interfaces, attributes and APIs).
  • When you design a form and want standard forms with the same Design pattern (for example SimpleList or DetailsMaster).
  • As a first step for Copilot: the agents use the same search (xpp_find_examples) before they design code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration (Select Environment).
  • The cross-reference database of the configuration must be reachable. On a UDE, F&O Studio restores it during Connect to Environment. Without it you get The cross-reference database is not available: <reason>.
  • Form pattern searches read the form files from disk the first time (see How it works).

docs.title: For an element
docs.text:
1. Right-click an element in Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view and choose Find Similar Standard Implementations. The command is also in the context menu of the Element Designer root node.
  2. A notification shows Finding implementations like <element>….
  3. A pick list opens. Its title explains what was searched, for example objects sharing the most distinctive references (base class, interfaces, attributes, APIs, tables) with <element>.

For a menu item, F&O Studio compares what the menu item opens (its form, class or report), because a menu item itself references very little. The title then starts with <menu item> opens <target>.

docs.title: For a description, or the element in the editor
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Find Similar Standard Implementations from the Command Palette, or in the Dynamics 365 view open Find and choose Find Similar Standard Implementations….
  2. An input box asks you to describe what you need, for example batch job with contract, number sequence on a new table, form with list page pattern.
  3. If an X++ code view is active, you can leave the box empty: F&O Studio then searches for implementations like the object in the editor.
  4. Press Enter. The pick list title shows how F&O Studio read your text, for example SysOperation controllers (batch jobs with a contract and a service); data contract classes ([DataContract]).

docs.title: The result list
docs.text:
Each entry shows:

Part Content Example Label Element name CustPrepaymentAutoSettlementController Description Element type and model Classes · ApplicationSuite Detail Why it was listed extends SysOperationServiceController (2 methods)

Up to 50 elements are listed, best first. Type in the list to filter by name, type, model or reason. Select an entry to open it: classes open in the X++ Code View, other elements in the Element Designer.

If nothing is found you see No similar standard implementations found for <subject>. followed by the interpretation, which tells you what F&O Studio tried.

docs.title: What a description finds
docs.text:
F&O Studio recognizes framework patterns by key words in your text. Up to three patterns are used per search.

Words in your text What is listed sysoperation, batch, batch job, service operation, controller Classes that extend SysOperationServiceController data contract, contract, parameters class Classes attributed with [DataContract] runbase, dialog Classes that extend RunBaseBatch (legacy; prefer SysOperation for new code) number sequence, numseq Classes that extend NumberSeqApplicationModule business event Classes that extend BusinessEventsBase report, ssrs, data provider, dp class Classes that extend SrsReportDataProviderBase report controller, print management, printmgmt Classes that extend SrsPrintMgmtController ui builder Classes that extend SysOperationAutomaticUIBuilder custom service, web service, service class, json service, entry point Code attributed with [SysEntryPoint] lookup, systablelookup Code that uses SysTableLookup workflow Classes that extend WorkflowDocument chain of command, coc, extension class, extensionof Classes attributed with [ExtensionOf] data event, event handler Data event handlers ([DataEventHandler]) form event Form event handlers ([FormEventHandler]) delegate, subscribes, subscriber Delegate subscribers ([SubscribesTo]) test, unit test, systest Classes that extend SysTestCase query builder, query run, dynamic query Code that uses QueryBuildDataSource feature, feature management, feature flag Code that uses IFeatureMetadata infolog, message, action center Code that uses the Message API multithread, task bundle, batch task, parallel Classes that extend SysOperationServiceBase data entity, entity Data entities with code excel, export to excel Office and Excel integration (ExportToExcelDataEntityContext) email, mail Code that uses SysMailerMessageBuilder file upload, upload, download, file File upload and download (FileUploadTemporaryStorageResult) json, rest, http JSON serialization (FormJsonSerializer)

For these patterns the smallest elements come first (fewest methods): a small, focused example is the easiest to read and copy. The detail shows the method count, for example extends SysOperationServiceController (3 methods).

docs.title: Form patterns
docs.text: When your text names a form Design pattern, forms with that pattern are listed, smallest file first. Recognized patterns: DetailsMaster, DetailsTransaction, ListPage, SimpleList, SimpleListDetails, TableOfContents, Dialog, DropDialog, Lookup, Wizard, Workspace, Operational Workspace, FormPart, FactBox, SimpleDetails, TaskSingle, TaskDouble, HubPart. Write the pattern as one word (simplelist) or as separate words (simple list).

docs.title: Free text
docs.text: When no pattern is recognized, F&O Studio looks for classes whose names contain the most of your words, then for classes with methods whose names contain them. Common words (how, the, create, example, similar...) are ignored, and simple endings are removed (posting becomes post). Up to five words are used. The detail shows name matches <words> or method <name> matches <words>.

docs.title: Similar to an element: how the ranking works
docs.text:
For an element, F&O Studio collects everything the element and its methods reference in the cross-reference database: calls, type references, the base class and attributes. It then finds other elements of the same kind (for example other classes) that use the same targets, and scores each one:

  • Every shared target adds 1 / log(1 + n), where n is the number of elements that use that target. A rare target (a specific framework class) counts much more than a common one.
  • Targets with fewer than 2 or more than 4,000 references in the database, and targets that only one element of that kind uses, are ignored.

The detail of each result shows how many distinctive references it shares, and for the top five results the four rarest shared targets, for example shares 12 distinctive reference(s): SysOperationServiceController, ....

docs.title: What is left out
docs.text:
• Your own models (every model under the custom metadata folder) are never listed: the command finds standard examples.
  • Microsoft test packages (models whose name contains Test) are left out unless your text mentions tests.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for this command. The number of results is fixed at 50 in the command (the agent tool defaults to 15).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/findExamples.ts takes the element from the tree node, or asks for a description, and sends the language action find_examples to the language server process.
  2. CodeIntel.cs passes it to CodeExamples.cs.
  3. CodeExamples opens the cross-reference database (SQL Server, usually (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB) and runs:
  4. for an element: the similarity query over the References and Names tables described above;
  5. for a description: one query per recognized pattern (elements that extend, call, or are attributed with the framework class), then a count of methods per candidate;
  6. for free text: LIKE queries over class and method names.
  7. Form patterns are not in the cross-reference database. F&O Studio scans the Design element of every form file once and caches the result in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\cache\form-patterns.json. The cache is rebuilt when the number of form files or the form folders' timestamps change.
  8. Results from all sources are merged, duplicates removed (best score kept), custom and test models filtered out, and the top results returned with their reason.

Copilot agents call the same search through the xpp_find_examples tool and then read the best results with xpp_read_object. See MCP Agent Tools.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Depends on the cross-reference database. Standard code is fully covered on a UDE (the database ships with the metadata); elements in your models only count after a build with cross-reference data (xpp.build.crossReference).
  • The description search knows the patterns in the table above. Other text falls back to name matching, which finds classes by name only.
  • "Similar to an element" compares elements of the same kind (classes with classes, forms with forms).
  • It lists elements, not methods. Open the element and read it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The cross-reference database is not available: ... The database in the active configuration cannot be opened. Check the environment in Select Environment; on a UDE, rerun the setup in Connect to Environment. Unknown objectType error The element type has no cross-reference folder. Run it on a class, table, form, menu item or another referenced element type. Results are only name matches No pattern word was recognized. Use words from the table above, for example batch job or lookup. First form pattern search is slow Every form file is scanned once. Wait; later searches use the cache. No results for an element of your model The element was not built with cross-reference data. Build with xpp.build.crossReference on, see Build Project and Model.

docs.title: Find Tag References
docs.text: Find Tag References lists every element that carries a given tag. Tags are free-text markers that you set in the Tags property of an element (or of a field or method). Teams use them to group the objects of one feature, change request or work item across models and element types. This is the VS Code version of Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 > Find Tag References command and reads the same cross-reference database.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You tagged the objects of a feature (tables, classes, forms, menu items) and want to see them all in one list.
  • You join a team that tags its changes and want to find every object of a change request.
  • You prepare a release or a review and want the objects of one tag, across all models.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The cross-reference database of the active configuration must be reachable. On a UDE it is restored during Connect to Environment.
  • Tags are recorded in the cross-reference database when the package is built with cross-reference data. For your own models keep the setting xpp.build.crossReference on (the default) and build after you change tags (Build Project and Model).

docs.title: Setting a tag
docs.text: Open the element in the Element Designer. The Tags property is shown in the Data category of the Properties grid, next to Name, as in Visual Studio. Properties of elements in your models can be changed there; standard elements are read-only. Save, then build to update the cross-reference database.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the command:
  2. In the Dynamics 365 view, open Find and choose Find Tag References….
  3. Run F&O Studio: Find Tag References… from the Command Palette.
  4. Type the tag, or a part of it, and press Enter. Leave the box empty to list all tags.
  5. F&O Studio lists the tags whose name contains the text (up to 500, sorted by name):
  6. exactly one match is used directly;
  7. several matches open a pick list titled Tags; pick one;
  8. no match opens an empty list titled No tags found.
  9. A pick list opens with the title <N> element(s) tagged '<tag>'. Each entry shows:
Part Content Example Label Element name ContosoOrderStatus Description Where in the element the tag is, when it is on a member TableFieldString/StatusId Detail Element type and module (package) Tables · ContosoExtensions

The list is sorted by module, then by path. Type to filter by name or member. 5. Select an entry to open the element in the Element Designer.

docs.title: Tips for using tags in a team
docs.text:
These are common practices, not rules that F&O Studio enforces:

  • Agree on a tag format, for example the work item number (CR1234) or a feature code (ContosoCreditCheck), so a filter finds all of them.
  • Tag the elements you create and also the members you add to standard elements through extensions (fields of a table extension, methods of a Chain of Command class), so the tag shows the whole change.
  • Use a common prefix for the team's tags; then an empty or prefix filter lists them all.
  • Combine tags with source control: Show Changed Elements and Review My Changes show your current changes, tags show what belongs to a feature over time.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Builds update the cross-reference database, including the tags of your models.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The command lives in src/d365Tools.ts (findTagReferences). It calls two bridge actions on the metadata server: list_tags with your filter, then tag_references with the chosen tag.
  2. Both actions are registered by the tool router (ToolRouter.cs) as read actions that do not use the metadata API, so they run without waiting for other metadata requests.
  3. XRefQuery.cs queries the cross-reference database:
  4. tags are the entries of the Names table whose path starts with /Tags/;
  5. the references of a tag are the rows of the References table whose target is /Tags/<tag>, with the source path, line and module (up to 1,000 rows).
  6. Source paths use the cross-reference's own element kinds (for example Table/X/TableFieldString/F or Class/X/Method/m). F&O Studio maps them back to element types so that the element can be opened.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Read only: the command does not add or remove tags.
  • It shows what the cross-reference database knows. Tags changed since the last build with cross-reference data are not shown, or shown with their old value.
  • Up to 500 tags per filter and 1,000 references per tag.
  • Selecting an entry opens the whole element in the designer, not the tagged field or method.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix An error about the cross-reference database The database in the active configuration cannot be opened. Check the environment in Select Environment; on a UDE, rerun the setup in Connect to Environment. No tags found No tag contains the text, or your model was not built with cross-reference data. Leave the filter empty to see all tags; build your model with xpp.build.crossReference on. A newly tagged element is missing The model was not built since the tag was set. Build the project or model. Selecting an entry does nothing The element type could not be mapped from the cross-reference path. Open the element by name with Open Element.

docs.title: Form Designer and Preview
docs.text: When you open a form (or a form extension) in the Element Designer, a third pane draws the form the way the Finance and Operations web client shows it: the action pane, the page header, tabs, fast tabs, table of contents, grids, groups and fields. The preview follows the form pattern and the layout properties of the controls, updates when you change a property, and is linked to the node tree: click a control in the preview to select it in the tree, select a node in the tree to show it in the preview. Visual Studio's form designer has a preview pane too; F&O Studio's draws the web client's look.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see what a standard form looks like without opening the web client, for example to find where a field sits before you extend the form.
  • You change layout properties on your own form (Width, Columns, ArrangeMethod, DisplayLength, ...) and want to see the effect immediately.
  • You want to see which controls are hidden, which ones extensions added, and which ones depend on a configuration key.
  • You want to find a control in a large form tree: click it in the preview.

To add fields and groups to a standard form through a form extension, use the form layout view instead: Form Layout and Form Extensions.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). The preview is drawn from local metadata only; it does not call the environment.
  • Changing the form needs the form to be in one of your own models. Standard forms are read-only in the designer.

docs.title: Opening the form designer
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer or the project view, click a form, or right-click it > Open Designer.
  2. The designer opens with the node tree, the Properties grid and, on the right, the preview.

A form extension (for example CustGroup.ContosoExtensions) opens the same way. Its preview shows the base form with all its extensions merged.

docs.title: Working with the preview
docs.text:
• Click a control in the preview: the tree expands to it and selects it, and the Properties grid shows its properties.
  • Select a node in the tree: the preview highlights the control and scrolls to it. When the control is on a tab page that is not shown, in a closed fast tab, on another action pane tab or in the details view of a details form, the preview switches there first.
  • Click a tab header, action pane tab or fast tab header: the preview switches tab or opens and closes the fast tab, and selects that page in the tree.
  • Menu buttons and drop dialog buttons open their list below them, as in the web client. A drop dialog without items shows "Opens as a drop dialog". Click elsewhere to close the list.
  • Details forms (patterns Details Master and Details Transaction) open on the list (grid) view, as the web client does. Click the link in the first grid column, or double-click the list, to open the details view. The back button or the form name link in the header returns to the list.

    • The other toolbar buttons (Edit or Save, search, More, Office, attachments, refresh, open in new window) are drawn for the look only; they do nothing.

docs.title: Show hidden controls and markers
docs.text:
The check box Show hidden controls and markers at the top of the preview:

  • shows controls whose Visible is No (dimmed);
  • outlines controls added by extensions with a green dashed line;
  • outlines controls that a configuration key controls with an amber dotted line (amber dashed when both apply).

Hovering any control shows a tooltip with its name and, when it applies, "added by " and "configuration key ". The web client hides a control whose configuration key is off in the environment; the preview only marks these, because whether a key is on is environment data.

When you select a hidden control in the tree while the check box is off, the preview shows that control and its parents dimmed so you can find it.

docs.title: Changing the form
docs.text: On a form of your own model, change properties in the Properties grid. After every property change the tree and the preview are reloaded, so the drawing follows your edit. Node operations (New, Rename, Duplicate, Move Up/Down, Delete, drag and drop) work as described in Element Designer. Undo a property change with Ctrl+Z.

docs.title: How the preview lays out a form
docs.text: The preview applies the web client's layout rules. Knowing them helps you predict what a property change does.

docs.title: Page
docs.text:
• The action pane sits at the top as a card: a toolbar row with Back, then Edit (read mode) or Save (other forms with a data source, except dialogs), then the buttons placed directly on the action pane, then the action pane tabs. Without tabs, an Options tab is drawn. The active tab's button groups are shown below in a flyout, each group with its caption.
  • Command buttons without a label show the web client's caption for their command: New, Delete, Save, Refresh, Edit, Copy, Paste, Print, Find. Menu item buttons without a label show the menu item's label.
  • The page header shows the form caption and a "Standard view" selector. List pages, simple lists and details forms put the caption above the view selector (the details view shows the form name as a link back to the list); other forms put the view selector above the caption.
  • Forms with a Details pattern open in read mode (fields read, underlined); other forms open in edit mode (fields boxed).
  • A group with style DetailTitleContainer is the record title of details forms and is not drawn in the body.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
A tab control is drawn by its Style: FastTabs, VerticalTabs, Tabs or Panorama. When the style is Auto, the form pattern decides:

Pattern Tab at the top levels is drawn as Table of Contents Vertical tabs (a navigation list on the left) Details Master, Simple Details, Details Transaction Fast tabs Others Tabs; deeper tabs whose pages hold only groups and tabs become fast tabs
  • Fast tabs: only the first one is open, as in the web client. Closed fast tabs show their summary fields in the header (controls with FastTabSummary = Yes), drawn as -- because the preview has no data.
  • Table of contents: the vertical tab's pages show their fast tabs as sections of a white panel.
  • On details forms, the main tab with a DetailsFormGrid page and a DetailsFormDetails page (or the transaction variants) switches between list and details view instead of showing tab headers.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
• A group's caption shows when it has a label and its FrameType is not None.
  • Child groups side by side: when every child of a group is a container (group, tab, grid, ...) and the group's Columns is Auto (-1) or more than 1, the children sit next to each other and wrap. With Columns = 1 they stack.
  • ArrangeMethod: HorizontalLeft, HorizontalRight and HorizontalWrap put every child in one row (HorizontalRight aligns them right; only HorizontalWrap wraps). Vertical is the default and changes nothing.
  • A group of fields with Columns greater than 1 flows its fields into that many columns.
  • A tab page whose children are all containers also lays them out side by side.
  • A group bound to a table field group (DataGroup) and without child controls shows the field group's fields.
  • A group with style CustomFilter is the list page filter row: quick filter and filter fields side by side.
  • With markers on, an empty group shows "empty".

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The field drawing follows the bound table field (or the control type when the control is not bound):

Field Drawn as Enum NoYes (or boolean) Toggle with "No" Other enums, combo boxes Drop-down Integer and real Number box Int64 (reference), reference groups, segmented entries Box with a drop-down arrow Date, date-time Box with a calendar icon Text Text box; multi-line text (MultiLine = Yes or DisplayHeight > 1) is DisplayHeight lines high (3 when not set)
  • The field label is the control's label, else the table field's label, else its EDT's (following Extends), else its enum's. ShowLabel = No hides it.
  • DisplayLength (with DisplayLengthMode Fixed) sets the width: about 7.4 pixels per character plus padding.
  • Alignment Right or Center aligns the value.
  • Controls bind to derived data sources (table inheritance) and referenced data sources by name; labels resolve through them.

docs.title: Size properties
docs.text:
• WidthMode Manual with Width, and HeightMode Manual with Height, are pixels.
  • WidthMode SizeToAvailable fills the space left in the container.
  • Defaults are left out: Width/Height count only in Manual mode, DisplayLength only in Fixed mode.

docs.title: Grids
docs.text: A grid draws its columns (labels as above, numbers right-aligned) and placeholder rows. The first column looks like the record link. VisibleRows (with VisibleRowsMode Fixed) sets the number of rows, up to 30; a grid with HeightMode SizeToAvailable shows 8 rows; otherwise 4. List views and trees are drawn like grids.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The preview has no settings. The Show hidden controls and markers check box is per preview and is not saved.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The preview is media/formPreview.js with media/formPreview.css. The same script draws the preview in the form layout view (media/designer.js). Sizes, fonts and colours were measured on a live web client page (light theme).
  • The element designer (src/elementDesigner.ts) loads the element tree and, for forms and form extensions, the bridge action get_form_tree for the base form.
  • get_form_tree (MetaModelBridge.Designer.cs) builds the effective form: copies of the base form and of every form extension are merged with D365FO's extension merger (MetaModelBridge.FormExtensions.cs). It returns the caption, pattern, extension names, data sources (with the extension that added them) and the control tree, at most 3,000 controls.
  • Per control the server adds what the drawing needs (MetaModelBridge.FormRender.cs): the resolved label, the field kind, the fields of a bound field group, style, columns, frame type, show label, visible, command, fast tab summary, configuration key (the control's own, else its menu item's), the extension that added it, and only the non-default size and arrangement properties.
  • Labels are resolved from the en-US label text files and cached per file with its write time, so a label you create shows its text right away.
  • Clicking in the preview sends the control name to the tree; form control names are unique in a form.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The preview is a drawing, not a running form. There is no data, no lookups, no code, and the toolbar buttons do nothing.
  • Configuration keys are marked, not evaluated.
  • Form parts, custom controls and other control types the preview does not know are drawn as a box with their type and caption.
  • Only en-US label texts are shown.
  • Forms with more than 3,000 controls are cut off.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No preview pane The element is not a form or form extension, or get_form_tree failed Check the designer's error line; refresh with Refresh Designer A control is missing from the preview Its Visible is No Turn on Show hidden controls and markers, or select the control in the tree A field shows an @... reference instead of text The label file or label was not found in en-US Check the label in the Label Editor The preview did not change after a property edit The edit failed (see the error line) or the property is not one the preview draws Check the message; see the layout rules above

docs.title: Form Layout and Form Extensions
docs.text: The form layout view shows a form with every extension merged into it: an outline of all controls, the web client preview, and a small properties panel. From it you add fields and groups to a form and hide, show or relabel existing controls. Changes to a standard form go into a form extension in your project's model (<Form>.<YourModel>), which F&O Studio creates and adds to your project the first time. It is the counterpart of opening a form extension in Visual Studio's designer, but you start from the form and see the merged result.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need to add a field from a form data source to a standard form, after a given control or at the end of a group, tab page or the design.
  • You need a new group (for example a field group for your new fields) on a standard form.
  • You want to hide a standard control, show a hidden one, or give a control a different label, without touching the standard form.
  • You want to see which extensions already change a form and which controls each one added, before you add your own.

For full control over a form extension (data sources, every control property, methods, events) open the extension itself in the Element Designer.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD).
  • A D365FO project (.rnrproj) is open. Its model receives the form extension. Without a project you see "Open a D365FO project (.rnrproj) so changes go into a form extension in its model."
  • The form is not in your project's model. For a form of your own model the view refuses with " is in your own model; edit it directly. The designer only writes extensions for now." Edit such a form in the Element Designer.
  • If you extend data, add the table fields first (for example with a table extension; see Create Extension). The field picker lists the fields of the table and all its table extensions.

docs.title: Opening the form layout
docs.text:
Place How Application Explorer or project view Right-click a form > Open Form Layout… Element designer of a form or form extension Form Layout in the editor title, or right-click the element node > Open Form Layout… Command Palette F&O Studio: Open Form Layout…, then type the form name

From a form extension, the view opens the base form (CustGroup.ContosoExtensions opens CustGroup). One tab per form, titled <Form> [Design]; it comes back after a window reload.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Toolbar: the form name, its model, "(read-only, changes go to a form extension)" for forms outside your models, the number and names of the form's extensions, and Refresh.
  • Outline (left): every control of the merged form, with its name and type. Controls added by an extension are shown in green with a dashed outline; their tooltip says "Added by ". Controls whose Visible is No are dimmed. Click the arrow to collapse or expand a container.
  • Preview (middle): the web client drawing described in Form Designer and Preview, including Show hidden controls and markers. Clicking a control selects it in the outline.
  • Properties (right): for the selected control: Type, Label, Data source, Data field, Field group, Visible, Added by ((base form) for standard controls) and the number of children, followed by the action buttons.

docs.title: Adding fields
docs.text:
1. Select where the fields go:
  2. select a container (the design, a group, a tab page...) to add the fields at its end; the button reads Add fields inside…;
  3. select a control that is not a container to add the fields right after it; the button reads Add fields after….
  4. Click the button.
  5. Pick the data source the fields are bound to. Data sources added by extensions say "added by ".
  6. Pick one or more fields of that data source's table (including fields of table extensions). Each entry shows the field type, the EDT or enum, and the label. The list filters on all of these.
  7. F&O Studio places one control per field, named <DataSource>_<Field> (a number is added when the name is taken), in the order you picked them.
  8. The status bar shows "Added N field(s) in " and the view reloads with the new controls marked as added by your extension.

docs.title: Adding a group
docs.text:
1. Select a container (group added at its end) or a control (group added after it).
  2. Click Add group inside… or Add group after….
  3. Enter the group name (letters, digits and _).
  4. Enter the caption: plain text or a label reference such as @ContosoLabels:OrderDetails. Leave it empty for no caption.
  5. The group is added. Select it and use Add fields inside… to fill it.

docs.title: Hiding, showing and relabelling controls
docs.text:
Select any control except the design:

  • Hide sets Visible to No in your extension; Show (on a hidden control) sets it back to Yes.
  • Change label… asks for the new label: text or a label reference (@File:Id). It is saved as a control modification in your extension.

The note under the buttons reminds you: "Changes are saved to the form extension . in your project."

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
You want the customer group form CustGroup to show a new field ContosoReviewRequired that a table extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions adds:

  1. Open Open Form Layout… on CustGroup.
  2. In the outline, select the grid (or the group) where the field belongs.
  3. Add fields inside… > data source CustGroup > field ContosoReviewRequired.
  4. The control CustGroup_ContosoReviewRequired appears in green. The form extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions (named after your project's model) is created in your model and added to your project.
  5. Build the model (see Build Project and Model).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The form layout view has no settings. The target model is the model of the active project (see D365FO Projects).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The view is src/designer.ts with the webview media/designer.js and the shared preview media/formPreview.js.
  • It loads the merged form with bridge action get_form_tree. The server reads the base form and every form extension named <Form>.*, works on copies, and merges them with D365FO's extension merger, recording which extension added each control and data source (MetaModelBridge.FormExtensions.cs, MetaModelBridge.Designer.cs). Extensions that cannot be read show as warnings.
  • Field pickers use get_table_fields, which returns the table's fields plus the fields of all its table extensions.
  • Changes are sent as an object update: controls (new controls with parent, position end or after and previous sibling) or controlModifications (Visible, Label). The first change creates the extension with create_object for AxFormExtension in the project's model and adds it to the project with add_to_project; later changes use update_object. These are the same bridge actions the agent tools xpp_create_object and xpp_update_object use.
  • When several fields are added after a control, each one is sent separately so that each anchors on the one before; fields added at the end of a container go in one request.
  • On the server, a form extension update:
  • checks the placement before anything is written: the parent exists and can contain controls, the previous sibling is a direct child of the parent, names are unique in the whole form, data sources and fields exist (a group bound to a field group gets one control per field);
  • sets the property values the form's patterns require for the new controls;
  • saves through the metadata provider;
  • runs the compiler's form extension checks and, if the change introduces an error the build would report, restores the previous version and refuses with the build's message;
  • re-applies all extensions with D365FO's applier and verifies that each control landed where requested.
  • Errors the form already had before your change are reported but do not block it.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The view writes only form extensions. It does not change forms of your own model, and it does not remove, move or rename existing controls; use the Element Designer on your extension for that.
  • New controls are added at the end of a container or after a control; to put one at the beginning, use the extension's designer or an agent with xpp_update_object.
  • Only Visible and Label are changed from this view. Other properties of base controls are changed in the extension's designer.
  • The extension name is always <Form>.<ProjectModel>. To write into another existing extension, open it in the element designer.
  • The preview does not evaluate configuration keys (see Form Designer and Preview).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Open a D365FO project (.rnrproj) so changes go into a form extension in its model." No active project Open or select a project (D365FO Projects) " is in your own model; edit it directly. The designer only writes extensions for now." The form belongs to your project's model Edit it in the Element Designer "Form extension not saved. Fix these and retry ..." with a list The placement check failed (parent not found, not a container, sibling under another parent, name already used, field not found...) Select another target, or rename; refresh the view if other extensions changed "Form extension not saved (previous version kept): with this change the build would report: ..." The change breaks a form pattern or another compiler check Put the control in a container whose pattern allows it; read the reported pattern rule "Saved AxFormExtension ..., but the placement check failed" The merge put a control somewhere other than requested Check the outline; move the control in the extension's designer The field you need is not in the field list The table extension that adds it is not saved or not in the metadata yet Create the field first, then Refresh "The form is still loading." An action was clicked before the tree loaded Wait and retry

docs.title: Formatting and Folding
docs.text: Format Document lays out X++ code the way Visual Studio's X++ editor does: four-space indentation and Allman braces (each { and } on its own line). Format Selection fixes the indentation of the selected lines. Folding collapses methods, statement blocks, case sections, comments and // region blocks. Syntax colouring comes from a TextMate grammar, and optional semantic highlighting colours names by what they are.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Clean up code pasted from elsewhere, or code written by an agent, before you commit it.
  • Re-indent a block after you moved it into an if or a while select.
  • Hide the methods you are not working on in a long class such as SalesFormLetter.
  • Group related methods with // region comments and fold them.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An X++ document: a code view, an .xpp file or an untitled X++ editor.
  • Formatting changes the text only; to keep it in a standard element you need the element to be in your model (the code view of a standard element is read-only).
  • xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting on (the default) for formatting. Folding is always on.

docs.title: Format Document
docs.text:
1. Open the code.
  2. Run Format Document (right-click in the editor, or the command palette).
  3. The whole document is reformatted as one edit; undo it with Ctrl+Z.

What changes:

  • an opening brace at the end of a line moves to its own line:
// before
if (custGroup.RecId) {
    info("Found");
} else {
    warning("Not found");
}

// after
if (custGroup.RecId)
{
    info("Found");
}
else
{
    warning("Not found");
}
  • } else, } catch and } finally are split so the brace stands alone;
  • every line is re-indented with four spaces per level; tab characters in a re-indented line become four spaces;
  • case and default: labels sit one level inside switch, and their statements one level below the label;
  • a statement that continues on the next line (for example a where clause of a select, or a condition without braces) is indented one extra level;
  • trailing whitespace is removed and blank lines are kept (empty).

What does not change:

  • text inside strings (including multi-line @"..." and @'...' verbatim strings) and comments, apart from tab characters as noted above;
  • lines that start inside a multi-line string or a block comment;
  • the order of the code, spaces inside a line, line breaks other than around braces, and blank lines.

If the document is already formatted, nothing happens.

You can also use VS Code's Format on Save (editor.formatOnSave) for X++.

docs.title: Format Selection
docs.text:
1. Select lines.
  2. Run Format Selection.
  3. Only the indentation of the selected lines changes. Braces are not moved.

The indentation of a line depends on the lines above it, so F&O Studio indents the whole document and keeps only the selected lines.

docs.title: Folding
docs.text:
Fold with the arrows in the gutter, or with VS Code's Fold, Unfold, Fold All and Fold All Regions commands. Foldable ranges:

Range Folded from Notes Brace block (method, if, while, switch, try...) The header line An Allman block collapses to if (x) …; a brace alone on its line belongs to the statement above if ... } else The if header to the line before } } else stays visible when the if block is folded case and default: section The label line Ends before the next label or the end of the switch; trailing blank lines are left out Block comment /* ... */ The first line Folded as a comment (Fold All Block Comments) Two or more // lines in a row The first line Doc comments (///) too // region Name ... // endregion The region line Also // #region and // #endregion; regions can nest

Example:

// region Validation
public boolean validateWrite()
{
    boolean ret = super();
    return ret;
}
// endregion

docs.title: Syntax colouring
docs.text: The grammar colours comments (line, block and /// doc comments), strings (double-quoted, single-quoted and verbatim), attributes, label references (@SYS7149, @File:Id), numbers, keywords (control flow, SQL keywords such as select, firstonly, where, modifiers and operators) and primitive types.

docs.title: Semantic highlighting
docs.text:
Turn on xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting to colour names by what they are: classes, tables (and views, data entities, maps), enums, EDTs, methods, fields and enum values. Your colour theme decides the colours.

It is off by default because it looks up every capitalized name of three or more letters in the open document (up to 200 distinct names per document) in the metadata.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting true Format Document and Format Selection for X++ xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting false Semantic highlighting (slow) editor.formatOnSave (VS Code) false Format on save; scope it to X++ with "[xpp]": { "editor.formatOnSave": true }

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• src/codeIntel/formatter.ts: formatXpp first splits braces (splitBraces), then reindent walks the lines once. A small scanner (codeOf) blanks strings and drops comments so braces inside them don't count, and tracks multi-line block comments and verbatim strings. A stack of open blocks (block or switch) gives the depth; a line that doesn't end with ;, {, }, : or ] (and is not a # preprocessor line or a case label) makes the next line a continuation.
  • src/codeIntel/folding.ts: foldingRanges uses the same scanner, a stack of brace starts, open case sections per depth, block comments, runs of line comments and region markers. When two ranges start on the same line, the outer one is kept.
  • The providers are registered in src/codeIntel/providers.ts for the xpp language in xpp: code views, files and untitled editors.
  • The grammar is syntaxes/xpp.tmLanguage.json (scope source.xpp).
  • language-configuration.json sets // and /* */ comments (so Toggle Line Comment works), bracket pairs, auto-closing of brackets, quotes and /* */, region markers, and the indentation rules for typing (indent after {, outdent on }).
  • Semantic highlighting runs in the extension: it classifies names by their position (after ::, after ., before (), then looks up candidate type names with the bridge action find_object (cached).

The formatter and the folding are plain text functions with no server call. node scripts/source-test.js in the repository tests the source parsing and the formatter (see Testing the Extension).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The formatter changes indentation and brace placement only. It does not align declarations, wrap long lines, change spacing around operators or sort methods.
  • Saving a code view doesn't format it unless you turn on editor.formatOnSave: the code view saves with formatCode: false, so your layout is kept.
  • Formatting a standard element's code view can't be saved (read-only).
  • Semantic highlighting looks up at most 200 distinct names per document.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Format Document does nothing xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting is off, or the code is already formatted Turn the setting on "There is no formatter for 'xpp' files installed" or another formatter runs Another extension is the default formatter Set "[xpp]": { "editor.defaultFormatter": "MNazmi.xpp-vscode" } A region doesn't fold The end marker is missing or misspelled Use // endregion (or // #endregion) Names are not coloured as classes or tables Semantic highlighting is off (default) Turn on xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting

docs.title: Generate SysTest Class
docs.text: Generate SysTest Class creates a unit test class for an X++ class: a SysTestCase subclass with one test method per public method, each laid out as Arrange, Act and Assert. The variant Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL) also creates test data (customers, vendors, items, warehouses, sites) with Microsoft's Acceptance Test Library and adds the model references it needs. Visual Studio has no generator for X++ tests; you write the class from scratch.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You wrote a class and want a test skeleton for every public method in one step.
  • You want to start testing an existing class and need a structure to fill in.
  • The class works with customers, vendors, items, warehouses or sites and you want test records without writing the setup code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The class to test must exist and have at least one public method (other than new, classDeclaration and main).
  • The test class is created in your project's model, or in one of your models that you pick.
  • For the ATL variant, your model must reference the packages AtlFoundation and AtlApplicationSuite. F&O Studio offers to add them.
  • To run the tests you need Run Tests or the Test Explorer. On a UDE tests run against the deployed code, so deploy first.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the command:
  2. Right-click a class in Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view and choose Generate SysTest Class or Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL).
  3. Right-click the root node of a class in the Element Designer and choose Generate SysTest Class.
  4. Run F&O Studio: Generate SysTest Class or F&O Studio: Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL) from the Command Palette. If a class is open in the code view, that class is used; otherwise you type part of a class name and pick the class.
  5. If you have no active project, pick the model for the test class.
  6. Enter the test class name. The default is <Class>Test. The name must not exist yet.
  7. For the ATL variant, if your model lacks the ATL references, a message says <model> needs references to AtlFoundation and AtlApplicationSuite to use the Acceptance Test Library. Click Add References to add them to the model (see Models and Model Dependencies).
  8. F&O Studio creates the class, adds it to the project and opens it in the code view. The status bar shows Created <TestClass> with N test method(s). Fill in the expected values, then run it with Run Tests.
  9. Fill in the expected values and the checks, build, and run the tests.

docs.title: The class
docs.text:
[SysTestTarget(classStr(ContosoCreditCheck), UtilElementType::Class)]
public final class ContosoCreditCheckTest extends SysTestCase
{
}

The SysTestTarget attribute links the test class to the class under test.

docs.title: One test method per public method
docs.text:
For each public method of the class itself (not inherited ones), a method test<MethodName> with the [SysTestMethod] attribute. When two methods would get the same name, a number is added (testPost2).

  • Arrange
  • For an instance method, the object under test: <Class>::construct() when the class has a public static construct() without parameters, otherwise new <Class>().
  • A local variable for each parameter, named after the parameter without the leading _. Parameters with a default value get it; boolean, int, int64, real and str get a sample value (true, 1, 1, 1.0, "Test"); other types are declared without a value.
  • For methods that return a primitive type, a variable expected for you to fill in.
  • Act: the call, with the result stored in result when the method returns a value.
  • Assert
  • void methods: a comment where you check the side effects.
  • Primitive return types (int, str, boolean, date, real, utcdatetime, container, guid, RecId and similar): this.assertEquals(expected, result, '<method> returns the expected value');
  • Other return types (tables, classes, EDTs, enums): this.assertNotNull(result, '<method> returns a value');. Types are recognized by name, so a method returning an EDT such as CustAccount gets assertNotNull; change it to assertEquals when you compare values.

Example for a class with the method public boolean isOnHold(CustAccount _accountNum):

[SysTestMethod]
public void testIsOnHold()
{
    // Arrange
    ContosoCreditCheck target = ContosoCreditCheck::construct();
    CustAccount accountNum;
    boolean expected;

    // Act
    boolean result = target.isOnHold(accountNum);

    // Assert
    this.assertEquals(expected, result, 'isOnHold returns the expected value');
}

docs.title: With test data (ATL)
docs.text:
The ATL variant reads the source of the class and looks for these table names. For each one found, every test method gets a record from the Acceptance Test Library:

Table in the class's code Variable Expression CustTable customer data.cust().customers().default().record() VendTable vendor data.vend().vendors().default().record() InventTable item data.products().items().default() InventLocation warehouse data.invent().warehouses().default() InventSite site data.invent().sites().default()

A parameter of one of these types is passed the ATL variable instead of an empty local. The class also gets a member AtlDataRootNode data; and a setUp method:

/// <summary>
/// Test data from the Acceptance Test Library, created in the test's transaction and rolled back after it.
/// </summary>
public void setUp()
{
    super();
    data = AtlDataRootNode::construct();
}

Example for public boolean isOnHold(CustTable _custTable) in a class whose code uses CustTable:

[SysTestMethod]
public void testIsOnHold()
{
    // Arrange
    CustTable customer = data.cust().customers().default().record();
    ContosoCreditCheck target = ContosoCreditCheck::construct();
    boolean expected;

    // Act
    boolean result = target.isOnHold(customer);

    // Assert
    this.assertEquals(expected, result, 'isOnHold returns the expected value');
}

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings. The test class name is asked each time.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/generateTests.ts gets the class from the tree node, the code view or a picker.
  2. It reads the class's members with the bridge action type_members and keeps public methods owned by the class. Method headers are parsed to get parameters, default values and the return type.
  3. For the ATL variant it reads the class source (read_object) to find the table names, and the model's references (get_model); Add References calls update_model.
  4. It checks that the test class name is free (find_object), builds the declaration and the methods, and creates the class with create_object through the metadata API, then add_to_project.
  5. The new class opens in the X++ Code View.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Classes only. Tables, forms and other element types are not supported.
  • The generated tests compile but test nothing until you fill in the expected values and assertions.
  • Protected, private and inherited methods get no test.
  • ATL data covers five tables only, with the library's default records.
  • Non-primitive parameters (other than the ATL tables) are declared but not created; set them up yourself.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Tests can be generated for classes only. The element is not a class. Run it on a class. <class> has no public methods to test. All methods are protected, private, inherited, or new/main. Add public methods, or write tests by hand. Class <name> already exists. Choose another name. The test class name is taken. Enter another name. Build errors about AtlDataRootNode The model does not reference the ATL packages. Run the ATL variant again and click Add References, or add AtlFoundation and AtlApplicationSuite in Models and Model Dependencies.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: F&O Studio for VS Code lets you develop Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365FO) X++ code in VS Code, without Visual Studio. It works on unified developer environments (UDE), cloud-hosted environments (CHE) and VHD environments, and uses the same metadata API, compiler and scripts as Visual Studio, so projects and models open in both tools. This page takes you from installing the extension to your first build, your first data query and your first Copilot request.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need Why Windows F&O Studio runs Microsoft's D365FO tools (metadata API, xppc, LabelC), which are Windows only VS Code 1.101 or later The minimum version the extension declares A D365FO development environment A unified developer environment, or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment SQL Server LocalDB For the cross-reference database (where-used, rename, references diagrams) GitHub Copilot (optional) Only for the Copilot agents and the agent tools Power Platform CLI pac (optional) Only for the two (pac) commands. Deploy and database sync do not need it C# extension (cloud-hosted and VHD only) The debugger on a local AOS uses its .NET debugger. F&O Studio offers to install it

On a unified developer environment you also need about 16 GB of free disk space for the standard metadata, and an account that can sign in to the environment's Dataverse organization.

On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, run VS Code as administrator, as Visual Studio does, so builds can write into PackagesLocalDirectory.

F&O Studio never ships Microsoft's D365FO assemblies. It loads them from your own installation at run time: from the metadata it downloads on a UDE, or from PackagesLocalDirectory on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment.

docs.title: Step 1: install the extension
docs.text:
1. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X) in VS Code.
  2. Search for F&O Studio for VS Code (publisher MNazmi, ID MNazmi.xpp-vscode) and select Install.
  3. An F&O Studio icon appears in the activity bar. Select it to open the F&O Studio views.

The extension starts when VS Code has finished starting, when a workspace contains a .rnrproj file, or when you open an X++ code view.

The Get started with F&O Studio walkthrough (Help > Welcome, or Welcome: Open Walkthrough... in the Command Palette) has the same steps as this page, with buttons that run each command.

docs.title: Unified developer environment
docs.text:
A UDE runs in the cloud; your machine needs a copy of the standard metadata, the compiler and the cross-reference database. Connect to Environment… does what Visual Studio's Connect to Dataverse does.

  1. Open the Dynamics 365 view in the F&O Studio side bar and expand Environment, then select Connect to Environment…. Or run F&O Studio: Connect to Environment… from the Command Palette.
  2. Enter the environment's Dataverse URL, for example https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com. You find it as "Environment URL" in the Power Platform admin center. You can also paste the environment's web client URL (https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com); F&O Studio looks up the matching Dataverse URL.
  3. Sign in when VS Code asks. F&O Studio uses VS Code's Microsoft account sign-in.
  4. Watch the six steps in the Environment group of the Dynamics 365 view and in the notification:
  5. Sign in to Dataverse
  6. Check SQL Server LocalDB
  7. Download metadata and tools
  8. Extract PackagesLocalDirectory
  9. Restore cross-reference database
  10. Configure this machine
  11. When it finishes you see "Environment connected. The Application Explorer, designers and code views now use it."

If a step fails, the notification says "Environment setup failed: ..." with Retry, Show Log and Report Problem. Retry also appears in the Environment group. See Troubleshooting.

Before a long download you can run Check Environment Connection: it signs in and runs every read-only step of the setup (environment type, versions, download links) and writes the result to the X++ output.

The setup writes the same configuration Visual Studio reads, so Visual Studio on the same machine can use it too. See Connect-to-Environment and Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: Cloud-hosted or VHD environment
docs.text: There is nothing to set up. F&O Studio uses the local PackagesLocalDirectory, AOS and AxDB. UDE-only commands (Deploy Models to Environment, Run Tests, the (pac) commands) are hidden. See Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments.

docs.title: Several environments
docs.text: You can connect several UDEs. Select Environment… (or the environment name in the status bar) switches between them without a reload, and each workspace remembers its own environment. See Select-Environment.

docs.title: Step 3: pick your starting point
docs.text:
A project is optional. The Application Explorer and the agent tools work without one.

You want to Do this Work on your team's code Open Team Repository… clones or picks a repository, links its packages into the metadata folder and builds them in dependency order. See Open-Team-Repository Open an existing project Open D365FO Project… (or Open Recent D365FO Project…) in the D365FO Project view. See D365FO-Projects Start a new project Create D365FO Project… writes a .rnrproj and a .slnx, as Visual Studio does Create a model first Create Model… in the Dynamics 365 view under Create. See Models-and-Model-Dependencies Just look around Use the Application Explorer

Opening a project opens its own workspace with the project folder and its model folder. New elements go into the project's model.

docs.title: Step 4: find your way around
docs.text:
• Application Explorer lists every model's elements, like Visual Studio's. Switch between the classic view (elements by type) and the model view (elements by model) with the buttons at the top. See Application-Explorer.
  • Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O) finds any element by name. A prefix narrows the type: t:cust finds tables, c: classes, f: forms. See Open-Element.
  • Click a class to open its code; click a label file to open the label editor; click any other element to open its designer. Right-click for everything else: Find References, Create Extension, Create Code Extension, View Hierarchy, Browse Table Data and more. See Element-Designer and X++ code view.
  • In code, F12 goes to a definition, Shift+F12 finds references and Ctrl+F12 lists implementations, including Chain of Command extensions and event handlers. See Go-to-Definition and Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command.
  • The Dynamics 365 view groups the commands of Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 menu by task. Every command is listed in the Command-Reference.

docs.title: Step 5: create and build
docs.text:
1. In the D365FO Project view, select + (New Element…) and pick an element type, or a wizard such as New Batch Job (SysOperation)…. See New-Element.
  2. To change a standard element, right-click it in the Application Explorer and choose Create Extension (metadata) or Create Code Extension (Chain of Command). See Create-Extension and Create-Code-Extension.
  3. Build with Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ code view, or select the project name in the status bar. Unsaved code views are saved first. Builds use xppc and LabelC, the compilers Visual Studio uses.
  4. Errors and warnings go to the Problems view, on the right line of the code view. When a build fails, the notification offers Show Problems and Show Output (the full compiler log in the X++ Build output).

See Build-Project-and-Model and Compiler-Diagnostics.

docs.title: Step 6: deploy, test and debug
docs.text:
Environment Deploy Tests Debug Unified developer environment Deploy Models to Environment uploads your packages as built on this machine, through the environment's Dataverse, with an optional database sync Run Tests runs SysTest classes on the environment; they also appear in VS Code's Test Explorer Launch Debugger attaches through Microsoft's debugger proxy Cloud-hosted or VHD Not needed: the build goes into the local PackagesLocalDirectory, and the running AOS restarts after a successful build Not available in F&O Studio; run tests from Visual Studio on the VM Launch Debugger attaches to the local AOS with the C# extension's .NET debugger

Tests and the debugger run the code deployed on the environment. When your build is newer than the last deploy, F&O Studio warns you and offers Deploy First. See Deploy-to-Environment, Run-Tests and Debugger.

docs.title: Step 7: look at the data
docs.text:
• Right-click a table and choose Browse Table Data to see its rows, with enum names, a company filter, column filters and a record inspector. See Browse-Table-Data.
  • New SQL Query opens a read-only query panel with Explain Plan. See SQL-Query-Panel.
  • On a UDE, F&O Studio requests temporary database credentials for you (the same request Visual Studio makes); they are kept in VS Code's secret storage until they expire. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment it uses the local AxDB with Windows authentication. See Database-Access.

docs.title: Step 8: ask Copilot
docs.text:
With GitHub Copilot installed, F&O Studio registers its agent tools automatically and adds F&O agents to the chat's agent picker (F&O Developer, Code Reviewer, Support, Functional Explainer and others).

  1. Run F&O Studio: Start Copilot Checkpoint first if you want to be able to undo everything Copilot changes.
  2. Open Copilot Chat in agent mode and pick an F&O agent, or let Copilot suggest one.
  3. Ask, for example:
  4. Create a table extension of CustTable with a field for the customer's loyalty tier, and show it on the CustTable form.
  5. Which roles can open the SalesTable form, and what license do they need?
  6. Why does posting fail with "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in."? Find where the message comes from.
  7. Watch what it does in the Copilot Activity view in the F&O Studio panel.
  8. Keep the changes with End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes), or undo them with Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint….

Agent tools write only to your own models, and every write is all or nothing. See Copilot-Agents, MCP-Agent-Tools and Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

docs.title: What you see in the status bar
docs.text:
Item Shows Click Environment The active environment's name; a warning icon when the environment runs a newer application version Opens the environment menu Database The local database name, or the role and expiry time of temporary UDE credentials; hidden while you have no database access Opens the Database menu Project The active project and the last build result; a cloud icon when the build is newer than the last deploy Builds the project X++ server Only while the metadata loads, or when the server stopped Restarts the server when it stopped Copilot checkpoint An open Copilot checkpoint Opens the checkpoint menu

See Status-Bar.

docs.title: Where to look when something goes wrong
docs.text:
• The X++ output channel has the server and setup log. X++ Build, X++ Deploy and X++ Tests have the build, deploy and test logs.
  • Error notifications offer Show Log and Report Problem.
  • Troubleshooting lists the common messages and their fixes; FAQ answers common questions.

docs.title: Git Changes in the Project View
docs.text: The project view marks every element of your models that differs from Git with Git's own change letter and colour: M modified, A added, D deleted, R renamed. The same marks appear on the tabs of X++ code views. With a base branch set, the marks also include what your branch changed since it left that branch, so you see the whole change set of a pull request in the project, not only what is still uncommitted. Visual Studio's Solution Explorer shows similar source control glyphs on project items.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• While you work: see at a glance which elements of the project you already touched.
  • Before you commit: check that only the elements you meant to change are marked.
  • Before a pull request: with xpp.git.baseBranch set, see every element the branch changed.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project open (Open D365FO Project…), so the project view lists its elements.
  • The project's model in a Git working tree (directly, or through a junction from the custom metadata folder; see Source Control for X++).
  • Git on the PATH.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the project. The project view lists the elements by folder.
  2. Change an element (designer, code view, agent tool) and save it. The element's line gets a coloured letter at its right edge, and the name takes Git's colour for that change:
Letter Meaning Colour (theme) M Modified gitDecoration.modifiedResourceForeground A Added (new file, also when untracked) gitDecoration.addedResourceForeground D Deleted gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground R Renamed gitDecoration.renamedResourceForeground
  1. Hover over the element. The tooltip shows the element type and the change, for example Class · Modified. When the change is only on the branch (already committed), the tooltip ends with on this branch, for example Table · Added on this branch.
  2. Open the element's code view. Its editor tab carries the same letter and colour.
  3. To see every changed element in one list, including those not in the project, run Show Changed Elements from the command palette or the Dynamics 365 view (Model and project). Pick an element to open its designer; deleted elements are listed but do not open. See Show Changed Elements.

docs.title: Uncommitted only, or the whole branch
docs.text:
xpp.git.baseBranch Marked elements empty (default) Uncommitted changes in the working tree: modified, staged, untracked. Once you commit, the mark goes away. main (or another branch) Uncommitted changes, plus every element changed between the merge base of HEAD and main and HEAD. Committed changes stay marked until the branch is merged.

When an element is both changed on the branch and changed again in the working tree, the uncommitted change wins: the letter is the working tree's and the tooltip has no on this branch.

To set the base branch, open the settings (Options… in the Dynamics 365 view) and search for xpp.git.baseBranch, or add it to the workspace settings:

{
  "xpp.git.baseBranch": "main"
}

If the base branch exists only as a remote branch on your machine, use its remote name, for example origin/main.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Branch your work is compared with. Empty: only uncommitted changes. Also used by Show Changed Elements and as the proposed value in Review My Changes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• ChangeDecorations in src/changes.ts is a VS Code file decoration provider. Project view items carry the element's code view URI (xpp: scheme) as their resource, so the same decoration applies to the project item and to the code view tab (src/project.ts).
  • The list of changed elements comes from changedElements(baseBranch):
  • For each of your custom models, resolve the real path of the model folder and find its repository with git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
  • Run git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <model path>. Untracked files (??) count as added; for renames the new path is used.
  • With a base branch: git merge-base HEAD <base>, then git diff --name-status <merge base> HEAD -- <model path>.
  • Keep only paths of the form <AxType>/<Name>.xml directly under the model folder; each becomes an element.
  • The list is refreshed every 30 seconds and each time you save a document. Only items whose mark changed are redrawn.
  • The decorations do not propagate to the folders of the project view (a folder is not marked because one of its elements changed).
  • Elements are matched by type and name. Every element without a change still gets a tooltip with its type.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only elements are marked: the .rnrproj, descriptors, label text files and C# files are not. VS Code's Source Control view and Explorer show those.
  • The Application Explorer does not show change marks; only the project view and code view tabs do.
  • Changing xpp.git.baseBranch takes effect at the next refresh (within 30 seconds, or when you save a file).
  • Elements of standard models are never marked: only custom models in the custom metadata folder are checked.
  • Git only. When a git command fails in a model folder, that model simply gets no marks; no error is shown.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No marks at all The model folder is not in a Git working tree, or git is not on the PATH. Run git rev-parse --show-toplevel in the model folder (or in the folder its junction points to). Install Git or fix the PATH, then reload the window. Committed changes are not marked xpp.git.baseBranch is empty. Set it to the branch you branched from. Committed changes are not marked although the base branch is set git merge-base HEAD <base> fails: the branch name does not exist locally. Use origin/main (or fetch and create the local branch). Marks appear late The list refreshes every 30 seconds or on save. Save the element, or wait for the next refresh. An element shows A but you only edited it The file was never committed (untracked files count as added). Commit it once; afterwards edits show as M.
