docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Terms used in this wiki, in F&O Studio and in Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations development. Where F&O Studio has a page for the term, it is linked.

docs.title: A
docs.text:
• .axpp: The project export file of Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 tools: a zip with the project, the model information and the elements. Export Project… and Import Project… read and write the same format. See Export-and-Import-Projects.

  • Agent tools (MCP tools): The tools F&O Studio's server gives GitHub Copilot through the Model Context Protocol, such as xpp_read_object, xpp_create_object, xpp_find_references and xpp_build. They work through the metadata API and write only to your own models. See MCP-Agent-Tools.

  • AOS (Application Object Server): The Finance and Operations server process that runs X++ code. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment it runs locally (in IIS or IIS Express, plus the batch service); on a unified developer environment it runs in the cloud.

  • AOT (Application Object Tree): The tree of all application elements (tables, classes, forms...). In Visual Studio and F&O Studio it is shown as the Application Explorer.

  • Application Explorer: The view that lists every model's elements, in a classic view (by element type) or a model view (by model). See Application-Explorer.

  • Application version: The version of the Finance and Operations application (for example 10.0.xxxx.xx). The metadata on your machine must match the environment's application version. See Version-Drift-Guard.

  • ATL (Acceptance Test Library): Microsoft's X++ library for creating test data in SysTest tests. Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL) uses it. See Generate-SysTest-Class.

  • AxDB: The business database of a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, on the same machine. F&O Studio uses it with Windows authentication. See Database-Access.

docs.title: B
docs.text:
• Batch service: The Windows service that runs batch jobs on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (Batch.exe). F&O Studio can restart it after a build and attach the debugger to it.

  • Best practice checks (xppbp): Microsoft's rule checker for X++ code and metadata, the one Visual Studio runs. See Best-Practice-Checks.

  • Bridge action: A named JSON request from the extension to its metadata server, for example get_element_tree or where_used. See Bridge-Protocol.

  • Business event: An event raised from X++ that external systems can subscribe to through the business events catalog. See Wizard-Business-Event.

docs.title: C
docs.text:
• CHE (cloud-hosted environment): A Finance and Operations development VM deployed through Lifecycle Services into your Azure subscription, with the AOS, AxDB and PackagesLocalDirectory on the VM. See Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments.

  • Chain of Command (CoC): The X++ way to wrap a method of a standard class, table or form in an extension class ([ExtensionOf(...)] with next). Create Code Extension creates one. See Create-Code-Extension and Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command.

  • Code view: F&O Studio's text editor for an element's X++ code, laid out the way Visual Studio shows it. See X++ code view.

  • Configuration (XPPConfig): A JSON file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig that names the metadata folders, the custom metadata folder and the cross-reference database of one environment. The registry value CurrentMetadataConfig selects the active one. Visual Studio and F&O Studio share it. See Select-Environment.

  • Copilot checkpoint: A point you set with Start Copilot Checkpoint; everything Copilot changes afterwards can be reverted. See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

  • Copilot scope: The set of elements Copilot may change, set with Set Copilot Scope….

  • Cross-reference database (XRef): A SQL Server database (in LocalDB on a developer machine) that records which code uses which element. Find References, rename and the references diagrams query it. Builds update it when xpp.build.crossReference is on.

  • Custom metadata folder (model store folder): The folder that holds your own packages and models, separate from the standard PackagesLocalDirectory on a UDE. Only models in this folder can be built and changed.

docs.title: D
docs.text:
• Data entity: An element that exposes data for OData, data management (import and export) and integrations, usually with a staging table. See Wizard-Data-Entity and Try-Data-Entity-OData.

  • Dataverse: Microsoft's Power Platform data service. A unified developer environment is managed through its Dataverse organization (https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com): F&O Studio uses Dataverse actions for setup, deploy, database sync, tests and database credentials.

  • Database synchronization (DB sync): Updating the SQL database schema to match the tables, views and indexes in the metadata. On a UDE it runs through Dataverse; on cloud-hosted and VHD environments through SyncEngine. See Synchronize-Database.

  • DebuggerProxy: Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe, Microsoft's debugger proxy from the FinOps tools. It tunnels the debugger to a unified developer environment. See Debugger.

  • Deployable package: A zip of built packages for deployment through Lifecycle Services or Power Platform. Create Deployment Package… creates one. See Create-Deployment-Package.

  • Descriptor: The XML file in a package's Descriptor folder that describes a model: name, display name, layer, dependencies.

  • Duty, privilege, role: The security layers of Finance and Operations: a privilege grants access to entry points such as menu items; a duty groups privileges; a role groups duties and is assigned to users. See Security-View.

docs.title: E
docs.text:
• EDT (extended data type): A reusable data type with properties such as label, size and relations, which table fields are based on.

  • Element: One item of metadata: a table, class, form, EDT, enum, menu item, security object, report and so on. Also called an object.

  • Entry point: Something a privilege grants access to: a menu item, a service operation or a data entity.

  • Event handler: A static method that runs on an element's event (for example a form control's OnClicked or a table's onInserted), declared with attributes such as [DataEventHandler]. See Event-Handlers.

  • Extension: An element in your model that adds to a standard element without changing it (for example CustTable.ContosoExtensions). See Create-Extension.

docs.title: F
docs.text:
• FinOps tools: Microsoft's Visual Studio extension for Finance and Operations development, downloaded by Connect to Environment…. F&O Studio uses parts of it (for example the debugger proxy) without Visual Studio.

  • Form extension: An extension of a standard form that adds controls, data sources or property changes. See Form-Layout-and-Form-Extensions.

docs.title: I
docs.text: • Infolog: The list of info, warning and error messages X++ code shows to the user. F&O Studio's Infolog view shows them while you debug. See Infolog.

docs.title: J
docs.text: • JIT credentials (just-in-time database access): Temporary SQL credentials for a unified developer or sandbox environment's database, issued by the environment on request (Reader or Writer role) for a limited time. Request Database Credentials asks for them. See Database-Access.

docs.title: L
docs.text:
• Label, label file: A translatable text referenced as @File:Id (for example @SYS7149). A label file holds the labels of one file ID in every language. See Label-Editor and Label-Tools.

  • LabelC: Microsoft's label compiler, in PackagesLocalDirectory's bin folder. Builds run it.

  • LCS (Lifecycle Services): Microsoft's portal for managing Finance and Operations implementations, including cloud-hosted environments and deployable packages.

  • LocalDB (SQL Server Express LocalDB): A lightweight SQL Server that runs on demand. It holds the cross-reference database on a developer machine.

docs.title: M
docs.text:
• MCP (Model Context Protocol): The protocol through which Copilot calls tools. F&O Studio registers its server as an MCP server in VS Code. See MCP-Agent-Tools.

  • Metadata API: Microsoft's .NET API for reading and writing D365FO metadata, which Visual Studio uses. F&O Studio's server uses the same API, loaded from your installation. See Metadata-Server.

  • Model: A group of elements that belongs to one package and one layer, for example ContosoExtensions. New elements go into the model of your project. See Models-and-Model-Dependencies.

docs.title: O
docs.text: • OData: The REST protocol through which public data entities are read and written. See Try-Data-Entity-OData.

docs.title: P
docs.text:
• pac (Power Platform CLI): Microsoft's command-line tool for Power Platform. F&O Studio uses it only for its two (pac) commands. See Power-Platform-CLI.

  • Package: The unit that is compiled and deployed: a folder with one or more models, built into assemblies in its bin folder.

  • PackagesLocalDirectory (PLD): The folder with all packages and the compiler tools (bin). On cloud-hosted and VHD environments it is under AosService; on a UDE machine Connect to Environment… downloads it.

  • Pdb2Pdb: Microsoft's tool that converts Windows PDB files into portable PDBs. F&O Studio runs it after each successful build, because VS Code's debugger reads only portable PDBs.

  • Precision design: An SSRS report design laid out to exact positions on the page. See Report-Designer.

  • Project (.rnrproj): A Visual Studio project file for Finance and Operations: the working set of elements of one model that you build and deploy. F&O Studio uses the same file. See D365FO-Projects.

docs.title: R
docs.text:
• RDL: Report Definition Language, the XML format of SSRS report designs.

  • reportsc: Microsoft's report compiler. Builds run it so reports are part of the package.

  • RuntimePackagesDirectory: A folder of junctions that combines the standard packages and your custom metadata folder, so the compiler sees both. Connect to Environment… creates it.

docs.title: S
docs.text:
• Sandbox: A Finance and Operations test environment (not a developer environment). Database credentials can be requested for sandboxes too.

  • Segregation of duties (SoD): Rules that keep two duties apart so one person cannot do both (for example maintain vendors and pay them). See Segregation-of-Duties.

  • SSRS (SQL Server Reporting Services): The report technology of Finance and Operations. See Report-Element-Designer.

  • SyncEngine: Microsoft's database synchronization tool in PackagesLocalDirectory's bin folder, used on cloud-hosted and VHD environments.

  • [SysObsolete]: An attribute that marks a class, table or method as obsolete, often with the replacement. F&O Studio warns about uses of obsolete APIs. See Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings.

  • SysOperation: The framework for batch jobs and dialogs: a data contract, a service and a controller. See Wizard-Batch-Job.

  • SysTest: The X++ unit test framework. See Run-Tests and Test-Explorer.

docs.title: T
docs.text:
• Team rules: The file .xpp/agent-rules.md in your repository, added to the Copilot agent instructions of everyone working in it. See Team-Rules.

  • TempDB / InMemory table: Temporary tables whose rows exist only while code runs. They cannot be browsed in the database.

  • Trace (.etl): A performance trace of the web client recorded in Event Tracing for Windows format. See Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: U
docs.text: • UDE (unified developer environment): A Finance and Operations developer environment hosted in Power Platform and managed through its Dataverse organization. Development happens on your own machine against downloaded metadata; deploy, database sync, tests and the debugger reach the environment through Dataverse. Its deployment type is OnlineDev. See Connect-to-Environment.

docs.title: V
docs.text:
• VHD environment: A Finance and Operations development VM you run from Microsoft's downloadable virtual hard disk, with everything on the VM. F&O Studio treats it like a cloud-hosted environment.

  • vsdbg: The .NET debugger engine VS Code uses. On a UDE, Microsoft's debugger proxy runs in vsdbg mode for F&O Studio.

docs.title: W
docs.text:
• Web client: The browser interface of Finance and Operations (https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com). See Copy-Name-and-Open-in-Browser.

  • Workspace: VS Code's set of open folders. Opening a D365FO project opens its own workspace with the project folder and its model folder.

docs.title: X
docs.text:
• X++: The programming language of Finance and Operations.

  • xppc: Microsoft's X++ compiler, in PackagesLocalDirectory's bin folder. F&O Studio builds with it, as Visual Studio does. See Build-Project-and-Model.

  • XRef: Short for the cross-reference database.

docs.title: Go to Definition
docs.text: Go to Definition (F12) and Peek Definition jump from a name in X++ code to where it is defined: an element's code view, or the signature line of a method, also in a base class. Ctrl+click on the argument of an intrinsic function such as tableStr(CustTable) or on a label literal such as "@SYS7149" opens that element or label. This is the equivalent of Go To Definition in Visual Studio's X++ editor. F&O Studio resolves names through the metadata and does not need the X++ language server.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Follow a call such as CustGroup::find(...) or salesTable.type() to its code.
  • Open the class a variable is declared as, or the base class of the current class (super.).
  • Jump from formControlStr(CustTable, Name) or menuItemDisplayStr(CustTable) to the form or menu item.
  • Open the label behind "@SYS7149" in the label editor.
  • Go from X++ to the C# code of a project your X++ project references, and from C# back to X++.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration. Definitions read the metadata of all installed models.
  • The code must be in an X++ document: a code view (xpp:), an .xpp file or an untitled X++ editor (such as Run Snippet).
  • No cross-reference database is needed for definitions. It is needed for references and implementations.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Put the cursor on a name in X++ code.
  2. Press F12 (Go to Definition), or right-click and choose Go to Definition or Peek > Peek Definition.
  3. The target opens:
  4. an element name opens the element's code view at the top;
  5. a method opens the code view of the class (or table, form...) that declares it, at the signature line;
  6. a field or enum value opens the element at the first line that names it, if there is one.

docs.title: What F&O Studio recognizes
docs.text:
You put the cursor on Resolved as CustGroup (a type name, 3 characters or more, not a keyword) The first element with that name, looked up in this order: class, table, enum, EDT, view, data entity, map, query, form method in CustGroup::find( Static method find of CustGroup Value in SalesStatus::Invoiced The member Invoiced of enum SalesStatus (enum values have no code) method in this.method( or element.method( Method of the current element method in super.method( Method of the base class (from the extends clause) method in variable.method( Method of the variable's declared type: the nearest declaration above the cursor, else a class member method( with no qualifier A method of the current element or one of its base classes; else a global function on class Global Namespace.Type::Member (dotted) A .NET name, sent to the C# navigation

When a method is not found in the element's own code, F&O Studio follows the extends clause up to six levels of base classes.

docs.title: Ctrl+click links
docs.text:
The code view also has links you Ctrl+click. Hover over them to see the tooltip ("Open CustTable", "Open label @SYS7149").

Code Opens tableStr(X), tableNum, fieldStr(X, F), fieldNum, fieldPName, indexStr, indexNum, tableMethodStr, tableStaticMethodStr, tableFieldGroupStr, tablePName Table, view, data entity or map X (the first that exists) classStr, classNum, methodStr, staticMethodStr, delegateStr, attributeStr Class formStr, formControlStr, formDataSourceStr, formDataFieldStr, formMethodStr Form enumStr, enumNum, enumLiteralStr Enum extendedTypeStr, extendedTypeNum EDT queryStr, queryDataSourceStr, queryMethodStr Query menuItemDisplayStr, menuItemActionStr, menuItemOutputStr Menu item of that kind ssrsReportStr, dataEntityDataSourceStr, viewStr Report, data entity, view configurationKeyStr, configurationKeyNum, licenseCodeStr, licenseCodeNum Configuration key, license code menuStr, tileStr Menu, tile workflowApprovalStr, workflowTaskStr, workflowTypeStr Workflow approval, task, type dutyStr, roleStr, privilegeStr Security duty, role, privilege "@SYS7149", "@ContosoLabels:OrderStatus" The label in the Label Editor

The link is on the first argument (the element name). Classes open in the code view; every other element type opens in the Element Designer. Links inside comments are ignored. When no element of the expected types exists, you see "X was not found."

docs.title: X++ and C
docs.text:
• In X++ code, a name that is not an X++ element goes to the C# projects of your solution: definition and hover show the .NET type or member from their source. See Solution View and C# References.
  • In a C# file that uses Dynamics.AX.Application, Go to Definition on an X++ type goes to its X++ code view.

docs.title: Designers
docs.text: In the Element Designer, right-click a node or property that names another element and choose Go to Referenced Element…. One reference opens directly; several open a picker (for example the EDT, the enum and the label of a field). See Properties Grid and Pickers.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Go to Definition and the Ctrl+click links are always on; no setting switches them off. The related hover is described in Hover.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• src/navigation.ts (XppNavigation) is the definition provider for X++ documents. resolve reads the word at the cursor and the text before and after it on the line, and decides between a type, a qualified member (::, .) and an unqualified call.
  • Type names are looked up with the bridge action find_object (exact match). Results are cached per name for the session.
  • Declared types are found by declaredType, a text search for Type name declarations in the document.
  • definition opens the owner's code view (xpp:/AxClass/Name.xpp), finds the method with methodSpans from src/xppSource.ts, and returns the line of the signature. For a base class it reads the extends clause of the code view.
  • The Ctrl+click links come from XppReferenceLinks in src/codeLinks.ts. They run the internal command xpp.openReference, which looks up the name with find_object and opens the first match among the expected types.
  • Designer references use xpp.goTo.referenced in src/goTo.ts; the server reports which properties of a node name other elements.
  • C# names go through clrNavigation.ts (the C# projects of the solution).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Name resolution is textual, not a full compiler analysis. A variable's type comes from the nearest declaration above the cursor; chained calls such as CustTable::find(x).name() don't resolve the second member, and var declarations don't give a type.
  • When a name exists as several element types (for example a table and a class with the same name), the first in the lookup order wins.
  • Fields, enum values and kernel methods have no code; F&O Studio opens the owning element instead. For elements without X++ code (EDTs, enums), use the Open designer link in the Hover.
  • Methods added by a Chain of Command class are not found by Go to Definition on the base type; use Implementations and Chain of Command.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Nothing happens on F12 right after startup The server is still starting; type lookups are not cached until it answers Wait a moment and try again F12 on a short name does nothing Names shorter than 3 characters and keywords are not looked up as types Put the cursor on the method or a longer name F12 on obj.method() opens nothing The variable's declared type was not found in the document Use the type name: Type::method, or open the type with Open Element… "X was not found." after Ctrl+click No element of the expected types has that name Check the spelling; for a label, check the label file ID

docs.title: Hierarchy and Reference Diagrams
docs.text: F&O Studio draws three element diagrams that replace Visual Studio's DGML diagrams: View Hierarchy (the base classes or tables of an element and what derives from it), View References (everything that uses an element, grouped by type) and View Dependencies (everything an element uses). Each diagram is a clickable tree: click a node to open the element or the line of code. You can copy or export every diagram as a Mermaid flowchart.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• View Hierarchy: see where a class sits in its inheritance chain, for example the base classes of SalesFormLetter_Invoice and the classes that derive from SalesFormLetter, before you choose which class to extend with Chain of Command.
  • View References: see at a glance who uses an element, grouped by element type, for example every class, form and table that references CustGroup, and jump to each place.
  • View Dependencies: see what an element needs, for example which tables, EDTs and classes a class uses, before you move it to another model or assess an upgrade.
  • Export a diagram to Mermaid for a design document, a pull request or a wiki page.

For call graphs inside code (callers and callees of a method, subtypes and supertypes in the editor), see Call and Type Hierarchy. For tables and their relations, see Entity Relationship Diagram.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata.
  • View References, View Dependencies and the derived part of View Hierarchy read the cross-reference database. It knows what was built with cross references; build your models with cross references to see your own code (see Build Project and Model). Standard code is in the cross-reference database that comes with the environment (on a UDE it is restored during setup; see Connect to Environment).

docs.title: Where to find the commands
docs.text:
Command Application Explorer, project view, element designer (right-click the element) Dynamics 365 view Command Palette View Hierarchy Classes and tables View and run > View Hierarchy… F&O Studio: View Hierarchy View References Element types the cross-reference database indexes (classes, tables, forms, enums, EDTs, views, queries, data entities, maps, menus, menu items, table and enum extensions, reports, security roles, duties and privileges, tiles, configuration keys) View and run > View References… F&O Studio: View References View Dependencies Same types as View References View and run > View Dependencies… F&O Studio: View Dependencies

From the Dynamics 365 view and the Command Palette, F&O Studio asks for the element first (classes and tables for View Hierarchy).

docs.title: View Hierarchy
docs.text:
The diagram opens in a tab titled <Type> hierarchy: <name>, for example Class hierarchy: SalesFormLetter. It shows:

  1. the chain of base elements, from the top base down, following each element's Extends property;
  2. the element itself, marked "this element";
  3. the elements that derive from it, two levels deep (children and grandchildren), sorted by name.

For tables, Extends is table inheritance (for example DirPartyTable and the tables derived from it).

docs.title: View References
docs.text:
The diagram opens in a tab titled References to <name> (with "(first 1000)" when there are more). Under the element:

  • one node per referencing element type (Classes, Forms, Tables, ...) with the number of elements;
  • under it, one node per referencing element with its number of references;
  • under that, one node per reference: the member (for example the method) with the line number, and the reference kind.

Click an element node to open the element. Click a reference node to open the code at that line, as Find All References does.

docs.title: View Dependencies
docs.text:
The diagram opens in a tab titled Dependencies of <name> (with "(first 200)" when there are more). Under the element (with the number of elements it depends on):

  • one node per element type of the dependencies, with their number;
  • under it, each element the selected element uses, with the number of references and their kinds.

Labels and tags are left out. When the cross-reference database records nothing, F&O Studio says: "The cross-reference database records no dependencies of . Build its model with cross references to fill it."

docs.title: Model dependencies
docs.text: View Model Dependencies… in the Dynamics 365 view (Model and project) uses the same diagram for models: the packages a model references, and the models that reference its package. See Models and Model Dependencies.

docs.title: Opening nodes
docs.text: In all diagrams, nodes shown as links open what they stand for: a class in the X++ Code View, any other element in its designer (a label file in the Label Editor), a reference at its line. Group nodes (element types) are not links.

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text:
Every diagram has two buttons:

  • Copy Mermaid copies a Mermaid flowchart of the tree to the clipboard.
  • Export Mermaid… saves it as .mmd, or as .md wrapped in a ```mermaid block. The default file name is the root node's name.

The flowchart has one box per node (with its description in small text) and an arrow from each node to its children, left to right. For a class ContosoOrderService that extends ContosoDocumentService and has one derived class:

flowchart LR
  n0["ContosoDocumentService"]
  n1["ContosoOrderService<br/><small>this element</small>"]
  n2["ContosoOrderServiceExport"]
  n1 --> n2
  n0 --> n1

For hierarchies the root of the export is the top base class.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The diagrams have no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The diagrams are built in src/diagrams.ts and shown by its DiagramPanel, a webview with a nested list. The commands are registered in src/d365Tools.ts.
  • View Hierarchy reads the Extends property of the element and of each base with bridge action get_element_properties until there is no base (or a loop). Derived elements come from bridge action where_used with reference kind ClassExtended (up to 200 per level) on the cross-reference database.
  • View References uses where_used (up to 1,000 references), the same structured cross-reference query as Find References (XRefQuery.cs).
  • View Dependencies uses bridge action element_dependencies (up to 200 elements). The server lists every element the element's code and metadata reference in the cross-reference database, with the number of references and their kinds, and leaves labels and tags out.
  • The Mermaid text is generated from the same tree that is shown.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The tree is a list, not a graph layout. Elements that appear in several places are repeated.
  • Derived elements are shown two levels deep; open a derived element's hierarchy to go further.
  • References and dependencies reflect the cross-reference database as of the last build with cross references. Code that was not built on this machine is missing.
  • View References stops at 1,000 references, View Dependencies at 200 elements.
  • Diagrams are not refreshed automatically; run the command again after a build.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The hierarchy shows no derived classes The cross-reference database has no ClassExtended references for it, or is unavailable Build with cross references; check the cross-reference database in the environment setup "The cross-reference database records no dependencies of . ..." The element's model was not built with cross references Build the model with cross references "Dependencies are not available for ." The element type is not indexed by the cross-reference database Use View References on a related element, or Find References References to your new code are missing The last build with cross references is older than the code Build again

docs.title: Hover
docs.text: Hover over a name in X++ code to see what it is without leaving the editor: the element type and model, its label, links to open it, the signature of a method, the text of a label reference, the base type and size of an EDT, or the values of an enum. It replaces the Quick Info tooltips of Visual Studio's X++ editor and adds a few one-click actions.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Read the text behind "@SYS7149" or "@ContosoLabels:OrderStatus" without opening the label file.
  • Check which model an element comes from, and whether it is yours.
  • See the signature of a method before you call it.
  • See what an EDT is based on (type, size, enum, reference table) or which values an enum has.
  • Jump from a name to its designer, its references, its table data or a performance analysis.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration.
  • The code in an X++ document (code view, .xpp file or untitled X++ editor).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: Move the mouse over a name and wait, or put the cursor on it and use VS Code's Show or Focus Hover command. Several hover sections can show at once.

docs.title: Element names
docs.text:
Hovering a type name such as CustGroup shows:

CustGroup · Table in model `<model>`
<label text of the table>
Open designer · Find references · Browse data · Analyze performance
  • The first line: the element, its type, its model, and "(yours)" when it is in one of your models.
  • The second line: the element's label, when it has one that resolves to text.
  • The links:
  • Open designer: opens the Element Designer;
  • Find references: runs Find References (Find All References);
  • Browse data: tables only, opens the table data (Browse Table Data);
  • Analyze performance: classes, tables and forms (Analyze Performance).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Hovering a method in CustGroup::find(, this.validateWrite(, super.run( or salesTable.type( shows the declaring element and the signature:

CustGroup.find · method of Table CustGroup
public static CustGroup find(CustGroupId _custGroupId, boolean _forupdate = false)

When the method is inherited, the element shown is the base class that declares it. Fields, enum values and kernel methods have no signature line in code; the hover then names the member and its element only.

docs.title: Label references
docs.text:
Hovering @SYS7149 or @ContosoLabels:OrderStatus inside code shows the label text, for example "@GLS390: Marking this field may cause inconsistency in calculation of Brazilian taxes."

The label literal is also a link: VS Code adds "Open label @X (ctrl + click)", which opens the Label Editor at that label.

docs.title: EDTs and enums
docs.text: Hovering an EDT adds one line with what is set among its type, the EDT it extends, its string size, its enum type and its reference table (for example type ... · extends ... · size ...), and the EDT's label. Hovering an enum lists its values (20 at most, then …) and its label.

docs.title: C# names
docs.text: In X++ code, hovering a .NET type or member of the C# projects of your solution shows its C# declaration. See Solution View and C# References.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.hover true The label text, EDT and enum details. The element and method hover and the label link are always on

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Two hover providers are registered for X++ documents; VS Code shows their results together.

  1. Navigation hover in src/navigation.ts: resolves the name the same way as Go to Definition. For an element it calls the bridge action find_object (exact match) for the model and label, and builds the links as trusted command links (only the four commands above are allowed). For a method it finds the signature line in the owner's code view, following extends up to six base classes. Names that are not X++ go to the C# hover.
  2. Detail hover in src/codeIntel/providers.ts:
  3. a label reference (@File:Id or @ABC123) is read with the bridge action read_label (label file ID and label ID) and its text shown;
  4. an EDT or enum is read with read_object; the EDT properties EdtType, Extends, StringSize, EnumType, ReferenceTable and Label, or the enum values and Label, are shown.
  5. The Ctrl+click link on label literals comes from the document link provider in src/codeLinks.ts.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Name resolution is textual (see Go to Definition): no hover for members of chained calls or of var variables.
  • Element labels that are label references (@SYS...) are not resolved in the element hover.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No label text over "@..." xpp.codeIntelligence.hover is off, or the label doesn't exist Turn the setting on; check the label ID No EDT or enum line xpp.codeIntelligence.hover is off Turn it on No hover over a variable's method The declared type was not found Hover the type name, or declare the variable with its type The links in the hover do nothing The command failed; see the error message Use Show Log in the error message

docs.text:

Source: Hover on the wiki.

docs.title: Implementations and Chain of Command
docs.text: Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) answers "what else runs when this runs?". On a method it lists the Chain of Command wrappers, the pre/post and delegate event handlers and the overrides in subclasses. On an element it lists the Chain of Command classes, the event handlers, the subclasses and the metadata extensions (table, form, enum, EDT extensions...). Show Extensions and Handlers… shows the same for any element in a grouped picker. Visual Studio has no single command for this; you would combine Find References, the extension list in Application Explorer and the event handler search.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you change or wrap a standard method, see who already wraps or handles it (Microsoft's own extensions and yours, and ISV code installed with the metadata).
  • Find out why a standard method behaves differently than its code suggests: a Chain of Command class or an event handler adds code around it.
  • Find every subclass that overrides a method.
  • List every extension of a table or form, including metadata extensions that have no code.
  • From a Chain of Command class or handler class, jump back to what it extends (see Code Lens).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Cross-reference database with the standard application (restored by Connect to Environment). Overrides, subclasses, metadata extensions and the standard Chain of Command classes and handlers come from it.
  • Your own code is read from disk, so Chain of Command classes and handlers you wrote since the last build count.
  • The extension index (below) builds in the background the first time an X++ document opens. Until it is ready you see "Extension index still building; Chain of Command and handlers may be missing" in the status bar.
  • The setting xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation must be on (the default) for Go to Implementations.

docs.title: Go to Implementations in code
docs.text:
1. In a code view, put the cursor on:
  2. a method name (in its signature or in a call such as salesFormLetter.run()), for the method's implementations;
  3. the element name on the declaration line, for the element's implementations;
  4. anywhere inside a method of the current element, for that method.
  5. Press Ctrl+F12, or right-click and choose Go to Implementations or Peek > Peek Implementations.
  6. One result opens directly; several open in a peek list. Each entry opens the code at the class or the method.

What you get:

Cursor on Results A method, e.g. SalesFormLetter.run Chain of Command methods that wrap it (next run()), Event handler methods ([PreHandlerFor], [PostHandlerFor], delegate subscribers, and form/data event handlers on that method), Override methods in subclasses An element, e.g. SalesFormLetter or CustTable Chain of Command class ([ExtensionOf(...)] of the element, its data sources or its controls), Event handler methods on the element's events, Subclass (classes that extend it), Metadata extension (CustTable.ContosoExtensions)

Metadata extensions have no code, so the editor can't show them. When some results are left out for that reason you see "N more without code (metadata extensions); see Show Extensions and Handlers" in the status bar.

docs.title: Show Extensions and Handlers…
docs.text:
1. Run Show Extensions and Handlers…:
  2. from the context menu of an element with code or an extensible element in the Application Explorer or the project view;
  3. from the Element Designer context menu;
  4. from the Code Intelligence node in the Dynamics 365 view;
  5. from the command palette (F&O Studio: Show Extensions and Handlers…). It uses the element of the active code view; without one it asks "Show extensions of" (for example SalesTable, SalesFormLetter, CustTable).
  6. A picker titled "N extension(s) of X" opens. Results are grouped under separators in this order: Chain of Command class, Event handler, Metadata extension, Subclass. Each row shows the name, a detail such as "extends SalesFormLetter" or "Post handler of SalesFormLetter.run", and the element type.
  7. Pick a row. Classes and methods open in the code view; metadata extensions open in the designer.

When nothing extends the element you see "Nothing extends X."

docs.title: Event handlers of a designer node
docs.text: In the Element Designer, the Events node of a table, a form data source, a data source field or a form control lists the handlers of those events from the same index. See Event Handlers.

docs.title: Rebuild Extension Index
docs.text:
The index is cached and refreshed on its own. Run Rebuild Extension Index (command palette, or the Code Intelligence node in the Dynamics 365 view) when:

  • you restored a new cross-reference database, or built many packages;
  • results look out of date.

The node shows the index status: reading cross references, reading your models, scanning form/data event handlers, then ready (N extension classes, N wrapped methods, N handlers) or failed: <reason>. While it builds, the Code Intelligence node says "indexing…".

Rebuilding also reloads the obsolete API list.

docs.title: Writing Chain of Command
docs.text:
F&O Studio gives you several ways to start a wrapper:

  • Create Code Extension on an element creates the [ExtensionOf] class (Create Code Extension).
  • The quick fix create a Chain of Command wrapper writes the wrapper method (Quick Fixes).
  • The snippets coc, coctable, cocform, cocformds, cocmethod and cocmethodret (Snippets).

Completion after . on a type lists the methods its Chain of Command classes add, marked "(extension)" (Completion and Signature Help).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation true Go to Implementations, call hierarchy and type hierarchy xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex true Include [FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler] and similar handlers. The first scan of all packages takes about a minute; it is cached afterwards xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens true Counts of Chain of Command, handlers and overrides above methods (Code Lens)

docs.title: The extension index
docs.text:
ExtensionIndex in server/Ported/Tools/ExtensionIndex.cs knows who extends what, in both directions, and keeps it in memory. It merges three sources:

  1. Cross-reference database (set-based queries over the whole application, about 6 seconds). An [ExtensionOf] attribute row (reference kind Attribute to /Classes/ExtensionOf) and the type reference on the same line give the extended element: a class, table, form, form data source or control, data entity, view or map. A wrapper is a method of the extension class that calls the method of the same name (its next call). Pre/post handlers and delegate subscribers come from their attribute row and the method reference on the same line. The result is cached on disk in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\cache\extensions-<database>.json and reused until the database changes.
  2. Your own models, read from the class files on disk on each refresh (at most every 20 seconds), so extensions written since the last build count.
  3. Form and data event handlers ([FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler], [FormEventHandler], [FormDataSourceEventHandler]...). The cross-reference database doesn't record them, so the reference packages are scanned once (about a minute) and cached in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\cache\event-handlers-<hash>.json. This part only runs when xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex is on.

docs.title: The requests
docs.text:
Code intelligence runs in a second F&O Studio server process, separate from the one the designers use. The extension (src/codeIntel/providers.ts) sends xpp/lang requests; CodeIntel in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs answers them:

  • implementations waits up to 15 seconds for the index, then adds from the index the Chain of Command classes or wrappers and the handlers, and from the cross-reference database the subclasses (kind ClassExtended, at most 500), the overrides (kind MethodOverride, at most 500) and the metadata extensions (paths such as TableExtension/CustTable.<suffix>, at most 50 per extension type);
  • status and refresh_index start or force the index build; the extension polls the status every 3 seconds until it is ready;
  • event_handlers answers the designer's Events node.

Each result is an element path such as /Classes/SalesFormLetter_Extension/Methods/run. The extension turns it into a code view location (xpp:/AxClass/...), or opens the designer when the element has no code.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Standard Chain of Command classes and handlers are only as current as the cross-reference database.
  • Classes of your models are found from source; other custom packages (for example ISV packages) are found only when they are in the cross-reference database.
  • Form and data event handlers are missing while xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex is off.
  • Go to Implementations doesn't show metadata extensions in the editor; use Show Extensions and Handlers….
  • Up to 500 subclasses or overrides are listed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Status bar: "Extension index still building; Chain of Command and handlers may be missing" The index is not ready after 15 s Wait for ready on the Code Intelligence node, then try again Index status failed: cross-reference database unavailable: ... The cross-reference database can't be used See Find All References troubleshooting A form control handler is missing eventHandlerIndex is off, or the scan is still running Turn it on in Configure Code Intelligence… and wait for ready A new standard extension is missing after an update The cache is from the old database Run Rebuild Extension Index Ctrl+F12 does nothing xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation is off Turn it on "No class, table, form or other element named X." The name typed in Show Extensions doesn't exist Check the name

docs.title: Infolog
docs.text: The Infolog view shows the messages that the code you debug raises with info(), warning(), error() and checkFailed(), as they happen, the way Visual Studio's Infolog window does while debugging. Each message has its severity icon and time, you can filter by severity and text, copy the list, and jump from any message to the label and code that raise it with Find Message Source.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You step through a process and want to see each message at the moment it is raised, not only the final Infolog the user sees in the browser.
  • You need the exact text of an error to find where it comes from.
  • You want to keep the messages of a run (copy them into a work item or a chat).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A running debug session (Debugger). The Infolog view fills only from debugger output: on a UDE through the debugger proxy, on cloud-hosted and VHD environments through the C# extension's debugger (Debugging on Cloud-Hosted).
  • Nothing to configure.

docs.title: Open the view
docs.text:
• The Infolog view is in the F&O Studio panel, next to Results and Copilot Activity.
  • In the Dynamics 365 view, Debug > Infolog focuses it.
  • When the first message of the session arrives while the view is hidden, F&O Studio reveals it.

docs.title: Read messages
docs.text:
1. Start the debugger (F&O Studio: Launch Debugger, also a button in the Infolog view's title bar).
  2. Run the code in the environment. Each message appears at the top of the list (newest first) with:
  3. an icon: error, warning or info;
  4. the message text;
  5. the time it arrived (as a description).
  6. Hover a message for its severity and full text.

Each message is also written to the X++ output channel as [Infolog <Kind>] <message>, so you can see it next to the debugger's own log.

docs.title: Title bar buttons
docs.text:
Button Command What it does Launch Debugger F&O Studio: Launch Debugger Starts a debug session Filter F&O Studio: Filter Infolog Two steps: pick the severities to show (Error, Warning, Info; several allowed), then type text that messages must contain (empty shows all). Escape at either step keeps the current filter Clear F&O Studio: Clear Infolog Removes all messages Copy F&O Studio: Copy Infolog Copies the messages that pass the filter, one per line as <time> <kind>: <message>; the status bar shows "Infolog copied"

The filter is case-insensitive. Messages of any other kind than Error or Warning count as Info for the filter.

docs.title: Find where a message comes from
docs.text: Every message has Find Message Source (inline button and context menu). It searches the labels with that text and the code that raises them, values included, as described on Find Message Source. For example, for "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." it first lists the mandatory table fields with that label, then the code that raises the message for one of them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Running a class like this in the debugger:

internal final class ContosoCheckCustomers
{
    public static void main(Args _args)
    {
        CustTable custTable;
        int missing;

        while select custTable
            where custTable.CustGroup == ''
        {
            missing++;
            warning(strFmt("Customer %1 has no customer group.", custTable.AccountNum));
        }
        info(strFmt("%1 customers have no customer group.", missing));
    }
}

adds one warning per customer without a group and one info line at the end. Copy Infolog gives, for example:

10:42:18 Info: 2 customers have no customer group.
10:42:18 Warning: Customer C-0002 has no customer group.
10:42:17 Warning: Customer C-0001 has no customer group.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for the Infolog. The filter is kept until you change it or reload the window.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The code is parseInfolog and InfologProvider in src/debug.ts.

  1. F&O Studio registers a debug adapter tracker for the xpp debug type (UDE) and for the clr debug type (the local AOS). The tracker sees every message the debugger sends to VS Code.
  2. The server writes Infolog messages into the debugger's output, as XML, the way Visual Studio's InfologListenerService reads them:
<InfologMessage xmlns="..."><Kind>Warning</Kind><Message>Customer C-0001 has no customer group.</Message></InfologMessage>
  1. For each output event, F&O Studio finds every <InfologMessage xmlns…>…</InfologMessage> block, reads Kind (Info when missing) and Message, decodes the XML entities (<, >, ", ', &) and adds an entry with the current time.
  2. The view (xpp.infolog) is a tree with one item per message, newest first. The filter and copy work on the list held in memory.

The Debug Console still shows the debugger's raw output, including these XML blocks.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only messages raised while a debugger is attached reach the view. It is not a log of the environment.
  • Messages are kept in memory for the window; reloading the window clears them. Clear Infolog clears them too.
  • The time is when VS Code received the message, not when the server raised it.
  • Only the kind and the text of each message are read. The web client's grouping of messages under a prefix (setPrefix) is not rebuilt: you see each message as the server wrote it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The view stays empty No debug session, or the code raised no messages while attached Start the debugger, then run the code Some messages are missing The filter hides them Filter Infolog: select all severities and clear the text Copy Infolog copies fewer lines than raised Copy takes only the messages that pass the filter Clear the filter first

docs.title: Label Editor
docs.text: The label editor opens a label file (AxLabelFile) as a table of its labels: label ID, the text in each language side by side, and the comment. You search labels, compare and fill in translations, add, edit and delete labels in label files of your own models, and copy the @File:Id reference to use in properties and code. It replaces Visual Studio's label editor.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Look up the text of a label and its translations, for example @SYS7149.
  • Add the labels for a new feature to your model's label file, in all its languages at once.
  • Fix a text or a translation, or add the missing translation of a label.
  • Delete a label you no longer need (see also Find Unused Labels… in Label Tools).
  • Copy a label reference to paste into a property or into X++ code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). The label editor reads the label text files on disk; it does not need the environment.
  • Editing is possible only when every language of the label file lies in your custom metadata folder (a label file of your own model). Standard label files open read-only.
  • To create a label file, ask Copilot or use the agent tool xpp_create_object with objectType AxLabelFile and the languages in properties.Languages (for example en-US,de). The wizards put their labels in your model's en-US label file when it has one.

docs.title: Opening a label file
docs.text:
Place How Application Explorer or project view Click a label file (Label Files node), or right-click > Open Designer A property that holds a label The go-to button in the Properties grid opens the file on that label X++ code view, Go to Referenced Element… Following a label reference (the link on @File:Id in code) opens its file on that label

One tab per label file, titled <Id> [Label file]. When the editor opens on a label (Go to Label), the search box holds the label ID, the matching row is marked and scrolled into view. The tab comes back after a window reload.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Toolbar: the title <Id> label file, a read-only badge for label files outside your models, the search box, Languages…, New label (your files only), Properties and Refresh.
  • Table: one row per label with Label ID, one column per shown language, Comment, and the row buttons. A language without a text for the label shows (none).
  • Footer: how many labels match, for example "37 label(s) match (2140 in en-US)." When there are more than 500 matches: "Showing 500 of 812 matching labels (2140 in en-US). Refine the search to see others."

docs.title: The primary language
docs.text: The editor opens a label file in one language, the primary language: the language of the AxLabelFile element you opened (for example ContosoLabels_en-US), else en-US, else the first language the file has. Rows, search and the label count come from the primary language. Other languages are shown next to it.

docs.title: Searching
docs.text: Type in Search ID, text or comment. The table updates 300 ms after you stop typing and shows the labels whose ID, primary-language text or comment contains the text (not case-sensitive). Rows are in label ID order. At most 500 rows are shown; refine the search to see others.

docs.title: Showing other languages
docs.text: When a label file has at most six languages, all of them are shown side by side. With more, only the primary language is shown at first. Click Languages…, tick the languages you want and click Show. The choice stays while the tab is open.

docs.title: Adding a label
docs.text:
1. Click New label (only on your own label files). An edit row appears at the top.
  2. Enter the Label ID: letters, digits and _, for example ContosoOrderStatus.
  3. Enter the text in one or more languages. Languages you leave empty are not written.
  4. Optionally enter a Comment (it is saved with the primary language's text).
  5. Click Save or press Enter. Cancel or Escape discards the row.

The status bar shows what was written, for example @ContosoLabels:ContosoOrderStatus: en-US created, de updated. The label is inserted in label ID order, as Visual Studio does. Use the reference @ContosoLabels:ContosoOrderStatus in properties and code.

docs.title: Editing a label
docs.text:
1. Click Edit on the row.
  2. Change texts and the comment. Clearing a language's text leaves that language as it is; it does not delete the text.
  3. Save (or Enter) writes every language you filled in. The comment belongs to the primary language; other languages keep their own comments.

Texts are stored on one line: line breaks you paste become spaces.

docs.title: Deleting a label
docs.text:
1. Click Delete on the row.
  2. Confirm "Delete label in every language of this label file?". The dialog warns: "Code and properties that reference it will show the raw label ID."
  3. The label and its comment are removed from every language file.

    4. Before deleting, check where the label is used with Find All References or Find Unused Labels… (Label Tools).

docs.title: Copying the reference
docs.text: Copy @ref on any row (also on read-only files) copies @<File>:<Id>, or the ID itself when it already starts with @ (legacy files such as SYS store IDs like @SYS7149). The status bar says "Copied ...".

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Properties opens the label file in the Element Designer to see the AxLabelFile element's properties.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The label editor has no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The panel is src/labelEditor.ts with the webview media/labelEditor.js. xpp.openDesigner sends label files here instead of to the element designer (src/extension.ts).
  • Label files are read and written as the platform stores them: text files <root>\<Package>\<Model>\AxLabelFile\LabelResources\<language>\<Id>.<language>.label.txt, one Id=Text line per label, a comment on the next line starting with ;, sorted by ID. The server's LabelStore finds every language of a label file ID (one model holds a label file ID), inserts new labels in ID order, updates or removes the label and its comment line, and writes the file as UTF-8 with a byte order mark.
  • Bridge actions (LabelService.cs):
  • label_file_entries: the primary language's labels filtered by search, at most 500, with the texts of the shown languages, the list of all languages, the total and match counts, and whether the file is editable;
  • save_label: creates or updates one label; empty texts leave that language alone; a language the file does not have is refused;
  • delete_label: removes the label from every language.
  • Writes are allowed only when every language file lies under the custom metadata folder. Metadata elements are not touched; the label text files are not AOT metadata.
  • The designers and the form preview resolve labels from the same files and notice changes by the file's write time, so new texts show at once.
  • Labels take effect in the application after the model is built (LabelC compiles the label files; see Build Project and Model).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• At most 500 labels are listed per search.
  • New label files and new languages of a label file are not created here (create the AxLabelFile element instead).
  • Texts are single-line.
  • Deleting a label does not update the code or properties that use it.
  • The editor does not track changes made outside it while it is open; click Refresh.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix read-only badge, no Edit or Delete buttons The label file is not in your models Add labels to a label file of your own model "Enter a label ID." / "Enter the text in at least one language." The new label row is incomplete Fill in the ID and at least one text "The label ID must be letters, digits or _ (e.g. MyFieldLabel)." The ID has other characters Change the ID "Label file '' has no language ." A text was given for a language the file does not have Add the language to the label file first "No label texts found for label file ''." No LabelResources text files exist for that ID Check the label file element and its model folder "Label '' not found in ." The label was already deleted (for example by another tool) Click Refresh

docs.title: Label Tools
docs.text: F&O Studio has five commands for working with labels across a whole label file: Find Labels… to find a label by its text and insert its reference, Translate Missing Labels… to fill in missing translations with the Copilot chat model, Find Unused Labels… to clean up labels nobody uses, and Export Labels… / Import Labels… to exchange a label file with translators as CSV. They complement the Label Editor, which edits one label file interactively.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Find Labels…: you write code or set a property and want to reuse an existing standard label instead of creating a new one (Visual Studio's Find labels).
  • Translate Missing Labels…: your label file has several languages and new labels exist only in the primary language.
  • Find Unused Labels…: before a release, you want to remove labels that are no longer used in code or metadata.
  • Export Labels… / Import Labels…: you send a label file to translators or reviewers and load their changes back.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata.
  • Translate Missing Labels…, Find Unused Labels… and Import Labels… work on label files of your own models. Find Labels… and Export Labels… offer every label file, standard ones included.
  • Translate Missing Labels… needs a Copilot chat model: sign in to GitHub Copilot in VS Code.
  • Find Unused Labels… needs the cross-reference database, filled by a build with cross references (see Build Project and Model).
  • A label file has more than one language when its model has <Id>_<language>.xml files in AxLabelFile, for example ContosoLabels_en-US.xml and ContosoLabels_de.xml.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text: All five commands are in the Dynamics 365 view under Labels, and in the Command Palette with the prefix F&O Studio:.

docs.title: Find Labels…
docs.text:
1. Run Find Labels….
  2. Pick the label file, for example SYS.
  3. Enter the text to search for, for example customer group. The search uses en-US when the file has it, else its first language, and matches the label ID or the text.
  4. A picker lists up to 100 matches with their reference (" label(s) — select one to insert or copy its reference").
  5. Pick a label:
  6. when an X++ code view is the active editor, the reference replaces the selection, in quotes, for example "@SYS7149";
  7. otherwise the reference is copied to the clipboard ("Copied @SYS7149.").

    8. To set a label property in a designer, the label picker in the Properties grid is quicker: it searches your label files and can create a label.

docs.title: Translate Missing Labels…
docs.text:
1. Run Translate Missing Labels… and pick one of your label files. The picker shows its languages.
  2. F&O Studio reads the whole file in every language and lists the labels that have a text in the primary language (en-US when the file has it) but none in another language.
  3. When nothing is missing: "Every label of has a text in ." (or " has only ." for a single-language file).
  4. Confirm the summary, for example "Translate 42 missing text(s) of ContosoLabels (de: 30, fr: 12) with the chat model and save them?". The dialog notes these are machine translations.
  5. A progress notification shows the language and count. You can cancel it; translations already saved stay.
  6. At the end: "Saved of translation(s) in . Review them in the label editor afterwards."
  7. Open the Label Editor, show the languages side by side and review the new texts.

    8. The chat model is asked to keep placeholders such as %1 and %2, keep label references (@File:Id) unchanged, and use the terminology of Microsoft business software. Labels are sent in batches of 40. A translation the model does not return, or returns empty, is skipped. Existing texts and comments in the target language are not changed.

docs.title: Find Unused Labels…
docs.text:
1. Run Find Unused Labels… and pick one of your label files.
  2. F&O Studio collects the uses of the file's labels from two sources:
  3. the cross-reference database: every @<File>:<Id> that X++ code references (as of the last build with cross references);
  4. the metadata XML of all your models (labels in properties of fields, EDTs, menu items, forms...). The label file folders themselves are skipped.
  5. When every label is used: "Every label of is used."
  6. Otherwise a multi-select picker lists the unused labels with their text and comment. Its title says how many there are and where F&O Studio looked.
  7. Select the labels to delete and confirm "Delete label(s) from every language of ?". The dialog warns that uses the cross-reference database cannot see (texts built at run time, other packages not built here) would show the raw label ID.
  8. The labels are removed from every language: "Deleted label(s) from ."

    Review the list before deleting. A label referenced only from a package that is not built on this machine, or built from a string at run time, looks unused.

docs.title: Export Labels…
docs.text:
1. Run Export Labels… and pick a label file (any model).
  2. Choose where to save the .csv file (default <file>.csv in the workspace folder).
  3. F&O Studio writes one row per label of the primary language with the columns Id, Comment, then one column per language, primary language first. Missing texts are empty.
  4. "Exported label(s) of in language(s)." Click Open to open the file.

    The file is UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel opens it with the right characters. Values with commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted (RFC 4180).

    Example:

    Id,Comment,en-US,de
ContosoOrderStatus,Status of the order,Order status,Auftragsstatus
ContosoReviewRequired,,Review required,

docs.title: Import Labels…
docs.text:
1. Run Import Labels… and pick one of your label files.
  2. Choose the CSV file. It needs an Id column and one column per language, as Export Labels… writes them; a Comment column is optional. Column names are not case-sensitive for Id and Comment; language columns must match the file's languages exactly.
  3. F&O Studio compares each row with the label file:
  4. rows with an empty ID, or an ID with characters other than letters, digits and _, are skipped;
  5. a label that does not exist yet is new;
  6. for an existing label, only texts that differ (and are not empty) are changed; a changed comment is saved with the primary language's text.
  7. When nothing differs: " already has every text of ."
  8. Confirm "Import into : new label(s), changed label(s)?". Labels that are not in the CSV stay as they are.
  9. A cancellable progress notification saves the labels. At the end: "Imported of label(s) into ." with the first failures, if any.

    An empty cell never deletes a text. To delete labels, use the Label Editor or Find Unused Labels….

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The label tools have no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Find Labels… is in src/d365Tools.ts; the other four are in src/labels.ts.
  • Label files and their languages are listed from the AxLabelFile folders of the models (<Id>_<language>.xml).
  • Reading uses bridge action read_label (Find Labels) or label_file_entries (the other tools, with all languages). Writing uses save_label and deleting delete_label; see Label Editor for how the server writes the label text files.
  • Translations are saved with the label file opened in its primary language, so the comment of the target language is left alone.
  • Translate Missing Labels… uses VS Code's language model API (vscode.lm) with a Copilot model; each batch is one request whose answer must be a JSON object mapping label IDs to translations.
  • Find Unused Labels… asks bridge action label_usage, which queries the cross-reference database's Names and References tables for /Labels/@<File>:<Id> targets that have at least one reference. It then scans the XML files of your custom models for @<File>:<Id>.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Find Labels… searches one label file and one language at a time, up to 100 matches.
  • Translate Missing Labels… translates from the primary language only, and only into languages the label file already has. The translations are machine translations; review them.
  • Find Unused Labels… only sees code uses recorded in the cross-reference database and metadata uses in your own models. It cannot see labels built from strings at run time or used by packages that are not on this machine.
  • Import Labels… does not add languages and does not delete labels or texts.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No chat model is available. Sign in to GitHub Copilot." Copilot is not signed in or has no chat model Sign in to GitHub Copilot in VS Code "The cross-reference database is not available: ..." The XRef database is missing or unreachable Check the environment setup; build with cross references (see Find All References) Many labels look unused that are in use The last build with cross references is old, or the code is in another package Build the models with cross references, then run it again "The CSV needs an "Id" column and one column per language, as Export Labels writes it." Missing Id column or no language columns Use the header row of Export Labels… " has no language. Its languages: ..." A language column the label file does not have Remove the column, or add the language to the label file A label file is missing from the picker Import, Translate and Find Unused only list label files of your models Use a label file of your model

docs.title: MCP Agent Tools
docs.text:
F&O Studio gives GitHub Copilot (and any other agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol) a set of xpp_* tools that work on the real D365FO metadata through Microsoft's metadata API, the same API Visual Studio uses. The agent reads, creates, extends, validates and builds elements with these tools instead of reading or writing AOT XML files. There is no Visual Studio equivalent: in Visual Studio, Copilot has no access to the metadata API.

This page explains what the tools are, how they reach Copilot, the guarantees they give and how they are registered. The tools themselves are described one by one on four pages:

Page Tools Agent-Tools-Metadata Read, create, update, validate and delete elements; find and list elements; models and environment; labels; the project Agent-Tools-Analysis References, examples, code search, message source, security and license, performance, traces, deprecations and upgrade, documentation, the development guide Agent-Tools-Reports SSRS precision designs: read, save, render, measure a scan, compare with a scan Agent-Tools-Build-and-Data Build, best practice, deployment package, Git changes, tests, business data, opening an element in the editor

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
You don't call the tools yourself. Copilot picks them when you ask it to work on X++ in agent mode, for example:

  • "Add a field ContosoPriority to CustGroup through a table extension in my model and put it on the CustGroup form."
  • "Who calls SalesFormLetter.construct? Show me how the callers use it."
  • "Which license does the role TradeSalesClerk need, and why?"
  • "Build my model and fix every error."

The F&O Studio agents (Copilot-Agents) are written around these tools, but the tools also work in plain Copilot agent mode and in other MCP hosts (MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio installed and an active D365FO configuration (see Connect-to-Environment or Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments). The server loads Microsoft's assemblies from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin of that configuration.
  • GitHub Copilot in VS Code, with agent mode. The tools appear under the MCP server F&O Studio in Copilot's tool picker.
  • A D365FO project (.rnrproj) for tools that add to a project or build with scope=project (D365FO-Projects).
  • The cross-reference database of the configuration for xpp_find_references, xpp_find_message_source and the [SysObsolete] part of xpp_find_deprecations.
  • Database credentials only for xpp_query_data (Database-Access).

docs.title: The two kinds of tools
docs.text:
Kind Tools Served by Available outside VS Code MCP tools 38 tools, from xpp_create_object to xpp_compare_layout XppVsCode.Server.exe over stdio Yes VS Code language model tools xpp_open_element, xpp_run_tests, xpp_query_data The extension (vscode.lm.registerTool) No

The three VS Code tools need the extension itself: xpp_open_element opens an editor, xpp_run_tests uses the extension's Dataverse sign-in, and xpp_query_data uses the database credentials the extension keeps. In Copilot chat you can reference them by name in a prompt: #xppOpenElement, #xppRunTests, #xppQueryData.

The server also serves one unlisted alias, xpp_update_current_object. It runs the same action as xpp_update_object and is not shown in tools/list.
