docs.title: How Copilot gets the tools
docs.text:
You don't configure anything. When the extension starts it registers an MCP server definition provider (contributes.mcpServerDefinitionProviders, id xpp.mcp, label "F&O Studio (Dynamics 365 F&O)"). VS Code asks the provider for the server and starts it when Copilot needs it:

server\bin\XppVsCode.Server.exe --config <active XPPConfig json> --activity-log [--project <rnrproj>] [--rules <.xpp\agent-rules.md>]
  • --config is the configuration of the environment selected in this window (Select-Environment).
  • --project is the active D365FO project of the workspace, when there is one.
  • --rules is the first workspace folder's .xpp/agent-rules.md (Team-Rules), when it exists.
  • --activity-log makes the server record each tool call for the Copilot-Activity view.

The provider gives the server a version made of the configuration, the project and the rules file's time stamp. When you switch environment, change xpp.project or edit the team rules, the version changes and VS Code restarts the server with the new arguments. If the provider can't read the active environment, it writes MCP server not started: ... to the F&O Studio output channel and offers no server.

When the server starts, its initialize answer carries the agent instructions: the built-in instructions (server/Resources/XppCopilotSystemPrompt.txt: tool-first rules, ownership, extensibility decision tree, workflow, naming and best practices) followed by your team rules, cut at 20,000 characters, under the heading TEAM RULES. The team rules refine the built-in rules where they are stricter.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text: The tools are built so an agent can't damage standard code or leave half-saved elements. These rules are enforced by the server, not left to the agent's instructions.

docs.title: Metadata goes through the metadata API
docs.text: Every read and write of elements goes through IMetaModelService and the disk metadata provider. Tool descriptions and the agent instructions forbid reading or writing metadata files with the terminal. Parameters are JSON only: XML or CDATA in methods or declaration is rejected with an error.

docs.title: Only your models change
docs.text:
Write actions are registered with a write kind (Edit, Create, Copy) and checked centrally before they run:

Write kind Check Message when refused Edit (update, delete, report design...) The element must belong to one of your models <Type> '<Name>' belongs to <model>, which you can't change. Create an extension in your model instead. Create, Copy The target model must be one of your models Model '<model>' is not one of your custom models. Create objects in your own model.

"Your models" means models whose package lives in the custom metadata folder of the configuration (the ModelStoreFolder) with a descriptor there. A partner's sealed model in that folder is still yours; a model in the reference packages is not. Label files are written only under the custom metadata folder.

docs.title: All or nothing
docs.text: xpp_create_object checks everything first (for example every relation: the related table and both fields must exist) and saves nothing when any part fails. After a create or update the server validates the result and adds a Validation: PASSED or Validation: FAILED line. A failed validation is reported as an error, with the hint to fix the element with xpp_update_object or delete it with xpp_delete_object.

docs.title: Copilot scope and checkpoints
docs.text:
The extension's commands Set Copilot Scope…, Start Copilot Checkpoint, Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… and End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes) write %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\agentSession.json. The MCP server reads it before every agent write:

  • Elements outside the scope are refused with a message that lists the allowed elements. New elements are allowed and join the scope.
  • While a checkpoint is open, the state of each element before its first change is saved, so the extension can restore it through the metadata API or delete elements the agent created.

See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

docs.title: Bounded output
docs.text: The agent's context is the budget, so outputs are capped: xpp_read_object returns a summary for objects over 25,000 characters and lets the agent ask for sections; searches have maxResults with small defaults and hard maximums; name scans stop after a few seconds and return partial results with a message; xpp_get_guide returns one topic.

docs.title: No business data and no secrets
docs.text: The MCP server Copilot starts never serves business data: the data service exists only in the extension's own server processes, which start with --allow-data. xpp_query_data runs in the extension, asks you to confirm each query, and the agent never sees the connection or credentials.

docs.title: Process and transport
docs.text:
XppVsCode.Server.exe is a .NET Framework 4.8 x64 console program. It reads one JSON-RPC message per line on stdin and writes one per line on stdout; logs go to stderr. Before it touches a D365FO type it registers an AssemblyResolve handler that loads assemblies from <FrameworkDirectory>\bin; no Microsoft assembly ships with F&O Studio.

Methods it answers:

Method Used by initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call Any MCP client xpp/bridge, xpp/lang, xpp/trace The extension (designers, code view, language features, trace panel) xpp/data The extension's own processes only (started with --allow-data)

docs.title: Parallel reads, ordered writes
docs.text: Tools registered as read-only (ParallelRead) run on worker threads, so a search doesn't wait behind another search. Other tools run in order. Calls that need the metadata API still take turns on one lock, because Microsoft's metadata provider is not thread-safe. Cross-reference queries don't use the metadata API and don't take the lock.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
Each tool is registered once in ToolRouter.RegisterTools (server/Ported/Tools/ToolRouter.cs) with a name, traits and a handler:

Trait Meaning ParallelRead Read-only; runs in parallel with other requests WritesElement Changes one element (objectType/objectName); the activity log keeps the element before and after Unlisted Served but not listed in tools/list (an alias)

The definitions agents see (description and input schema) are in server/Resources/Tools.json, embedded in the exe. At start McpToolRegistry.AttachDefinitions (server/Ported/Tools/McpTools.cs) matches the two: a definition without a registered tool, a listed tool without a definition, or a duplicate stops the server. tools/list is generated from the registry, so what agents discover and what the server serves can't drift apart.

Most metadata tools pass their arguments to a bridge action (server/Ported/MetaModel/MetaModelBridgeServer.cs): xpp_create_object → create_object, xpp_build → build, xpp_package → create_package. The bridge dispatcher applies the lock, the write policy, the agent scope and the error envelope from each action's registration. See Bridge-Protocol and Metadata-Server.

docs.title: Result format
docs.text:
Every tool returns MCP content: a text part and isError. xpp_render_report, xpp_measure_image and xpp_compare_layout add PNG image parts. An unknown tool name gets JSON-RPC error -32602.

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"xpp_find_object","arguments":{"objectName":"CustGroup","objectType":"AxTable","exactMatch":true}}}

docs.title: Activity log
docs.text: With --activity-log, each call appends one line to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activity.jsonl: time, tool, arguments (first 400 characters), duration, success, element. For WritesElement tools, the element file is copied to %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\snapshots before the call (the last 200 are kept) so the change can be shown as a diff. The log is halved when it passes 2 MB.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Windows only, with a D365FO configuration whose packages are on disk.
  • The metadata loads once per server process; the first call after a start waits for it.
  • Where-used, message source and obsolete-API checks are only as complete as the cross-reference database.
  • xpp_run_tests, xpp_query_data and xpp_open_element exist only inside VS Code.
  • The tools don't deploy or synchronize a UDE database: use Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No F&O Studio tools in Copilot's tool list The provider could not read the active environment (MCP server not started: ... in the output) Select or connect an environment; the provider offers the server again when the environment changes MetaModel bridge is not available. Check that the active D365FO configuration points to an extracted PackagesLocalDirectory. The configuration's packages are missing Finish Connect-to-Environment or fix the configuration ... belongs to <model>, which you can't change. Create an extension in your model instead. The agent tried to edit a standard or other-ISV element Expected: the agent must create an extension ... is outside the elements the user allows Copilot to change (F&O Studio: Set Copilot Scope) The element is not in the Copilot scope Add it with Set Copilot Scope… or clear the scope No active project. Select one with xpp_select_project. The server started without a project Open the project (D365FO-Projects) or let the agent call xpp_select_project A call timed out in the client but the element changed The server finished after the client gave up Read the element with xpp_read_object before retrying (the tool descriptions tell agents this) Unknown tool: ... The client calls a tool the server doesn't serve Update F&O Studio; check the name

docs.title: MCP Server Outside VS Code
docs.text:
F&O Studio's metadata server, XppVsCode.Server.exe, is a standard MCP server over stdio. Inside VS Code the extension starts it for Copilot. You can also run it on its own and connect it to another MCP host (an agent CLI, another editor, an agent framework), so that host's agent gets the same xpp_* tools on your D365FO metadata. Every GitHub release includes the server as a separate zip with its SHA-256 checksum for this purpose.

This page explains what is in the package, what the server needs, how to start and test it, and what is different from VS Code. For the tools themselves see MCP-Agent-Tools.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You use an agent other than GitHub Copilot in VS Code and want it to read, extend and build X++ through the metadata API.
  • You build your own automation (for example a review bot on a developer machine) that calls the tools over MCP.
  • You use F&O Studio's Claude Code plugin, which uses this server package for its tools and @fno-studio/core for cloud operations (Core-Library).

If you work in VS Code with F&O Studio installed, you don't need this page: the extension registers the server for Copilot automatically.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Requirement Why Windows, x64, .NET Framework 4.8 The server is a .NET Framework 4.8 x64 program A D365FO configuration on the machine The server reads it to find the metadata, the custom model folder and the cross-reference database PackagesLocalDirectory extracted, with its bin folder The server loads Microsoft's D365FO assemblies from <FrameworkDirectory>\bin at run time; none are shipped Git (optional) For xpp_diff_changes Cross-reference database (optional) For where-used, message source and obsolete-API checks Internet access to learn.microsoft.com (optional) For xpp_search_docs

A configuration is a JSON file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig. The machine gets one when you connect a unified developer environment with F&O Studio (Connect-to-Environment) or Visual Studio, or with runUdeSetup of the core library. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments see Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments.

docs.title: Get the server
docs.text:
1. Open the project's GitHub releases (https://github.com/nazmolla/xpp-vscode/releases) and pick the version.
  2. Download fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip and fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip.sha256.
  3. Check the checksum:
$expected = ((Get-Content .\fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip.sha256 -Raw) -split '\s+')[0]
$actual = (Get-FileHash .\fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected) { throw "Checksum mismatch" }
  1. Extract the zip to a folder of your choice, for example C:\Tools\FnoStudioServer.

What is in the zip: the content of the extension's server\bin folder, with XppVsCode.Server.exe and its XppVsCode.Server.exe.config. The release build refuses to package any .dll or Microsoft.Dynamics.* file, so the zip never holds a Microsoft assembly. The agent instructions, tool definitions and development guide are embedded in the exe.

The release build signs the exe only when code signing is configured for the repository; otherwise it ships unsigned. Check the signature with Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\XppVsCode.Server.exe and always check the SHA-256.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
XppVsCode.Server.exe [--config <XPPConfig json>] [--project <rnrproj>] [--rules <agent-rules.md>] [--activity-log]
Option Meaning --config <file> The configuration JSON to use. Without it, the server reads CurrentMetadataConfig under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations (the active configuration, shared with Visual Studio) --project <file> The active D365FO project: new elements are added to it, scope=project builds use it. Without it, the agent can pick one with xpp_select_project --rules <file> A team rules file (normally <repo>\.xpp\agent-rules.md), appended to the agent instructions (first 20,000 characters) --activity-log Record each tool call in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\activity.jsonl and keep element copies before writes in snapshots. VS Code's Copilot Activity view reads this file --allow-data Never use it for an MCP server. It turns on the business data service (xpp/data), which only F&O Studio's own processes use

The server speaks MCP over stdio: one JSON-RPC message per line on stdin and stdout. Logs go to stderr, starting with xpp-vscode server <version> | config <file> | project <file or none>. If no usable configuration is found, it logs No usable D365FO configuration (...) and exits with code 1.

docs.title: Connect it to an MCP host
docs.text:
Most MCP hosts take a command and arguments for a stdio server. The exact file and key names depend on the host; a typical entry looks like this:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fno-studio": {
      "command": "C:\\Tools\\FnoStudioServer\\XppVsCode.Server.exe",
      "args": [
        "--config", "C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Dynamics365\\XPPConfig\\<config>.json",
        "--project", "C:\\Repos\\ContosoExtensions\\ContosoExtensions.rnrproj",
        "--rules", "C:\\Repos\\ContosoExtensions\\.xpp\\agent-rules.md"
      ]
    }
  }
}

The server answers initialize with:

  • serverInfo.name xpp-vscode and the server version;
  • capabilities.tools;
  • instructions: the built-in agent instructions plus your team rules. Hosts that pass server instructions to the model give the agent the same rules Copilot gets in VS Code.

Then tools/list returns the 38 tools of server/Resources/Tools.json, and tools/call runs them.

docs.title: Test it by hand
docs.text:
Send a few lines and read the answers, always with a timeout so no session is left waiting:

$psi = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo 'C:\Tools\FnoStudioServer\XppVsCode.Server.exe'
$psi.Arguments = '--config "C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig\<config>.json"'
$psi.UseShellExecute = $false; $psi.RedirectStandardInput = $true; $psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true; $psi.RedirectStandardError = $true
$p = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($psi)
function Ask($line) {
    $p.StandardInput.WriteLine($line)
    $answer = $p.StandardOutput.ReadLineAsync()
    if ($answer.Wait(120000)) { $answer.Result } else { 'No answer within 2 minutes' }
}
Ask '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}}'
Ask '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"xpp_find_object","arguments":{"objectName":"CustGroup","objectType":"AxTable","exactMatch":true}}}'
$p.StandardInput.Close()
if (-not $p.WaitForExit(10000)) { $p.Kill() }

Each answer is one line of JSON. Read each answer before you close stdin: the server stops when stdin closes, and read-only tools answer from a worker thread. The first metadata call takes longer, because the metadata loads once per process.

The repository's scripts/smoke-test.ps1 does the same with 16 read-only tool calls; see Testing-the-Extension.

docs.title: What is different from VS Code
docs.text:
Feature In VS Code Outside VS Code The 38 MCP tools Yes Yes xpp_open_element, xpp_run_tests, xpp_query_data Yes (extension tools) No: they need the extension's editor, sign-in and database credentials Arguments kept up to date (environment, project, team rules) The extension restarts the server when they change You pass them; restart the server after a change Write limits to your own models, all-or-nothing creates, validation Yes Yes (enforced by the server) Copilot scope and checkpoints Set with the F&O Studio commands The server still reads %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\agentSession.json before agent writes when --activity-log is on, but only the VS Code extension writes that file and reverts checkpoints Activity log Copilot Activity view Only the activity.jsonl file, with --activity-log Report preview runtime F&O Studio: Install Report Preview Runtime xpp_render_report and xpp_compare_layout need the same runtime in %LOCALAPPDATA%\FOStudio\ReportViewer; install it once with the VS Code command

For deploy, database sync, tests and SQL credentials on a UDE outside VS Code, use the core library (Core-Library): it has deployPackages, syncDatabase, runTests and requestSqlCredentials with a sign-in your host provides.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Program.Main reads the configuration (from --config or the registry), registers AssemblyResolve to <FrameworkDirectory>\bin, and only then runs the code that uses D365FO types (server/Program.cs).
  • McpStdioServer reads stdin line by line; read-only tools run in parallel, everything else in order, and one lock guards the metadata API (server/McpStdioServer.cs).
  • Tools come from the registry in ToolRouter and the embedded Tools.json; the server refuses to start when the two differ (MCP-Agent-Tools).
  • The release workflow builds the server against Microsoft's compiler package, checks that server\bin holds no Microsoft DLL, zips it and writes the .sha256 (.github/workflows/release.yml). See Release-Process.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Windows only, on a machine with a D365FO configuration and its packages; the server does no cloud setup itself.
  • No sign-in: tools that need Dataverse or SQL credentials exist only in the VS Code extension or through the core library.
  • The server is unsigned unless the release was signed.
  • One server process serves one configuration; start another process for another environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The process exits at once with code 1; stderr says No usable D365FO configuration (...) No configuration in the registry, or the file passed with --config has no usable packages Pass --config with a valid configuration, or set up the environment first Tools answer MetaModel bridge is not available... The configuration points to a PackagesLocalDirectory that is missing or not extracted Finish the environment setup The host shows no tools The host could not start the process, or the arguments are wrong Check the command path and arguments; read the server's log on stderr xpp_find_references explains the cross-reference database is missing No XRef database for the configuration Restore it (Connect-to-Environment) No active project. Select one with xpp_select_project. Started without --project Pass --project or let the agent select one The report preview needs Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime The runtime is not installed Install it once with F&O Studio: Install Report Preview Runtime in VS Code

docs.title: Metadata Server
docs.text:
XppVsCode.Server.exe is F&O Studio's .NET Framework 4.8 (x64) server. It replaces what Visual Studio hosts for Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations development: the metadata services, the label store, the project system, cross-reference queries and the X++ parser. It is also the MCP server that gives Copilot its agent tools.

It loads Microsoft's D365FO assemblies from your own PackagesLocalDirectory\bin at run time; none of them ship with F&O Studio.

docs.title: When this page helps
docs.text:
• You want to know what runs when you open a designer, save code or let Copilot change an element.
  • You change the server and need to know where things are and what to test.
  • You run the server outside VS Code (see MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code).

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
XppVsCode.Server.exe --config <XPPConfig json> [--project <file.rnrproj>] [--allow-data] [--activity-log] [--rules <agent-rules.md>]
XppVsCode.Server.exe --sql-check ...
XppVsCode.Server.exe --restore-xref ...
Argument Effect --config The D365FO configuration to use instead of the registry's active one --project The active D365FO project (.rnrproj); project tools and "project only" builds use it --allow-data Serves business data (xpp/data) and Copilot checkpoint listing and revert. The extension passes it to its own processes only --activity-log Writes every tool call to activity.jsonl and enforces the Copilot scope and checkpoints. The extension passes it to the MCP server only --rules Appends the team's .xpp/agent-rules.md (up to 20,000 characters) to the MCP instructions --sql-check, --restore-xref Setup helpers for Connect to Environment (SQL Server LocalDB check, cross-reference database restore); no metadata is loaded

The server exits with code 1 and logs "No usable D365FO configuration" when the configuration has no FrameworkDirectory or no reference packages.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
server/Program.cs:

  1. Reads the configuration (DynamicsConfigurationReader): --config if given, else the registry's CurrentMetadataConfig. It takes ModelStoreFolder as the custom metadata folder, ReferencePackagesPaths as reference folders, and FrameworkDirectory.
  2. Registers AppDomain.AssemblyResolve to load assemblies from <FrameworkDirectory>\bin.
  3. Calls Run, marked NoInlining, so that D365FO types are resolved only after the handler exists.
  4. Run composes the services (see below), creates the bridge dispatcher, the in-process BridgeClient, the ToolRouter with its cross-reference actions, and the stdio server, and starts reading requests.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    STDIO["McpStdioServer<br/>(stdin/stdout, one JSON message per line)"]
    ROUTER["ToolRouter<br/>agent tools (Tools.json)"]
    CI["CodeIntel<br/>xpp/lang"]
    DATA["DataQueryService<br/>xpp/data"]
    TRACE["TraceService<br/>xpp/trace"]
    BC["BridgeClient (in-process)"]
    DISP["MetaModelBridgeServer<br/>action registry, lock, write policy"]
    SVC["BridgeServices<br/>MetaModelBridge, BuildService, ModelService,<br/>LabelService, ProjectPackageService, ..."]
    HOST["MetadataHost<br/>disk provider + IMetaModelService"]
    LBL["LabelStore"]
    PRJ["XppProject (.rnrproj)"]
    XREF["XRefQuery (cross-reference DB)"]

    STDIO -->|tools/list, tools/call| ROUTER
    STDIO -->|xpp/bridge| BC
    STDIO --> CI
    STDIO --> DATA
    STDIO --> TRACE
    ROUTER --> BC
    ROUTER --> XREF
    CI --> BC
    CI --> XREF
    BC --> DISP
    DISP --> SVC
    SVC --> HOST
    SVC --> LBL
    SVC --> PRJ

docs.title: Transport: McpStdioServer
docs.text:
server/McpStdioServer.cs reads one JSON-RPC message per line from stdin and writes one single-line response per request to stdout. Stdout is protocol only; logs go to stderr with a timestamp.

Method Answer initialize Protocol version (as requested, default 2025-06-18), capabilities.tools, serverInfo name xpp-vscode, and instructions: the embedded system prompt plus the team rules ping {} tools/list The listed agent tools with their definitions tools/call The tool's result xpp/bridge Raw JSON of a bridge action (for the extension) xpp/lang Language features (CodeIntel) xpp/data Business data; "Method not found" unless started with --allow-data xpp/trace Trace analysis (analyze, children, close)

Messages without an id (notifications) get no response. Unknown methods get error -32601; exceptions become -32603 with the message.

Concurrency: read-only tool calls (trait ParallelRead), xpp/data and xpp/trace run on the thread pool. Everything else runs in order on the reading thread. Calls that need the metadata API still take turns on the dispatcher's lock. Writes to stdout are locked so lines never interleave.

docs.title: The bridge dispatcher
docs.text: MetaModelBridgeServer registers every metadata action once, with its WriteKind. Dispatch takes the lock (the metadata provider is not thread-safe), applies the write policy and the agent scope, runs the handler and turns exceptions into {"success":false,"message":...}. Cross-reference actions are registered by ToolRouter.AddXRefActions with usesMetadata: false and run without the lock. Details: Bridge-Protocol.

docs.title: Services by role
docs.text:
server/Ported/MetaModel/MetadataServices.cs splits the metadata operations into role interfaces. Program.Run composes them into BridgeServices:

Role Interface Implementation Create, read, change, validate, delete elements IObjectStore MetaModelBridge Find elements, type schemas, form layout, environment IMetadataDiscovery MetaModelBridge Designer node tree, properties, node edits, drops, methods IElementDesigner MetaModelBridge Active project and items, C# references IProjectService MetaModelBridge Build, best practice, deployable package, table sync IBuildService BuildService Models and packages IModelService ModelService Label files ILabelService LabelService .axpp export and import IProjectPackageService ProjectPackageService Table relations (ERD, incoming relations) ITableRelations TableRelationsService Table data shape (labels, enums, per-company, date-effective) ITableDataShape TableDataShapeService Static performance findings IPerformanceAnalysis PerformanceAnalysisService Extension compatibility, wrapper drift, collisions IExtensionCompatibility ExtensionCompatibilityService SSRS report designs and preview IReportDesigns MetaModelBridge Write policy (custom models only) IWritePolicy MetaModelBridge Copilot scope and checkpoints IAgentSession MetaModelBridge; AgentWrites only with --activity-log, Checkpoints only with --allow-data

MetaModelBridge is split into partial files by section (Validation, Discovery, TypeOperations, Apply, Extract, ElementDesigner, FormRender, Reports, Security and more). MetaModelBridge.ElementTypes.cs is the table of element types with type-specific create, update and read code; types without an entry use the generic metadata-provider paths. Create saves a blank element and then applies the request through Update, so both share one code path.

docs.title: Host/: headless replacements for Visual Studio
docs.text: Class Replaces How MetadataHost Visual Studio's metadata services new MetadataProviderFactory().CreateDiskProvider(...) over the reference folders and the custom folder, then new MetaModelServiceFactory().Create(provider). New packages go to the custom folder (MetadataPath) LabelStore Label editor storage Reads and writes <root>\<Package>\<Model>\AxLabelFile\LabelResources\<lang>\<Id>.<lang>.label.txt (Id=Text, comment lines start with ;, sorted by ID). Writes only under the custom metadata folder; validates label file IDs and languages before building paths XppProject Project system Edits .rnrproj (MSBuild XML) the way Visual Studio saves it: <Content Include="AxClass\Name"> items, <Folder> entries, references to C# projects and assemblies ProjectReferences Visual Studio's build tasks Builds referenced C# projects with MSBuild and copies their run-time files into the package bin; same rules as the extension's src/dotnetReferences.ts ThreadHelper Visual Studio's UI thread checks No-op; the dispatcher serializes calls instead BridgeClient The HTTP bridge of the Visual Studio version In-process call to MetaModelBridgeServer.Dispatch DataQueryService, ReadOnlySql, QueryPlan none Business data (xpp/data: test, browse, query, plan, cancel) TraceService Trace Parser .etl analysis with the platform's event manifests ActivityLog none activity.jsonl and element snapshots for Copilot Activity SqlSetup Power Platform Tools setup LocalDB check and cross-reference restore Reports/* Report designer runtime Report preview, rendering and image measuring

docs.title: Metadata loading
docs.text: MetadataHost.EnsureLoaded loads the provider and the meta-model service once, under a lock, and publishes the pair only when both are complete. Microsoft's descriptor reader uses a process-wide dictionary without a lock; two loads at once fail with "An item with the same key has already been added". Background work, such as the form extension validator warm-up, must never trigger the first load. Reset() drops the cache so the next access sees files changed outside the process.

docs.title: Agent tools
docs.text:
ToolRouter (server/Ported/Tools/ToolRouter.cs) registers each tool with a handler and traits (McpTools.cs):

Trait Meaning ParallelRead Read-only; runs in parallel with other requests WritesElement Changes one element; the activity log keeps it before and after Unlisted Served but not in tools/list (an alias, such as xpp_update_current_object)

Tool definitions (name, description, input schema) are in server/Resources/Tools.json, embedded in the exe. AttachDefinitions checks that every definition has a registered tool and every listed tool has a definition; otherwise the server refuses to start. tools/list is generated from the registry. Tools.json currently defines 38 tools. See MCP-Agent-Tools.

Other tool classes: XRefQuery (where-used through SQL against the cross-reference database), ModelObjectLister (model contents from disk), CodeSearch, CodeExamples, MessageTrace, SecurityAnalysis, DeprecationReport, DocSearchHandler (Microsoft Learn only), ReportTools, ChangedElementsReport and AgentGuide.

docs.title: Builds run by the server
docs.text: The extension builds with xppc and LabelC itself (Build-Project-and-Model). The server has its own BuildService for the agent tools xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice and xpp_package: it runs LabelC.exe, xppc.exe, xppbp.exe and RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from the same bin folder. The bridge action sync_tables runs SyncEngine.exe for given tables on cloud-hosted and VHD environments.

docs.title: Analysis and tracing
docs.text:
• server/Analysis/PerformanceRules.cs holds the static performance rules (Performance-Rules-Reference).
  • server/Analysis/TraceAnalyzer.cs and server/Tracing/ (EtwFileReader, EventManifest) read .etl files without Trace Parser. The server keeps the most recent traces in memory so the panel can load calls the first report left out. See Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: Files the server writes

• Windows, x64, .NET Framework 4.8. It needs a D365FO installation (UDE metadata, cloud-hosted or VHD) whose bin folder has Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Metadata.dll.

  • Microsoft's X++ language server is not used; language features come from CodeIntel and the cross-reference database.

docs.title: Models, Packages and Versioning
docs.text: In D365FO, a model is a set of elements with a name, publisher, layer and version, and a package is the unit that is compiled, deployed and referenced. Every model belongs to one package; a package can hold one or more models. Your ALM decisions follow from that: packages decide what compiles into one assembly and what deploys together; models and their descriptors are what you put under source control. This page explains the concepts as they appear on disk, the F&O Studio commands that create and change models, and how versions are handled in packages and deployments.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You create the models of a new project and decide how to split them into packages.
  • You change a model's referenced packages because a new element uses another package.
  • You need a versioned deployable package and want to know which version ends up where.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with a custom metadata folder.
  • Model changes need the metadata server (it starts with the extension).

docs.title: Models and packages on disk
docs.text:
<custom metadata folder>\
  ContosoExtensions\                       <- package (module) "ContosoExtensions"
    Descriptor\
      ContosoExtensions.xml                <- descriptor of model "ContosoExtensions"
    ContosoExtensions\                     <- the model's elements
      AxClass\ ... AxTable\ ... AxForm\ ...
    bin\Dynamics.AX.ContosoExtensions.dll  <- the compiled package

The descriptor holds the model's name, display name, publisher, layer, version, description and the referenced packages (ModuleReferences). F&O Studio reads ModuleReferences to show dependencies and to find the build order of a team repository.

Concept Unit of In F&O Studio Package Compilation (one assembly), deployment, references Build Model builds the model's package; deploy and deployable packages pick packages; the model view of the Application Explorer shows the package name Model Ownership of elements, layer, publisher, version New elements go to the open project's model; projects (.rnrproj) belong to one model (<Model>) Referenced packages What the package may use Update Model Parameters…, View Model Dependencies…

General practice:

  • Extension models in their own packages. Since D365FO no longer allows overlayering of standard code, every custom model is an extension model in its own package that references the standard packages it extends.
  • Few packages, split by deployment and dependency, not by developer. Each package is a separate assembly and deployment unit. Split when parts must deploy separately (an ISV solution and its customer extensions) or when one part must not depend on another.
  • No cycles. Package A cannot reference B when B references A.

docs.title: Create Model…
docs.text:
Where: command palette, or the Dynamics 365 view (Create > Create Model…).

  1. Model name (letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter), for example ContosoExtensions.
  2. Publisher, for example Contoso.
  3. Layer: USR, CUS, VAR or ISV.
  4. Referenced packages: a multi-select list of all packages, with ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation and ApplicationSuite preselected.

F&O Studio creates the model through Microsoft's metadata API in a new package with the same name, version 1.0.0.0, customization set to Allow (an extension model). The message tells you to create a project for it with Create D365FO Project….

docs.title: Update Model Parameters…
docs.text:
Where: command palette, the Dynamics 365 view (Model and project), or the context menu of a model in the Application Explorer. Only your own models can be changed.

  1. Pick the model (when not started from a model node).
  2. Change the display name and description.
  3. Change the referenced packages: the list shows every package with the model's current references checked.

Add a reference when the compiler reports that a type of another package is unknown. Commit the changed descriptor with the elements that need it.

docs.title: View Model Dependencies…
docs.text: Shows a diagram with two branches: References (the packages the model references, from its descriptor) and Referenced by (the models whose descriptors reference this model's package). Use it before you remove a reference or move elements between packages. See Models and Model Dependencies.

docs.title: Export Project… and Import Project…
docs.text: Visual Studio's .axpp project export: a zip with the project, the model information and the project's elements. Import Project… shows how many elements the file holds, whether the model exists (it is created if not) and how many elements already exist, then offers Import and overwrite or Import new only. Useful to move a project between environments without source control; with a repository, prefer Git. See Export and Import Projects.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
There are three version numbers, used by different tools:

Version Where Who sets it Model version The model descriptor (major, minor, build, revision) Created as 1.0.0.0 by Create Model…. F&O Studio has no command to change it. In pipelines, Microsoft's Update Model Version task stamps it (general practice). Deployable package version The package created by RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 You enter it in Create Deployment Package… (default 1.0.0.0, format n.n.n.n), or the pipeline sets it. xpp_package defaults to 1.0.0.0 too. UDE deploy package version fnomoduledefinition.json in the zip uploaded by Deploy Models to Environment Computed from the current time, as Visual Studio and pac compute it. The zip is always named <Package>_1_0_0_1_managed.zip.

A common convention (general practice): the pipeline stamps the model versions and names the deployable package with the build number (for example ContosoFinOps-2026.11.25.3.zip), and the release tag in Git points at the commit that was built. That makes the package in LCS traceable back to the commit.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: No settings affect models or versions. The model folder is the custom metadata folder of the active configuration (see Select Environment).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Model commands: src/d365Tools.ts (createModel, updateModel, modelDependencies) call the bridge actions create_model, get_model, update_model and list_packages of the metadata server, which use IMetaModelService.CreateModel / UpdateModel (server/Ported/MetaModel/ModelService.cs).
  • Dependencies are read from the descriptors' ModuleReferences without the server.
  • Deployable package: RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin with -packageNames, -metadataDir, -modelDir, -binDir, -packageVersion and -outputDir, run as a VS Code task (see Create Deployment Package).
  • UDE deploy package: core/src/deploy.ts (moduleDefinition, packageVersion, zipName).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No command to change the model version or layer after creation, to rename a model or to move elements between models.
  • Create Model… always creates a new package; adding a model to an existing package is not offered.
  • Only custom models (in the custom metadata folder) can be changed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "A model named '...' already exists." Model names are unique across all packages. Choose another name. "Unknown package(s): ..." A referenced package is not in the metadata. Pick packages from the list only. "(model) is not one of your models." Update Model Parameters… on a standard model. Only custom models can be changed. Build error: a type from another package is unknown The model does not reference that package. Update Model Parameters…, add the package, build again.

docs.title: Models and Model Dependencies
docs.text: A model is the unit your elements belong to; a package (module) holds one or more models and is what xppc compiles into one assembly. F&O Studio covers Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 > Model Management: Create Model…, Update Model Parameters… and View Model Dependencies…. They read and write the model descriptor through Microsoft's metadata API, so Visual Studio sees the same models.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You start a new customization or ISV solution and need a model of your own.
  • The compiler cannot find a standard type (CustTable, SalesFormLetter, LedgerJournalTable) because your model does not reference its package.
  • You want to know which packages your model depends on, or which models depend on yours, before you remove a reference or move code.
  • You need to rename a model's display name or update its description.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An environment with metadata on this machine (Connect to Environment).
  • Create and update work only on your own models: models in the custom metadata folder (ModelStoreFolder). On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, where all packages share one folder, a package counts as standard when all its models have a publisher that starts with Microsoft.
  • No project is needed.

docs.title: Models in the Application Explorer
docs.text:
The Application Explorer's model view (Switch to Model View (Elements by Model)) lists every model by display name, your own models first with a package icon. The tooltip shows the display name, model name, package and folder. Right-click a model node for:

Action Shown on Update Model Parameters… Your own models View Model Dependencies… All models Upgrade Readiness Your own models (Upgrade Readiness) Standard Code Drift of Wrapped Methods… Your own models (Standard Code Drift)

The commands are also in the Dynamics 365 view: Create > Create Model…, and Model and project > Update Model Parameters…, View Model Dependencies… and Refresh Models. All three are in the Command Palette under F&O Studio.

docs.title: Create a model
docs.text:
1. Run Create Model….
  2. Create model (1/4) — the model name: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Example: ContosoExtensions.
  3. Create model (2/4) — the publisher, for example Contoso. It may be empty.
  4. Create model (3/4): layer — USR, CUS, VAR or ISV.
  5. Create model (4/4): referenced packages — a multi-select list of all packages, each with the display names of its models. ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation and ApplicationSuite are preselected. Pick every package whose elements your code uses or extends.
  6. F&O Studio creates the model and shows Created model ContosoExtensions in package ContosoExtensions. Create a project for it with F&O Studio: Create D365FO Project, or add objects to it from the agent tools.

The new model:

Property Value Name, package (module) The name you entered; the model gets its own new package Display name The name Publisher, layer As entered Version 1.0.0.0 Customization Allow Module references The packages you picked Folder <custom metadata folder>\<Name>\<Name>, with the descriptor in <custom metadata folder>\<Name>\Descriptor\<Name>.xml

Next: create a project for it and build once so the package exists for deployment.

docs.title: Update model parameters
docs.text:
1. Right-click your model in the model view and choose Update Model Parameters…, or run the command and pick one of your models.
  2. : display name — change or keep it.
  3. : description — change or keep it.
  4. : referenced packages — the package list with the current references checked. Check the packages to add, uncheck those to remove.
  5. F&O Studio saves the descriptor and shows Updated model .

    The publisher, layer and version are not changed by this command. A standard model gives is not one of your models.

    Adding a package reference is the fix when the build reports that a type from another package is unknown. Removing one fails the build if your code still uses that package; check with View Model Dependencies… and Find All References first.

docs.title: View model dependencies
docs.text:
1. Right-click any model and choose View Model Dependencies…, or run the command and pick a model.
  2. A panel titled Dependencies of [], package opens with two groups:
  3. References (n) — the packages the model references (outgoing), each marked package;
  4. Referenced by (n) — the models whose package references this model's package (incoming), with their model names.
  5. Like the other diagram panels, it can be exported as Mermaid (Hierarchy and Reference Diagrams).

    6. Example: for ApplicationSuite (display name Application Suite, folder Foundation), Referenced by lists every model that builds on top of it, standard and yours. For your model ContosoExtensions, References typically lists ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation, ApplicationSuite and whatever else you picked.

docs.title: Refresh
docs.text: Refresh Models (Dynamics 365 view) and Refresh Application Explorer read the model list from disk again, for example after Visual Studio or a Git pull added a model.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Model management has no settings. The models come from the active configuration; see Select Environment.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Commands: createModel, updateModel and modelDependencies in src/d365Tools.ts.
  • Create and update go to the metadata server (bridge actions create_model, update_model, get_model, list_packages), implemented by ModelService in server/Ported/MetaModel/ModelService.cs. It builds a ModelInfo and calls IMetaModelService.CreateModel or UpdateModel of Microsoft's metadata API, the same calls Visual Studio's model wizard makes. The disk provider writes the descriptor in the custom metadata folder. The server checks the name, that no model of that name exists, the layer, and that every referenced package exists (Unknown package(s): …). After a change it reloads the metadata so the new model is visible at once.
  • update_model refuses models that are not yours: Only your own models can be changed.
  • View Model Dependencies… does not call the server. It reads <ModuleReferences> from each model's descriptor file (<package>\Descriptor\<Model>.xml) and shows the result with the diagram panel of src/diagrams.ts.
  • Whether a model is yours: in the Application Explorer by the folder it is in (see Application Explorer); for write checks on the server by the same rule (IsCustomModel). Writes to standard models are refused everywhere (Security Model).
  • For agents, xpp_list_models and xpp_get_model_info return the models, their layer, version and dependencies (Agent Tools: Metadata).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Create Model always creates a new package with the model's name. Adding a model to an existing package (the old overlayering setup) is not offered.
  • The layer list offers USR, CUS, VAR and ISV.
  • Update Model Parameters does not change the publisher, layer, version or model name.
  • Models are not deleted from F&O Studio. Remove a model's folders yourself, or use Microsoft's tooling.
  • View Model Dependencies shows direct references only, not the full transitive chain.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A model named '…' already exists. The name is taken (also by a standard model) Choose another name Unknown package(s): … A referenced package is not in the active configuration Pick packages from the list only  is not one of your models. Update on a standard model Update your own model Build error: a standard type is not found Your model does not reference its package Update Model Parameters… and add the package A new model does not appear The model list is cached Refresh Models Create D365FO Project… says no custom model exists No model of yours in this configuration Create Model… first

docs.title: New Element
docs.text: New Element… creates an X++ element in your model, adds it to your project and opens it. It is the F&O Studio equivalent of Visual Studio's Solution Explorer Add > New Item. One picker lists every plain element type, every extension type and all the wizards, so you start every new piece of metadata from the same place.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need one new element: a class, table, EDT, enum, form, menu item, query, view, tile, menu, security object, configuration key, service or service group.
  • You need an extension of a standard element (table, form, enum, EDT, data entity, duty or role extension).
  • You need a Chain of Command class for a class, table, form, data entity, view or map.
  • You want a complete standard pattern (batch job, report, approval workflow, custom service, table with form, data entity, business event, number sequence, feature). The picker starts the matching wizard.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• F&O Studio is connected to an environment with metadata (see Connect to Environment). The metadata server must be running, because the name check and the creation go through it.
  • A D365FO project is open (see D365FO Projects). Without a project, F&O Studio asks which of your custom models gets the element, and the element is not added to a project.
  • The target model is one of your own models. Elements are never created in Microsoft's models.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Project view title bar The + button (shown when a project is open) Project view folder The inline + on a folder, or right-click the folder > New Element…. The folder's element type is preselected when the picker knows that type. Project view, empty project The hint node No elements yet: New Element… Dynamics 365 view Create > New Element… Command Palette F&O Studio: New Element… Open Element picker When no element matches the name you typed, the picker offers New Element named '...'…

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Run New Element….
  2. Pick the type in the New Element picker. Type to filter; the filter also matches the description line. Your last five choices are listed first under Recently used.
  3. What happens next depends on the type:
  4. Plain element: enter the name (see below). For an Extended Data Type you also pick the base type.
  5. Extension type (for example Table Extension): enter part of the name of the element to extend, pick it from the matches, then name the extension. This is the same flow as Create Extension.
  6. Code extension (Chain of Command): runs Create Code Extension.
  7. Wizards: runs the wizard (see the table below).
  8. F&O Studio creates the element in the model, adds it to the project and opens it: a class opens in the X++ code view, any other element in the Element Designer.

docs.title: The name prompt
docs.text:
The input box is titled New <type> in <model> and asks for a Name with your prefix. While you type, it checks:

  • The name is 3 to 61 characters of letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. Otherwise: Letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
  • No element of the same type has the name yet, in any model. A quarter of a second after you stop typing, it searches the metadata and shows, for example, CustGroup already exists in ApplicationSuite. You cannot accept a name that is taken.

Press Enter to create the element, or Escape to cancel. Nothing is created until you accept.

docs.title: Extended data type base types
docs.text: For Extended Data Type, a second picker titled New extended data type <Name>: base type asks for the base type: String, Int, Int64, Real, Date, UtcDateTime, Enum, Time, Guid or Container.

docs.title: Element types in the picker
docs.text: The picker groups types as follows. The description is the line shown under each entry.

docs.title: Code
docs.text: Entry Creates Class X++ class with an empty declaration: class <Name> { } Code extension (Chain of Command) final class wrapping a class, table or form (Create Code Extension)

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Entry Description in the picker Table table with fields, indexes and relations Table Extension add fields, indexes and field groups to a table View view over tables Query reusable query for forms, reports and batch jobs Data Entity Extension add fields to a data entity (and its staging table)

docs.title: Data types
docs.text: Entry Description in the picker Base Enum enumeration Extended Data Type extended data type: string, integer, real, date… Base Enum Extension add values to an extensible enum Extended Data Type Extension change label, help text or size of an EDT

docs.title: User interface
docs.text: Entry Description in the picker Form form Form Extension add controls and data sources to a form Display Menu Item opens a form Output Menu Item runs a report Action Menu Item runs a class Menu menu Tile workspace tile

docs.title: Reports, security, configuration and services
docs.text: Entry Description in the picker Report empty report: add datasets and designs in the designer Security Privilege grants menu items and data entities Security Duty groups privileges Security Role groups duties Security Duty Extension add privileges to a standard duty Security Role Extension add duties to a standard role Configuration Key switches a feature on or off Service service with operations Service Group publishes services

docs.title: Wizards
docs.text:
Wizards have a sparkle icon. Each one creates a set of elements in the project's model.

Entry Description in the picker Page Batch job (SysOperation) contract, service, controller, menu item, privilege Wizard Batch Job Report (wizard) temporary table, data provider, contract, controller, design Wizard Report Approval workflow workflow type, approval, handlers, menu items Wizard Approval Workflow Custom service service class, contracts, service group, privilege Wizard Custom Service Table with form key EDT, table, list form, menu item, View/Maintain privileges Wizard Table with Form Data entity entity, staging table, View/Maintain privileges Wizard Data Entity Business event contract, event class, table trigger Wizard Business Event Number sequence EDT, module reference, parameters method, table default Wizard Number Sequence Feature (Feature management) IFeatureMetadata class with isEnabled() Wizard Feature Management

Report and Report (wizard) are different. Report creates an empty report, as Visual Studio's Add New Item does; you then add datasets and designs in the Report Element Designer. Report (wizard) creates the whole chain: data provider, contract, controller, menu item and privilege.

docs.title: Example: a new enum
docs.text:
1. Click + on the project view.
  2. Type enum and pick Base Enum.
  3. Type ContosoOrderStatus. The box stays clear because no enum has that name.
  4. Press Enter. The enum is created in your model, added to the project and opened in the Element Designer, where you add its values.

docs.title: Example: a new EDT
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: New Element….
  2. Pick Extended Data Type.
  3. Type ContosoVehicleId and press Enter.
  4. Pick String as the base type.
  5. The EDT opens in the designer. Set Extends, Label and StringSize in the Properties grid.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
New Element has no settings of its own.

Setting Default Effect xpp.project (empty) The D365FO project of the workspace, set by Open D365FO Project. Its model receives new elements; without a project you pick a custom model.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The picker is built in src/scaffolding/newElement.ts. Each entry is a "kind": an element type, a group, a description and, for wizards and the code extension, the command to run instead.
  2. The last five kinds you used are stored in VS Code's global state (key xpp.newElement.recent).
  3. When the command comes from a project folder, the folder's element type is passed in and the picker is skipped for plain types.
  4. For extension types, F&O Studio looks up the base type (for example AxTableExtension extends AxTable, table in src/aot.ts), asks for the base element, then runs xpp.createExtension.
  5. The target model is the project's model, or a model you pick from your custom models (targetModel in src/d365Tools.ts).
  6. The name check uses the find_object bridge action with an exact match.
  7. Creation is the create_object bridge action on the metadata server. The server creates the element through Microsoft's metadata API (never by writing XML), refuses names that already exist (... already exists (model ...). Nothing was changed), and reloads the metadata so the new element is visible right away.
  8. add_to_project adds the element to the .rnrproj the way Visual Studio saves it, then the trees refresh.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• New Element creates an empty element. Fields, methods, controls and properties are added afterwards in the designer or the code view.
  • Only the types in the picker are offered. Other types (for example workflow elements, maps, labels) are created by the wizards, by Copilot, or not at all.
  • The Report entry gives an empty report; use Report (wizard) for a working report.
  • Elements go only to your own models.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ... already exists in ... under the name An element of that type already uses the name, possibly in a standard model Choose another name, usually with your prefix Letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. The name has spaces, dots or starts with a digit, or is shorter than 3 characters Use a valid X++ name You are asked for a model No D365FO project is open Open a project, or pick the model; the element is then not added to a project ... already exists (model ...). Nothing was changed after Enter Someone created the element between the check and the creation Choose another name Could not resolve model ... The project points to a model that does not exist in the active configuration Check the environment with Select Environment

docs.title: Open Element
docs.text: Open Elementâ€¦ finds any element of any model by name and opens it, the way a click in the Application Explorer does. It shows the elements you opened recently, ranks exact and prefix matches first, and narrows the search to one element type with a short prefix such as t: for tables. It replaces Visual Studio's habit of filtering Application Explorer or using metadata search to jump to a known element.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You know the element name, or part of it: CustGroup, SalesFormLetter, PurchTable.
  • You want only one type: the table SalesTable and not the dozens of SalesTable* classes.
  • You want to reopen something you looked at a minute ago.
  • You want to open an element beside the current editor, view a table's code directly, or add one of your elements to the project without leaving the keyboard.

To browse by type or model, use the Application Explorer. To search inside code, use Search Code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Metadata of an environment on this machine (Connect to Environment, or a cloud-hosted / VHD environment).
  • The search runs in the F&O Studio metadata server. The first search after the window opens can take a few seconds while the server loads the metadata.
  • No project is needed. The Add to Project button needs an open project (D365FO Projects).

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Keyboard Ctrl+Alt+O Application Explorer title bar Open Elementâ€¦ button D365FO Project title bar Open Elementâ€¦ button Dynamics 365 view Find > Open Elementâ€¦ Command Palette F&O Studio: Open Elementâ€¦ Walkthrough Find an element step of Get started

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+Alt+O. The picker titled Open Element opens.
  2. With an empty box, the picker lists Recently opened elements (up to 15, kept per workspace). Pick one to open it again.
  3. Type at least 3 characters of the name. After a short pause the results appear, up to 50.
  4. Each result shows an icon for its type, the name, and a description with the type and model, for example Table Â· Application Suite. Elements of your own models are marked (yours).
  5. Press Enter (or click) to open the selected element:
  6. a class opens in the X++ Code View;
  7. a label file opens in the Label Editor;
  8. any other element opens in the Element Designer.

If you press Enter before the results arrive, F&O Studio runs the search at once and opens the element when the name identifies one: an exact name match that is unique, or a single result.

docs.title: Type prefixes
docs.text:
Start the text with a letter and a colon to search one kind of element:

Prefix Searches Example c: Classes c:SalesFormLetter t: Tables t:SalesTable f: Forms f:CustTable e: Extended data types e:CustGroupId n: Base enums n:SalesStatus q: Queries q:Cust v: Views v:Cust d: Data entities d:CustCustomerV3Entity m: Display, action and output menu items m:CustTable s: Security roles, duties and privileges s:TradeSalesClerk x: Table, form, enum, EDT and data entity extensions x:CustTable

The 3-character minimum applies to the text after the prefix. A space after the colon is allowed (t: CustGroup).

docs.title: Buttons on each result
docs.text:
Hover a result to see its buttons:

Button Shown for What it does View Code Tables, forms, views, data entities, queries, maps (classes open in code anyway) Opens the element's X++ code view instead of its designer Open to the Side All elements Opens the designer (or a class's code) in the editor group beside the current one Add to Project Elements of your own models Adds the element to the open project; the picker stays open so you can add more

Each button also adds the element to the recent list.

docs.title: When nothing matches
docs.text: If no element matches, the picker shows one entry, New Element named ''â€¦. Pick it to start New Element.

docs.title: How the results are ranked
docs.text:
The metadata server collects every element whose name contains the text (case-insensitive), across all element types or the prefix's types, then sorts them:

  1. the exact name first;
  2. then names that start with the text;
  3. then shorter names.

This is why SalesTable finds the table SalesTable at the top and not one of the many classes whose name contains it. The search stops collecting after 5,000 candidates or a time budget, and returns at most 50 results. Type more of the name when the element you want is not in the list.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Open Element has no settings. The keyboard shortcut is Ctrl+Alt+O (command xpp.openObject); change it in Keyboard Shortcuts like any VS Code binding.

The recent list is stored in the workspace state, so each project workspace has its own list.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The picker is openObject in src/navigation.ts. It is a VS Code quick pick that searches 300 ms after you stop typing.
  • Each search sends the bridge action find_object (objectName, exactMatch: false, maxResults: 50, and objectType when the prefix names one type) to the metadata server. The server's FindObject (in MetaModelBridge.Discovery.cs) walks the element names of Microsoft's metadata API per type, ranks them as described above, and returns the type, name, model and whether the model is yours.
  • When a prefix covers several types (m:, s:, x:), the extension filters the results to those types.
  • Opening uses the same rule as the Application Explorer (elementOpenCommand in src/aot.ts): vscode.open on xpp:/AxClass/<Name>.xpp for classes, Open Designer for the rest.
  • The recent list (key xpp.openObject.recent) keeps the last 15 elements opened from the picker, newest first, without duplicates.

docs.title: For Copilot
docs.text: Copilot does not use the picker. It finds elements with the agent tool xpp_find_object and shows them to you with xpp_open_element, which opens an element in the code view (at a method or a piece of text) or in the designer, the same way. See Agent Tools: Metadata.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• At least 3 characters are needed, after the prefix.
  • Results are capped at 50. A very common fragment such as Cust does not list everything; use a longer name or a prefix.
  • The search matches element names only. It does not search labels, properties or code. Use Search Code, Find Labels or Find Message Source for those.
  • Sub-nodes (fields, methods, controls) are not results. Open the element and use the designer or the code view's outline (Outline and Workspace Symbols; Ctrl+T finds Class.method).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The list stays empty while you type Fewer than 3 characters after the prefix Type more Only New Element named 'â€¦' appears No element name contains the text, or the prefix limits the types Check the spelling; remove the prefix The first search is slow The metadata server loads the metadata on the first request Wait; later searches are fast The element is not in the results More than 50 matches; it was ranked lower Type the full name or use a type prefix Add to Project fails No project is open, or the element is not in the project's model Open a project for that model (D365FO Projects)

docs.title: Open Team Repository
docs.text:
Open Team Repository… gets a new developer from "here is our Git repository" to "everything is built and the project is open" in one command. It clones a repository (or uses a folder already on the machine), finds the D365FO packages in it, links them into your custom metadata folder with directory junctions, builds them in dependency order and opens the repository's project. It automates what teams usually do by hand for Visual Studio: create junctions from PackagesLocalDirectory (or the custom metadata folder) to the packages in the source-controlled folder.

This feature is a preview: it has not been verified on a real team repository yet.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You join a team and need its models on your machine.
  • You set up a new environment or machine and want the team's packages linked and built.
  • You cloned the repository yourself and now want the packages linked and built.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active environment: a unified developer environment connected with Connect to Environment, or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments). The packages are linked into its custom metadata folder (ModelStoreFolder).
  • For cloning: VS Code's Git extension and access to the repository. The clone uses VS Code's Git sign-in.
  • The repository holds package folders in the usual layout: <Package>\Descriptor\<Model>.xml, plus the element folders (AxClass, AxTable...). A typical layout is Metadata\<Package>\....

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Open Team Repository… from the Command Palette, or from the Dynamics 365 view: Model and project > Open Team Repository….
  2. Choose the source:
  3. Clone a Repository…: enter the URL (https://... or git@...; the placeholder shows an Azure DevOps URL such as https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo), then pick the parent folder and click Clone Here. VS Code's Git extension clones the repository and returns the new folder.
  4. Use a Folder Already on This Machine…: pick the repository folder and click Use Repository.
  5. A multi-select list titled Packages to link into shows the packages found. Each shows its name and its path in the repository. All are checked; uncheck the ones you do not want.
  6. F&O Studio links each package, refreshes the Application Explorer and builds the packages in dependency order. A cancellable notification Building the team's packages shows <package> (n/m). Build output goes to X++ Build and errors to the Problems view, as for Build Project and Model.
  7. A summary appears, for example "Linked 3 package(s) into C:\CustomXppMetadata...; all built." or "...; build failed for ContosoExtensions (see Problems).", with buttons:
  8. UDE: Deploy (Deploy to Environment) and Synchronize Database (Synchronize Database).
  9. Cloud-hosted or VHD: Synchronize Database.
  10. If the repository contains .rnrproj projects, F&O Studio opens one: the only one directly, or the one you pick from Open a project of the repository (up to 20 are listed).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A repository with this layout:

contoso-fno/
  .xpp/workspace.json
  Metadata/
    ContosoCore/
      Descriptor/ContosoCore.xml
      ContosoCore/AxClass/...
    ContosoExtensions/
      Descriptor/ContosoExtensions.xml      (references ContosoCore and ApplicationSuite)
      ContosoExtensions/AxClass/...
  Projects/
    ContosoExtensions/ContosoExtensions.rnrproj

Open Team Repository links C:\CustomXppMetadata...\ContosoCore and ...\ContosoExtensions to the two folders, builds ContosoCore first and ContosoExtensions second (its descriptor references ContosoCore; ApplicationSuite is a standard package and is already built), then opens ContosoExtensions.rnrproj.

docs.title: The .xpp/workspace.json file
docs.text:
The first time packages are linked from a repository, F&O Studio writes .xpp/workspace.json at the repository root with the packages you chose, as paths relative to the root:

{
  "packages": [
    "Metadata/ContosoCore",
    "Metadata/ContosoExtensions"
  ]
}

Commit it. The next developer who opens the repository gets exactly these packages offered, instead of a search. The file is never overwritten once it exists; edit it by hand when the team adds a package.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings specific to this command. The build uses the build settings (for example xpp.build.msbuildPath for C# references, xpp.build.restartLocalAos on cloud-hosted and VHD environments); see Settings Reference.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The command is in src/teamRepository.ts.

docs.title: Finding packages
docs.text:
1. If .xpp/workspace.json lists packages, those folders are used (only folders inside the repository that exist).
  2. Otherwise the repository is searched up to 4 levels deep for folders that contain a Descriptor folder. Folders starting with ., and node_modules, bin and obj, are skipped. The search does not go below a package folder.
  3. For each package, the model descriptors (Descriptor\*.xml) are read and the package names in <ModuleReferences> are collected.

If no package is found: "No D365FO packages found in (folders with a Descriptor folder holding model descriptors)."

docs.title: Linking
docs.text:
For each chosen package, a directory junction <custom metadata folder>\<package name> → <repository>\...\<package> is created. If something with that name already exists:

  • a junction to the same repository folder is left as it is;
  • anything else (a real folder, or a link to another place) is left untouched, and the summary says ": already exists and is not a link to this repository; it was left as it is."

    Junctions do not need administrator rights. Because the files stay in the repository folder, every change you make in F&O Studio (or Visual Studio) shows up in Git.

docs.title: Build order
docs.text: The chosen packages are sorted so that referenced packages come first. References to packages outside the repository (standard packages) are ignored because they are already built. Cycles do not loop. Each package is built with the same build as Build Models…; a failed build is recorded and the next package is still built. Cancel stops the build; the remaining packages are not built.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview; not verified on a real team repository.
  • Does not create branches, pull or switch branches. Use VS Code's Git features or Branching and Team Workflow.
  • Existing folders with the package's name in the metadata folder are not replaced. Remove them yourself if they are old copies.
  • .xpp/workspace.json is written only once; it is not updated when you later choose other packages.
  • Only up to 20 projects are listed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "An https:// or git@ URL." The URL does not start with https:// or git@ Enter the clone URL from Azure DevOps or GitHub. "No D365FO packages found in ..." No Descriptor folder within 4 levels, or .xpp/workspace.json lists paths that do not exist Check the layout; fix or remove .xpp/workspace.json. "... already exists and is not a link to this repository; it was left as it is." A folder or another junction with the package name is in the metadata folder Rename or delete it (keep a copy), then run the command again. "build failed for ... (see Problems)" Compile errors, or a package depends on another that is not linked Fix the errors, or link the missing package; build again with Build Models…. "No active D365FO configuration found..." No environment on this machine Run Connect to Environment… first.

docs.title: Open in SSMS
docs.text: Open Database in SQL Server Management Studio starts SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) connected to the same database F&O Studio uses: the local AxDB with Windows authentication on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, or the unified developer environment's Azure SQL database with the JIT credentials F&O Studio requested. The password is put on the clipboard, never on a command line. Use it when you need what the SQL Query Panel does not offer: graphical plans, actual execution plans, Activity Monitor, or longer scripts.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want the graphical or actual execution plan, beyond the summary of Explain Plan.
  • You need SSMS tools: Object Explorer, Activity Monitor, Query Store reports, index properties.
  • You prefer SSMS's editor for a long investigation script.

For a quick look at rows, Browse Table Data and the SQL Query Panel stay inside VS Code and are read-only by default. SSMS is not.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• SQL Server Management Studio installed under Program Files or Program Files (x86) in a folder named Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio <version>. F&O Studio finds SSMS 21 and later (under Release\Common7\IDE) and older versions (under Common7\IDE), and starts the newest.
  • Database access for the active environment. See Database Access. On a unified developer environment, F&O Studio asks for JIT credentials if there are none.
  • On a UDE, your public IP address must be within the addresses you allowed when requesting the credentials.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Run it from one of these places:
  2. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Open Database in SQL Server Management Studio.
  3. Database menu: click the database item in the status bar, or Dynamics 365 view > Data > Database…, then Open in SQL Server Management Studio.
  4. On a UDE, a notification says: "The database password is on the clipboard: paste it in SSMS's sign-in, then clear the clipboard."
  5. SSMS receives the connection on its command line:
  6. Server: the database server.
  7. Database: the business database.
  8. Sign-in: Windows authentication on a local database, SQL Server authentication with the JIT user name on a UDE.
  9. On a UDE, SSMS needs the password: paste it (Ctrl+V) when SSMS asks for it, and connect.
  10. When you are done, clear the clipboard (for example, copy something else).

docs.title: Getting the details by hand
docs.text: If SSMS is installed somewhere else, or you use another client (Azure Data Studio, the mssql extension, sqlcmd), use F&O Studio: Copy Database Connection Detail. It lets you copy Server, Database, and, on a UDE, User name and Password, one at a time. See Database Access.

docs.title: What to do in SSMS that the panel does not
docs.text:
Task In SSMS In F&O Studio instead Graphical estimated plan Query > Display Estimated Execution Plan Explain Plan gives a text summary Actual plan with real row counts Query > Include Actual Execution Plan, then run Not available (the panel never runs a query to get its plan) Query Store reports Object Explorer > the database > Query Store "Most expensive queries" in Database Performance Insights Scripts with variables or temporary tables Any query window Not possible in read-only mode (DECLARE, INTO are refused) Browse a table with labels and enum names Not available Browse Table Data Follow relations between records Write the joins yourself The record inspector in Browse Table Data

With Reader credentials on a UDE, some of these may be refused by the database's permissions.

docs.title: Be careful in SSMS
docs.text:
SSMS is not limited the way F&O Studio's panel is:

  • With Writer credentials or on a local database, statements you run are committed unless you wrap them in a transaction yourself.
  • Changes made in SQL skip X++ business logic: insert/update/delete methods, validation, the database log, events, number sequences and the server's caches.
  • Request Reader credentials when you only need to read.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for SSMS. The connection comes from Database Access.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/database/ssms.ts:

  1. F&O Studio gets the database target: the local server and database from the active configuration, or the stored JIT credentials (asking for them if needed).
  2. It looks in %ProgramFiles% and %ProgramFiles(x86)% for folders named Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio <n>, checks <folder>\Release\Common7\IDE\SSMS.exe and <folder>\Common7\IDE\Ssms.exe, and takes the highest version that exists.
  3. It starts SSMS detached from VS Code with:
  4. -S <server> -d <database> -E for Windows authentication, or
  5. -S <server> -d <database> -U <user> for SQL authentication. The password is written to the clipboard instead of the command line, where other processes on the machine could read it.
  6. If SSMS fails to start, an error shows the reason.

SSMS connects to the database directly; F&O Studio's server process is not involved.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only SSMS is started. Other clients need the details from Copy Database Connection Detail.
  • SSMS installations outside Program Files folders with the standard name are not found.
  • The JIT credentials expire. An open SSMS session stops working when they do; request new credentials and connect again.
  • The password is on the clipboard until you replace it; clipboard history tools may keep it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "SQL Server Management Studio was not found. Install it, or use New SQL Query here." No SSMS in the expected folders Install SSMS, or use the SQL Query Panel or Copy Database Connection Detail "SSMS could not start: …" Windows could not start the executable Check the SSMS installation SSMS sign-in fails on a UDE right after requesting credentials Azure SQL applies the firewall rule and password within minutes Wait a minute and connect again SSMS sign-in fails later Credentials expired or replaced, or your public IP changed Run Request Database Credentials and open SSMS again SSMS asks for a password Expected with JIT credentials: it is on the clipboard Press Ctrl+V in the password box
