docs.title: Outline and Workspace Symbols
docs.text: The outline lists the members of the element in the active code view: the fields of its declaration and its methods. It feeds VS Code's Outline view, the breadcrumbs above the editor and Go to Symbol in Editor. Go to Symbol in Workspace (Ctrl+T) finds elements and methods across all models by name, from the cross-reference database. Together they replace the method list of Visual Studio's code editor and part of its metadata search.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Jump to a method in a long class such as SalesFormLetter or SalesTable without scrolling.
  • See where you are in the code: the breadcrumbs show the element and the method around the cursor.
  • Open CustGroup.find or SalesFormLetter.run from anywhere, by typing part of the name.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• For the outline: an X++ document. The element node and the fields appear in a code view (xpp:); other X++ documents list their methods.
  • For workspace symbols: the cross-reference database (see Find All References).
  • xpp.codeIntelligence.outline and xpp.codeIntelligence.workspaceSymbols on (the defaults).

docs.title: Outline view and breadcrumbs
docs.text:
1. Open a code view, for example CustGroup.xpp.
  2. Open the Outline view in the Explorer side bar. It shows one root node, the element (a table shows as a structure, other elements as a class, with the element type such as Table or Class as detail), with:
  3. the fields declared before the first method, with their types (CustGroupId custGroupId);
  4. the methods, in code order, with the text of the signature before the name as detail (public static CustGroup).
  5. Click an entry to move the cursor there. Use the Outline view's Follow Cursor and sorting options as usual.

The breadcrumbs above the editor show AxTable > CustGroup.xpp > CustGroup > find. Click a part to pick another method.

A nested method document (a form data source or control method) shows just that method, without a root node.

docs.title: Go to Symbol in Editor
docs.text: Run Go to Symbol in Editor and type part of a method name. Type @: to group by kind (fields, methods).

docs.title: Go to Symbol in Workspace
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+T (or run Go to Symbol in Workspace).
  2. Type at least two characters:
  3. CustGr finds elements whose name starts with it, such as the CustGroup table and form;
  4. CustGroup.find, CustGroup:find or CustGroup::find finds methods: elements starting with CustGroup and methods starting with find.
  5. Each result shows the name, its kind (class or method) and the element type or the owning element.
  6. Pick one. An element opens in its code view; a method opens at its signature line.

Results come in this order of element types: classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, maps, queries. The server returns up to 100 names (enums, EDTs and menu items among them are left out of the list).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.outline true Outline, breadcrumbs and Go to Symbol in Editor xpp.codeIntelligence.workspaceSymbols true Go to Symbol in Workspace (Ctrl+T) over elements and methods of all models

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Outline. symbols in src/codeIntel/providers.ts runs in the extension, without a server call:

  • the methods come from methodSpans in src/xppSource.ts, the same parser the code view uses to save; each method range runs to the line before the next method, and the selection is the method name on its signature line;
  • macro lines of the declaration (#define...) are not listed;
  • fields are lines before the first method that look like Type name; or Type name = value;, with optional modifiers (public, private, static, const...) and array brackets; keywords are not taken as types, primitive types (int, str, real...) are.

Workspace symbols. workspaceSymbols sends symbols to the code intelligence server process. Symbols in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs runs prefix searches on the Names table of the cross-reference database, one per element folder (/Classes/CustGr%, /Tables/CustGr%...). With a . or : in the query it searches /Classes/<prefix>%/Methods/<prefix>%. The search uses the path index, so it is fast even over the whole application. When you pick a method, the extension finds its signature line in the code view.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Workspace symbols match the beginning of names, not the middle; use Open Element (Ctrl+Alt+O) to search inside names, or Search Code for text.
  • Workspace symbols cover elements with code (classes, tables, forms, views, data entities, maps, queries). For enums, EDTs, menu items and other types use Open Element.
  • Only elements in the cross-reference database are found: a new element appears after a build with cross references.
  • The outline is built from the text; a field declared on several lines, or several fields on one line, may be listed incompletely.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The Outline view is empty xpp.codeIntelligence.outline is off, or the braces don't balance Turn the setting on; fix the braces (the syntax check shows where) Ctrl+T finds nothing for an X++ name Fewer than 2 characters typed, workspaceSymbols off, or the cross-reference database not usable Type more; turn the setting on; see Find All References Your new class is not found by Ctrl+T Not built with cross references yet Build the project, or use Open Element…

docs.title: Performance Rules Reference
docs.text:
This page lists every rule of Analyze Performance and of the agent tool xpp_analyze_performance: what each rule detects, why it matters, the fix, and an example of slow code next to the faster version. The rule id is what you see in the Problems view after X++ performance, for example X++ performance(QueryInLoop).

The rules are heuristics over source text and metadata. They do not know row counts. A finding on a loop over a few setup rows can be harmless; the same finding on a loop over transactions is often the main cost of a process. Confirm with a trace (Analyze Trace) or the data (Database Performance Insights) before large changes.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Rule id Severity Applies to In short QueryInLoop Warning Methods A select, while select or set-based statement inside a loop. RowOperationInLoop Info Methods insert(), update(), delete(), doInsert(), doUpdate(), doDelete() or write() on a table buffer inside a loop. UnbalancedTransaction Warning Methods ttsbegin and ttscommit/ttsabort counts differ in the method. CrossCompany Info Methods crossCompany without a company list. AllFields Info Methods while select without a field list. ForUpdateWithoutWrite Warning Methods select forUpdate on a buffer the method never updates or deletes. RowByRowFallback Warning Methods insert_recordset, update_recordset or delete_from that the table forces to run row by row. NoMatchingIndex Info Methods A where clause with == on fields that no index of the table starts with. TableCache Warning or Info Tables CacheLookup that does not fit the TableGroup. UncachedDisplayMethod Info Forms A display method in a grid without cacheAddMethod. OnlyFetchActive Warning (lookup forms) or Info Forms A data source that reads every field but shows a few, only in grids. FormLinkType Warning or Info Forms A joined data source with LinkType Delayed or Active where a join would do. EntityPublicNames Warning Data entities Public entity without PublicEntityName or PublicCollectionName. EntityKey Warning Data entities No entity key. EntityStaging Warning Data entities Data management enabled without a staging table, or the staging table does not exist. EntityStagingFields Warning Data entities Entity fields missing from the staging table. EntityMandatoryFields Warning Data entities Mandatory fields of the root table that the entity does not map. EntitySetBased Warning or Info Data entities Set-based processing that cannot work, or code that set-based imports skip.

Method rules run on the methods of every analyzed element (class, table, form and data entity). Findings of the element-level rules show the method as (table), (form) or (entity) and point to the first line of the code view.

docs.title: How loops are recognized
docs.text: A loop is the { } body after while, for, do or while select. Nested loops count. A loop body without braces is not tracked. Comments, strings and labels are ignored.

docs.title: How table buffers are recognized
docs.text: A variable is a table buffer when it is declared with a table type in the method or in the class declaration, for example SalesLine salesLine; or a parameter CustTable _custTable. Buffers declared with var are not recognized.

docs.title: QueryInLoop
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: every method.

Detects one of these inside a loop body:

  • a select statement (the message says select firstonly inside a loop when the select has firstOnly);
  • a while select (a nested loop of queries);
  • an insert_recordset, update_recordset or delete_from.

Why it matters. Each query is a round trip to SQL Server. A query inside a loop runs once per row of the loop, so a loop over 50,000 rows sends 50,000 queries. The round trips, not the queries themselves, are usually the cost.

Fix.

  • For select and while select: join the tables in one while select (join, exists join, notexists join), or move the query out of the loop.
  • For a lookup with firstOnly: join the looked-up table into the outer while select, or use exists join / notexists join when only its existence matters.
  • For set-based statements: widen the where clause (or join) so one statement covers every row.

Slow:

SalesLine salesLine;
InventTable inventTable;

while select salesLine
    where salesLine.SalesId == _salesId
{
    select firstonly inventTable
        where inventTable.ItemId == salesLine.ItemId;

    if (inventTable.ItemType == ItemType::Service)
    {
        // ...
    }
}

Faster:

SalesLine salesLine;
InventTable inventTable;

while select salesLine
    where salesLine.SalesId == _salesId
    join ItemType from inventTable
        where inventTable.ItemId == salesLine.ItemId
           && inventTable.ItemType == ItemType::Service
{
    // ...
}

Set-based statement in a loop, and the fix:

// Slow: one update_recordset per customer group
while select custGroup
{
    update_recordset custTable
        setting Blocked = CustVendorBlocked::All
        where custTable.CustGroup == custGroup.CustGroup;
}

// Faster: one statement for every row
update_recordset custTable
    setting Blocked = CustVendorBlocked::All
    exists join custGroup
        where custGroup.CustGroup == custTable.CustGroup;

docs.title: RowOperationInLoop
docs.text:
Severity: Info. Applies to: every method.

Detects a call to insert(), update(), delete(), doInsert(), doUpdate(), doDelete() or write() on a table buffer, inside a loop.

Why it matters. Each call is one database round trip and, for insert()/update()/delete(), runs the table's own logic for each row. When every row gets the same change, one set-based statement does the work in a single round trip.

Fix.

  • Inserts: use insert_recordset, or collect the rows in a RecordInsertList (or RecordSortedList) and insert them at once.
  • Updates: use update_recordset when every row gets the same change.
  • Deletes: use delete_from when every row is deleted.

It is Info, not Warning, because the row-by-row loop is often needed: different values per row, logic in update() that must run, or validation per record.

Slow:

ContosoOrderLog log;

while select salesTable
    where salesTable.SalesStatus == SalesStatus::Backorder
{
    log.clear();
    log.SalesId     = salesTable.SalesId;
    log.CustAccount = salesTable.CustAccount;
    log.insert();
}

Faster:

ContosoOrderLog log;

insert_recordset log (SalesId, CustAccount)
    select SalesId, CustAccount from salesTable
        where salesTable.SalesStatus == SalesStatus::Backorder;

Or, when the values differ per row:

ContosoOrderLog log;
RecordInsertList list = new RecordInsertList(tableNum(ContosoOrderLog));

while select SalesId, CustAccount from salesTable
    where salesTable.SalesStatus == SalesStatus::Backorder
{
    log.clear();
    log.SalesId     = salesTable.SalesId;
    log.CustAccount = salesTable.CustAccount;
    list.add(log);
}
list.insertDatabase();

docs.title: UnbalancedTransaction
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: every method that contains at least one ttsbegin.

Detects a method where the number of ttsbegin differs from the number of ttscommit plus ttsabort. The finding points to the first ttsbegin.

Why it matters. A transaction opened in one method and closed in another is easy to leave open on an error path. Long transactions hold locks, block other sessions and make the transaction log grow.

Fix. Open and close the transaction in the same method, around the smallest unit of work.

Slow:

public void post()
{
    ttsbegin;
    this.createJournal();
    this.postLines();
    // ttscommit is in postLines()
}

Faster:

public void post()
{
    ttsbegin;
    this.createJournal();
    this.postLines();
    ttscommit;
}

docs.title: CrossCompany
docs.text:
Severity: Info. Applies to: every method.

Detects a select or while select with the crossCompany keyword and no company list (crossCompany : container).

Why it matters. Without a list, the query reads the rows of every company (legal entity) in the database. In a system with many companies that is many times more data than needed.

Fix. Limit it to the companies needed:

// Slow: every company
while select crossCompany custTable
    where custTable.CustGroup == _custGroup
{
    // ...
}

// Faster: only the companies you need
container companies = ['USMF', 'USRT'];

while select crossCompany : companies custTable
    where custTable.CustGroup == _custGroup
{
    // ...
}

docs.title: AllFields
docs.text:
Severity: Info. Applies to: every method.

Detects a while select without a field list (no from keyword), which reads every field of every row.

Why it matters. Wide tables such as CustTable, SalesTable or InventTable have many fields. Reading all of them for every row moves far more data from SQL Server to the AOS than the loop uses, and prevents covering indexes.

Fix. List the fields the loop uses:

// Slow
while select custTable
    where custTable.CustGroup == _custGroup
{
    total += custTable.CreditMax;
}

// Faster
while select CreditMax from custTable
    where custTable.CustGroup == _custGroup
{
    total += custTable.CreditMax;
}

Do not use a field list when the loop calls methods that read other fields of the buffer, or updates the record: a buffer read with a field list has empty values in the other fields.

docs.title: ForUpdateWithoutWrite
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: every method.

Detects select forUpdate buffer (without a field list) on a buffer declared in the method or class, when the method never calls buffer.update(), buffer.delete(), buffer.write(), buffer.doUpdate() or buffer.doDelete() and does not return buffer;. Methods that return the buffer (the find(..., _forUpdate) pattern) are not reported.

Why it matters. forUpdate takes update locks inside a transaction. Locks that are never used block other sessions for nothing.

Fix. Drop forUpdate. If the write happens in another method, select forUpdate there.

// Slow: locks the record but only reads it
ttsbegin;
select forupdate salesTable
    where salesTable.SalesId == _salesId;
info(salesTable.SalesName);
ttscommit;

// Faster
select firstonly SalesName from salesTable
    where salesTable.SalesId == _salesId;
info(salesTable.SalesName);

docs.title: RowByRowFallback
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: every method.

Detects an insert_recordset, update_recordset or delete_from whose target table makes the statement run one row at a time. The causes it checks:

Statement Cause Can it be skipped? insert_recordset The table overrides insert(). buffer.skipDataMethods(true) update_recordset The table overrides update(). buffer.skipDataMethods(true) delete_from The table overrides delete(). buffer.skipDataMethods(true) delete_from The table has delete actions. buffer.skipDeleteActions(true) any The table is date-effective (ValidTimeState). No

A cause is not reported when the method calls the matching skip... method on the target buffer.

Why it matters. The statement looks set-based but the platform turns it into a loop with one round trip per row, plus the table's logic per row. The code reads as fast and runs as slow.

Fix. Remove the cause where its logic may be skipped. Database log and alerts on the table also force row by row; they are environment setup and are not checked here (skipDatabaseLog, skipEvents).

// Runs row by row when ContosoOrderLine overrides update()
update_recordset orderLine
    setting Processed = NoYes::Yes
    where orderLine.BatchId == _batchId;

// Set-based, when the logic in update() may be skipped for this change
orderLine.skipDataMethods(true);
update_recordset orderLine
    setting Processed = NoYes::Yes
    where orderLine.BatchId == _batchId;

Skipping update(), insert(), delete() or delete actions also skips their business logic. Check what they do before you skip them.

docs.title: NoMatchingIndex
docs.text:
Severity: Info. Applies to: every method.

Detects a select or while select whose where clause compares fields of a table buffer with ==, when no index of that table (including indexes added by table extensions) starts with one of those fields. Comparisons on RecId are always considered indexed. Tables without any index are not reported.

Why it matters. SQL Server can only seek on an index whose leading column is filtered. Without one, the query may scan the table or a large part of it. On a large table that is the difference between milliseconds and seconds.

Fix. Filter on the leading field of an existing index, or add an index that starts with these fields. Weigh how often the table is written: every index slows inserts and updates.

// No index of ContosoOrderLog starts with CustAccount
select firstonly contosoOrderLog
    where contosoOrderLog.CustAccount == _custAccount;

Add an index on CustAccount (in the table or a table extension), or filter on the leading field of an existing index. Check the plan with Explain Plan and missing indexes with Database Performance Insights.

docs.title: TableCache
docs.text:
Severity: Warning or Info. Applies to: tables with TableType Regular.

Detects a CacheLookup that does not fit the table's TableGroup:

TableGroup CacheLookup Severity Message and fix Transaction..., Worksheet..., Main EntireTable Warning Every insert, update or delete flushes the whole cache on every server. Use Found (or NotInTTS) for tables written during normal work. Parameter None or NotInTTS Info Setup data is read far more than written. Use EntireTable for parameter tables. Group, Reference, Framework None or NotInTTS Info Setup data is read far more than written. Use Found, or EntireTable when the table is small. Main None Info find() lookups by key go to the database every time. Use Found so lookups by a unique index are cached.

Why it matters. Record caching saves a round trip for every lookup by a unique key. A table cached entirely is flushed on every write, on every AOS, which hurts tables that are written all day.

Fix. Change CacheLookup in the table's properties (Element Designer).

docs.title: UncachedDisplayMethod
docs.text:
Severity: Info. Applies to: forms.

Detects a grid control (at any depth inside an AxFormGridControl) bound to a display method of a data source (DataMethod, not a static Class::method), when no form or data source method calls cacheAddMethod for that method.

Why it matters. A display method in a grid runs for every row shown, every time the grid refreshes. If it queries the database, a grid of 100 rows is 100 queries. cacheAddMethod makes the form compute the values together with the rows and cache them.

Fix. In the data source's init(), after super():

[DataSource]
class ContosoOrderStatus
{
    public void init()
    {
        super();
        ContosoOrderStatus_ds.cacheAddMethod(tableMethodStr(ContosoOrderStatus, customerName));
    }
}

The finding gives the exact line, with the data source and table names of your form.

docs.title: OnlyFetchActive
docs.text:
Severity: Warning on lookup forms, Info on other forms. Applies to: forms.

Detects a form data source without OnlyFetchActive = Yes when all of its visible bound controls are inside grids, and either:

  • the form is a lookup form (its design pattern contains "Lookup", or its name ends with "Lookup"); or
  • the table has 30 fields or more and the form shows 10 or fewer of them.

Hidden controls (Visible = No) are not counted.

Why it matters. Without OnlyFetchActive the form reads every field of the table for every row, even when the grid shows three columns. Lookups open often and must be fast.

Fix. Set OnlyFetchActive = Yes on the data source, unless code reads fields of the record that no control shows (those fields would be empty).

docs.title: FormLinkType
docs.text:
Severity: Warning or Info. Applies to: forms.

Detects a data source with a JoinSource:

  • Warning when its fields are shown in the same grid as its join source and its LinkType is Delayed or Active. The data source is queried separately for the current parent record instead of with the grid's rows.
  • Info when its LinkType is Active (and it is not in the parent's grid): it queries again on every move in the parent, even while the user scrolls.

Data sources with LinkType Passive are not reported: they are refreshed by code on purpose.

Why it matters. A Delayed or Active link is a second query per selected record. In the parent's grid it also shows wrong or empty values for the rows that are not selected.

Fix.

  • In the parent's grid: join it with LinkType InnerJoin (or OuterJoin when the record may be missing), so the grid reads both tables in one query.
  • Elsewhere: use LinkType Delayed, which waits until the user stops on a record.

docs.title: EntityPublicNames
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: data entities.

Detects an entity with IsPublic = Yes and an empty PublicEntityName or PublicCollectionName.

Why it matters. OData exposes public entities by these names. Without them the entity cannot be exposed.

Fix. Set PublicEntityName (singular, for example ContosoOrderStatus) and PublicCollectionName (plural, for example ContosoOrderStatuses).

docs.title: EntityKey
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: data entities.

Detects an entity with no entity key (empty Keys node).

Why it matters. OData updates and data management imports find existing records by the entity key. Without one, updates and imports fail.

Fix. Add a key on the natural key fields of the root data source (for a customer entity, the customer account).

docs.title: EntityStaging
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: data entities.

Detects either:

  • DataManagementEnabled = Yes but no DataManagementStagingTable; or
  • a staging table name that does not exist in the metadata.

Why it matters. Data management imports and exports go through the staging table.

Fix. Generate the staging table (right-click the entity > Regenerate staging table), or regenerate it when it is missing.

docs.title: EntityStagingFields
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: data entities with a staging table.

Detects entity fields that are mapped to a table field of one of the entity's data sources but are missing from the staging table (fields added by staging table extensions count as present). Up to 15 names are listed. Unmapped and computed fields, Int64 RecId reference fields and system fields are not staged and are not reported.

Why it matters. Imports and exports of the missing fields fail.

Fix. Add the fields to the staging table, or to a staging table extension, with the same names and types.

docs.title: EntityMandatoryFields
docs.text:
Severity: Warning. Applies to: data entities.

Detects fields of the root data source's table with Mandatory = Yes that no entity field maps. Up to 10 names are listed.

Why it matters. Inserts through the entity (OData, data management, dual-write) fail with a mandatory field error unless code sets these fields.

Fix. Map the fields, or default them in the entity's initValue or mapEntityToDataSource.

public void mapEntityToDataSource(DataEntityRuntimeContext _entityCtx, DataEntityDataSourceRuntimeContext _dataSourceCtx)
{
    super(_entityCtx, _dataSourceCtx);

    if (_dataSourceCtx.name() == dataEntityDataSourceStr(ContosoOrderStatusEntity, ContosoOrderStatus))
    {
        ContosoOrderStatus status = _dataSourceCtx.getBuffer();
        if (!status.StatusGroup)
        {
            status.StatusGroup = 'Default';
        }
    }
}

docs.title: EntitySetBased
docs.text:
Severity: Warning or Info. Applies to: data entities with EnableSetBasedSqlOperations = Yes.

Detects:

  • Warning when a data source of the entity is a view, another data entity or a table that is not Regular (a temporary table). Imports then fall back to row by row or fail.
  • Info when the entity overrides insertEntityDataSource, updateEntityDataSource, insert or update. Set-based imports skip this code.

Why it matters. Set-based processing moves staging rows to the target tables with SQL statements, without running X++ per row. It only works on regular tables, and it ignores per-row X++ logic.

Fix.

  • For the Warning: turn off EnableSetBasedSqlOperations, or use regular tables only.
  • For the Info: move the logic to the staging-to-target step, or turn off set-based processing.

docs.title: Power Platform CLI
docs.text: The Power Platform CLI (pac) is Microsoft's command-line tool for Power Platform and Dataverse, including unified developer environments (UDE). F&O Studio does not need it: deploy, database sync, tests and environment setup all call the environment's Dataverse directly. Two commands remain for developers who run pac themselves: Sign In to Environment (pac) keeps one pac auth profile per environment, and Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) creates a pac package project for your models.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You run your own pac commands (scripts, pipelines you test locally, pac solution work) and want a pac profile for the environment this window uses.
  • You want a pac ERP package project in your workspace to package or deploy with pac yourself.

You do not need pac to:

Task F&O Studio uses Connect to a UDE Dataverse and Microsoft's developer tools service (Connect to Environment) Deploy models Dataverse (msprov_fnopackages, msprov_deploypackagetofinopsasync) (Deploy to Environment) Synchronize the database Dataverse (msprov_dbsynctofinopsasync) on UDE, SyncEngine.exe on cloud-hosted and VHD (Synchronize Database) Run SysTest tests Dataverse (Run Tests) Database credentials Dataverse (msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync) (Database Access)

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The Power Platform CLI installed, on PATH or at the path in xpp.pacPath.
  • A unified developer environment. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the (pac) commands are hidden from the Command Palette and the Dynamics 365 view; run from elsewhere, they show "This is a cloud-hosted or VHD environment: your models run on the local AOS once they are built, so there is nothing to deploy."
  • For Initialize Deployment Solution (pac): a folder open in VS Code.

docs.title: Sign In to Environment (pac)
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Sign In to Environment (pac) from the Command Palette, or Sign In (pac) in the Dynamics 365 view's Environment group or the status bar environment menu.
  2. The environment is the one this window uses (Select Environment). If none is selected, enter the Dataverse URL in Dataverse environment URL (https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com).
  3. F&O Studio selects the profile named after the environment's org (pac auth select --name <org>).
  4. If the profile exists, it becomes pac's active profile and you see "pac uses its profile for ." with Sign In Again. Click it to delete the profile and create it again (for example after a password change or when the account was wrong).
  5. If it does not exist, F&O Studio creates it: pac auth create --name <org> --environment <url>. pac opens its own browser sign-in.
  6. The pac commands run as visible tasks in the terminal panel (source X++), so you see pac's output and can answer its prompts.

    7. Because each environment has its own named profile, environments in different tenants keep their own accounts. Switching the window to another environment and running Sign In again selects that environment's profile. Your own pac commands in the terminal then use it.

    Profile names are the org name, cut to 30 characters (the pac limit).

docs.title: Initialize Deployment Solution (pac)
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) from the Command Palette, or Initialize Deployment Solution… in the Dynamics 365 view's Deploy group.
  2. Enter the model names in Model(s) for the deployment solution (comma-separated). The box is filled with the active project's model.
  3. F&O Studio runs, as a visible task named Initialize erp solution:
pac package init --package-type erp --model <models> --outputDirectory <first workspace folder>

The result is pac's package project in your workspace folder. Build and deploy it with pac yourself; F&O Studio's Deploy Models to Environment does not use it.

docs.title: Using pac in the terminal after Sign In
docs.text:
After Sign In to Environment (pac), the environment's profile is pac's active profile, so your own commands in any terminal go to that environment. For example, to check which profile and org pac uses:

pac auth list
pac org who

When you switch the window to another environment with Select Environment…, run Sign In to Environment (pac) again: it only selects that environment's existing profile, without a new sign-in.

docs.title: Automating deploy and sync without pac
docs.text:
If you used pac in scripts to deploy and sync from your machine, the xpp task type does the same through Dataverse, with your local build. Add tasks to .vscode/tasks.json:

{
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "tasks": [
        { "type": "xpp", "action": "buildModel", "label": "Build model" },
        { "type": "xpp", "action": "deploy", "dbSync": "Module", "label": "Deploy and sync my package" },
        { "type": "xpp", "action": "syncDatabase", "mode": "Full", "label": "Full database sync" }
    ]
}

deploy deploys the package of the active project's model as built on this machine (dbSync: None by default, Module or Full). syncDatabase takes mode (Full by default, or Module with modules, a comma-separated list that defaults to the project's model). See Build Tasks.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.pacPath empty Path to pac. Empty: pac on PATH. A value that contains a quote character is ignored and pac is used. xpp.environmentUrl empty Default environment; the sign-in uses the window's environment.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The commands are in src/pac.ts (class PacCommands, which also holds deploy and database sync, which no longer use pac).

  • pac runs through a shell task (ShellExecution) because pac from PATH is usually a .cmd shim. The task is revealed in the shared terminal panel and its exit code is awaited.
  • Selecting the profile runs pac auth select --name <org> in the background (60-second timeout). Success means the profile exists.
  • A non-zero exit fails the command with "pac failed (exit n). Is the Power Platform CLI installed and signed in? See the terminal output."
  • pac keeps its profiles in its own store. F&O Studio never reads or stores pac's tokens. Its own Dataverse calls use VS Code's Microsoft account (Sign-In and Authentication), so signing in with pac does not sign in F&O Studio, and the other way round.

docs.title: Why deploy does not use pac
docs.text: Earlier versions deployed with pac. pac's package compile recompiles a scaffolded copy of your model with pac's own compiler, so the build you made locally (and its PDBs for the debugger) never reached the environment. F&O Studio now deploys the packages exactly as built on your machine, the way Visual Studio's Deploy Models to Online Environment does. See Deploy to Environment. The Dynamics 365 view still shows pac as the description of some Deploy entries; they run through Dataverse.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only sign-in and package initialization are wrapped. Other pac commands you run yourself in the terminal.
  • Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) writes into the first workspace folder only.
  • UDE only.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "pac auth create failed (exit n). Is the Power Platform CLI installed and signed in?..." pac not found or the sign-in failed Install the Power Platform CLI or set xpp.pacPath; read the task output. The sign-in uses the wrong account The profile was created with another account Run Sign In to Environment (pac) and click Sign In Again. "Open a workspace folder first." Initialize Deployment Solution (pac) needs a folder Open your workspace folder. The (pac) commands are missing from the Command Palette The active environment is cloud-hosted or VHD Not needed there. xpp.pacPath seems ignored The path contains quotes Remove the quotes from the setting.

docs.title: Pre-Deploy Checklist
docs.text: The Pre-Deploy Checklist runs the checks you should pass before you package or deploy a D365FO project, in one go: build, best practice, performance, security gaps, leftover scratch code, and a reminder about tests. The result is one report in the Results view that says "Ready to package and deploy." or "Not ready: fix the failed steps first." When every blocking step passes, F&O Studio offers to create the deployable package or to deploy. Visual Studio has no equivalent; there you run each of these checks by hand.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before Create Deployment Package… or Deploy Models to Environment.
  • At the end of a work item, after Review My Changes.
  • Before you hand a build to a tester or a sandbox.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Open a D365FO project (see D365FO Projects). The checklist works on the project's model and the project's elements. Without a project it stops with "Open a D365FO project first."
  • An active D365FO configuration (Select Environment).
  • The build and best practice steps use the Microsoft tools in the configuration's bin folder (xppc, xppbp).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the checklist from one of these places:
  2. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Pre-Deploy Checklist.
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Build and check > Pre-Deploy Checklist.
  4. Project view title bar: Check menu > Pre-Deploy Checklist.
  5. The empty Results view: the Pre-Deploy Checklist link.
  6. Progress appears in the Results view (Pre-deploy checklist: <project>) with the current step: build, best practice, performance, security. You can cancel; a cancelled run shows no report.
  7. The Results view shows one section per step, with a pass or error icon. Steps whose detail has several lines (the security step) list each line as a finding.
  8. If every step passed, a notification "The checklist passed." offers:
  9. Create Deployment Package: runs Create Deployment Package… (see Create Deployment Package).
  10. Deploy: runs Deploy Models to Environment (see Deploy to Environment). This button is only offered when the active environment is not a local one (cloud-hosted or VHD).
  11. If a step failed, fix it and use Run Again in the Results view title bar.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text: Step What it does Passes when Detail shown Build Builds the project's model with xppc, like Build Project. Diagnostics are limited to the project's elements. The build succeeds. "Succeeded." or "Failed: fix the errors in the Problems view." Best practice Runs xppbp on the model and counts the results of the project's elements. 0 best practice errors (warnings do not fail it). <n> error(s), <n> warning(s) in the project's elements. or "Could not run." Performance Runs the static performance analysis on each class, table, form and data entity of the project and counts the warnings. Always (informational). <n> warning(s); run Analyze Performance on the project's classes to see them. or "No warnings." Security Runs the security gap analysis (xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps) on the model. No finding of severity Error. The first 12 lines of the gap report. Scratch code Looks for Run Snippet's scratch class <Model>ScratchRunner in the model. The class is not in the model. Tells you to delete the class (project view > Delete) before packaging. Tests Reminder only. Always. On a unified developer environment: run tests after deploying (Test Explorer or Run Tests). On a local VM: run tests on the VM.

docs.title: Build
docs.text: The build is the same as Build Project and Model: xppc always compiles the whole package, but only the diagnostics of the project's elements are reported. A failed build fails the checklist.

docs.title: Best practice
docs.text: The same checker as Run Best Practice Checks on Project (see Best Practice Checks). The results also go to the Problems view. Only errors block; warnings are counted.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The same rules as Analyze Performance, including the data entity readiness rules for data entities. Only Warning-level findings are counted. This step never blocks, because the rules are heuristics. To see the findings, run Analyze Performance on the elements.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The gap analysis of Find Security Gaps for the project's model. Errors block the deployment:

Kind Severity Meaning UngrantedMenuItem Error No privilege grants the menu item: users without System administrator cannot open it. MissingEntryPoint Error A privilege points to a menu item that does not exist. MissingPrivilege Error A duty contains a privilege that does not exist. MissingDuty Error A role (or your role extension) contains a duty that does not exist. OrphanPrivilege Warning The privilege is in no duty or role. EmptyPrivilege Warning The privilege grants nothing. OverGrant Warning / Info A View privilege grants more than Read, or an action menu item is granted more than Invoke. LicenseUpgrade Warning A View privilege's grant needs a higher license. OrphanDuty Warning The duty is in no role. UnsecuredEntity Warning No privilege has permissions on the data entity.

Each line has the form - <Severity> <Kind> <ObjectType> <Name>: <message>.

docs.title: Scratch code
docs.text: Run Snippet creates a scratch class in your model to run code. Its name is the model name without non-word characters, followed by ScratchRunner (for model ContosoExtensions: ContosoExtensionsScratchRunner). If that class is in the project's model, the step fails, because the class would ship in the package.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
The Markdown report (from Copy Report as Markdown or Export Report…) looks like this, with a pass or fail mark before each step name:

# Pre-deploy checklist: ContosoOrders (ContosoExtensions)

**Not ready: fix the failed steps first.**

## Build

Succeeded.

## Best practice

0 error(s), 3 warning(s) in the project's elements.

## Performance

2 warning(s); run Analyze Performance on the project's classes to see them.

## Security

2 security finding(s) in ContosoExtensions:
- Error UngrantedMenuItem AxMenuItemDisplay ContosoOrderStatus: No privilege grants this menu item: users without System administrator cannot open it.
- Warning OrphanPrivilege AxSecurityPrivilege ContosoOrderStatusView: The privilege is in no duty or role, so nobody gets it.

## Scratch code

No scratch runner in the model.

## Tests

Run them after deploying: Test Explorer or Run Tests (they run against the deployed code).

The Results view header shows "Ready to package and deploy" or "Not ready: fix the failed steps first".

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
The checklist has no settings of its own. The build steps follow the build settings, for example:

Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Update the cross-reference database while building. xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules false Run AppChecker rules during the build. xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Save unsaved X++ code views before a build, so the compiler sees your latest changes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The command is in src/checklist.ts:

  1. readProject() gives the project's model and items.
  2. Build: XppBuilder.build(model, token, items) in src/build.ts.
  3. Best practice: XppBuilder.bestPractice(model, token, items) (xppbp).
  4. Performance: bridge action analyze_performance for each AxClass, AxTable, AxForm and AxDataEntityView of the project.
  5. Security: agent tool xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps and the model, run in-process. A line starting with - Error makes the step fail.
  6. Scratch code: bridge action find_object for the exact class name, filtered to the project's model.
  7. Tests: reads whether the active environment is local.
  8. The report goes to the Results view with a rerun entry.

Nothing is sent to an environment by the checklist itself; only the Deploy button deploys.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
The F&O Release Manager agent prepares a release in chat: it runs xpp_build for every model to release, xpp_check_best_practice, xppRunTests, xpp_analyze_security (op=gaps) and checks labels; summarizes the changes with xpp_diff_changes and their risk; creates the deployable package with xpp_package (which asks first); and deploys only to development, sandbox or build environments with your permission. See Agents for Developers.

Example prompt: "Get the ContosoExtensions model ready to deploy and tell me what blocks it."

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• It checks one project and its model. To release several models, run it per project.
  • It does not run tests. On a unified developer environment tests run against deployed code, so run them after deploying (Run Tests, Test Explorer).
  • It does not check for uncommitted Git changes; use Show Changed Elements for that.
  • Performance warnings never block.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Open a D365FO project first." No project is open, or the project has no model. Open a project with Open D365FO Project…. Build: "Failed: fix the errors in the Problems view." Compiler errors in the model. Fix them; see Compiler Diagnostics. Best practice: "Could not run." xppbp failed or was cancelled. See the F&O Studio output; run Run Best Practice Checks on Project alone. Security fails with UngrantedMenuItem. A new menu item is not in any privilege. Add it to a privilege (Add to Privilege). Security: "Could not run." The security analysis failed. Run Find Security Gaps… to see the error. Scratch code fails. Run Snippet's scratch class is still in the model. Delete the class from the project view, then run the checklist again. No Deploy button after a pass. The active environment is local (cloud-hosted or VHD). Use Create Deployment Package and deploy through your usual process.

docs.title: Properties Grid and Pickers
docs.text: The Properties grid is the right-hand pane of the Element Designer. It lists the properties of the selected node, grouped in categories like Visual Studio's Properties window, and lets you change them on elements of your own models. Pickers help you fill in properties that name an element or a label: an element search for EDTs, enums, tables, forms, menu items and other references, and a label picker that finds an existing label or creates a new one.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Read a property of any element: the EDT of a field, the table of a data source, the label of a menu item (with its text resolved).
  • Change properties of nodes in your own models: labels, help texts, EDTs, enum types, configuration keys, sizes, Visible, Mandatory and so on.
  • Find the properties that differ from their default (what the developer actually set).
  • Jump from a property to the element it names.
  • Give a field or control a label without leaving the designer: find an existing one or create a new label in one of your label files.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Open an element in the Element Designer and select a node (not a folder, method or event).
  • Editing needs the element to be in one of your own models. On other elements the grid is read-only.
  • The label picker creates labels only in label files of your own models that have an en-US language.

docs.title: The grid
docs.text:
1. Select a node in the tree. The grid shows the node type as a header (for example TableFieldString), a toolbar and the property rows.
  2. Each row has the property name on the left and its value on the right.
  3. Hover or focus a row to see its description in the footer under the grid. Properties changed from their default say "Changed from the default." when they have no description.

Rows are grouped by category in this order: Identification, Data, Appearance, Behavior, Configuration and security, Misc. A property's category is the metadata's own category when it has one; otherwise F&O Studio derives it from the property name (for example names containing Label, Visible or Width go to Appearance, names containing Table, Field or ExtendedDataType to Data). Report nodes use Visual Studio's report designer names and categories, sorted alphabetically, and show sub-objects such as Page Size or Margin as expandable rows (see Report Element Designer).

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Control What it does Filter properties (Ctrl+F) Shows only rows whose name, display name or value contains the text. Ctrl+F anywhere in the designer puts the cursor here. Filled circle toggle: Only properties changed from their default Hides properties that still have their default value Tree toggle: Group by category (off: alphabetical) Switches between categories and one alphabetical list

The filter and toggles stay as they are while you select other nodes.

docs.title: Changed values
docs.text: A property whose value differs from the default of a new node of the same type is marked with a dot and shown in bold. Its tooltip says "(changed from the default)". This is how you see at a glance what was set on a standard field or control.

docs.title: Editing values
docs.text:
On elements of your own models:

Property kind Editor Commit Text and numbers Text box Press Enter or leave the box. Escape restores the old value. Enums Drop-down with the enum's values On selection Yes/No (boolean) Drop-down with False and True On selection Name Read-only Use Rename… in the tree's right-click menu Complex values Read-only Edit the child nodes instead

Each change is saved immediately through the metadata API. The value is converted to the property's type; when that fails you see "'' is not a valid value." Changes can be undone with Ctrl+Z and redone with Ctrl+Y (see Element Designer).

On forms, every property change also redraws the form preview, so you see the effect of Width, Columns, ArrangeMethod and the other layout properties right away (see Form Designer and Preview).

docs.title: Labels in properties
docs.text: When a property holds a label reference such as @SYS7149 or @ContosoLabels:OrderStatus, the grid shows the reference and, under it, the label text (en-US). The go-to button next to it opens the label in the Label Editor on that label.

docs.title: References and Go to
docs.text:
When a property names another element (an EDT, an enum, a table, a form, a menu item, a configuration key, a base class...), the row offers several ways to go there:

  • the go-to button at the end of the value (tooltip "Go to ()");
  • Ctrl+click on the value box;
  • on read-only elements, click the value (it is shown as a link);
  • right-click the row > Go to Referenced Element….

    • In the tree, F12 on a node opens the first element it refers to, and Go to Referenced Element… on the node lists all of them.

docs.title: The element picker
docs.text:
String properties that name an element have a … button (or press Alt+Down in the value). The picker searches while you type:

  1. Type at least 3 characters of the element name.
  2. F&O Studio searches the metadata (up to 50 matches) and lists the elements of the right type with their type and model.
  3. Pick one. The property is set to its name and saved.

Properties with a picker include ExtendedDataType (EDT), EnumType (enum), Table and RelatedTable (table), ConfigurationKey, Extends (EDT or class), FormRef and Form (form), MenuItemName (display, action or output menu item), Query and Class. Any other property the server recognizes as a reference gets a picker for its referenced type.

On a report dataset, the Query property's … button opens the data source and field selection instead (see Report Datasets).

docs.title: The label picker
docs.text:
The label properties Label, HelpText, Caption, Description, DeveloperDocumentation and SingularLabel have a … button (or Alt+Down) that opens the label picker:

  1. Type the text you want, for example Order status.
  2. After 3 characters the picker searches the en-US texts of the label files of your models (up to 20 matches per file). Matches show the text with the reference, for example @ContosoLabels:OrderStatus.
  3. Below a separator, one entry per label file offers Create label "Order status" in .
  4. Pick an existing label to use it, or a create entry to add a new label.
  5. You can also type a reference directly, such as @SYS7149; the picker offers Use @SYS7149.

    6. When you create a label, F&O Studio builds the label ID from the text: words are capitalized and joined, other characters removed, at most 40 characters (Order status becomes OrderStatus). An ID that does not start with a letter gets an L in front. When the ID already exists, a number is added (OrderStatus1, OrderStatus2, ...). The label is created in en-US. Translate it later with the Label Editor or Label Tools.

    The picker opens on the current text of the property (not the reference) so you can refine it.

docs.title: Dropping elements on properties
docs.text: Drag an element from the Application Explorer or the project view onto a string property row (hold Shift while dropping into the designer). The property is set to the element's name when the property refers to that kind of element. Where a property depends on another one, that one follows: dropping a menu item on MenuItemName also sets MenuItemType; dropping a form, class, report or query on a menu item's Object sets its ObjectType; dropping a menu item on a security entry point's ObjectName sets its ObjectType.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The grid and pickers have no settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The grid is rendered by media/element.js; the panel and the message handling are in src/elementDesigner.ts; the pickers are in src/pickers.ts.
  • Bridge action get_element_properties returns, per property: name, value, kind (enum, bool, string, number, other), read-only flag, category, description, enum options, whether the value differs from the default, the resolved label text and the referenced element. It is implemented in MetaModelBridge.ElementDesigner.cs by reflection: only members marked [AxProperty] are listed, and defaults come from a new instance of the node's metadata class.
  • Bridge action set_element_property reads the element fresh, refuses non-custom models, walks to the node, converts the text to the property type, sets it and saves the element with the metadata provider's Update. Only [AxProperty] members that can be written are accepted; Name never.
  • Undo and redo keep the before and after values in the designer tab's memory and call set_element_property again.
  • The element picker calls bridge action find_object (250 ms after you stop typing) and filters the matches by type.
  • The label picker lists your label files from the models' AxLabelFile folders, searches with read_label (300 ms after you stop typing) and creates with create_label. Labels are written to the label text files (<Id>.en-US.label.txt) in ID order by the server's LabelStore.
  • Drops on property rows call drop_on_property (MetaModelBridge.Drops.cs).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Properties with complex values (anything that is not text, number, enum or Yes/No) are read-only in the grid.
  • The label picker searches and creates en-US texts only, and only in label files of your models.
  • Label text shown under a reference is the en-US text.
  • Undo covers property changes in the current designer tab only.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Values are plain text, no editors The element is not in your model, or the node is a base node of an extension Edit through your own element or extension The element picker shows nothing Fewer than 3 characters typed, or no element of that type matches Type more of the name The label picker offers no Create label entries None of your models has a label file with en-US Create a label file in your model (see New Element) "The label could not be created: ..." The server refused the label (for example the file is not writable) Read the message; check the label file belongs to your model "'' is not an editable property of ." The property is read-only or not a designer property Change it through another node or in code "'' can't be set by dropping an element." The property is not a string reference property Use the picker or type the value

docs.title: Quick Fixes
docs.text: F&O Studio adds X++ code actions to the light bulb in the code editor: Extract to label, Generate find() and exist(), Implement missing interface methods and Create Chain of Command wrapper. They automate the small, repetitive edits that every D365FO developer makes many times a day. Visual Studio has no such light bulb actions for X++; there you write these by hand or copy them from another object.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Quick fix Use it when Extract to label You typed a user-facing string in code and need a label for it (best practice requires labels). Generate find() and exist() You created a table and need the standard find and exist methods on its primary key. Implement missing interface methods Your class implements an interface and you need stubs for its methods. Create Chain of Command wrapper You read a standard method and want to extend it with Chain of Command.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The quick fixes work in X++ documents: the X++ Code View of an element, and .xpp files.
  • The edits go to elements in your models only. Standard elements are read-only in the code view; the only action offered there is the Chain of Command wrapper, which creates code in your model.
  • Extract to label needs a label file in one of your models (create one with New Element).
  • Generate find() and exist() and the Chain of Command wrapper need the element's code view (they read the element's metadata).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Put the cursor where the action applies (see each section).
  2. Press Ctrl+. or click the light bulb.
  3. Choose the action. Some actions ask questions; others edit the code right away.
  4. Save the document to write the change to the metadata (except the Chain of Command wrapper and labels, which are saved by the server directly).

docs.title: Extract to label
docs.text:
Where: cursor inside a string literal ("...", '...', or a verbatim @"..." / @'...') in an editable document. Not offered for strings that already start with @ (a label reference), for empty strings, or inside a // comment.

Steps:

  1. Choose Extract to label.
  2. Pick the label file. Only label files of your models are listed. With one label file there is no question. The file you used last is listed first.
  3. Enter the label ID. The suggestion is the string in PascalCase, for example "Customer not found" gives CustomerNotFound. The ID must start with a letter or _ and contain only letters, digits and _.
  4. If a label with that ID already exists with a different text, a dialog asks:
  5. Use It: use the existing label as it is;
  6. Overwrite: replace its text with the string.

If the existing label already has the same text, it is reused without a question. 5. The label is saved with the string as its text in every language of the label file. The string in code is replaced with "@<LabelFile>:<LabelId>". Single-quoted and verbatim strings become double-quoted, because X++ resolves labels only in double-quoted strings.

Example, with label file ContosoLabels:

// Before
throw error("Customer not found");

// After
throw error("@ContosoLabels:CustomerNotFound");

If the line changed while the dialogs were open, the label is still created and you see The label @<file>:<id> is ready, but the string moved; replace it by hand.

To translate the new label into the other languages later, see Label Tools.

docs.title: Generate find() and exist()
docs.text:
Where: anywhere in the code view of a table in your model that lacks find, exist or both. The action is titled with what is missing, for example Generate find() and exist() or Generate exist().

What it generates: the methods use the fields of the table's primary index as parameters. When the table has no primary index, or its primary index is the surrogate key, RecId is used. Parameter types are the fields' EDTs (or enum, or base type when the field has neither). Each method gets an XML documentation comment.

Example for a table ContosoOrderStatus whose primary index has the field StatusId with the EDT ContosoStatusId:

/// <summary>
/// Finds the ContosoOrderStatus record by its primary key.
/// </summary>
/// <param name = "_statusId">The StatusId value.</param>
/// <param name = "_forUpdate">true to select the record for update; optional.</param>
/// <returns>The ContosoOrderStatus record, or an empty buffer when none is found.</returns>
public static ContosoOrderStatus find(ContosoStatusId _statusId, boolean _forUpdate = false)
{
    ContosoOrderStatus contosoOrderStatus;

    if (_statusId)
    {
        contosoOrderStatus.selectForUpdate(_forUpdate);

        select firstonly contosoOrderStatus
            where contosoOrderStatus.StatusId == _statusId;
    }

    return contosoOrderStatus;
}

/// <summary>
/// Checks whether a ContosoOrderStatus record exists.
/// </summary>
/// <param name = "_statusId">The StatusId value.</param>
/// <returns>true if the record exists; otherwise, false.</returns>
public static boolean exist(ContosoStatusId _statusId)
{
    return _statusId
        && (select firstonly RecId from ContosoOrderStatus
            where ContosoOrderStatus.StatusId == _statusId).RecId != 0;
}

With several key fields, every field becomes a parameter, the guard checks all of them (&&), and the where clause compares each one. The methods are inserted before the closing brace of the table's code.

docs.title: Implement missing interface methods
docs.text:
Where: cursor on the class declaration (any line up to the first {) of a class whose declaration has implements, in an editable document.

What it does:

  1. Reads the methods of every interface after implements.
  2. Skips methods the class already has, including methods inherited from its base classes.
  3. Adds a stub for each missing method, before the class's closing brace. The stub keeps the interface method's modifiers (without abstract; public is added when there is no access modifier), return type and parameters with their default values:
public void run()
{
    throw error(Error::wrongUseOfFunction(funcName()));
}

The status bar shows Added N method(s). or All interface methods are implemented. If an interface cannot be read, a warning lists it under Not checked:.

docs.title: Create Chain of Command wrapper
docs.text:
Where: cursor on the header of a method (the lines from the method name to its opening brace, including comment and attribute lines above) in the code view of a standard class, table, form, view, data entity or map. Not offered for private methods or the class declaration.

Steps:

  1. Choose Create Chain of Command wrapper for .
  2. The model is your project's model; without a project you pick one of your models.
  3. Enter the extension class name. The suggestion is <Element>_<Model>_Extension, for example SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension. The name must end with _Extension.
  4. F&O Studio creates the class if it does not exist, with the ExtensionOf attribute that fits the element type (classStr, tableStr, formStr or mapStr):
    5. [ExtensionOf(classStr(SalesFormLetter))]
final class SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    public void run()
    {
        next run();
    }
}

    For a method that returns a value, the wrapper keeps the result:

        public boolean validateWrite()
    {
        boolean result = next validateWrite();

        return result;
    }
    1. The wrapper keeps the method's modifiers except abstract, final, server and client, and its parameters without default values.
    2. If the extension class exists already, the wrapper is added to it. If it already wraps that method, you see <class> already wraps <method>. If the class exists but is not an extension of the element, or exists in a model that is not yours, the action stops with an error.
    3. The class is added to the active project and opens in the code view at the new method.

    See Create Code Extension for creating an extension class from Application Explorer, and Implementations and Chain of Command to see existing wrappers.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for the quick fixes. Extract to label remembers the label file you used last.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/productivity/quickFixes.ts registers a code action provider for X++ documents. For each light bulb request it checks the line under the cursor and the document:

  • whether the document can be saved (the code view marks standard elements read-only);
  • string literals on the line (outside // comments);
  • the methods of the document (with the same parser as the code view);
  • the element behind the code view URI.

The actions call the metadata server (bridge actions):

Action Bridge actions Extract to label label_file_entries (languages, existing ID), save_label Generate find() and exist() table_erd (primary key and field types) Implement missing interface methods type_members (interface and class methods) Create Chain of Command wrapper find_object, read_object, create_object or update_object, add_to_project

Find/exist and interface stubs are applied as a normal editor edit, so you can undo them and you save them yourself. Labels are written to the label text files of your model by the server. The Chain of Command class is created or updated through the metadata API.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Extract to label only handles a string on one line.
  • The label is created with the same text in every language of the label file; translate it afterwards.
  • Generate find() and exist() uses the primary index. Tables keyed on another unique index need hand-written methods.
  • Interface stubs throw an error until you write the body.
  • The Chain of Command wrapper is offered only on standard elements and not on private methods.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix None of your models has a label file. Create one (Label File) in your model first. No label file in your models. Create a label file with New Element. Label file <file> can't be changed. The label file is not in your custom metadata folder. Pick a label file of your model. The class's closing brace was not found at the end of the document. The document does not end with }. Fix the code layout so the class ends with its closing brace. Table <name> not found. The table is not in the metadata (not saved yet). Save the table first. Could not read the header of <method>. The method header could not be parsed. Put the cursor on the method's first line and try again. <class> exists but is not an extension of <element>. The class name is taken by another class. Choose another name. No light bulb on a standard method The method is private, or the cursor is in the body. Move the cursor to the method header.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
F&O Studio releases are built from the public source by a GitHub Actions workflow, not on a developer machine. A version tag vX.Y.Z starts the build; the workflow compiles and tests everything, has the server signed when signing is set up, packages the VSIX and a stand-alone server zip, and creates the GitHub release. The VSIX then goes to the Visual Studio Marketplace.

This page describes the steps and what each check protects. It is for maintainers and for users who want to know how the published extension is made.

docs.title: What a release contains
docs.text:
Asset Contents xpp-vscode-X.Y.Z.vsix the extension: out/, core/dist/, server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe and its .config, tools/pdb2pdb/, media, grammar, agents, CHANGELOG.md fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip server/bin on its own, for hosts outside VS Code (see MCP-Server-Outside-VS-Code) fno-studio-server-X.Y.Z.zip.sha256 the zip's SHA-256

No asset contains a Microsoft D365FO assembly. The server loads them at run time from the user's own installation.

docs.title: Versioning and branches
docs.text:
• Work happens on main. Releases are tags vX.Y.Z, not branches.
  • The version in package.json is the release version. The tag must match it exactly, or the build stops with "Tag ... does not match package.json version ...".
  • The same version goes into the server exe's file metadata (build-server.ps1 passes -p:Version).

docs.title: Release steps
docs.text:
1. Set the version in package.json.
  2. Write the release notes in docs/FEATURES.md under ## What's new in X.Y (one section per minor version, at the top). This is the only place release notes are written.
  3. Run npm run changelog. It writes CHANGELOG.md from the "What's new" sections; the Marketplace shows it as the Changelog tab. Never edit CHANGELOG.md by hand.
  4. If agents changed, run npm run agents.
  5. Commit and push main. Images in FEATURES.md resolve to docs/images on GitHub, so push before publishing.
  6. Tag and push the tag:
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z
  1. Wait for the Release build workflow to pass.
  2. Publish the VSIX to the Marketplace (automatic when the workflow has a Marketplace token; otherwise by hand, see below).

docs.title: The workflow
docs.text:
.github/workflows/release.yml runs on a pushed v* tag, or by hand (workflow_dispatch) as a dry run. It has two jobs on windows-latest.

flowchart TD
    T["tag vX.Y.Z pushed"] --> V["Version: tag must match package.json"]
    V --> R["Restore Microsoft's D365 compiler package (private feed)"]
    R --> NS["npm ci"]
    NS --> BS["Build and test the server<br/>build-server.ps1 -Test, check-bridge-actions.js"]
    BS --> NM["No Microsoft DLL in server/bin;<br/>exe metadata = F&O Studio + version"]
    NM --> BE["Build and test the extension<br/>compile, test:core, offline tests,<br/>agents --check, changelog --check"]
    BE --> SG["Sign the server (SignPath, when configured)"]
    SG --> ZIP["Server zip + SHA-256<br/>(no Microsoft files)"]
    ZIP --> VSIX["Fetch Pdb2Pdb, check it runs, vsce package"]
    VSIX --> P["publish job"]
    P --> C1["zip matches SHA-256"]
    C1 --> C2["VSIX holds the server, Pdb2Pdb, changelog, core;<br/>no Microsoft DLL; signature valid when signing is configured"]
    C2 --> N["Release notes from 'What's new in X.Y'"]
    N --> GH["GitHub release (create or update)"]
    GH --> MP["Marketplace publish (when a token is set)"]

docs.title: Build job
docs.text: Step What it does Why Version Reads package.json; on a tag, compares with the tag name The release, the VSIX and the exe all carry the same version Restore compiler package Restores Microsoft's Dynamics 365 compiler package from a private feed and sets XPP_BIN The server compiles against Microsoft's assemblies; they are never part of the repository, an artifact or the VSIX npm ci Installs development dependencies Build and test the server build-server.ps1 -Test (build plus test/server unit tests), then check-bridge-actions.js Server correctness, contract with the extension Never ship Microsoft assemblies Fails when server/bin has any .dll; checks the exe's ProductName "F&O Studio for VS Code" and ProductVersion Licensing; signing requires the metadata Build and test the extension npm run compile, npm run test:core, source-test.js, form-preview-test.js, xpp-config-test.js, vs-tools-test.js, build-agents.js --check, changelog.js --check No stale generated files Upload the unsigned server Artifact for signing Sign the server Submits the exe to SignPath and waits (every request needs a manual approval), only when signing is configured Code signing (see below) Use the signed server Copies the signed exe back and prints its Authenticode status. On a tag with signing configured, an invalid signature stops the release; without signing configured the server ships unsigned with a warning Package the server Zips server/bin, fails on any .dll or Microsoft.Dynamics.* file and when the exe is missing, writes the SHA-256 Hosts outside VS Code Package the VSIX npm run build:tools, checks Pdb2Pdb exists and runs, then vsce package with docs/FEATURES.md as the overview Deploy and debugging need Pdb2Pdb

docs.title: Publish job
docs.text: Step What it does Zip hash The downloaded server zip must match its .sha256 VSIX contents extension/server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe, its .config, extension/tools/pdb2pdb/Pdb2Pdb.exe, extension/changelog.md and extension/core/dist/index.js must be there; no Microsoft.Dynamics.*.dll. When signing is configured and this is a tag, the exe must carry a valid SignPath Foundation signature Release notes Takes the ## What's new in X.Y section of docs/FEATURES.md (fails when there is none) and adds an install line GitHub release On a tag: creates release "F&O Studio X.Y.Z" with the VSIX, the server zip and its hash, marked latest. Re-running the workflow for the same tag updates the release instead of failing Marketplace On a tag: publishes the VSIX when a Marketplace token is configured; otherwise prints a warning with the manual command Dry run On a manual run: everything except the GitHub release and publishing

docs.title: Publishing to the Marketplace by hand
docs.text:
When the workflow did not publish, publish the release's own VSIX (the one with the signed server, if signing is configured), never a local build:

gh release download vX.Y.Z --pattern *.vsix
npx vsce publish --packagePath xpp-vscode-X.Y.Z.vsix

The publisher is MNazmi; vsce needs a login for it on the machine. npm run publish refuses on purpose with a message that points to the workflow, because a local build's server is unsigned. npm run package still makes a local VSIX for testing.

docs.title: Code signing
docs.text:
From the public code signing policy in the README:

  • Free code signing is provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.
  • What is signed: the F&O Studio server (server/bin/XppVsCode.Server.exe) in the published extension. The release workflow builds it from the repository's source on GitHub Actions and submits it to SignPath. The Visual Studio Marketplace signs the extension package itself.
  • Microsoft's assemblies are restored from a private feed during the build only; they are never part of the repository or the extension.
  • Every signing request is approved by hand.

The workflow signs only when signing is configured for the repository. Without it, the server ships unsigned and the build shows a warning.

docs.title: Checklist before tagging
docs.text:
• package.json version bumped.
  • ## What's new in X.Y in docs/FEATURES.md describes the user-visible changes.
  • npm run changelog run and CHANGELOG.md committed.
  • node scripts/build-agents.js --check passes.
  • Server changes: npm run test:server, scripts/smoke-test.ps1, node scripts/security-probes.js all pass (see Testing-the-Extension).
  • Refactorings: golden master IDENTICAL.
  • main pushed, then the tag.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Tag vX.Y.Z does not match package.json version ..." Tag and package.json differ Delete the tag, fix the version, tag again "docs/FEATURES.md has no section ## What's new in X.Y" No release notes for the minor version Add the section, run npm run changelog, push, re-run changelog.js --check or build-agents.js --check fails Generated files out of date Run npm run changelog / npm run agents and commit "server/bin must hold only F&O Studio's own files" A Microsoft assembly was copied to the output Check that every D365FO reference has <Private>false</Private> "Pdb2Pdb is missing" or "Pdb2Pdb doesn't run" The tool download failed Re-run; check scripts/fetch-pdb2pdb.ps1 "The server is not signed ... although signing is configured" The signing request was rejected or timed out Approve the request in SignPath and re-run the workflow Warning: Marketplace was not updated No Marketplace token in the workflow Publish by hand as above
