docs.title: Rename and Refactoring
docs.text:
F&O Studio renames X++ code across models, using the cross-reference database to find the uses:

  • Rename Symbol (F2) on a method of your models renames the method and the calls the database knows.
  • Rename… on a field of your table in the designer renames the field, the table's own field groups, indexes and relations, the X++ code that uses it and the metadata of your other elements.
  • Rename… on one of your elements in the Application Explorer or the project view renames the element itself, the code that uses it and the metadata of your elements that name it.

Code changes always go through VS Code's refactor preview first, so you see every edit before anything changes.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Fix a method name in your model before a release, with all its callers.
  • Rename a field of your table and keep the forms, data entities and code that use it working.
  • Rename a class or table of your model that has the wrong prefix or a misleading name.

For other refactorings, see Quick Fixes: extract to label, generate find() and exist(), implement missing interface methods, and create a Chain of Command wrapper.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The target must be in one of your models. Standard elements and methods can't be renamed; extend them instead.
  • Build with cross references first (xpp.build.crossReference, on by default). The references come from the cross-reference database as of the last build; uses written since then are not found.
  • Save your open code views: the rename edits the code views and saves them through the metadata API.
  • Use source control, so you can review and undo the whole change (see Source Control for X++).

docs.title: Rename a method (F2)
docs.text:
1. In a code view, put the cursor on the method name: in its signature or in a call such as this.contosoValidate() or ContosoOrderHelper::checkStatus(.
  2. Press F2 (or right-click and choose Rename Symbol).
  3. Type the new name and press Enter. The name must be letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.
  4. The refactor preview opens with "Rename ContosoOrderHelper.checkStatus to newName". It lists each change:
  5. the method's own signature;
  6. every call checkStatus( found at the references;
  7. names in methodStr(ContosoOrderHelper, checkStatus), staticMethodStr(...), tableMethodStr(...) and other ...MethodStr(Type, name) intrinsics.
  8. Review, uncheck changes you don't want, and choose Apply.
  9. Save the changed code views (Ctrl+S, or File > Save All). Each save writes the element through the metadata API.
  10. Build to check (Build Project and Model).

docs.title: Rename a field of your table
docs.text:
1. Open your table in the Element Designer.
  2. Right-click the field under Fields and choose Rename….
  3. Type the new name (letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter).
  4. A confirmation tells you how many places change: "N place(s) in X++ code (shown in the refactor preview), the metadata of N other element(s) of your models, and N element(s) outside your models that can't be changed". Choose Rename.
  5. The refactor preview opens for the code changes: fieldNum(ContosoOrderTable, OldName), fieldStr(...), fieldPName(...) and .OldName member access at each reference. Apply it.
  6. F&O Studio renames the field (its own field groups, indexes and relations follow), saves the changed code views and updates the metadata of your other elements: form controls and data sources, data entity fields, relations and similar properties.
  7. A message summarizes the result: code changes, metadata references, failures, and "Not changed (outside your models): ..." for elements it couldn't change. Build to check.

For a field of a table extension, or any other node whose rename F&O Studio doesn't carry through, the designer renames only the node. When the field is used, it warns first: "N reference(s) in X++ code and other elements (cross-reference database). They are not renamed." Choose Rename Anyway or cancel, and fix the others with Find All References.

docs.title: Rename an element
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer or the project view, right-click one of your elements (not an extension) and choose Rename…. From the command palette, F&O Studio: Rename… asks for the element.
  2. Type the new name.
  3. The confirmation explains what will happen: the element "is copied to NewName in ContosoExtensions and then deleted", the number of code places, the metadata of your elements, and the elements outside your models that can't be changed. For a table it adds: "Data in the old table is not moved: the next database sync drops it."
  4. Choose Rename, then apply the refactor preview.
  5. F&O Studio:
  6. duplicates the element under the new name in the same model and adds it to the project;
  7. replaces the old name in the copy's own code (OldName::find(), new OldName());
  8. saves the changed code views of the elements that use it;
  9. updates the metadata of your elements that name it;
  10. deletes the original;
  11. opens the renamed element in the designer.
  12. Build to check.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Keep the cross-reference database current when you build, so renames find your code

docs.title: Method rename
docs.text:
XppRename in src/rename.ts is the rename provider for X++ documents:

  1. prepareRename resolves the symbol (Go to Definition rules) and checks that it is a method with code, and that its owner is in a custom model (bridge action find_object).
  2. provideRenameEdits asks for the references with the declaration included (the same where_used query as Find All References, up to 200).
  3. At each reference line and the two lines after it (a reference can point a line or two before the call, for attributes or wrapped statements), it replaces name( and ...MethodStr(Type, name) with the new name. Every edit is marked as needing confirmation, which opens the preview.

docs.title: Field and element rename
docs.text:
src/refactor.ts:

  1. where_used returns up to 1,000 references. More than that is refused ("rename it in smaller steps").
  2. References in code (with a line, in a code element) become text edits in the code views, applied with isRefactoring, so the preview shows them.
  3. References without a line or in elements without code are metadata references. Elements in your models get the bridge action replace_references (old name, new name, and the table for a field); others are listed as "not changed".
  4. The field is renamed with rename_element_node; an element is copied with duplicate_object, added with add_to_project and removed with delete_object.

Every write goes through the metadata API in the server, which only allows changes in your models (Security Model).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only methods, table fields and elements of your models. Extensions can't be renamed this way: duplicate them under the new suffix and delete the original.
  • Uses not recorded in the cross-reference database are not changed: code written since the last build, dynamic calls (method names built in strings, DictClass), and packages built without cross references.
  • References in standard elements or other models can't be changed; they are listed in the result.
  • Renaming a table creates a new table: the data stays in the old table and the next database sync drops it.
  • Element types the cross-reference database doesn't index (some menu item kinds, for example) are renamed without updating references.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Message Cause Fix "Rename works on method names." The cursor is not on a method Put the cursor on the method name; use the designer or Application Explorer for fields and elements "X is not a method in code." The name resolves to a field, enum value or kernel method Rename it in the designer "X.m belongs to a standard model; only methods of your models can be renamed." Standard method Wrap it with Chain of Command instead "X is not in one of your models; only your own elements can be renamed." / "... add a field through a table extension instead." Standard element or table Extend it "... Rename needs the cross-reference database: build the model with cross references first." The database is not usable Build with xpp.build.crossReference on "X has more than 1000 references; rename it in smaller steps." Too many references Rename per area, or by hand with Find All References "... was not renamed: ... Undo the code changes (Ctrl+Z) before saving them." The metadata rename failed after the code edits were applied Undo the edits in the open code views, fix the cause, retry A call was not renamed Written after the last build with cross references Rename it by hand, or build and run the rename again

docs.title: Report Build
docs.text: When you build a model, F&O Studio compiles its SSRS reports with Microsoft's report compiler (reportsc.exe) right after X++, as Visual Studio's build does. The compiled RDL files land in the package's Reports folder, which the AOS reads at run time, so Deploy Models to Environment puts working reports on the environment. Without this step a deployed report has no compiled design and doesn't run.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After you change a report's datasets, designs or parameters.
  • After you change the data provider, contract or labels a report uses.
  • Before you deploy or create a deployment package with reports.

You don't start it separately: it is part of Build Model and Build Project.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The model builds without X++ errors: reports compile only after a successful X++ compile.
  • The package's models and the standard packages are on this machine (the active configuration's metadata).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Run Build Model or Build Project (see Build-Project-and-Model), from the status bar, the command palette or Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ editor.
  2. Watch the X++ Build output. After xppc, when the package has reports, reportsc runs; its warnings and errors are printed as WARNING … and ERROR … lines.
  3. The last line counts report errors with the X++ errors, for example === ContosoExtensions: BUILD FAILED (report compilation) - 1 error(s), 0 warning(s) ===.
  4. Deploy with Deploy Models to Environment (see Deploy-to-Environment) or package with Create Deployment Package… (see Create-Deployment-Package).

Copilot's xpp_build tool does the same: its result says "Reports compiled to …\Reports." or shows the end of the reportsc log when it failed (see Agent-Tools-Build-and-Data).

docs.title: Which reports are compiled
docs.text:
• Every report (AxReport) of every model in the package, by name, whether you built the project or the whole model: xppc and reportsc always work on the whole package.
  • Compiled designs (<Report>.<Design>.rdl in <package>\Reports) of reports that are no longer in the package are deleted, with a line in the output ("Removed …: its report is no longer in the package."), so they aren't deployed.
  • A package without reports skips the step.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Updates the cross-reference database during the X++ compile; the report data provider picker reads it (see Report-Datasets). It doesn't change report compilation.

There is no setting to turn report compilation off.

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
F&O Studio runs reportsc.exe from the platform bin folder with:

reportsc.exe
  -metadata=<metadata root>
  -modelmodule=<package>
  -name=<Report1>,<Report2>,...
  -output=<package folder>\Reports
  -LabelsPath=<metadata root>
  -log=<log folder>\Dynamics.AX.<package>.reportsc.log
  -xmllog=<log folder>\Dynamics.AX.<package>.reportsc.xml
  • -name is always passed: without it reportsc first deletes every .rdl in the output folder.
  • Diagnostics come from the XML log; informational messages are left out, and errors and fatal errors fail the build.

docs.title: The metadata root
docs.text:
reportsc reads one metadata folder, so your packages and the standard packages must sit side by side.

  • Cloud-hosted and VHD environments: the custom and standard packages already share PackagesLocalDirectory; that folder is used.
  • Unified developer environments (UDE): your packages live in the custom metadata folder and the standard ones in the downloaded PackagesLocalDirectory. F&O Studio keeps a folder of junctions to every package under %LOCALAPPDATA%\FOStudio\ReportMetadata\<configuration name>. A package in the custom folder wins over a standard package of the same name. The links are recorded in links.txt; links whose target changed or whose package is gone are removed (only the junction, never what it points to) and missing ones are created on the next build.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
• Extension build: compileReports in src/build.ts and the arguments, metadata root and stale-file clean-up in src/reports/reportCompiler.ts.
  • Agent build (xpp_build): ReportCompiler in server/Host/ReportCompiler.cs, called from server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs. The two follow the same rules.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text: Deploy zips the built package folder, including Reports, and sends it to the environment the way Visual Studio does (see Deploy-to-Environment). The AOS then reads the compiled designs from it.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Reports compile only when the X++ compile succeeded.
  • Report diagnostics appear in the X++ Build output and in the error count, not as entries in the Problems view.
  • reportsc checks the report definition; it doesn't run the report. Use the Report-Preview locally, then run the report on the environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix BUILD FAILED (report compilation) reportsc reported an error. Read the ERROR lines in the X++ Build output, or Dynamics.AX.<package>.reportsc.log; fix the report and build again. Could not link … into … A junction under %LOCALAPPDATA%\FOStudio\ReportMetadata couldn't be created. Check that the folder is writable and the package folder exists; build again. A deleted report still runs on the environment Its compiled design was deployed before. Build again (stale .rdl files are removed), then deploy. reportsc doesn't run after a build The X++ compile failed, or the package has no reports. Fix the X++ errors first; check that the report is in a model of this package.

docs.title: Report Datasets
docs.text: A report dataset says where a report's rows come from: a report data provider (RDP) class and its temporary table, an AOT query, or an enum. F&O Studio sets a dataset's source the way Visual Studio's report designer does: you pick the source and its fields, and the dataset's fields and parameters and the report's parameters are created by Microsoft's own schema analyzers. This replaces Visual Studio's "Select a Report Data Provider", "Select a Query" and "Select Fields" dialogs.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You created an empty report and need its data.
  • You changed a data provider's temporary table or contract and want the dataset's fields and parameters to follow (Visual Studio's Restore).
  • You need an enum dataset for a parameter drop-down.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The report is in a model you can change.
  • For Report Data Provider: the cross-reference database is available and your data provider class has been built with cross-references (setting xpp.build.crossReference, on by default). The list of data provider classes comes from it.
  • The data provider class has at least one method with [SRSReportDataSetAttribute] returning a table record.

docs.title: Choosing the data source type
How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the report in the element designer (see Report-Element-Designer).
  2. Select a dataset under Datasets, or create one: right-click Datasets → New… → Data Set.
  3. Set Data Source Type in the Properties window.
  4. Click the … button on the Query property (or press Alt+Down on it). What follows depends on the type.

docs.title: Report Data Provider
docs.text:
1. A quick pick lists the classes that extend SrsReportDataProviderBase, directly or through other classes (for example SrsReportDataProviderPreProcessTempDB). Pick your class.
  2. F&O Studio reads the class and its base classes for methods with [SRSReportDataSetAttribute] that return a record.
  3. One data table: it is used directly.
  4. Several (a provider can return several datasets): pick the table, shown as Class.Table.
  5. None: you get a warning that the class has no data tables.
  6. The field picker opens with every field selected. Each entry shows the field name, its label and, below, alias (type). Clear the fields you don't want and confirm.
  7. The dataset is saved. The status bar shows a summary such as "Set ContosoCustGroupList.CustGroup to ContosoCustGroupDP.ContosoCustGroupTmp: 5 field(s), 5 added, 7 parameter(s)."

docs.title: Query
docs.text:
1. Pick an AOT query in the element picker.
  2. The field picker opens with the query's fields, all selected. Confirm.
  3. The dataset is saved.

docs.title: Enum Provider
docs.text:
1. Pick an enum in the element picker.
  2. There is no field picker. The dataset gets the fields Name (string), Value (integer) and Label (string), as standard enum datasets have, and the framework parameters.

docs.title: Selecting all fields or some
docs.text:
• Keep every field selected: the Query is written as SELECT * FROM …, so fields added to the source later are picked up the next time you set the Query.
  • Select some fields: the Query lists their aliases, for example SELECT AccountNum,Name FROM ContosoCustDP.ContosoCustTmp.

docs.title: What gets filled in
docs.text: When you confirm, F&O Studio updates the dataset and the report the way Visual Studio does when the Query changes.

docs.title: Dataset fields
docs.text:
• Fields are matched to the source by alias. Existing fields keep their names; their data type is updated.
  • New source fields are added. A name that is taken gets a number (Name1).
  • Fields whose alias ends in () (methods) become calculated fields.
  • Enum fields are marked not to be created automatically in data regions.
  • Fields that are no longer in the source are removed, unless you added them yourself (UserDefined).
  • New fields get the source's label as caption (or the field name when there is none).

docs.title: Dataset and report parameters
docs.text:
• Every parameter the schema reports (the contract's data members, the framework parameters) becomes a dataset parameter tied to a report parameter in the default parameter group (Parameters).
  • Framework parameters (AX_PartitionKey, AX_CompanyName, AX_UserContext, AX_RenderingCulture, AX_ReportContext…) are created hidden; all but AX_CompanyName also allow blank and null values.
  • A report parameter with the same name is reused; otherwise a new one is added.
  • An empty prompt string is filled from the contract's label.
  • Data types and multi-value follow the source.

docs.title: Dynamic filters
docs.text: When the dataset's Dynamic Filters property is on, F&O Studio adds the dynamic filter parameter Visual Studio creates: <provider class, at most 21 characters>_DynamicParameter, of type Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Framework.Services.Client.QueryMetadata, hidden, allowing blank and null, with its AOT query set. This applies to a report data provider with [SRSReportQueryAttribute] and to Query datasets. New datasets start with Dynamic Filters off: turn it on first, then set the Query.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Builds update the cross-reference database. Your data provider classes only appear in the picker after a build with cross-references.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The … button on a dataset's Query sends pickReportQuery from media/element.js to src/elementDesigner.ts, which runs pickDataSetQuery in src/reports/reportDesigner.ts.
  • The data provider list is the language action report_providers: a recursive cross-reference query for classes that extend SrsReportDataProviderBase (server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs).
  • Data tables and fields come from the bridge action report_datasource_schema; saving is set_report_dataset_query (a write action) (MetaModelBridge.ReportDataSets.cs).
  • The schema is read with Microsoft's analyzers in Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Metadata.Extensions (from your PackagesLocalDirectory\bin): AxReportProviderMetadata.GetSchemaAnalyzer for a data provider and AxQuerySchemaAnalyzer for a query, the ones Visual Studio's designer calls. Framework parameters are recognised with Microsoft's AxSchemaAnalyzerHelper.IsFrameworkParameter.
  • The report is saved through the metadata API, then the element designer reloads the tree and properties.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Business Logic and Database Stored Procedure datasets: type the Query yourself.
  • The picker shows data provider classes only from the cross-reference database. A new class appears after a build with cross-references.
  • An enum dataset has no field selection.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The cross-reference database is not available. The report data provider list comes from it." No cross-reference database for the active configuration, or it can't be opened. Check the configuration (see Select-Environment); build with xpp.build.crossReference on. Your data provider class is not in the list The class wasn't built with cross-references yet, or it doesn't extend SrsReportDataProviderBase. Build the model (see Build-Project-and-Model) and check the class's extends. "Class has no data tables: a report data provider returns them from methods with [SRSReportDataSetAttribute]." No method with the attribute returns a record. Add a getter with [SRSReportDataSetAttribute(tableStr(…))] returning the temporary table. "F&O Studio picks the Query of Report Data Provider, Query and Enum Provider datasets. For … type it in the property." The Data Source Type is Business Logic or Database Stored Procedure. Type the Query in the property. "… has no fields to use among the selected ones." The field selection matched nothing. Pick at least one field. "Could not read …: …" The class, table or query can't be analyzed (not found, not built). Check the name and build the model. The dynamic filter parameter is missing Dynamic Filters was off when the Query was set. Turn it on and set the Query again.

docs.title: Report Designer
docs.text: The Report Designer lays out the precision design (SSRS RDL) of a D365FO report in VS Code: a page with margins, header, body and footer, rulers in millimetres or inches, grid and snap, and textboxes, rectangles, lines, images and tablixes you place to the tenth of a millimetre. It is the VS Code counterpart of Visual Studio's precision design editor, with layout warnings for preprinted stationery, a scanned-form overlay and a preview by Microsoft's report engine.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need exact positions: cheques, preprinted purchase orders, invoices, labels, forms with boxes.
  • You want to change a precision design you generated from an auto design.
  • You want to copy the layout of a standard report into your own report and adjust it.

For list-style reports whose layout SSRS can generate, an auto design is often enough (see Report-Element-Designer).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The report exists and has at least one dataset if you want to place fields (see Report-Datasets).
  • To change a report, it must be in a model you can change. Standard reports open read-only.
  • For the preview: Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime (see Report-Preview).

docs.title: Open a design
docs.text:
• Element designer: right-click the report or a precision design → Open Report Designer, or double-click a precision design (or select it and press Enter).
  • Application Explorer or project view: right-click a report → Open Report Designer.
  • Command palette: F&O Studio: Open Report Designer asks for the report name.

Which design opens:

  • You picked a design: that one.
  • The report has several designs: a quick pick lists them. An auto design is marked "auto design: creates a precision design from it"; picking it runs Create Precision Design….
  • The report has no precision design: the designer shows the report's auto designs with a button Create precision design from name… for each, and Create blank precision design with a name box (default Report).

Each design opens once: opening it again shows the existing tab. The tab title is Report.Design [Report], with ● in front while there are unsaved changes.

docs.title: The window
docs.text:
Area Content Toolbar Report name, the Design drop-down (switches design; auto designs are listed as "(auto design: create a precision design…)"), model name and "read-only" for standard reports, then the tool groups below. Report data (left) Datasets with their fields and types, Parameters (without the hidden AX_* ones), Built-in fields, and Labels. Page (centre) The sheet with rulers, margins (dashed), the page header, body and page footer, and the items. Properties (right) Properties of the selection, or of the page when nothing is selected. Warnings Layout warnings under the page. Status bar Pointer position in mm and inches, the selected item's position and size in mm from the sheet's top-left corner, and messages.

The body area beyond the first page (a body taller than the paper) is hatched in red. Items whose Hidden is true are drawn faded; items hidden by an expression have a dashed outline; textboxes that can grow have an orange corner mark. Text shows fields as «Field», parameters as [@Parameter], built-in fields as [&PageNumber], labels with their text (when the label is found), and other expressions as «Expr».

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Group Buttons File Save (Ctrl+S), Undo (Ctrl+Z), Redo (Ctrl+Y) Add Textbox, Rectangle, Line, Image: click the button, then click on the page. Escape cancels. Arrange Align lefts / centers / rights / tops / middles / bottoms (to the first selected item), Make same width, Make same height (two or more items), Distribute horizontally / vertically (three or more), Bring to front, Send to back Zoom Zoom out, Zoom in (steps of 25 %, from 25 % to 800 %), Actual size (100%) Grid Show grid, Snap to grid, grid size (0.5 mm, 1 mm, 2 mm, 0.1 in, 1/8 in, 5 mm), Scan overlay, Measure Mode Design, Preview Other View the RDL (opens the current RDL as an untitled XML document), Report properties (opens the report in the element designer)

Zoom, grid settings and preview settings are remembered for the panel.

docs.title: Adding items
docs.text:
Item Created with Textbox 40 × 5 mm, Segoe UI 9 pt, no border, padding 0, Can grow off Rectangle 50 × 30 mm, solid border Line 50 mm horizontal, solid 1 pt Image asks for an image file (png, jpg, jpeg, bmp, gif, tif, tiff), embeds it in the report and places it at 30 × 20 mm, Fit proportional

Items go into the section or rectangle you click in. New names are the type plus a number (Textbox1). Positions snap to the grid when snap is on.

docs.title: Placing data
docs.text:
Drag from the Report data pane:

Dragged Onto the page Into a tablix cell Dataset field Textbox =First(Fields!Name.Value, "DataSet") =Fields!Name.Value when the tablix uses the same dataset Parameter =Parameters!Name.Value same Built-in field =Globals!PageNumber (also TotalPages, OverallPageNumber, OverallTotalPages, ExecutionTime, ReportName, RenderFormat.Name) same

Labels: type a label reference in the Labels box (@SYS12345 or @File:Id) and click the add button. A textbox =Labels!@… is placed at 5 mm, 5 mm in the body. Double-click a textbox to jump to its Value.

docs.title: Selecting, moving and resizing
docs.text:
• Click an item to select it; Ctrl+click or Shift+click adds or removes items. The first selected item is the reference for align and same-size.
  • Drag on an empty area to select with a rectangle (items fully inside).
  • Drag an item to move it; drag one of the eight handles to resize it (one item selected). Moves snap to the grid when snap is on.
  • Click the table grip on a tablix to select the tablix; click a cell to select its textbox.
  • Items inside tablix cells don't move or resize with the mouse or keys; change column widths and row heights instead.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text:
The page must have focus (click it first).

Key Action Arrow keys Move the selection by the grid size (snap on) or 0.5 mm (snap off) Ctrl+arrow keys Move by 0.1 mm Shift+arrow keys Resize by the same step (Ctrl+Shift+arrow: by 0.1 mm) Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V Copy, cut, paste. Pasted items are renamed and offset by 2 mm; they go into the selected rectangle or the selection's container. Ctrl+D Duplicate (copy and paste) Delete Delete the selection. In a tablix cell, clears the textbox's value. Ctrl+A Select every item of the body Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undo / redo (up to 200 steps) Ctrl+S Save Escape Cancel the add or measure tool and clear the selection Alt+drag Measure

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
With one item selected:

Group Properties General Name (letters, digits, underscores; must be unused) Position (mm from the container) x, y, Width, Height, Z-order; a hint shows the position on the sheet Visibility Hidden: true, false or an expression Text (textbox) Value (text or expression), Can grow, Can shrink, Format (.NET format such as N2, d, dd/MM/yyyy) Font (textbox) Family (suggests the fonts D365FO reports offer, marked when installed here), Size (pt), Weight, Style, Decoration, Color Alignment and padding (textbox) Horizontal, Vertical, Padding left/right/top/bottom (pt) Border and fill (textbox, rectangle, image) Border, Border width, Border color, Background Line Style, Width, Color Image Source (Embedded, Database, External), Value, Sizing (AutoSize, Fit, FitProportional, Clip), Embed image… Tablix Dataset, Keep together, No rows message, column widths and row heights in mm, its groups Cell (item in a tablix) Column left, Column right, Delete column, Row above, Row below, Delete row, Column width (mm), Row height (mm), Select tablix

With several items selected, the panel says how many and points to the toolbar.

With nothing selected, the panel shows the page:

Group Properties Paper (mm) Size presets (Letter portrait/landscape, Legal portrait, A4 portrait/landscape, A5 portrait, Executive portrait, Cheque 8.5 x 3.5 in, or Custom), Width, Height Margins (mm) Left, Right, Top, Bottom Body (mm) Width, Height, Fit width to page Page header / Page footer Show, Height (mm), First page, Last page Design Units for new sizes (inches, centimetres, millimetres) and the RDL schema version Scan overlay See Scan-Overlay-and-Measure

Values you type are in mm; the designer writes them back in the unit the RDL already used for that value (inches stay inches). New values use the design's unit (rd:ReportUnitType), or the one you pick under Units for new sizes.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
Shown under the page while you design, and again after saving:

  • Body width plus margins wider than the page: every page gets an extra blank page.
  • Body height taller than the space between header and footer: the body breaks onto another page.
  • A font that is not in Microsoft's list of fonts available to D365FO reports (the cloud substitutes another), or that is not installed on this machine (the preview substitutes it).
  • A textbox that can grow and pushes the items below it down.
  • An item that ends right of the body's edge.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Save (Ctrl+S) stores the RDL as the precision design's text through the metadata API. Images embedded in the RDL become the report's embedded images. The status bar says to build the model to compile the report (see Report-Build).

Unsaved changes are kept as a draft. When you reopen the design after closing VS Code or the tab, you are asked Restore Changes or Discard. Closing the tab with unsaved changes shows a warning. Switching designs with unsaved changes asks Discard and Switch.

docs.title: Standard reports
docs.text: A report in a model you can't change opens read-only, with a banner and Duplicate into my model…. Duplicate the report into your model (Microsoft's extension pattern for report layouts), change the copy, then select it in print management or redirect the controller to it.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: No settings. Zoom, grid, preview settings and the scan placement are stored in the panel's state.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The panel is src/reports/reportDesigner.ts; the editor is media/reportDesigner.js. The RDL is edited as an XML DOM in the webview, so every element the designer doesn't touch (charts, gauges, maps, subreports, custom properties, code) is kept as it was, with its schema version (2005 to 2016) and units.
  • Loading uses the bridge actions report_info and get_report_design, which return the RDL, the labels it uses with their text, the fonts D365FO supports (with an installed flag), the embedded images, datasets and parameters (MetaModelBridge.Reports.cs).
  • Save calls set_report_design (a write action), which checks that the text is RDL in a known namespace, sets AxReportPrecisionDesign.Text and imports the embedded images. Create blank precision design saves the blank Letter design the same way.
  • Warnings are computed in the webview and by RdlPreview.Check on the server (server/Host/Reports/RdlPreview.cs). The supported font list is Microsoft's published list of fonts for D365FO reports, embedded in the server.
  • Drafts are kept in the workspace state; the panel is restored after a window reload.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Charts, gauges, maps, subreports and custom report items are drawn as placeholders ("kept as is"); change them in the RDL.
  • Tablix: columns can be inserted and deleted only in tablixes without column groups (not in a matrix); rows only next to fixed rows (headers and footers), not inside a group.
  • Rich text: the Value edits the first text run of the first paragraph; other runs and paragraphs are edited in the RDL.
  • Borders set per side are drawn, but edited in the RDL.
  • There is no expression editor: type expressions in Value, Hidden or the other fields.
  • SSRS keeps overlapping items in PDF and print, but moves them apart in interactive (HTML) viewing; the preview renders like PDF and print.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The design is not valid XML; open it as RDL text to fix it." The saved RDL doesn't parse. Fix it with View the RDL or the agent tools, then save it again. "The design is not a report definition (root in one of the RDL 2005-2016 namespaces)." Saving text that isn't RDL. Keep the Report root and its namespace. "'…' is not a valid, unused name." The item name is taken or has other characters. Use letters, digits and underscores, and a name not used in the design. "This tablix has column groups (a matrix); change its columns in the RDL." Column insert/delete on a matrix. Edit the RDL. "Rows can be added next to the tablix's fixed rows (headers and footers)…" Row insert inside a group. Edit the RDL. Every page is followed by a blank page Body width plus margins exceed the paper width. Use Fit width to page under Body. Nothing moves with the arrow keys The page doesn't have focus, or the item is in a tablix cell. Click the page first; change cell sizes through column widths and row heights. Toolbar and properties are disabled The report is in a model you can't change. Duplicate into my model…

docs.title: Report Element Designer
docs.text: An SSRS report (AxReport) opens in the F&O Studio element designer with the same tree and Properties window as Visual Studio's report designer: Datasets, Designs, Images and Parameters. You add datasets, create auto designs and their data regions, and generate precision designs from auto designs, all through Microsoft's metadata API. The layout of a precision design is edited in the Report Designer; this page covers the report element itself.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need a new report and want to build it yourself, element by element, as you would in Visual Studio.
  • You want to look at how a standard report (for example Cheque_US, SalesInvoice, PurchPurchaseOrder) is built: its datasets, designs and parameters.
  • You want a quick list-style report: an auto design with a table or list region generated from a dataset.
  • You want to turn an auto design into a precision design for exact positioning (preprinted forms, cheques).

If you want the whole chain (temporary table, data provider, contract, controller, menu item, privilege) created for you, use the report wizard instead: see Wizard-Report.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration and the F&O Studio metadata server running (see Getting-Started).
  • A model you can change. Reports in standard models open read-only; you can still browse them.
  • For report data provider datasets: a cross-reference database. The list of data provider classes comes from it (see Report-Datasets).

docs.title: Create an empty report
docs.text:
1. Run New Element… (Application Explorer, project view or the command palette).
  2. Under Reports, pick Report ("empty report: add datasets and designs in the designer"). The wizard entry Report (wizard) is the other option and runs New Report….
  3. Enter the name, for example ContosoCustGroupList. The report is created in your model and opens in the element designer.

To open an existing report, click it in the Application-Explorer or the project view, or use Open Designer from its context menu.

docs.title: The report tree
docs.text:
The tree follows Visual Studio's report designer:

Node What it holds Datasets The report's datasets (DataSets in metadata). Each dataset has Fields, Field Groups and Parameters. Designs Auto designs and precision designs. Images The report's embedded images (EmbeddedImages). Parameters The parameters of the default parameter group, listed directly.

Some details match Visual Studio on purpose:

  • An auto design shows its data regions (table, list, matrix, chart) directly under it. A table or list shows Groupings, Sortings, Filters and Data; the fields sit directly under Data. A matrix shows Row Groupings, Column Groupings, Filters and Data; a chart shows Series, Filters and Data.
  • Visual Studio has no Data Methods node; F&O Studio hides it too (the data methods stay in the metadata).
  • A precision design's Text property (the whole RDL) is not shown in the Properties window. You edit it in the Report-Designer.
  • Report sub-objects such as Page Size, Margin, Interactive Size, Size To Fit, padding and styles are expandable rows in the Properties pane (for example PageSize.Width), not tree nodes.
  • Property categories are alphabetical, and enum values read as in Visual Studio ("Report Data Provider" for ReportDataProvider); the value saved is still the enum name.

See Element-Designer and Properties-Grid-and-Pickers for the general behaviour of the tree and the Properties grid.

docs.title: Add a dataset
docs.text:
1. Right-click Datasets and choose New…, then Data Set. The new dataset starts with Dynamic Filters off, as in Visual Studio.
  2. Set Data Source Type (Query, Report Data Provider or Enum Provider).
  3. Click the … button of the Query property (or press Alt+Down on it) to pick the source and its fields. The fields, the dataset parameters and the report parameters are filled in for you.

The full flow is on Report-Datasets.

You can also drag a query or a class from the Application Explorer onto Datasets: a query creates a Query dataset (SELECT * FROM <query>), a class creates a Report Data Provider dataset on the temporary table named in its SRSReportDataSetAttribute. Then use the Query … button to fill the fields. See Drag-and-Drop.

docs.title: Add a design
docs.text:
Right-click Designs, choose New…, then:

  • Auto Design: a design whose layout SSRS generates from its data regions.
  • Precision Design: a fixed layout. A new precision design starts as an empty page (Letter portrait, half-inch margins, 2016 RDL schema), which the Report Designer opens.

docs.title: Add a data region to an auto design
docs.text:
1. Right-click an auto design, or the Designs folder, and choose Add Data Region from Data Set….
  2. On Designs, enter the name of the new auto design (default Report, or Report1 when Report is taken).
  3. If the report has several datasets, pick one.
  4. Pick the layout:
  5. Table: one row per record, a column per field.
  6. List: fields side by side, a block per record.

F&O Studio adds Table1 (or List1, numbered on when taken) with every field of the dataset, except fields marked not to be created in a data region (enum fields from the schema). A new auto design gets Letter page and interactive sizes, half-inch margins and the standard layout template ReportLayoutStyleTemplate; tables use TableStyleTemplate, lists ListStyleTemplate.

If the report has no dataset yet, you get a warning to add one first.

docs.title: Create a precision design from an auto design
docs.text:
1. Right-click an auto design and choose Create Precision Design….
  2. Enter the name of the new design (default <auto design>Precision; letters, digits and underscores).
  3. F&O Studio runs Microsoft's report generator on the auto design, saves the result as a new precision design and opens it in the Report-Designer. The auto design stays as it is.

The auto design must have at least one data region. When a data region is shown in the document map, the new precision design keeps that setting, as in Visual Studio.

docs.title: Open the Report Designer
docs.text:
• Right-click the report (root node) or a precision design and choose Open Report Designer.
  • Double-click a precision design, or select it and press Enter.
  • In the Application Explorer or project view, Open Report Designer is on the context menu of every report.

When the report has several designs and you didn't pick one, a quick pick asks which design to open. Picking an auto design runs Create Precision Design… for it.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Where Effect New Element… → Report Application Explorer, project, command palette Creates an empty report. New Report… command palette, New Element → Report (wizard) Runs the report wizard. Open Report Designer report in Application Explorer or project; report root or precision design in the element designer; command palette Opens the precision design in the Report Designer. From the palette it asks for the report name. Create Precision Design… auto design in the element designer (editable reports only) Generates a precision design from the auto design. Add Data Region from Data Set… auto design or Designs folder in the element designer (editable reports only) Adds a table or list region.

Create Precision Design… and Add Data Region from Data Set… are not in the command palette; they need the node they work on.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The element designer is generated from Microsoft's metadata classes (AxReport, AxReportDataSet, AxReportAutoDesign, AxReportPrecisionDesign…). Node order, folder labels, hidden nodes and the expandable sub-objects for reports are defined in server/Ported/MetaModel/MetaModelBridge.ElementDesigner.cs.
  • New… lists the concrete metadata types a collection accepts; for reports they are named as in Visual Studio's New menu (Data Set, Auto Design, Precision Design, Table, List…), and the abstract base design type is left out (MetaModelBridge.DesignerActions.cs).
  • Add Data Region from Data Set… calls the bridge action add_report_data_region; Create Precision Design… calls create_precision_design. Both are write actions on the report and are saved through the metadata API (MetaModelBridge.Reports.cs).
  • The precision design is generated by ReportGenerator from Microsoft.Dynamics.Framework.Tools.Reports.Build.dll in your PackagesLocalDirectory\bin, in Designer mode, the generator reportsc uses (server/Host/Reports/ReportDesignGenerator.cs). F&O Studio does not ship it. Images embedded in the generated RDL become the report's embedded images.
  • The commands live in src/reports/reportDesigner.ts; the element designer's context keys (xppReportName, xppReportDesign) come from media/element.js.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Standard reports can't be changed in place. Duplicate the report into your model (see Report-Designer, Duplicate into my model…).
  • Add Data Region from Data Set… creates tables and lists only. Matrix and chart regions can be added with New…, but their contents are set up in the tree by hand.
  • Precision designs are laid out in the Report Designer, not in the tree. An auto design can't be saved as a precision design under its own name.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Report has no datasets yet: add one under Data Sets first" Add Data Region from Data Set… needs a dataset. Add a dataset and set its Query first. "Auto design '…' has no data regions yet" Create Precision Design… on an empty auto design. Run Add Data Region from Data Set… first. "Report '…' already has a design '…'" The precision design name is taken. Pick another name. "The report generator (Microsoft.Dynamics.Framework.Tools.Reports.Build.dll) is not in this environment's bin folder." The generator assembly is missing from PackagesLocalDirectory\bin. Check the active configuration's metadata; see Select-Environment. "Design '…' is a precision design: lay it out in the Report Designer." You tried to add a data region to a precision design. Use the Report Designer, or add the region to an auto design. Create Precision Design and Add Data Region are missing from the menu The report is in a model you can't change. Duplicate the report into your model.

docs.title: Report Preview
docs.text: The Report Designer's Preview renders a precision design with Microsoft's own report engine (the Report Viewer runtime), with the same hard page layout as PDF and print. You see the real pages, with labels in the language you choose and sample data or rows you type, without deploying the report. Visual Studio has no local preview for D365FO reports; there you deploy and run the report on the environment.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Check a layout to the millimetre before you build and deploy: page breaks, growing textboxes, blank pages, fonts.
  • Compare the rendered page with a scanned form (see Scan-Overlay-and-Measure).
  • Check how long values (names, amounts) fit in their boxes, with the values printed on your sample form.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A precision design open in the Report-Designer. The preview renders precision designs only.
  • Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime, downloaded once from nuget.org after you accept Microsoft's licence. F&O Studio doesn't ship it. See Installing the runtime.
  • No environment connection is needed: rendering runs on your machine.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. In the Report Designer, click Preview in the toolbar. The first time, the preview renders right away.
  2. If the runtime isn't installed, the licence prompt opens first (see below).
  3. The pages appear in the centre. A line above them says which pages are shown, the total page count and the resolution, for example "Pages 1–3 of 5 · rendered by Microsoft's report engine (as PDF and print) at 110 dpi". Warnings follow.
  4. Change the settings in the right panel and click Render to render again.
  5. Click Design to go back to the layout.

The preview renders the design as it is in the designer, including unsaved changes.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect Language en-US Language of the label texts and the AX_RenderingCulture parameter. Labels missing in that language fall back to en-US. Company USMF Value of the AX_CompanyName parameter. Sample rows 1 Rows generated for each dataset you leave empty (0 to 200). Pages 3 Number of pages rendered (1 to 20). Resolution (dpi) 110 Resolution of the page images (48 to 300). Show scan under the page off Only when a scan is loaded: lays the scan under each page and blends them.

Settings are remembered for the panel.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Under Data (JSON rows per dataset) there is a text box per dataset. Type a JSON array of rows, field name to value:

[
  { "AccountNum": "US-001", "Name": "Contoso Retail San Diego", "AmountCur": 1234567.89, "TransDate": "2026-01-31" },
  { "AccountNum": "US-002", "Name": "Contoso Wholesale", "AmountCur": 42.5, "TransDate": "2026-02-01" }
]
  • The placeholder of each box shows a sample row built from the dataset's fields.
  • A box that isn't a JSON array is rejected with a message when you leave it.
  • Fields you leave out of a row get a generated value.
  • Datasets left empty get Sample rows generated rows.

Generated values are chosen to show realistic widths: text fields get the field name (Name, Name 2…), numbers 12345.67 (times the row number), integers the row number, dates 31 January 2026 plus the row number in days, and booleans false.

Tip: type the values printed on your sample form, so the widths you see are the widths that print.

docs.title: What the preview does with D365FO specifics
docs.text:
• Labels (=Labels!@SYS12345, @File:Id, and plain label references in values) are replaced by their text in the chosen language.
  • Parameters: every report parameter, the framework parameters (AX_PartitionKey, AX_CompanyName, AX_UserContext, AX_RenderingCulture, AX_ReportContext, AX_RdpPreProcessedId) and any parameter the design uses get a value: the company and language above, false for booleans, 0 for numbers, today for dates, empty text otherwise.
  • D365FO report functions that need an AOS session are replaced by local stand-ins: for example ToDisplayStringAmount, ToDisplayStringDate, ConvertUtcToAxUserTimeZoneForUser, GetFullCompanyNameForUser, NumeralsToTxt (amount in English words), SplitReportItem, GetExtendedDataTypeFormat, PostDataMethodEvaluation. Functions without a stand-in are shown empty, and a warning names them: "Shown empty in the preview (they need the environment): …".
  • Datasets and fields the design uses but the report doesn't define are added so the render doesn't fail, with a warning ("Dataset '…' is used by the design but not defined on the report.").
  • Embedded images of the report are included.

docs.title: Installing the runtime
docs.text:
The first Preview (or the command Install Report Preview Runtime) shows a modal prompt:

The report preview uses Microsoft's report engine (the Report Viewer runtime), which F&O Studio does not include. Install it now? …

  • View Licence Terms opens Microsoft's licence terms for both packages in the browser, then asks again.
  • Accept Licence and Install downloads and installs.
  • Closing the prompt cancels; the preview then says it needs Microsoft's report engine and shows Install runtime….

What is installed:

Package (nuget.org) Version Files used Microsoft.ReportingServices.ReportViewerControl.Winforms 150.1652.0 Microsoft.ReportViewer.Common, .DataVisualization, .ProcessingObjectModel, .WinForms and their resources (net40) Microsoft.SqlServer.Types 14.0.1016.290 Microsoft.SqlServer.Types.dll

The download is about 15 MB. Each package is checked against a pinned SHA-512 hash, and each extracted file against a pinned SHA-256 hash; nothing is installed when a hash doesn't match. The files go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\FOStudio\ReportViewer\150.1652.0, with a .licence.txt per package recording the licence link.

The same runtime is used by Copilot's report tools xpp_render_report and xpp_compare_layout (see Agent-Tools-Reports).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
There are no VS Code settings for the preview. The preview settings above are stored in the panel.

Command Effect Install Report Preview Runtime Checks the runtime; asks for the licence and installs it when it is missing or changed.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The designer sends the current RDL, your rows and the settings to the extension (src/reports/reportDesigner.ts), which makes sure the runtime is installed (src/reports/reportRuntime.ts) and calls the bridge action render_report.
  2. The server checks the runtime folder again: it loads the runtime only when every file matches its pinned hash (server/Host/Reports/ReportRuntime.cs).
  3. RdlPreview.Prepare builds a renderable report from the design (server/Host/Reports/RdlPreview.cs): it removes the design's code modules, data sources, datasets and parameters; resolves labels; rewrites the D365FO helper calls to the local stand-ins (a VB Code block); declares a local data source, the report's datasets (from the metadata) and its parameters; and fills a DataTable per dataset with your rows or sample rows.
  4. ReportRenderer renders it with LocalReport in a separate application domain whose base folder is the runtime folder, as PNG pages ("IMAGE" renderer with the chosen dpi), one page at a time (server/Host/Reports/ReportRenderer.cs). External images and hyperlinks are off. The domain is recycled every 50 renders to keep memory bounded.
  5. The result returns the pages, the total page count, the page geometry, each item's position in mm and the warnings (layout checks, preparation notes and the engine's own warnings).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only precision designs render; for an auto design, create a precision design first.
  • Data is local: sample rows or rows you type. The data provider doesn't run, so values computed in X++ aren't there.
  • D365FO report functions without a local stand-in show empty. Stand-ins approximate the AOS (for example GetEnumLabelFromValue shows the value, time-zone conversion keeps the value as given).
  • Fonts not installed on your machine are substituted (a warning says which). MICR and barcode fonts are often not installed locally; check those on the environment.
  • At most 20 pages per render.
  • The runtime is Windows .NET Framework code and is downloaded, not shipped; without internet access to nuget.org you can't install it from F&O Studio.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The preview needs Microsoft's report engine (Install Report Preview Runtime)." You declined or closed the licence prompt. Click Install runtime… or run Install Report Preview Runtime. "The Report Viewer runtime in … is incomplete or was changed (…). Run 'F&O Studio: Install Report Preview Runtime' again." A runtime file is missing or doesn't match its hash. Run Install Report Preview Runtime. "Downloading … from nuget.org failed: HTTP …" No access to nuget.org, or a proxy blocks it. Allow api.nuget.org and try again. "… from nuget.org is not the package F&O Studio expects (hash mismatch); nothing was installed." The downloaded package differs from the pinned one. Try again; check for a proxy that changes downloads. "The report engine could not render …: …" The engine rejected the RDL or an expression. Read the message; fix the expression or item in the designer. "Design '…' is an auto design; the preview renders precision designs." The design is an auto design. Create a precision design from it. "Dataset: enter a JSON array of rows (…)." The data box isn't a JSON array. Wrap rows in [ ] and use valid JSON. Values show empty The textbox uses a D365FO function without a stand-in. See the "Shown empty in the preview" warning; check on the environment.

docs.title: Report a Problem
docs.text: Report a Problem… turns a failure into a GitHub issue for F&O Studio without leaking your code, your customer or your environment. It builds a short report (versions, environment type, the recent failures and, if you turned it on, your local command counts), removes paths, URLs, names and quoted text, and shows it to you before anything leaves the machine. You then decide: file it as an issue with your GitHub account, open it in the browser, or copy it. Nothing is sent automatically.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• A command fails with an error you did not expect (not a "do this first" message such as "Open a D365FO project first.").
  • Connect to Environment… fails and Retry does not help.
  • A panel (designer, data panel, report designer) shows an error.
  • Something behaves differently from Visual Studio and you want to tell the maintainer.

For messages with a known fix, check Troubleshooting first.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Nothing is needed to create and copy the report.
  • To file the issue directly, you need a GitHub account. VS Code asks you to sign in to GitHub the first time.
  • To open the issue in the browser, you need to be signed in to github.com in your browser.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Where What happens Report Problem button on an error notification Starts the report for the command that just failed, with that command's recent failures Report Problem button after "Environment setup failed: ..." Starts the report for the environment setup Report a Problem… at the bottom of the Dynamics 365 view Starts the report with the latest failures of this session Command Palette: F&O Studio: Report a Problem… Same as above

Errors from commands show two buttons: Show Log opens the X++ output, Report Problem starts the report. Errors from panels, pickers and background work show Report Problem only.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Start the report from one of the places above.
  2. Report a problem (1/2): an input box asks "What did you do, and what happened? (optional)". Describe the steps in a sentence or two, or leave it empty. Press Escape to cancel; nothing is created.
  3. A Markdown preview of the report opens in an editor. This is exactly what the report contains. You can edit it: add detail, or remove anything you do not want to share.
  4. Report a problem (2/2): a dialog says "this is everything the report contains (paths, URLs, names and quoted text are removed). Edit it if you like." Choose one:
Button What happens Create GitHub Issue Files the issue on github.com/nazmolla/xpp-vscode with your GitHub account. VS Code asks you to sign in to GitHub the first time. You then see "Thanks! Issue #... was created." with Open Issue Open in Browser Opens a new issue page on GitHub with the title and the report filled in. You review it and submit it yourself Copy to Clipboard Copies the report. Paste it wherever you like, for example into an existing issue Cancel (close the dialog) Nothing is sent. The preview stays open so you can copy it later
  1. If you edited the preview, the edited text is what is sent or copied.

If the issue cannot be created directly (for example you declined the GitHub sign-in or GitHub refused the request), you see "The issue could not be created directly (...); it opens in the browser instead." and the browser opens with the report, as with Open in Browser.

Long reports do not fit in a URL. When the report is 6000 characters or longer, Open in Browser puts the report on the clipboard and the issue page says "The report is on the clipboard: paste it here."

docs.title: What the report contains
docs.text:
## What happened

<your description, or "(not described)">

## Environment

- F&O Studio 0.17.2, VS Code 1.101.0, Windows_NT 10.0.26100
- Environment: unified developer environment, application 10.0.xxxx.xx

## Recent failures

**xpp.buildProject** (10:42:13): <error message>
```
<first 8 lines of the stack trace>
```

## Most used commands (local counts)

- xpp.openObject: 42
- xpp.buildProject: 17
Section Content What happened Your description from step 2 Environment F&O Studio version, VS Code version, Windows version; the environment type (unified developer environment or cloud-hosted/VHD, or "none configured") and its application version Recent failures For the failed command: up to 3 of its recent failures. Otherwise: the last 5 failures of this session. Each with the command ID, the time, the message and the first 8 lines of the stack. "none recorded in this session" when there are none Most used commands Only when Usage-Statistics is on: the 15 most used commands and their counts

The issue title is the failed command and the start of its message (at most 80 characters), or "Problem report" when no failure was recorded.

docs.title: What is removed
docs.text:
Before you see the report, F&O Studio replaces:

Found in the text Replaced with Access tokens (JWTs starting with eyJ) <token> Long random strings (40 or more letters, digits, +, /, _, -), such as keys and SAS signatures <secret> URLs (http://..., https://...) <url> E-mail addresses <email> GUIDs <guid> User folders (C:\Users\<name>...) <user folder> Dataverse and Finance and Operations host names (*.crm*.dynamics.com, *.operations.dynamics.com, *.sandbox.operations.dynamics.com, *.cloudax.dynamics.com) <environment> Text in single or double quotes (3 characters or more), such as element names, labels or values in messages '…' or "…"

The removal runs on the whole report, including your description. Element names that are not in quotes (for example in a stack trace) stay. Read the preview and remove anything else you do not want to share.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Almost every F&O Studio command runs through one wrapper (Launch Debugger, the Infolog commands and Run Tests report their errors their own way). When a command throws, the wrapper writes the error and its stack to the X++ output, remembers it in memory, and shows the error with Show Log and Report Problem.
  • Errors outside commands (webview panels, pickers, background tasks, environment setup) are remembered the same way.
  • At most 20 failures are kept, in memory only. They are gone when you close the window; they are never written to disk.
  • The report reads the active environment the same way the rest of the extension does (registry and XPPConfig), only for its type and application version.
  • Create GitHub Issue asks VS Code for a GitHub session with the public_repo scope and calls the GitHub REST API (POST /repos/nazmolla/xpp-vscode/issues). The token stays in VS Code; it is not stored by F&O Studio.

Source: src/reportProblem.ts, the command wrapper in src/extension.ts.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
• F&O Studio collects no telemetry. Report a Problem only talks to GitHub when you choose Create GitHub Issue or Open in Browser.
  • Issues on nazmolla/xpp-vscode are public. Never paste customer data, code you may not share, credentials or environment URLs into the description or the preview.
  • The redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee. You are the last check: read the preview.

docs.title: Writing a useful report
docs.text:
• Say what you did, step by step: the command, the element (use a standard element such as CustTable or SalesFormLetter if you can reproduce it there), and what you expected.
  • Say which environment type you use: UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD.
  • If the X++ output has more detail, copy the relevant lines into the preview after checking them for names and paths.
  • If you can, try Restart X++ Server and run the command again first; say whether that helped.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Failures from earlier sessions are not in the report, because they are kept in memory only.
  • The redaction cannot recognise element or model names outside quotes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The issue could not be created directly (GitHub answered 401 ...)" or another status The GitHub sign-in was refused or expired Continue in the browser, or sign in to GitHub again in VS Code (Accounts menu) The browser issue page says "The report is on the clipboard: paste it here." The report is too long for a URL Paste it into the issue body "Recent failures" says "none recorded in this session" The window was reloaded after the failure, or the failure happened in another window Reproduce the problem, then report it from the same window

docs.title: Results View
docs.text: The Results view is the place where F&O Studio's checks put their findings: Review My Changes, the Pre-Deploy Checklist, Upgrade Readiness, Standard Code Drift and Show Feature Usage. Each run is a tree of sections and clickable findings, with a Markdown version of the report that you can copy or export. The view keeps the earlier runs of the session so you can switch back to them. It is the closest thing to Visual Studio's Error List for these reports, but grouped by check.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• To work through the findings of a check one by one: click, fix, go to the next.
  • To paste a report into a pull request, a work item or an email (Copy Report as Markdown).
  • To keep a report as a file (Export Report…), for example the Pre-Deploy Checklist of a release.
  • To compare the current run with an earlier one in the same session.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
The Results view is in the F&O Studio panel, next to Infolog and Copilot Activity. It opens by itself (without taking the keyboard focus) when a check finishes. To open it yourself, open the panel (View > Appearance > Panel) and choose the F&O Studio tab.

When there is no run yet, the view shows "Checks of your code appear here, with findings you can click." and links to Review My Changes, Pre-Deploy Checklist and Upgrade Readiness.

While a check runs, its progress shows in the view (for example "Reviewing your changes", "Checking ContosoExtensions for obsolete APIs…").

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
Results  Review My Changes since main · 14:32
  [report]  5 changed element(s) in 2 model(s)            <- summary (header)
  [info]    Pull request summary          5 element(s)
              Classes (2)                 ContosoSalesTable_Extension (new), ...
              Security impact             no roles, duties or privileges changed.
  [error]   Chain of Command              1
              ContosoSalesTable_Extension.validateWrite   does not call next (...)
  [pass]    Best practice and compiler    no warnings
  [warning] Performance                   2
              ...
  [history] Earlier runs
              Pre-Deploy Checklist: ContosoOrders         14:05:12
Part Content View description The current run's title and the time it ran (hours and minutes). Header The run's summary, with a report icon (not every check has one). Section A group of findings. Its icon is the worst severity in it; its description is a short status (for example "no warnings") or the number of findings. Sections with findings are expanded. Finding One result: a label (usually element and method), a description (line, message), and a tooltip with more detail (for example the suggested fix). Earlier runs The previous runs of this session, newest first, each with its time and an icon for its worst severity.

docs.title: Severities
docs.text:
Icon Severity Typical meaning Error error Blocks: a failed checklist step, a wrapper that skips next, a broken extension. Warning warning Should be looked at: performance findings, obsolete API uses, collisions that depend on deployment order. Info info For information: summary lines, wrappers that could not be checked. Pass pass The section or step passed.

The icons use the theme's Problems and Testing colours.

Screen readers read each section and finding with its severity in words, for example "warning: ContosoSalesHelper.post, line 42: uses ..." (see Accessibility).

docs.title: Working with findings
docs.text:
• Click a finding to open the element at the place it refers to:
  • findings with a method and line open the element's X++ code view at that line, counted from the method's first line;
  • findings with only a line open the code view at that line;
  • Upgrade Readiness findings look the element up by name first, then open its code;
  • Standard Code Drift findings open a diff editor instead.
  • Run Again (refresh icon in the view title) repeats the current run with the same input (for example the same base branch or model). It is shown when the current run can be repeated.
  • Copy Report as Markdown (copy icon) copies the current run's full report. The status bar says "Report copied as markdown" for a few seconds.
  • Export Report… (save icon) saves the current run's report as a .md file you choose.
  • Clear Results (clear-all icon) removes all runs.
  • Earlier runs: click a past run to make it the current one again. Run Again, Copy and Export then apply to it.
  • The view title also has Collapse All.

The four title commands are also in the Command Palette (category F&O Studio) while there is a run.

docs.title: The Markdown report
docs.text:
Every check builds a Markdown version of its report next to the tree. It is often more complete than the tree: for example, Review My Changes' report has the pull request summary as text, and Upgrade Readiness' report has the full text of all three checks. See the report formats on each check's page:

  • Review My Changes: the report
  • Pre-Deploy Checklist: the report
  • Standard Code Drift: the report

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
The Results view has no settings.

Context key True when xpp.results.hasRun There is at least one run (Copy, Export and Clear are shown). xpp.results.canRerun The current run can be repeated (Run Again is shown).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The view is ResultsView in src/results.ts, a tree view with the id xpp.results. Each check builds a ResultRun:

Field Content title, time Shown in the view description and in Earlier runs. summary Optional header line. sections Title, severity, description and findings. markdown The report for Copy and Export. rerun The command and arguments for Run Again.

A finding opens either through its own command (Upgrade Readiness uses xpp.results.goToElement, which looks the element up with bridge action find_object; Standard Code Drift uses vscode.diff) or through its location (xpp.results.goTo), which opens the element's code view and finds the method's first line.

The view keeps the last 10 runs, in memory only: they are gone when you close the window. Nothing is written to disk unless you export a report.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Runs are not kept across restarts. Export a report to keep it.
  • Copy, Export and Run Again work on the current run only. Click an earlier run first to use them on it.
  • Findings are a snapshot: after you fix code, run the check again to update them.
  • Clicking a finding of an element that no longer exists shows an error (" was not found.").

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The view is empty after a check. The check found nothing to report and said so in a message (for example "No changed elements in your models"), or it was cancelled. Read the notification; run the check again. Run Again is missing. There is no run, or the current run cannot be repeated. Start the check from its command. A finding opens the code at the wrong line. The code changed since the run. Run the check again. An earlier run disappeared. Only the last 10 runs are kept. Export reports you need to keep.
