docs.title: Review My Changes
docs.text: Review My Changes reviews the elements you changed before you open a pull request. It finds the changed elements of your models in Git, writes a pull request summary (elements by type, security impact, work items), and checks the changed code: best practice (xppbp) and compiler warnings, performance heuristics, and Chain of Command wrappers that do not call next. The result appears in the Results view as clickable findings and as a Markdown report you can paste into the pull request. Visual Studio has no direct equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you commit or open a pull request: copy the summary into the pull request description.
  • As a self-review step: fix the warnings in your changed elements before a colleague reviews them.
  • After Copilot changed code, to see what changed and whether it breaks rules.
  • When you review someone else's branch: check it out and run the review against the base branch (see Scenario: Review a Pull Request).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your custom models must be in a Git repository, and git must be on the PATH. The change list is the one of Show Changed Elements.
  • An active D365FO configuration (see Select Environment): the review reads elements through the metadata server.
  • Best practice checks run xppbp.exe from the bin folder of the active configuration.
  • No project is needed: the review covers all your models.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the review from one of these places:
  2. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Review My Changes.
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Build and check > Review My Changes.
  4. Project view title bar: the Check menu > Review My Changes (shown when a project is open).
  5. The empty Results view: the Review My Changes link.
  6. An input box asks: "Compare with this branch (empty: only uncommitted changes)". The box is pre-filled with xpp.git.baseBranch, or main if the setting is empty.
  7. Keep or type a branch name to review what the branch changed since it left that branch, plus your uncommitted changes.
  8. Clear the box to review only uncommitted changes.
  9. Press Escape to cancel.
  10. The review runs with progress in the Results view: "finding changed elements", then one step per changed element, then "best practice checks". You can cancel it.
  11. The Results view shows the report. Click a finding to open the element's code at that line.
  12. Use Copy Report as Markdown in the Results view title bar to copy the full report for the pull request, or Export Report… to save it as a .md file. Run Again repeats the review with the same base branch.

If nothing changed, you see "No changed elements in your models since main (models must be in a Git repository)." and no report is created.

docs.title: Pull request summary
docs.text:
Built from the list of changed elements (including deleted ones):

Item Content Severity in Results Elements by type One line per element type, with the count and the names. New elements are marked (new), deleted ones (deleted). info Security impact Lists the changed roles, duties and privileges (and their extensions) and reminds you to check role licenses (Security view > Analyze License) and segregation of duties. Otherwise "no roles, duties or privileges changed." warning when security changed New menu items need a privilege Only when menu items were added: their names. warning Work items Work item IDs found in the branch's commit messages (#123 or AB#123). Without any: "none named in the commit messages (Link Work Item… adds one)." Only with a base branch. warning when none

The work items come from git log --format=%B <base>..HEAD. Use Link Work Item… to put the mention into the commit message (see Work Items and Pipelines).

docs.title: Chain of Command
docs.text:
For each changed class (not deleted) that is a Chain of Command extension of a class, table or form ([ExtensionOf(classStr(...))], tableStr or formStr), the review reads the base element and checks every method of the extension that has the same name as a method of the base element. If the method's code has no next <method>( call, it is reported as an error:

ContosoSalesTable_Extension.validateWrite wraps SalesTable.validateWrite but never calls `next validateWrite(...)`:
the standard logic is skipped (only allowed for [Replaceable] methods).

Fix it by calling next in the wrapper:

[ExtensionOf(tableStr(SalesTable))]
final class ContosoSalesTable_Extension
{
    public boolean validateWrite()
    {
        boolean ret = next validateWrite();
        // your checks
        return ret;
    }
}

When every wrapper calls next, the section shows "every wrapper calls next".

docs.title: Best practice and compiler
docs.text:
1. For each model with changed elements, F&O Studio runs the best practice checks (xppbp, the same checker as Visual Studio's "Run best practice checks") and keeps the results of the changed elements. The report shows one line per model: ContosoExtensions: 0 error(s), 2 warning(s) in the changed elements.
  2. It then collects the errors and warnings that are in the Problems view for each changed element (best practice, compiler, syntax check and obsolete API warnings), except the performance ones, which have their own section.

If xppbp could not run, the report says "Not run." and the section says "not run".

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: For each changed class, table, form and data entity (not deleted), the review runs the same static analysis as Analyze Performance and keeps the findings of severity Warning. Each finding names the method and line, the message, and the suggested fix (in the tooltip). The rules are listed in Performance Rules Reference; for data entities they include the data entity readiness checks.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
The Results view shows four sections:

Section Content Pull request summary The summary items above. Chain of Command Wrappers that do not call next. Best practice and compiler Errors and warnings from the Problems view for the changed elements. Performance Performance warnings.

The header line says, for example, 5 changed element(s) in 2 model(s). The run is titled Review My Changes since main (or Review My Changes without a base branch).

Copy Report as Markdown copies a report like this:

# Review of my changes (since main, plus uncommitted)

## Pull request summary

4 element(s) in 1 model(s):

- **Classes** (2): ContosoSalesTable_Extension (new), ContosoOrderStatusService
- **Display Menu Items** (1): ContosoOrderStatus (new)
- **Security Privileges** (1): ContosoOrderStatusView (new)

**Security impact:** ContosoOrderStatusView changed; check role licenses (Security view > Analyze License) and segregation of duties.
New menu items need a privilege: ContosoOrderStatus.

**Work items:** #1234, #1240

## Best practice

- ContosoExtensions: 0 error(s), 1 warning(s) in the changed elements.

## Findings

- ContosoOrderStatusService.run line 14: <performance message> *<suggested fix>*
- ContosoOrderStatusService line 22: <best practice or compiler message> (<rule code>)

_Best-practice results are also in the Problems view. Performance findings are heuristics; confirm before changing code._

The "Findings" list combines the Chain of Command, performance and Problems findings, without duplicates. When there are none, it says "No warnings."

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Pre-fills the branch prompt. Empty pre-fills main.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The command is in src/review.ts:

  1. changedElements(base) from src/changes.ts lists the changed elements (git status plus git diff --name-status from the merge base). Deleted elements are in the summary but not checked.
  2. Work items: branchWorkItems in src/devops.ts.
  3. For each changed AxClass, AxTable, AxForm and AxDataEntityView: bridge action analyze_performance.
  4. For each changed class: bridge action read_object for the class and for the element it extends, then a text check for next <method>( in each wrapping method.
  5. Per model: XppBuilder.bestPractice in src/build.ts runs xppbp.exe -metadata=<custom metadata> -packagesRoot=<PackagesLocalDirectory> -module=<package> -model=<model> -all and publishes the results of the changed elements to the Problems view.
  6. The Problems view diagnostics of each changed element's code view are collected (errors and warnings, except source X++ performance).
  7. The run goes to the Results view with its Markdown and a rerun entry that keeps the base branch.

Everything runs on your machine; nothing is sent to an environment.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
The F&O Code Reviewer agent does the same kind of review in chat: it lists the changes with xpp_diff_changes (base branch main unless you name another), reads each changed element, runs xpp_check_best_practice and xpp_analyze_performance, xpp_find_deprecations when the model calls obsolete APIs, and xpp_analyze_security (op=gaps) for new menu items, forms and services. It then checks what the tools miss (for example missing ttsbegin/ttscommit, hard-coded text, team rules). See Agents for Developers.

Example prompt: "Review my branch against main and list the findings by severity."

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only your own models, and only elements under Git (see Show Changed Elements).
  • The Chain of Command check is a text check: it covers extensions of classes, tables and forms (classStr, tableStr, formStr), not form data source or control extensions. A method marked [Replaceable] that intentionally skips next is still reported; judge it yourself.
  • Performance findings are heuristics. Only Warning-level findings are shown.
  • The Problems-based findings depend on what is in the Problems view: compiler errors appear only after a build.
  • Work items are only read with a base branch, and only from commit messages.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No changed elements in your models since main (models must be in a Git repository)." Nothing changed, the model folder is not in Git, or the base branch name cannot be resolved. Check git status in the model folder; try origin/main as the base branch. Best practice shows "Not run." xppbp failed or the run was cancelled. Run Run Best Practice Checks on Project and read the F&O Studio output. See Best Practice Checks. Work items: "none named in the commit messages". No #123 or AB#123 in the commit messages of the branch. Use Link Work Item… before committing. A wrapper is reported though it calls next. The call is written differently, for example with a line break between next and the method name. Write next methodName( on one line. Compiler errors are missing. The Problems view only has compiler errors after a build. Build first (Build Project and Model), then review.

docs.title: Run Snippet
docs.text: Run Snippet in Environment runs a piece of X++ code (a main method) in your environment without creating a runnable class by hand. F&O Studio copies the code into a scratch class in your model, builds the project, offers to deploy when the environment needs it, and opens the class in the web client through SysClassRunner. It replaces the "Job" of older AX versions and the usual Visual Studio routine of creating a runnable class, setting it as startup object and pressing F5.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Try an API call or a query and look at the result in the infolog.
  • Fix or inspect data with a one-off script in a development environment.
  • Check how a standard method behaves with certain parameters before you build on it.

Do not use it in production. The scratch class becomes part of your model until you delete it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An open D365FO project, or at least one model of your own: the scratch class is created in the project's model (or a model you pick).
  • A working build: the snippet is compiled with the project (Build Project and Model).
  • The web client URL of the environment. F&O Studio takes it from the active environment's configuration; when that has none, it uses the setting xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl, and asks for it once if that is empty.
  • On a UDE (online environment), the code only runs after a deploy, see Deploy to Environment. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment the build on the machine is enough.

docs.title: 1. Write the snippet
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Run Snippet in Environment from the Command Palette when no X++ snippet is open. F&O Studio opens a new untitled X++ document from a template, named after your project's model (MyScratch without a project):
internal final class ContosoExtensionsScratch
{
    public static void main(Args _args)
    {
        info("Hello");
    }
}

A message tells you to write the code in main and run the command again. 2. Write your code in main. You can add class variables and other methods; they are kept.

internal final class ContosoExtensionsScratch
{
    public static void main(Args _args)
    {
        CustGroup custGroup;

        while select custGroup
        {
            info(strFmt("%1: %2", custGroup.CustGroup, custGroup.Name));
        }
    }
}

You can also use an .xpp file on disk instead of an untitled document.

docs.title: 2. Run it
docs.text:
1. With the snippet as the active editor, run F&O Studio: Run Snippet in Environment again, or click the play button in the editor title bar (shown for untitled X++ documents).
  2. A notification shows Saving the snippet to <Model>ScratchRunner…. F&O Studio:
  3. creates the class <Model>ScratchRunner in your model, for example ContosoExtensionsScratchRunner, or updates it when it exists;
  4. adds it to the active project.
  5. F&O Studio builds the project with Build Project. If the build fails or is cancelled you see The build of <model> failed or was cancelled; <runner> was not run. See Problems and the X++ Build output. Fix the errors in your snippet and run again.
  6. On an online environment, a dialog asks <runner> is built. Deploy <model> to the online environment before running it?:
  7. Deploy and Run runs Deploy Models to Environment and then opens the class;
  8. Run Without Deploying opens the class right away (use it when the model is already deployed with the same runner code);
  9. closing the dialog stops here.
  10. The web client opens at https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com/?mi=SysClassRunner&cls=<runner>, which runs main. Infolog messages appear in the browser.
  11. A message reminds you: Delete it (project view > Delete) before packaging: the Pre-Deploy Checklist reports it.

docs.title: 3. Clean up
docs.text: The scratch runner is a real class in your model. Delete it from the D365FO Project view before you create a deployable package or commit. The Pre-Deploy Checklist has a Scratch code step that fails while <Model>ScratchRunner is in the model.

docs.title: What happens to your code
docs.text:
F&O Studio does not run your class as you wrote it. It builds the scratch runner from it:

Your snippet Scratch runner Class name (any) <Model>ScratchRunner, declared internal final class Class variables in the declaration Kept main and other methods Copied, indented to fit the class body Methods of an earlier run that are not in the snippet Removed from the runner

The snippet must contain static void main(Args <name>); without it the command opens the template instead (and a snippet whose methods lose main fails with The snippet needs a method public static void main(Args _args).).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl empty Web client URL used when the active environment's configuration has none. Filled in when you answer the prompt.

The model is the active project's model. Without a project you pick one of your models each time.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/runSnippet.ts checks the active editor: an X++ document, untitled or a file, that contains a main(Args ...) method. Otherwise it opens the template.
  2. It splits the snippet into declaration and methods with the code view's parser (src/xppSource.ts) and builds the runner's declaration and methods.
  3. Through the metadata server it looks up the runner (find_object). If it exists in a standard model it stops; if it exists in your model it reads it (read_object) and updates it (update_object, removing old methods); otherwise it creates it (create_object). Then add_to_project.
  4. It runs the xpp.buildProject command and continues only when the build reports success.
  5. It decides whether a deploy is needed: the workspace has a deployment solution (.erp\xpp.json) or an online environment URL is selected. Then it asks and, if you choose, runs xpp.pac.deploy.
  6. It opens the class with Open in Browser (src/d365Tools.ts), which builds the mi=SysClassRunner&cls=<class> URL.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The code runs in the environment through the web client, not in VS Code. Output is the browser's infolog.
  • On a UDE, each change needs a deploy of the model before it runs.
  • The runner is a real class: it is part of your model, builds and source control until you delete it.
  • One runner per model: a second snippet replaces the first one's code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A template opens instead of running The active editor is not an X++ document with static void main(Args ...). Make the snippet the active editor and check the main signature. <runner> exists in <model>, which is not one of your models. A class with the runner's name exists in a model that is not yours. Run the snippet from a project of another model, or remove the conflicting class. The build of <model> failed or was cancelled ... Compile errors in the snippet or elsewhere in the model. See Problems and the X++ Build output (Compiler Diagnostics). The browser runs old code The model was not deployed after the change on a UDE. Choose Deploy and Run. The browser asks for a URL No web client URL in the configuration or settings. Enter the URL; it is saved in xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl. Pre-Deploy Checklist fails on Scratch code The runner is still in the model. Delete <Model>ScratchRunner from the project.

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text: Run Tests runs X++ SysTest classes on your unified developer environment (UDE), the way Visual Studio's Test Explorer does for UDEs: F&O Studio sends a test suite to the environment through Dataverse, the environment's cloud runtime runs the tests against the code deployed there, and F&O Studio downloads and shows the result of every test method. The same runner serves the Run Tests command, VS Code's Test Explorer and the Copilot tool xpp_run_tests.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After you build and deploy a change, to check it with your unit tests.
  • When Copilot wrote or changed a SysTest class and should prove that it passes.
  • To run one test class from the Application Explorer, the project view or the element designer.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A unified developer environment. Tests run through Dataverse, which only UDEs have. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the command is hidden; if you run it anyway it fails with "Tests run through Dataverse, which only unified developer environments have. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, run them from Visual Studio on the VM."
  • A selected environment you are signed in to. See Connect to Environment and Sign In and Authentication.
  • An open D365FO project. The tests run from the package of the project's model, even when you start them from a class elsewhere.
  • Built and deployed code. The tests run against the code deployed to the environment, not your last build. Build (Build Project and Model) and deploy (Deploy to Environment) first.
  • Test classes F&O Studio can find:
  • the class declaration extends a class whose name contains Test (for example SysTestCase, or your own base class such as ContosoTestBase);
  • test methods are public (not private or protected) and either start with test or carry [SysTestMethod].

Example test class:

class ContosoOrderStatusTest extends SysTestCase
{
    public void testDefaultStatus()
    {
        ContosoOrderStatusTable record;
        record.initValue();
        this.assertEquals(ContosoOrderStatus::Open, record.Status);
    }

    [SysTestMethod]
    public void statusCanBeClosed()
    {
        this.assertTrue(ContosoOrderStatusHelper::canClose(ContosoOrderStatus::Open));
    }
}

To create a test class, see Generate SysTest Class.

docs.title: Run the project's tests
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Run Tests from the command palette, click Build and check > Run Tests in the Dynamics 365 view, or use Check > Run Tests in the title bar of the D365FO Project view.
  2. If the project's model was built after its last deploy from this machine, a warning asks first: " was built (...) after its last deploy (...). Running tests uses the deployed code."
  3. Deploy First starts Deploy Models to Environment and does not run the tests; run them again after the deploy.
  4. Continue runs the tests against the code on the environment.
  5. The X++ Tests output opens and a notification "Running X++ tests" shows progress. Click Cancel to stop waiting.
  6. When the run ends, a message shows the first line of the summary: an information message when every test passed, an error message otherwise.

docs.title: Run one class
docs.text: Right-click a class in the Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view, or right-click in the Element Designer of a class, and choose Run Tests. Only that class runs. If the class has no test methods, the message is the "No tests found" text below.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
The X++ Tests output shows the progress lines and a summary:

Discovered 2 test(s) in 1 class(es).
Suite: ...\xpp-vscode-tests\1764090000000\ContosoExtensions_0_done.tsx
Uploading test suite to Dataverse...
Starting execution on the cloud runtime...
  status: <state> / <status>
  status: <state> / <status>
Downloading results...
TESTS FAILED: 1 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (of 2 requested) on https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com.
  PASSED ContosoOrderStatusTest.testDefaultStatus (00:00:00.8120000)
  FAILED ContosoOrderStatusTest.statusCanBeClosed (00:00:01.0450000)
    <assertion message>
    Infolog: <Infolog text of the failed test>
  • The first line counts passed, failed and skipped tests (NotExecuted and Skipped count as skipped).
  • Each test has its outcome and duration; failures show the assertion message and the Infolog.
  • If no results come back, the summary says: "No results were returned. Check that the package is deployed and the test classes exist on the environment."

The status lines show the state and status of the environment's test suite record; their exact text comes from the environment.

docs.title: Run tests with Copilot
docs.text:
The language model tool xpp_run_tests (reference it in chat as #xppRunTests) runs the same tests. VS Code asks you to confirm first: "The tests run on the connected environment against the deployed code and may create test data there." Inputs:

Input Effect Default classes Test class names. Every test class of the active project methods Only these test methods of the given classes. All test methods timeoutMinutes How long to wait for results. 30

When the build is newer than the last deploy, the tool's result starts with a warning that the tests ran against the deployed code. The F&O Test Engineer agent writes SysTest classes and runs them this way; see Agents for Developers.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no test-specific settings. The run uses the selected environment and the open project.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The runner is in the VS Code-free core library, core/src/tests.ts; the command and the agent tool are registered in src/tests.ts.

  1. Discovery. Without classes in the request, the test classes are the classes of the open project. Each class is read through the metadata server (bridge action read_object). Classes whose declaration does not extend a *Test* class are skipped; public methods that start with test or carry [SysTestMethod] are tests.
  2. Test suite. F&O Studio writes a test suite file <model>_0_done.tsx in %TEMP%\xpp-vscode-tests\<timestamp>, in the XML format of Visual Studio's test adapter: one TestCaseInformation per test with the name Class.method, the fully qualified name Dynamics.AX.Application.Class.method, the executor executor://SysTestExecutor/v1 and the test source <runtime packages folder>\<model>\bin\Dynamics.AX.<model>.dll.
  3. Upload. It creates an msprov_unittestsuites record in the environment's Dataverse and uploads the suite into its msprov_unittestsuiteconfig file column.
  4. Execution. It calls the Dataverse action msprov_unittestexecutiononfinopsasync with the suite, which starts a system job.
  5. Polling. Every 5 seconds it reads the system job (asyncoperations) and the suite record's state and status, until the suite is completed or inactive, the job fails, or the timeout (30 minutes by default) passes.
  6. Results. It downloads msprov_unittestresult (a zip with .trx files, or one .trx), extracts it and reads every UnitTestResult: test name, outcome, duration, message and Infolog.

Sign-in uses your Microsoft account in VS Code (a Dataverse token for the selected environment). The built-versus-deployed warning comes from the deploy state that F&O Studio records on this machine (see Status Bar).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• UDEs only. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, run tests from Visual Studio on the VM.
  • Tests run the deployed code. A build alone does not change what is tested.
  • The test package is always the package of the open project's model.
  • Discovery is by name pattern: a test class whose base class name does not contain Test is not found.
  • Cancelling stops waiting; the test run may continue on the environment.
  • Tests may create data on the environment; write tests that create their own data.
  • There is no debug run profile; Run Tests only runs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Tests run through Dataverse, which only unified developer environments have." Cloud-hosted or VHD environment. Run tests from Visual Studio on the VM. "Open a D365FO project first: tests run from the package of the project's model." No project is open. Open the project that holds the tests. "No tests found. Test classes must extend SysTestCase (or a subclass) and test methods must be public and start with "test" or carry [SysTestMethod]." Discovery found no test methods. Check the class declaration and method names. "Class not found." A class passed to the tool does not exist. Check the class name. "No environment selected." No environment is selected in this window. Run Connect to Environment or Select Environment. "Timed out after 30 minutes waiting for test results" The run took longer than the timeout. Pass a larger timeoutMinutes to the agent tool, or run fewer tests. "Test execution job failed (...)" or "Test suite ended with status ..." The environment could not run the suite. Check that the package is deployed; deploy and run again. Old behaviour is tested The build is newer than the deploy. Choose Deploy First, then run the tests again.

docs.title: SQL Query Panel
docs.text: The SQL query panel runs T-SQL against the active environment's business database in an editor tab. It is read-only by default: one SELECT (or WITH … SELECT), always rolled back. It shows several result sets, exports CSV, and explains the estimated plan of a query without running it. When you really need to change data on a development database, Allow changes commits a batch after a confirmation each run. Visual Studio has no built-in equivalent; there you would switch to SQL Server Management Studio.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Joins and aggregates that a single-table Browse Table Data tab cannot show.
  • Checking what a while select in your code really reads, then looking at its plan with Explain Plan.
  • Running a Database Performance Insights query and adjusting it.
  • Fixing test data on a development database (with Allow changes, knowing it skips X++ logic).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Database access for the active environment. See Database Access. On a unified developer environment the panel asks for JIT credentials the first time you run something.
  • SQL names are the database names: tables and fields in upper case as SQL Server stores them (for example CUSTTABLE.ACCOUNTNUM), company in DATAAREAID in lower case ('usmf').
  • To change data you need a local database (cloud-hosted or VHD) or Writer credentials on a UDE.

docs.title: Open the panel
docs.text:
• Command Palette: F&O Studio: New SQL Query opens an empty tab named SQL query.
  • Dynamics 365 view: Data > New SQL Query.
  • Database menu (status bar or Data > Database…): New SQL Query.
  • From a Browse tab: Open as SQL opens the current view as a query.
  • From Database Performance Insights: the chosen query opens and runs.

Query tabs come back after a window reload with their SQL, but they do not run again by themselves.

docs.title: Write and run a query
docs.text:
1. Type the query in the editor. The placeholder shows the form:
SELECT TOP 100 ACCOUNTNUM, PARTY FROM CUSTTABLE WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
  1. Choose the row limit: 100, 200 (default), 500, 1000 or 5000 rows per result set.
  2. Click Run (Ctrl+Enter), or press Ctrl+Enter in the editor.
  3. While it runs, the status line shows Running… and Cancel is enabled. Cancel stops the SQL command on the server. Closing the tab cancels too.
  4. The results appear below the editor, one grid per result set, each with its row count and an Export CSV button. The status line shows the elapsed time, for example 184 ms, or no rows returned.
  5. Messages from SQL Server (for example the warning "Null value is eliminated by an aggregate or other SET operation", or PRINT output in a batch with changes allowed) show under the results, at most 50.
  6. Errors show in a red box above the results.

Example: customers per customer group in one company.

SELECT CUSTGROUP, COUNT(*) AS Customers
FROM CUSTTABLE
WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
GROUP BY CUSTGROUP
ORDER BY Customers DESC

Example with a common table expression (allowed, it is one statement that starts with WITH):

WITH Lines AS (
  SELECT SALESID, COUNT(*) AS LineCount
  FROM SALESLINE
  WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
  GROUP BY SALESID
)
SELECT TOP 20 s.SALESID, s.CUSTACCOUNT, l.LineCount
FROM SALESTABLE s
JOIN Lines l ON l.SALESID = s.SALESID
WHERE s.DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
ORDER BY l.LineCount DESC

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text: Control What it does Run (Ctrl+Enter) Runs the editor's text Cancel Stops the running query Rows The row limit per result set Explain Plan Shows the estimated plan of the SELECT without running it. See Explain Plan. Allow changes Commits the batch (asks every time). Disabled unless the database is local or the credentials are Writer; its tooltip says why. Target (right) Database, server and credential role, for example AxDB on localhost

docs.title: Read-only rules
docs.text:
Without Allow changes, the server refuses a batch before it runs when:

Message Why "The query is empty." Nothing to run "Run one statement at a time." More than one statement (a ; other than a trailing one) "Only SELECT queries run in read-only mode." The batch starts with something other than SELECT or WITH "'INTO' is not allowed in read-only mode." (or another keyword) A write or session keyword appears outside strings, quoted names and comments "A string is not closed." / "A quoted name is not closed." / "A comment is not closed." The check could not parse the batch

The refused keywords include INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, INTO, EXEC, DECLARE, SET, BEGIN, USE, WAITFOR and others; the full list is on Database Access. So SELECT … INTO #temp, variables and stored procedure calls are not possible in read-only mode.

Even when a batch passes the check, it runs in a transaction that is rolled back. Words inside string literals, [quoted names] and comments do not count, so WHERE NAME = 'Update' is fine.

docs.title: Allow changes
docs.text:
1. Check Allow changes.
  2. Click Run. A modal asks: Run this batch with changes on <database>? and explains that changes made in SQL skip X++ business logic: insert/update/delete methods, validation, the database log, events, number sequences and the server's caches. The changes are committed and cannot be undone here.
  3. Choose Run and Commit to run, or close the dialog to cancel.
  4. The status line shows <n> row(s) changed and committed.

With Allow changes the read-only check is skipped: the batch may hold several statements. It still runs in one transaction, committed only when the whole batch succeeds; on an error it is rolled back.

Example of a small test-data fix on a development database:

UPDATE CUSTGROUP SET NAME = 'Wholesale customers'
WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf' AND CUSTGROUP = '10'

Do not use this for anything that X++ would normally do: posting, number sequences, or tables with database log or business events.

docs.title: Export CSV
docs.text: Export CSV on a result set asks where to save and proposes query.csv. The file holds the loaded rows of that result set, RFC 4180 quoted, with the column names as the header row.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The panel has no settings. The time limit per query is 60 seconds. See Database Access for the access settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The panel is a webview (src/database/dataPanel.ts, media/dataPanel.js). Every value is written as text, never as HTML.
  2. Run sends a query request with the SQL, the row limit and the allowWrite flag through DataClient (core/src/data/client.ts) to the extension's own server process (xpp/data), with the connection attached.
  3. The server (DataQueryService.cs) checks read-only batches with ReadOnlySql.cs, opens a connection, starts a READ COMMITTED transaction and runs the batch.
  4. It reads up to 5 result sets, each up to the row limit (at most 10,000), then rolls the transaction back (read only) or commits it (changes allowed).
  5. Values come back exact: 64-bit integers (RecId) and decimals as text, dates as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fff, binary as hex (first 64 bytes), text cut at 4,000 characters.
  6. Each run has an ID. Cancel sends cancel with that ID and the server calls SqlCommand.Cancel.

The same read-only path serves the agent tool xpp_query_data, which never sets allowWrite. See Database Access.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One statement per read-only run; no variables, temporary tables or procedure calls.
  • At most 5 result sets and the chosen row limit per set; + and "(limit reached)" mark a cut result.
  • No syntax highlighting or completion in the editor.
  • Changes skip X++ business logic. On a UDE they need Writer credentials.
  • SQL names can differ from AOT names: the elements of an array field after the first have their own columns, such as FIELD2_.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Allow changes is disabled Reader credentials on a UDE Request new credentials with the Writer role (Request Database Credentials) "Only SELECT queries run in read-only mode." The batch does not start with SELECT or WITH Rewrite as a SELECT, or use Allow changes if you meant to change data "Run one statement at a time." Two statements in one batch Run them one by one "Invalid object name 'CUSTTABLE'." (SQL error) The table is not in this database, or the name is wrong Check the SQL name; synchronize the table Cancelled. You pressed Cancel or ran another query Run again A query stops after about a minute The 60-second time limit Add filters or TOP; check the plan with Explain Plan "No database access. Request credentials with F&O Studio: Request Database Credentials, then run again." You declined the credentials dialog Run Request Database Credentials

docs.text:

  • Browse Table Data
  • Explain Plan
  • Database Performance Insights
  • Open in SSMS
  • Agent Tools: Build and Data

docs.title: Scan Overlay and Measure
docs.text: The scan overlay lays a scanned or photographed form under the Report Designer's page, at the size of the paper it shows, so you can place each field on the preprinted stationery it will print on. The measure tool reads distances on the page in millimetres and inches. The scan is a design aid only: it is never saved in the report. Visual Studio's report designer has neither.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You design a report for preprinted stationery: cheques, purchase order or invoice forms, labels, government forms.
  • You have a sample of the form (a scan, a PDF converted to an image, or a photo) and need the fields where the boxes are.
  • You want to compare the rendered report with the scan in the Report-Preview.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A precision design open in the Report-Designer.
  • An image of the whole sheet: PNG, JPG/JPEG, BMP, GIF or TIF/TIFF. Scan at 100 % (no "fit to page") and keep the sheet straight; the overlay is not deskewed.
  • Set the design's paper size first (Properties with nothing selected → Paper (mm)), because a new scan is laid at the page size.

docs.title: Load a scan
docs.text:
1. Click the camera button Scan overlay in the toolbar.
  2. Pick the image file.
  3. The scan appears under the page at the paper's width and height, at 45 % opacity, and the page properties show the Scan overlay (not saved in the report) group.

docs.title: Adjust it
docs.text:
With nothing selected, the Properties panel shows, below the page settings:

Setting Effect Paper Size the scan to Letter, Legal, A4, A5 or Executive, or Custom Width (mm), Height (mm) The size the whole image covers on the page Offset x (mm), Offset y (mm) Moves the scan from the sheet's top-left corner Opacity 0.1 to 1 Remove scan Removes the scan from the designer

To calibrate, measure a known distance on the scan with the measure tool (for example the width of a box printed as 50 mm) and change Width (mm) and Height (mm) until it reads right; then align a printed corner or rule with the offsets.

docs.title: Show or hide it
docs.text: Click the camera button again to hide the scan; once more to show it. The image stays loaded while the design is open in the panel (switching to another design clears it).

docs.title: Place fields on it
docs.text:
1. Drag fields from Report data onto the boxes of the scan.
  2. Read the exact position in the status bar ("Name: x …, y …, width × height mm", from the sheet's top-left corner) or in Position (mm from the container).
  3. Nudge with Ctrl+arrow keys (0.1 mm) and resize with Shift+arrow keys.
  4. For fixed positions, keep Can grow off and padding at 0 (new textboxes are created that way); a growing textbox pushes the fields below it down (the designer warns about it).

docs.title: Compare in the preview
docs.text:
1. Click Preview.
  2. Turn on Show scan under the page in the preview settings.
  3. Render. The rendered page is blended over the scan, so the report's text and the printed form show together.
  4. Type the values printed on the sample into Data (JSON rows per dataset) so the texts line up with the sample.

docs.title: Measure
docs.text:
1. Click Measure (ruler button), or hold Alt and drag on the page at any time.
  2. Drag from one point to another. A line follows the pointer with the distance, for example "38.1 mm (Δx 38.1, Δy 0) · 1.5 in".
  3. When you release, the status bar keeps "Measured: …"; the line disappears after a few seconds.

Escape cancels the measure tool. The status bar always shows the pointer position in mm and inches.

docs.title: What is remembered
docs.text:
• The scan image stays in the panel's memory only. It is not saved in the report, the project or the workspace.
  • Its placement (size, offset, opacity and file name) is remembered per report design. When you reopen the design, the status bar says "A scan overlay was used last time (name); load it again with the camera button." Load the image again and it takes the remembered placement. Remove scan forgets the placement.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: No settings. The placement is stored in the panel's state.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The camera button asks the extension for a file (src/reports/reportDesigner.ts), which reads it and passes it to the webview as base64 data. The webview draws it as an image under the sheet (media/reportDesigner.js); nothing is sent to the server and nothing is uploaded.
  • Positions are computed from the RDL in millimetres (the page is drawn at 96 px per inch times the zoom), so readings don't depend on the zoom.
  • In the preview, the scan is placed with the same size and offset under each rendered page and the page image is blended with a multiply mode.

docs.title: With Copilot
docs.text:
Copilot can do this end to end with the F&O Report Builder agent and its tools (see Agent-Tools-Reports and Copilot-Agents):

  • xpp_measure_image calibrates a scan (paper size, scan dpi or two reference points), straightens it, finds ruled lines and boxes, and reads the text with Windows' built-in OCR on this machine, with each position in mm.
  • xpp_compare_layout renders the design, lays it on the calibrated scan and returns an overlay plus each textbox's offset in mm.

See Scenario-Report-from-a-Scanned-Document.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The overlay is not deskewed or scaled automatically; you size and offset it by hand. (xpp_measure_image does deskew and calibrate, for the agent.)
  • The image must be reloaded after the panel is closed.
  • PDF files can't be loaded directly; convert the page to an image first.
  • The measure tool shows a straight-line distance; it doesn't snap to items.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The scan doesn't match the page The image has margins or was scaled when scanned. Change Width (mm) and Height (mm) until a known distance measures right, then set the offsets. The scan settings aren't in the Properties panel An item is selected. Click an empty area of the page (or press Escape). The scan is gone after reopening Only the placement is remembered. Click the camera button and pick the same file. Fields are right in the designer but move in the preview Textboxes grow, or padding moves the text. Turn Can grow off and set padding to 0; check the warnings. Text in the preview looks wider than on the form A font isn't installed here and is substituted. See the font warning; check on the environment.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Report-Designer
  • Report-Preview
  • Agent-Tools-Reports
  • Scenario-Report-from-a-Scanned-Document
  • Copilot-Agents

docs.title: Scenario: Batch Job End to End
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers who need a new batch job: from a standard precedent, through the SysOperation classes, security and tests, to a job scheduled in the web client and monitored afterwards.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Credit control wants a nightly job that reviews customers: for each customer with an overdue balance above a limit, it writes a row to a custom table ContosoCreditReview so a collector can follow up the next morning. Users must be able to run it on demand with a date, or schedule it as a recurring batch job.

You build it in the ContosoExtensions model with the standard SysOperation pattern:

Element Purpose ContosoCreditReviewContract Parameters (the date, plus the limit you add). [DataContractAttribute]. ContosoCreditReviewService The work, in process(ContosoCreditReviewContract _contract). Extends SysOperationServiceBase. ContosoCreditReviewController Dialog and batch scheduling. Extends SysOperationServiceController. ContosoCreditReview Action menu item that starts the controller. ContosoCreditReviewGenerate Privilege that grants the menu item (Invoke).

The ContosoCreditReview table already exists in the model (create it with New Element… > Table if not).

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Need Why A connected environment (Connect-to-Environment) Metadata and build. The ContosoExtensions project open The wizard creates the elements in the project's model. A label file with an en-US language in the model The wizard puts the caption in a label; without one it uses plain text, which best practice reports. A UDE (or cloud-hosted/VHD) with customer data To run and schedule the job. Database access (optional) To check the result rows and the batch history.

docs.title: Phase 1: Find a precedent
docs.text:
1. Run Find Similar Standard Implementations (Dynamics 365 view > Find) and describe the task, for example "batch job with contract". It returns ranked standard elements with the reason they match. See Find-Similar-Implementations.
  2. Open one or two of them and read how they split the work, use transactions and report progress.
  3. Decide the unit of work. Here: one customer per transaction, so a restart can continue and one bad customer does not roll back the rest.

docs.title: Phase 2: Generate the classes
docs.text:
1. Run New Batch Job (SysOperation)… (Dynamics 365 view > Create > New Batch Job…, or New Element… > Wizards > Batch job (SysOperation)).
  2. Answer the two prompts:
  3. name: ContosoCreditReview (the classes get Contract, Service and Controller appended);
  4. caption: Customer credit review (what users see on the menu and in the batch job list).
  5. The wizard creates the five elements in one step (all or nothing) and they compile without warnings:
  6. the contract with a parmTransDate data member;
  7. the service with an empty process method;
  8. the controller with main (it starts process of the service) and defaultCaption;
  9. the action menu item ContosoCreditReview pointing at the controller;
  10. the privilege ContosoCreditReviewGenerate granting the menu item with Invoke.
  11. The message says "Add the privilege ContosoCreditReviewGenerate to a duty, then write the job in ContosoCreditReviewService.process." Click Open Service.

See Wizard-Batch-Job.

docs.title: Phase 3: Write the job
docs.text:
1. Add the limit to the contract. In the code view of ContosoCreditReviewContract, type the parm method snippet (see Snippets) or copy the pattern of parmTransDate:
[DataMemberAttribute]
public AmountMST parmMinOverdue(AmountMST _minOverdue = minOverdue)
{
    minOverdue = _minOverdue;
    return minOverdue;
}

and add AmountMST minOverdue; to the class declaration. 2. Write process in the service. Keep reads set-based and write one transaction per unit of work:

public void process(ContosoCreditReviewContract _contract)
{
    CustTable custTable;

    while select AccountNum from custTable
    {
        AmountMST overdue = ContosoCreditReviewService::overdueAmount(custTable.AccountNum, _contract.parmTransDate());

        if (overdue >= _contract.parmMinOverdue())
        {
            ttsbegin;
            ContosoCreditReview::create(custTable.AccountNum, overdue, _contract.parmTransDate());
            ttscommit;
        }
    }
}
  1. Use labels for any message (the extract to label quick fix, Ctrl+.), and hover to check signatures. See Quick-Fixes and Hover.
  2. Run Analyze Performance on the service. It flags queries and row-by-row writes inside loops, while select of every field, select firstonly inside while select, and unbalanced ttsbegin/ttscommit. Above, the while select reads only AccountNum. If overdueAmount runs a query per customer, consider one set-based query instead. See Analyze-Performance.
  3. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B). Fix everything in Problems.

docs.title: Phase 4: Security and menu
docs.text:
1. Put the privilege in a duty. Run New Element… > Security duty extension, pick the duty credit control uses, and add ContosoCreditReviewGenerate to it in the designer. Or create your own duty with New Element… > Security duty.
  2. Check placement and cost: Analyze License on ContosoCreditReviewGenerate, and Who Can Access on the menu item ContosoCreditReview after you add it. See Analyze-License and Who-Can-Access.
  3. Run Find Security Gaps: an uncovered menu item shows here. See Find-Security-Gaps.
  4. To show the job on a module menu, add the menu item to a menu extension. New Element… has no menu extension type; the agent tools do (ask F&O Developer, below), or users can run it from a workspace tile or the URL.

docs.title: Phase 5: Try it
docs.text:
1. Quick check on a UDE: run Deploy Models to Environment (database sync Module if ContosoCreditReview is new). See Deploy-to-Environment.
  2. Right-click the menu item ContosoCreditReview and choose Open in Browser. The web client opens ?mi=action:ContosoCreditReview, which runs the controller and shows the job's SysOperation dialog.
  3. Run it once interactively with a small limit. Then check the rows: right-click ContosoCreditReview (table) > Browse Table Data. See Browse-Table-Data.
  4. For a quick experiment on one customer without the menu item, use Run Snippet in Environment with a main method that builds a contract and calls the service. Delete the scratch class afterwards. See Run-Snippet.

docs.title: Phase 6: Test
docs.text:
1. Right-click ContosoCreditReviewService > Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL). It creates ContosoCreditReviewServiceTest with an arrange/act/assert test per public method, customer data from the Acceptance Test Library, and offers Add References for the ATL packages. See Generate-SysTest-Class.
  2. Write two tests: a customer above the limit gets a row; a customer below does not.
  3. Build, deploy, and run the tests from Test Explorer or Run Tests. F&O Studio warns when the build is newer than the last deploy and offers Deploy First. See Run-Tests.

docs.title: Phase 7: Schedule and monitor
docs.text:
1. In the web client, open the dialog again, turn on batch processing, set the recurrence (for example daily at 02:00) and the batch group. This is standard D365FO, not F&O Studio.
  2. After a few runs, run Database Performance Insights > Slowest batch jobs (last 7 days): runs, average and longest duration per job and company. See Database-Performance-Insights.
  3. If a run is slow, capture a trace while it runs and use Analyze Trace…: the trace lists the batch sessions, and you can filter on them. See Analyze-Trace and Scenario-Performance-Tuning-a-Slow-Process.
  4. If a run fails, take the message from the batch job log to Find Message Source. See Scenario-From-Error-Message-to-Fix.

Debugging the job. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, set "processName": "Batch.exe" in the xpp launch configuration to attach to the batch service. See Debugging-on-Cloud-Hosted. Run it interactively (without batch processing) to debug it in the web client's process instead.

docs.title: Phase 8: Review and ship
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes and the Pre-Deploy Checklist. The checklist fails while Run Snippet's scratch class is in the model. See Review-My-Changes and Pre-Deploy-Checklist.
  2. Commit, link the work item, push.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
F&O Developer builds the job:

Create a SysOperation batch job ContosoCreditReview in ContosoExtensions: contract with a date and a minimum overdue amount, a service that writes a ContosoCreditReview row per customer above the limit (one transaction per customer, set-based reads), a controller, an action menu item in a menu extension of the Accounts receivable menu, and a privilege added to a duty extension. Follow a standard batch job precedent. Build until clean and run the best practice checks.

What it does: xpp_find_examples for a precedent, xpp_get_guide for the SysOperation pattern, xpp_create_object for the classes, menu item, privilege and extensions, xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice, and xppOpenElement to show you the service. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint first; watch Copilot Activity.

F&O Performance (read-only) checks it before volume:

Review ContosoCreditReviewService for performance with 200,000 customers: loops, queries per row, transactions, and whether it should split the work into batch tasks.

It runs xpp_analyze_performance and reads the tables' indexes; use Implement the fixes to hand back to F&O Developer.

F&O Test Engineer writes and runs the tests:

Write ATL-based SysTests for ContosoCreditReviewService: above the limit gets a row, below doesn't, and a rerun for the same date doesn't duplicate rows. Build and run them.

F&O Support (read-only) investigates a failed run:

Last night's Customer credit review batch job ended with an error in its log: . Find where it comes from and why.

Checkpoints: - The plan names a standard precedent before anything is created. - The service uses one transaction per unit of work; performance analysis is clean. - The privilege is in a duty; no security gaps. - Tests pass on the deployed code.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Standard precedent read.
  • [ ] Wizard created contract, service, controller, menu item and privilege.
  • [ ] Contract parameters added; process written with one transaction per unit.
  • [ ] Analyze Performance clean; build clean.
  • [ ] Privilege in a duty; menu item reachable; Find Security Gaps clean.
  • [ ] Deployed; run interactively; result rows checked.
  • [ ] Tests written and passing.
  • [ ] Scheduled in the web client; batch history checked after some runs.
  • [ ] Scratch class deleted; Review My Changes and Pre-Deploy Checklist pass.

docs.title: Scenario: Build a Feature End to End
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers (and the consultants who work with them) who take one requirement from design to a deployed, tested and reviewed change. It chains the wizards, extensions, Chain of Command, security, tests, review and deploy, and shows where the F&O agents fit.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Sales wants a delivery priority on sales orders: a small setup list (Standard, Express, Same day), a field on the sales order header that defaults from the customer, and a way to turn the behaviour on or off per environment.

You build it in the ContosoExtensions model:

Element Created with Purpose ContosoDeliveryPriorityId (EDT), ContosoDeliveryPriority (table, form, menu item), ContosoDeliveryPriorityView / ContosoDeliveryPriorityMaintain (privileges) New Table with Form… The setup list. CustTable.ContosoExtensions, SalesTable.ContosoExtensions Create Extension The field on the customer and on the order header. SalesTable.ContosoExtensions (form extension) Open Form Layout… The field on the Sales order form. SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension Create Code Extension Defaults the priority from the customer. ContosoDeliveryPriorityFeature New Feature (Feature Management)… Turns the defaulting on or off. SalesOrderMaintain.ContosoExtensions New Element… > Security duty extension Grants the setup form to the sales order duty. ContosoDeliveryPriorityTest Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL) Regression test.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Need Why A connected UDE (Connect-to-Environment) Metadata, deploy, tests. Cloud-hosted and VHD work too, but Run Tests and Deploy are UDE-only. The ContosoExtensions project open Wizards and new elements go to the project's model. A label file in the model (with an en-US language) Wizards put their captions in it; without one they use plain text, which best practice reports. ContosoExtensions in Git, xpp.git.baseBranch set (for example main) Review My Changes and Show Changed Elements. Database access (optional) To check data while testing.

docs.title: Phase 1: Design
docs.text:
1. Find out what standard offers. Use Find Similar Standard Implementations with a description ("setup table with SimpleList form", "default a sales order field from the customer") to find precedents. See Find-Similar-Implementations.
  2. Look at the standard objects you will touch: SalesTable (table and form), CustTable, and the method SalesTable.initFromCustTable. Use Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O), View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) and Show Extensions and Handlers… to see what other models already add.
  3. Write down the elements, names with your prefix, labels and security. The table in The situation is the result.
  4. The F&O Solution Designer agent can produce this design for you (see below).

docs.title: Phase 2: Create the setup list
docs.text:
1. Run New Table with Form… (Dynamics 365 view > Create, or New Element… > Wizards > Table with form).
  2. Answer the prompts:
  3. name: ContosoDeliveryPriority;
  4. label: Delivery priorities;
  5. key field label: Delivery priority.
  6. The wizard creates, all or nothing: the EDT ContosoDeliveryPriorityId (extends SysGroup), the table with the key and Description, an alternate key, field groups and find()/exist(), a SimpleList form with a quick filter and grid, the display menu item, and the privileges ContosoDeliveryPriorityView and ContosoDeliveryPriorityMaintain. The result compiles without warnings.
  7. Click Open Table or Open Form in the message. Add more fields if you need them, and add them to the Overview field group.

See Wizard-Table-with-Form.

docs.title: Phase 3: Extend the standard tables and form
docs.text:
1. Right-click CustTable in the Application Explorer > Create Extension > accept CustTable.ContosoExtensions. In the designer, add a string field ContosoDeliveryPriorityId with EDT ContosoDeliveryPriorityId (use Alt+Down for the picker). Do the same on SalesTable (SalesTable.ContosoExtensions).
  2. Add a relation from each new field to ContosoDeliveryPriority under Relations in the extension, so lookups and validation work.
  3. Right-click the SalesTable form > Open Form Layout…. Select the control the field should follow on the header, click Add fields after…, pick the SalesTable data source and the new field. The control is saved to SalesTable.ContosoExtensions (form extension). Do the same on the CustTable form if users set the default there.

See Create-Extension, Form-Layout-and-Form-Extensions and Scenario-Extend-a-Standard-Form-and-Table for the details.

docs.title: Phase 4: Feature flag and logic
docs.text:
1. Run New Feature (Feature Management)…. Answer: class name ContosoDeliveryPriorityFeature (the prompt asks for a name ending with Feature), the name administrators see, a summary, the module, and Off by default or On by default. The message offers Copy Check, which copies the isEnabled() check. See Wizard-Feature-Management.
  2. Right-click SalesTable (table) > Create Code Extension > accept SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension. The class opens with [ExtensionOf(tableStr(SalesTable))].
  3. Write the wrapper. Completion after . and :: includes methods added by Chain of Command; Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) lists other wrappers and handlers of the same method.
[ExtensionOf(tableStr(SalesTable))]
final class SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    void initFromCustTable()
    {
        next initFromCustTable();

        if (ContosoDeliveryPriorityFeature::isEnabled())
        {
            this.ContosoDeliveryPriorityId = CustTable::find(this.CustAccount).ContosoDeliveryPriorityId;
        }
    }
}
  1. Check the signature against the standard method: hover shows it, and the code lens above the method shows its references and Chain of Command classes. See Code-Lens and Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command.

docs.title: Phase 5: Security
docs.text:
1. Decide where the privileges go. Analyze License on ContosoDeliveryPriorityMaintain shows the license it needs; Who Can Access on the SalesTable menu item shows the duties and roles that already reach sales orders. See Analyze-License and Who-Can-Access.
  2. Run New Element… > Security duty extension, pick SalesOrderMaintain, accept SalesOrderMaintain.ContosoExtensions, and add ContosoDeliveryPriorityView to its privileges in the designer. Add ContosoDeliveryPriorityMaintain to the setup duty your team uses.
  3. Run Find Security Gaps (Security view title, or Dynamics 365 view > Security). It lists menu items, forms and services of your model that no privilege covers. See Find-Security-Gaps.
  4. To add a menu item to an existing or new privilege later, right-click the menu item > Add to Privilege…. See Add-to-Privilege.

docs.title: Phase 6: Build and check
docs.text:
1. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B) until Problems shows no errors or warnings in your elements.
  2. Run Run Best Practice Checks on Project (xppbp). See Best-Practice-Checks.
  3. Run Analyze Performance on SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension. See Analyze-Performance.

docs.title: Phase 7: Deploy and test
docs.text:
1. Run Deploy Models to Environment, pick ContosoExtensions and database sync Module (new tables and fields). Progress shows in X++ Deploy. See Deploy-to-Environment.
  2. In the web client: Feature management > Check for updates lists the new feature; turn it on. Open the setup form with Open in Browser on the ContosoDeliveryPriority menu item and add Standard, Express and Same day.
  3. Right-click SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_Extension > Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL). The prompt proposes SalesTable_ContosoExtensions_ExtensionTest; type ContosoDeliveryPriorityTest instead. Accept Add References if the model lacks the Acceptance Test Library packages. Write two tests: the priority defaults from the customer with the feature on, and stays empty with it off.
  4. Build, deploy again, and run the tests from Test Explorer or Run Tests. Results go to X++ Tests. See Run-Tests and Test-Explorer.

docs.title: Phase 8: Review and release
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes: the changed elements against xpp.git.baseBranch, each with its best practice and performance findings, and a pull request summary to copy. See Review-My-Changes.
  2. Run Pre-Deploy Checklist: build, best practice, performance, security gaps, the scratch class check and a reminder about tests, in one report in the Results view. When it passes it offers Create Deployment Package and Deploy. See Pre-Deploy-Checklist.
  3. Link the work item with Link Work Item…, commit and push. See Work-Items-and-Pipelines.
  4. For a release outside your UDE, Create Deployment Package… runs the same script Visual Studio runs. Moving the package to sandbox or production happens outside F&O Studio, by your team's process. See Create-Deployment-Package.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Use one agent per stage, and hand off between them. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint before any agent that changes elements, and watch Copilot Activity.

  1. F&O Fit-Gap Analyst (consultants) classifies the requirement:

Sales wants a delivery priority per sales order, defaulted from the customer. Is this standard, configuration, extension or ISV? Show the evidence.

  1. F&O Solution Designer (read-only) writes the design:

Design the delivery priority feature for ContosoExtensions: setup table and form, field on CustTable and SalesTable, default from the customer behind a Feature management flag, security and test scenarios.

  1. F&O Developer builds it (handoff Build it from the Solution Designer, or ask directly):

Implement the design above. Use the table-with-form pattern for the setup list, extensions for CustTable, SalesTable and the SalesTable form, a Chain of Command wrapper of SalesTable.initFromCustTable guarded by the feature class, and add the View privilege to a SalesOrderMaintain duty extension. Build until clean and run the best practice checks.

It reads the standard elements and a precedent (xpp_find_examples, xpp_read_object, xpp_get_form_layout), confirms the plan when it creates several elements, creates them with xpp_create_object / xpp_update_object / xpp_create_label, adds them to the project, builds with xpp_build and checks with xpp_check_best_practice.

  1. F&O Security & License (read-only) checks the security design: xpp_analyze_security with op=placement, op=license and op=gaps.

Where should ContosoDeliveryPriorityView and ContosoDeliveryPriorityMaintain go, what license do they need, and are there gaps in ContosoExtensions?

  1. F&O Test Engineer writes and runs the tests (handoff Write tests from F&O Developer). It runs them with xppRunTests, which asks first and warns when the deployed code is older than the build.

  2. F&O Code Reviewer (read-only) reviews the branch with xpp_diff_changes, xpp_check_best_practice, xpp_analyze_performance and xpp_analyze_security, and checks by hand that the wrapper calls next.

  3. F&O Release Manager runs the checks and creates the package with xpp_package (it asks first). It deploys only to development, sandbox or build environments and only with your permission; there is no deploy tool, so you run Deploy Models to Environment yourself.

  4. F&O Test Scenarios and F&O Release Notes write the functional test steps and the user-facing notes.

Checkpoints: - The design names a standard precedent per element before anything is created. - Copilot Activity shows only ContosoExtensions elements changed. - BUILD SUCCEEDED, best practice clean, no security gaps. - Tests pass on the deployed code. - End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes) once reviewed, or Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint….

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Design written: elements, names, labels, security, tests.
  • [ ] Setup table, form, menu item and privileges created by the wizard.
  • [ ] Table and form extensions created; relations added.
  • [ ] Feature class created; logic guarded by isEnabled().
  • [ ] Chain of Command wrapper calls next.
  • [ ] Privileges in duties; Find Security Gaps clean.
  • [ ] Build, best practice and performance clean.
  • [ ] Deployed with Module sync; feature turned on; setup data entered.
  • [ ] Tests written and passing.
  • [ ] Review My Changes and Pre-Deploy Checklist pass; work item linked.

docs.title: Scenario: Debug Standard Code on a UDE
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers who need to step through Microsoft's own X++ code on a unified developer environment (UDE) to understand a behaviour, for example where a default comes from, before deciding where to extend it. You set breakpoints in the standard element's code view, attach the debugger from VS Code, trigger the code in the web client and inspect variables, without Visual Studio.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
A purchasing user asks why a new purchase order gets a delivery address that is not the vendor's. Reading the code helps, but PurchTable defaults many fields from several places. You want to see it run:

  • the init method of the PurchTable form, which runs when the form opens;
  • the initFromVendTable method of the PurchTable table, which copies values from the vendor when you pick one.

You will set breakpoints in both, create a purchase order in the UDE's web client, and step through.

If you work on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment instead, the debugger attaches to the local AOS with the C# extension's .NET debugger; see Debugging-on-Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Need Why A UDE connected with Connect to Environment… It downloads the FinOps tools that contain Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe. The environment selected in this window (Select Environment…) The debugger signs in to it and asks it for its web client URL. The metadata on this machine at the environment's version Breakpoint lines and symbols must match the code the environment runs. Check Environment Application Version tells you. A Microsoft account with access to the UDE The debugger proxy uses your Dataverse token. A test company and a vendor To create the purchase order. A moment when pausing the UDE is acceptable While the debugger is stopped, the environment's server is paused for every user.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prepare
docs.text:
1. Run Check Environment Application Version. If the environment runs a newer version than your metadata, update it first (the Environment group offers Update Metadata to …). See Version-Drift-Guard.
  2. If you also changed code in your own model, deploy it first with Deploy Models to Environment: the environment runs the code last deployed to it. When the project's build is newer than the last deploy, starting the debugger warns and offers Deploy First or Continue. See Deploy-to-Environment.
  3. In the web client, open the purchase order form once. Code that has run once binds its breakpoints right away.

docs.title: Phase 2: Set the breakpoints
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+Alt+O, type f:PurchTable and open the form. Right-click it in the Application Explorer and choose View Code to open its X++ code view.
  2. Find the init method (use the Outline view or Ctrl+Shift+O) and set a breakpoint (F9, or click the gutter) on the first line after super().
  3. Open table PurchTable (t:PurchTable) > View Code, find initFromVendTable and set a breakpoint on its first statement.
  4. Set breakpoints in the element's code view. F&O Studio decides which standard elements to load symbols for from the breakpoints in code views when the debugger starts. See Breakpoints-and-Source-Mapping.

docs.title: Phase 3: Start the debugger
docs.text:
1. Run Launch Debugger: from the Dynamics 365 view > Debug, from the Infolog view's title bar, or from the command palette. You can also use Run and Debug with the configuration Attach to Dynamics 365 (unified developer environment).
  2. The notification "Preparing X++ debugging…" shows the steps: signing in, then writing debug sources. F&O Studio:
  3. writes the debug source of each element as the compiler numbers it (for forms, with their data source and control classes), so lines match;
  4. for each standard element with a breakpoint, finds the module that holds it and loads only that module's symbols, as Visual Studio does;
  5. starts DebuggerProxy on a free local port, tunnelled to the environment, and attaches to AXHost.exe.
  6. The X++ output lists the standard elements it prepared, for example "Debugging standard code too: PurchTable (…)".
  7. The breakpoints turn solid when they bind. Hollow means the module has not loaded yet: trigger the code.

See Debugger and Debugging-Standard-Code.

docs.title: Phase 4: Trigger the code and step
docs.text:
1. Right-click the PurchTable menu item (or the form) and choose Open in Browser. For a form, F&O Studio finds a menu item that opens it.
  2. The form opens and the debugger stops in the form's init. VS Code shows the stop in the form's code view (not in a separate debug copy). Look at the variables, then continue (F5).
  3. Create a purchase order and pick the vendor. The debugger stops in PurchTable.initFromVendTable.
  4. Use the Run and Debug view:
  5. Variables: this (the purch order buffer), _vendTable, locals;
  6. Watch: add expressions such as this.DeliveryPostalAddress;
  7. Call Stack: who called initFromVendTable, down to the form's data source;
  8. step over (F10), into (F11) and out (Shift+F11), continue (F5).
  9. Step until the delivery address is assigned. Note the method and the condition that set it.
  10. Messages the code writes appear in the Infolog view of the F&O Studio panel. Each message has Find Message Source. See Infolog.

While the debugger is stopped, the environment's server is paused for every user. Continue or disconnect promptly.

docs.title: Phase 5: More breakpoints during the session
docs.text:
• Breakpoints you add or move in the code view of an element prepared at the start, or in your own code, are picked up right away.
  • A standard element that had no breakpoint when you started has no symbols loaded. Stop, set the breakpoint, and start again. Or add its module with additionalModules (phase 7).

docs.title: Phase 6: Stop safely
docs.text:
1. Disconnect (Shift+F5) or close the window. F&O Studio resumes the environment first and only detaches; it never ends the environment's process.
  2. A debugger left attached by a VS Code window that crashed is stopped the next time F&O Studio starts.

docs.title: Phase 7: Tune the debugger (optional)
docs.text:
The debugger works without a configuration. To change it, add an xpp configuration to .vscode/launch.json (Run and Debug > create a launch.json file > X++):

{
  "type": "xpp",
  "request": "attach",
  "name": "Attach to Dynamics 365",
  "additionalModules": ["Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.*.netmodule"],
  "logging": { "exceptions": false }
}
Option Use justMyCode On by default. Turning it off sends every exception the environment throws through the debugger, which can make the environment stop responding. Leave it on. additionalModules More modules whose symbols load. Wildcards allowed. symbolOptions Replaces the symbol options entirely. logging vsdbg logging. processName, sourceFileMap Process to attach to (AXHost.exe) and extra source mappings.

If DebuggerProxy is not in the default location, set xpp.debuggerProxyPath. See Debugger-Options.

docs.title: Phase 8: From understanding to change
docs.text:
1. Now you know the method that sets the address. Check who else hooks into it: Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) on the method lists overrides, Chain of Command classes and handlers. See Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command.
  2. Find All References (Shift+F12) and Call Hierarchy show the other callers. See Find-All-References and Call-and-Type-Hierarchy.
  3. If the behaviour must change, right-click PurchTable (table) > Create Code Extension and wrap the method. Build, deploy, and debug your wrapper next to the standard code: breakpoints in your own code bind after the deploy. See Create-Code-Extension.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Select the environment first: F&O Studio: Select Environment." No environment in this window. Run Select Environment…. "Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe was not found." The FinOps tools are not on this machine. Run Connect to Environment…, or set xpp.debuggerProxyPath. Breakpoint stays hollow in standard code The code has not run since attach, or the element had no breakpoint when you started. Trigger the code; or stop, set the breakpoint, start again. Breakpoint on the wrong line Metadata on this machine differs from the environment's version. Check Environment Application Version, then update the metadata. Your own breakpoints don't stop The environment runs an older deploy. Deploy Models to Environment, then debug again. The environment hardly responds The debugger is stopped (the server is paused), or justMyCode is off. Continue or disconnect; leave justMyCode on. "X++ debugging stopped: …" The proxy or the connection ended. See the X++ output for details.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Agents don't drive the debugger. They read code and metadata, so they are useful before and after a session.

F&O Code Archaeologist (read-only) explains the flow before you debug:

Explain how a new purchase order gets its delivery address: which methods of the PurchTable form and table and related classes set it, in what order, and from which setup. Give me the methods where I should put breakpoints.

It reads the methods with xpp_read_object and traces callers with xpp_find_references.

F&O Support (read-only) turns what you saw into a cause:

While debugging PurchTable.initFromVendTable I saw the delivery address come from the vendor's delivery location even though the user's site has its own. Read the code path and tell me the exact condition and whether it is setup or code.

When the change is clear, use Fix in code to hand over to F&O Developer:

Create a Chain of Command wrapper of PurchTable.initFromVendTable in ContosoExtensions that keeps the site's address when the site has one. Call next first. Build and open the class.

Checkpoints: - Breakpoint locations come from the code the agent read (method names you can open). - The wrapper calls next. - After deploy, your breakpoint in the wrapper and the standard breakpoint both stop.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Metadata version matches the environment.
  • [ ] Own code deployed (if any).
  • [ ] Code run once in the web client.
  • [ ] Breakpoints set in the code views of the standard elements before starting.
  • [ ] Launch Debugger; standard elements listed in the X++ output.
  • [ ] Breakpoints bound; variables, call stack and Infolog checked.
  • [ ] Disconnected promptly; environment responsive.
  • [ ] Next step decided: setup change, or a Chain of Command extension.
