docs.title: Scenario: Design a security role and reduce license cost
docs.text: This walkthrough is for functional consultants and developers who design security together. The goal: a new role that gives a job exactly what it needs, at the cheapest user license that still works, without segregation-of-duties conflicts, with a sign-off document for the customer. F&O Studio reads the security metadata of all packages, so you can analyze standard and custom roles without an environment; you only need one to deploy and test the role.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
The finance team wants a role Accounts receivable clerk – view only for auditors and new team members. They must look up customers, customer invoices and payment status, but never create or change anything. Today they get the standard role Accounts receivable clerk (CustInvoiceAccountsReceivableClerk), which can also maintain transactions, so its license follows its maintain grants.

You want to:

  • reuse the standard inquiry duties of the clerk role (for example CustCustomerMasterInquire, CustCustomerReferenceDataInquire, CustInvoiceCustomerInvoiceStatusInquire, CustInvoiceInvoiceAndCashPoliciesInquir, PaymCustomerPaymentsStatusInquire);
  • leave out every Maintain duty;
  • see which license the new role needs, and what drives it;
  • build the role as ContosoARClerkViewOnly in the model ContosoExtensions.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• F&O Studio with an active environment configuration (the analysis reads metadata; no database access needed).
  • To build and deploy the role: a project in ContosoExtensions and a development environment (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD).
  • To test with users: access to the environment's client as a system administrator, or the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server for the agents.

docs.title: Phase 1: Understand the standard role
docs.text:
1. Open the Security view (F&O Studio activity bar). It has two groups: Your roles (roles of your models and the standard roles they extend, with their license) and All roles. Nothing loads until you expand a group; the first load reads the security metadata of all packages and takes up to a minute. See Security View.
  1. Use Filter Roles… in the view's title bar and type receivable. All roles opens with the matching roles. Clear it later with Clear Role Filter.
  2. Expand CustInvoiceAccountsReceivableClerk: its duties, their privileges, and down to the entry points (menu items) and their grants.
  3. Right-click the role and choose Analyze License. The panel shows:
  4. the license the role needs, with the number of entry points, duties and privileges;
  5. Entry points by license: how many entry points need each license;
  6. What drives the license: the menu items with their grant, their View and Maintain license, and the duty and privilege they come through;
  7. Read-only alternatives: the menu items where granting only Read would lower the license;
  8. Missing objects: references that don't exist in the metadata.

The license is the highest View or Maintain user license of the menu items the role grants, depending on the access. See Analyze License.

  1. Use Copy as Markdown in the panel to keep the result for later comparison.

docs.title: Phase 2: Check what the job needs
docs.text:
1. List the forms the job opens: All customers, customer details, open invoices, payment status. Find the menu items behind them in the Application Explorer, for example the display menu item CustTable.
  2. Right-click the menu item and choose Who Can Access. The panel lists the menu items with their View and Maintain license, the privileges that grant access with their grant, and the duties and roles each privilege is in. Select a role to analyze its license. See Who Can Access.
  1. From the privileges list, note the inquiry privileges and duties that grant Read. Those are the building blocks of the new role. Prefer standard duties over new privileges: they follow Microsoft's updates.
  2. If a form the job needs is reachable only through a Maintain privilege, note it. You need a Read-only privilege for it (Phase 4).

docs.title: Phase 3: Create the role
docs.text:
1. In the project view, click + (New Element…) and pick Security Role. Name it ContosoARClerkViewOnly. See New Element.
  2. In the Element Designer, set the Label with the label picker (find or create the label "Accounts receivable clerk – view only") and a Description. See Properties Grid and Pickers.
  3. Add the duties: right-click Duties and choose Add from Application Explorer…, or drag the duties from the Application Explorer onto the node (Visual Studio's drop rules apply). Add the inquiry duties from Phase 2. See Drag and Drop.
  4. Save. Run Build Project.

docs.title: Phase 4: Bring the license down
docs.text:
1. Right-click ContosoARClerkViewOnly in the Security view (under Your roles, after Refresh Security) or in the project view, and choose Analyze License.
  2. Read What drives the license. Each row is a menu item that sets the license, with its grant and the path (duty, privilege) it comes through. Typical causes in a "view only" role:
  3. a duty that looks like an inquiry but contains a privilege with Update or Create on a menu item;
  4. an action menu item (grant Invoke), whose license applies whatever you do with it;
  5. a menu item whose View license is already high.
  6. Read Read-only alternatives. These menu items would lower the license with Read only.
  7. Fix them one by one:
  8. remove the duty that brings the expensive grant;
  9. give the menu item through your own privilege with Read only: right-click the menu item and choose Add to Privilege… > New privilege…, kind View. The suggested name is the menu item's name plus View; use your prefix instead (for example ContosoCustTableView) so it doesn't clash with a standard privilege. Keep only Read in the grants (the default for a View privilege on a display menu item). Then put the privilege in the role (or in a duty of yours). See Add to Privilege.
  10. Run Analyze License again. Repeat until the license matches what you expect for a view-only job, or until the remaining drivers are things the job really needs. Write down the drivers you accept, for the sign-off.

docs.title: Phase 5: Check segregation of duties
docs.text:
1. Right-click the role and choose Check Segregation of Duties. Without a selection it asks for Roles of your models or Pick a role…. See Segregation of Duties.
  1. The panel lists the roles and rules checked and each conflict: role, rule, severity, reason, and the two conflicting duties. High severity conflicts show as errors.
  2. A view-only role should have none. If your company has its own rules, run Edit Segregation of Duties Rules. With no rules file set, it writes the built-in rules to .xpp/sod-rules.json in the workspace and sets xpp.security.sodRulesFile to it. Change the file, then check again. Rules that name duties that don't exist are listed under Skipped rules.

docs.title: Phase 6: Check for gaps
docs.text:
1. Run Find Security Gaps and pick ContosoExtensions. It reports, by severity, menu items no privilege grants, privileges in no duty, duties in no role, over-granting, missing objects and data entities without permissions. See Find Security Gaps.
  2. A privilege you created in Phase 4 that is in no duty is fine if the role holds it directly; the panel tells you what it found, and you decide.

docs.title: Phase 7: Write the sign-off document
docs.text:
1. Run Security Report…. Choose Pick roles… and pick ContosoARClerkViewOnly (and the standard clerk role, to compare), then Markdown ("sign-off document") or CSV ("for Excel"). Markdown opens with a preview next to it; CSV goes through a save dialog. See Security Report.
  2. Add the license analysis from Phase 4 and the accepted license drivers.

docs.title: Phase 8: Deploy and test with a user
docs.text:
1. Deploy the model (Deploy Models to Environment on a UDE; no database sync is needed for security elements). See Deploy to Environment.
  2. In the client, assign the role to a test user (System administration > Users > Users > Assign roles). Sign in as the user and open every form of the job. Check that edit buttons are disabled and that forms outside the job are not in the menu.
  3. Use the client's own security tools to confirm, for example the security configuration and the license reports your tenant uses. F&O Studio analyzes metadata; actual license counts come from the environment.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Three agents share this work:

  • F&O Role Designer (functional consultants) designs roles from a job description. It is read-only and hands building to the developer.
  • F&O Security & License (developers and consultants) verifies a design: access chains, license impact, conflicts. Read-only.
  • F&O Developer creates the privileges, duties and role.

Start with the Role Designer:

Design a role "Accounts receivable clerk – view only". The user looks up customers, customer invoices and payment status. They must not create, change or post anything. Reuse standard duties where possible and keep the license as low as possible. Compare it with the standard Accounts receivable clerk role.

What it does:

Step Tool Finds which privileges, duties and roles reach each menu item of the job xpp_analyze_security with op=access Ranks standard roles for a new duty by what they already reach and by name xpp_analyze_security with op=placement License of the candidate role and what drives it xpp_analyze_security with op=license Segregation-of-duties conflicts xpp_analyze_security with op=sod Reads users' role assignments in the live environment, when connected Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server tools

Its answer is a role design: roles and duties to assign, duties or privileges to add or remove, license per role, conflicts and mitigations.

Then use the handoffs:

  • Verify switches to F&O Security & License: "Verify the role design above for access, license and conflicts." It answers with the chain role > duty > privilege > entry point > access level and the cheapest license that still works.
  • Build the role switches to F&O Developer: "Create the roles, duties and privileges designed above in ContosoExtensions." Before it writes, run Start Copilot Checkpoint; limit what it may change with Set Copilot Scope… if the project holds other work. The developer creates the elements through the metadata API, builds and runs best practice. See Copilot Checkpoints and Scope.

More prompts:

  • "Which menu items make ContosoARClerkViewOnly need more than the lowest license, and would Read-only fix them?"
  • "Who can open the CustTable menu item today, and with which grant?"
  • "Write a security report for ContosoARClerkViewOnly as Markdown for client sign-off." (op=report)

Agents change security only after you allow it, and never in production. See Agents for Functional Consultants.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The job's forms and actions are listed (what it must do and must not do).
  • [ ] Standard inquiry duties reused; no Maintain duty in the role.
  • [ ] Analyze License run on the new role; every license driver understood or removed.
  • [ ] Read-only alternatives applied where the job only looks.
  • [ ] Check Segregation of Duties: no conflicts (with your company's rules if you have them).
  • [ ] Find Security Gaps: no errors in the model.
  • [ ] Security Report exported for sign-off, with the license analysis.
  • [ ] Role deployed and tested with a user in the client.

docs.title: Scenario: Expose Data to an Integration
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers and integration consultants who need to give an external system access to D365FO data: read and write over OData, bulk import and export with data management, or call an action through a custom service. It goes from picking the right entity to calling it on your UDE and saving the request for the integration team.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
An external CRM needs three things from D365FO:

  1. Customer groups, including the credit category you added to CustGroup in Scenario-Extend-a-Standard-Form-and-Table (field ContosoCreditCategory). Read over OData, nightly.
  2. Delivery priorities, your own setup table ContosoDeliveryPriority from Scenario-Build-a-Feature-End-to-End. Read over OData and loaded once with data management.
  3. An action: the CRM asks D365FO to put a customer on credit review. That is a request with logic, not a row to write, so it fits a custom service.
Need Choice F&O Studio Customer groups with the new field Standard entity CustCustomerGroupEntity (public collection CustomerGroups, staging CustCustomerGroupEntityStaging), extended Create Extension on the entity, Try Data Entity (OData)… Delivery priorities New entity over ContosoDeliveryPriority New Data Entity… Put a customer on credit review Custom service New Custom Service…, Try Service Operation…

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Need Why A connected UDE (Connect-to-Environment) Try Data Entity and Try Service Operation call the active environment's web client URL with your Microsoft sign-in. The ContosoExtensions project open New elements go to the project's model. A label file with an en-US language in the model The wizards' labels. A workspace folder Saved requests go to .xpp/requests/ in it. Rights on the environment to read the entity and call the service Calls run with your account.

Try Data Entity (OData)… and Try Service Operation… are preview features. Both appear on the context menu of an entity or service in the Application Explorer or project view, not in the command palette.

docs.title: Phase 1: Find the standard entity
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+Alt+O and type CustCustomerGroupEntity. The element designer shows its data sources, fields, keys and properties. Check IsPublic (Yes), PublicEntityName (CustomerGroup), PublicCollectionName (CustomerGroups), DataManagementEnabled and DataManagementStagingTable (CustCustomerGroupEntityStaging).
  2. Check which fields it maps: CustomerGroupId, Description, PaymentTermId and others. The new ContosoCreditCategory field is not there; you add it in phase 3.
  3. Right-click the entity > Who Can Access: the privileges, duties and roles that reach it. The integration's app user needs one of them. See Who-Can-Access.
  4. Right-click > Analyze Performance: for a data entity it also checks readiness: public names, keys, staging fields, mandatory fields and set-based processing. See Analyze-Performance.

Prefer a standard entity, then an extension of one, then a new entity.

docs.title: Phase 2: Try the standard entity
docs.text:
1. Right-click CustCustomerGroupEntity > Try Data Entity (OData)…. If the entity is not public (IsPublic = Yes and a PublicCollectionName are needed), it says so.
  2. Enter an optional $filter (for example dataAreaId eq 'usmf'), pick $top (10, 50 or 200) and the companies: All companies (cross-company=true) or Default company only.
  3. F&O Studio sends GET /data/CustomerGroups?... to the active environment with your sign-in and shows the response beside the editor, with the status line on top.
  4. Click Save as .http to keep the request in .xpp/requests/ (REST Client format). The access token is never written to the file: it is a {{token}} variable.

See Try-Data-Entity-OData.

docs.title: Phase 3: Extend the standard entity with the new field
docs.text:
1. Right-click CustCustomerGroupEntity > Create Extension > accept CustCustomerGroupEntity.ContosoExtensions. The designer opens with the entity's nodes; your own are in bold.
  2. Add a mapped field ContosoCreditCategory on the CustGroup data source's field of the same name.
  3. The staging table needs the same field, or data management can't import it: extend CustCustomerGroupEntityStaging with Create Extension and add the field there too. The agent tools do both in one step (entity extensions include their staging tables), so this is a good part to hand to Copilot.
  4. Run Analyze Performance on the entity again: readiness findings point at missing staging fields.
  5. Run Build Project and fix Problems.

See Create-Extension.

docs.title: Phase 4: Create a new entity for your own table
docs.text:
1. Run New Data Entity… (Dynamics 365 view > Create, or New Element… > Wizards > Data entity).
  2. Answer the prompts:
  3. table: ContosoDeliveryPriority;
  4. entity name: ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntity (proposed);
  5. label: what users see in data management;
  6. public name (OData, singular): proposed from the table name, without a short all-capitals prefix such as ABC (ContosoDeliveryPriority stays as it is); type DeliveryPriority;
  7. public collection name (OData, plural): proposed as the public name plus s; type DeliveryPriorities;
  8. fields: all supported fields are preselected; RecId references and containers are not offered.
  9. The entity key comes from the table's replacement key (else its primary index). If the table has none, the wizard asks for the key fields. The key fields must be among the picked fields.
  10. The wizard creates, all or nothing:
  11. the staging table ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntityStaging with the data management fields (DefinitionGroup, ExecutionId, IsSelected, TransferStatus) and the picked fields;
  12. the entity: public, data management enabled, category Reference, the key, and the company context when the table saves data per company;
  13. the privileges ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntityView (Read) and ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntityMaintain (Read, Update, Create, Delete).
  14. The message says: add the privileges to duties, build and synchronize the database; the entity is then at /data/DeliveryPriorities and in data management.

See Wizard-Data-Entity.

docs.title: Phase 5: Create the custom service
docs.text:
1. Run New Custom Service… (Dynamics 365 view > Create).
  2. Answer: name ContosoCreditReviewRequest and a description.
  3. It creates the request and response contracts (ContosoCreditReviewRequestRequest, ...Response), the service class with a process operation that runs in the request's company inside a transaction and returns success and a message, the service ContosoCreditReviewRequestService, the service group ContosoCreditReviewRequestServiceGroup and the privilege ContosoCreditReviewRequestInvoke.
  4. The message gives the endpoint after deployment: /api/services/ContosoCreditReviewRequestServiceGroup/ContosoCreditReviewRequestService/process.
  5. Click Open Service Class. Replace the request's sample Description member with your fields (for example the customer account) and write the logic where the comment says.

Pick a short base name: the wizard appends Request, Response, Service and ServiceGroup. See Wizard-Custom-Service.

If the CRM should be told when something happens rather than call D365FO, use New Business Event… instead. See Wizard-Business-Event.

docs.title: Phase 6: Security
docs.text:
1. Add the entity privileges and ContosoCreditReviewRequestInvoke to a duty, and the duty to the role of the integration's app user. Use New Element… > Security duty / Security role, or extensions of standard ones.
  2. Run Find Security Gaps: services and entities no privilege covers show here. See Find-Security-Gaps.
  3. Analyze License on the role shows the license it needs. See Analyze-License.

docs.title: Phase 7: Build, deploy, call
docs.text:
1. Build Project, then Run Best Practice Checks on Project.
  2. Deploy Models to Environment with database sync Module: the entities and staging tables need it. See Deploy-to-Environment.
  3. Right-click ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntity > Try Data Entity (OData)…: the new collection answers.
  4. Right-click the service ContosoCreditReviewRequestService > Try Service Operation…:
  5. pick the operation (process);
  6. confirm the service group (proposed from the service name);
  7. a JSON request body opens, filled from the operation's data contract (members of [DataMember] parm methods, with sample values);
  8. edit it, then click Send or Save as .http. Send asks first ("The service runs its code with your account and may change data.").
  9. Hand the saved .http files to the integration team. They set their own token.

See Try-Service-Operation.

docs.title: Phase 8: Data management and errors
docs.text:
1. In the web client, data management lists the new entity. Export a template, fill it, and import into a test company. This is standard D365FO, not F&O Studio.
  2. When an import fails with a message such as "Field 'Delivery priority' must be filled in.", paste it into Find Message Source. For "must be filled in" it lists the mandatory fields with that label first. See Find-Message-Source.
  3. Check the staging rows with Browse Table Data on ContosoDeliveryPriorityEntityStaging.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
F&O Integration designs, builds and troubleshoots integrations. It may change elements after you allow it, in a development environment.

The CRM needs customer groups with our new ContosoCreditCategory field over OData, delivery priorities over OData and data management, and a way to put a customer on credit review. Pick standard entities where possible, extend CustCustomerGroupEntity with the field (and its staging table), create an entity for ContosoDeliveryPriority, and propose a custom service for the action. Tell me keys, direction and error handling per flow.

What it does: xpp_find_object and xpp_list_objects on data entities to find standard ones, xpp_read_object for fields, keys and public names, then entity extensions (with their staging tables) or new entities through xpp_create_object. It builds with xpp_build. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint first.

To check the result on the environment, ask it to call the entity through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server if you have it, or use Try Data Entity (OData)… yourself.

F&O Data Migration (handoff Plan the data migration) plans the load:

Plan the initial load of delivery priorities and the customer group credit categories for three companies: which entities, keys, required fields, order and validation steps.

It reads the entities' mandatory fields and keys (xpp_read_object) and, for import errors, uses xpp_find_message_source and the staging records.

F&O Security & License (read-only) checks the app user's access:

What's the minimum role for the CRM's app user to read CustomerGroups and DeliveryPriorities and call ContosoCreditReviewRequestService, and what license does it need?

Checkpoints: - Standard entities were considered before new ones. - Entity extensions include the staging table field. - Every entity and service is covered by a privilege; no security gaps. - Calls work on the UDE; saved .http files contain no token.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Standard entity found and its public names, keys and staging checked.
  • [ ] Standard entity tried with Try Data Entity (OData)….
  • [ ] Entity extension and staging table extension with the new field.
  • [ ] New entity for the custom table, with staging table and privileges.
  • [ ] Custom service created; logic written; endpoint noted.
  • [ ] Privileges in duties and a role for the app user; Find Security Gaps clean.
  • [ ] Built, deployed with Module sync.
  • [ ] OData calls and the service call work; .http files saved for the integration team.
  • [ ] Data management import tested; errors traced with Find Message Source.

docs.title: Scenario: Extend a Standard Form and Table
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers who need to add a field to a standard table and show it on the standard form, without changing Microsoft's code. You use a table extension, a form extension and, when needed, a Chain of Command class, all in your own model. The result builds, deploys and shows up in the web client.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Credit control wants to classify customer groups as low, medium or high credit risk. The classification belongs on the customer group (CustGroup table) and must be visible and editable on the Customer groups form (CustGroup form, menu item CustGroup), next to the existing fields.

You build it in the ContosoExtensions model:

Element Type Purpose ContosoCreditCategory Enum Values Low, Medium, High. CustGroup.ContosoExtensions Table extension New field ContosoCreditCategory. CustGroup.ContosoExtensions Form extension The field on the form. Labels in ContosoLabels Label file Field label, help text, enum value labels.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Need Why A connected environment (Connect-to-Environment) Metadata of CustGroup. The ContosoExtensions project open (D365FO-Projects) New elements go to the project's model. The form layout needs a project to know where to write the extension. A label file in ContosoExtensions (for example ContosoLabels) Field and enum labels. ContosoExtensions references ApplicationSuite CustGroup is in ApplicationSuite. Check with View Model Dependencies…; add it with Update Model Parameters…. A UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD environment To deploy, sync and test.

docs.title: Phase 1: Check the standard first
docs.text:
1. Open the table: Ctrl+Alt+O, type t:CustGroup. The element designer shows its fields, field groups, indexes, relations and methods; the Properties grid shows the properties. See Element-Designer.
  2. Check that no existing field already does the job. Hover the fields' labels in the code view, or browse the data with Browse Table Data.
  3. See who uses the table: View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) shows related tables, Find References where it is used. See Entity-Relationship-Diagram.
  4. See the form as users see it: right-click the CustGroup form and choose Open Form Layout…. It shows the form with every extension merged.
  5. Check what other models already add: Show Extensions and Handlers… lists the table's extensions and handlers. A field with the same name in another extension would collide.

docs.title: Phase 2: Create the enum
docs.text:
1. In the project view, click + (or run New Element…), pick Enum under Data types, and name it ContosoCreditCategory. The element is created in the project's model, added to the project and opened. See New-Element.
  2. In the designer, use New… on the enum to add the values Low, Medium and High.
  3. For each value, set Label with the label picker: it finds an existing label or creates one in your label file. Set the enum's own Label too.
  4. Set IsExtensible if other models should be able to add values later.

See Properties-Grid-and-Pickers and Label-Editor.

docs.title: Phase 3: Create the table extension and the field
docs.text:
1. Right-click CustGroup (table) in the Application Explorer and choose Create Extension.
  2. Accept the name CustGroup.ContosoExtensions. The name must start with CustGroup.. The extension is created in the project's model, added to the project and opened in the designer.
  3. The designer shows the base table's nodes; your extension's own nodes are in bold.
  4. Right-click Fields and choose New…, pick the enum field type, and name it ContosoCreditCategory.
  5. In the Properties grid:
  6. EnumType: press Alt+Down for the element picker and pick ContosoCreditCategory;
  7. Label and HelpText: use the label picker;
  8. leave Mandatory at No unless every group must have a value (a mandatory field raises "Field '…' must be filled in." on save).
  9. Changed values are marked in the grid. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.

See Create-Extension.

Need a default or a check in code? Right-click CustGroup and choose Create Code Extension. It proposes CustGroup_ContosoExtensions_Extension (the name must end with _Extension), creates the class with [ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustGroup))] and opens it. Write the wrapper; the create a Chain of Command wrapper quick fix (Ctrl+.) and the Chain of Command snippet help. A wrapper must call next. See Create-Code-Extension and Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command.

docs.title: Phase 4: Put the field on the form
docs.text:
1. Right-click the CustGroup form in the Application Explorer and choose Open Form Layout… (also in the element designer's title bar as Form Layout). The tab is called CustGroup [Design].
  2. In the control outline, select the control the new field should follow (for example the payment terms field in the grid), or a group or grid to add inside it.
  3. Click Add fields after… (or Add fields inside… on a container).
  4. Pick the data source CustGroup, then the field ContosoCreditCategory. The field list includes fields from table extensions.
  5. The control is saved to the form extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions in your project's model. If it doesn't exist yet, it is created and added to the project. The status bar says "Added 1 field(s) in CustGroup.ContosoExtensions".
  6. Use Change label…, Hide or Show on a control when you need it. These changes go to the same extension.
  7. Check the preview: it is drawn like the web client. In the element designer of the form extension, Show hidden controls and markers outlines what extensions added.

If the form is in your own model, the layout view refuses and tells you to edit it directly; it writes extensions only. See Form-Layout-and-Form-Extensions and Form-Designer-and-Preview.

docs.title: Phase 5: Build, deploy and synchronize
docs.text:
1. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B). Fix every error and warning in Problems. See Build-Project-and-Model.
  2. Run Run Best Practice Checks on Project: missing labels or help text show here. See Best-Practice-Checks.
  3. The table changed, so the database must be synchronized:
  4. UDE: Deploy Models to Environment, pick ContosoExtensions, database sync Module. Progress is in the X++ Deploy output. See Deploy-to-Environment.
  5. Cloud-hosted or VHD: right-click the CustGroup table and choose Synchronize Table(s) with the Database (it syncs only the tables you pick), or run Synchronize Database from the command palette, which runs a full SyncEngine sync of the local AxDB. The successful build already restarted the local AOS. See Synchronize-Database.

docs.title: Phase 6: Verify
docs.text:
1. Right-click the CustGroup menu item and choose Open in Browser. The Customer groups form shows the new column. Set a value on a group and save.
  2. Right-click the CustGroup table and choose Browse Table Data: the new column shows the enum name next to its value.
  3. Optional: Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot) (preview) turns your changed elements into check steps for Copilot agent mode with the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server. See Verify-Changes-in-Running-App.

docs.title: Phase 7: Check the impact
docs.text:
1. Who Can Access on the CustGroup menu item shows the roles that reach the form, so you know who sees the new field. Field-level security is not needed for this change. See Who-Can-Access.
  2. Integrations: the standard entity CustCustomerGroupEntity (OData CustomerGroups) does not carry the new field until you extend it. See Scenario-Expose-Data-to-an-Integration.
  3. Run Upgrade Readiness on ContosoExtensions before the next version update: it reports table, form and enum extensions that no longer match and collisions with other models' extensions (the same field or form control). See Upgrade-Readiness.
  4. Run Review My Changes and commit. See Review-My-Changes.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
F&O Solution Designer (read-only) writes the design first:

Credit control wants a credit category (Low, Medium, High) on customer groups, visible and editable on the Customer groups form. Check whether standard already has something similar, then design the extension in ContosoExtensions: elements, names, labels, security and test scenarios.

It searches documentation and standard precedents (xpp_search_docs, xpp_find_examples), reads CustGroup and the form layout (xpp_read_object, xpp_get_form_layout) and returns the design. Use the handoff Build it to switch to F&O Developer.

F&O Developer builds it:

Implement the design: enum ContosoCreditCategory with labelled values, table extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions with the field ContosoCreditCategory, and the field on the CustGroup form after the payment terms in the grid through a form extension. Use labels in ContosoLabels. Build until there are no errors or warnings in these elements, run the best practice checks, and open the form extension.

Before you send it, run Start Copilot Checkpoint. The agent reads the form's patterns with xpp_get_form_layout, creates the elements with xpp_create_object (form controls are placed and checked against the form's patterns), creates labels with xpp_create_label, adds them to the project, builds with xpp_build and runs xpp_check_best_practice. Every write is all or nothing and goes only to your models; an existing name is never overwritten. Follow the calls in Copilot Activity; each changed element links to its designer.

F&O Code Reviewer reviews before merge:

Review my branch against main: the CustGroup extensions and the enum. Check labels, extension naming and anything that could collide with other models.

When you're happy, End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes). If not, Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint….

Checkpoints: - The plan names the elements before anything is created. - No standard element changed; only ContosoExtensions elements in Copilot Activity. - BUILD SUCCEEDED and no best practice errors. - The field appears in the form layout and, after deploy and sync, in the web client.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Standard checked: no existing field does the job; no collision in other extensions.
  • [ ] Enum created with labelled values.
  • [ ] Table extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions with the labelled field.
  • [ ] Form extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions with the control in the right place.
  • [ ] Build and best practice clean.
  • [ ] Deployed with Module sync (UDE) or tables synchronized (cloud-hosted/VHD).
  • [ ] Field visible and editable in the web client; value in Browse Table Data.
  • [ ] Integration and upgrade impact checked.
  • [ ] Changes reviewed and committed.

docs.title: Scenario: From Error Message to Fix
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers who get an error message from a user, a batch job log or an integration, and need to find where it comes from, why it happens and how to fix it. Functional consultants can follow phases 1 and 2 (or use the F&O Functional Triage agent) to decide whether the cause is setup, data or code.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
A user reports: "When I create a customer I get Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." At the same time, the nightly import of web shop customers, a custom class ContosoCustomerImport in the ContosoExtensions model, logs the same message for some rows.

Two causes are possible:

  • The platform raises "Field '%1' must be filled in." when a field whose Mandatory property is Yes is empty when the record is saved. On CustTable, the field CustGroup (label "Customer group") is mandatory.
  • Code can raise the same label text for its own checks.

So the question is: which field is empty, who should have filled it, and is it setup, data or code?

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Need Why A connected environment (Connect-to-Environment) Metadata and the cross-reference database. The cross-reference database Find Message Source and Find References use it for where-used. The project of the model you will fix (ContosoExtensions) Build, tests and deploy work on the project. Database access (optional) To check the data behind the error. A UDE to reproduce on, never production Fixes and test data go to development environments only.

docs.title: Phase 1: Get the exact message
docs.text:
1. Copy the message exactly as the user saw it, values included. Do not retype or translate it. For an integration, copy the text from the log row.
  2. If you can reproduce it while debugging, the message shows in the Infolog view of the F&O Studio panel. Each message has Find Message Source inline and in its context menu. See Infolog.
  3. Note the context: the form (Customers, CustTable), the action (New, then Save), the company and, for the import, the input row.

docs.title: Phase 2: Find where the message comes from
docs.text:
1. Run Find Message Source (Dynamics 365 view > Find > Find Message Source…, or the command palette). If you selected the text in an editor first, it is filled in.
  2. Paste Field 'Customer group' must be filled in. and press Enter.
  3. Read the result list. For this message the list has three parts:
Section What it shows What it means here Mandatory fields · platform check Table fields with the label "Customer group" whose Mandatory property is Yes, with the model and whether the table or an extension sets it. CustTable.CustGroup, Mandatory = Yes, set by the table. The platform raises the message when it is empty. Code that raises it for "Customer group" Code lines that use the same label for one of those fields. Validation code that checks the customer group itself. Same text, other fields Code that reuses the text for other fields. Usually not your case; kept apart.

Labels whose text matches are listed with their IDs. Placeholders (%1) match any value. 4. Click CustTable.CustGroup to open the table designer on that field. Click a code line to open the X++ code view at that line. 5. If a label shows "Not used in X++ code", the platform raises it, or the package was not built with cross-reference data. If where-used is unavailable, the list says why (for example, no cross-reference database).

See Find-Message-Source.

Decision point. The platform check means the record was saved with an empty CustGroup. Now find out who left it empty:

  • A user in the form: data entry or setup (for example a customer template or default that should fill it). Hand it to a functional consultant, or use the F&O Functional Triage agent (below).
  • Code that creates customers: a code defect. Continue with phase 3.

docs.title: Phase 3: Find the code that saves the record
docs.text:
1. Find every place your model inserts customers. Run Search Code in All Packages (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F) with CustTable and insert, or a regular expression such as custTable\.(insert|write)\(. Results list the element, method, line and model. See Search-Code.
  2. Narrow it with Find References on CustTable (right-click in the Application Explorer) and look for elements of ContosoExtensions. The list shows element, member, line and kind. See Find-All-References.
  3. Open ContosoCustomerImport and read the method that builds the customer. In the code view, F12 goes to definitions, and Call Hierarchy shows who calls the method. See Call-and-Type-Hierarchy.
  4. In the example, the method sets AccountNum, the party and the currency, then calls insert() without a customer group when the web shop sends none.

To see how standard code creates customers with a group, run Find Similar Standard Implementations on your class, or describe the task ("create a customer from code"). See Find-Similar-Implementations.

docs.title: Phase 4: Check the data
docs.text:
1. With database access (Database-Access), right-click CustTable and choose Browse Table Data. Filter on the company and sort by the created date to see the last imported customers.
  2. For the rejected rows, open New SQL Query and check the input of the import (your staging or log table). The query panel is read-only by default: one SELECT, always rolled back. See SQL-Query-Panel.
  3. Check which customer group the business wants as default for web shop customers, for example WEB, and that it exists in CustGroup for that company.

docs.title: Phase 5: Fix the code
docs.text:
1. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint only if you plan to let Copilot edit. For your own edit, no checkpoint is needed.
  2. In the code view of ContosoCustomerImport, set the customer group before the insert, from a parameter or the input, and stop with a clear message when neither has one. Use a label for the message: the Quick Fix (Ctrl+.) offers extract to label. See Quick-Fixes.
custTable.CustGroup = _input.parmCustGroup()
    ? _input.parmCustGroup()
    : ContosoWebShopParameters::find().DefaultCustGroup;

if (!custTable.CustGroup)
{
    throw error("@ContosoLabels:WebShopCustomerGroupMissing");
}
  1. Save. Syntax errors show while you type; obsolete APIs are underlined. See Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings.
  2. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B). Errors go to Problems at the right line; a failed build offers Show Problems. See Build-Project-and-Model.

If the fix belongs in a standard class instead (for example defaulting in a standard method), use Create Code Extension on that class to get a Chain of Command class in your model. See Create-Code-Extension.

docs.title: Phase 6: Prove the fix
docs.text:
1. On a UDE, run Deploy Models to Environment. Pick the ContosoExtensions package (preselected) and the database sync (None is enough for a code-only change). Progress shows in the X++ Deploy output. See Deploy-to-Environment.
  2. Try the import for one row with Run Snippet in Environment: write a class with a main method in an untitled X++ editor, then run the command. It saves the code into the scratch class ContosoExtensionsScratchRunner, builds, offers Deploy and Run or Run Without Deploying, and opens the class in the browser. Delete the scratch class afterwards; the Pre-Deploy Checklist fails while it is in the model. See Run-Snippet.
  3. Add a regression test: right-click ContosoCustomerImport and run Generate SysTest Class with Test Data (ATL). It creates ContosoCustomerImportTest with a test per public method and customer data from the Acceptance Test Library, and offers Add References when the model lacks the ATL packages. Write the assert: an import without a group gets the default group. See Generate-SysTest-Class.
  4. Build, deploy, and run Run Tests (or use VS Code's Test Explorer). When the build is newer than the last deploy, F&O Studio warns first and offers Deploy First or Continue. Results go to the X++ Tests output. See Run-Tests.
  5. Ask the user to retry in the UDE, or open the form with Open in Browser on the CustTable menu item.

docs.title: Phase 7: Review and hand over
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes. It lists the changed elements against xpp.git.baseBranch with their best practice and performance findings and a pull request summary to copy. See Review-My-Changes.
  2. Link the work item with Link Work Item… so the commit message carries it. See Work-Items-and-Pipelines.
  3. Commit and push. Tell the user what changed and what setup the default group needs.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick the agent by who you are and what you have.

F&O Functional Triage (read-only, for consultants and key users) turns the report into a cause and a fix in business terms. It uses xpp_find_message_source and, when available, the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server to look at the record in the environment. If the cause is code, it hands over to F&O Support.

A user in company USMF gets "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." when saving a new customer on the All customers form. What is the cause and how does the user fix it? Check the customer templates and defaults too.

F&O Support (read-only, for developers) finds the condition and where it is:

The nightly ContosoCustomerImport logs "Field 'Customer group' must be filled in." for some rows. Find where the message comes from, which code in ContosoExtensions saves CustTable without CustGroup, and the exact condition. Check the last imported customers in the database.

What it does: xpp_find_message_source with the text as shown (it lists the mandatory fields first), xpp_read_object with methodNames for the raising and saving methods, xpp_find_references for callers, and xppQueryData for a read-only SELECT on the UDE after you confirm. Its answer names the cause, the evidence, the fix and how to verify it. Use the handoff Fix in code to switch to F&O Developer.

F&O Developer implements the fix:

Implement the fix above in ContosoCustomerImport: default the customer group from the web shop parameters, raise a labelled error when there is none, build, run the best practice checks and open the changed method.

Before you send it, run Start Copilot Checkpoint and Set Copilot Scope… to ContosoCustomerImport (and the label file). The agent changes code through xpp_update_object, creates the label with xpp_create_label, builds with xpp_build, runs xpp_check_best_practice and opens the method with xppOpenElement.

F&O Test Engineer writes and runs the regression test:

Write a SysTest for ContosoCustomerImport with ATL data: an input without a customer group gets the default group, and no default raises the error. Build and run it.

It builds and runs the test with xppRunTests, which asks before running on the environment and warns when the deployed code is older than the build.

Checkpoints: - The cause is stated as a condition (field, method, line), not a guess. - Copilot Activity shows only the elements you allowed changed. - The build says BUILD SUCCEEDED and the test passes on the deployed code. - If something went wrong, Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… undoes every element, label and project change.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The exact message, context, company and record are recorded.
  • [ ] Find Message Source shows the mandatory field or the raising code.
  • [ ] Decided: setup, data or code.
  • [ ] The saving code is found (Search Code, Find References).
  • [ ] The data behind the error is checked.
  • [ ] Fix built without errors; messages use labels.
  • [ ] Deployed to the UDE and verified (Run Snippet or the user).
  • [ ] Regression test added and passing.
  • [ ] Review My Changes clean; work item linked.
  • [ ] Run Snippet's scratch class deleted.

docs.title: Scenario: From Work Item to Deployed Change
docs.text: For a D365FO developer on a team that uses Git, Azure Boards and a build pipeline. You follow one work item from the board to a change that runs on your unified developer environment, passes review and is merged, and you see where the pipeline and the release process take over. Every step names the F&O Studio command or agent to use.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Work item #4711 in Azure Boards: "Sales clerks need an order status on the sales order (Open, On hold, Released). Invoicing must stop with an error when the order is on hold."

The team's repository ContosoFinOps (Azure Repos) holds the model ContosoExtensions; the project ContosoExtensionsProject is already set up (see Scenario: Set Up ALM for a Team). The change needs:

  • an enum ContosoOrderStatus and a field on SalesTable (table extension);
  • the field on the SalesTable form (form extension);
  • a Chain of Command extension of SalesFormLetter that stops invoicing when the status is On hold;
  • labels in ContosoLabels;
  • a test.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Your UDE connected and selected, the repository cloned and linked (Open Team Repository…), the project open.
  • xpp.git.baseBranch set to main.
  • Access to the Azure DevOps project.

docs.title: Phase 1: Pick up the work item
docs.text:
1. Run Open Work Item… and enter 4711. The work item opens in Azure Boards in your browser. Read the acceptance criteria and set it to Active.
  2. In VS Code, pull main and create the branch feature/4711-order-status (Source Control view, or git switch -c feature/4711-order-status).
  3. Run Build Model so the package matches the branch. See Branching and Team Workflow.

docs.title: Phase 2: Make the change
docs.text:
1. Read the standard code first: Open Element… SalesFormLetter, check how invoicing runs; use Find Similar Standard Implementations for an existing validation pattern (see Find Similar Implementations).
  2. New Element… > Enum ContosoOrderStatus with the values Open, OnHold, Released, each with a label (see New Element, Label Editor).
  3. In the Application Explorer, right-click SalesTable > Create Extension; add the field ContosoOrderStatus (see Create Extension). Do the same for the SalesTable form and place the field.
  4. Right-click SalesFormLetter > Create Code Extension, wrap the method that runs the posting and call next (see Create Code Extension). Example of the shape (adapt the method to the one you wrap):
[ExtensionOf(classStr(SalesFormLetter))]
final class SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension
{
    public void run()
    {
        // Validate before the standard logic runs; next must always be called.
        next run();
    }
}
  1. Watch the project view: the new elements are marked A, changed ones M (see Git Changes in the Project View).
  2. Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B). Fix every error in the Problems view (see Build Project and Model).
  3. Generate SysTest Class for the validation and write the test (see Generate SysTest Class).

docs.title: Phase 3: Commit with the work item
docs.text:
1. Run Link Work Item…, enter 4711. The commit message box gets #4711 and the Source Control view opens.
  2. Write the message, for example Order status on sales orders, block invoicing on hold #4711, and commit.
  3. Commit in small steps; link each commit.

See Work Items and Pipelines.

docs.title: Phase 4: Deploy to your UDE and test
docs.text:
1. Run Deploy Models to Environment. ContosoExtensions is preselected. Choose Module for the database sync: the new field must be created in the database.
  2. Wait for "Deployed ContosoExtensions." The project's status bar item no longer shows the cloud-upload icon.
  3. Run Tests (or Test Explorer). They run the deployed code; if you build again later, F&O Studio warns and offers Deploy First (see Run Tests, Status Bar).
  4. Check the form in the browser (Open in Browser), or run Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot).

See Deploy to Environment and Environments and Promotion.

docs.title: Phase 5: Review before the pull request
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes and accept main as the base branch. The Results view shows:
  2. Pull request summary: the changed elements by type (ContosoOrderStatus (new), SalesTable.ContosoExtensions, ...), the security impact and the work items (#4711);
  3. Chain of Command: an error for any wrapper that does not call next;
  4. Best practice and compiler and Performance findings for the changed elements.
  5. Fix what it reports. A new menu item would be flagged under "New menu items need a privilege".
  6. Run Pre-Deploy Checklist for build, best practice, performance, security gaps and Run Snippet's scratch class in one report (see Pre-Deploy Checklist).
  7. Use View History on an element to see what each commit changed in its code (see Element History).

See Review My Changes.

docs.title: Phase 6: Pull request and pipeline
docs.text:
1. Push the branch.
  2. Create the pull request in Azure Repos. In the Results view, Copy Report as Markdown and paste the review into the description. Check that #4711 is linked.
  3. Run Open Pipelines and follow the pull request build. A failure that does not happen locally is usually an element you did not commit: run Show Changed Elements (see Build Automation and Pipelines).
  4. Address review comments in new commits (with Link Work Item…), push again.
  5. After approval, complete the pull request. Switch to main, pull, delete the branch, build.

docs.title: Phase 7: Beyond your environment (general practice)
docs.text:
1. The pipeline builds main and publishes the deployable package.
  2. The release manager deploys that package to the sandbox through Lifecycle Services or the Power Platform admin center; testers verify #4711 there.
  3. Production follows by the team's change process.

F&O Studio's part ends at phase 6. See Environments and Promotion.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Phase Agent Example prompt What it does 2 F&O Developer "Work item 4711: add an order status enum (Open, On hold, Released) to SalesTable and its form in ContosoExtensions, and stop invoicing in SalesFormLetter when the status is On hold. Follow the team rules." Reads the standard elements, finds a precedent, plans the elements, creates them with xpp_create_object / xpp_update_object and labels with xpp_create_label, builds with xpp_build and runs xpp_check_best_practice. 2 F&O Test Engineer "Write and run tests for the order status validation." Writes SysTest classes and runs them. 5 F&O Code Reviewer "Review this branch against main." Lists the changes with xpp_diff_changes, runs best practice, performance and security checks, checks next calls and the team rules; read-only. 6-7 F&O Release Manager "Summarize the risk of this change for the sandbox release." Runs the checks, summarizes xpp_diff_changes with database sync and security impact; asks before xpp_package; never deploys to production. 7 F&O Release Notes "Write release notes for work item 4711 for the sales team." Reads the changes, commit messages and linked work items and writes user-facing notes.

Checkpoints:

  • Run Start Copilot Checkpoint before the developer agent changes elements, so you can revert its changes (see Copilot Checkpoints and Scope).
  • Read every element the agent created before you commit; the project view's A and M marks show which.
  • The agents do not commit, push or link work items: you do that with Link Work Item… and the Source Control view.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Work item opened and set to Active; branch created from the latest main.
  • [ ] Model built after switching branches.
  • [ ] Elements created as extensions; every wrapper calls next; texts are labels.
  • [ ] Build without errors; tests written.
  • [ ] Every commit mentions #4711.
  • [ ] Deployed to your UDE with a module sync; tests pass on the deployed code.
  • [ ] Review My Changes clean; Pre-Deploy Checklist passed.
  • [ ] Pull request with the review report and the linked work item; pipeline green.
  • [ ] After merge: branch deleted, main pulled and built.

docs.title: Scenario: Investigate why a record looks wrong
docs.text:
This walkthrough is for functional consultants and developers who get the question "why does this record look like this?": a sales order total that is too high, an invoice with an unexpected discount, a voucher on the wrong account. At the end you know which data, setup or code produced the value, you have the evidence (records, fields, values) to show the user, and you know whether the fix is setup, data or code.

F&O Studio gives you the database (read-only by default), the table relations from the metadata, and the standard code that computes the values, side by side.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
A sales clerk in company USMF reports: "Sales order 001234 for customer US-004 shows a total of 1,095.00 in Totals, but the order has two lines of 500.00 each. Why is it 95.00 more?"

The total of a sales order is more than the line amounts: charges (on the header and on lines), sales tax, and the discounts and prices that trade agreements set on each line all play a part. You need to find out which one it is here.

Standard objects involved:

Object Role SalesTable order header: CustAccount, CurrencyCode, InclTax, TaxGroup, PriceGroupId, LineDisc, MultiLineDisc, EndDisc, DiscPercent SalesLine lines: ItemId, SalesQty, SalesPrice, PriceUnit, LineDisc, LinePercent, MultiLnDisc, MultiLnPercent, SalesMarkup, LineAmount, TaxGroup, TaxItemGroup MarkupTrans charges, linked to the header or a line by TransTableId and TransRecId: MarkupCode, MarkupCategory, Value MarkupAutoTable automatic charges setup PriceDiscTable trade agreements: Relation, ItemRelation, AccountRelation, Amount, Percent1, FromDate, ToDate, QuantityAmountFrom SalesTotals, SalesLine.calcLineAmount the code that adds it all up

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A development or sandbox environment where the problem can be seen, with the data. Never investigate by changing production data.
  • Database access from F&O Studio (see Database Access):
  • on a UDE or sandbox: Request Database Credentials. It asks for a reason ("Why do you need access to the database? The reason is recorded with the request."), the allowed IPv4 addresses and the access: Reader ("Read data only (recommended)") or Writer. Choose Reader. The credentials stay in VS Code's secret storage until they expire;
  • on cloud-hosted and VHD environments: the local AxDB with Windows authentication, nothing to request.
  • Optional: the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, so Copilot agents can read the record as users see it in the client.

docs.title: Phase 1: Get the exact facts
docs.text:
1. Write down the record and the context: company (USMF), order (001234), what the user sees (Totals shows 1,095.00), what they expected (1,000.00), and when it started.
  2. If the user saw a message (for example a warning when confirming), copy it exactly. You use it in Phase 6.
  3. Run Test Database Connection to make sure F&O Studio can reach the database. See Database Access.

docs.title: Phase 2: Look at the header
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer, right-click the table SalesTable and choose Browse Table Data (also in the table's designer). See Browse Table Data.
  2. In the data panel:
  3. set Company to USMF;
  4. add a column filter SalesId = 001234;
  5. keep the row limit low; Refresh.
  6. Select the row. The record inspector on the right shows every field with its label, enum values with their names, and links to related rows (from the table relations in the metadata). Type in Field to filter the fields.
  7. Note CurrencyCode, InclTax (are prices including tax?), TaxGroup, PriceGroupId, EndDisc and DiscPercent. A total discount or a price group can explain a lot.
  8. Click the relation link to CustTable (the order customer) in the inspector to open the customer row: check its price group and discount groups against what the order has. The header also links to the charges group (MarkupGroup), which Phase 4 needs.

docs.title: Phase 3: Look at the lines
docs.text:
1. Browse SalesLine with the company USMF and the filter SalesId = 001234. (The inspector's relation links follow the relations the browsed table defines, so they lead from a line to its order, not the other way.)
  2. For each line compare:
  3. SalesQty × SalesPrice ÷ PriceUnit (a price unit of 100 where the user assumed 1 is a classic);
  4. LineDisc and LinePercent (line discount), MultiLnDisc and MultiLnPercent (multiline discount);
  5. SalesMarkup (line charges included in the line);
  6. LineAmount, the result.
  7. Click Open as SQL to turn the view into an editable query, and narrow it to the columns you compare:
SELECT SALESID, LINENUM, ITEMID, SALESQTY, SALESPRICE, PRICEUNIT,
       LINEDISC, LINEPERCENT, MULTILNDISC, MULTILNPERCENT, SALESMARKUP, LINEAMOUNT
FROM SALESLINE
WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf' AND SALESID = '001234'

Run it with Run (Ctrl+Enter). The query is read-only by default: one SELECT, always rolled back. See SQL Query Panel. 4. If the line amounts add up to 1,000.00, the difference is outside the lines: charges or tax.

docs.title: Phase 4: Find the charges
docs.text:
1. Run New SQL Query and look for charges on the header and on the lines. MarkupTrans points to its parent by table ID and record ID:
SELECT m.MARKUPCODE, m.MARKUPCATEGORY, m.VALUE, m.CURRENCYCODE, m.TRANSTABLEID, m.TRANSRECID
FROM MARKUPTRANS m
WHERE m.DATAAREAID = 'usmf'
  AND (m.TRANSRECID = (SELECT RECID FROM SALESTABLE WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf' AND SALESID = '001234')
       OR m.TRANSRECID IN (SELECT RECID FROM SALESLINE WHERE DATAAREAID = 'usmf' AND SALESID = '001234'))

Check that TRANSTABLEID belongs to SalesTable or SalesLine (record IDs are unique per table, not across tables). 2. In the example the result is one header charge FREIGHT with value 95.00. That is the difference. 3. Find where it came from. Browse MarkupAutoTable (automatic charges) for the customer, its charges group, or "all"; enum fields show their names next to the values, so you can read the account and item codes. 4. If you need the query plan of a slow investigation query, use Explain Plan. See Explain Plan.

docs.title: Phase 5: Check prices and discounts when the lines are off
docs.text:
If Phase 3 showed a line amount you didn't expect, look at trade agreements:

  1. Browse PriceDiscTable with filters on ItemRelation (the item, or its item group), AccountRelation (the customer, or its price or discount group) and the date window FromDate / ToDate. Relation shows its enum name (price, line discount, multiline discount, total discount).
  2. Check QuantityAmountFrom: a quantity break can switch the price.
  3. Compare the order's date with FromDate and ToDate: an agreement that started or ended recently is a common cause.

docs.title: Phase 6: Read the code that computes the value
docs.text:
1. Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O), type t:SalesLine, open it, and find calcLineAmount in the code view (Outline or Ctrl+Shift+O). See Open Element and X++ Code View.
  2. F12 on calls follows the logic; hover shows labels and signatures. See Go to Definition and Hover.
  3. For totals, open the class SalesTotals (charges through calcMarkupForTable, tax through getTax).
  4. Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) on a standard method shows Chain of Command classes and handlers from your own and ISV models that run too. A custom wrapper can be the reason a value differs from standard. See Implementations and Chain of Command.
  5. If the user saw a message, run Find Message Source (Dynamics 365 view > Find) and paste it as shown, values included. It lists the labels and the code that raises it. For "Field '…' must be filled in." it lists the mandatory table fields with that label first. See Find Message Source.
  6. If reading isn't enough, reproduce the order on the environment and debug: a breakpoint in SalesLine.calcLineAmount or in your wrapper. See Scenario: Debug Standard Code on UDE.

docs.title: Phase 7: Conclude and fix
docs.text:
1. Write the answer in the user's terms: "The order total includes an automatic freight charge of 95.00 from the automatic charges setup for all customers. It is added when the order is created."
  2. Show the evidence: the MarkupTrans row, the MarkupAutoTable row, the menu path of the setup.
  3. Decide the fix:
  4. setup: change or limit the automatic charge (functional);
  5. data: correct this order in the client (remove the charge), never in SQL: SQL changes skip X++ business logic;
  6. code: a custom wrapper computes it wrong; hand it to a developer with the method and the condition.
  7. Use Copy Database Connection Detail or Open Database in SQL Server Management Studio if a colleague needs to look too. See Open in SSMS.
  8. When done, run Forget Database Credentials on a shared machine.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Data Investigator in the agent picker. It is read-only, answers in business terms, and investigates one record at a time.

Sales order 001234 in USMF shows a total of 1,095.00 in Totals, but its two lines are 500.00 each. Find out where the extra 95.00 comes from and which setup caused it.

What it does:

Step Tool Reads the order, lines and charges as users see them, when connected Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server (data_*, form_*) Otherwise reads the database on a development environment: one read-only SELECT per call, after your confirmation xppQueryData Reads the table relations to join correctly xpp_read_object Finds the setup and code that produced the values xpp_find_object, xpp_read_object, xpp_find_references

Checkpoints:

  • Every database query shows a confirmation, Run a read-only query on the environment database, with the SQL. Read it before you allow it. The query runs read-only (SELECT only, rolled back), filters by company (DATAAREAID = 'usmf', lower case), returns 50 rows by default and at most 500. The agent never sees the credentials. If it answers that there is no database access, run Request Database Credentials yourself.
  • The agent keeps queries narrow: specific records, few columns, row limits.
  • Its answer: what happened to the record, step by step, with the evidence and the setup or action that caused it, and how to correct it.

Then:

  • Handoff Check the setup switches to F&O Setup Advisor: "Check the automatic charges setup for USMF and tell me which rule adds freight to every order." It reads the setup and gives a checklist: setting, current value, expected value, impact, fix. It changes setup only with your permission and never in production.
  • If the user had an error message, start with F&O Functional Triage instead: "A user gets 'Field 'Customer group' must be filled in.' when creating a customer in USMF." It finds the cause and hands code causes to F&O Support.
  • If the cause is code, F&O Support finds the condition in the code: "SalesLine.LineAmount on order 001234 line 2 is 10 percent lower than the trade agreement price. Which code sets it?"

See Agents for Functional Consultants.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Exact facts: company, record, what the user sees, what they expected, the message text.
  • [ ] Database access with Reader credentials (UDE, sandbox) or local AxDB.
  • [ ] Header checked: currency, tax inclusion, price group, discounts.
  • [ ] Lines checked: quantity, price, price unit, discounts, charges, line amount.
  • [ ] Charges found (MarkupTrans) and traced to their setup.
  • [ ] Trade agreements checked when line prices or discounts are off.
  • [ ] Code read (and custom wrappers found) when data and setup don't explain it.
  • [ ] Answer written in business terms with the evidence; fix classified as setup, data or code.
  • [ ] No data changed in SQL; corrections made in the client.

docs.title: Scenario: Onboard to an existing codebase
docs.text: This walkthrough is for a developer who joins a team with an existing D365FO codebase, or a consultant who inherits a customer's custom models. At the end your machine has the team's packages linked and built, you know which models exist and how they depend on each other, where the code hooks into the standard application, what the team's rules are, and where the risky parts are. You can make your first change on day one.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
You join a team that keeps its X++ code in an Azure DevOps repository:

ContosoErp/
  .xpp/
    agent-rules.md        team rules for Copilot
    sod-rules.json        the team's segregation-of-duties rules
    workspace.json        the packages of the repository
  Metadata/
    ContosoCore/          package: shared tables, EDTs, labels
      Descriptor/
      ContosoCore/
    ContosoExtensions/    package: extensions of standard sales and customer processes
      Descriptor/
      ContosoExtensions/
  Projects/
    ContosoExtensions/ContosoExtensions.rnrproj

ContosoExtensions references ContosoCore. Nobody wrote down what the extensions do; the people who built them left. Your first task will be a change to how sales orders are validated.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A development environment set up for F&O Studio: a UDE connected with Connect to Environment…, or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment. See Scenario: Set Up a New Developer Machine.
  • Access to the repository (VS Code's Git signs you in when it clones).
  • The repository URL, for example https://dev.azure.com/contoso/erp/_git/ContosoErp.
  • Optional: GitHub Copilot for the F&O Code Archaeologist and F&O Architect agents.

docs.title: Phase 1: Get the team's packages on your machine
docs.text:
1. Run Open Team Repository… (Dynamics 365 view > Model and project, or the command palette). It is a preview feature. See Open Team Repository.
  2. Choose Clone a Repository… and paste the URL (it must start with https:// or git@), then pick the folder to clone into. VS Code's Git extension clones it with its sign-in. If you cloned it already, choose Use a Folder Already on This Machine….
  3. F&O Studio finds the packages: the ones listed in .xpp/workspace.json, or else every folder (up to four levels deep) that has a Descriptor folder with model descriptors. Pick the packages to link; all are selected.
  4. Each package is linked into your custom metadata folder with a junction, the way teams set up Visual Studio. If a folder of that name already exists there and is not a link to this repository, it is left as it is and the summary says so.
  5. If the repository has no .xpp/workspace.json, F&O Studio writes one with the packages you picked. Commit it, so the next developer gets the same set.
  6. F&O Studio builds the packages in dependency order (here ContosoCore before ContosoExtensions; references to standard packages are already built). Progress shows per package; build errors go to Problems.
  7. The summary says how many packages were linked and whether all built, and offers Deploy and Synchronize Database (only Synchronize Database on cloud-hosted and VHD). On a UDE, deploy so the environment runs the team's code: Deploy runs Deploy Models to Environment; pick both packages and a Module sync. See Deploy to Environment.
  8. If the repository has projects (*.rnrproj), F&O Studio opens one (it asks which when there are several). Each project opens in its own workspace with its project and model folders. See D365FO Projects.

docs.title: Phase 2: Map the landscape
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer, run Switch to Model View (Elements by Model). Models show by display name; expand ContosoCore and ContosoExtensions to see what each contains by type.
  1. Run View Model Dependencies… and pick ContosoExtensions. The diagram shows which models it references. A custom model that depends on many standard models touches many areas. See Models and Model Dependencies.
  1. Use Filter Application Explorer… with the team's prefix (Contoso) in the classic view to see every custom element grouped by type, next to the standard ones.
  2. Note the counts per type: many extensions and Chain of Command classes mean a model that changes standard behaviour; many tables and forms mean a model that adds its own module.

docs.title: Phase 3: Read the team's rules
docs.text:
1. Open .xpp/agent-rules.md. It holds the team's naming, model, code, security and review rules, and Copilot follows it. If there is none, create it with Create Team Rules for Copilot and agree on it with the team. See Team Rules.
  2. If xpp.security.sodRulesFile points to .xpp/sod-rules.json, those are the team's segregation-of-duties rules; Check Segregation of Duties uses them instead of the built-in rules. See Segregation of Duties.
  3. Ask which branch pull requests go into and set xpp.git.baseBranch, so Review My Changes and the project view's Git marks compare with it. See Branching and Team Workflow.

docs.title: Phase 4: Find where the code hooks into standard
docs.text:
Your first task is about sales order validation, so start there.

  1. Open SalesTable (Open Element…, Ctrl+Alt+O, type t:SalesTable) and go to validateWrite in the code view.
  2. The code lens above the method shows references, overrides, Chain of Command classes and handlers. Click it, or use Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12), to list the team's wrappers and handlers next to Microsoft's. See Code Lens and Implementations and Chain of Command.
  3. Run Show Extensions and Handlers… on SalesTable for the full list: table extensions, Chain of Command classes, and event handlers on its form and data events (the cross-reference database doesn't record those; F&O Studio's own event handler index does).

  1. Open each wrapper of the team and read what it does before and after next.
  2. For the team's own classes, right-click and choose View Hierarchy (base and derived classes) and View References (who uses it). View Dependencies shows what an element uses. Each diagram exports Mermaid. See Hierarchy and Reference Diagrams.
  3. For custom tables, View Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) shows the relations; choose the levels, direction and fields. See Entity Relationship Diagram.
  4. Find References on a custom element lists every user from the cross-reference database, with the calling code. See Find All References.

docs.title: Phase 5: Learn why the code is the way it is
docs.text:
1. Right-click a custom element and choose View History. Pick a commit to see its code change; the commit message often names the work item. See Element History.
  2. If commit messages name work items (#123), Open Work Item… opens them in Azure Boards. See Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration.
  3. Compare Code… a team class with the standard class it was copied from, when you suspect a copy of standard code. See Compare Code and Metadata.

docs.title: Phase 6: Take a health check
docs.text:
These reports show where the risk is, before you change anything.

  1. Upgrade Readiness on each team model (right-click the model in the Application Explorer): obsolete API uses, extensions that no longer match the installed application, collisions with other models. See Upgrade Readiness.
  2. Analyze Performance on the team's busiest classes. See Analyze Performance.
  3. Run Best Practice Checks on Project on the project you opened. See Best Practice Checks.
  4. Find Security Gaps on the team models, and the Security view's Your roles to see the team's roles and the standard roles they extend, with their license. See Security View.
  5. Find Unused Labels… on the team's label files, to see how tidy the model is. See Label Tools.
  6. Keep the reports: Export Report… in the Results view.

docs.title: Phase 7: Look at the data
docs.text:
1. Right-click a custom table and choose Browse Table Data (database access needed; see Database Access). Use the company filter and the record inspector, which follows relations to the related rows. See Browse Table Data.
  2. Check which companies use the team's features and how much data there is. That tells you how careful a change must be.

docs.title: Phase 8: Make your first change
docs.text:
1. Create a branch in the Source Control view.
  2. Make the change, Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B), run the tests.
  3. Run Link Work Item… so the commit names the work item.
  4. Run Review My Changes before you open the pull request. See Scenario: Review a Pull Request.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Code Archaeologist in the agent picker. It explains legacy and unfamiliar custom code: what a model or element does, how it hooks into standard, dead code and leftovers from upgrades. It is read-only.

Example prompts:

  • "Explain the model ContosoExtensions: what it adds, what it extends, and how it hooks into the sales order process. Draw the main flow."
  • "What do the team's wrappers of SalesTable.validateWrite check, and in which order do they run?"
  • "Find dead code in ContosoCore: elements and methods nothing references, obsolete calls, and copies of standard code that an extension point would replace."

What it does:

Step Tool Maps the model: object counts per type, then names per type xpp_list_model_objects Model details and dependencies xpp_get_model_info Follows the entry points (menu items, wrappers, handlers, batch jobs) and reads the code xpp_read_object Traces callers and users xpp_find_references Obsolete calls xpp_find_deprecations

Its answer: what the model does in plain words, how it hooks into standard (entry points and wrappers), a Mermaid diagram of the main flow, risks, and clean-up candidates with evidence. The handoff Clean up switches to F&O Developer for the dead code it found (start a checkpoint first; see Scenario: Work Safely with Copilot).

For the bigger picture, pick F&O Architect:

  • "Look at the models in this environment (ContosoCore, ContosoExtensions) and recommend whether the split and dependencies make sense. What would you change before the team grows?"

It inspects the landscape with xpp_list_models and xpp_get_model_info and answers with options, trade-offs and a recommendation.

For functional context, F&O Functional Explainer explains a form, field or process in business terms: "What does the field Credit review required on the customer form do, and which setup drives it?"

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Environment set up; repository cloned and its packages linked with Open Team Repository….
  • [ ] .xpp/workspace.json in the repository (committed).
  • [ ] All packages built in dependency order; deployed (UDE) with a module sync.
  • [ ] Models and their dependencies understood (model view, View Model Dependencies…).
  • [ ] Team rules read (.xpp/agent-rules.md, SoD rules); xpp.git.baseBranch set.
  • [ ] Entry points into standard found for your first task (code lens, implementations, extensions and handlers).
  • [ ] Health check reports kept (upgrade readiness, performance, best practice, security).
  • [ ] First change on its own branch, linked to its work item, reviewed with Review My Changes.
