docs.title: Scenario: Performance Tuning a Slow Process
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers asked to make a slow business process faster. It goes from a user's complaint to a measured fix: capture a trace, find the hot spot, review the code statically, look at the database, change the code, and measure again.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Posting a sales invoice for an order with 300 lines takes four minutes in your UDE. Last month it took under one minute. Since then the team added a Chain of Command class SalesInvoiceJournalPost_ContosoExtensions_Extension in the ContosoExtensions model that writes a row to a custom table ContosoInvoiceLog for every invoice line, and reads ContosoInvoiceLog again to check for duplicates.

You suspect the extension, but you want evidence before you change anything, and a number to compare after the fix.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Need Why A connected environment (Connect-to-Environment) Metadata for the static analysis and the trace's code links. A web client trace (.etl) of the slow posting The trace analyzer reads it; no Trace Parser and no import database. Database access (optional) Database Performance Insights and Explain Plan. See Database-Access. The ContosoExtensions project To change, build and deploy the fix. A UDE or sandbox with realistic data Never tune on production; never change data there.

The trace analyzer needs the event manifests (*.man). It looks in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring (UDE), AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring and the registered trace providers. If it reports "No event manifests (*.man) found", set xpp.trace.manifestFolder to the folder that holds DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man. See Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: Phase 1: Reproduce and capture a trace
docs.text:
1. In the web client of the UDE, start a trace (Settings > Trace in the client), post the invoice for the 300-line order, then stop the trace and download the .etl file.
  2. Write down the baseline: the order, the number of lines, the duration, the company, and the time (UTC) you posted.
  3. Keep the trace short. A trace covers every AOS and session that ran while it recorded, including other users, batch and integrations.

docs.title: Phase 2: Find the hot spot in the trace
docs.text:
1. Run Analyze Trace… (Dynamics 365 view > Analyze, or right-click the .etl file in the VS Code Explorer) and pick the file.
  2. The panel lists the requests on a timeline per AOS and thread, with UTC times, and every AOS and session with its user. Click your session to filter on it, so other users and batch work drop out.
  3. Open the slowest request. Look at:
  4. hot methods: methods by exclusive time;
  5. call tree: the path from the request to the hot method; calls the report leaves out load when you expand a call or click Show N more calls;
  6. SQL per method: the statements each method ran, with their count and time;
  7. pauses: gaps where nothing ran.
  8. In the example, the call tree under SalesInvoiceJournalPost shows SalesInvoiceJournalPost_ContosoExtensions_Extension with 300 calls, and the SQL view shows one SELECT and one INSERT on CONTOSOINVOICELOG per line: 600 round trips.
  9. Click the method to open its code. A kernel class has no X++ code to open; the panel says so.

See Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: Phase 3: Static review of the code
docs.text:
1. Right-click SalesInvoiceJournalPost_ContosoExtensions_Extension in the project view and choose Analyze Performance (also in the code view's context menu, and in the Dynamics 365 view > Analyze).
  2. The message says how many findings, how many warnings and in how many methods. Click Show Problems. Each finding is in Problems on the line, with source X++ performance, the rule and the fix.
  3. Typical findings for this pattern:
Finding Fix Query inside a loop Read once before the loop, or join. Row-by-row insert inside a loop Collect rows in a RecordInsertList, or use insert_recordset. select firstonly inside while select Use a join or exists join. forupdate without a write Drop forupdate. Unbalanced ttsbegin/ttscommit Balance them in the same method.
  1. Run it on the table ContosoInvoiceLog too: it reports missing indexes and cache settings, and set-based statements that would silently run row by row because the table overrides insert, has delete actions or is date-effective.
  2. Run it on standard objects you call, if the trace points there. Findings on standard code are context, not your fix.

See Analyze-Performance and Performance-Rules-Reference.

docs.title: Phase 4: Look at the database
docs.text:
1. Run Database Performance Insights (Dynamics 365 view > Data > Performance Insights…). Pick one of the four read-only queries:
Insight What it shows Missing indexes Indexes SQL Server would have used, by estimated benefit. Add them as table indexes in your model, not in SQL. Most expensive queries (last 24 hours) From Query Store: total duration, executions, slowest run and the query text. Slowest batch jobs (last 7 days) Runs, average and longest duration per job and company. Number sequences that serialize work Continuous sequences and non-continuous ones without preallocation.
  1. In the example, Missing indexes suggests an index on CONTOSOINVOICELOG by invoice ID and line number, and Most expensive queries lists the SELECT on CONTOSOINVOICELOG with thousands of executions.
  2. Select the query in the SQL panel and use Explain Plan to see the plan: a scan instead of a seek confirms the missing index. See Explain-Plan and Database-Performance-Insights.
  3. If the process is a form rather than posting, Telemetry Queries (Application Insights KQL) on the form gives KQL for the slowest forms and X++ exceptions, filtered to that form. See Telemetry-Queries.

docs.title: Phase 5: Fix
docs.text:
1. Decide the fix from the evidence. Here:
  2. add an index on ContosoInvoiceLog (InvoiceId, LineNum) in the table designer, as an alternate key if the pair is unique;
  3. read the existing log rows for the invoice once, before the line loop, instead of once per line;
  4. collect the new rows in a RecordInsertList and insert them once per invoice.
  5. Open the code view and make the change. Use Find Similar Standard Implementations with "RecordInsertList" or the snippets for transactions with retry if you want a standard precedent. See Find-Similar-Implementations and Snippets.
RecordInsertList logRows = new RecordInsertList(tableNum(ContosoInvoiceLog));
// ... inside the loop, instead of logRow.insert():
logRows.add(logRow);
// ... after the loop:
logRows.insertDatabase();
  1. Check that the wrapper still calls next and keeps the same transaction scope. A Chain of Command wrapper that skips next changes standard behaviour.
  2. Run Analyze Performance again: the loop findings are gone.
  3. Run Build Project. On a UDE, run Deploy Models to Environment with database sync Module, because the table got a new index. See Deploy-to-Environment and Synchronize-Database. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, use Synchronize Table(s) with the Database on the table instead; the build restarts the local AOS for you (xpp.build.restartLocalAos).

docs.title: Phase 6: Measure again
docs.text:
1. Post the same kind of invoice (same number of lines, same company) and capture a new trace.
  2. Run Analyze Trace… on it and compare: the request duration, the calls of your wrapper, the SQL count on CONTOSOINVOICELOG.
  3. Run Most expensive queries again later to see the query drop out of the top list.
  4. Write the before/after numbers in the work item or pull request.

docs.title: Phase 7: Keep it from coming back
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes: it includes performance findings for every changed element. See Review-My-Changes.
  2. The Pre-Deploy Checklist counts performance warnings for the project's classes, tables, forms and data entities. See Pre-Deploy-Checklist.
  3. Add the rule to .xpp/agent-rules.md (for example "No database calls inside per-line loops in posting extensions") so Copilot follows it. See Team-Rules.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
F&O Performance (read-only) finds why it is slow and ranks the fixes:

Sales invoice posting for a 300-line order takes 4 minutes on our UDE. Here is the trace: C:\Traces\invoice-300-lines.etl. Find the slowest request, the hot methods and the repeated SQL, run the static analysis on the ContosoExtensions classes involved and on ContosoInvoiceLog, and check the indexes. Rank the fixes by expected gain.

What it does: xpp_analyze_trace on the file (slowest requests, hot methods, SQL by total time), then again with session, user or method to narrow it; xpp_analyze_performance on the classes and the table; xpp_read_object for the indexes; xppQueryData for row counts on the UDE after you confirm the query. The answer lists each finding with where, why (evidence), the fix and how to measure it.

Use the handoff Implement the fixes to switch to F&O Developer:

Implement fixes 1 and 2: add the InvoiceId+LineNum index to ContosoInvoiceLog, read the existing log rows once per invoice and insert the new rows with a RecordInsertList. Keep the next call and the transaction as they are. Build, run the best practice checks and the performance analysis again.

Before that, run Start Copilot Checkpoint and Set Copilot Scope… to the extension class and the table. Follow the calls in Copilot Activity. See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.

F&O Code Reviewer checks the result before merge:

Review the changes on this branch against main, focused on the posting extension: next calls, transactions, set-based fallbacks and anything that runs per line.

Checkpoints: - Every finding cites the trace or the analysis (method, SQL, count), not a guess. - The wrapper still calls next. - xpp_analyze_performance returns no warnings for the changed class. - The second trace shows the drop.

Agents don't capture traces or post invoices; you do that in the web client.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Baseline recorded: process, volume, duration, company, UTC time.
  • [ ] Trace captured and analyzed; your session filtered.
  • [ ] Hot method and repeated SQL identified.
  • [ ] Analyze Performance run on the classes and tables involved.
  • [ ] Database insights and Explain Plan checked.
  • [ ] Fix built; Chain of Command still calls next.
  • [ ] Deployed with Module sync (new index) or tables synchronized locally.
  • [ ] Second trace taken; before/after numbers recorded.
  • [ ] Review My Changes shows no performance warnings.

docs.title: Scenario: Prepare and ship a release
docs.text:
This walkthrough is for the developer or lead who takes a finished change set from a feature branch to a deployable package. At the end you have a change set that builds without errors, passed best practice, performance and security checks, ran its tests on a unified developer environment (UDE), and a deployable package (.zip) with a version number that your release process can take to a sandbox and, later, to production.

F&O Studio covers everything up to and including the package and the deploy to development and test environments. Uploading the package to Lifecycle Services (LCS) or the Power Platform admin center and the production deployment follow your team's process outside F&O Studio.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Your team works in the model ContosoExtensions (package ContosoExtensions) in a Git repository. Sprint work for work item 4711 "Credit review flag on customers" is done on the branch feature/credit-review:

  • a table extension CustTable.ContosoExtensions with a new field ContosoCreditReviewRequired;
  • a form extension CustTable.ContosoExtensions that shows the field on the customer form;
  • a Chain of Command class CustTable_Contoso_Extension that wraps CustTable.validateWrite;
  • a display menu item ContosoCustCreditReviewList and its form ContosoCustCreditReviewList;
  • a privilege ContosoCustCreditReviewListView.

The release goes to the team's UDE for a test round, then a deployable package goes to the test sandbox. You want to be sure nothing is missing before you hand the package over.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A UDE connected with Connect to Environment… (see Connect to Environment), or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (see Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments). Deploy, Run Tests and Synchronize Database through Dataverse are UDE-only.
  • The D365FO project of the change open (Open D365FO Project…, see D365FO Projects). The Pre-Deploy Checklist needs it.
  • Your model folder in a Git repository. Review My Changes and Show Changed Elements read Git. If the packages are linked into the metadata folder with junctions (as Open Team Repository… sets them up), F&O Studio follows the links to the repository.
  • Optional: xpp.git.baseBranch set to your main branch (for example main), so you are not asked every time.
  • Optional: GitHub Copilot, for the F&O Release Manager agent and its tools.

docs.title: Phase 1: Know exactly what ships
docs.text:
1. Run Show Changed Elements from the command palette (category F&O Studio). It lists every element of your models that changed in Git: uncommitted changes, plus everything the branch changed since it left xpp.git.baseBranch. Each entry shows the element type, the Git letter (M modified, A added, D deleted, R renamed) and (branch) when the change is already committed. Pick an entry to open its designer. See Show Changed Elements.
  2. Compare the list with what you expect. In the example you expect the five elements above. If you see an element you did not mean to change (for example a label file touched by accident), fix it in Git before you go on.
  3. Look at the project view. It marks changed elements with the same letters and Git colours, so you can spot uncommitted work. See Git Changes in the Project View.
  4. Make sure the commits name the work item. Run Link Work Item… (Dynamics 365 view > Deploy, or the command palette) and enter 4711. F&O Studio adds #4711 (Azure Repos) or AB#4711 (GitHub linked to Azure Boards) to the commit message box of the Source Control view. Review My Changes later lists the work items it finds in the branch's commit messages. See Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration.

docs.title: Phase 2: Review the change set
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes (project view check menu, Dynamics 365 view > Build and check, or the command palette). It asks "Compare with this branch (empty: only uncommitted changes)" with xpp.git.baseBranch (or main) filled in. Press Enter.
  2. The report opens in the Results view with four sections:
  3. Pull request summary: the changed elements by type, the security impact (roles, duties or privileges that changed), new menu items that need a privilege, and the work items found in the commit messages.
  4. Chain of Command: wrappers that wrap a base method but never call next. In the example, if CustTable_Contoso_Extension.validateWrite forgot next validateWrite(), it shows here as an error, because the standard validation would be skipped.
  5. Best practice and compiler: xppbp results for the changed elements, plus errors and warnings in Problems.
  6. Performance: warnings of the static performance rules on changed classes, tables, forms and data entities.
  7. Click a finding to open the element at the method and line. Fix, save, then use Run Again on the report.
  8. When it is clean, use Copy Report as Markdown and paste the pull request summary into the pull request description. See Review My Changes and Results View.

docs.title: Phase 3: Build and check
docs.text:
1. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ editor, or click the project item in the status bar). Unsaved code views are saved first when xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild is on (the default). Errors go to the Problems view at the right line; a failed build offers Show Problems. See Build Project and Model and Compiler Diagnostics.
  2. Before a release, also run Build Model once. Build Project reports only the project's problems; Build Model covers every element of the model, including ones that are not in the project.
  3. Run Run Best Practice Checks on Project. It runs xppbp, the checker Visual Studio runs, and puts the warnings in Problems. The status bar shows the error and warning count for a few seconds. See Best Practice Checks.
  4. Run Analyze Performance on the classes that do real work (right-click in the project view, or from the code editor's context menu). In the example, check CustTable_Contoso_Extension and the list form. See Analyze Performance.
  5. Run Find Security Gaps (Security view title bar or Dynamics 365 view > Security). Pick ContosoExtensions. An error such as a menu item that no privilege covers blocks the release. In the example the new menu item must be in ContosoCustCreditReviewListView; if it is not, right-click the menu item and run Add to Privilege…. See Find Security Gaps and Add to Privilege.
  6. If the change wraps standard methods or the environment was updated recently, run Upgrade Readiness on the model (right-click the model in the Application Explorer, or Dynamics 365 view > Build and check). See Upgrade Readiness.

docs.title: Phase 4: Run the Pre-Deploy Checklist
docs.text:
1. Run Pre-Deploy Checklist (project view check menu or Dynamics 365 view > Build and check). It runs, in order, for the open project's model:
Step What it checks Blocks the release Build Builds the project's elements Yes, when the build fails Best practice xppbp on the project's elements Yes, when there are errors Performance Static performance warnings on classes, tables, forms and entities No, it reports the count Security Security gaps of the model (xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps) Yes, for gaps of severity Error Scratch code Run Snippet's scratch class <Model>ScratchRunner left in the model Yes Tests Reminder: run tests after deploying (UDE), or on the VM (cloud-hosted, VHD) No
  1. The report opens in the Results view with a pass or fail per step and the headline "Ready to package and deploy." or "Not ready: fix the failed steps first." See Pre-Deploy Checklist.
  2. If the scratch code step fails, open the project view and Delete the ContosoExtensionsScratchRunner class that Run Snippet in Environment left in the model. It would otherwise ship in the package. See Run Snippet.
  3. When every blocking step passes, F&O Studio shows "The checklist passed." with Create Deployment Package and, on a UDE, Deploy. Choose Deploy first if you want a test round on the UDE.

docs.title: Phase 5: Deploy to the team's UDE and test
docs.text:
1. Run Deploy Models to Environment (in the Dynamics 365 view it is "Deploy Models to Online Environment…" under Deploy). F&O Studio deploys the packages as they were built on this machine, through the environment's Dataverse, as Visual Studio does. Nothing is recompiled. See Deploy to Environment.
  2. Pick the packages under "Packages to deploy (as built on this machine)". Your project's package is preselected.
  3. Pick the database sync under "Database sync after deploy":
  4. None: no sync. Use it when no table, view or entity changed.
  5. Module: synchronizes the tables of the deployed packages. In the example the new field on CustTable needs at least this.
  6. Full: synchronizes the whole database. Slow; use it only when you have a reason.
  7. Watch the X++ Deploy output. Before uploading, F&O Studio builds and copies the C# projects the X++ project references, and converts the PDBs to portable PDBs so the debugger can read them.
  8. If you deployed with None and later find you need a sync, run Synchronize Database and choose Full or Module. See Synchronize Database.
  9. Check the status bar. The project item shows when the build is newer than the last deploy from this machine. Run Tests, the debugger and Verify Changes in the Running App warn you about that and offer Deploy First. See Status Bar.
  10. Run the tests: Run Tests from the project view check menu, or the VS Code Test Explorer. Tests run against the deployed code on the environment. See Run Tests and Test Explorer.
  11. Optional (preview): run Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot). It turns the changed menu items, form extensions and entity extensions into check steps (for example "Open form CustTable (through its menu item) and find the controls ...") and opens Copilot agent mode to run them with the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, read-only. See Verify Changes in Running App.

docs.title: Phase 6: Create the deployable package
docs.text:
1. Make sure the last build is the one you want to ship. Create Deployment Package uses the package as built.
  2. Run Create Deployment Package… (Dynamics 365 view > Deploy, or the command palette).
  3. Answer the three prompts:
  4. Create deployment package: packages: pick ContosoExtensions (you can pick several of your packages).
  5. Package version: defaults to 1.0.0.0; it must have four parts. Use your release number, for example 1.4.0.0.
  6. Output folder for the deployable package: a folder outside the metadata folder, for example a drop folder.
  7. F&O Studio runs RunPackageCreationAll.ps1 from the platform bin folder, the same script Visual Studio's Create Deployment Package runs, as a VS Code task named "Create deployment package". Watch the terminal for errors. See Create Deployment Package.
  8. Take the package to the next environment the way your team does it (for example upload to the LCS asset library, or the Power Platform admin center). This step is general D365FO practice; F&O Studio does not upload or apply packages to sandbox or production. See Environments and Promotion.

docs.title: Phase 7: Document the release
docs.text:
1. If roles, duties or privileges changed, run Security Report… and choose Roles of model… > ContosoExtensions and Markdown ("sign-off document") or CSV ("for Excel"). Attach it to the release for the security sign-off. See Security Report.
  2. In the Results view, use Export Report… on the Pre-Deploy Checklist and the Review My Changes report and keep them with the release.
  3. Ask the F&O Release Notes agent for user-facing notes (see below).

docs.title: Repeating releases with tasks
docs.text:
For the build and deploy part you can use tasks in .vscode/tasks.json instead of the commands. The deploy task deploys the package of the open project's model without asking which packages:

{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    { "type": "xpp", "action": "buildModel", "label": "Build model" },
    { "type": "xpp", "action": "deploy", "dbSync": "Module", "label": "Deploy with module sync",
      "dependsOn": "Build model" }
  ]
}

dbSync takes None, Module or Full. See Build Tasks.

docs.title: On cloud-hosted and VHD environments
docs.text:
• Deploy Models to Environment and Run Tests are hidden; the environment runs what you build. After a successful build, F&O Studio restarts the running AOS hosts so they load it (xpp.build.restartLocalAos).
  • Synchronize Database (command palette) runs a full sync of the local AxDB; Synchronize Table(s) with the Database syncs only the project's tables.
  • The Pre-Deploy Checklist tells you to run tests on the VM. Create Deployment Package works the same way.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Release Manager in the Copilot agent picker. It runs the checks, summarizes the change set with its risk and creates the package when you ask. It changes nothing and deploys nowhere without your permission, and only to development, sandbox or build environments, never to production.

Example prompts:

  • "Prepare the ContosoExtensions model for release. Compare the branch with main, run the build, best practice and security gaps, and give me a release summary with risks."
  • "The checks passed. Create the deployable package for ContosoExtensions with version 1.4.0.0."
  • "Which of the changes need a database sync, and which change security?"

What the agent does:

Step Tool Lists the changed elements against the base branch xpp_diff_changes Builds each model to release xpp_build Runs best practice xpp_check_best_practice Runs the tests on the UDE (it warns when the deployed code is older than the build) xppRunTests Checks security gaps xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps Creates the package, only when you asked for one xpp_package

Checkpoints for you:

  • Read the release summary: checks with results, changes with their risk (data model changes that need a sync, security changes, integrations, upgrade risks), package path, deployment steps and rollback notes.
  • The agent's tool calls show in the Copilot Activity view with their arguments and results. See Copilot Activity.
  • Before that, hand the branch to F&O Code Reviewer ("Review the changes on this branch against main"); its handoff Prepare the release brings you back to the Release Manager.
  • After the release, use the handoff Write release notes, or pick F&O Release Notes and ask: "Write release notes for the changes on feature/credit-review for the accounts receivable team." It groups the changes by business process and audience, with new setup and training notes.

See Agents for Developers and Copilot Agents.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Show Changed Elements lists only the elements you meant to change.
  • [ ] Commits name the work item (Link Work Item…).
  • [ ] Review My Changes: no Chain of Command wrapper without next, no best practice errors, performance warnings understood.
  • [ ] Build Model succeeds without errors.
  • [ ] Run Best Practice Checks on Project: no errors.
  • [ ] Find Security Gaps: no errors; every new menu item is in a privilege.
  • [ ] Pre-Deploy Checklist: "Ready to package and deploy."
  • [ ] No Run Snippet scratch class in the model.
  • [ ] Deployed to the UDE with the right database sync; tests pass against the deployed code.
  • [ ] Deployable package created with the right version from the last build.
  • [ ] Security report and release notes attached to the release.

docs.title: Scenario: Report from a scanned document
docs.text:
This walkthrough is for developers who must print a business document on a given layout: a vendor cheque on preprinted cheque stock, a purchase order or an invoice that has to match a sample from the business. At the end you have a copy of the standard report in your model with a precision design placed to the millimetre against the scan, one small hook that routes printing to it, a preview made with Microsoft's report engine, and a build that compiles the report for deployment.

You can do it by hand in the Report Designer, or let the F&O Report Builder agent do the measuring and placing. This page shows both.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Accounts payable prints vendor cheques from the payment journal on preprinted US cheque stock (Letter, 8.5 x 11 in): the bank's logo, the cheque frame, the MICR band area and the stub frames are already printed. The bank sent a new stock, and the fields that the standard Cheque_US report prints (date, amount, amount in words, payee name and address, cheque number, MICR line) no longer land in their boxes.

You have:

  • a 300 dpi scan of one blank sheet of the new stock, C:\Scans\cheque-stock.png;
  • a ruler measurement from the real sheet: the top edge of the sheet to the top of the amount box is 22 mm;
  • the model ContosoExtensions, where the copy of the report must go.

Facts from the standard application that matter here:

  • Cheque_US has one precision design, Report, and one dataset, Cheque_USDS, filled by the report data provider ChequeDP from the temporary table ChequeTmp (fields such as ChequeDate, AmountCur, AmountInWords, RecipientName, RecipientAddress, ChequeNum, MICRLine, Void).
  • Cheques don't use print management. ChequeController.determineReportMenuOutput picks the report from the cheque form type of the bank account's cheque layout (ChequeFormType::USStyle gives Cheque_US).
  • Standard reports can't be changed in place: you duplicate the report into your model and route printing to the copy.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A development environment (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD) with F&O Studio connected, and a project in ContosoExtensions (see D365FO Projects).
  • The scan as PNG, JPEG, TIFF or BMP. Export a PDF page as a 300 dpi image first.
  • The report preview runtime. The first preview asks you to accept Microsoft's licence and downloads Microsoft's Report Viewer runtime (about 15 MB) from nuget.org. You can install it ahead with Install Report Preview Runtime. F&O Studio doesn't ship it.
  • For the agent: GitHub Copilot. The agent's xpp_measure_image reads text with Windows' built-in OCR on this machine; nothing is uploaded.

docs.title: Phase 1: Decide what to create
docs.text:
Keep the element list short. For a cheque layout you need exactly two elements:

Element Why ContosoCheque_US, a copy of the report Cheque_US the new precision design; it keeps Microsoft's dataset from ChequeDP ChequeController_ContosoExtensions_Extension, a Chain of Command class on ChequeController routes US-style cheques to the copy

You don't need a new data provider, contract, controller, menu item or privilege: the standard cheque printing keeps running them. A table extension of ChequeTmp and a Chain of Command on ChequeDP are only needed when you print a field the standard data provider doesn't fill. For invoices, purchase orders and confirmations the hook is the print management registration instead (see Report Element Designer).

docs.title: Phase 2: Copy the standard report into your model
docs.text:
1. Open the report: Open Element… (Ctrl+Alt+O), type Cheque_US, Enter. Or find it in the Application Explorer under Reports.
  2. Right-click the report and choose Open Report Designer. A standard report opens read-only with a banner saying that it belongs to a model you can't change, and the button Duplicate into my model….
  3. Choose Duplicate into my model… (it runs Duplicate…, which you can also pick by right-clicking the report in the Application Explorer). Pick the model ContosoExtensions and enter the name ContosoCheque_US. F&O Studio creates the copy through the metadata API, adds it to the project and opens it.
  4. Open the copy in the Report Element Designer. Check that the dataset Cheque_USDS is still there with its Query SELECT * FROM ChequeDP.ChequeTmp. See Report Datasets.

docs.title: Phase 3: Lay the scan under the page
docs.text:
1. Right-click the precision design Report of ContosoCheque_US and choose Open Report Designer (or double-click it). See Report Designer.
  2. Check the page properties: paper Letter (215.9 x 279.4 mm), margins, body size. The designer warns when the body is wider than the page (that prints blank pages) and when items sit outside the body.
  3. Click the Scan overlay button (camera icon) and pick C:\Scans\cheque-stock.png. The scan lies under the page at the size of the paper it shows. The overlay is never saved in the report.
  4. In Scan overlay (not saved in the report) in the properties pane, set Paper to Letter, or type Width (mm) and Height (mm). Use Offset x (mm) and Offset y (mm) when the scan does not start at the sheet's corner, and the Opacity slider to see both the scan and the design.
  5. Check the scale with the Measure tool (ruler icon, or hold Alt and drag): measure from the top of the page to the top of the amount box. It must read 22 mm, as on the real sheet. If it doesn't, fix the overlay's size first. See Scan Overlay and Measure.

docs.title: Phase 4: Place the fields
docs.text:
1. Select a textbox, for example the one showing =Fields!AmountCur.Value, and drag it into the amount box of the scan. Arrow keys move by the grid, Ctrl+arrows by 0.1 mm, Shift+arrows resize.
  2. For each fixed field use what preprinted stock needs:
  3. Can grow and Can shrink off, so a long value never pushes the next field down (the designer warns about growing textboxes that push others);
  4. padding 0 pt;
  5. the font size you measured, amounts right-aligned.
  6. Remove items that the stock already prints (frames, captions, the bank logo). On preprinted stock you print only the data.
  7. Fonts: use only fonts D365FO renders. The designer warns about fonts D365FO doesn't offer and fonts that aren't installed on this machine (the preview substitutes them, the environment doesn't). The MICR line uses a MICR font such as MICR E13B 2.1.
  8. Drag more fields from the report data onto the page when the new stock has a field the old one didn't, for example RecipientAddress in a window envelope position.
  9. Save. The designer keeps the RDL's schema version, units and everything it doesn't edit.

docs.title: Phase 5: Preview with Microsoft's report engine
docs.text:
1. Click Preview. F&O Studio renders the design with Microsoft's report engine, the same hard page layout as PDF and print. See Report Preview.
  2. In the preview settings set Language, Company, Sample rows, Pages and Resolution (dpi). Under Data (JSON rows per dataset), each dataset has a box that takes a JSON array of rows; datasets left empty get generated sample rows. Enter the values printed on a real cheque in the Cheque_USDS box so the widths are realistic, for example:
[
  { "ChequeNum": "000123", "ChequeDate": "2026-11-25", "AmountCur": 1234.56,
    "AmountInWords": "One thousand two hundred thirty-four and 56/100",
    "RecipientName": "Contoso Supplies", "Void": "" }
]
  1. Turn on Show scan under the page and click Render to see the rendered page over the scan. Fix the positions in the designer and preview again until every field sits in its box.
  2. Read the warnings above the pages: they come from the engine and from the layout checks.

docs.title: Phase 6: Route cheque printing to the copy
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer, right-click the class ChequeController and choose Create Code Extension. Accept or change the name (it must end with _Extension). See Create Code Extension.
  2. Wrap determineReportMenuOutput. The standard method sets the protected member chequeReport from the cheque form type and returns it:
[ExtensionOf(classStr(ChequeController))]
final class ChequeController_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    protected str determineReportMenuOutput(ChequeFormType _chequeFormType, BankChequeLayout _bankChequeLayout)
    {
        str report = next determineReportMenuOutput(_chequeFormType, _bankChequeLayout);

        if (_chequeFormType == ChequeFormType::USStyle)
        {
            chequeReport = ssrsReportStr(ContosoCheque_US, Report);
            report = chequeReport;
        }
        return report;
    }
}
  1. Decide with the business whether every US-style layout should use the new stock. If only some bank accounts use it, add a condition (for example on _bankChequeLayout) instead of switching all of them.
  2. Peek the wrapper from the standard method with Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) to confirm it is picked up. See Implementations and Chain of Command.

docs.title: Phase 7: Build, deploy and print a test
docs.text:
1. Run Build Project. The build compiles the reports with Microsoft's reportsc into the package, as Visual Studio does, plus the controller extension. Fix every error. See Report Build and Build Project and Model.
  2. On a UDE, run Deploy Models to Environment (no database sync is needed for a report and a class). On cloud-hosted and VHD environments the build is what runs. See Deploy to Environment.
  3. In the client, print a test cheque from the bank account's cheque layout on plain paper and hold it over a sheet of the preprinted stock against the light. Print at actual size, never "fit to page".
  4. Confirm on the real printer. MICR lines in particular need a test on the bank's requirements; F&O Studio has not tested MICR on a real printer.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Report Builder in the agent picker. It turns the scan into the report: it measures the scan, decides between a new report and a copy of the standard one, lists the elements it will create before creating any, writes the precision design at the measured positions, renders it and compares it with the scan until every field lines up, then builds.

First prompt (give it what it can't see):

Build a vendor cheque layout from C:\Scans\cheque-stock.png. It is preprinted US cheque stock, Letter size, scanned at 300 dpi. From the top edge of the sheet to the top of the amount box is 22 mm. It replaces the standard US cheque for all bank accounts. Fields: date, amount, amount in words, payee name and address, cheque number, MICR line. Model: ContosoExtensions.

What the agent does:

Step Tool Measures the scan: scale, deskew, boxes, ruled lines, text lines in mm from the sheet's top-left corner, a mm grid picture; crops to areas for finer readings xpp_measure_image Reads the standard report's designs, datasets and item positions xpp_get_report_design on Cheque_US Copies the standard report into your model, then saves the precision design xpp_set_report_design (duplicateOf, modelName) Creates the Chain of Command class on ChequeController.determineReportMenuOutput xpp_create_object Renders the design with sample data that shows the values on the scan xpp_render_report Overlays the render on the scan and reports each textbox's offset in mm; repeats until every item is within 0.5 mm (or your tolerance) xpp_compare_layout Compiles the report and the class xpp_build

Checkpoints for you:

  • The agent asks first what it can't see: preprinted or plain paper, paper size, whether it replaces a standard document, which data each field shows, the target model, the scan's dpi, and one or two ruler measurements.
  • Before creating anything it lists the elements with one line each on why. If it proposes extras (a parameter to switch the layout, a label file, menu items), they are proposals; it doesn't create them unless you ask.
  • Start a checkpoint before you let it write (Start Copilot Checkpoint), so Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… undoes everything. Watch its calls in Copilot Activity. See Copilot Checkpoints and Scope.
  • Its answer lists the elements, the comparison result per field, and what you must still do: deploy, print a test on plain paper over the stock, confirm on the real printer at actual size, and fonts this machine doesn't have.
  • Open the result in the Report Designer yourself and check it with the scan overlay.

Follow-ups:

  • "Move the payee address 1.5 mm down and render again." (the agent re-renders and compares)
  • Handoff Review to the F&O Code Reviewer, or Release to the F&O Release Manager.
  • For a report that is not a layout copy (a new list report with its own data provider and contract), use the F&O Report Developer agent or the New Report… wizard (see Wizard Report).

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Elements kept to the minimum: the report copy and one routing hook.
  • [ ] The copy keeps the standard dataset and data provider.
  • [ ] Scan overlay at the right paper size; one ruler measurement checked with the Measure tool.
  • [ ] Fixed fields: no Can grow, padding 0, measured font size, amounts right-aligned.
  • [ ] Nothing printed that the stock already shows.
  • [ ] Only fonts D365FO renders; MICR font for the MICR line.
  • [ ] Preview with realistic data and the scan under the page: every field in its box.
  • [ ] Controller extension routes the right cheque form type (and only the right bank accounts).
  • [ ] Build compiles the report without errors; deployed.
  • [ ] Test print on plain paper over the stock at actual size; confirmed on the real printer.

docs.text:

docs.title: Scenario: Review a pull request
docs.text: This walkthrough is for the developer or lead who reviews a colleague's X++ pull request. A pull request of a D365FO change is a set of AOT XML files; reading them in a web diff is hard. F&O Studio turns the branch back into elements: which ones changed, their code in the X++ layout, their history, and the checks Visual Studio would run, plus a few it wouldn't. At the end you have a review with findings by element and method, ready to post on the pull request.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
A colleague opened a pull request from feature/credit-review into main for work item 4711 "Credit review flag on customers". The description says:

  • new field ContosoCreditReviewRequired on CustTable (table extension) and on the customer form (form extension);
  • validation in CustTable_Contoso_Extension.validateWrite (Chain of Command);
  • new list form ContosoCustCreditReviewList with a display menu item and a privilege;
  • a change to the role extension CustInvoiceAccountsReceivableClerk.ContosoExtensions that adds the privilege.

The team repository is set up on your machine with Open Team Repository…, so its packages are linked into your metadata folder. See Open Team Repository.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• The team repository cloned and linked (see Scenario: Onboard to an Existing Codebase).
  • VS Code's Git (Source Control view) to check out the pull request branch.
  • xpp.git.baseBranch set to main (or the branch pull requests go into). Review My Changes asks for it otherwise.
  • A development environment for building; a UDE if you also want to run the tests.
  • Optional: GitHub Copilot for the F&O Code Reviewer agent.

docs.title: Phase 1: Check out the branch
docs.text:
1. Commit or stash your own work first. Review My Changes also lists uncommitted changes, and you don't want yours in the review.
  2. In the Source Control view, check out feature/credit-review (or fetch the pull request branch the way your host offers).
  3. Run Refresh Application Explorer so the Application Explorer and designers read the branch's files. If the project of the change is in the repository, open it with Open D365FO Project…. See D365FO Projects.

docs.title: Phase 2: See what the pull request changes
docs.text:
1. Run Show Changed Elements. It lists the elements of your models that differ: committed on the branch since it left xpp.git.baseBranch (marked (branch)) and uncommitted ones. Each shows its type and Git letter: M modified, A added, D deleted, R renamed. See Show Changed Elements.
  2. Compare the list with the pull request description. Things to catch now:
  3. an element the description doesn't mention (an accidental change, a leftover test class);
  4. a deleted element that something else still uses;
  5. a change in a model that the work item has no business touching.
  6. In the project view, changed elements carry the same letters and Git colours; the tooltip says "on this branch" for committed changes. See Git Changes in the Project View.
  7. Read the requirement: run Open Work Item… and enter 4711 to open it in Azure Boards. For a GitHub repository, open it from Azure Boards (AB# mentions link there). See Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration.

docs.title: Phase 3: Run Review My Changes
docs.text:
1. Run Review My Changes and accept main. Despite the name, it reviews whatever is checked out: the branch since it left main, plus uncommitted changes. See Review My Changes.
  2. The Results view shows:
  3. Pull request summary: elements by type (new and deleted marked), the security impact ("... changed; check role licenses (Security view > Analyze License) and segregation of duties."), new menu items that need a privilege, and the work items named in the branch's commit messages. "none named in the commit messages" is itself a finding if your team links every commit.
  4. Chain of Command: wrappers that don't call next. CustTable_Contoso_Extension.validateWrite must call next validateWrite(); skipping it is only allowed for [Replaceable] methods.
  5. Best practice and compiler: xppbp results for the changed elements and the errors and warnings in Problems.
  6. Performance: static performance warnings in changed classes, tables, forms and data entities, including data entity readiness.
  7. Click a finding to open the element at the method and line. See Results View.

docs.title: Phase 4: Read the changes element by element
docs.text:
1. Open each changed element from Show Changed Elements or the project view. Classes open in the X++ code view (the declaration with the methods inside the braces, as Visual Studio shows them); other elements open in the element designer, where an extension shows the base element's nodes and its own nodes in bold. See X++ Code View and Element Designer.
  2. Right-click a changed element and choose View History. Pick a commit to see its change as a code diff (classes, tables, forms) or a metadata diff. Item buttons compare a commit with the current version or show the metadata (XML) changes. "Uncommitted changes" shows the working tree. See Element History.
  3. For metadata that has no code (the role extension, the menu item), use View History with the metadata view, or Compare Metadata… against another element. See Compare Code and Metadata.
  4. Check the impact of changed methods:
  5. Find All References (Shift+F12) on a changed method shows its callers from the cross-reference database. See Find All References.
  6. Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) on CustTable.validateWrite shows every wrapper and handler, including those of other models. Two models wrapping the same method can interfere. See Implementations and Chain of Command.
  7. Code lens above the methods shows references, overrides, Chain of Command classes and handlers. See Code Lens.
  8. For the form extension, open the form designer of CustTable and look at the preview with Show hidden controls and markers: it outlines what extensions added. Check that the new control sits where the description says. See Form Layout and Form Extensions.

docs.title: Phase 5: Build and run the checks yourself
docs.text:
1. Run Build Model on the changed model. The pull request must build on a clean machine, not only on the author's. See Build Project and Model.
  2. Run Find Security Gaps on the model: the new menu item must be in a privilege, the privilege in a duty or role. See Find Security Gaps.
  3. Because a role extension changed, run Analyze License on CustInvoiceAccountsReceivableClerk (Security view or Application Explorer) and Check Segregation of Duties on it. A new privilege can raise the license every user of the role needs. See Analyze License and Segregation of Duties.
  4. Run Upgrade Readiness on the model when the branch adds wrappers or extensions: its Collisions with other models section finds the same field, control or method changed by another model. See Upgrade Readiness.
  5. Optional: deploy the branch to your UDE and run the project's tests (Run Tests or the Test Explorer). See Run Tests.
  6. Open the pull request's pipeline with Open Pipelines (Azure Pipelines of the project, or the GitHub Actions of the branch) to see whether the CI build passed. F&O Studio opens the page; it doesn't run pipelines. See Work Items and Pipelines.

docs.title: Phase 6: Write the review
docs.text:
1. In the Results view, use Copy Report as Markdown on the Review My Changes report.
  2. Post your findings on the pull request in Azure DevOps or GitHub. F&O Studio doesn't post review comments itself.
  3. Order findings by severity and name the element and method in each. Example:
Severity Element and method Finding Fix Blocker CustTable_Contoso_Extension.validateWrite never calls next validateWrite(): standard validation is skipped call next first and combine the results Major ContosoCustCreditReviewList (display menu item) in no privilege add to ContosoCustCreditReviewListView Minor CustTable.ContosoExtensions (form extension) hard-coded caption use a label
  1. When you are done, switch back to your branch and run Refresh Application Explorer.

docs.title: What to look at per kind of change
docs.text:
Change in the pull request What to check Where in F&O Studio Chain of Command class calls next; logic before or after next is in the right place; no other model wraps the same method in a conflicting way Review My Changes (Chain of Command), Go to Implementations, Upgrade Readiness (collisions) Table extension new fields have labels and EDTs; indexes and relations make sense; a database sync is needed Element designer, Analyze Performance (missing indexes, cache settings) Form extension control placement; data source of the new control; no hidden duplicates Form designer preview with markers, Find Event Handlers New table or form find/exist, table group, cache lookup, form pattern Element designer, Best practice checks, Quick fixes Menu item in a privilege with the right grant Who Can Access, Find Security Gaps Role, duty or privilege license impact; segregation of duties Analyze License, Check Segregation of Duties, Security Report… Data entity public names, keys, staging fields, mandatory fields, set-based processing Review My Changes and Analyze Performance (data entity readiness) Labels no hard-coded text; translations present Find Labels…, Translate Missing Labels… Deleted element nothing else still uses it Find References before you approve

See Element Designer, Who Can Access, Analyze Performance and Label Tools.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Code Reviewer in the agent picker. It is read-only: it never creates, changes or deletes elements and never builds or deploys.

Review the changes on this branch against main. Focus on the Chain of Command wrapper and the security changes.

What it does:

Step Tool Lists the changed elements against main (or the branch you name) xpp_diff_changes Reads each changed element xpp_read_object Best practice and static performance on the changed elements xpp_check_best_practice, xpp_analyze_performance Obsolete API use when the model calls obsolete APIs xpp_find_deprecations Security gaps for new menu items, forms and services xpp_analyze_security with op=gaps Team rules .xpp/agent-rules.md, added to its instructions

It also checks by hand what the tools miss: Chain of Command wrappers that don't call next, logic in the wrong layer, set-based operations that fall back to row by row, missing ttsbegin/ttscommit, hard-coded text instead of labels, missing find/exist.

Its answer: findings by severity (Blocker, Major, Minor) with element and method, problem, impact and fix; then what is good, and what it couldn't verify. No style nitpicks.

More prompts:

  • "Write a pull request summary of this branch for the reviewers: what changed, why, the security impact and the test focus."
  • "Does anything in this branch change the license of a standard role?" (then switch to F&O Security & License)
  • "Are there other models that wrap CustTable.validateWrite, and could they conflict with ours?"

Handoffs:

  • Fix the findings switches to F&O Developer (on the author's machine, with a checkpoint; see Scenario: Work Safely with Copilot).
  • Prepare the release switches to F&O Release Manager once the review is done.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Own work committed or stashed; pull request branch checked out; Application Explorer refreshed.
  • [ ] Show Changed Elements matches the pull request description.
  • [ ] Work item read; commits name it.
  • [ ] Review My Changes: no wrapper without next, no best practice errors, performance warnings understood.
  • [ ] Each changed element read; history and diffs looked at.
  • [ ] Impact checked: references, other wrappers, form layout.
  • [ ] Build Model succeeds on your machine.
  • [ ] Security: no gaps; license and segregation of duties checked for changed roles.
  • [ ] CI pipeline passed.
  • [ ] Findings posted by severity with element and method.

docs.title: Scenario: Set Up ALM for a Team
docs.text: For a technical lead who starts a D365FO project with a team of developers in VS Code. At the end, the team has one Git repository on Azure DevOps with the model and project, every developer gets the code onto their own unified developer environment with one command, work items link to commits, reviews run before each pull request, and a pipeline (set up with Microsoft's tools) builds the deployable package.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Contoso starts a Finance implementation. Four developers, each with their own unified developer environment (UDE), will extend sales order processing (SalesTable, SalesFormLetter) and customer groups (CustGroup). Work items live in an Azure DevOps project FinOps. The lead has to set up:

  • a model ContosoExtensions (publisher Contoso, layer USR) referencing the standard application packages;
  • a repository ContosoFinOps in Azure Repos, with branch protection on main;
  • a project ContosoExtensions that every developer opens;
  • the team's naming rules for Copilot;
  • a build pipeline that produces the deployable package.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A UDE for each developer, connected on their machine with Connect to Environment… (see Connect to Environment and Scenario: Set Up a New Developer Machine).
  • Git installed on every machine.
  • Azure DevOps project administrator rights (for the repository, policies and pipeline).
  • For the pipeline (general practice): the Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations Tools extension in the Azure DevOps organization and Microsoft's X++ build NuGet packages in an Azure Artifacts feed.

docs.title: Phase 1: Create the repository (Azure DevOps, general practice)
docs.text:
1. In Azure DevOps, create the repository ContosoFinOps in project FinOps, initialized with a README so main exists.
  2. On main, add branch policies: minimum reviewers, Check for linked work items, and later a build validation with the pipeline from phase 6.
  3. Clone it on your machine, for example to C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps (VS Code's Git: Clone, or git clone).

docs.title: Phase 2: Create the model and the project (F&O Studio)
docs.text:
1. Run Create Model… (Dynamics 365 view > Create). Enter ContosoExtensions, publisher Contoso, layer USR, and keep ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation and ApplicationSuite as referenced packages. Add other packages your extensions need. The model is created in its own package in the custom metadata folder. See Models, Packages and Versioning.
  2. Run Create D365FO Project…. Pick the model, keep the name ContosoExtensionsProject or change it, choose Browse… and pick C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps\Projects. F&O Studio writes Projects\ContosoExtensionsProject\ContosoExtensionsProject.rnrproj and a .slnx next to it. See D365FO Projects.

Decision: one model or several? Start with one. Split into more packages only when parts must deploy separately or must not depend on each other; ask the F&O Architect agent if unsure (see below).

docs.title: Phase 3: Put the package into the repository and link it (F&O Studio)
docs.text:
The package was created inside the custom metadata folder. Move it into the repository so Git tracks it, and link it back:

  1. Close VS Code, so nothing holds files of the package.
  2. Move the folder <custom metadata folder>\ContosoExtensions to C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps\Metadata\ContosoExtensions.
  3. Open VS Code and run Open Team Repository… > Use a Folder Already on This Machine… and pick C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps.
  4. F&O Studio finds the package by its Descriptor folder and lists it (checked). Confirm. It then:
  5. creates the junction <custom metadata folder>\ContosoExtensions -> C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps\Metadata\ContosoExtensions;
  6. writes .xpp\workspace.json with the package folder (Metadata/ContosoExtensions);
  7. refreshes the Application Explorer and builds the package;
  8. offers Deploy and Synchronize Database, and opens the repository's project.
  9. Check the summary message: "Linked 1 package(s) into ... ; all built."

See Open Team Repository.

docs.title: Phase 4: Add the team files (F&O Studio and Git)
docs.text:
1. Add a .gitignore at the repository root that keeps build output out (**/bin/, **/BuildLogs/, **/Resources/, **/Reports/, **/XppMetadata/, **/obj/, .vs/). The full list and reasons are in Source Control for X++.
  2. With the project open, run Create Team Rules for Copilot (Dynamics 365 view > Copilot). It creates .xpp\agent-rules.md in the first workspace folder (the project folder) with example rules. Replace the ABC examples with your rules, for example:
## Naming
- Prefix every new element with `Contoso`.
- Chain of Command classes: `<BaseObject>_Contoso_Extension`. Metadata extensions: `<BaseObject>.ContosoExtensions`.

## Code
- Every user-visible text is a label in the label file `ContosoLabels`.
- Batch work uses SysOperation (contract, service, controller); no RunBaseBatch.

The MCP server adds this file to Copilot's instructions and restarts when it changes. See Team Rules. 3. Set xpp.git.baseBranch to main in your settings, and tell every developer to do the same. Change marks, Show Changed Elements and Review My Changes then cover the whole branch. See Git Changes in the Project View. 4. Commit everything on main (or through a first pull request if the policy already applies): Metadata\ContosoExtensions\..., Projects\..., .xpp\workspace.json, the project's .xpp\agent-rules.md and .gitignore. Push.

docs.title: Phase 5: Onboard each developer (F&O Studio)
docs.text:
Each developer, on their own machine with their UDE connected:

  1. Runs Open Team Repository… > Clone a Repository…, enters https://dev.azure.com/contoso/FinOps/_git/ContosoFinOps and picks a parent folder. VS Code's Git extension clones it with the developer's sign-in.
  2. The packages listed in .xpp\workspace.json are offered, all checked. F&O Studio links them, builds them in dependency order and opens the project.
  3. Picks Deploy in the summary message (or runs Deploy Models to Environment later) so their UDE runs the code. See Deploy to Environment.
  4. Sets xpp.git.baseBranch to main.

If a developer already has a folder with the package's name in their metadata folder, F&O Studio leaves it alone and says so; they remove or rename their folder and run the command again.

docs.title: Phase 6: Set up the pipeline (general practice)
docs.text:
1. Publish Microsoft's X++ build NuGet packages (compiler and reference packages matching your application version) to an Azure Artifacts feed.
  2. Add packages.config and nuget.config to the repository.
  3. Create a pipeline that restores the packages, builds the solution or .rnrproj with MSBuild, and runs Create Deployable Package; publish the package as an artifact.
  4. Add the pipeline as build validation on main.
  5. In VS Code, Open Pipelines now opens https://dev.azure.com/contoso/FinOps/_build.

F&O Studio does not create or run this pipeline. See Build Automation and Pipelines for the steps and Microsoft's documentation.

docs.title: Phase 7: Agree on the daily workflow
docs.text:
Write the team's working agreement (in the README, for example):

  1. One branch per work item, feature/<id>-<name>, from main.
  2. Link Work Item… on every commit.
  3. Review My Changes against main before every pull request; paste the report into the pull request.
  4. Pre-Deploy Checklist and a deploy to your own UDE before asking for review.
  5. Sandbox and production deployments only from pipeline packages, through LCS or the Power Platform admin center.

See Branching and Team Workflow and Scenario: From Work Item to Deployed Change.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Agent Use it for Example prompt F&O Architect The model and package split, dependencies, environment plan "We will extend sales order processing, customer groups and add two integrations. Propose models and packages and their references, and the environment plan." F&O Code Reviewer Checks that reviews follow the team rules in .xpp/agent-rules.md "Review this branch against main." F&O Release Manager Release checks, change summary, deployable package "Prepare ContosoExtensions for a sandbox release: run the checks and summarize the risk."

Checkpoints:

  • The architect is read-only: it proposes, you create the models with Create Model….
  • The reviewer lists changes with xpp_diff_changes, which needs the models in Git; run it after phase 4.
  • The release manager asks before creating a package with xpp_package and never deploys to production.

See Copilot Agents and Team Rules.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Repository created, main protected with reviewers, linked work items and build validation.
  • [ ] Model created with the right publisher, layer and referenced packages.
  • [ ] Project created inside the repository.
  • [ ] Package folder moved into the repository and linked with Open Team Repository….
  • [ ] .xpp\workspace.json, .xpp\agent-rules.md, .gitignore committed.
  • [ ] Every developer onboarded with Open Team Repository…, built and deployed to their UDE.
  • [ ] xpp.git.baseBranch set to main on every machine.
  • [ ] Pipeline builds main and publishes the deployable package.
  • [ ] Working agreement written down.

docs.title: Scenario: Set Up a New Developer Machine
docs.text: This walkthrough is for a D365FO developer who joins a project and gets a new Windows machine with VS Code. At the end you have the environment's metadata and cross-reference database on the machine, the team's code linked and built, a project open, database access, and Copilot ready to work on your models. No Visual Studio is needed.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
You join a team that builds the ContosoExtensions model. The team works on unified developer environments (UDE). Your UDE is provisioned in the Power Platform admin center, and its Dataverse URL is https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com. The team's code is in an Azure DevOps Git repository that holds the ContosoExtensions package and a project ContosoExtensions.rnrproj.

On your first day you want to:

  1. get the metadata and the cross-reference database of your UDE on the machine;
  2. get the team's package linked into your metadata folder and built;
  3. open the team's project, build it, and look at real data;
  4. let Copilot help, with the team's rules.

If you work on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment instead, skip phase 2: F&O Studio uses the local PackagesLocalDirectory, AOS and AxDB without a connection step (see Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments).

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Need Why Windows, VS Code 1.101 or later F&O Studio is Windows only. F&O Studio from the VS Code Marketplace The extension. SQL Server LocalDB The cross-reference database is restored into (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB. At least 16 GB free disk space on the drive of %LOCALAPPDATA% Connect to Environment refuses to start with less. A Microsoft account that can sign in to the UDE's Dataverse Sign-in uses VS Code's Microsoft account. Git and access to the team repository Open Team Repository clones through VS Code's Git extension. GitHub Copilot (agent mode) For the F&O agents and the agent tools. Optional. Power Platform CLI (pac) Only for the (pac) commands. Deploy and database sync do not need it.

On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, run VS Code as administrator, as Visual Studio does, so the build can write into PackagesLocalDirectory.

docs.title: Phase 1: Install and open F&O Studio
docs.text:
1. Install F&O Studio from the Extensions view and reload if VS Code asks.
  2. Open the F&O Studio view in the activity bar. It has four views: Application Explorer, D365FO Project, Security and Dynamics 365.
  3. Optional: open the Get started with F&O Studio walkthrough (Help > Welcome). Its steps are the same as this page: connect, open or create a project, find an element, build, look at the data, ask Copilot.

See Getting-Started.

docs.title: Phase 2: Connect the machine to your UDE
docs.text:
1. In the Dynamics 365 view, expand Environment and click Connect to Environment… (or run F&O Studio: Connect to Environment… from the command palette).
  2. Enter the Dataverse URL, for example https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com. The prompt accepts the URL of the environment's Dataverse, not the finance and operations URL.
  3. Sign in with your Microsoft account when VS Code asks.
  4. Watch the six steps in the Environment group of the Dynamics 365 view. Each shows its state and current detail:
Step What happens Sign in to Dataverse Reads the environment's integration and application details. Check SQL Server LocalDB Makes sure LocalDB can take the cross-reference database. Download metadata and tools System metadata (PackagesLocalDirectory), the cross-reference backup and the FinOps tools. Extract PackagesLocalDirectory Unzips the metadata under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\. Restore cross-reference database Restores XRef_<org><version> into LocalDB. Configure this machine Writes the XPPConfig configuration, the runtime links and the registry entry Visual Studio reads too.
  1. When it ends you see "Environment connected. The Application Explorer, designers and code views now use it." If a step fails, the error offers Retry, Show Log and Report Problem, and the Environment group shows Retry on the failed step. The full log is in the X++ output.

The download is large and takes a while. You can cancel it from the progress notification.

See Connect-to-Environment and Sign-In-and-Authentication.

docs.title: Phase 3: Check the environment
docs.text:
1. Run Show Active Environment (the Environment group shows it as Show Active Configuration). It writes the active configuration as JSON to the X++ output: check the configuration name, the folders and the URLs.
  2. Run Check Environment Connection to test the sign-in and the Dataverse calls again without downloading anything. The result goes to the X++ output.
  3. Run Check Environment Application Version. It warns when the UDE runs a newer application version than the metadata on this machine. When the version drift guard finds a newer version, the Environment group offers Update Metadata to …. See Version-Drift-Guard.
  4. If you have more than one environment, Select Environment… (also from the status bar item) switches between them without a window reload. Each workspace remembers its own environment. See Select-Environment.
  5. If Visual Studio with the FinOps tools is also installed, run Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version. It offers to install the tools that match the environment's metadata, because Visual Studio's Application Explorer does not open when they differ. F&O Studio itself never needs Visual Studio. See Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

docs.title: Phase 4: Get the team's code
docs.text:
1. In the Dynamics 365 view, expand Model and project and click Open Team Repository….
  2. Pick Clone a Repository… and paste the repository URL (https://dev.azure.com/yourorg/yourproject/_git/yourrepo), then pick the folder to clone into. VS Code's Git extension clones with its own sign-in. If the repository is already on the machine, pick Use a Folder Already on This Machine… instead.
  3. F&O Studio lists the packages it finds (folders with a Descriptor folder). Keep ContosoExtensions checked.
  4. It links each package into your metadata folder with a junction, writes .xpp/workspace.json for the next developer, refreshes the Application Explorer and builds the packages in dependency order.
  5. When the build ends, the message offers Deploy and Synchronize Database (on a UDE). Deploy now if you want the UDE to run the team's current code.
  6. Pick the project to open, ContosoExtensions.rnrproj. It opens in its own workspace.

If a folder with the package name already exists in the metadata folder and is not a link to the repository, it is left as it is and the summary says so.

Open Team Repository is a preview feature. See Open-Team-Repository.

No team repository yet? Create the model and the project yourself:

  1. Create Model… (Dynamics 365 view > Create). Answer the four prompts: model name (ContosoExtensions), publisher, layer (USR, CUS, VAR or ISV) and the referenced packages (ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation and ApplicationSuite are preselected).
  2. Create D365FO Project…. Pick the model, accept the name ContosoExtensionsProject or type another, and pick the parent folder (by default your source\repos folder). It writes the .rnrproj and a .slnx the way Visual Studio does.

See Models-and-Model-Dependencies and D365FO-Projects.

docs.title: Phase 5: First look and first build
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+Alt+O (Open Element…) and type CustGroup. Use a type prefix to narrow it: t: for tables, c: for classes, f: for forms. See Open-Element.
  2. In the Application Explorer, use Filter Application Explorer… and switch between Switch to Model View (Elements by Model) and Switch to Classic View (Elements by Type). See Application-Explorer.
  3. Open a class of ContosoExtensions in the X++ code view. Check that hover, F12 and completion work. If you want fewer features (or semantic highlighting, which is off by default), run Configure Code Intelligence…. See Code-Intelligence-Settings.
  4. Run Build Project (Ctrl+Shift+B in an X++ editor, or the status bar item). The build uses xppc and LabelC, writes to the X++ Build output and puts errors in Problems. The status bar shows the project and the last build result. See Build-Project-and-Model and Status-Bar.
  5. On a UDE, a build is not yet on the environment: the project's status bar item shows when the build is newer than the last deploy from this machine. Use Deploy Models to Environment when you need the environment to run it. See Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: Phase 6: Database access
docs.text:
1. In the Dynamics 365 view, expand Data and click Database…, then Request Database Credentials…. F&O Studio makes the same just-in-time request Visual Studio makes. Pick Reader (read data only, recommended) or Writer (changes in SQL skip X++ business logic).
  2. The credentials are kept in VS Code's secret storage until they expire. The Data group shows the role and the time they expire.
  3. Run Test Database Connection. It reports the database, server, user and SQL Server version.
  4. Right-click table CustGroup in the Application Explorer and choose Browse Table Data to see rows with enum names, the company filter and the record inspector.

On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment the local AxDB is used with Windows authentication; there are no credentials to request. See Database-Access and Browse-Table-Data.

docs.title: Phase 7: Copilot ready for the team
docs.text:
1. Open Copilot Chat in agent mode. The F&O Studio agent tools (xpp_*) are registered automatically; there is nothing to configure. See MCP-Agent-Tools.
  2. Pick an F&O agent in the agent picker, for example F&O Code Archaeologist to learn the model or F&O Developer to build. See Copilot-Agents.
  3. If the repository has no team rules yet, run Create Team Rules for Copilot. It creates .xpp/agent-rules.md, which is added to the agent instructions of everyone working in the repository. Write your naming prefix, label file and review rules there and commit it. See Team-Rules.
  4. Before letting an agent change elements, run Start Copilot Checkpoint and, if you want, Set Copilot Scope…. See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope.
  5. If functional colleagues use the consultant agents, set up the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server separately; those agents use it to read the live environment.

docs.title: Phase 8: Optional settings
docs.text:
Open Options… (Dynamics 365 view) for the F&O Studio settings. Common ones on a new machine:

Setting Default When to change it xpp.environmentUrl empty Your default UDE's Dataverse URL, used when a workspace has no environment of its own. xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl empty Web client URL for Open in Browser when the configuration has none. xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild true Saves unsaved code views before a build. xpp.build.crossReference true Updates cross references while building. xpp.git.baseBranch empty The branch Review My Changes compares with, for example main. xpp.debuggerProxyPath empty Only if DebuggerProxy is not in the default location. xpp.pacPath empty Only for the (pac) commands.

See Settings-Reference.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Connecting the environment, cloning and building are commands you run yourself; agents do not run Connect to Environment or Open Team Repository. Once the machine is set up, agents help you understand what you inherited.

F&O Code Archaeologist (read-only) maps the model and its hooks into standard:

Map the ContosoExtensions model for me: what it adds, which standard tables, forms and classes it extends, the Chain of Command wrappers and event handlers, and any batch jobs. Draw the main flow as a Mermaid diagram.

It uses xpp_list_model_objects and xpp_get_model_info to map the model, xpp_read_object to read the entry points, xpp_find_references to trace callers and xpp_find_deprecations for obsolete calls.

F&O Architect (read-only) explains the landscape:

We have ContosoExtensions and a second model for integrations. Look at both models' dependencies and tell me whether the split and the package references make sense, and what you'd change.

F&O Developer confirms the toolchain works end to end:

Build the ContosoExtensions project and run the best practice checks. List the errors and warnings by element. Don't change anything yet.

The agent calls xpp_build (scope project) and xpp_check_best_practice. Check the result in the Copilot Activity view, which lists every tool call with its arguments, duration and result. See Copilot-Activity.

Checkpoints: - The agent reports BUILD SUCCEEDED, or the errors with element, method and line. - No element changed (Copilot Activity shows only read tools).

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Connect to Environment finished all six steps (or: cloud-hosted/VHD, nothing to connect).
  • [ ] Show Active Environment shows the right configuration and version.
  • [ ] Check Environment Application Version reports no drift.
  • [ ] The team's packages are linked and built (Open Team Repository), or your model and project are created.
  • [ ] Build Project succeeds; the status bar shows the result.
  • [ ] Database credentials requested (UDE) and Test Database Connection succeeds.
  • [ ] Browse Table Data shows rows of CustGroup.
  • [ ] Copilot agent mode lists the F&O agents; .xpp/agent-rules.md exists.
  • [ ] Visual Studio (if installed) has matching FinOps tools.
