docs.title: Scenario: Upgrade to a new version
docs.text: This walkthrough is for developers who own custom models when the application under them changes: Microsoft services your unified developer environment (UDE) with a new application version, or your project moves to the next service update. At the end your model builds against the new version, its Chain of Command wrappers, event handlers and extensions still match the standard code, obsolete API calls are replaced, the tests pass, and the old version's metadata is off your disk.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
Your model ContosoExtensions has been running for a year. It contains, among other things:

  • SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension, a Chain of Command class that wraps SalesFormLetter.run;
  • CustTable_Contoso_Extension, which wraps CustTable.validateWrite;
  • table, form and enum extensions such as CustTable.ContosoExtensions and SalesTable.ContosoExtensions;
  • a few event handlers on standard forms;
  • some older code that still calls APIs Microsoft has since marked [SysObsolete].

This morning VS Code shows: "The environment now runs application <new>; this machine has the metadata of <old>. Builds compile against the old version and deploys can fail." You need to bring the machine up to date, find what the update broke, and fix it before the next deploy.

The same steps apply when you plan an update in advance on a separate environment that already runs the target version.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A UDE connected with Connect to Environment…, or a cloud-hosted or VHD environment with the new version installed. The version drift warning is for UDEs only.
  • About 16 GB free on the system drive for the new version's PackagesLocalDirectory.
  • SQL Server LocalDB, for the new cross-reference database.
  • Your model in a project (optional, but it helps with build, tests and the Pre-Deploy Checklist).
  • To compare standard code: the earlier version's PackagesLocalDirectory still on disk. F&O Studio keeps it under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version> until you remove it.

docs.title: Phase 1: Notice the new version
docs.text:
1. F&O Studio checks the environment's application version about 15 seconds after start and whenever you switch environments, without asking you to sign in. When the environment runs a newer version than your metadata, it shows the warning above with Update Metadata and Later. See Version Drift Guard (preview).
  2. To check by hand at any time, run Check Environment Application Version. If nothing differs it says "The metadata on this machine matches the environment's application version (or the environment could not be reached without signing in)."
  3. Do not build and deploy against the old metadata in the meantime: builds compile against the old version and deploys can fail.

docs.title: Phase 2: Get the new metadata
docs.text:
1. Choose Update Metadata in the warning. It runs Connect to Environment… for the same environment.
  2. Connect to Environment downloads the new version's metadata, restores the new cross-reference database and writes the configuration for the new version. It shows each step in the Dynamics 365 view and can retry a failed one. See Connect to Environment.
  3. The earlier version stays in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<old>. Keep it for now: Standard Code Drift uses it in Phase 5.
  4. When it is done, the Application Explorer, designers and code views use the new version. Run Show Active Environment to confirm: the output shows the active configuration, including its application version.
  5. If you also use Visual Studio on this machine, run Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version. Visual Studio's Application Explorer does not open when its FinOps tools differ from the metadata version; the command offers the matching tools. F&O Studio itself does not need Visual Studio. See Visual Studio Side by Side.

docs.title: Phase 3: Build against the new version
docs.text:
1. Run Build Model and pick ContosoExtensions (or Build Project if the project covers the whole model).
  2. Read the Problems view. Typical results after an update:
  3. errors where a wrapped method changed its signature or disappeared;
  4. errors or warnings where your code calls something marked [SysObsolete];
  5. errors in extensions whose base field, field group or control was removed.
  6. Leave the fixes for later; first get the full picture in Phase 4. See Build Project and Model and Compiler Diagnostics.
  7. In the code view, F&O Studio also warns on calls to [SysObsolete] APIs while you type (xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings). See Syntax Check and Obsolete Warnings.

docs.title: Phase 4: Run Upgrade Readiness
docs.text:
1. In the Application Explorer, right-click the model ContosoExtensions and choose Upgrade Readiness, or run it from Dynamics 365 view > Build and check and pick the model (the project's model is marked "project model").
  2. The report opens in the Results view with three sections:
Section What it lists Obsolete API uses Every place your code uses a class, table or method marked [SysObsolete], with the attribute's message (often the replacement) and whether it is marked as an error (it will stop compiling). Read from the cross-reference database. Extension compatibility Chain of Command wrappers whose target method is gone, changed its signature (static, return type, parameters) or can no longer be wrapped (private, final, Wrappable(false), Hookable(false), internal); event handlers whose class, method, delegate or table is gone; table, form and enum extensions whose base element, fields, field groups or controls are gone. Collisions with other models The same field, index, field group, enum value or form control added by another model's extension, and several wrappers of one method.
  1. Click a finding to open the element at the method and line. Findings marked as errors come first in importance: they block the build.
  2. Use Copy Report as Markdown or Export Report… to keep the list as your upgrade work list. See Upgrade Readiness and Results View.

docs.title: Phase 5: See what changed under your wrappers
docs.text:
A wrapper can still compile while the standard code around next changed its behaviour. Standard Code Drift shows those cases.

  1. Right-click the model in the Application Explorer and choose Standard Code Drift of Wrapped Methods…, or run it from Dynamics 365 view > Build and check.
  2. Pick the earlier version. F&O Studio lists the application versions under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365 that still have a PackagesLocalDirectory. If none is there (for example on a cloud-hosted environment), it asks for the folder: "PackagesLocalDirectory of the earlier version", button Compare With This Version.
  3. The Results view lists, per wrapped method whose standard code changed, the number of lines that differ and the wrapper class: for example SalesFormLetter.run: 12 line(s) differ · wrapped by SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension. Formatting-only changes are ignored. The summary line counts the wrappers, the changed and unchanged targets, and the ones not found in one of the versions.
  4. Click an entry to open a diff of the standard method: old version on the left, installed version on the right.
  5. For each changed method, decide whether your code before or after next still does the right thing. Typical cases: a value you set before next is now overwritten inside the method, or a new parameter or early return changes when your code runs. See Standard Code Drift.

docs.title: Phase 6: Fix the findings
docs.text:
Work through the list from Phase 4 and 5. Useful tools:

  1. Go to Definition (F12) on the standard method to read its new code. See Go to Definition.
  2. Go to Implementations (Ctrl+F12) on a standard method to see every Chain of Command class and handler that wraps it, including other models' wrappers that may collide with yours. See Implementations and Chain of Command.
  3. Search Code in All Packages (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F) for the replacement API named in the [SysObsolete] message, to see how Microsoft's own code calls it. See Search Code.
  4. Find Similar Standard Implementations when a whole pattern changed (for example a new extension point that replaces your wrapper). See Find Similar Implementations.
  5. Compare Code… between your wrapper and the standard method, or two standard classes, in VS Code's diff editor. See Compare Code and Metadata.
  6. For a broken extension (a field group that is gone), open the extension in the designer and move or remove the node. See Element Designer.
  7. After each group of fixes, run Build Model again and use Run Again on the Upgrade Readiness report until it has no errors.

docs.title: Phase 7: Check and test
docs.text:
1. Run Best Practice Checks on Project. New versions sometimes come with new rules. See Best Practice Checks.
  2. On a UDE, run Deploy Models to Environment with a Module sync (your table extensions need it if base tables changed), then Run Tests or the Test Explorer. Tests run against the deployed code; F&O Studio warns first when your build is newer than the last deploy. See Deploy to Environment and Run Tests.
  3. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, a successful build restarts the running AOS hosts so they load it; run tests on the VM.
  4. Debug what still behaves differently: set a breakpoint in the standard method that changed (for example SalesFormLetter.run) and in your wrapper, and step through both. See Debugging Standard Code.
  5. Run the Pre-Deploy Checklist before you hand the update over. See Pre-Deploy Checklist.

docs.title: Phase 8: Free the disk
docs.text:
1. When the update is done, run Clean Up Old Application Versions….
  2. F&O Studio measures each version folder and lists the ones that are not active, with their size and the configurations that use them ("Used by the configuration of ... (it stops working)").
  3. The newest older version is not selected by default, so you can keep it for Standard Code Drift. Select what to remove and confirm Delete. Cross-reference databases are not removed. See Version Drift Guard.

docs.title: Planning an update in advance
docs.text:
• To prepare before your UDE moves, connect a second workspace to an environment that already runs the target version (Select Environment… remembers the environment per workspace) and run Phases 3 to 7 there.
  • View Model Dependencies… shows which models yours depends on; an ISV model that yours depends on must be available for the new version too. See Models and Model Dependencies.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
Pick F&O Upgrade Reviewer in the agent picker. It is read-only: it reports and recommends, and hands fixes to the F&O Developer.

Example prompts:

  • "The UDE moved to a new application version. Check ContosoExtensions for upgrade issues and give me a readiness report."
  • "Compare the standard code that ContosoExtensions wraps with the previous version in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\\PackagesLocalDirectory. Which wrappers need a second look?"
  • "Search the release notes and deprecated features for the target version and tell me what affects our model."

    • What the agent does:

    Step Tool Obsolete API uses, extension compatibility and collisions; with the earlier PackagesLocalDirectory also the wrapped methods whose standard code changed xpp_find_deprecations (with previousPackagesFolder) Reads the affected standard elements and the SysObsolete message xpp_read_object Checks the model's dependencies xpp_get_model_info Searches release notes and deprecated-feature lists xpp_search_docs

    The answer is a readiness report per model: blockers, required changes, recommended changes, the replacement for each obsolete call, and the test focus for the update.

    Then use the handoff Fix the upgrade issues, which switches to F&O Developer. Before it changes code, run Start Copilot Checkpoint so you can undo the whole session with Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… (see Scenario: Work Safely with Copilot). Example prompts for the developer:

    • "Replace the obsolete calls in the readiness report with the replacements their SysObsolete messages name. Build after each class."
    • "SalesFormLetter.run changed between the versions. Read both versions and adjust SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension.run so our logic still runs after the standard posting."

    The developer agent builds with xpp_build until there are no errors or warnings in your elements, runs xpp_check_best_practice, and runs tests with xppRunTests when they exist. The F&O Performance agent helps when a process got slower after the update (see Scenario: Performance Tuning a Slow Process).

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Version drift warning handled: Update Metadata (or Connect to Environment…) for the new version.
  • [ ] Visual Studio's FinOps tools match, if you use Visual Studio on this machine.
  • [ ] Build Model run once to see the raw errors.
  • [ ] Upgrade Readiness: no errors in Obsolete API uses or Extension compatibility; collisions reviewed.
  • [ ] Standard Code Drift: every changed wrapped method reviewed against your wrapper.
  • [ ] Obsolete calls replaced; broken extensions fixed.
  • [ ] Build Model succeeds; best practice checks clean.
  • [ ] Deployed (UDE) and tests pass; key processes debugged where behaviour changed.
  • [ ] Pre-Deploy Checklist passes.
  • [ ] Old versions removed with Clean Up Old Application Versions… (newest older one kept if you still need it).

docs.title: Scenario: Work safely with Copilot
docs.text:
This walkthrough is for developers who let Copilot agents change X++ metadata and code, and for leads who want the team to do so with control. At the end you know how to set the rules before the agent starts, limit what it may change, watch every tool call, review the result like any other change, and undo the whole session with one command when you don't like it.

Copilot works on real metadata through F&O Studio's agent tools: it reads, creates, extends and builds elements through the metadata API, the same way the designers do. That is what makes it useful, and why the guard rails below matter.

docs.title: The situation
docs.text:
You ask the F&O Developer agent to add a field Credit review required to customer groups and show it on the customer group form:

  • a table extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions with the field ContosoCreditReviewRequired;
  • a form extension CustGroup.ContosoExtensions with the control;
  • a label in your label file ContosoLabels;
  • added to your project ContosoCustomerCredit.

The project also holds other work in progress that the agent must not touch. You want to see what the agent does, and to be able to undo it all if the result is wrong.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• GitHub Copilot in VS Code, in agent mode. The F&O Studio tools are registered automatically (see MCP Agent Tools).
  • A D365FO project open (the scope and the checkpoint use it), in a Git repository.
  • Your team's naming rules, if you have them.
  • A development environment. The agents change data, setup or metadata only after you allow it, and only in development, sandbox or build environments, never in production.

docs.title: Phase 1: Give the agent your team's rules
docs.text:
1. Run Create Team Rules for Copilot (Dynamics 365 view > Copilot, or the command palette). It creates .xpp/agent-rules.md in the first workspace folder (your repository) and opens it. If the file exists it just opens it. See Team Rules.
  2. Replace the template's examples with your rules. The template has sections for Naming, Models, Code, Security and Reviews, for example:
## Naming
- Prefix every new element with `Contoso` (tables, classes, EDTs, enums, menu items, security objects).
- Metadata extensions: `<BaseObject>.ContosoExtensions`.

## Code
- Every user-visible text is a label in the label file `ContosoLabels`.
- Batch work uses SysOperation (contract, service, controller); no RunBaseBatch.

## Security
- Every new menu item gets View and Maintain privileges.
  1. Commit the file: everyone who opens the repository gets the same rules. F&O Studio passes the file to the agent tools' server, which adds it after its own instructions ("follow them where they are stricter"). When the file changes, the server restarts with the new rules.

docs.title: Phase 2: Choose the right agent
docs.text:
1. Open Copilot chat, switch to agent mode, and pick an agent in the agent picker. For this change pick F&O Developer. See Copilot Agents.
  2. Read-only agents (F&O Code Reviewer, F&O Solution Designer, F&O Code Archaeologist, the Security, Performance, Upgrade and Support agents, and most functional agents) never create, change or delete elements, files, data or setup, and never build or deploy. Start with one of them when you only want advice.
  3. Agents that may change things (F&O Developer, F&O Test Engineer, F&O Report Developer, F&O Report Builder, F&O Workflow & Events, F&O Release Manager, F&O Integration, F&O Setup Advisor, F&O Data Migration) do it only after you allow that change. When they don't know what kind of environment it is, they ask, and treat an unknown environment as production.

docs.title: Phase 3: Limit what the agent may change
docs.text:
1. Run Set Copilot Scope…. It offers:
  2. The Project's Elements: the project's elements, plus new elements Copilot creates;
  3. Pick Elements…: some of the project's elements (multi-select), plus new elements Copilot creates;
  4. No Limit: Copilot may change any element of your models (the default).
  5. For this change choose Pick Elements… and select nothing but the elements the change may touch (for example the existing label file). New elements the agent creates are allowed and join the scope.
  6. A lock icon appears in the status bar; its tooltip says how many elements Copilot may change.
  7. The agent tools' server enforces the scope on every write. A write to an element outside it is refused with a message the agent sees: the element "is outside the elements the user allows Copilot to change (F&O Studio: Set Copilot Scope)", with the allowed list. The agent then has to ask you.
  8. Independently of the scope, writes are always limited to your own models, every write is all or nothing, and an existing name is never overwritten. Deleting through the agent works only on your own models and checks where-used first. See Copilot Checkpoints and Scope and Security Model.

docs.title: Phase 4: Start a checkpoint
docs.text:
1. Run Start Copilot Checkpoint (Dynamics 365 view > Copilot > Start Checkpoint, or click the scope's status bar item when it shows). F&O Studio copies the project file and your models' label files, and from now on the server keeps each element's state before Copilot's first change to it.
  2. The status bar shows a history icon with the number of elements Copilot changed since the checkpoint. It updates every few seconds.
  3. If a checkpoint is already open, you can Keep Its Changes and Start a New One.

docs.title: Phase 5: Let the agent work, and watch it
docs.text:
1. Ask for the change:

Add a Yes/No field "Credit review required" to customer groups and show it on the customer group form, in the General group. Follow our team rules. Plan first and wait for my OK.

  1. Read the plan. A good plan names the standard precedent for each element, the elements to create or extend with their names, labels and security. Reply with changes or OK.
  2. Open the Copilot Activity view (F&O Studio panel). It lists every tool call, newest first: tool, element, time, duration; a search icon for reads, an edit icon for writes, an error icon for failures. Hover for the arguments. See Copilot Activity.

  1. After each successful write, a notification says "Copilot changed CustGroup.ContosoExtensions (TableExtension)." (or created, deleted) with View Changes and Open. View Changes opens a diff of the element file before Copilot's change and now. Clicking a write in the Activity view does the same.
  2. VS Code also asks you to approve tool calls, depending on your Copilot settings. Two F&O Studio tools have their own rules:
  3. database queries (xppQueryData) show the read-only SELECT and wait for your confirmation; the agent never sees the credentials;
  4. the deployable package tool (xpp_package) tells the agent to create a package only when you asked for one, and it never deploys.
  5. If the agent runs tests or you start a check in the running app while your build is newer than the last deploy, F&O Studio warns that the environment still runs the deployed code.

docs.title: Phase 6: Review the result like any change
docs.text:
1. Click the checkpoint item in the status bar (Copilot Checkpoint…). It lists the elements Copilot changed (an add icon marks new ones). Pick one to open its designer.
  2. Read the code and metadata yourself: the Element Designer, the Form Designer and Preview for the new control, the Label Editor for the label.
  3. Run Build Project and Run Best Practice Checks on Project. The agent should already have built until there were no errors or warnings in its elements, but check it yourself.
  4. Run Review My Changes: Chain of Command wrappers without next, best practice, performance. See Review My Changes.
  5. Optional: ask the F&O Code Reviewer for a second opinion (the F&O Developer's handoff Review the changes).
  6. Optional (preview): after deploying, Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot) builds check steps from the changed elements and runs them read-only through the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server. See Verify Changes in Running App.

docs.title: Phase 7: Keep or revert
docs.text:
• Keep: run End Copilot Checkpoint (Keep Changes). It asks "Keep Copilot's changes and end the checkpoint? They can no longer be reverted here (only through Git)." Choose End Checkpoint, then commit to Git.
  • Revert: run Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint…. A dialog lists what happens (Restore or Delete per element) and warns that the project file and label files go back to their state at the checkpoint, including your own changes to them since. Confirm Revert. Changed elements are restored through the metadata API, new ones are deleted, and the project and label files are copied back. If the revert fails, the checkpoint stays open and the message names the element.
  • Either way, the scope stays until you change it with Set Copilot Scope… > No Limit.

docs.title: Phase 8: Keep the history clean
docs.text:
1. Use Clear Copilot Activity when you start a new task, so the view shows only the current session.
  2. Commit in small steps. A checkpoint covers one session; Git covers everything else. View History on an element shows its commits with diffs. See Element History.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
This page is about Copilot itself, so here are prompts that keep a session safe.

Before writing:

  • "Plan the change first: list every element you will create or extend, with names, labels and the standard precedent you follow. Don't create anything until I say OK." (F&O Developer)
  • "Read CustGroup and its form layout and tell me where the field fits. Don't change anything." (F&O Developer or F&O Code Archaeologist)

While writing:

  • "Build after every element and fix every error and warning in your elements before you continue."
  • "Only change elements of the project ContosoCustomerCredit. If you need anything else, ask me." (the scope enforces it anyway)

After writing:

  • "Summarize what you changed: element, member, why; and what is left for me (deploy, database sync, security assignment)." The F&O Developer's output includes this by design.
  • Handoff Review the changes to the F&O Code Reviewer, or Write tests to the F&O Test Engineer.

What the F&O Developer uses:

Purpose Tools Understand the standard elements xpp_find_object, xpp_read_object, xpp_get_form_layout, xpp_find_examples, xpp_get_guide Create and change, through the metadata API xpp_create_object, xpp_update_object, xpp_create_label, xpp_add_to_project Prove it works xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice, xppRunTests Show you the result xppOpenElement

Every call shows in Copilot Activity; every write respects the scope and is recorded in the checkpoint.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Team rules in .xpp/agent-rules.md, committed.
  • [ ] The right agent picked; a read-only agent when you only want advice.
  • [ ] Copilot scope set to the elements the task may touch.
  • [ ] Checkpoint started before the first write.
  • [ ] Plan reviewed before the agent creates elements.
  • [ ] Copilot Activity open; each write's diff looked at.
  • [ ] Build, best practice and Review My Changes run by you.
  • [ ] Checkpoint ended (keep) and committed, or reverted.
  • [ ] Scope reset when the task is done.

docs.title: Search Code
docs.text: Search Code in All Packages finds text or a regular expression in the X++ source of every package on your machine, standard and custom. It answers questions such as "where does standard code call CustGroup::find(?" or "which classes use NumberSeq::newGetNum(?". Results come back as a pick list of matching lines, and selecting one opens the code at that line. Visual Studio has no X++-aware equivalent: there you would run Find in Files over the XML files in PackagesLocalDirectory and then locate the method yourself.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to see how standard code uses an API before you call it yourself.
  • You need precedents: every place that raises a certain error, sets a certain field, or uses a label ID.
  • You look for a string, a field name or a method name in code, not for a typed reference. For typed references (where a table, class or method is used) prefer Find All References, which uses the cross-reference database and is exact.
  • You want to find code in your own models that is not built yet. Search Code reads the source files, so it sees changes that the cross-reference database does not know about.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration (see Connect to Environment and Select Environment). Search Code reads the metadata folders of that configuration: the custom metadata folder and every reference metadata folder (for a UDE, the downloaded PackagesLocalDirectory).
  • No cross-reference database is needed, no build is needed and no database access is needed.
  • The first search over everything reads all source files from disk and can take 30 to 60 seconds. Later searches are much faster because Windows keeps the files in its file cache.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start the command in one of these ways:
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F. The shortcut works in an X++ editor and when Application Explorer, the D365FO Project view, the Dynamics 365 view or the Infolog view has focus.
  3. Click the search icon in the title bar of Application Explorer.
  4. In the Dynamics 365 view, open Find and choose Search Code… ("all packages").
  5. Run F&O Studio: Search Code in All Packages from the Command Palette.
  6. An input box opens. If you selected text on a single line in the editor, that text is filled in. Otherwise the last pattern you searched for is filled in.
  7. Use the two buttons on the right of the input box, as in the editor's Find widget:
  8. Regular expression (regex icon) switches between literal text and a .NET regular expression.
  9. Match case (case-sensitive icon) switches case-sensitive matching.

The title of the input box shows the current state, for example Search X++ code in all packages (regex off, match case off). Both switches are remembered for the next search. 4. Type the text and press Enter. With regex on, an invalid expression is reported under the input box before you can submit it. 5. A notification shows Searching X++ code for <pattern>… while the search runs. 6. The result pick list opens. Its title shows the number of matches, a + when the list was cut off, and the time the search took, for example 500+ match(es) for CustGroup::find( (4.2 s).

Each entry shows:

Part Content Example Label Object.method:line PriceAttributeCustomerProvider.jumpRef:16 Description The matching line, trimmed CustGroup custGroup = CustGroup::find(stringControl.text()); Detail Model, element type, and for nested methods the path inside the element Foundation · Classes

The line number counts from the first line of the method (the method header is line 1), not from the top of the object. 7. Type in the pick list to filter the results further. The filter also matches the matching line and the detail, so you can type a model name or a type such as Forms to narrow the list. 8. Select a result. F&O Studio opens it: - A method of a class, table, form, view, data entity, query or map opens in the X++ Code View of the object, with the cursor on the matching line and column. - A method nested inside a form (on a data source, a data source field or a control) opens in its own method document at the matching line. - The declaration (classDeclaration) opens at the top of the object's code.

If nothing matches, you see No X++ code matches <pattern>.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Goal Pattern Regex Calls of a find method CustGroup::find( off A label used in code @SYS26332 off Assignments to SalesQty on a buffer named salesLine salesLine\.SalesQty\s*= on Calls to checkFailed that mention a customer checkFailed\(.*Cust on A method name in any object validateWrite off

docs.title: What is searched
docs.text:
Search Code looks at the X++ source stored in the metadata files of these element types:

Element type What is searched Classes Declaration and every method Tables Declaration and every method Forms Declaration, form methods, data source methods, data source field methods, control methods Views Declaration and methods Data entities Declaration and methods Queries Declaration and methods Maps Declaration and methods

It does not search properties, labels, reports, security objects or any other metadata. To find label text use Label Tools (Find Labels). To find where an element is referenced in metadata use Find All References.

Matching is per line: a pattern cannot match across two lines of code.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting or state Default Effect Regular expression button off Treat the pattern as a .NET regular expression. Remembered between searches. Match case button off Case-sensitive matching. Remembered between searches. Last pattern empty Filled into the input box when no text is selected. Keybinding Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F declared by the extension Change it in Keyboard Shortcuts (command xpp.searchCode).

There are no xpp.* settings for Search Code. The options are kept in VS Code's global state for the extension.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Limit Value What happens Minimum pattern length 3 characters Shorter patterns are refused by the server with pattern must have at least 3 characters. Results 500 The search stops at 500 matching lines; the title shows 500+. Time 90 seconds The search stops and returns what it found, marked as cut off. Regular expression time per file 2 seconds A pattern that takes longer on one file skips that file. Matching line text 300 characters Longer lines are shortened in the result.

When you hit a limit, make the pattern more specific.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/productivity/searchCode.ts shows the input box and sends the language action search_code (pattern, regex, case sensitivity, maxResults: 500) to the language server process. That process is a second instance of the F&O Studio server that serves code intelligence, so a long search never blocks the designers or the agent tools.
  2. The server's CodeIntel.cs passes the request to CodeSearch.cs.
  3. CodeSearch lists the folders to read: for each package and model under the custom metadata folder and the reference metadata folders of the active configuration, the AxClass, AxTable, AxForm, AxView, AxDataEntityView, AxQuery and AxMap folders. A model that exists in more than one root is read once.
  4. It reads the files in parallel (half the processor count, at least two threads). A quick test on the raw file text skips every file without a match, so only matching files are parsed.
  5. Matching files are parsed as XML. The declaration and every method source are split into lines and each line is tested. Each hit records the element type and name, the model, the member path (for example DataSources/CustGroup/Methods/validateWrite), the line inside the method, the column and the line text.
  6. Hits are sorted by element type, element name, member path and line, then returned to the extension.
  7. When you pick a result, openSearchItem opens the code view document of the object (or the nested method's own document), finds the method with the same parser the code view uses, and moves the cursor to the line and column.

The search reads the files directly from disk. It does not load the metadata API and does not use the cross-reference database, so it also finds code that has never been built.

The same search is available to Copilot agents as the xpp_search_code tool, which can also limit the search to some element types or to one model or package. See MCP Agent Tools.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Text search only: it does not understand X++ semantics. find( matches every method called find.
  • One line at a time: a statement split over several lines can only be found by one of its lines.
  • Comments and strings are searched like code.
  • The command in VS Code always searches all packages and all code element types. Use Copilot with xpp_search_code when you want to narrow by model or element type.
  • Results are capped at 500 lines.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix pattern must have at least 3 characters. The server needs at least 3 characters. Type a longer pattern. Invalid regular expression: ... under the input box Regex is on and the pattern is not a valid .NET expression. Fix the expression, or switch regex off to search the literal text (for example CustGroup::find( needs regex off or \(). The first search takes a minute All source files are read from disk the first time. Wait; later searches use the file cache. Title shows + 500 results or 90 seconds reached. Use a more specific pattern. A recently changed method is not found The change is not saved yet. Save the object; the search reads the saved metadata files. Nothing found in your own code The active configuration points to another custom metadata folder. Check the environment in Select Environment.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text:
F&O Studio runs local programs (the X++ compiler, a metadata server, the debugger proxy), signs in to your Dynamics 365 environments, and lets Copilot read and change metadata. This page explains what it is allowed to do, what it refuses, and how those rules are enforced and tested.

In short: only your own models are writable, the server enforces that for every write, Copilot works inside the scope you set, business data never reaches Copilot's server process, credentials stay in VS Code's secret storage, and no Microsoft assemblies or data leave your machine through F&O Studio.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text: Rule Where it is enforced Standard models and their elements are never changed Bridge dispatcher, centrally for every write action (IWritePolicy) Metadata changes go through Microsoft's metadata API, not hand-written XML Server design; .rnrproj and label text files are the only files edited directly Copilot changes only elements you allow, and you can revert them MCP server: scope check and checkpoint before every agent write Copilot's server process cannot read business data xpp/data exists only with --allow-data, which the MCP server never gets The agent never sees database credentials xpp_query_data runs in the extension's process Credentials are not written to settings, logs or files VS Code secret storage; the data service gets them per request and never stores or logs them Microsoft's assemblies are never redistributed Build references with <Private>false</Private>; the release fails when a Microsoft DLL is in the output

docs.title: Workspace trust and machine settings
docs.text:
• capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.supported is false. F&O Studio does not run in Restricted Mode, because it runs the compiler, debugger and metadata server for the workspace's projects.
  • Settings that point at programs F&O Studio runs have machine scope, so a workspace's .vscode/settings.json cannot set them: xpp.pacPath, xpp.debuggerProxyPath, xpp.build.msbuildPath and xpp.trace.manifestFolder.
  • pac runs without a shell (unless it is a .cmd shim), and quotes in its arguments are refused.

docs.title: Writes to metadata
docs.text:
Every bridge action is registered with a WriteKind (see Bridge-Protocol). Before the handler runs, the dispatcher checks:

Kind Check Refusal message (example) Edit The existing element must belong to one of your custom models (skipped for checkOnly) AxTable 'CustGroup' belongs to <model>, which you can't change. Create an extension in your model instead. Create, Copy The target model must be one of your custom models Model '<model>' is not one of your custom models. Create objects in your own model. Read none

Because the check sits in the dispatcher, it applies equally to the designers, the code view, refactorings and every agent tool that delegates to a bridge action. Elements of standard models open read-only in the designers; the editor title offers Create Extension instead.

Label writes are checked separately: label text files are written only under the custom metadata folder, and label file IDs and languages are validated before any path is built. Names of new elements are validated, so traversal (..\..\), absolute paths, markup and control characters are refused; method source is stored literally (a ]]> inside a string stays text).

docs.title: Copilot: scope, checkpoints and activity
docs.text:
The MCP server Copilot uses is started with --activity-log. In that process only:

  1. Scope. Before an Edit or Create action, the server reads %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\agentSession.json, written by the extension when you run Set Copilot Scope…. An existing element outside the scope is refused with a message that lists the allowed elements. A new element is allowed and joins the scope.
  2. Checkpoint. While a checkpoint is open (Start Copilot Checkpoint), the server saves each element's state before its first change under checkpoints\<id>\. Revert Copilot Changes Since the Checkpoint… restores them through the metadata API; elements that did not exist are removed. Checkpoint ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$, so an id cannot be a path.
  3. Activity. Every tool call is logged to activity.jsonl (tool, arguments cut to a maximum length, duration, success), with a copy of your element before and after a write, for the Copilot Activity view and its diffs.

Listing and reverting checkpoints is only available in the extension's own process (--allow-data); the MCP server answers "Not available in this process."

See Copilot-Checkpoints-and-Scope and Copilot-Activity.

docs.title: Team rules and instructions
docs.text: .xpp/agent-rules.md is appended to the server's instructions (up to 20,000 characters) after the built-in rules, which say to follow the team rules where they are stricter. It refines the agent's behaviour; it does not change what the server enforces. See Team-Rules.

docs.title: Agents and production
docs.text: The generated Copilot agents share a rule: they change data, setup or metadata only after you allow it, and only in development, sandbox or build environments, never in production. This is an instruction to the model; the hard limits are the server checks above.

docs.title: Business data
docs.text:
• Where: the business database of the active environment: the local AxDB with Windows authentication on cloud-hosted and VHD environments, or a UDE's Azure SQL database with temporary credentials.
  • Credentials: Request Database Credentials calls the Dataverse action msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync (the same request Visual Studio makes), with the role Reader unless Writer is asked for explicitly. The result is kept per environment in VS Code's secret storage (Windows Credential Manager) until it expires.
  • Transport: the connection travels with each xpp/data request to the extension's server process. The server never stores or logs it.
  • Read-only by default: ReadOnlySql accepts a single SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT), ignoring keywords inside strings, quoted identifiers and comments. The data service also runs read-only batches in a transaction it always rolls back. Writes happen only when you turn on Allow changes in the SQL panel, with a confirmation each run.
  • Copilot: xpp_query_data is a VS Code language model tool, not an MCP tool. VS Code asks you to confirm each query ("Run a read-only query on the environment database"), showing the SQL. It runs read-only and rolled back, 50 rows by default and 500 at most, with output capped at 20,000 characters. The connection and credentials stay in the extension.

See Database-Access and SQL-Query-Panel.

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
Call When Microsoft sign-in Through VS Code's Microsoft account provider; optionally with your own Entra app (xpp.auth.clientId) Dataverse Web API of your environment Deploy, sync, tests, credentials, setup Power Platform developer tools service Connect to Environment (metadata and tool downloads) Microsoft Learn xpp_search_docs only: https with the exact host, default port and no user info, checked on the URL and on every redirect nuget.org Report Viewer runtime, only after you accept Microsoft's licence Public address service To fill in the address for database credentials GitHub Report a Problem… when you file the report as an issue

F&O Studio sends no telemetry. xpp.usageStatistics counts commands in VS Code's local state only; nothing is sent. Try Data Entity and Try Service Operation save requests as .http files without the access token.

docs.title: Hardening against hostile input
docs.text:
The server treats input from agents and webviews as untrusted:

  • Designer node paths, label file IDs, checkpoint ids and folders from callers are validated; wrapper_drift reads only a PackagesLocalDirectory.
  • Report RDL with a DTD is refused (no external entities). render_report does not overwrite an existing file unasked and refuses network paths; xpp_measure_image reads PNG images only and refuses network paths.
  • Cross-reference queries use parameters; SQL in element names is data.
  • Regular expressions in Search Code have a match timeout and the whole search a time limit.
  • Every JSON response escapes all control characters, so a response is always one valid line; malformed JSON, deep nesting and very large payloads do not stop the server.
  • Webviews use a Content-Security-Policy with nonces from crypto.randomBytes.

docs.title: How it is tested
docs.text:
node scripts/security-probes.js --model <your custom model> runs dynamic probes against the built server. Every probe must pass after a server change.

Area Examples of probes Object names traversal, absolute paths, markup, NUL, 5,000-character and empty names are refused; no file is written outside the metadata tree Ownership create_object in a standard model, update_object and xpp_update_object on Global, designer edits on CustGroup are refused Method source a CDATA break-out is stored literally Designer paths .. segments and very deep paths are refused Labels traversal in label file IDs and languages reads nothing; CRLF label IDs and standard label files are refused Checkpoints and drift traversal checkpoint ids, wrapper_drift on a non-package folder, references on standard models are refused Reports standard report designs are not written; DTDs, network paths and overwrites are refused; images only Agent tools SQL injection in names is data; catastrophic regex is bounded; non-Learn URLs, file:, metadata endpoints and other ports are refused Protocol malformed JSON, 20,000-level nesting, a 5 MB payload and unknown methods; the server stays up and every response is valid JSON

Probes on standard objects carry a payload the handler rejects before saving, so even a missing ownership check cannot change standard metadata. Unit tests in test/server check the write policy through the dispatcher. Review findings and their status are in docs/review-findings.md. See Testing-the-Extension.

docs.title: Code signing and supply chain
docs.text:
• The server exe in the published extension is built from the public source on GitHub Actions and signed through SignPath (certificate by SignPath Foundation) when signing is configured; each signing request is approved by hand. The Marketplace signs the extension package.
  • Microsoft's compiler package is used only to compile the server during the build, from a private feed; it is never part of the repository or the extension.
  • Pdb2Pdb is downloaded at a pinned version and checked against a pinned SHA-256.
  • The extension has no runtime npm dependencies.

See Release-Process.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The policy protects metadata and files F&O Studio writes. It does not limit what you do yourself in the SQL panel with Allow changes, or what X++ code you run with Run Snippet in Environment in a development environment.
  • The "never in production" rule of the agents is an instruction; use development environments and database Reader credentials for agent work.
  • Code you build and deploy runs with the environment's permissions; review it as usual (Review-My-Changes, Pre-Deploy-Checklist).

docs.title: Security Report
docs.text: Security Report… writes one document about a set of roles: the license each role needs and why, its read-only alternatives, its segregation of duties conflicts, its duties and every entry point it grants. It comes as Markdown, for a sign-off document, or as CSV, for Excel. Use it to hand security design to a client, an auditor or a functional lead without screenshots of the Application Explorer. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Sign-off of the roles you built or extended, before they go to test or production.
  • A review with the functional team of what each role can do and which license it costs.
  • A comparison in Excel of the entry points and grants of several roles.
  • Documentation of all roles of a model, including the standard roles the model extends.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). No sign-in or database.
  • For CSV, a place to save the file. Markdown opens in an editor tab; save it where you want.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text: From How Security View, on a role Right-click a role > Security Report…. If several roles are selected (Ctrl+click), the report covers the role you clicked and the selected roles. Security View title bar The file button (Security Report…). Dynamics 365 view Security > Security Report… Command Palette F&O Studio: Security Report…

docs.title: Choose the roles
docs.text:
When not started on a role, a picker asks for the scope:

Option Roles in the report Selected roles (N) The roles selected in the Security view. Shown only when roles are selected. Roles of model… Pick a model: every role of that model, plus every standard role the model extends with a role extension, sorted by name. Pick roles… Type part of a role name or label (empty: roles of your models), then select one or more roles.

docs.title: Choose the format
docs.text: Format Description in the picker Result Markdown sign-off document Opens in a new untitled editor, with the Markdown preview to the side. Save it with File > Save As. CSV for Excel A save dialog opens, proposing security-report.csv, security-report-<model>.csv or security-report-<role>.csv in the first workspace folder. The file is UTF-8 with a byte order mark so Excel reads it correctly. A notification offers Open.

docs.title: What the Markdown report contains
docs.text:
# Security report: model ContosoExtensions

Generated 2026-11-25 10:30 from the metadata (all packages). Licenses follow the menu items'
ViewUserLicense (Read) and MaintainUserLicense (other grants).

| Role | License | Duties | Privileges | Entry points |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ContosoOrderClerk | Activity | 4 | 12 | 37 |
| ContosoOrderSupervisor | ... | ... | ... | ... |

## ContosoOrderClerk (<role label>)

**License:** Activity (Activity: 5, Team Members: 20, None: 12 entry points)

Menu items that require it (first 5 of 5):
- <menu item> [Read,Update] via Role ContosoOrderClerk > Duty <duty> > Privilege <privilege> [Read,Update]

Read-only alternatives:
- <menu item>: Read,Update needs Activity; Read only would need Team Members

Segregation of duties: no conflicts with the default rules.

Duties: <duty>, <duty>, ...

| Entry point | Type | Grant | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| ContosoOrderStatus | MenuItemDisplay | Read | Team Members |

In detail:

  1. Title and note. Security report, with : model <name> when you picked a model, the date and time it was generated, and how licenses are computed.
  2. Summary table. One row per role: license, number of duties, privileges and entry points it reaches. A role that is not found has the row <role> | not found.
  3. One section per role, headed by the role name and its label as stored in the metadata:
  4. License with the number of entry points per license (see Analyze License for the rules).
  5. Menu items that require it: the entry points that drive an Activity or Operations license, up to 25, each with its grant and the paths that grant it.
  6. Read-only alternatives: up to 10 grants that would lower the license if they were Read only.
  7. Segregation of duties: the conflicts with the built-in rules, each as **<severity>** <rule>: <first duty> + <second duty> (<reason>), or "no conflicts with the default rules".
  8. Duties: every duty the role reaches (including sub-roles and role extensions), sorted.
  9. Entry points table: every entry point the role reaches, sorted by name, with type, merged grant and the license that grant needs. Up to 400 rows; a last row says how many more there are.

docs.title: What the CSV contains
docs.text:
One header row and one row per entry point of each role:

Column Content Role The role name. License The role's license. Duty or role path The first path that grants the entry point, for example Role TradeSalesClerk > Duty <duty> > Privilege <privilege> [Read]. Privilege Empty; the privilege is the last step of the path. Entry point type MenuItemDisplay, MenuItemOutput or MenuItemAction. Entry point The menu item name. Grant The merged grant, for example Read,Update,Create,Delete. Entry point license The license this grant needs.

Roles that are not found are left out of the CSV. Values with commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: None. The report always uses the built-in segregation of duties rules, even when xpp.security.sodRulesFile is set; run Segregation of Duties to check your own rules.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Command xpp.security.report in src/security/index.ts (report). CSV is saved by exportText in src/security/securityPanel.ts.
  • The extension calls the server's security language action with op: 'report', the roles or the model, and the format.
  • server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs (Report) runs License, Expand and SegregationOfDuties (built-in rules) for each role over the cached security index and writes the text. With a model and no roles, it takes the roles whose model is that model or that the model extends.
  • Copilot agents produce the same report with xpp_analyze_security op=report (roles or model, format markdown or csv); see Agent Tools: Analysis.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Metadata only: no users, no role assignments, nothing from the environment.
  • Role labels are written as stored (a label ID such as @SYS12345 is not translated in the report).
  • Up to 25 license drivers, 10 read-only alternatives and 400 entry points per role in the Markdown report. The CSV has every entry point.
  • Data entity and table permissions are not listed in the report.
  • Segregation of duties uses the built-in rules only.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Give roles, or a model whose roles (or role extensions) to report." The picked model has no roles and extends none. Pick another model, or pick roles. A role row says not found The role name is not in the metadata, or the index is stale. Check the name; click Refresh Security in the Security View. Conflicts from your rules file are missing The report uses the built-in rules. Run Check Segregation of Duties for your rules and attach its export.

docs.title: Security View
docs.text: The Security view lists the security roles of your models and the standard roles your models extend, each with the user license it needs. You expand a role down to its sub-roles, duties, privileges and finally the entry points, data entities and tables it grants, with the grant and the license of each entry point. It replaces the round trip through the Application Explorer's Security nodes in Visual Studio, where a role's license and its effective access are not shown at all.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You changed a role, duty or privilege and want to see what a role now grants and which license it needs.
  • You want to know which duties and privileges a role extension of your model adds to a standard role.
  • You look for a standard role by name or label (for example every role with "clerk" in its label) to reuse it.
  • You start one of the other security analyses from a role, duty, privilege or entry point: Analyze License, Who Can Access, Segregation of Duties and the Security Report.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration (see Select Environment). The view reads the metadata of every package of that configuration on disk. It works the same on unified developer environments (UDE), cloud-hosted environments and VHDs.
  • No sign-in, no database and no deployed environment are needed. The view shows what the installed code says, not which users have which roles.
  • "Your models" are the models in the custom metadata folder of the active configuration (the folder new elements are saved to).

docs.title: Open the view
docs.text:
The Security view is in the F&O Studio side bar, below D365FO Project. It starts collapsed: click its title to expand it. The view has two groups:

Group What it lists Your roles Roles that belong to one of your models, plus standard roles that one of your models extends with a role extension. Each role shows its user license. Up to 500 roles. All roles Every role in every package, by name. Up to 2,000 roles; use the filter to narrow the list. No license is computed here, to keep the list fast.

Nothing loads until you expand a group. The first expand reads the security metadata of all packages, which can take up to a minute (the group's tooltip says so). After that the data is cached and later expands are fast.

docs.title: Read a role
docs.text:
Each role node shows:

  • the role name, with a shield icon;
  • in Your roles, its license (Team Members, Activity, Operations, Self-serve, None...) and ext when one of your models extends it. The shield is coloured by license: orange for Operations, yellow for Activity, green for Team Members;
  • a tooltip with the label, the name and type, the model, the license and "Extended by your models" when that applies.

If your models have no roles and extend none, Your roles shows "Your models have no roles and extend none."

docs.title: Expand down to the grants
docs.text:
Expanding a node shows one level of the hierarchy:

Node Children Role Sub-roles (description sub-role), then duties, then privileges added directly to the role. Items added by a role extension say (added by <extension name>). Duty Its privileges, including privileges added by duty extensions. Privilege Its entry points (menu items, with the grant and the license that grant needs, for example Read,Update - Operations), its data entity permissions and its table permissions (with the grant).

Duties and privileges show their label when it differs from the name. A node with no children shows "Empty".

Entry points (menu items), data entities and tables are leaves. Clicking one opens it the way the Application Explorer does.

docs.title: Filter the roles
docs.text:
1. Click Filter Roles… (the filter icon in the view's title bar).
  2. Type part of a role name or label and press Enter.

The filter applies to All roles: the group opens by itself, its description says matching '<text>' and the view's description shows filter: <text>. Labels are matched in en-US. To remove the filter, click Clear Role Filter (the filled filter icon that replaces the filter button while a filter is set).

docs.title: Actions in the view
docs.text:
Title bar of the view:

Button Command Filter icon Filter Roles… / Clear Role Filter Checklist icon Find Security Gaps (Find Security Gaps) Law icon Check Segregation of Duties (Segregation of Duties) File icon Security Report… (Security Report) Refresh icon Refresh Security ... menu Edit Segregation of Duties Rules

Right-click menu of a node:

Node Commands Role Open Designer, Analyze License, Check Segregation of Duties, Security Report… Duty, privilege Open Designer, Analyze License Menu item, data entity, table Open Designer, Who Can Access

Analyze License (on roles, duties and privileges) and Who Can Access (on entry points, data entities and tables) are also inline buttons that appear when you hover the node.

The view allows multi-select (Ctrl+click). When you select several roles and run Security Report… on one of them, the report covers all selected roles (see Security Report).

docs.title: Refresh
docs.text: The cache is rebuilt automatically when security, menu item or data entity files are added to or removed from a package. Editing an existing file does not always change what the cache checks, so after you change a role, duty or privilege, click Refresh Security to reread the metadata. Refresh also clears the expanded nodes.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: The view has no settings of its own. Segregation of Duties uses xpp.security.sodRulesFile.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The view is src/security/securityView.ts (SecurityTreeProvider); the commands are registered in src/security/index.ts.
  • Every request goes to the F&O Studio server's security language action with an op: roles (the two groups, with customOnly and withLicense for Your roles), children (one level below a node) and refresh.
  • On the server, server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs builds one index from the XML files of every package: AxSecurityRole, AxSecurityRoleExtension, AxSecurityDuty, AxSecurityDutyExtension, AxSecurityPrivilege, the three menu item types and the data entity names. Role and duty extensions are merged into their base role or duty, and the index remembers which extension added what.
  • The index is cached in the server process. Its cache key is the number of these folders and their last write times; Refresh Security forces a rebuild.
  • The license of each role is computed as described in Analyze License.
  • Labels are resolved from the en-US label files.
  • Clicking an entry point, data entity or table uses the same open command as the Application Explorer.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The view reads metadata only. It does not show users, user role assignments or anything from a running environment. Ask the F&O Security & License agent for live data (see Copilot Agents).
  • All roles stops at 2,000 roles and Your roles at 500.
  • Role licenses are shown only in Your roles. For any other role, run Analyze License on it.
  • Labels are shown in en-US.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Expanding a group takes a long time The first load reads the security metadata of all packages. Wait; the next expands use the cache. A change to a role does not show The cache did not notice an edit of an existing file. Click Refresh Security. "Your models have no roles and extend none." No role and no role extension is in a model of the custom metadata folder. Expected; use All roles to browse standard roles. "No roles match ''." The filter matches no role name or en-US label. Change or clear the filter. A node shows an error message The server request failed (for example the server is not running). Expand the node again; the failed result is not cached. Check the F&O Studio output.

docs.title: Segregation of Duties
docs.text: Check Segregation of Duties finds roles that hold two duties one person should not have together, such as maintaining vendors and paying them. It checks your roles (or one role) against a set of rules: ten built-in rules for classic financial controls, or your own rules in a JSON file you keep with your code. D365FO has segregation of duties rules in the running application; F&O Studio checks the metadata on your machine, before the role is deployed. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You extend a standard role with new duties and want to make sure you do not create a conflict.
  • You design a new role from several standard duties.
  • You prepare security for sign-off by auditors or the client's controllers (the Security Report includes the built-in checks).
  • Your organization has its own conflict rules and you want every developer to check against them.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). No sign-in or database.
  • To check your own rules, a rules file (see below). Without one, the built-in rules are used.

docs.title: Run the check
docs.text:
From How Security View Right-click a role > Check Segregation of Duties, or the law button in the view's title bar. Application Explorer or the D365FO project view Right-click a role (or a role extension) > Check Segregation of Duties. Element Designer Title bar menu of a role > Check Segregation of Duties. Dynamics 365 view Security > Segregation of Duties… Command Palette F&O Studio: Check Segregation of Duties

Run on a role, it checks that role. Run from the title bar, the Dynamics 365 view or the Command Palette, you choose:

  • Roles of your models: every role in your models and every role your models extend with a role extension.
  • Pick a role…: type part of a role name or label (empty lists the roles of your models), then pick one role.

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
For each role, F&O Studio collects every duty the role reaches: its own duties, duties added by role extensions, and the duties of its sub-roles (recursively). A rule is a pair of duties (First, Second). The role conflicts with the rule when it reaches both duties.

Rules whose duties do not exist in the installed application are skipped and listed, so a rules file written for one version still runs on another.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
The security panel opens, titled Segregation of duties (or Segregation of duties: <role>):

  • Summary: N role(s), N rule(s) checked, N conflict(s). Rules: <file path or built-in> (Edit rules). Edit rules runs Edit Segregation of Duties Rules.
  • Conflicts:
Column Meaning Role The role; click it to run Analyze License on it. Rule The rule's Name. Severity The rule's Severity. High rows have a red bar, any other severity a yellow bar. Reason The rule's Reason. First, Second The two duties; click one to open it in the designer.
  • When there is no conflict: "No conflicts."
  • Skipped rules: each skipped rule with the duties that were not found.

Copy as Markdown and Export… copy or save the result (default file name sod.md, or sod-<role>.md).

docs.title: Built-in rules
docs.text:
Name First duty Second duty Severity Reason Vendor master vs vendor payments VendVendorMasterMaintain PaymVendorPaymentsMaintain High Create or change a vendor (bank account) and pay it. Vendor master vs vendor invoices VendVendorMasterMaintain VendInvoiceVendorInvoicesMaintain High Create a vendor and invoice it. Purchase orders vs vendor invoices PurchOrderMaintain VendInvoiceVendorInvoicesMaintain Medium Order and invoice the same goods. Vendor payments vs payment approval PaymVendorPaymentsMaintain PaymVendorPaymentTransactionsApprove High Enter and approve the same payment. Bank accounts vs vendor payments BankBankAccountsMaintain PaymVendorPaymentsMaintain High Change bank accounts and pay. Customer master vs customer payments CustCustomersMaintain PaymCustomerPaymentsMaintain Medium Create a customer and post its payments. Customer payments vs payment approval PaymCustomerPaymentsMaintain PaymCustPaymentTransactionsApprove Medium Enter and approve the same payment. Credit limits vs sales orders CredManCustCreditAdjustmentsMaintain SalesOrderMaintain Medium Raise a credit limit and sell against it. Fixed assets vs fixed asset approval AssetFixedAssetsMaintain AssetFixedAssetsApprove Medium Create and approve the same asset. Security administration vs journals SysSecSecurityMaintain LedgerJournalsAndTransactionsMaintain High Grant yourself access and post.

Any of these duties that does not exist in your application version makes its rule show under Skipped rules.

docs.title: The rules file format
docs.text:
The rules file is a JSON array. Each rule is an object with five properties:

Property Meaning Name A short name shown in the Rule column. First The name of the first duty (AxSecurityDuty). Second The name of the second duty. Severity Free text. High is shown in red; anything else (for example Medium, Low) in yellow. Reason Why the pair is a conflict, shown in the Reason column.

Example with one built-in rule and one rule on a custom duty:

[
    {
        "Name": "Vendor master vs vendor payments",
        "First": "VendVendorMasterMaintain",
        "Second": "PaymVendorPaymentsMaintain",
        "Severity": "High",
        "Reason": "Create or change a vendor (bank account) and pay it."
    },
    {
        "Name": "Order status override vs sales orders",
        "First": "ContosoOrderStatusOverrideMaintain",
        "Second": "SalesOrderMaintain",
        "Severity": "Medium",
        "Reason": "Change an order's status and enter orders."
    }
]

Write the property names exactly as above. The file replaces the built-in rules: copy the built-in rules you want to keep into it.

docs.title: Create and edit the file
docs.text:
Run Edit Segregation of Duties Rules (Security view ... menu, Dynamics 365 view Security group, the Edit rules link in a result, or the Command Palette):

  1. If xpp.security.sodRulesFile is set, it opens that file.
  2. If it is empty and a folder is open, it uses .xpp\sod-rules.json in the first workspace folder. With no folder open, it asks where to save the file.
  3. If the file does not exist, it is created with the ten built-in rules.
  4. If the setting was empty, it is set to the file's full path: in the workspace settings when a folder is open, in the user settings otherwise.
  5. The file opens in the editor. Save it; the next check uses it.

Commit .xpp\sod-rules.json with your code so the whole team checks against the same rules.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.security.sodRulesFile empty Path of the rules file. Empty uses the built-in rules. A relative path is under the first workspace folder; ${workspaceFolder} is replaced by the first workspace folder.

See Settings Reference.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Commands xpp.security.checkSod and xpp.security.editSodRules in src/security/index.ts. Before calling the server, the extension reads the rules file and checks that it is valid JSON.
  • It calls the server's security language action with op: 'sod', the role (if any) and the file's text as rulesJson.
  • server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs (SegregationOfDuties) parses the rules, falls back to DefaultSodRules when there are none, skips rules with a missing duty, expands each role with the same expansion as Analyze License and reports every rule whose two duties the role reaches.
  • Copilot uses xpp_analyze_security with op=sod; agents can pass their own rules in rulesJson with the same format (see Agent Tools: Analysis).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Rules are duty pairs only. Conflicts between privileges, or between duties held through two different roles of the same user, are not checked: the check works per role and does not know user role assignments.
  • The Security Report always uses the built-in rules, not your rules file.
  • Metadata only: segregation of duties rules configured in the environment are not read.
  • Recent security edits may need Refresh Security in the Security View.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The segregation of duties rules file ... was not found. Fix xpp.security.sodRulesFile or clear it to use the built-in rules." The setting points to a missing file. Correct the path, clear the setting, or run Edit Segregation of Duties Rules after clearing it. "sod-rules.json is not valid JSON: ..." Syntax error in the file. Fix the JSON at the position the message gives. The summary names your file but the built-in rules seem to run The file is valid JSON but not an array of rule objects, or the array is empty; the server then uses the built-in rules. Make the file a JSON array of objects with Name, First, Second, Severity, Reason. A rule is under Skipped rules One of its duties does not exist in this application version (or is misspelt). Check the duty name with Open Element. "Role '' not found." The role is not in the metadata or the index is stale. Check the name; click Refresh Security.
