Source: Segregation-of-Duties on the wiki.

docs.title: Select Environment
docs.text: Select Environment… switches the window to another environment that is already connected on this machine. Each workspace remembers its own environment, so two VS Code windows can work with two environments (or two application versions of different environments) at the same time. Switching does not reload the window: the metadata servers restart and the views reload. Visual Studio has one active configuration per machine; F&O Studio keeps that machine-wide configuration as the fallback and lets each workspace choose.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You work with more than one unified developer environment, for example a personal environment and a shared one.
  • You opened a second workspace for another environment and want it to use that environment's metadata.
  • You want a workspace to go back to your default environment.

To add an environment that is not on this machine yet, use Connect to Environment. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments there is nothing to select; see Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• At least one environment connected on this machine with Connect to Environment…, or with Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools. Both write configuration files to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig.
  • For a workspace-specific choice, open a folder or workspace. With no folder open, the choice is stored as your default.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the picker in one of these ways:
  2. Status bar: click the environment item (it shows the environment name), then Select Environment….
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Environment group > Select Environment….
  4. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Select Environment….
  5. The Get started walkthrough: Select an Environment.
  6. The picker's title is Environment for this workspace when a folder is open, or Default environment when none is. The placeholder shows the current environment (or "machine-wide configuration"), or "No environment is connected on this machine yet."
  7. Each entry is one environment:
  8. Label: the org name (the first part of the Dataverse host).
  9. Description: the application version; (current) is added to the one in use.
  10. Detail: the web client URL from the configuration (CloudInstanceURL), when it has one.
  11. You can type to filter on the name, version or URL.
  12. Pick an environment. F&O Studio finds its Dataverse URL (see How it works). If it cannot, it asks: Dataverse URL of , prefilled with https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com. The URL must start with https://<org>. of the picked environment.
  13. The window switches. The status bar briefly shows X++ environment: <org> (<version>).

    14. Other entries at the bottom of the picker:

    Entry What it does Connect to Another Environment… Runs Connect to Environment. Use the Default Environment Shown only when this workspace has its own choice. Removes it, so the workspace follows xpp.environmentUrl again (or the machine-wide configuration when that setting is empty). The description names the default environment.

    Picking the environment that is already current does nothing.

docs.title: The status bar item and environment menu
docs.text:
The status bar item on the left shows the active environment's name with a server icon. It shows a warning icon when:

  • the selected environment has no metadata on this machine, so F&O Studio uses the machine-wide configuration (the tooltip says " has no metadata on this machine; this is the machine-wide configuration. Connect to Environment downloads it."), or
  • the Version Drift Guard found a newer application version on the environment.

    • The tooltip also shows the application version, the web client URL and whether this is a cloud-hosted or VHD environment or the machine-wide configuration shared with Visual Studio. Clicking the item (command F&O Studio: Environment…) opens a menu:

    Menu entry Command Shown on Update Metadata to … Connect to Environment… for the new version when drift is found Select Environment… Select Environment… all Connect to Environment… Connect to Environment… all Check Environment Connection Check Environment Connection all Check Application Version Check Environment Application Version UDE Clean Up Old Versions… Clean Up Old Application Versions… UDE Sign In (pac) Sign In to Environment (pac) UDE Database… Database all Show Active Configuration Show Active Environment all

    The Environment group of the Dynamics 365 view has the same entries (without Check Application Version and Database). While Connect to Environment… runs, the group shows the setup phases instead.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.environmentUrl empty Dataverse URL of your default unified developer environment (user setting). Every window without its own choice uses it. Changing it switches those windows.

The per-workspace choice is not a setting. It is stored in VS Code's workspace state (key xpp.environmentUrl), so it is never written to .vscode/settings.json or committed with the repository. Every developer has an environment of their own.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The selection is in src/environment.ts; the picker, status bar item and Environment group are in src/environmentPicker.ts. Reading configurations is in the core library: core/src/environment/discovery.ts.

docs.title: Which environment a window uses
docs.text:
The selected Dataverse URL is, in order:

  1. the workspace's own choice (workspace state), else
  2. the xpp.environmentUrl user setting, else
  3. none.

When a URL is selected and this machine has a configuration for its org, that configuration is used. Otherwise F&O Studio falls back to:

  1. the machine-wide configuration named in the registry value CurrentMetadataConfig under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations (shared with Visual Studio), if it is a .json file that exists, else
  2. a configuration made from the local AOS of a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, else
  3. the error "No active D365FO configuration found. Connect to a unified developer environment first, or work on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (AosService\PackagesLocalDirectory)."

The result is cached for 5 seconds, because many parts of the extension ask at the same time (status bar, trees, the MCP server).

docs.title: Listing environments
docs.text: The picker lists the files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig named <org>___<application version>.json. When an org has several (an application update leaves the old configuration), only the newest version is listed. Environments are sorted by name.

docs.title: Finding the Dataverse URL
docs.text: A configuration file only names the org. F&O Studio assumes the UDE's finance and operations host https://<org>.operations.dynamics.com and looks up <org>.crm.dynamics.com, <org>.crm2.dynamics.com up to the other regional Dataverse hosts in DNS. The first one that resolves is used. If none does, you are asked for the URL.

docs.title: Storing the choice
docs.text:
When you select an environment (or Connect to Environment… finishes):

  • With a folder open, the URL goes into the workspace state. The user setting xpp.environmentUrl is also set, but only if it is still empty: your first environment becomes the default.
  • With no folder open, the URL goes into the user setting xpp.environmentUrl.

Check Environment Connection does not switch: it only selects the environment when none is selected yet, and otherwise offers Use This Environment.

docs.title: What happens on a switch
docs.text:
An environment change event restarts both metadata server processes (designers and language features), refreshes the Application Explorer and the project view, refreshes open element designers and reloads open code views that have no unsaved changes. The MCP server definition for Copilot changes too, so Copilot's tools use the new configuration (the server is started with --config <configuration file>). The Version Drift Guard checks the new environment.

When the active environment is cloud-hosted or VHD, the context key xpp.localEnvironment is set. It hides UDE-only commands from the Command Palette (Check Environment Application Version, Clean Up Old Application Versions…, Deploy Models to Environment and the (pac) commands), and the Dynamics 365 view hides its UDE-only entries (such as Run Tests and Deploy Models to Online Environment…).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only environments connected on this machine are listed. Use Connect to Another Environment… to add one.
  • Only the newest application version of each org is listed. To go back to an older version's configuration, the file must be the newest one for that org.
  • Finding the Dataverse URL assumes the UDE naming (<org>.operations.dynamics.com and <org>.crmN.dynamics.com); otherwise you type it.
  • The machine-wide registry value is changed only by Connect to Environment…, not by Select Environment…. Visual Studio keeps using its own active configuration when you switch in VS Code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The picker is empty ("No environment is connected on this machine yet.") No configuration in XPPConfig Run Connect to Environment…. Status bar shows a warning and the tooltip says the selected environment has no metadata on this machine The workspace or default points to an org without a configuration here Run Connect to Environment… for it, or Use the Default Environment. You are asked for the Dataverse URL after picking The regional Dataverse host could not be found by DNS Paste the Environment URL from the Power Platform admin center. "The URL must start with https://." The URL entered belongs to another org Enter the URL of the picked environment. "No environment selected. Run "F&O Studio: Connect to Environment" or "F&O Studio: Select Environment" first." A cloud operation (deploy, tests, database credentials) needs a selected UDE Select or connect an environment. The status bar item is hidden No configuration could be loaded Connect to an environment, or check the error with Show Active Environment.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text: This page lists every setting F&O Studio contributes, with its type, default value, allowed values, scope and the feature it affects. It also covers the two other places where you configure F&O Studio: the xpp debug configuration in .vscode/launch.json and the xpp task type in .vscode/tasks.json.

docs.title: Opening the settings
docs.text:
• Run F&O Studio: Options… from the Command Palette, or click Options… at the bottom of the Dynamics 365 view. It opens the Settings editor filtered on F&O Studio (@ext:MNazmi.xpp-vscode).
  • Or open File > Preferences > Settings and search for xpp..
  • The code intelligence switches are also in the Dynamics 365 view under Code Intelligence > Configure Code Intelligence…. See Code-Intelligence-Settings.

All settings are in the F&O Studio section and start with xpp..

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
VS Code applies a setting at one of several levels. Four F&O Studio settings declare a scope:

Scope Meaning in VS Code Settings machine Only in the user settings of this machine; a workspace cannot set it xpp.build.msbuildPath, xpp.pacPath, xpp.debuggerProxyPath, xpp.trace.manifestFolder window User or workspace settings xpp.project (not declared) VS Code's default: user, workspace or workspace folder settings all other settings

xpp.project is special: F&O Studio writes it into a project's own workspace, and a value in your user settings is not used.

docs.title: All settings at a glance
docs.text:
Setting Type Default Affects xpp.project string "" D365FO-Projects xpp.environmentUrl string "" Select-Environment xpp.auth.clientId string "" Sign-In-and-Authentication xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl string "" Copy-Name-and-Open-in-Browser xpp.build.crossReference boolean true Build-Project-and-Model xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules boolean false Build-Project-and-Model xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild boolean true Build-Project-and-Model xpp.build.restartLocalAos boolean true Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments xpp.build.msbuildPath string "" Solution-View-and-CSharp-References xpp.pacPath string "" Power-Platform-CLI xpp.debuggerProxyPath string "" Debugger xpp.trace.manifestFolder string "" Analyze-Trace xpp.codeIntelligence.outline boolean true Outline-and-Workspace-Symbols xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation boolean true Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command, Call-and-Type-Hierarchy xpp.codeIntelligence.workspaceSymbols boolean true Outline-and-Workspace-Symbols xpp.codeIntelligence.completion boolean true Completion-and-Signature-Help xpp.codeIntelligence.hover boolean true Hover xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens boolean true Code-Lens xpp.codeIntelligence.syntaxCheck boolean true Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings boolean true Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting boolean true Formatting-and-Folding xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex boolean true Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command, Event-Handlers xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting boolean false Code-Intelligence-Settings xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave boolean false Compiler-Diagnostics xpp.erd.depth integer (1–5) 1 Entity-Relationship-Diagram xpp.erd.direction string (enum) "outgoing" Entity-Relationship-Diagram xpp.erd.fields string (enum) "keys" Entity-Relationship-Diagram xpp.usageStatistics boolean false Usage-Statistics xpp.git.baseBranch string "" Review-My-Changes, Show-Changed-Elements, Git-Changes-in-the-Project-View xpp.security.sodRulesFile string "" Segregation-of-Duties

The sections below describe each setting.

docs.title: xpp.project
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty. Scope: window.
  • The D365FO project (.rnrproj) of this workspace. Open D365FO Project… sets it in the project's own workspace. A value in the user settings is not used.
  • You normally never edit it by hand: open projects with Open D365FO Project….
  • Affects: D365FO-Projects, the project status bar item (Status-Bar), and the project the agent tools work on (MCP-Agent-Tools).

docs.title: xpp.environmentUrl
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty.
  • The Dataverse URL of your default unified developer environment, for example https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com.
  • Select Environment… chooses another environment per workspace, so two VS Code windows can work with two environments.
  • Affects: Select-Environment, Connect-to-Environment.

docs.title: xpp.auth.clientId
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty.
  • An optional Microsoft Entra application (client) ID to sign in with, for tenants that do not allow VS Code's default sign-in for Dataverse. When set, F&O Studio asks VS Code's Microsoft account provider for a token with that client ID.
  • Affects: every Dataverse call (connect, deploy, sync, tests, database credentials, debugger). See Sign-In-and-Authentication.

docs.title: xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty.
  • The web client URL, for example https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com. Open in Browser and Open Table Browser use it when the selected environment's configuration has none.
  • Affects: Copy-Name-and-Open-in-Browser.

docs.title: xpp.build.crossReference
docs.text:
• Type: boolean. Default: true.
  • Updates the cross-reference database while building, so where-used (Find References, rename, references diagrams) includes your own code.
  • Affects: Build-Project-and-Model, Find-All-References.

docs.title: xpp.build.runAppCheckerRules
docs.text:
• Type: boolean. Default: false.
  • Runs the AppChecker rules during the build.
  • Affects: Build-Project-and-Model, Best-Practice-Checks.

docs.title: xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild
docs.text:
• Type: boolean. Default: true.
  • Saves unsaved X++ code views before a build, so the compiler sees your latest changes. When it is off, unsaved code views are compiled from the metadata on disk, without your unsaved edits.
  • Affects: Build-Project-and-Model.

docs.title: xpp.build.restartLocalAos
docs.text:
• Type: boolean. Default: true.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD environments only: after a successful build, restarts the AOS hosts that are running (IIS Express or the AOS application pool in IIS, and the batch service) so they load the new build, as Visual Studio does. Batch tasks that were running are cut off.
  • Not used on unified developer environments.
  • Affects: Cloud-Hosted-and-VHD-Environments, Debugging-on-Cloud-Hosted.

docs.title: xpp.build.msbuildPath
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty. Scope: machine.
  • The MSBuild.exe used to build the C# projects and assemblies your X++ project references. They are copied into the package before X++ is compiled and deployed, as Visual Studio does.
  • Empty: Visual Studio's or the Build Tools' MSBuild, else the .NET SDK's (dotnet msbuild).
  • If the path you set does not exist, the build stops with "MSBuild not found at ... (setting xpp.build.msbuildPath)."
  • Affects: Solution-View-and-CSharp-References, Build-Project-and-Model, Deploy-to-Environment.

docs.title: xpp.pacPath
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty (uses pac on the PATH). Scope: machine.
  • Path to the Power Platform CLI. Only the (pac) commands use it: Sign In to Environment (pac) and Initialize Deployment Solution (pac). Deploy and database sync do not need pac.
  • Affects: Power-Platform-CLI.

docs.title: xpp.debuggerProxyPath
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty. Scope: machine.
  • Path to Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe. Empty: the FinOps tools that Connect to Environment… installed.
  • If the proxy is not found, debugging stops with "Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.DebuggerProxy.exe was not found. Run F&O Studio: Connect to Environment, or set xpp.debuggerProxyPath."
  • Affects: Debugger, Debugging-Standard-Code.

docs.title: xpp.trace.manifestFolder
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty. Scope: machine.
  • Folder with the Dynamics 365 trace event manifests (DynamicsAXXppExecutionTraces.man) for Analyze Trace….
  • Empty: F&O Studio looks in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin\Monitoring, AosService\WebRoot\Monitoring or the registered trace providers' folder.
  • Affects: Analyze-Trace.

docs.title: Code intelligence
docs.text:
Each of these switches one code intelligence feature on or off. All of them are also in the Dynamics 365 view under Code Intelligence > Configure Code Intelligence…, which shows which ones are on. See Code-Intelligence-Settings.

Setting Default What it turns on Page xpp.codeIntelligence.outline true Outline and breadcrumbs: methods and members of the open object Outline-and-Workspace-Symbols xpp.codeIntelligence.navigation true Go to Implementations (overrides, Chain of Command, event handlers, subclasses), call hierarchy and type hierarchy Implementations-and-Chain-of-Command, Call-and-Type-Hierarchy xpp.codeIntelligence.workspaceSymbols true Go to Symbol in Workspace (Ctrl+T) over elements and methods of all models Outline-and-Workspace-Symbols xpp.codeIntelligence.completion true Completion after . and ::, label references in strings, keywords; signature help Completion-and-Signature-Help xpp.codeIntelligence.hover true Hover details: label texts, EDT and enum details, method signatures Hover xpp.codeIntelligence.codeLens true Code lens: reference, override, Chain of Command and handler counts; what a CoC or handler method wraps Code-Lens xpp.codeIntelligence.syntaxCheck true Live syntax check with the X++ compiler's parser Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings true Calls to methods and uses of classes and tables marked [SysObsolete] are reported in Problems (as errors when the attribute says so) Syntax-Check-and-Obsolete-Warnings xpp.codeIntelligence.formatting true Format Document / Format Selection with a 4-space Allman layout Formatting-and-Folding xpp.codeIntelligence.eventHandlerIndex true Includes form and data event handlers ([FormControlEventHandler], [DataEventHandler], ...), which the cross-reference database does not record. The first scan takes about a minute and is cached Event-Handlers xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting false Semantic highlighting: colours classes, tables, enums, EDTs, methods and fields. Looks up every identifier of the open document (slow) Code-Intelligence-Settings xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave false Builds the project with the X++ compiler after you save code, so semantic errors reach Problems (about 10 s per save) Compiler-Diagnostics

The last two are off by default because they are slow. eventHandlerIndex is on by default but is slow the first time.

docs.title: Entity relationship diagram
docs.text:
These are the defaults the ERD starts with; you can change all three in the diagram itself.

Setting Type Default Values xpp.erd.depth integer 1 1 to 5: levels of related tables the diagram follows from the table it starts from xpp.erd.direction string "outgoing" outgoing: tables the table refers to (its relations); incoming: tables that refer to the table (their relations to it); both xpp.erd.fields string "keys" keys: primary key and the fields of the drawn relations; all: all fields

Affects: Entity-Relationship-Diagram.

docs.title: xpp.git.baseBranch
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty.
  • The branch your work is compared with, for example main. Show Changed Elements, Review My Changes and the change marks in the project view include what the current branch changed since it left this branch.
  • Empty: only uncommitted changes.
  • Affects: Review-My-Changes, Show-Changed-Elements, Git-Changes-in-the-Project-View.

docs.title: xpp.security.sodRulesFile
docs.text:
• Type: string. Default: empty (built-in rules).
  • A JSON file with segregation of duties rules. Each rule has Name, First, Second, Severity and Reason; First and Second are duty names.
  • Edit Segregation of Duties Rules creates the file from the built-in rules.
  • A relative path is resolved under the first workspace folder.
  • If the file is missing, the check fails with "The segregation of duties rules file ... was not found. Fix xpp.security.sodRulesFile or clear it to use the built-in rules."
  • Affects: Segregation-of-Duties.

Example rule file:

[
  {
    "Name": "Vendor master vs vendor payments",
    "First": "VendVendorMasterMaintain",
    "Second": "PaymVendorPaymentsMaintain",
    "Severity": "High",
    "Reason": "Create or change a vendor (bank account) and pay it."
  }
]

This is one of the built-in rules. Run Edit Segregation of Duties Rules to get the full built-in list as a starting point.

docs.title: xpp.usageStatistics
docs.text:
• Type: boolean. Default: false.
  • Counts which F&O Studio commands you run, on this machine only. Nothing is sent anywhere. Show Usage Statistics lists the counts.
  • Affects: Usage-Statistics, Report-a-Problem.

docs.title: Example settings.json
docs.text:
{
  "xpp.environmentUrl": "https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com",
  "xpp.git.baseBranch": "main",
  "xpp.build.saveBeforeBuild": true,
  "xpp.codeIntelligence.semanticHighlighting": false,
  "xpp.erd.depth": 2,
  "xpp.erd.direction": "both"
}

docs.title: Debug configuration (launch.json)
docs.text:
The debugger works without a configuration: Launch Debugger starts it. To change it, add a configuration of type xpp to .vscode/launch.json (Run and Debug > create a launch.json file > X++). The only request type is attach.

Attribute Type Default Description processName string "AXHost.exe" Process to attach to. On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, for example Batch.exe to debug the batch server; without it the debugger attaches to the AOS of the runtime host type set in Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 options (IIS or IIS Express) justMyCode boolean true Step only through code that has symbols loaded. Turning it off makes every exception the environment throws go through the debugger, which can make the environment stop responding additionalModules array [] More modules whose symbols load, added to your packages and the module of each standard element with a breakpoint. Wildcards allowed. Each extra module makes loading slower symbolOptions object none Replaces F&O Studio's symbol options entirely (vsdbg symbolOptions). Use additionalModules to add modules instead logging object none vsdbg logging options, for example { "exceptions": false } to stop printing exceptions in the Debug Console sourceFileMap object none Extra source path mappings 
{
  "type": "xpp",
  "request": "attach",
  "name": "Attach to Dynamics 365",
  "justMyCode": true,
  "additionalModules": ["Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.Forms.*.netmodule"],
  "logging": { "exceptions": false }
}

See Debugger-Options for details.

docs.title: Task definition (tasks.json)
docs.text:
F&O Studio contributes the task type xpp. action is required.

Property Type Values Description action string buildProject, buildModel, deploy, syncDatabase buildProject reports the problems of the project's elements; buildModel those of the whole model; deploy deploys the package of the active project's model, as built on this machine, to the unified environment; syncDatabase synchronizes the database (through Dataverse on a unified environment, SyncEngine on cloud-hosted and VHD) model string model name Model to build. Defaults to the active project's model dbSync string None, Module, Full For deploy: the database sync after the deploy (Module synchronizes the deployed package). Default None mode string Full, Module For syncDatabase on a unified environment. Default Full modules string comma-separated For syncDatabase with mode Module. Defaults to the active project's model 
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    { "label": "Build project", "type": "xpp", "action": "buildProject", "group": "build" },
    { "label": "Deploy with module sync", "type": "xpp", "action": "deploy", "dbSync": "Module" }
  ]
}

See Build-Tasks.

docs.title: Settings that are not settings
docs.text:
Some choices are stored by F&O Studio itself, not in settings.json:

  • The environment selected with Select Environment… is remembered per workspace.
  • Temporary database credentials are kept in VS Code's secret storage until they expire. Forget Database Credentials removes them. See Database-Access.
  • Team rules for Copilot live in .xpp/agent-rules.md in your repository. See Team-Rules.
  • The active D365FO configuration (metadata folders, cross-reference database) comes from the registry and the XPPConfig JSON files that Visual Studio also uses. See Select-Environment and Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side.

Source: Settings-Reference on the wiki.

docs.title: Show Changed Elements
docs.text: Show Changed Elements lists the elements of your models that differ from Git: what you have not committed yet and, if you set a base branch, everything the current branch changed since it left that branch. It works on element level (a class, a table extension, a privilege), not on XML files, so you see your change set the way you think about it. The same list drives the Git change marks in the project view and on code view tabs, and it is the input of Review My Changes. Visual Studio has no direct equivalent; there you read the file list of Team Explorer or Git Changes.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you commit or open a pull request, to see which elements you touched.
  • When you come back to a branch and want to know what is on it.
  • To jump to a changed element quickly: pick it in the list and it opens.
  • To check that an element you expected to change really changed (for example after Copilot edited code).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your custom models must be in a Git repository. F&O Studio finds the repository from each model folder. Model folders are often junctions (symbolic links) from the custom metadata folder into the repository; F&O Studio resolves the real path first, so junctions work.
  • git must be on the PATH. F&O Studio runs the Git command line, not the VS Code Git extension.
  • Only your own models are checked (models in the custom metadata folder). Standard and ISV models in the reference packages are ignored.
  • Optional: set xpp.git.baseBranch to the branch your work is compared with (for example main).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Show Changed Elements from the Command Palette, or open the Dynamics 365 view and click Model and project > Show Changed Elements.
  2. A quick pick opens. Its title is Changed elements, or Changed elements (since main, plus uncommitted) when a base branch is set.
  3. Each entry shows:
Part Content Example Label Element name ContosoCustGroup_Extension Description Element type without the Ax prefix, the Git status letter, and (branch) when the change is only committed on the branch Class · M (branch) Detail Model name ContosoExtensions
  1. Type to filter. The filter matches the name and the description, so typing Table also finds tables and table extensions by their type.
  2. Press Enter on an entry to open the element's designer. Deleted elements (status D) do not open, because they no longer exist in the metadata.

If nothing changed, you see the message "No changed elements in your models (they must be in a Git repository)."

docs.title: Status letters
docs.text:
The status letters are Git's own:

Letter Meaning Notes M Modified The element XML changed. A Added New element. Untracked files (?? in git status) count as added. D Deleted The element XML was removed. R Renamed The element is listed under its new name.

When an element is changed both on the branch and in the working tree, the uncommitted status wins and the (branch) suffix is not shown.

docs.title: Change marks in the project view and code view tabs
docs.text:
The same change list decorates elements in two places:

  • the elements in the project view (the solution view of your D365FO project);
  • the tabs of X++ code views (xpp: documents).

A changed element gets Git's letter as a badge and Git's colour for that status (the theme colours gitDecoration.modifiedResourceForeground, gitDecoration.addedResourceForeground, gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground, gitDecoration.renamedResourceForeground). The tooltip shows the element type and the status, for example Class · Modified, or Class · Modified on this branch when the change is only committed on the branch. Unchanged elements only get the element type as tooltip.

The marks refresh when you save any document and every 30 seconds. See Git Changes in the Project View for more on the project view marks.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Branch your work is compared with (e.g. main). Show Changed Elements, Review My Changes and the project view change marks then also include what the current branch changed since it left this branch. Empty: only uncommitted changes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The logic is in src/changes.ts (changedElements), the command in src/extension.ts.

For each custom model:

  1. F&O Studio resolves the model folder's real path (following junctions) and runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel there to find the repository. A model that is not in a repository is skipped.
  2. It runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <model path> for the uncommitted changes.
  3. With a base branch, it runs git merge-base HEAD <base> and then git diff --name-status <merge-base> HEAD -- <model path>. This is what the branch changed since it left the base, not the difference with the base branch's current tip, so later commits on the base do not show up as your changes.
  4. Each changed path is mapped to an element. Only files of the form <AxType>/<Name>.xml directly under the model folder count (for example AxClass/ContosoCustGroup_Extension.xml). Other files of the model, such as the model descriptor, are not elements and are left out.
  5. Elements are merged by type and name and sorted by type, then name.

Nothing is cached between calls, except the decorations, which keep the last list to know which marks changed. The check does not start the metadata server: it only reads Git and the model list.

Copilot agents get the same list through the xpp_diff_changes tool (uncommitted changes, plus the branch's changes with baseBranch). See Agent Tools: Build and Data.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Element level only. The list does not show which methods or properties changed; use Compare Code and Metadata or Element History for that.
  • Label files, .rnrproj files and other non-element files are not listed.
  • Your models must be in Git. Other version control systems (for example TFVC) are not supported.
  • If the base branch does not exist locally (for example main is only on the remote as origin/main), git merge-base fails and only uncommitted changes are shown. Set xpp.git.baseBranch to a name Git can resolve, such as origin/main.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No changed elements in your models (they must be in a Git repository)." The model folders are not inside a Git repository, git is not on the PATH, or nothing changed. Check that git status in the model folder works. Commit or link the model folder into a repository (see Source Control for X++). Branch changes are missing; only uncommitted changes appear. xpp.git.baseBranch is empty, or Git cannot resolve the branch name. Set xpp.git.baseBranch, for example to main or origin/main. A changed element is not listed. The element belongs to a standard or ISV model, or the file is not <AxType>/<Name>.xml under the model folder. Only your own models are checked. Picking an entry does nothing. The element was deleted (D). Deleted elements cannot be opened. Project view marks are out of date. The marks refresh on save and every 30 seconds. Save a file or wait a moment.

docs.title: Sign-In and Authentication
docs.text:
F&O Studio signs in to your unified developer environment (UDE) through VS Code's built-in Microsoft account, the same account system VS Code uses for Settings Sync and other Microsoft services. It never asks for a password itself, never stores tokens, and never handles credentials: VS Code shows the browser sign-in and keeps the session. This page explains which features sign in, to what, how to use your own Microsoft Entra app when your tenant blocks VS Code's default one, and what is stored where.

Visual Studio's equivalent is the account you use in Power Platform Tools' Connect to Dataverse.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Read this page when:

  • a sign-in prompt appears and you want to know why;
  • your tenant does not allow VS Code's sign-in for Dataverse and you need xpp.auth.clientId;
  • you work with environments in more than one tenant;
  • you want to know which credentials F&O Studio keeps.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A Microsoft Entra account with access to the environment's Dataverse org (for setup, deploy, sync and tests you need the rights Visual Studio's Power Platform Tools need for the same actions).
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD environments need no sign-in for metadata, build, database sync or debugging: everything is local. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Run a command that needs the environment, for example Connect to Environment… or Check Environment Connection.
  2. If VS Code has no session for that Dataverse org yet, it asks to sign in with Microsoft. Allow it; a browser window opens.
  3. Sign in with the account that has access to the environment.
  4. VS Code keeps the session. Later commands for the same org reuse it without a prompt.

To see or sign out of the session, use VS Code's Accounts menu (the person icon in the activity bar).

docs.title: What signs in, and to what
docs.text:
Feature Resource (scope <resource>/.default) Prompt Connect to Environment, Check Environment Connection Dataverse org, https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com Interactive if needed Deploy to Environment, Synchronize Database (UDE) Dataverse org Interactive if needed Run Tests, Test Explorer Dataverse org Interactive if needed Database Access: requesting temporary SQL credentials Dataverse org Interactive if needed Debugger on a UDE Dataverse org; the token is passed to Microsoft's debugger proxy (--accessToken) Interactive if needed Version Drift Guard Dataverse org Silent only: skipped when there is no session Try Data Entity (OData), Try Service Operation Finance and operations web client, https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com Interactive if needed Report a Problem (filing the issue) GitHub, scope public_repo Interactive if needed (pac) commands pac's own sign-in and profile store, not VS Code's account pac opens its own browser sign-in

All Dataverse sign-ins use the selected environment of the window (Select Environment). When you enter a finance and operations URL, F&O Studio first finds the org's regional Dataverse host and signs in to that.

docs.title: Using your own Microsoft Entra app
docs.text:
Some tenants block the application VS Code signs in with, or require admin consent for it. Then register an app in Microsoft Entra ID (or ask your administrator) and tell F&O Studio to use it:

  1. Ask your administrator for an app registration in your tenant that is allowed to sign users in to Dataverse from VS Code, or create one following your organisation's rules.
  2. In VS Code settings, set xpp.auth.clientId to the app's Application (client) ID.
  3. Run Check Environment Connection. VS Code signs in with your app.
{
    "xpp.auth.clientId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}

The client ID applies to the Dataverse sign-ins in the table above. It is not used by Try Data Entity (OData) and Try Service Operation, which sign in to the web client with VS Code's default app.

docs.title: Several tenants
docs.text: Each Dataverse sign-in asks VS Code for a session with the scope of that org (<org URL>/.default). When an environment is in another tenant, sign in with the account of that tenant when VS Code asks, and pick that account again later if VS Code offers several. For pac, Sign In to Environment (pac) keeps one named profile per environment (Power Platform CLI).

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.auth.clientId empty Optional Microsoft Entra app (client) ID to sign in with, if your tenant does not allow VS Code's default sign-in for Dataverse. xpp.environmentUrl empty Default environment; decides which org the sign-in is for. xpp.pacPath empty Path to pac for the (pac) commands, which sign in on their own.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The sign-in is in src/ude.ts:

  • getDataverseToken(url) calls VS Code's authentication API, vscode.authentication.getSession('microsoft', scopes, { createIfNone: true }), with the scope <url>/.default. When xpp.auth.clientId is set, the scope VSCODE_CLIENT_ID:<id> is added, which tells VS Code's Microsoft provider to use that app.
  • getDataverseTokenSilently(url) asks with { silent: true } and returns nothing instead of prompting.
  • dataverseTokens wraps both as the TokenProvider the core library expects (interactive: true or false).

The core library (core/src/host.ts, core/src/dataverse.ts) never signs in or shows UI itself: the host passes in the token provider. The same core is used by hosts outside VS Code (such as a Claude Code plugin), which supply their own sign-in. See Core Library.

The Dataverse client sends the token as Authorization: Bearer ... to https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/... with OData 4.0 headers. Error responses are reduced to Dataverse's error message.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
Item Where Notes Microsoft and GitHub sessions VS Code's account storage Managed by VS Code; sign out from the Accounts menu. Temporary SQL credentials for UDE databases VS Code's secret storage (Windows Credential Manager), one entry per environment Kept until they expire; never in settings or logs. See Database Access. pac profiles pac's own store Managed by pac. Access tokens Not stored by F&O Studio Requested when needed. The token for Try Service Operation is never written to the saved .http file.

The MCP server that Copilot uses gets no token: its tools work on local metadata. Data queries for Copilot go through the extension's own processes. See Security Model.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only VS Code's Microsoft account provider is used for Dataverse; there is no device-code or service-principal sign-in.
  • xpp.auth.clientId is one app for all environments.
  • The version drift check never prompts, so it stays quiet until another command has signed in.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Not signed in to https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com." You cancelled or closed the sign-in Run the command again and complete the sign-in. The sign-in fails with a consent or "application is blocked" error from Microsoft Entra Your tenant blocks VS Code's default app Set xpp.auth.clientId to an app your tenant allows. ... returned 401 or 403 from Dataverse The account has no access to the org, or lacks rights for the action Sign out from the Accounts menu and sign in with the right account; ask for access to the environment. You signed in with the wrong account VS Code reuses the session for that org Sign out of that account in the Accounts menu, then run the command again. No drift warning although the environment changed version No session yet; the guard only asks silently Run Check Environment Connection once. pac uses another account than F&O Studio pac signs in separately Sign In to Environment (pac) > Sign In Again.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text: F&O Studio ships X++ code snippets for the patterns D365FO developers write most: Chain of Command classes and wrappers, event handlers, SysOperation controller, service and contract, RunBase batch classes, table find() and exist(), parm methods, transactions with retry, select statements, SysTest classes and Infolog messages with labels. Type a prefix such as coc or tablefind and press Tab to insert the code with placeholders.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Start a Chain of Command class or a wrapper method without looking up the attribute syntax.
  • Write an event handler with the right attribute, event type and parameters.
  • Add the standard find() and exist() methods to a new table.
  • Write a transaction with retry on deadlock and update conflict the way standard code does.
  • Start a SysTest class.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An X++ editor: a code view of an element in your model, an .xpp file or an untitled X++ editor.
  • Snippets insert text only. They don't create elements: create the class first with New Element, Create Code Extension or a wizard, then add code with the snippets.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. In the code, type a prefix, for example tablefind.
  2. The suggestion list shows the snippet (with its description). Press Tab or Enter to insert it. Press Ctrl+Space if the list doesn't open.
  3. The first placeholder is selected. Type its value; every place that uses the same placeholder changes with it.
  4. Press Tab to go to the next placeholder, Shift+Tab to go back. Placeholders with a choice (for example the event type of a data event handler) show a list.
  5. The last Tab puts the cursor where the code goes ($0).

You can also run Insert Snippet from the command palette and pick from the list.

docs.title: Example: table find
docs.text:
Typing tablefind, then ContosoOrderTable, ContosoOrderId, orderId, orderTable, OrderId gives:

public static ContosoOrderTable find(ContosoOrderId _orderId, boolean _forUpdate = false)
{
    ContosoOrderTable orderTable;

    if (_orderId)
    {
        orderTable.selectForUpdate(_forUpdate);

        select firstonly orderTable
            where orderTable.OrderId == _orderId;
    }

    return orderTable;
}

docs.title: Example: Chain of Command wrapper
docs.text:
coc with SalesFormLetter and ContosoExtensions, then cocmethod inside it with run:

[ExtensionOf(classStr(SalesFormLetter))]
final class SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    public void run()
    {
        next run();

    }
}

docs.title: Chain of Command
docs.text: Prefixes Inserts coc, cocclass, extensionof [ExtensionOf(classStr(BaseClass))] final class BaseClass_Model_Extension coctable, extensionoftable [ExtensionOf(tableStr(TableName))] final class TableName_Model_Extension cocform, extensionofform [ExtensionOf(formStr(FormName))] final class FormName_Model_Extension cocformds, extensionofformdatasource [ExtensionOf(formDataSourceStr(FormName, DataSourceName))] final class FormNameDataSourceNameDS_Model_Extension cocmethod, nextwrapper A public void wrapper method that calls next cocmethodret, nextwrapperret A wrapper with a return value: ret = next method(...), your code, return ret;

docs.title: Event handlers
docs.text: Prefixes Inserts dataeventhandler, deh [DataEventHandler(tableStr(T), DataEventType::...)] with a choice of event (Inserted, Inserting, Updated, Updating, Deleted, Deleting, ValidatedWrite, ValidatingWrite, ValidatedDelete, ValidatingDelete, InitializedRecord, ValidatedField, ModifiedField) and the cast of _sender to the table formeventhandler, feh [FormEventHandler(formStr(F), FormEventType::...)] with a choice of Initialized, Initializing, PostRun, Activated, Closing, PreRun formcontroleventhandler, fceh [FormControlEventHandler(formControlStr(F, C), FormControlEventType::...)] with a choice of Clicked, Modified, GotFocus, LostFocus, Lookup, Validating, Validated prehandler [PreHandlerFor(classStr(C), methodStr(C, m))] with XppPrePostArgs and _args.getThis() posthandler [PostHandlerFor(classStr(C), methodStr(C, m))] with XppPrePostArgs and _args.getThis()

docs.title: Batch and SysOperation
docs.text:
Prefixes Inserts sysopcontroller, sysoperationcontroller A controller extending SysOperationServiceController with construct (execution mode parameter) and main sysopservice, sysoperationservice A service extending SysOperationServiceBase with a process method taking the contract sysopcontract, datacontract A [DataContractAttribute] class with one parameter and its [DataMemberAttribute] parm method runbase, runbasebatch A RunBase or RunBaseBatch class (choice) with pack/unpack (#CurrentVersion, #CurrentList), run, description and main

For a complete SysOperation batch job (controller, service, contract, menu item, privilege), use the wizard: Wizard: Batch Job.

docs.title: Tables and data
docs.text: Prefixes Inserts tablefind Static find(key, _forUpdate = false) with selectForUpdate and select firstonly tableexist Static exist(key) with select firstonly RecId parm, parmmethod A [DataMemberAttribute] parm method; the method name is the variable name capitalized (custAccount gives parmCustAccount) whileselect while select ... where ... loop selectforupdate, selectfirstonly select firstonly forupdate ... where ...;

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: Prefixes Inserts tts, ttsbegin ttsbegin; ... ttscommit; trycatchretry, tryretry #OCCRetryCount, a transaction in try, and catch blocks for Exception::Deadlock and Exception::UpdateConflict that retry while appl.ttsLevel() == 0 and the retry count is below #RetryNum

docs.title: Tests and messages
docs.text:
Prefixes Inserts systestclass, testclass A [SysTestTarget(...)] class extending SysTestCase with one [SysTestMethod] in Arrange / Act / Assert form systestmethod, testmethod A [SysTestMethod] method with Arrange / Act / Assert comments and assertEquals infolabel, warninglabel, errorlabel, strfmtlabel info, warning or error (choice) of strFmt("@LabelFile:LabelId", value)

To generate a test class from an existing class instead, see Generate SysTest Class.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Snippets have no F&O Studio setting. VS Code's editor settings apply, for example editor.snippetSuggestions (where snippets appear in the suggestion list) and editor.tabCompletion.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The snippets are a standard VS Code snippet file, snippets/xpp.json, contributed for the xpp language in package.json (contributes.snippets). They use VS Code's snippet syntax: numbered placeholders (${1:BaseClass}), mirrored placeholders (${1}), choices (${2|Inserted,Inserting,...|}) and a transform that capitalizes the parm method name (${3/(.*)/${1:/capitalize}/}). No server is involved.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Snippets don't create elements, add them to the project or check that the names exist. Build to check.
  • The Chain of Command class snippets name the class <Base>_<Model>_Extension; adjust it to your naming rules (see Team Rules).
  • The handler snippets don't know the methods or controls of the target; you type the names. To see the handlers an event already has, use Event Handlers in the designer.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Typing a prefix shows no snippet The document's language is not X++ Check the language in the status bar; code views are always X++ Changes don't save The code view is of a standard element (read-only) Write the code in your own class or extension

docs.title: Solution View and C# References
docs.text: The D365FO Project view shows the whole solution around your X++ project, as Visual Studio's Solution Explorer does: the X++ project with its References, the other X++ projects of the solution, and the C# projects with their files. You can reference C# projects and .NET assemblies from X++, create a C# class library for your model, and build it. When you build or deploy the X++ project, F&O Studio builds the referenced C# projects first and copies their assemblies into your package, the same way Visual Studio's build does.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Your X++ code calls .NET code you own: a parser, an integration client, a calculation library.
  • You need a third-party .NET assembly in your package (a .dll with its dependencies).
  • C# code needs to call X++ classes and tables (Dynamics.AX.Application).
  • You want to edit the C# code next to the X++ code, with the C# extension's IntelliSense.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An open D365FO project (D365FO Projects). References belong to an X++ project and its model; without one you get Open a D365FO project first: references belong to an X++ project and its model.
  • MSBuild to build C# projects. F&O Studio uses, in this order: the xpp.build.msbuildPath setting; Visual Studio's or the Visual Studio Build Tools' MSBuild (found with vswhere); the .NET SDK's MSBuild (dotnet msbuild).
  • For C# editing, the C# extension for VS Code (optional; F&O Studio does not need it to build).

docs.title: The solution in the project view
docs.text:
F&O Studio looks for a solution file (.slnx or .sln) that lists the open .rnrproj, in the project's folder and up to three folders above. If it finds one, the view shows:

Node What it shows The open X++ project Its References node, then its elements by folder References Each C# project (C# project) and assembly (assembly) the X++ project references. A missing file has a warning icon and · not found. Clicking a C# project reference opens its .csproj. Empty: Add Reference… hint. Other X++ projects of the solution Collapsed, marked · not open, with their elements. Open This Project switches the window to that project. C# projects Every .csproj of the solution (C#) and every C# project the X++ project references but the solution does not list (C# · not in the solution), with their files

The view's description is <solution> (solution).

docs.title: C# project files
docs.text:
• SDK-style projects (<Project Sdk="...">) show every file under the project folder, like Solution Explorer. bin, obj, node_modules, packages, TestResults, hidden folders, .csproj/.user files and subfolders that contain a project of their own are left out. At most 3,000 files are listed.
  • Older projects show the items they list (Compile, Content, None, EmbeddedResource, Page, Resource...) and their Folder entries. Wildcard items and files outside the project folder are not shown.
  • Folders come first, then files, each sorted by name.
  • Click a file to open it. Files you add or delete in the project folders, and changes to the .csproj and the solution file, refresh the view on their own (build output in bin and obj is ignored).

The C# project folders are also folders of the project's workspace (<Folder> (C#)), so the C# extension loads them.

docs.title: Add a reference
docs.text:
1. Run Add Reference… from the References node (inline + or right-click), the open project node, the Project submenu of the view, or the Command Palette.
  2. The picker Add Reference to offers:
  3. Projects in the solution: C# projects of the solution that the X++ project does not reference yet;
  4. Browse for a C# Project…: any .csproj;
  5. Browse for an Assembly (.dll)…: any .NET assembly;
  6. New C# Project…: see below.
  7. For a C# project, F&O Studio first builds it (output in the X++ Build output channel), as Visual Studio does, so the reference names the assembly it produces. If the build fails you get .csproj did not build. See the X++ Build output.
  8. F&O Studio then:
  9. creates an AxReference element named after the assembly in the project's model (unless the model already has it). Through it, the X++ compiler resolves the assembly's types;
  10. adds a ProjectReference (C# project) or a Reference with a HintPath (assembly) to the .rnrproj;
  11. for a C# project, adds it to the solution if the solution does not list it, and adds its folder to the project's workspace.
  12. The message reads, for example, Added a reference to ContosoLibrary.csproj; model ContosoExtensions now has the reference ContosoLibrary. Build the X++ project to copy it into the package.

    13. F&O Studio refuses:

    • an assembly whose name starts with Dynamics.AX. (a compiled X++ package): add its model to your model's dependencies instead (Models and Model Dependencies);
    • a file that is not a .NET assembly;
    • a reference to a model other than the open project's model.

docs.title: Remove a reference
docs.text:
1. Right-click a reference under References and choose Remove Reference (or run it from the Command Palette and pick the reference).
  2. Confirm: Remove the reference to ? The reference in model and the copy of .dll in its package go too. The C# project stays in the solution; an assembly file stays where it is.
  3. F&O Studio removes the .rnrproj item, the model's AxReference, and <assembly>.dll, .pdb and .xml from the package's bin folder, as Visual Studio does.

docs.title: Create a C# project
docs.text:
New C# Project… creates a class library for your model, next to the X++ project, and references it.

  1. Run New C# Project… (References node, open project node, Project submenu, or Add Reference… > New C# Project…).
  2. New C# Project (1/3): name — default <Model>Library. It is also the assembly name and the root namespace; parts separated by dots are allowed (Contoso.Integration).
  3. (2/3): X++ packages the C# code uses — the packages your model depends on that have a compiled assembly. ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationFoundation and ApplicationSuite are preselected. Their assemblies are referenced, not copied. Your own package is not offered (it will reference this project).
  4. (3/3): parent folder — next to the solution (or next to the X++ project's folder), or Browse…. The project goes to <parent>\<name>.
  5. F&O Studio writes <name>.csproj and a sample class Greeter.cs, adds the project to the solution, opens Greeter.cs, builds the project and adds the reference.

The generated project:

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net48</TargetFramework>
    <RootNamespace>ContosoLibrary</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>ContosoLibrary</AssemblyName>
    <DebugType>portable</DebugType>
    <PlatformTarget>AnyCPU</PlatformTarget>
    <FnOPackagesDirectory Condition="'$(FnOPackagesDirectory)' == ''">$([MSBuild]::GetRegistryValue('HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations', 'FrameworkDirectory'))</FnOPackagesDirectory>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Reference Include="Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Xpp.AxShared">
      <HintPath>$(FnOPackagesDirectory)\bin\Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Xpp.AxShared.dll</HintPath>
      <Private>false</Private>
    </Reference>
    <Reference Include="Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Xpp.Support">...</Reference>
    <Reference Include="Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite">
      <HintPath>$(FnOPackagesDirectory)\ApplicationSuite\bin\Dynamics.AX.ApplicationSuite.dll</HintPath>
      <Private>false</Private>
    </Reference>
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
  • .NET Framework 4.8, which the AOS runs.
  • Portable PDBs, which the VS Code debugger reads (Debugging C# Code).
  • Finance and Operations' assemblies are compiled against but never copied (Private false). Their folder comes from the registry value of the active configuration, so the project builds on every developer machine and follows the active version. A build pipeline can pass FnOPackagesDirectory instead.
  • X++ types are in the namespace Dynamics.AX.Application.

The sample class shows how X++ calls it:

namespace ContosoLibrary
{
    public static class Greeter
    {
        public static string Hello(string name)
        {
            return "Hello " + name;
        }
    }
}

str greeting = ContosoLibrary.Greeter::Hello('world');

docs.title: Build a C# project
docs.text: Right-click a C# project node and choose Build C# Project. It runs MSBuild with -t:Build and -restore and shows the output in the X++ Build output channel. Open Project File (inline or right-click) opens the .csproj.

docs.title: Build the X++ project with its references
docs.text:
You do not need to build the C# projects by hand before an X++ build. Build Project, Build Model (when the package being built is the open project's package), Deploy Models to Environment and the agent tool xpp_build run the reference step first, when the .rnrproj has references or items marked Copy to Output Directory:

  1. MSBuild runs on the .rnrproj itself. Visual Studio's build tasks need Visual Studio, so their import ($(BuildTasksDirectory)) is pointed at empty stand-in files, and a target that only resolves the references is added. This builds the referenced C# projects (with -restore).
  2. MSBuild reports the files to copy: the referenced assemblies with their dependencies, PDB and XML files and satellite assemblies (ReferenceCopyLocalPaths), and the files marked Copy to Output Directory (Copy always or Copy if newer).
  3. F&O Studio copies them into <package>\bin, keeping subfolders. Files marked Copy always are copied every time; the others when missing or newer.
  4. Files that are part of Finance and Operations (names starting with Dynamics.AX., or present in PackagesLocalDirectory\bin) are never copied: Not copied: … is part of Finance and Operations (reference it with Copy Local = False).
  5. Then xppc compiles X++. See Build Project and Model.

docs.title: Navigate between X++ and C
docs.text: Go to Definition works across the two languages: from X++ to the C# types and members of the referenced projects, and from C# to X++ elements in Dynamics.AX.Application. Hover and completion know the .NET types in X++. See Go to Definition.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.msbuildPath empty MSBuild.exe used to build the C# projects and assemblies your X++ project references. Empty: Visual Studio's or the Build Tools' MSBuild, else the .NET SDK's

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Solution and C# project reading: src/solution.ts (no VS Code dependency). .slnx files are parsed for <Project Path="...">; .sln files for Project(...) = "...", "<path>" lines ending in a project extension. Solution folders are ignored.
  • Adding a project to a solution: .slnx files are edited directly (a <Project Path="..."/> line before </Solution>); .sln files with dotnet sln <solution> add <project>.
  • The view: ProjectTreeProvider in src/project.ts.
  • Commands Add Reference…, Remove Reference, New C# Project…, Build C# Project, Open This Project and Open Project File: src/references.ts.
  • The reference items and the AxReference element are written by the metadata server: bridge actions add_reference and remove_reference in MetaModelBridge.AssemblyReferences.cs, which call Microsoft's metadata API (CreateReference, DeleteReference) for the AxReference (name, assembly display name, version, public key token) and XppProject (server/Host/XppProject.cs) for the .rnrproj. Paths in the .rnrproj are relative to the project folder (absolute when on another drive). A project reference also carries the C# project's GUID when it has one.
  • The reference step of the build: src/dotnetReferences.ts for the extension's build and deploy, and server/Host/ProjectReferences.cs for xpp_build. Both implement the same rules. MSBuild is called with -t:XppStudioResolveReferences -getItem:ReferenceCopyLocalPaths -getItem:AllItemsFullPathWithTargetPath -getResultOutputFile:<json>; the stand-ins and the extra target are written to %TEMP%\xpp-vscode-msbuild only when their content changes, so referenced projects are not rebuilt for nothing.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• C# editing, IntelliSense and refactoring come from the C# extension, not F&O Studio.
  • F&O Studio does not create test projects, NuGet packages or other project types; New C# Project… creates a class library.
  • .sln editing needs the .NET SDK (dotnet sln). .slnx files are edited without it.
  • References are kept per X++ project. The reference step runs for the open project's package only; other packages you build or deploy at the same time get no C# files copied.
  • Hitting a breakpoint in referenced C# code on a UDE or VHD is not tested yet (release notes of 0.16.0); see Debugging C# Code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Open a D365FO project first: references belong to an X++ project and its model. No project in this window Open a project .csproj did not build. See the X++ Build output. The C# project has compile errors, or MSBuild could not restore Read the X++ Build output and fix the C# project Build .csproj first: its assembly was not found. The build produced no assembly Build the project; check its output path … is a compiled X++ package: add its model to your model's dependencies instead. You picked a Dynamics.AX.* assembly Add the package with Update Model Parameters… … is not a .NET assembly. Native DLL Reference the .NET wrapper; copy native files with Copy to Output Directory in a C# project Building the references failed. MSBuild came from the .NET SDK … No Visual Studio or Build Tools MSBuild found Set xpp.build.msbuildPath, or install the Visual Studio Build Tools Not copied: … is part of Finance and Operations A referenced file is a Finance and Operations assembly Set Copy Local (Private) to false on that reference A reference shows · not found The .csproj or HintPath file moved Remove the reference and add it again … was not added to : … in the output dotnet sln add failed for a .sln Add the project to the solution yourself

docs.title: Source Control for X++
docs.text: X++ source is metadata: every element (class, table, form, EDT...) is one XML file in its model folder, and each package has a Descriptor folder that describes its models. Putting D365FO code under source control means putting those folders, and the .rnrproj projects, in a repository, and keeping build output out of it. This page explains the layout, what to commit and what to ignore, and how F&O Studio finds the repository of your models, even when the model folders are links from the custom metadata folder into the repository. Visual Studio teams use the same layout, so a repository works in both.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You put a new model under source control.
  • You set up the .gitignore of a D365FO repository.
  • F&O Studio does not show change marks, history or review results and you want to know why.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Git installed and on the PATH. F&O Studio supports Git only (no TFVC).
  • Your custom models in the custom metadata folder of the active configuration (the ModelStoreFolder of the configuration, for example C:\CustomXppMetadata... on a UDE or K:\AosService\PackagesLocalDirectory on a cloud-hosted environment).

docs.title: How X++ metadata is laid out on disk
docs.text:
A package folder in the metadata folder looks like this (package ContosoExtensions with one model of the same name):

<custom metadata folder>\
  ContosoExtensions\                 <- package folder
    Descriptor\
      ContosoExtensions.xml          <- model descriptor: name, layer, publisher, version, referenced packages
    ContosoExtensions\               <- model folder
      AxClass\
        ContosoOrderService.xml
        SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension.xml
      AxTable\
        ContosoOrderStatus.xml
      AxTableExtension\
        CustTable.ContosoExtensions.xml
      AxEdt\
      AxEnum\
      AxForm\
      AxLabelFile\
        ContosoLabels_en-US.xml
        LabelResources\
          en-US\
            ContosoLabels.en-US.label.txt
      ...
    bin\                             <- build output (Dynamics.AX.ContosoExtensions.dll, .netmodule, PDBs)
    BuildLogs\                       <- F&O Studio's build logs (xppc, LabelC, reportsc, xppbp)
    Resources\                       <- compiled labels (LabelC output)
    Reports\                         <- compiled reports (.rdl, reportsc output)

Each element is one file <model folder>\<AxType>\<Name>.xml. F&O Studio relies on this rule: a changed file AxClass/ContosoOrderService.xml under a model folder is the class ContosoOrderService. Files elsewhere in the model (for example label text files) are not reported as elements.

The project (.rnrproj) lives in its own folder, usually next to the metadata in the repository. A project created with Create D365FO Project… also gets a .slnx solution file, as Visual Studio creates it.

docs.title: What to commit
docs.text: Commit Why <Package>\Descriptor\*.xml The model definition; without it the package is not a package. Open Team Repository… finds packages by this folder. <Package>\<Model>\Ax*\*.xml The elements: the X++ source and metadata. <Package>\<Model>\AxLabelFile\... Label files and their LabelResources\<language>\*.label.txt texts. Project folders: *.rnrproj, *.slnx / *.sln Projects open in F&O Studio and Visual Studio. C# projects the X++ project references Their sources and .csproj; F&O Studio builds them and copies their output into the package bin before X++ is compiled. .xpp\workspace.json Written by Open Team Repository…: the package folders to link, so the next developer gets the same set. .xpp\agent-rules.md The team's rules for Copilot (see Team Rules).

docs.title: What to ignore
docs.text:
Build output is created on every machine and differs between builds. The following .gitignore is general D365FO practice, adapted to the folders F&O Studio's build writes; adjust the paths to your repository layout.

# Build output inside each package folder
**/bin/
**/BuildLogs/
**/Resources/
**/Reports/
**/XppMetadata/

# C# and Visual Studio leftovers
**/obj/
.vs/
*.user

# Build result files Visual Studio writes into the package folder
BuildProjectResult.*
BuildModelResult.*

Notes:

  • Resources and Reports at the package level are compiler output. The label sources are under the model's AxLabelFile folder, and the report sources are AxReport\*.xml elements; both are committed.
  • If your C# projects keep assemblies in a bin folder on purpose (for example a reference assembly checked in), narrow the bin rule instead of ignoring every bin folder.
  • F&O Studio does not create or change .gitignore files. The rules above are a starting point, not something the extension enforces.

The same files are kept out of deployments: F&O Studio's deploy skips the package's BuildLogs folder, the BuildProjectResult / BuildModelResult log files and .delete files when it zips a package (core/src/deploy.ts).

docs.title: Repository layouts
docs.text:
Two layouts are common. Both work with F&O Studio.

1. Repository holds the package folders, linked into the metadata folder (recommended for teams).

C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps\
  .xpp\workspace.json
  .xpp\agent-rules.md
  Metadata\
    ContosoExtensions\               <- package folder (Descriptor + model)
    ContosoIntegration\
  Projects\
    ContosoExtensions\ContosoExtensions.rnrproj

Each package folder is linked into the custom metadata folder with a directory junction (<custom metadata folder>\ContosoExtensions -> C:\Repos\ContosoFinOps\Metadata\ContosoExtensions). This is how teams set up Visual Studio, and it is what Open Team Repository… does for you. Packages linked this way are listed, built and offered for deploy like any other package in the folder.

2. The repository is inside the metadata folder. On cloud-hosted environments some teams map the repository to PackagesLocalDirectory directly. Git then sees the package folders without links. This also works: F&O Studio only needs each model folder to be inside a Git working tree.

docs.title: How F&O Studio finds the repository
docs.text:
F&O Studio never asks you for a repository path. It finds it from your models:

  1. It lists your custom models (the models in the custom metadata folder).
  2. For each model it resolves the real path of the model folder (fs.realpath), so a junction into the repository becomes the path inside the repository.
  3. It runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel in that folder. A model folder that is not in a Git working tree is skipped.
  4. It computes the model's path inside the repository and filters Git's output to files under it.

Each model is handled separately, so models in different repositories work at the same time. The work item and pipeline commands look first at the workspace folders and then at your models' real folders, and use the first one that is in a Git repository (see Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration).

docs.title: What source control gives you in F&O Studio
docs.text:
Feature What it uses Change marks in the project view and on code view tabs git status and, with a base branch, git diff --name-status (Git Changes in the Project View) Show Changed Elements The same list, in a quick pick (Show Changed Elements) Review My Changes The same list, plus checks on each element (Review My Changes) View History git log of the element's XML file and diffs of its code or metadata (Element History) xpp_diff_changes agent tool The same list for Copilot (Agent Tools: Build and Data) Link Work Item…, Open Work Item…, Open Pipelines The origin remote URL (Work Items and Pipelines)

Commits, branches, pushes, pulls and merges are done with VS Code's own Source Control view or the git command line. F&O Studio does not replace them.

docs.title: Metadata changes and Git
docs.text:
• Designers and agent tools save elements through Microsoft's metadata API, which rewrites the element's XML file. Git sees that file as modified; the project view marks it with M.
  • A new element is a new, untracked file; it shows as A (added) even before you stage it.
  • Deleting an element removes its file; it shows as D in the lists, and cannot be opened from them.
  • Renaming an element produces a delete and an add, or R when Git detects the rename.
  • The .rnrproj file changes when you add or exclude project items. It is not an element, so it shows in VS Code's Source Control view but not in F&O Studio's change lists.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No changed elements in your models (they must be in a Git repository)." No custom model folder resolves to a Git working tree. Check that the model folder (or the folder its junction points to) is inside a cloned repository: run git rev-parse --show-toplevel in it. Changes in the repository are not listed The files are not under a model folder in the <AxType>\<Name>.xml form (for example label text files, descriptors, projects). Expected: only element files are listed. Use VS Code's Source Control view for the other files. A package from the repository is missing in the Application Explorer The package is not linked into the custom metadata folder. Run Open Team Repository… and pick the folder, or create the junction yourself and run Refresh Application Explorer. Build output shows up as changes in VS Code's Source Control view No .gitignore for bin, BuildLogs, Resources, Reports. Add the rules above and remove the files from the index (git rm -r --cached).
