docs.title: Standard Code Drift
docs.text: Standard Code Drift of Wrapped Methods… compares the standard methods your Chain of Command code wraps between two installed application versions, and shows a diff for each method whose code changed. A wrapper can still compile after an update while the code around next now behaves differently: a new early return, a moved ttsbegin, a variable your wrapper relies on that is set elsewhere. This report finds those methods so you can read them before you test. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After an application update, together with Upgrade Readiness: Upgrade Readiness finds wrappers that break (missing methods, changed signatures); Standard Code Drift finds wrappers that still compile but may behave differently.
  • To decide what to regression-test after an update: every method in the list is a place where your logic meets changed standard logic.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Two application versions on this machine: the active one, and the earlier one's PackagesLocalDirectory. F&O Studio keeps each version under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\PackagesLocalDirectory. Clean Up Old Application Versions… keeps the newest older version by default, so it is still there for this comparison (see Version Drift Guard).
  • The earlier version can also be any other folder named PackagesLocalDirectory, for example a copy from another machine.
  • The model must be one of your models in the custom metadata folder.
  • The active configuration is the newer version (Select Environment).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start it from one of these places:
  2. Application Explorer: right-click one of your models (model node) > Standard Code Drift of Wrapped Methods….
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Build and check > Standard Code Drift… (wrapped methods).
  4. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Standard Code Drift of Wrapped Methods….
  5. Without a model from the context menu, pick the model in "Standard code drift: model". The project's model is marked "project model".
  6. Pick the version to compare with. The quick pick "Compare the standard code of with" lists the other versions under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365 that have a PackagesLocalDirectory. If there are none, or you press Escape, a folder dialog "PackagesLocalDirectory of the earlier version" opens; select the folder and click Compare With This Version.
  7. Progress shows in the Results view: "Comparing the code wraps…". The earlier version's metadata is loaded for this, which can take a while.
  8. The Results view shows one section, Wrapped methods whose standard code changed, with one finding per changed method:
  9. label: the target and method, for example Class SalesFormLetter.run;
  10. description: <n> line(s) differ · wrapped by <your class>.
  11. Click a finding to open a diff editor: the earlier version's method on the left, the current version's on the right, titled for example Class SalesFormLetter.run: 10.0.40.1 ↔ 10.0.41.0.
  12. Read the diff around the place your wrapper calls next, and decide whether your wrapper needs a change.

    13. When no wrapped method changed, the section shows a pass icon and "none; formatting-only changes are ignored".

docs.title: What it compares
docs.text:
For every method of a class in your model that:

  • is in a class with [ExtensionOf(...)], and
  • is a Chain of Command wrapper (it calls next on its own name),

F&O Studio finds the target method's code in both versions and compares it.

Target in ExtensionOf Where the method is looked up classStr(...) The class and its base classes tableStr(...) The table formStr(...) The form dataEntityViewStr(...) The data entity viewStr(...) The view formDataSourceStr(...) The form's data source

The comparison ignores formatting: each line is trimmed, runs of whitespace are reduced to one space and blank lines are dropped. A method whose code is the same after that counts as unchanged.

For a changed method, "line(s) differ" counts the lines of the current version that are not in the earlier one plus the lines of the earlier version that are not in the current one. Methods are sorted by this count, largest first.

A wrapper is "not found" when its target method has no X++ source in one of the versions, for example a kernel method such as insert that the table does not override, or a target type not in the table above.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
The Markdown report (Copy Report as Markdown, Export Report…):

# Standard code drift: ContosoExtensions (10.0.40.1 → 10.0.41.0)

14 Chain of Command wrapper(s); 2 target method(s) changed, 9 unchanged, 3 not found in one of the versions.

- Class SalesFormLetter.run: 12 line(s) differ · wrapped by ContosoSalesFormLetter_Extension
- Table SalesTable.validateWrite: 3 line(s) differ · wrapped by ContosoSalesTable_Extension

The Results view header shows, for example, 10.0.40.1 → 10.0.41.0: 2 wrapped method(s) changed. Run Again asks for the version again.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: No settings. The version list comes from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The command is in src/upgrade.ts (xpp.standardCodeDrift). It calls bridge action wrapper_drift with the model name and the earlier PackagesLocalDirectory. The server side is WrapperDriftJson in server/Ported/MetaModel/ExtensionCompatibilityService.cs:

  1. It checks that the model is one of yours and that the folder exists and is named PackagesLocalDirectory.
  2. It creates a second, read-only view of the earlier version's metadata with Microsoft's metadata API (its own disk provider and metadata service), next to the active one.
  3. It reads each wrapper class of the model from the active metadata, finds the target method in both versions and compares the normalized code.
  4. It returns the counts (wrappers, unchanged, not found) and up to 200 changed methods with both versions of their code (each capped at 20,000 characters).

The extension keeps both versions of each method in memory as virtual documents (scheme xpp-drift) and opens them with VS Code's diff editor when you click a finding. They are gone when you close VS Code.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text: Agents get the same comparison through xpp_find_deprecations with previousPackagesFolder: the report adds a "Standard code drift" section that names each changed method and the size of the change, without the code, and tells the agent to read both versions and check the logic around next. Ask the F&O Upgrade Reviewer agent, for example: "Compare the methods ContosoExtensions wraps with the previous version in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\10.0.40.1\PackagesLocalDirectory." See Upgrade Readiness and Agent Tools: Analysis.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only Chain of Command wrappers are compared. Event handlers and metadata extensions are not (Upgrade Readiness checks that their targets still exist).
  • It compares X++ source only. Changes in kernel methods without X++ source are not visible.
  • A changed line count says how much changed, not whether it matters; read the diff.
  • At most 200 changed methods are returned.
  • Loading the earlier version's metadata takes time and memory.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Pass the PackagesLocalDirectory folder of the earlier version." The selected folder does not exist or is not named PackagesLocalDirectory. Select the PackagesLocalDirectory folder itself, not its parent. "Model '...' is not one of your models in the custom metadata folder." A standard model or an unknown model. Pick one of your models. No version is offered in the quick pick. No other version folder with a PackagesLocalDirectory exists under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365. Use the folder dialog, or keep the older version when you run Clean Up Old Application Versions…. Many wrappers "not found in one of the versions". The targets are kernel methods without X++ source, or the method was removed. Check removed methods with Upgrade Readiness.

docs.title: Status Bar
docs.text: F&O Studio shows up to five items on the left of VS Code's status bar: the environment, the database connection, the metadata server's state, the active D365FO project with its last build and deploy state, and the Copilot checkpoint and scope. Each item appears only when it has something to say, and each one opens the matching command or menu when you click it. Short messages also appear there after a build or a best practice run.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• To see at a glance which environment this window works with, and whether its metadata matches the environment.
  • To build the project with one click and see whether the last build succeeded.
  • To know whether the environment runs your latest build or an older deploy (UDE).
  • To see that the database is connected and until when the temporary credentials are valid.
  • To notice that the metadata server stopped, and restart it.

docs.title: The items
docs.text:
From left to right:

Item Shown when Text Click Environment An environment configuration is active Environment name, with a warning icon when the metadata is out of date or missing Environment… menu Database A database connection is available Database name (cloud-hosted/VHD), or the credential role and expiry time (UDE) Database menu X++ server A metadata server is starting or has stopped "X++ server" with a spinner, or "X++ server stopped" Restart (when stopped) Project A D365FO project is open, or an X++ editor is visible Project name with a state icon Build Project Copilot checkpoint A Copilot checkpoint is open or a Copilot scope is set Lock icon (scope) and history icon with the number of changed elements Copilot Checkpoint… menu

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Text: the environment's name with a server icon. A warning icon replaces it when:
  • the environment now runs a newer application version than the metadata on this machine (see Version Drift Guard); or
  • the environment selected in this window has no metadata on this machine, so the X++ tools use the machine-wide configuration.
  • Tooltip: the environment name, the application version, the Finance and Operations URL, the version drift or mismatch note, or "Cloud-hosted or VHD environment (local AOS and PackagesLocalDirectory)".
  • Click: the Environment… menu with Select Environment…, Connect to Environment…, Check Environment Connection, on a UDE Check Application Version, Clean Up Old Versions… and Sign In (pac), then Database… and Show Active Configuration. When a newer version is available, Update Metadata to … comes first.

    See Select Environment and Connect to Environment.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• Cloud-hosted and VHD: the business database name (for example AxDB); tooltip " on (Windows authentication)".
  • UDE: hidden until you have just-in-time credentials. Then it shows the role (Reader or Writer) and the time they expire, for example "Reader until 14:30"; the tooltip shows the database, server, user and expiry. It updates itself when the credentials expire.
  • Click: the Database menu.

    • See Database Access.

docs.title: X++ server
docs.text:
The metadata server loads the D365FO metadata for this window. The item is hidden while the server runs normally.

  • While a server starts: "X++ server" with a spinning icon; tooltip "Loading the D365FO metadata…".
  • When a server stopped unexpectedly: "X++ server stopped" on an error background; the tooltip shows the reason and "Click to restart; details are in the X++ output." Clicking runs Restart X++ Server.

See Metadata Server.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
The project item combines the open project, the last build and, on a UDE, the deploy state:

Icon Meaning project icon Project open, not built in this session check mark Last build of the project's model in this session succeeded, and the deploy is current (or there is nothing to deploy) error icon Last build of the project's model failed cloud-upload icon UDE: the model was built after its last deploy from this machine, or never deployed from this machine

A failed build takes precedence over the deploy state.

The tooltip shows:

  • the project name, its model and the number of elements, and the .rnrproj file name;
  • the last build: "Last project build 10:42:13: succeeded, 0 error(s), 3 warning(s)" (or "model build"), or "Not built in this session";
  • on a UDE, for a model built in this environment: either "Built , deployed : tests and the debugger run the older deployed code." (or "not deployed from this machine") with a Deploy now link, or "Deployed : the environment runs the latest build.";
  • "Click to build the project."

    • Click the item to run Build Project.

    When no project is open but an X++ editor is visible, the item says "No D365FO project"; click it to run Open D365FO Project…. Without a project and without an X++ editor, the item is hidden.

    The item refreshes after every build, after a deploy, when you save a .rnrproj file and when xpp.project changes.

docs.title: Copilot checkpoint
docs.text:
Shown only while a Copilot checkpoint is open or a Copilot scope is set:

  • a lock icon when a scope limits which elements Copilot may change;
  • a history icon with the number of elements changed since the checkpoint started (refreshed every 10 seconds).

The tooltip explains both; click for the Copilot Checkpoint… menu (review or revert). See Copilot Checkpoints and Scope.

docs.title: Messages after a command
docs.text:
Some commands show a short message in the status bar instead of a notification:

Message After Shown for "Build succeeded" or "Build succeeded: N warning(s)" Build Project, Build Model 10 s "Best practice: N error(s), M warning(s)" Run Best Practice Checks on Project 10 s "X++ environment: ()" Select Environment… 5 s

docs.title: Built versus deployed
docs.text:
On a unified developer environment the environment runs the code last deployed to it, not your last build. F&O Studio keeps track of both, per environment and model:

  • Built: recorded when a build from F&O Studio's commands or tasks succeeds (also builds started by the Pre-Deploy Checklist, Run Snippet and Open Team Repository). Builds by Copilot's xpp_build tool run in the metadata server and are not recorded.
  • Deployed: recorded when Deploy Models to Environment or the deploy task succeeds, for every model in the deployed packages.
  • Stale: the model was built after its last deploy, or was built but never deployed from this machine.

The state is stored in VS Code's global state for the extension (key xpp.deployState), so it survives restarts and is shared by all windows on this machine. It is not shared with other machines, Visual Studio or pipelines: a deploy made elsewhere is not known.

The same state drives the warnings elsewhere:

  • Run Tests, the Debugger and Verify Changes in the Running App ask " was built (...) after its last deploy (...). uses the deployed code." with Deploy First and Continue.
  • The xpp_run_tests agent tool adds a warning to its result.

    • On cloud-hosted and VHD environments there is no deploy: the build updates the local AOS, so no deploy state is shown.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Effect on the status bar xpp.project The project shown by the project item (see D365FO Projects).

VS Code lets you hide any item: right-click the status bar and clear the item ("X++ Environment", "F&O Studio database", "F&O Studio server", "F&O Studio project", "Copilot checkpoint").

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Item Source Environment EnvironmentStatus in src/environmentPicker.ts Database DatabaseAccess in src/database/connection.ts X++ server src/serverStatus.ts, from the state events of each server client Project src/projectStatus.ts, from the builder's results and the deploy state Copilot checkpoint AgentSession in src/agentSession.ts

The built-versus-deployed logic is split between src/deployState.ts (recording and prompts) and core/src/environment/deployState.ts (the key <environment>/<model> in lower case, the stale rule and the message text).

The last build result is kept in memory only; after a restart the project item shows "Not built in this session" while the deploy state is still known.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The last build result is per VS Code session.
  • The deploy state knows only deploys from this machine through F&O Studio.
  • The project item reflects the project's model only, not other models you built.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No F&O Studio item at all No active configuration, no project and no X++ editor. Connect or select an environment; open a project. The project item keeps the cloud-upload icon after a deploy The deploy was made from Visual Studio, another machine or a pipeline, or it was cancelled. Deploy from F&O Studio, or ignore the warning if you know the environment is current. "X++ server stopped" The metadata server process ended. Click to restart; read the X++ output for the reason. Environment item shows a warning icon Version drift, or no local metadata for the selected environment. Read the tooltip; run Update Metadata or Connect to Environment. Database item disappeared on a UDE The credentials expired or were forgotten. Request new credentials from the Database menu.

docs.title: Synchronize Database
docs.text: Database synchronization creates and changes the SQL tables, views and indexes of the business database so that they match your tables, views and data entities. F&O Studio synchronizes the database the way each environment type needs: on a unified developer environment (UDE) through the environment's Dataverse (alone or as part of a deploy), on cloud-hosted and VHD environments with Microsoft's SyncEngine against the local AxDB. This replaces Visual Studio's Dynamics 365 > Synchronize database and the sync option of a deploy.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After you added or changed tables, fields, indexes, views or data entities, and deployed (UDE) or built (cloud-hosted/VHD) them.
  • When the web client shows errors about missing tables or fields after a change.
  • On cloud-hosted and VHD environments, to synchronize only a few tables quickly with Synchronize Table(s) with the Database.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Environment What you need Unified developer environment The environment selected in this window and signed in (Connect to Environment, Sign In and Authentication). The code you want synchronized must be deployed: the environment synchronizes from its deployed metadata. Cloud-hosted or VHD VS Code running as administrator (SyncEngine needs it). The configuration names the database server and business database (the full sync falls back to localhost and AxDB; Synchronize Table(s) with the Database needs both in the configuration). The model must be built.

docs.title: Sync together with a deploy
docs.text:
When you run Deploy to Environment, pick the Database sync after deploy:

  • None: no sync;
  • Module: synchronizes the tables of the deployed packages;
  • Full: synchronizes the whole database (slow).

This is the usual way: one system job deploys and synchronizes.

docs.title: Sync without a deploy
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Synchronize Database from the command palette, or click Deploy > Synchronize Database in the Dynamics 365 view.
  2. Pick the kind in Database synchronization:
  3. Full: the whole database;
  4. Module: only the modules you name.
  5. For Module, enter the modules in Modules to synchronize as a comma-separated list. The project's model is filled in.
  6. The X++ Deploy output opens:
Synchronizing the database (Module: ContosoExtensions)…
Database sync started (system job <id>).
  database sync: <status>
  database sync: <status>
Database synchronized.
  1. Click Cancel on the notification to stop waiting; the sync keeps running on the environment.

docs.title: On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment
Full sync
docs.text: Run F&O Studio: Synchronize Database from the command palette. There are no questions: F&O Studio runs SyncEngine for a full synchronization of the local business database in a task terminal named Synchronize database, where you see SyncEngine's output. (In the Dynamics 365 view the Synchronize Database entry is shown on UDEs only; use the command palette or the task on a VM.)

docs.title: Synchronize Tables
docs.text:
To synchronize only some tables, which is much faster:

  1. In the Application Explorer or the D365FO Project view, select one or more tables, right-click and choose Synchronize Table(s) with the Database. Or click Deploy > Synchronize Tables… in the Dynamics 365 view and pick a table.
  2. A notification "Synchronizing …" runs SyncEngine for those tables only.
  3. The first line of the result shows as a message ("Synchronized ." or "Synchronization FAILED (exit N) for ."); the full SyncEngine output is in the X++ output.

    The context menu entry is shown on cloud-hosted and VHD environments only. On a UDE the command answers "Unified developer environments synchronize the database when the package is deployed; there is no local database to synchronize."

docs.title: As a task
docs.text:
{ "label": "X++: sync module", "type": "xpp", "action": "syncDatabase", "mode": "Module", "modules": "ContosoExtensions" }

On a UDE mode defaults to Full and modules to the project's model; on cloud-hosted and VHD environments the task always runs a full SyncEngine sync. See Build Tasks.

docs.title: With Copilot
docs.text: The agent tool xpp_build accepts syncDatabase: true: after a successful build it runs a full SyncEngine sync where a local database exists. On a UDE it does not sync and says that the database is synchronized when the package is deployed. A failed build skips the sync. See Agent Tools: Build and Data.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no sync settings. The database server and business database come from the active configuration.

docs.title: Unified developer environment
docs.text:
src/pac.ts (PacCommands.syncDatabase) asks for the kind and modules and calls syncDatabase in core/src/deploy.ts:

  1. Checks that the org has the solution msprov_fnouploadersolution (a Finance and Operations environment).
  2. Calls the Dataverse action msprov_dbsynctofinopsasync with dbsynckind (Full 1, Module 2) and dbsyncargument ({"Modules":["ContosoExtensions"]} for Module, empty for Full).
  3. Polls the returned system job (asyncoperations) every 15 seconds, for at most 4 hours, and writes each new status. The sync succeeds when the job completes with status Succeeded; otherwise it fails with the environment's message.

During a deploy, the same sync kind is set on each package record (msprov_dbsyncoptions, msprov_dbsyncvalue) and in fnomoduledefinition.json, and the environment synchronizes as part of the deploy job. See Deploy to Environment.

docs.title: Cloud-hosted and VHD
docs.text:
Full sync (command, task, and xpp_build with syncDatabase):

SyncEngine.exe -syncmode=fullall
               -metadatabinaries=<PackagesLocalDirectory>
               -connect="Data Source=<server>;Initial Catalog=<AxDB>;Integrated Security=True;Enlist=True;Application Name=SyncEngine"
               -fallbacktonative=False

The command runs it as a VS Code task without a shell, so the connection string reaches SyncEngine as one argument.

Synchronize Tables runs in the metadata server (bridge action sync_tables, BuildService.SyncTablesJson in server/Ported/MetaModel/BuildService.cs). The table names are checked against the metadata first, then:

SyncEngine.exe -syncmode=partiallist -synclist=<Table1,Table2> -metadatabinaries=<PackagesLocalDirectory>
               -connect="<same connection string>" -fallbacktonative=False

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• UDE: the environment synchronizes its deployed metadata. A build that is not deployed is not synchronized.
  • UDE: there is no table-level sync; the smallest unit is a module.
  • Cloud-hosted and VHD: the command always runs a full sync; the mode and modules of the task are not used there. Use Synchronize Table(s) with the Database for a partial sync.
  • Cancelling a UDE sync only stops waiting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "SyncEngine failed (exit N). It needs VS Code running as administrator; see the terminal output." Full sync on a VM without administrator rights, or a sync error. Run VS Code as administrator; read the terminal output. "Synchronization FAILED (exit N) for ..." SyncEngine failed for the tables. Read the X++ output. "Pass existing table names." A table name was not found in the metadata. Pick existing tables. "The configuration names no database server/business database." The configuration lacks the database. Check the configuration (Select Environment). "Unified developer environments synchronize the database when the package is deployed; ..." Synchronize Table(s) with the Database on a UDE. Deploy with a Module sync, or run Synchronize Database. "The database sync ended with status : " The environment's sync failed. Read the message; fix the table or entity and deploy again. "The database sync did not start: Dataverse returned no system job." The action returned no job. Try again; check the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

docs.title: Syntax Check and Obsolete Warnings
docs.text: F&O Studio checks X++ code while you type, before you build. The live syntax check runs the X++ compiler's own parser on each method and reports syntax errors in Problems within a second. Obsolete API warnings mark calls to methods, and uses of classes and tables, that carry the [SysObsolete] attribute, with the message the attribute gives. Compile on save (off by default) runs a full project build after each save so semantic errors reach Problems too. Visual Studio shows syntax errors as you type and obsolete warnings only when you build.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Catch a missing ;, a wrong select clause or an unbalanced brace while you type.
  • See right away that SomeClass::oldMethod() is obsolete and what to call instead.
  • Prepare an upgrade: obsolete APIs are the first things to replace (see Upgrade Readiness).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration. The syntax check uses the compiler parser from the packages bin folder of your installation.
  • Obsolete warnings need the cross-reference database (it records which elements use the SysObsolete attribute).
  • Both checks are on by default; compile on save is off.

docs.title: Live syntax check
docs.text:
1. Open or edit code in a code view, an .xpp file or an untitled X++ editor.
  2. 600 ms after you stop typing, the changed code is parsed.
  3. Errors are underlined in the editor and listed in Problems with the source X++ syntax and the compiler's diagnostic code. Warnings from the parser show as warnings.

How the document is checked:

Document Parsed as A class layout (declaration, methods inside the braces) The declaration (closed with its brace) as a class or interface, and each method on its own A form-style layout (classDeclaration first, then methods) The declaration and each method on its own One method (a nested method document) or a single block One method

Because each method is parsed on its own, an error in one method doesn't hide errors in the others, and the line numbers in Problems point into the right method. Unchanged methods are not parsed again (results are cached by their text).

The debugger's copies of source files are not checked.

docs.title: Obsolete API warnings
docs.text:
1. Write or open code that uses an obsolete API.
  2. 600 ms after the last change, the use is marked with a strikethrough and listed in Problems with the source X++ obsolete:
ContosoOrderHelper::findOld is obsolete: Use ContosoOrderHelper::find instead.

The text after "is obsolete:" is the message of the [SysObsolete] attribute (or "marked [SysObsolete]." when it has none). When the attribute's second argument is true (the API is an error to use), the problem is an error; otherwise it is a warning.

What is found:

Code Reported when Type::method( method of Type is obsolete variable.method( The variable is declared with a type that has an obsolete method of that name A class or table name The whole class or table is obsolete

Uses inside the obsolete element itself are not reported. this., super. and element. calls are not checked.

The list of obsolete APIs is loaded once and reloaded when you run Rebuild Extension Index.

docs.title: Compile on save
docs.text:
Turn on Compile on save (xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave) when you want semantic errors (unknown methods, type mismatches, missing references) without building by hand:

  1. Save an X++ document.
  2. F&O Studio runs Build Project, which compiles the project with xppc (about 10 seconds per save).
  3. Compiler errors and warnings for the project go to Problems, at the right line of the code view.

Only one build runs at a time; a save during a build doesn't start a second one. See Build Project and Model and Compiler Diagnostics.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.codeIntelligence.syntaxCheck true Syntax errors while you type, with the X++ compiler's parser. Turning it off clears the problems it reported xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings true Warnings (or errors) where code uses [SysObsolete] methods, classes and tables xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave false Build the project after saving code (slow)

All three are also in Configure Code Intelligence… (Code Intelligence Settings).

docs.title: Syntax check
docs.text:
• scheduleSyntax and checkSyntax in src/codeIntel/providers.ts split the document into blocks with methodSpans from src/xppSource.ts and send one syntax request per block to the code intelligence server process, with the element type and name.
  • Syntax in server/Ported/Tools/CodeIntel.cs calls Microsoft's parser (Pass1.ParseClassOrInterface for a declaration, Pass1.ParseMethod for a method, from Microsoft.Dynamics.AX.Framework.Xlnt.XppParser) with an empty macro library and collects the diagnostics: line, column, severity, moniker (shown as the code) and message.
  • The extension shifts each diagnostic by the block's first line. Results are cached per block text (up to 2,000 blocks).

docs.title: Obsolete warnings
docs.text:
• ObsoleteWarnings in src/productivity/obsolete.ts sends the obsolete request once.
  • The server (CodeExamples.Obsolete) finds every element and method that references SysObsoleteAttribute (or SysObsolete) as an attribute in the cross-reference database, reads the attribute in its source to get the message and the error flag, and caches the list in %LOCALAPPDATA%\XppVsCode\cache\obsolete-<database>.json until the database changes.
  • The extension scans each line of the document, with strings and comments blanked out, for the three patterns above. Variable types come from the nearest declaration (the same rule as Go to Definition).

docs.title: Compile on save
docs.text: The save handler runs the command xpp.buildProject when the setting is on and no compile-on-save build is running.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The syntax check parses without metadata: it finds syntax errors only. Unknown types, methods or fields are found by the build.
  • The parser runs with an empty macro library; macro libraries (#SysAdmin and similar) are not loaded for the syntax check.
  • Obsolete warnings are textual: they don't follow inheritance (a variable declared as a subclass whose base method is obsolete is not flagged), method return values or var variables. Obsolete fields and EDTs are not checked.
  • The obsolete list covers what the cross-reference database knows; your own [SysObsolete] methods appear after a build with cross references and Rebuild Extension Index.
  • Compile on save builds the whole project, which takes about 10 seconds per save.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No syntax errors appear xpp.codeIntelligence.syntaxCheck is off, or the code intelligence server is not running Turn the setting on; run Restart X++ Server No obsolete warnings The cross-reference database is not usable ("Obsolete API list unavailable" in the X++ output) See Find All References troubleshooting A new [SysObsolete] of yours is not reported The list is cached Build with cross references, then run Rebuild Extension Index Each save takes 10 seconds Compile on save is on Turn off xpp.codeIntelligence.diagnosticsOnSave

docs.title: Team Rules
docs.text: Team rules are your team's own instructions for Copilot: naming prefixes, which model new elements go to, coding patterns, security conventions, the checks to run before finishing. You write them once in .xpp/agent-rules.md in your repository, commit the file, and everyone who opens the repository in VS Code with F&O Studio gets the same rules added to Copilot's F&O Studio instructions. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Your team has naming conventions (a prefix such as Contoso, extension class names like <BaseObject>_Contoso_Extension) that Copilot should follow without being told each time.
  • You want Copilot to use specific patterns (SysOperation instead of RunBaseBatch, labels for every text) or to run specific checks before it says it is done.
  • You want the F&O Code Reviewer to review against your rules: it checks the team rules in .xpp/agent-rules.md as part of every review.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A folder open in VS Code: the rules file lives in the workspace (your repository), so the whole team shares it through source control. A project opened with Open Project… opens its workspace folders.
  • GitHub Copilot using the F&O Studio MCP server (registered automatically; see MCP Agent Tools).

docs.title: Create the rules file
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Create Team Rules for Copilot from the Command Palette, or click Create Team Rules for Copilot in the Dynamics 365 view under Copilot.
  2. F&O Studio creates .xpp/agent-rules.md in the first workspace folder, filled with an example, and opens it. If the file already exists, it just opens it.
  3. Edit the rules. Delete the examples that don't apply, and be specific.
  4. Save. F&O Studio notices the change and restarts Copilot's F&O Studio MCP server so the new rules apply from the next request.
  5. Commit .xpp/agent-rules.md so the rest of the team gets it.

If no folder is open, the command fails with "Open a folder (your repository) first: the rules live in it, so the whole team shares them."

docs.title: The starting template
docs.text:
The file starts with this example, using the placeholder prefix ABC:

# Team rules for Copilot (F&O Studio)

Copilot reads this file with F&O Studio's own instructions (they are restarted when it changes). Write the rules your
team expects in every change; be specific. Delete the examples that don't apply.

## Naming
- Prefix every new element with `ABC` (tables, classes, EDTs, enums, menu items, security objects).
- Chain of Command classes: `<BaseObject>_ABC_Extension`. Metadata extensions: `<BaseObject>.ABCExtension`.

## Models
- New elements go to the model of the open project; never create elements in another model.

## Code
- Every user-visible text is a label in the label file `ABCLabels`.
- Batch work uses SysOperation (contract, service, controller); no RunBaseBatch.
- No direct SQL; no `doInsert`/`doUpdate` unless the reason is commented.

## Security
- Every new menu item gets View and Maintain privileges, added to the duty `ABC...`.

## Reviews
- Before finishing, run `xpp_analyze_performance` on changed classes and fix every Warning.

docs.title: Writing good rules
docs.text:
• Be concrete. "Prefix new elements with Contoso" works; "use good names" doesn't.
  • Name tools and objects. Rules can refer to F&O Studio agent tools (xpp_build, xpp_check_best_practice, xpp_analyze_performance) and to your label file, duties and models by name.
  • Keep it short. The rules are sent with every new MCP session; only the first 20,000 characters are used.
  • Make them stricter, not looser. The rules are added after F&O Studio's built-in instructions, with the note "follow them where they are stricter than the rules above". They refine the built-in rules; they can't switch off safety rules such as writing only to your own models.

Example for a team using the prefix Contoso:

# Team rules for Copilot

## Naming
- Prefix every new element with `Contoso`.
- CoC classes: `<BaseObject>_Contoso_Extension`, e.g. `SalesFormLetter_Contoso_Extension`.
- Table extensions: `<BaseTable>.ContosoExtensions`, e.g. `CustGroup.ContosoExtensions`.

## Models
- Business logic goes to model `ContosoExtensions`; reports to `ContosoReports`.

## Code
- Every user-visible text is a label in `ContosoLabels`.
- Validation errors use `checkFailed` and return false; never throw from `validateWrite`.
- Batch jobs use SysOperation and run in batch by default.

## Security
- Every new display menu item gets a View privilege and a Maintain privilege, added to the duty `ContosoSalesMaintain`.

## Before finishing
- `xpp_build` without errors or warnings in our elements, then `xpp_check_best_practice`.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/teamRules.ts creates the file from the template in the first workspace folder.
  2. src/mcpProvider.ts registers Copilot's MCP server. When it builds the server definition, it looks for .xpp/agent-rules.md in each workspace folder in order and uses the first one found, passing it as --rules <file>.
  3. A file watcher on **/.xpp/agent-rules.md reacts to create, change and delete. The server definition's version includes the file's modification time, so a change makes VS Code restart the MCP server with the new rules.
  4. The server (server/McpStdioServer.cs) reads the file (up to 20,000 characters) and appends it to the instructions it returns on the MCP initialize request, after its built-in system prompt, under the heading:
== TEAM RULES (from <workspace folder>/.xpp/agent-rules.md; follow them where they are stricter than the rules above) ==
  1. The X++ output channel logs the server start, including the rules file, e.g. X++ MCP server: config ..., project ..., team rules C:\Repos\ContosoFO\.xpp\agent-rules.md.

The rules are not enforced by code: they are instructions the model follows. What the server does enforce (own models only, all-or-nothing writes, the Copilot scope) applies regardless of the rules.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only the first workspace folder that has .xpp/agent-rules.md is used; rules files in other folders of a multi-root workspace are ignored.
  • Only the first 20,000 characters are read.
  • The rules reach Copilot through the F&O Studio MCP server's instructions. A Copilot session that does not use that server (or an MCP server started outside VS Code without --rules) doesn't see them.
  • Rules guide the model; they are not validated. Use Review My Changes, the F&O Code Reviewer and Best Practice Checks to check the result.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Open a folder (your repository) first..." No workspace folder is open Open the repository folder or a D365FO project. Copilot ignores a rule you just added The chat session started before the change, or the file was not saved Save the file and start a new chat; check the X++ output channel for the "team rules" log line. The output line shows no team rules The file is not at .xpp/agent-rules.md directly under a workspace folder Move it there (exact folder and file name). Rules near the end of a long file are ignored The file is longer than 20,000 characters Shorten it; put the most important rules first.

docs.title: Telemetry Queries
docs.text: Telemetry Queries (Application Insights KQL) opens a document with ready-made Kusto (KQL) queries for the telemetry that Finance and Operations sends to Azure Application Insights: the most opened forms, the slowest form loads, the most frequent X++ exceptions, exceptions per hour and custom events. Run from a form, the form queries are filtered to that form. It gives you production numbers (how often, how slow, for how many users) to set next to what Analyze Performance and Analyze Trace find in code and traces. Visual Studio has no equivalent.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Before you tune a form: check how often it opens and how slow its loads are in production (average, 95th percentile, maximum), so you work on what users feel.
  • After a release: compare the form's load times and the exception counts with the week before.
  • When users report errors you can't reproduce: list the most frequent X++ exceptions with how many users hit them and when they last happened.
  • To find which forms matter most in an environment (the most opened ones).
  • To see the custom events your code sends with SysApplicationInsightsTelemetryLogger and data management job events.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
The queries only return data when the environment sends telemetry to Application Insights. That is configured in Finance and Operations, not in F&O Studio (general setup, see Get started with telemetry):

  1. An Application Insights resource in Azure.
  2. The Monitoring and Telemetry feature enabled in Feature management.
  3. In System administration > Monitoring and Telemetry parameters: the environments, the Application Insights connection string per environment mode, and the types of telemetry to send (on the Configure tab).

To run the queries you need read access to that Application Insights resource (or its Log Analytics workspace) in the Azure portal. F&O Studio itself needs no environment, database or sign-in for this command; it only writes the queries.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the command from one of these places:
Where How Application Explorer or the project view Right-click a form > Telemetry Queries (Application Insights KQL). The form queries are filtered to that form. Dynamics 365 view Analyze > Telemetry Queries… (all forms). Command Palette F&O Studio: Telemetry Queries (Application Insights KQL) (all forms).
  1. A new untitled document opens with the queries. Its language is Kusto when an installed extension provides a language with the id kusto (you then get its colouring); otherwise it is plain text.
  2. Change the time range or the filters if needed (see below).
  3. Copy one query (from its comment line to the blank line after it).
  4. In the Azure portal, open the Application Insights resource > Logs, paste the query and run it.
  5. Save the document if you want to keep your edited version; it is an untitled document and nothing is saved for you.

F&O Studio does not connect to Application Insights and does not run the queries.

docs.title: The queries
docs.text:
All queries look at the last 7 days (timestamp > ago(7d)).

Query Table What it returns Most opened forms pageViews The 20 forms opened most often, with the number of opens. Slowest form loads pageViews Per form: opens, average, 95th percentile (P95) and maximum load time in seconds, ordered by P95. Only page views with a duration. Most frequent X++ exceptions exceptions The 20 most frequent exceptions by problemId and outerMessage, with the count, the number of distinct users and the last time. Exceptions per hour (spikes) exceptions Exceptions counted per hour, rendered as a time chart. Custom events customEvents Custom events counted by name: events your code sends with SysApplicationInsightsTelemetryLogger.trackEvent, and data management (DMF) job events.

Form loads are recorded as page views named after the form, so name is the form's AOT name (CustGroup, SalesTable).

docs.title: Filtered to a form
docs.text:
Run from a form in Application Explorer or the project view, both form queries get a filter on the form name, for example for CustGroup:

// Slowest form loads
pageViews
| where timestamp > ago(7d) and duration > 0
| where name == "CustGroup"
| summarize ['Opens'] = count(), ['Avg (s)'] = round(avg(duration) / 1000, 2), ['P95 (s)'] = round(percentile(duration, 95) / 1000, 2), ['Max (s)'] = round(max(duration) / 1000, 2) by name
| order by ['P95 (s)'] desc

The exception and custom event queries are not filtered by form.

docs.title: All forms
docs.text:
From the Dynamics 365 view or the Command Palette, the form queries cover every form except SysOperationSandboxForm, SysBoxForm and Dialog, which are left out:

// Most opened forms
pageViews
| where timestamp > ago(7d)
| where name !in ("SysOperationSandboxForm", "SysBoxForm", "Dialog")
| summarize ['Form opens'] = count() by name
| top 20 by ['Form opens'] desc

docs.title: Log Analytics workspaces
docs.text: The queries use the Application Insights table names (pageViews, exceptions, customEvents). When you query the Log Analytics workspace behind a workspace-based Application Insights resource instead, use AppPageViews, AppExceptions, AppEvents and AppTraces (the document's first comment says so). Some column names differ there too (for example TimeGenerated instead of timestamp); adjust the query before you run it.

docs.title: Adapting the queries
docs.text:
• Change ago(7d) to the window you need, for example ago(1d) after a release, or between (datetime(2026-11-01) .. datetime(2026-11-08)) to compare two weeks.
  • Change top 20 to see more rows.
  • Add | where user_Id == "<user>" to the exception queries to follow one user, or filter outerMessage with has to follow one message.
  • Add a bin(timestamp, 1d) to the form query's summarize to see the load time per day.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings. The time window and filters are in the query text; edit them in the document.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/telemetry.ts builds the query text and opens it with vscode.workspace.openTextDocument:

  • When the command runs on a tree item that is a form (AxForm), its name is added as where name == "<form>". Only letters, digits and underscores are kept from the name.
  • Otherwise the form queries exclude SysOperationSandboxForm, SysBoxForm and Dialog.
  • The document language is kusto when VS Code knows a language with that id, else plaintext.

No server call, no network access and no files are written.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• F&O Studio does not run the queries or show results; you run them in the Azure portal (or any tool that queries Application Insights).
  • The queries cover forms, exceptions and custom events. Other telemetry (for example batch, database or integration telemetry) is not included; the Microsoft documentation and its sample dashboards cover those.
  • The form filter applies to the form queries only.
  • The command only filters on forms. From other element types it is not in the context menu.
  • The queries return nothing when the environment does not send telemetry, or when that type of telemetry is not switched on in Monitoring and Telemetry parameters.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The query returns no rows. The environment does not send telemetry, or not this type (form runs, exceptions). Check the setup in Monitoring and Telemetry parameters and that the connection string points to the resource you query. The query fails because the table pageViews (or exceptions, customEvents) can't be resolved. You are querying a Log Analytics workspace. Use AppPageViews, AppExceptions and AppEvents, and their column names. The document has no colouring. No installed extension provides the kusto language. Install a Kusto language extension, or ignore it: the text is the same. No form filter in the queries. The command was run from the Dynamics 365 view or the Command Palette. Right-click the form in Application Explorer or the project view instead.

docs.title: Test Explorer
docs.text: F&O Studio adds your project's SysTest classes to VS Code's Testing view (the Test Explorer). Each test class is a node, each test method a child. Run a method, a class or all of them with Run on environment: the tests run on your unified developer environment through the same runner as Run Tests, and each method shows passed, failed or skipped with its duration and failure message. This is the VS Code counterpart of Visual Studio's Test Explorer for X++ tests.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• To see all test methods of your project at a glance and run any subset.
  • To rerun only the failed tests after a fix.
  • To read the assertion message and Infolog of a failed test next to the test.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An open D365FO project that contains your test classes (see D365FO Projects). Discovery reads the project's classes.
  • A unified developer environment (UDE), selected and signed in. Discovery works on any environment, but running needs a UDE.
  • The tests must be built and deployed: they run against the code deployed to the environment. See Build Project and Model and Deploy to Environment.
  • Test classes extend a class whose name contains Test (for example SysTestCase); test methods are public and start with test or carry [SysTestMethod]. See Run Tests for an example.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Open the Testing view (the beaker icon in the activity bar, or View: Show Testing).
  2. The X++ tests controller lists the test classes of the open project. Expand a class to see its test methods.
  3. Discovery runs when the Testing view first loads the tests.
  4. After you add test classes or methods, click Refresh Tests in the Testing view's title bar.
  5. Run tests:
  6. hover a method or class and click its run button;
  7. or click Run Tests at the top of the view to run everything;
  8. or right-click and choose Run Test. The run profile is called Run on environment; it is the default (and only) profile.
  9. While the tests run, the items show as queued, then running. The Test Results panel shows the same progress lines as the X++ Tests output of Run Tests, followed by the summary.
  10. When results arrive, each method shows:
  11. passed, with its duration;
  12. failed, with the assertion message and, when there is one, "Infolog: ..." below it;
  13. skipped, when the environment did not execute it or returned no result for it.
  14. Click a test item's Go to Test to open the class's code view.

docs.title: What a run includes
docs.text:
• Running a class runs all its test methods, except methods you excluded in the request.
  • Running a method runs only that method.
  • When you run methods of several classes, all selected methods go to the environment in one test suite.

docs.title: A typical loop
docs.text:
1. Write or change a test class in your project (or let the F&O Test Engineer agent write it; see Generate SysTest Class).
  2. Build the project (Ctrl+Shift+B in the code view).
  3. Deploy the package (Deploy to Environment); check that the project item in the status bar no longer shows the cloud-upload icon.
  4. Click Refresh Tests if you added methods, then run the class.
  5. Open a failed test's message to read the assertion and the Infolog, fix the code, and repeat from step 2.
  6. Use VS Code's Rerun Failed Tests to run only the failures again.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no Test Explorer settings. VS Code's own testing settings (for example whether the Testing view opens on a failure) apply as usual.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/testExplorer.ts creates a VS Code test controller xppTests ("X++ tests"):

  • Discovery calls the same discoverTests as Run Tests with no classes, so it reads the classes of the open project through the metadata server (read_object) and keeps public test* or [SysTestMethod] methods of classes that extend a *Test* class. Classes become items with the id <Class>, methods items with the id <Class>.<method>. Both point at the class's code view.
  • Running first checks the environment: on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment every selected test errors with "Tests run through Dataverse, which only unified developer environments have." Otherwise it passes the selected classes and method names to runTests (core/src/tests.ts), which uploads the suite to Dataverse, starts msprov_unittestexecutiononfinopsasync, polls, and downloads the .trx result. See Run Tests for those steps.
  • Matching results. TRX test names are Class.method, sometimes with a namespace in front; a result matches a test item when its name equals the item id or ends with .<id> (case-insensitive).
  • Outcomes. Passed becomes passed with the duration converted from the TRX format hh:mm:ss.fffffff; NotExecuted and Skipped become skipped; every other outcome becomes failed with the message and Infolog. A test without a result is skipped.
  • Errors. If the run itself fails (no environment selected, sign-in, timeout, the suite failed on the environment), every selected test errors with that message.

docs.title: Differences from the Run Tests command
docs.text:
Test Explorer Run Tests command xpp_run_tests Choose tests Any methods or classes The project's tests, or one class from a context menu classes, methods Built-versus-deployed warning No Yes (Deploy First / Continue) Yes, in the result text Results Per test item X++ Tests output and a message Text for the agent Timeout 30 minutes 30 minutes timeoutMinutes, default 30

Because the Test Explorer does not warn when your build is newer than the last deploy, check the project item in the Status Bar first: a cloud-upload icon means the environment runs older code.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• UDEs only for running; on cloud-hosted and VHD environments, run tests from Visual Studio on the VM.
  • Only the open project's classes are discovered. Test classes outside the project do not appear.
  • There is no debug profile and no coverage profile.
  • Items open the class code view, not the method line.
  • Tests run the deployed code; a build alone does not change what is tested.
  • Cancelling stops waiting; the run may continue on the environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A single item "Discovery failed: Pass test classes, or open a D365FO project whose test classes should run." No project is open. Open the project, then click Refresh Tests. The Testing view is empty The project has no class that matches the discovery rules. Check that the class extends SysTestCase (or a *Test* base) and its methods are public and start with test. A new test method is missing Discovery runs on load and on refresh only. Click Refresh Tests. Every test errors with the same message The run failed as a whole (environment, sign-in, timeout). Read the message; see Run Tests troubleshooting. Tests are skipped The environment returned no result for them. Check that the package is deployed and the classes exist on the environment. A fixed test still fails The fix is built but not deployed. Deploy, then run again.

docs.title: Testing the Extension
docs.text:
F&O Studio is tested at several levels: unit tests without an environment, checks that keep generated files and contracts in step, end-to-end scripts that drive the real server against a D365FO installation, security probes, and smoke tests inside a real VS Code. This page lists them, what each covers, and when to run it.

It is for contributors. If you only use F&O Studio and something fails, see Troubleshooting and Report-a-Problem.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Build first: npm run build (see Building-from-Source).
  • Most server tests need a D365FO installation with an active configuration (registry CurrentMetadataConfig) and a cross-reference database in SQL Server LocalDB.
  • Write tests need a custom model of your own. Tests write only throw-away objects with an Xvs prefix (XvsDast*, XvsGm*, XvsTest*) and delete them again. Never point a write test at a standard object or a production environment.
  • Some end-to-end scripts have the maintainer's demo project and model as defaults. Pass your own (-Project, --project, --model, <model> arguments) or edit the constants at the top of the script before you run it.
  • Always run the server with a timeout. The scripts do; if you write your own, use Process.WaitForExit(ms) or a timer and never leave a stdio session waiting.

docs.title: Which tests to run
docs.text: You changed Run core/ npm run test:core Server code npm run test:server, scripts/smoke-test.ps1, node scripts/security-probes.js A server refactoring that must not change behaviour golden master before and after A bridge action node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js (part of test:server) An agent tool node scripts/check-tools.js, node scripts/tool-regression.js Code view or formatter node scripts/source-test.js, node scripts/roundtrip.js Form preview node scripts/form-preview-test.js Report designer node scripts/report-designer-test.js, node scripts/report-test.js Wizards node scripts/scaffold-test.js Build with C# references node scripts/references-test.js, node scripts/dotnet-xpp-test.js Agents node scripts/build-agents.js --check Release notes node scripts/changelog.js --check UI wiring node scripts/run-smoke.js [suite ...]

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
npm run test:core

Runs node scripts/check-core.js (no VS Code in core/; see Core-Library) and then node --test in core/. The tests use a fake TokenProvider and recorded HTTP responses in core/test/fixtures for deploy, a failed database sync, a test run, SQL credentials and the UDE check. No network.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
npm run test:server

Builds the server with -Test, runs the xUnit project in test/server (dotnet test), then node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js. The unit tests cover JSON escaping, the Microsoft Learn URL allow-list, label file IDs and languages, the write policy through the dispatcher (standard objects refused, reads never consult the policy, agent writes follow the scope and the checkpoint), the bridge registry against the contract, and typed form metadata. They compile against the D365FO assemblies, so the build needs PackagesLocalDirectory\bin.

docs.title: Offline checks the release runs
docs.text: Script Checks node scripts/source-test.js code view splitting and the formatter on tricky X++: @'...' and @"..." verbatim strings, interfaces, tab-indented methods node scripts/form-preview-test.js form preview behaviour in headless Edge with a synthetic form (no server) node scripts/xpp-config-test.js configurations F&O Studio writes are readable by Visual Studio (offline checks; with a real configuration and FinOps tools, Visual Studio's own parser via scripts/vs-config-probe.ps1) node scripts/vs-tools-test.js detection of Visual Studio's FinOps tools node scripts/solution-test.js the solution helpers behind the project view node scripts/report-designer-test.js the report designer in headless Edge: edits by mouse and keyboard, save, resulting RDL

docs.title: Contract and generated-file checks
docs.text:
Script Fails when node scripts/check-bridge-actions.js src/bridgeContract.ts and the server's registered actions differ, or the extension calls an action the server does not serve node scripts/check-tools.js <exe> <config> tools/list is not valid JSON or a tool lacks an object input schema node scripts/build-agents.js --check agents/* or the agent contributions in package.json are out of date node scripts/changelog.js --check CHANGELOG.md is out of date with docs/FEATURES.md

The server also checks itself at start: it refuses to start when server/Resources/Tools.json and the registered tools differ.

docs.title: Server end-to-end tests
docs.text: These start server\bin\XppVsCode.Server.exe over stdio with your configuration.

docs.title: Smoke test
docs.text:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\smoke-test.ps1 -Project <your .rnrproj> -TimeoutSeconds 300

Sends initialize, tools/list and 16 read-only tool calls (environment, models, CustTable, SalesFormLetter.construct, SalesStatus, CustVendTable, the CustParameters form layout, references, labels, project items, validation, a type schema) and checks each result for expected text. All must PASS. Run it after every server change. Some expected texts name the maintainer's demo model and project items; adjust them for your own project.

docs.title: Security probes (DAST)
docs.text:
node scripts/security-probes.js --model <your custom model>

Every probe must PASS after a server change. See Security-Model for what they cover. Probes against standard objects carry a payload the handler rejects before saving, so even a missing ownership check cannot change standard metadata.

docs.title: Golden master
docs.text:
For refactorings that must not change behaviour:

node scripts\golden-master.js %TEMP%\gm-base.json
# ... make the change, rebuild ...
node scripts\golden-master.js %TEMP%\gm-after.json --compare %TEMP%\gm-base.json

It runs a fixed set of MCP methods, every bridge action, every listed tool (it fails when one is not exercised) and every element type, normalizes the responses and compares them. It must report IDENTICAL. Results that depend on the network, Git or the clock are compared by shape only. Writes go only to XvsGm* objects and a test label that is removed again.

docs.title: Feature scripts
docs.text:
Script Usage Covers tool-regression.js node scripts/tool-regression.js [--project <rnrproj>] [--cases <json>] [--issue <regex>] agent tool cases from scripts/tool-regression.json, each with an expected regex cold-start-test.js <exe> <config> [form] [runs] opening a form as the first request of fresh servers never races the metadata warm-up checkpoint-test.js <exe> <config> <model> Copilot checkpoint and scope end to end: the MCP server changes one class inside a checkpoint and is refused another outside the scope; the extension's server lists and reverts scaffold-test.js <exe> <config> <model> every wizard's elements are created, the model builds without errors or warnings in them, and everything is deleted write-test.js code view save path and form extension calls (XvsTest* objects) roundtrip.js <exe> <config> Type:Name ... real objects round-trip through composeSource and splitSource diag-test.js compiler errors map to the right code view lines data-test.js <config> <sqlServer> <database> [table] xpp/data and table_data_shape, with the cross-reference database standing in for AxDB trace-test.js <exe> <config> <file.etl> xpp/trace and xpp_analyze_trace on a real trace report-test.js <exe> <config> [report] [design] [outDir] [customModel] report metadata, rendering to PNG and PDF (needs the Report Viewer runtime) references-test.js C# references are built and copied into the package bin like Visual Studio (needs MSBuild) dotnet-xpp-test.js <exe> <config> <rnrproj> X++ calling C# and C# calling X++, built and cleaned up

Helpers for debugging: bridge-call.js, tool-call.js, source-shape.js, split-debug.js (see Bridge-Protocol).

docs.title: Extension-host smoke tests
docs.text:
These run the extension in a VS Code downloaded by @vscode/test-electron (under .vscode-test), with other extensions disabled and a separate user data folder, so they do not touch your installed VS Code.

$env:XPP_TEST_WORKSPACE = '<folder or .code-workspace of a test project>'   # optional
node scripts\run-smoke.js                 # every suite
node scripts\run-smoke.js goToSmoke reportSmoke

Suites in test/: workflowSmoke, databaseSmoke, securitySmoke, productivitySmoke, projectSmoke, solutionSmoke, definitionSmoke, goToSmoke, codeIntelSmoke, historySmoke, dragDropSmoke, debugAdapterSmoke, reportSmoke. Each writes its checks to a JSON file; run-smoke.js prints PASS or FAIL per check and exits with 1 when any fail. A single suite can also run with node test/runInDownloadedCode.js test/<suite>.js.

test/commandSweep.js runs every contributed command in a real extension host: without arguments as from the Command Palette, with tree items as from context menus, and with a designer open. Prompts are cancelled by default (XPP_SWEEP_ANSWER=cancel, or first for safe commands). It records errors, messages, opened panels, URLs, files written in the custom model, time and timeouts. Run it with node scripts/run-smoke.js commandSweep.

docs.title: Review records
docs.text: Findings from architecture reviews, static analysis, the security probes and end-to-end trials, with their status, are kept in docs/review-findings.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Smoke test prints TIMEOUT The server did not answer within -TimeoutSeconds (first metadata load is slow) Raise the timeout; check stderr in the output A smoke check fails on expected text The default project or model is not yours Pass -Project and adjust the expected texts Golden master reports differences you did not intend Your change altered behaviour Fix the change, or confirm and record the intended difference run-smoke.js says "no results" for a suite VS Code could not start or the suite crashed Run that suite alone with test/runInDownloadedCode.js and read its output test:server fails to build PackagesLocalDirectory\bin not found See Building-from-Source

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page collects the messages F&O Studio shows most often when something is missing or goes wrong, what causes them and how to fix them. The messages are quoted as the extension shows them; ... stands for a name, path or value that changes. For problems with one feature, also see the Troubleshooting section of that feature's page.

docs.title: First steps for any problem
docs.text:
1. Read the log. F&O Studio writes to four output channels (View > Output, then pick one):
Output channel Contains X++ The metadata server, environment setup, connection checks, debugger messages and every failed command with its stack X++ Build Compiler (xppc, LabelC) and C# project build output X++ Deploy Deploy and database sync progress X++ Tests Test runs
  1. Use the buttons on the error. An unexpected error shows Show Log (opens the X++ output) and Report Problem (see Report-a-Problem).
  2. Check the environment. Run Show Active Environment to write the active configuration to the X++ output, and Check Environment Connection for a unified developer environment.
  3. Restart the server. Restart X++ Server reloads the metadata. Use it after you change models or configurations outside F&O Studio.

docs.title: Environment setup and connection
docs.text: Message or symptom Cause Fix Application Explorer says "No D365FO metadata found on this machine." No D365FO configuration is active on this machine On a UDE, run Connect to Environment…. On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, check that AosService\PackagesLocalDirectory exists "No active D365FO configuration found. Connect to a unified developer environment first, or work on a cloud-hosted or VHD environment (AosService\PackagesLocalDirectory)." Same as above Same as above. See Select-Environment "Enter a URL such as https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com" (in the URL box) The text is not a URL Paste the environment URL "That is a portal page. Copy the environment's "Environment URL" (https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com) from the Power Platform admin center." Enter the Dataverse URL (https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com) from the Power Platform admin center." The Microsoft sign-in was cancelled or failed Run the command again and complete the sign-in. If your tenant blocks VS Code's default sign-in for Dataverse, set xpp.auth.clientId. See Sign-In-and-Authentication "Not a unified developer environment (type ...)." GB is available." One setup step failed Read the message, fix the cause and select Retry (also in the Environment group of the Dynamics 365 view). Show Log shows each step Warning: "The environment now runs application ...; this machine has the metadata of .... Builds compile against the old version and deploys can fail." docs.title: The X++ server
docs.text:
The metadata server (XppVsCode.Server.exe) loads the D365FO metadata for the Application Explorer, designers, code views and agent tools.

docs.title: Try Data Entity (OData)
docs.text: Try Data Entity (OData)… queries a public data entity on the active environment over OData, with your own Microsoft sign-in, and shows the JSON response in an editor. You choose a $filter, a $top and whether to read across companies. You can save the request as an .http file to run again later, without the access token in it. It replaces the usual detour through Postman or a browser when you build or debug an entity. Visual Studio has no equivalent. This feature is a preview: it has not been verified end to end on a live environment.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You created or extended a data entity and want to see what OData returns after deploying it.
  • An integration reports wrong or missing values and you want to see the entity's output for one record.
  • You want a ready .http request for a teammate or for the REST Client extension.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The active environment has a web client URL: CloudInstanceURL in its configuration. Environments connected with Connect to Environment and cloud-hosted or VHD machines have one.
  • The entity is in your metadata and public: IsPublic = Yes and a PublicCollectionName set. See Wizard: Data Entity.
  • The entity, with your latest changes, is deployed and the database synchronized on that environment (Deploy to Environment, Synchronize Database). F&O Studio reads the entity's properties from your local metadata, but the environment answers with what is deployed.
  • Your Microsoft account has access to the environment. VS Code asks you to sign in the first time.
  • To save requests, a folder open in the workspace.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. In Application Explorer or the project view, right-click a data entity and choose Try Data Entity (OData)…. The command is not in the Command Palette.
  2. $filter (optional). The prompt title is <PublicCollectionName>: $filter (optional). Enter an OData filter, for example dataAreaId eq 'usmf' or CustomerGroupId eq '10', or leave it empty. Press Escape to cancel.
  3. $top. Choose 10, 50 or 200.
  4. Companies. Choose All companies (cross-company=true) or Default company only (your default company in the environment).
  5. VS Code may ask you to sign in with your Microsoft account for the environment.
  6. A progress notification GET <Entity> (OData)… shows while the request runs.
  7. The response opens beside the current editor as a JSON document, pretty-printed, with two header comments:
// GET /data/CustomersV3?$top=10&$filter=CustomerGroupId%20eq%20'10'&cross-company=true
// 200 OK
{
  "@odata.context": "https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com/data/$metadata#CustomersV3",
  "value": [
    {
      "dataAreaId": "usmf",
      "CustomerAccount": "US-001",
      "CustomerGroupId": "10"
    }
  ]
}

(Shortened: the real response has all public fields of the entity.)

  1. A notification shows the status, for example CustCustomerV3Entity (OData): 200 OK, with a Save as .http button.

docs.title: Save as .http
docs.text:
Save as .http writes .xpp/requests/<Entity>_OData_.http in the first workspace folder and opens it, for example .xpp/requests/CustCustomerV3Entity_OData_.http:

@baseUrl = https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com
# @token: an access token for @baseUrl (for example from az account get-access-token --resource @baseUrl)

### CustCustomerV3Entity (OData)
GET {{baseUrl}}/data/CustomersV3?$top=10&$filter=CustomerGroupId%20eq%20'10'&cross-company=true
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Accept: application/json

The access token is never written. To run the file with an .http client (for example the REST Client extension), define the token variable yourself, for example with a line @token = <access token> that you do not commit. The comment shows one way to get a token with the Azure CLI. Running the same entity again overwrites the file.

Consider adding .xpp/requests/ to .gitignore if the requests contain test data you do not want to share.

docs.title: Writing filters
docs.text:
The filter is sent as you type it (URL-encoded). OData uses the entity's public field names (data entity field names), not table field names:

Goal $filter One company dataAreaId eq 'usmf' One record CustomerAccount eq 'US-001' Starts with startswith(CustomerAccount, 'US-') Combine dataAreaId eq 'usmf' and CustomerGroupId eq '10'

Without All companies, OData returns rows of your default company only, and a dataAreaId filter on another company returns nothing.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings. The URL comes from the active environment's configuration (CloudInstanceURL); the xpp.financeAndOperationsUrl setting is not used here.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/integration.ts:

  1. Reads the entity with the bridge action read_object (AxDataEntityView) from the metadata server and checks IsPublic and PublicCollectionName.
  2. Builds GET /data/<PublicCollectionName>?$top=<n>[&$filter=<encoded>][&cross-company=true].
  3. Reads the active environment's web client URL and keeps only its origin (https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com). Only that origin is called.
  4. Gets an access token from VS Code's Microsoft authentication provider for the scope <origin>/.default (it asks you to sign in when there is no session).
  5. Sends the request with Authorization: Bearer <token> and Accept: application/json.
  6. Shows the response: JSON is pretty-printed; anything else (an HTML error page, for example) is shown as it came.
  7. On Save as .http, writes the request in REST Client format with {{baseUrl}} and {{token}} variables.

The token stays in memory for the request. The call runs from the extension host, not from the metadata server or an agent.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview, not verified end to end on a live environment.
  • GET only: no create, update or delete through this command.
  • Only $filter, $top and cross-company. For $select, $expand, $orderby or $count, edit the saved .http file and run it with an .http client.
  • No paging: only the first page ($top rows).
  • Entities that are not public (OData off) are refused.
  • Only the active environment's own URL is called.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix " is not public (IsPublic = Yes and a PublicCollectionName are needed for OData)." The entity is not exposed to OData Set IsPublic to Yes and a PublicCollectionName, build, deploy and sync "Data entity not found." Not in your metadata Check the name "The active environment has no web client URL (CloudInstanceURL)." The configuration has no web client URL Reconnect with Connect to Environment 401 Unauthorized Your account has no access, or the token is for another tenant Sign in with an account that is a user of the environment (Sign-In and Authentication) 404 Not Found The entity is not deployed on the environment, or the collection name changed Deploy and synchronize; check PublicCollectionName 200 OK with an empty value No rows match, or rows are in another company Choose All companies or check the filter 400 Bad Request The $filter syntax or a field name is wrong Use public field names and OData syntax "Open a workspace folder to save requests." No folder open Open the project folder, then save again
