docs.title: Try Service Operation
docs.text: Try Service Operation… calls an operation of a custom service on the active environment with your own Microsoft sign-in. F&O Studio fills a JSON request body from the operation's parameters and data contracts, lets you edit it, asks before it calls (a service may change data), and shows the response in an editor. You can save the request as an .http file without the access token. Visual Studio has no equivalent; developers usually test custom services with Postman or a small client. This feature is a preview: it has not been verified end to end on a live environment.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You built a custom service (for example with Wizard: Custom Service) and want to call it after deploying it.
  • An integration fails and you want to send the same request yourself and read the error.
  • You need a request body template for the integration team.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The service, its class and its data contracts are in your metadata. F&O Studio reads them locally to build the body.
  • The service is in a service group, and the group is deployed on the environment (Deploy to Environment). Custom services are published as /api/services/<ServiceGroup>/<Service>/<Operation>.
  • The active environment has a web client URL (CloudInstanceURL in its configuration), as environments set up with Connect to Environment and cloud-hosted or VHD machines have.
  • Your Microsoft account is a user of the environment with access to the service operation. VS Code asks you to sign in the first time.
  • To save requests, a folder open in the workspace.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
Example service: ContosoOrderService, class ContosoOrderServiceClass with an operation getOrderStatus, in the service group ContosoOrderServiceGroup.

  1. In Application Explorer or the project view, right-click the service and choose Try Service Operation…. The command is not in the Command Palette.
  2. Operation. Pick the operation from the service's operations (title <Service>: operation).
  3. Service group. Enter the service group that publishes the service. The box is prefilled with the service name without the Service suffix plus ServiceGroup (here ContosoOrderServiceGroup). The name must be a single word (letters, digits, underscore).
  4. A JSON document opens with the request body built from the operation's parameters, for example:
{
    "_contract": {
        "SalesId": "",
        "IncludeLines": false
    }
}

Here the operation's method is getOrderStatus(ContosoOrderStatusContract _contract); the contract is shown below.

  1. Edit the body: fill in the values you want to send. Keep the document open.
  2. A notification says Edit the request body of <Service>.<operation>, then send it. with two buttons:
  3. Send: a modal asks Call <Service>.<operation> on the environment? ("The service runs its code with your account and may change data."). Choose Call to send.
  4. Save as .http: saves the request without calling it. The body is read from the document when you click the button, so edit it first.
  5. After Call, a progress notification shows POST <Service>.<operation>….
  6. The response opens beside the editor, pretty-printed when it is JSON, with the request line and status as comments:
// POST /api/services/ContosoOrderServiceGroup/ContosoOrderService/getOrderStatus
// 200 OK
{
  "Status": "Open"
}
  1. A notification shows the status with a Save as .http button.

docs.title: How the body is built
docs.text:
F&O Studio reads the service's class and finds the method behind the operation. Each parameter becomes a property named like the parameter:

Parameter type Sample value str "" int, int64 0 real 0.0 boolean false date "1900-01-01" utcdatetime "1900-01-01T00:00:00Z" A data contract class An object with one property per DataMember method Anything else (extended data types, enums, unknown types) ""

For a data contract, each method with a DataMember attribute becomes a property. Its name is the attribute's argument ([DataMember('SalesId')]), or the method name without parm when the attribute has none. Its value follows the method's return type, using the same table. Contracts inside contracts are expanded up to three levels; deeper ones are null.

A contract like this:

[DataContract]
class ContosoOrderStatusContract
{
    SalesId salesId;
    boolean includeLines;

    [DataMember('SalesId')]
    public SalesId parmSalesId(SalesId _salesId = salesId)
    {
        salesId = _salesId;
        return salesId;
    }

    [DataMember('IncludeLines')]
    public boolean parmIncludeLines(boolean _includeLines = includeLines)
    {
        includeLines = _includeLines;
        return includeLines;
    }
}

gives { "SalesId": "", "IncludeLines": false } for that parameter. SalesId is an extended data type, so it gets an empty string; fill in a value.

docs.title: Save as .http
docs.text:
Save as .http writes .xpp/requests/<Service>.<operation>.http in the first workspace folder and opens it:

@baseUrl = https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com
# @token: an access token for @baseUrl (for example from az account get-access-token --resource @baseUrl)

### ContosoOrderService.getOrderStatus
POST {{baseUrl}}/api/services/ContosoOrderServiceGroup/ContosoOrderService/getOrderStatus
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json

{
    "_contract": {
        "SalesId": "SO-000123",
        "IncludeLines": false
    }
}

The access token is never written. Define the token variable yourself (for example @token = <access token> in a line you do not commit) to run the file with an .http client such as the REST Client extension. Saving again overwrites the file.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings. The URL comes from the active environment's configuration (CloudInstanceURL).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/integration.ts:

  1. Reads the service with the bridge action read_object (AxService): its class and its operations (name and method name).
  2. Reads the class with read_object (AxClass), takes the operation's method source and its parameter list.
  3. For each parameter type that is not a primitive, tries to read a class of that name; when it is one, its DataMember methods become the object's properties.
  4. Opens the body as an untitled JSON document.
  5. On Send and Call, gets an access token from VS Code's Microsoft authentication provider for the scope <origin>/.default of the environment's web client URL, and sends POST <origin>/api/services/<group>/<service>/<operation> with Authorization: Bearer <token>, Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json.
  6. Shows the response; JSON is pretty-printed, anything else as it came.
  7. Save as .http writes the request in REST Client format with {{baseUrl}} and {{token}}.

Only the active environment's own origin is called. The token is kept in memory for the request only.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview, not verified end to end on a live environment.
  • The service group is not looked up; you type it.
  • The body is a starting point. Extended data types, enums and collection types (List) get an empty string; fill them in. The body is built from the first parameter list in the method's source, so an attribute with arguments written before the method declaration can give a wrong body: check it against the method.
  • No retries or paging. One call per run.
  • The service runs with your account and its security: a missing privilege gives an error, not data.
  • Service calls can change data. Use a development environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Service not found." The service is not in your metadata Check the name The operation list is empty The service has no operations Add operations to the service "A service group name." The service group box contains spaces or other characters Enter a single word "The active environment has no web client URL (CloudInstanceURL)." The configuration has no web client URL Reconnect with Connect to Environment 404 Not Found Wrong service group, or the group is not deployed Check the group that holds the service; deploy it 401 Unauthorized Your account has no access to the environment Sign in with a user of the environment (Sign-In and Authentication) 500 with an X++ error in the body The operation threw an error Read the message; debug the operation (Debugger) A body property is "" where a number is expected Extended data types and enums are not resolved Replace the value before sending "Open a workspace folder to save requests." docs.title: Upgrade Readiness
docs.text: Upgrade Readiness tells you what in one of your models breaks or needs attention on the installed application version. It reports three things: uses of APIs marked [SysObsolete] (with the replacement the attribute names), extensions that no longer match the installed code (Chain of Command wrappers, event handlers, table, form and enum extensions), and collisions with other models' extensions of the same elements. Run it after you download the metadata of a new version and before you build. Visual Studio has no equivalent; there you find these problems as build errors, one at a time.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• After a platform or application update: connect to (or download) the new version's metadata, then check each of your models.
  • Before you plan an upgrade: run it on the version you upgrade to, to size the work.
  • When you install an ISV solution or another team's model next to yours, to find collisions.
  • Periodically, to find obsolete calls before they become compile errors.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The model must be one of your models in the custom metadata folder. The model picker lists only those, and the extension checks refuse other models.
  • The obsolete API part reads the cross-reference database. It is as current as the last build with cross references (xpp.build.crossReference, on by default). Build the model first on the version you check.
  • The extension checks read the metadata of the active configuration. Select the configuration of the version you want to check (Select Environment).

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Start it from one of these places:
  2. Application Explorer: right-click one of your models (model node) > Upgrade Readiness.
  3. Dynamics 365 view: Build and check > Upgrade Readiness….
  4. Command Palette: F&O Studio: Upgrade Readiness.
  5. The empty Results view: the Upgrade Readiness link.
  6. Without a model from the context menu, a quick pick "Upgrade readiness: model" lists your models. The project's model is marked "project model".
  7. Progress shows in the Results view: "Checking for obsolete APIs…".
  8. The Results view shows three sections:
  9. Obsolete API uses
  10. Extension compatibility
  11. Collisions with other models

    12. Each section's description is its summary line; findings are listed below with error, warning or info icons. 5. Click a finding to open the element's code at the method (and line, for obsolete uses). 6. Copy Report as Markdown or Export Report… gives the full text report; Run Again checks the same model again.

docs.title: 1. Obsolete API uses
docs.text:
Every place the model's package uses a class, table or method marked [SysObsolete], from the cross-reference database. Each finding shows the method, the line, the obsolete API and the attribute's message (often the replacement). Uses of APIs whose attribute is marked as an error (they stop compiling in a later version) are errors; the others are warnings.

Summary line example:

Package ContosoExtensions: 3 use(s) of obsolete APIs, 1 of them marked as errors (they stop compiling in a later version).
- [error] ContosoSalesHelper.post line 42 uses SomeClass.oldMethod: Use SomeClass.newMethod instead.
- ContosoCustReport.run line 17 uses SomeTable.findOld: <SysObsolete message>

The report lists up to 500 uses. An obsolete element's own references to itself are left out. With no uses it says "Nothing to change. The result is as current as the last build with cross references."

While you type, the editor also marks calls to obsolete APIs (see Syntax Check and Obsolete Warnings).

docs.title: 2. Extension compatibility
docs.text:
Every Chain of Command wrapper, event handler and metadata extension of the model, checked against the installed code. The summary line counts what was checked:

Extension compatibility: 12 Chain of Command wrapper(s), 4 event handler(s) and 9 metadata extension(s) checked against the installed code; 2 finding(s):
- Error CocSignatureChanged: ContosoSalesFormLetter_Extension.run: The signature of Class SalesFormLetter.run changed: .... Update the wrapper's signature.

Rules:

Rule Severity Applies to Meaning CocTargetMissing Error Wrapper The class, table, form, data entity, view or form data source the extension targets no longer exists. CocMethodMissing Error Wrapper The target has no method of that name any more (also not in its base classes): the wrapper no longer compiles. CocNotWrappable Error Wrapper The target method is now [Wrappable(false)], [Hookable(false)], private, or final (without [Wrappable(true)]). CocInternal Warning Wrapper The target method is internal: it can only be wrapped from its own package. CocSignatureChanged Error Wrapper The target method's signature differs from the wrapper's (static, return type, parameters). CocTargetObsolete Warning Wrapper The target method is [SysObsolete]; move the logic to its replacement. CocNotChecked Info Wrapper The target method's signature could not be read; check it by hand. HandlerTargetMissing Error Event handler The class, form, table, method or delegate the handler subscribes to is gone, the table of a data event handler is gone, or the method is now [Hookable(false)] (pre/post handlers are no longer called). ExtensionBaseMissing Error Metadata extension The extended element no longer exists. ExtensionFieldMissing Error Table extension It modifies a field the table no longer has. ExtensionFieldGroupMissing Error Table extension It adds fields to a field group the table no longer has. ExtensionControlMissing Error Form extension It changes a control the form no longer has. ExtensionParentMissing Error Form extension It adds a control into a parent the form no longer has. ExtensionAnchorMissing Warning Form extension It places a control after a sibling the form no longer has. EnumNotExtensible Error Enum extension The enum is no longer extensible.

Details that avoid false alarms:

  • A method counts as a Chain of Command wrapper when its code calls next on its own name (next run(). Event handlers are recognized by their handler attributes.
  • Methods every table, form and form data source get from the kernel (for example insert, validateWrite, modifiedField on tables; init, run, close on forms; executeQuery, active, write on data sources) can be wrapped without an X++ override, so a missing override is not reported. Signature differences on these kernel methods are not reported either.
  • For classes, the base classes' methods count. If a class derives from a kernel class without X++ metadata, missing methods are not reported.
  • Controls added by your or other models' form extensions count as valid parents and anchors.
  • For form fields and controls as targets, only the form's existence is checked.

docs.title: 3. Collisions with other models
docs.text:
Your model's extensions compared with the other installed models' extensions of the same elements:

Rule Severity Meaning DuplicateTableExtensionMember Error Another model's extension of the same table also adds a field, index or field group with the same name; the packages can't be deployed together. DuplicateEnumValue Error Another model's extension of the same enum adds a value with the same name. DuplicateFormControl Error Another model's extension of the same form adds a control with the same name. SameControlModified Warning Another model's extension of the same form also changes the same control; which change wins depends on the deployment. SeveralWrappers Info A method your model wraps is also wrapped by another of your models' classes: the order they run in is not defined, so none may depend on another's changes.

Summary line example:

Collisions with other models: 9 extension(s) compared with the other installed models' extensions of the same elements; no clashes.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.build.crossReference true Update the cross-reference database while building. The obsolete API part needs it. xpp.codeIntelligence.obsoleteWarnings true Live obsolete API warnings in the editor (not used by the report itself).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The command is in src/upgrade.ts. It calls the agent tool xpp_find_deprecations with the model name, so the report is the same one Copilot gets. The tool (HandleFindDeprecations in server/Ported/Tools/ToolRouter.cs):

  1. Finds the model's package with bridge action get_model_info (the cross-reference database groups code by package).
  2. Obsolete uses: DeprecationReport (server/Ported/Tools/DeprecationReport.cs) reads the list of [SysObsolete] APIs (with their messages) from the cross-reference database and queries it for the references from the package's code to those APIs.
  3. Extension compatibility: bridge action extension_compatibility.
  4. Collisions: bridge action extension_collisions.

Both bridge actions are in ExtensionCompatibilityService (server/Ported/MetaModel/ExtensionCompatibilityService.cs). They read the model's element files from the custom metadata folder and the installed code through Microsoft's metadata API. Wrapper signatures are parsed from the method source and compared with the target method's signature.

The extension splits the text report into the three sections and turns each - ... line into a clickable finding. Clicking runs a find_object lookup by name and opens the code view at the method.

The text report lists at most 300 compatibility findings and 200 collisions.

docs.title: Doing it with Copilot
docs.text:
The F&O Upgrade Reviewer agent runs xpp_find_deprecations on each custom model, reads the affected standard elements to see what changed and what replaces an obsolete API, checks the model's dependencies with xpp_get_model_info, and searches release notes with xpp_search_docs. It returns a readiness report with blockers, required and recommended changes, and the test focus. See Agents for Developers.

xpp_find_deprecations also takes previousPackagesFolder (the PackagesLocalDirectory of the earlier version); the report then adds a "Standard code drift" section, like Standard Code Drift but without the code.

Example prompt: "We are moving to the new version. Check ContosoExtensions for upgrade problems."

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One model per run.
  • The obsolete API part is only as current as the cross-reference database: build with cross references first.
  • Only names and signatures are checked. A wrapper whose target still compiles but behaves differently is not found here; use Standard Code Drift for that.
  • Collisions with ISV or other models are only found when those models are installed in the same metadata.
  • The SeveralWrappers rule only looks at your own models in the custom metadata folder.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Model '...' is not one of your models in the custom metadata folder." You picked a standard model, or the model is not in the custom metadata folder. Run it on your own models only. "The cross-reference database is not available: ..." The XRef database could not be opened. Check the configuration's cross-reference database (Connect to Environment). 0 obsolete uses right after an update. The cross-reference database has not been rebuilt for your model on the new version. Build the model with xpp.build.crossReference on, then run it again. CocNotChecked findings. The target method's source could not be parsed. Compare the signatures by hand. Clicking a finding says " was not found." The element no longer exists (for example after a rename). Search for it with Open Element.

docs.title: Usage statistics
docs.text: F&O Studio can count how often you run each of its commands, on this machine only. The counts never leave the machine on their own: nothing is sent anywhere, and F&O Studio collects no telemetry. Counting is off until you turn it on. You see the counts with Show Usage Statistics, and, if you choose, they go into a problem report so the maintainer knows which features you rely on.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You want to know which F&O Studio commands you and your team actually use, for example to decide which shortcuts to bind or which features to show a new developer.
  • You report a problem and want to show which features you use most (see Report-a-Problem).
  • You give feedback on the extension and want to back it with numbers.

If none of this matters to you, leave it off. Nothing in F&O Studio depends on it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Nothing is needed. The feature works on every environment type, with or without a project, and without a network connection.

docs.title: Turn counting on
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Options… (or open File > Preferences > Settings).
  2. Search for xpp.usageStatistics.
  3. Select the check box Count which F&O Studio commands you run, on this machine only (nothing is sent anywhere).

Or add this to your user settings.json:

{
  "xpp.usageStatistics": true
}

Counting starts with the next command you run. No reload is needed.

docs.title: See the counts
docs.text:
1. Run F&O Studio: Show Usage Statistics from the Command Palette.
  2. A Markdown document opens in a preview tab:
# F&O Studio usage on this machine

Counted locally; nothing is sent anywhere.

| Command | Runs |
|---|---|
| xpp.openObject | 42 |
| xpp.buildProject | 17 |
| xpp.findReferences | 9 |
  1. Commands are sorted by count, highest first. The first column is the command ID; the Command-Reference lists the title of each ID.

The document is untitled and not saved. Save it yourself (Ctrl+S) if you want to keep a copy, for example to compare later or to share with your team.

docs.title: Turn counting off
docs.text: Clear the check box (or set "xpp.usageStatistics": false). Counting stops at once. The counts you already have are kept: Show Usage Statistics still lists them, with the line "Counting is off (setting xpp.usageStatistics)."

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect xpp.usageStatistics false true counts each F&O Studio command you run. Show Usage Statistics lists the counts, and Report a Problem… adds the 15 most used commands to the report

The setting has no declared scope, so you can set it in your user settings or per workspace. The counts themselves are stored once for all workspaces (see below).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Almost every F&O Studio command runs through one wrapper in src/extension.ts. Before it runs the command, the wrapper checks xpp.usageStatistics. When it is on, it adds 1 to the count of that command ID.
  • A command is counted when it starts, whether it then succeeds, fails or you cancel its prompt.
  • The counts are a single map of command ID to number, stored in VS Code's global extension state under the key xpp.usage. That storage is on this machine, shared by all your workspaces and windows, and it is not a file in your repository.
  • Only the command ID and a number are stored: no element names, no arguments, no times, no environment, no user name.
  • Show Usage Statistics reads the map and writes it as a Markdown table.
  • Report a Problem… reads the same map only when the setting is on, and adds the 15 highest counts to the report under "Most used commands (local counts)". You see and can edit the report before anything is sent, and you decide whether to send it at all.

docs.title: What is not counted
docs.text:
• Commands that F&O Studio registers outside the wrapper: Launch Debugger, Clear Infolog, Filter Infolog, Copy Infolog and Run Tests.
  • VS Code's own commands, even when F&O Studio provides their results: Go to Definition (F12), Find All References (Shift+F12), Go to Implementations, hover, completion, Format Document and rename (F2).
  • What happens inside panels (the element designer, the data panel, the report designer) unless it runs an F&O Studio command.
  • Copilot's use of the agent tools. Those calls appear in the Copilot-Activity view instead.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Question Answer Is anything sent automatically? No. F&O Studio has no telemetry and never sends the counts on its own Where are the counts? In VS Code's global storage for the extension, on this machine What is stored? Command IDs and counts only When can the counts leave the machine? Only inside a problem report, when counting is on, after you have seen the report and chosen to create an issue, open it in the browser or copy it Can I remove the counts from a report? Yes. Delete the "Most used commands" section from the preview before you send it, or turn the setting off before you start the report

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• There is no command to reset the counts. Turning the setting off stops counting but keeps the existing counts.
  • The counts are kept on one machine. They are not combined across machines or users; to compare, save each person's Show Usage Statistics document.
  • The table shows command IDs, not titles.

docs.title: Verify Changes in the Running App
docs.text: Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot) turns the elements you changed into a short check list (menu items to open, controls a form extension adds, fields an entity extension adds) and hands it to Copilot in agent mode. Copilot then runs the checks in the deployed environment with the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server's form and data tools, reading only, and reports PASS or FAIL per step. It is a quick smoke test after a deploy, done by the agent instead of by clicking through the client. Visual Studio has no equivalent. This feature is a preview.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Right after you deploy a change to a development or sandbox environment, to confirm that the new menu items open, the new controls are on the form and the entity returns the new fields.
  • Before you hand a change to a functional consultant for testing, to catch the obvious problems first.
  • After the Pre-Deploy Checklist and the deploy, as the last check on the test environment.

It does not replace functional testing: it checks that things open and show up, not that business logic is right. For full scenarios use the F&O Test Scenarios agent and Run Tests.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Need Why Your models in a Git repository The changes come from Git (uncommitted changes and, optionally, the branch's commits). The change built and deployed The checks run against the deployed code. See Deploy to Environment. GitHub Copilot in agent mode F&O Studio opens the chat in agent mode with the prompt. The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server connected to VS Code Copilot uses its form and data tools to open forms and read records. F&O Studio doesn't set it up; see Microsoft's Use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in VS Code. It must point at the environment you deployed to.

Use a development, sandbox or build environment.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Build and deploy your change.
  2. Run F&O Studio: Verify Changes in the Running App (Copilot) from the Command Palette, or click Verify in the Running App in the Dynamics 365 view under Build and check.
  3. If F&O Studio knows the deployed code is older than your last build of the project's model, it warns, for example:
ContosoExtensions was built (11/25/2026, 2:40:12 PM) after its last deploy (11/25/2026, 1:05:47 PM).
The check uses the deployed code.
  • Deploy First starts the deploy command and stops the check. Run it again after the deploy.

  • Continue runs the check against what is deployed now.

  • F&O Studio collects the changed elements of your custom models (see below) and plans the steps ("Planning the check..." in the status bar).

  • Copilot Chat opens in agent mode with a prompt like this:
Verify my changes in the running Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations environment
(https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com) with the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP tools (form and data tools).
Only read: do not save forms or change data. Close every form you open. For each step report PASS or FAIL with what you saw:
1. Open menu item ContosoCreditHold (display); confirm it opens without an error.
2. Open form CustGroup (through its menu item) and find the controls ContosoCreditHoldReason; confirm they are visible.
3. Read one record of data entity CustCustomerGroupEntity and confirm the fields ContosoCreditHoldReason are returned.
End with a table: step, result, notes. If the ERP MCP tools are not available, say so and stop.
  1. Copilot runs the steps with the ERP MCP tools and ends with a table of step, result and notes. Look at each FAIL and the notes: a missing control, an error when opening, or a field that is not returned.

docs.title: Which changes are checked
docs.text:
The changed elements are the ones Show Changed Elements uses: uncommitted changes in your custom models' Git repositories, plus the commits of the current branch since it left the base branch. The base branch is the xpp.git.baseBranch setting, or main when it is empty. Deleted elements are skipped.

Changed element Step planned Display, output or action menu item (AxMenuItemDisplay, AxMenuItemOutput, AxMenuItemAction) Open the menu item; confirm it opens without an error Form extension (AxFormExtension) Open the base form through its menu item and find the controls the extension adds (up to 10 names); confirm they are visible Data entity extension (AxDataEntityViewExtension) Read one record of the base entity and confirm the fields the extension adds (up to 10) are returned New data entity (AxDataEntityView, added) Read one record of the new entity New form (AxForm, added) Open the new form through its menu item; confirm it opens without an error

Other element types (classes, tables, table extensions, existing forms you modified) get no step of their own. Their effect shows through the forms and entities that use them.

If nothing is changed, F&O Studio says "No changed elements to verify (models must be in a Git repository)." If the changes contain nothing a user can open, it says "The changes have nothing a user can open (menu items, forms or data entities)." and no chat is opened.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Branch your work is compared with. Empty: Verify compares with main (other features use only uncommitted changes when it is empty).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. src/verify.ts reads the active environment (for its web client URL) and asks the deploy state whether the deployed code is current (src/deployState.ts, using staleDeployMessage from core). The deploy state is the last build and the last deploy made from this machine, per environment and model.
  2. src/changes.ts (changedElements) runs git status --porcelain and git diff --name-status <merge-base> HEAD on each custom model folder and maps the files to elements.
  3. For form and data entity extensions, the extension's server reads the element (bridge action read_object) to get the names of its controls or fields.
  4. The prompt is opened with VS Code's workbench.action.chat.open command in agent mode.
  5. From there everything is Copilot and the ERP MCP server: F&O Studio doesn't call the environment itself. The prompt tells Copilot to read only, not save forms, not change data, and close every form it opens.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview. This feature has not been verified end to end on a live environment yet.
  • The ERP MCP server is required and must target the environment you deployed to. If its tools are missing, Copilot is told to say so and stop.
  • "Read only" is an instruction in the prompt. The ERP MCP server's tools can save forms and change data; run the check on a non-production environment.
  • The steps check presence and opening, not behaviour, validations or posting logic.
  • The deploy-state warning knows only builds and deploys made from this machine with F&O Studio.
  • Changes outside Git, or models outside a Git repository, are not found.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "No changed elements to verify (models must be in a Git repository)." No uncommitted changes and no branch commits since the base branch, or the model folder is not in Git Check xpp.git.baseBranch; make sure the custom model folder is inside a Git repository. "The changes have nothing a user can open..." Only classes, tables or other non-UI elements changed Test through the forms that use them, or with Run Tests. Copilot says the ERP MCP tools are not available The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server is not connected Connect it (Microsoft Learn link above) and run the command again. A step fails because a control is not found, though it is in your extension The deployed code is older than your build Deploy, then run the check again (choose Deploy First at the warning). A form can't be opened "through its menu item" The form has no menu item, or the user of the ERP MCP connection has no access Add a menu item and privilege, or check security with Who Can Access.

docs.title: Version Drift Guard
docs.text:
Microsoft updates unified developer environments (UDE) to new application versions on its own schedule. The metadata on your machine (PackagesLocalDirectory and the cross-reference database) stays at the version you downloaded. When the two differ, builds compile against the old version and deploys can fail. The version drift guard compares the two, warns you, and offers Update Metadata, which downloads the new version with Connect to Environment. Clean Up Old Application Versions… then frees the disk space the old versions take. Visual Studio has no equivalent; there you notice the drift when a deploy fails.

This feature is a preview: it has not been verified end to end on a live environment update.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Always on: the check runs on its own after startup and when you switch environments.
  • Run Check Environment Application Version after you hear that the environment was updated, or before an important deploy.
  • Run Clean Up Old Application Versions… after an update, when your disk is filling up.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A unified developer environment selected in this window (Select Environment). The guard does nothing on cloud-hosted and VHD environments, where metadata and runtime are the same installation.
  • A Microsoft account session for the environment in VS Code. The guard never shows a sign-in: if VS Code has no session for the org yet (for example right after installing), the check is skipped silently. Any command that signs in, such as Connect to Environment… or Deploy Models to Environment, creates the session.

docs.title: The automatic check
docs.text:
1. About 15 seconds after VS Code starts, and every time the window switches environment, F&O Studio reads the environment's current application version from Dataverse and compares it with the version of the active configuration.
  2. If they differ, you see a warning:

The environment now runs application 10.0.y; this machine has the metadata of 10.0.x. Builds compile against the old version and deploys can fail.

with the buttons Update Metadata and Later. 3. Update Metadata runs Connect to Environment… for the environment's Dataverse URL, without asking for the URL. The new version is downloaded into its own folder and becomes the active configuration. Your custom metadata folder is kept, so your models are built against the new version. 4. Later closes the warning. You are warned once per new version per VS Code session; the drift stays visible: - The status bar environment item shows a warning icon, and its tooltip says "The environment now runs 10.0.y: update the metadata (Dynamics 365 view > Environment)." - The Dynamics 365 view's Environment group shows a warning icon with the description <name> · 10.0.y available, is expanded, and has a first entry Update Metadata to 10.0.y… with the description this machine: 10.0.x. - The status bar menu (click the environment item) starts with Update Metadata to 10.0.y….

docs.title: Check on demand
docs.text:
Run F&O Studio: Check Environment Application Version (in the status bar menu: Check Application Version). It runs the same comparison:

  • Drift found: the status bar and view update. The warning with Update Metadata appears if you have not been warned about this version in this session yet; otherwise use Update Metadata to 10.0.y… in the view or the status bar menu.
  • No drift: "The metadata on this machine matches the environment's application version (or the environment could not be reached without signing in)."

docs.title: Clean up old versions
docs.text:
Every application version leaves a folder %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version> of about 16 GB.

  1. Run F&O Studio: Clean Up Old Application Versions… (Dynamics 365 view > Environment > Clean Up Old Versions…, or the status bar menu).
  2. A notification Measuring application version folders… appears while the sizes are counted.
  3. A multi-select list titled Delete application versions (active: 10.0.y) shows every version folder except the active one:
  4. Label: the version. Description: its size in GB.
  5. Detail: "Used by the configuration of , ... (it stops working)" or "No configuration uses it".
  6. All versions are checked except the newest older one. That one is kept by default because Upgrade Readiness and Standard Code Drift compare against it. Check it too if you do not need those comparisons.
  7. Confirm the modal dialog Delete 10.0.a, 10.0.b (n GB)?. It explains that configurations using these versions stop working until you connect to that version again, and that cross-reference databases are not removed.
  8. F&O Studio deletes the folders and reports "Freed n GB." Folders that could not be fully deleted (for example files in use) are listed: "Not fully deleted (files in use?): ...".

    9. If there is nothing to delete you see "No other application versions are on this machine."

docs.title: A typical update
docs.text:
1. Microsoft updates your environment from 10.0.x to 10.0.y.
  2. The next time you start VS Code (or switch to that environment), the warning appears. Click Update Metadata.
  3. Connect to Environment runs for 10.0.y: it downloads PackagesLocalDirectory, the cross-reference database and the FinOps tools for 10.0.y into a new version folder, writes <org>___10.0.y.json and makes it active. Your custom metadata folder stays the same.
  4. Build your models again (Build Project and Model) and fix any new errors or warnings.
  5. Optionally run Upgrade Readiness and Standard Code Drift to see what changed in the standard code you extend or wrap.
  6. Deploy (Deploy to Environment).
  7. If you also use Visual Studio, update its FinOps tools (Visual Studio Side by Side).
  8. When you no longer need 10.0.x, run Clean Up Old Application Versions….

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: There are no settings for the guard. It uses the selected environment (xpp.environmentUrl or the workspace choice, see Select Environment) and the sign-in settings in Sign-In and Authentication.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The guard and the clean-up are in src/versionGuard.ts. The status bar and view entries are in src/environmentPicker.ts.

docs.title: The comparison
docs.text:
1. The active configuration is read. The check stops (no drift) when it is a local environment, has no application version, or no environment URL is selected.
  2. The local version comes from the configuration file name <org>___<application version>.json.
  3. The Dataverse URL is the selected environment's (a finance and operations URL is resolved to the regional Dataverse host).
  4. A token is requested silently from VS Code's Microsoft account. No token: no check.
  5. The Dataverse message msprov_getfinopsapplicationdetails returns applicationversion (together with RetrieveFinanceAndOperationsIntegrationDetails, the same read Connect to Environment does).
  6. If the remote version differs from the local one, a drift { local, remote, dataverseUrl } is recorded and the status bar and view update.

Errors during the check (network, permissions) count as "no drift"; nothing is shown.

docs.title: Why a new version gets its own folder
docs.text: Connect to Environment puts each application version in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\ and writes a new configuration <org>___<version>.json. The old configuration stays, which is why the clean-up lists which configurations use a folder. Select Environment always lists the newest configuration of each org.

docs.title: The clean-up
docs.text:
• Only folders named like a four-part version (10.0.x.y) directly under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365 are listed. The folder of the active configuration's version is never offered.
  • Sizes are measured by walking every file.
  • Folders are deleted with the Windows long-path prefix (\\?\), because PackagesLocalDirectory has paths longer than 260 characters.
  • Configuration files in XPPConfig, cross-reference databases in LocalDB and the runtime links are not deleted.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Preview; not verified end to end on a live update.
  • The check needs an existing VS Code session for the org; it never asks you to sign in.
  • One warning per new version per VS Code session.
  • Only the application version is compared, not the platform version.
  • Clean-up removes version folders only. Old cross-reference databases remain in LocalDB; remove them with SQL Server tools if you need the space.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No warning although the environment was updated No VS Code session for the org yet, or the check failed silently Run any command that signs in (for example Check Environment Connection), then Check Environment Application Version. "The metadata on this machine matches ... (or the environment could not be reached without signing in)." Versions match, or no silent token Same as above if you expected drift. Builds fail with unknown standard elements or methods after an update Drift: the local metadata is older Update Metadata. A configuration stopped working after clean-up Its version folder was deleted Run Connect to Environment… for that environment again. "Not fully deleted (files in use?): ..." A process (Visual Studio, the metadata server, a terminal) holds files in that folder Close the process and run the clean-up again.

docs.title: Visual Studio Side by Side
docs.text: F&O Studio never needs Visual Studio, but many developers keep Visual Studio on the same machine, or a team uses both. The two share the same files: the active metadata configuration, the custom metadata folder, the cross-reference database and the .rnrproj projects. This page explains what is shared, what F&O Studio does to keep Visual Studio working, and how Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version keeps Visual Studio's Finance and Operations tools in step with the metadata.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You use Visual Studio and VS Code on the same machine, for example Visual Studio for a task F&O Studio does not cover yet.
  • After Connect to Environment downloaded a new application version and Visual Studio's Application Explorer no longer opens.
  • Your team is moving from Visual Studio to VS Code gradually.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Visual Studio 2022 with Microsoft's Finance and Operations tools (extension DynamicsFnO.DeveloperTools) installed, if you want to use it. If no such Visual Studio is installed, F&O Studio's Visual Studio checks do nothing.
  • For a unified developer environment (UDE), a configuration written by Connect to Environment… (it keeps the FinOps tools it downloaded).

docs.title: What is shared
docs.text:
Item Where Notes Active configuration Registry HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Dynamics\AX7\Development\Configurations, values CurrentMetadataConfig and FrameworkDirectory Connect to Environment… sets both, so Visual Studio switches to the same environment. Select Environment… in VS Code does not change them. Configuration files %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig\<org>___<version>.json Written by either tool; read by both. Visual Studio lists them in Manage local XPP configurations. System metadata %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\<version>\PackagesLocalDirectory Same download, same layout. Custom metadata folder ModelStoreFolder, for example C:\CustomXppMetadata... Your models. Changes in one tool are visible in the other. Cross-reference database (LocalDB)\MSSQLLocalDB, XRef_... Same database for find references in both. Projects .rnrproj files F&O Studio edits them the way Visual Studio saves them. Build output and PDBs The package's bin folder F&O Studio converts PDBs to portable PDBs after every build; Visual Studio debugs the converted PDBs too.

On a cloud-hosted or VHD environment, F&O Studio writes its own configuration into its extension storage and does not touch the registry or Visual Studio's files. Both tools build into the same PackagesLocalDirectory. See Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments.

docs.title: Configurations Visual Studio can read
docs.text:
Visual Studio reads configuration files with a strict serializer: a file that lacks a required member (AosWebsiteName, AudienceUri, DatabaseServer, DebugSourceFolder, DefaultModelForNewProjects, EnableOfflineAuthentication, ModelStoreFolder, WebRoleDeploymentFolder) is silently left out of Manage local XPP configurations, and Visual Studio cannot load metadata with it.

  • Connect to Environment… writes every member of Microsoft's Template_xppconfig.json (from the downloaded FinOps tools, or the same values built in), so its files are always complete.
  • Configurations written by older F&O Studio versions are completed automatically when the extension starts. Only files whose Description says they were generated "by X++ for VS Code" or "by F&O Studio for VS Code" are touched; missing members are added and existing values are kept. Each completed file is logged in the X++ output channel: Completed configuration <file> for Visual Studio (added ...).

You do not need to do anything for this.

docs.title: Keep Visual Studio's FinOps tools in step
docs.text:
Visual Studio's FinOps tools must match the metadata version of the active configuration, or its Application Explorer fails to open. After a connect to a new application version, they usually do not.

Automatic prompt

  1. About 15 seconds after VS Code starts, F&O Studio looks for Visual Studio installations with the FinOps tools.
  2. If one has a different FinOps tools version than the active configuration needs, you see a warning:

Visual Studio 2022 has FinOps tools 7.0.a, but the active configuration's metadata needs 7.0.b. Visual Studio's Application Explorer will not load until they match. F&O Studio is not affected.

with Update Visual Studio and Don't Ask Again. 3. Don't Ask Again is remembered for this Visual Studio instance and this pair of versions; a later version mismatch asks again.

Nothing is shown when no Visual Studio with the FinOps tools is installed, when the versions match, or when there is nothing to compare.

On demand

Run F&O Studio: Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version from the Command Palette. It reports every outcome:

Message Meaning "No Visual Studio with the Finance and Operations tools is installed on this machine; there is nothing to update." No Visual Studio, or none with the FinOps tools. "The active configuration has no FinOps tools downloaded by F&O Studio (for example a cloud-hosted environment), so there is nothing to compare." The active configuration's version folder has no FinOpsTools folder. "Visual Studio's FinOps tools match this environment ()." Nothing to do. The warning above, with Update Visual Studio A mismatch.

Update Visual Studio

  1. Click Update Visual Studio.
  2. F&O Studio uses the FinOps tools VSIX that Connect to Environment… downloaded (<version folder>\Microsoft.Dynamics.FinOps.ToolsVS2022.vsix). If it is not there (older setups deleted it), it packs one from the extracted FinOpsTools folder into your temp folder (notification Preparing FinOps tools …).
  3. Visual Studio's VSIX Installer opens for that Visual Studio instance. A message tells you: "Close Visual Studio, then confirm the install in the VSIX Installer (it asks for administrator approval)."
  4. Close Visual Studio and confirm in the installer.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: No settings. The "Don't Ask Again" answers are stored in VS Code's global state.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Configuration template and repair: core/src/environment/config.ts; the repair runs at activation in src/extension.ts.
  • FinOps tools check: src/visualStudioTools.ts and src/vsFinOpsTools.ts.

docs.title: Finding Visual Studio and its FinOps tools
docs.text:
1. Visual Studio installations come from vswhere.exe -all -prerelease -format json (in %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer). If vswhere.exe is missing, there is no Visual Studio.
  2. For each installation, the extension folders are searched up to three levels deep for an extension.vsixmanifest with the identity DynamicsFnO.DeveloperTools:
  3. <install>\Common7\IDE\Extensions (machine-wide install)
  4. %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\VisualStudio\<major>.0_<instance id>\Extensions (per-user install)
  5. The version is the Version attribute of that <Identity> element (Microsoft's manifest also holds a commented-out template identity, which is ignored).

docs.title: The version the environment needs
docs.text: The needed version is read the same way from <version folder>\FinOpsTools\extension.vsixmanifest, which Connect to Environment… extracts. The version folder is the parent of the active configuration's FrameworkDirectory.

docs.title: Packing and installing
docs.text:
When the downloaded VSIX is missing, the files of FinOpsTools are zipped with the Windows tar.exe (zip format, forward-slash paths as VSIX packages need). The installer is started as:

<install>\Common7\IDE\VSIXInstaller.exe /instanceIds:<instance id> <vsix>

The VSIX Installer asks for confirmation and elevation itself.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only Visual Studio installations that vswhere reports are found.
  • Only the first mismatched installation is offered per run.
  • Visual Studio must be closed for the VSIX Installer to finish.
  • Select Environment… changes only the VS Code workspace; Visual Studio keeps the active configuration from the registry until you connect again or change it in Visual Studio.
  • On cloud-hosted and VHD environments there is nothing to compare: the FinOps tools come with the VM.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Visual Studio's Application Explorer does not open after a connect Its FinOps tools do not match the new metadata Run Check Visual Studio's FinOps Tools Version and Update Visual Studio. Visual Studio does not list a configuration F&O Studio wrote The file lacks a member Visual Studio requires Restart VS Code (generated files are completed at startup) and check the X++ output for "Completed configuration". "VSIXInstaller.exe was not found in ..." The Visual Studio installation is incomplete Repair Visual Studio with the Visual Studio Installer. "... does not hold the FinOps tools." FinOpsTools is empty or incomplete Delete the FinOpsTools folder in the version folder and run Connect to Environment… again; it downloads and extracts the tools again. "Packing the FinOps tools failed: ..." tar.exe failed (disk full, temp folder not writable) Free space and try again. Visual Studio works with another environment than VS Code Each VS Code workspace has its own choice; Visual Studio uses the registry Run Connect to Environment… for the environment you want in Visual Studio, or switch in Visual Studio.

  • Select Environment
  • Compared with Visual Studio
  • D365FO Projects
  • Version Drift Guard
  • Cloud-Hosted and VHD Environments

Source: Visual-Studio-Side-by-Side on the wiki.

docs.title: Who Can Access
docs.text: Who Can Access lists the privileges, duties and roles that reach a menu item, form, table or data entity, with the grant each privilege gives. It answers "which roles can open this?" from the metadata of all packages, before you deploy. In Visual Studio you would search the privileges for the menu item by hand and then walk up to their duties and roles.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You added a menu item and want to check which roles reach it (or that none does yet).
  • A user cannot open a form and you want to know which roles would give them access.
  • You plan to change a standard privilege through an extension and want to know which roles it affects.
  • You need to know which roles can read or change a table or data entity directly.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An active D365FO configuration with its packages on disk (UDE, cloud-hosted or VHD). No sign-in or database.
  • The element can be standard or yours.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
From How Application Explorer or the D365FO project view Right-click a menu item, form, table or data entity (or an extension of one) > Who Can Access. Element Designer Title bar menu of a menu item, form, table or data entity > Who Can Access. Security View Right-click an entry point, data entity or table under a privilege > Who Can Access, or its inline person button. Dynamics 365 view Security > Who Can Access… Command Palette F&O Studio: Who Can Access

From the Dynamics 365 view or the Command Palette, an element picker opens, limited to display, output and action menu items, forms, tables and data entities. Run on an extension (for example a table extension), it analyzes the base element.

docs.title: What is searched for each element type
docs.text:
Element Access found through Menu item (display, output, action) Privileges with that menu item as an entry point. Form Privileges with an entry point on any menu item that opens the form. Table Privileges with a table permission on it, plus privileges with an entry point on a menu item that opens a form with the table as a data source. Data entity Privileges with a data entity permission on it.

For each privilege found, F&O Studio lists the duties that contain it and the roles that get it: roles that have the privilege directly, roles that have one of those duties, and, going up, every role that has one of those roles as a sub-role. Role and duty extensions are included.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
The result opens in the security panel:

  • Title: Who can access <type> <name>.
  • Summary: N privilege(s) grant access, in M role(s).
  • Menu items: the menu items considered (for a form or table, every menu item that opens it), with type, view license and maintain license. Click a name to open it.
  • Privileges:
Column Meaning Privilege Click to open it in the designer. Model The privilege's model. Grant What the privilege grants: <menu item>: Read,Update,... for entry points, table: <grant> for table permissions, entity: <grant> for data entity permissions. Duties The duties that contain the privilege; click one to open it. Roles The roles that get it; click one to run Analyze License on it.
  • Through forms (tables only): the forms that have the table as a data source, up to 200. Click one to open it.

When no privilege grants access, the panel says: "No privilege grants access. Use Add to Privilege on its menu item." See Add to Privilege.

Copy as Markdown and Export… in the panel header copy or save the result (default file name access-<name>.md).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Who Can Access on the table CustGroup lists the menu items that open forms with CustGroup as a data source (such as the CustGroup display menu item), the privileges that grant those menu items or have a table permission on CustGroup, and the roles that reach them. Click a role to see what license it needs.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: None.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Command xpp.security.whoCanAccess in src/security/index.ts (whoCanAccess); the supported types are AccessTypes in src/security/securityView.ts.
  • The extension calls the server's security language action with op: 'access'.
  • server/Ported/Tools/SecurityAnalysis.cs (WhoCanAccess) searches the cached security index: the privileges' entry points, data entity permissions (DataEntityPermissions) and table permissions (DirectAccessPermissions); reverse maps give the duties and roles, and parent roles are added through sub-roles.
  • For tables, FormsUsingTable scans the DataSources of every form once and caches the table-to-forms map until form folders change.
  • A display menu item without an ObjectType is treated as opening a form.
  • Copilot uses the same analysis through xpp_analyze_security with op=access (see Agent Tools: Analysis).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Metadata only: it does not tell you which users have the roles. The F&O Security & License agent can read role assignments from a live environment (see Copilot Agents).
  • Access to a table through forms is found from form data sources only. Access through code, other forms' data methods or queries is not traced.
  • Forms are reached only through menu items whose object is the form; a form opened from code or through another form is not listed.
  • Grants of the system administrator role, which reaches everything at runtime, are not modelled.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "Who Can Access works on menu items, forms, tables and data entities." Run on another element type. Run it on one of these types; for roles, duties and privileges use Analyze License. "No privilege grants access." for a new menu item No privilege has it as an entry point. Use Add to Privilege, then put the privilege in a duty or role. A privilege you just created is missing Cached security index. Click Refresh Security in the Security View and run it again. A table shows no roles but users can see its data The table is reached through a form not opened by a menu item, through code, or through a data entity. Run it on the data entity or the form's menu item.

docs.text:

  • Find Security Gaps
  • Find All References

docs.title: Wizard: Approval Workflow
docs.text: New Approval Workflow… adds a complete approval workflow to one of your tables: the status enum, the workflow document and query, the workflow category, type and approval, the event handlers, the submit and resubmit class, the seven action menu items of the workflow buttons, and privileges for submitters and approvers. It also adds the status field and workflow methods to the table and turns on the workflow bar of the table's form when it can. It follows the standard pattern used by BankReconciliationApproval. In Visual Studio this is a long series of manual steps.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Records of a custom table (for example an expense request or a change request) must be approved before they are used.
  • You want the workflow editor in the web client to offer your workflow type with one approval step, and the form to show the workflow bar (Submit, Approve, Reject...).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The table belongs to the project's model. The wizard changes the table, so it refuses standard tables and tables of other models.
  • The table does not have a canSubmitToWorkflow method yet.
  • A display menu item opens the form of the records. To have the form changed automatically, the form must be in the same model and have a data source on the table.
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the workflow label.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Approval Workflow… New Element Wizards > Approval workflow Command Palette F&O Studio: New Approval Workflow…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New approval workflow: table A table of your model; it gets the workflow status field and methods ContosoExpenseRequest 2 New approval workflow: name Base name with your prefix; the elements get Type, Approval, Document, Submit... appended ContosoExpenseRequestApproval 3 New approval workflow: label What users see in the workflow editor Expense request approval 4 New approval workflow: document menu item The display menu item that opens the form of the records ContosoExpenseRequest 5 New approval workflow: module (workflow category) A value of the ModuleAxapta enum, listed from the metadata the module the records belong to 6 New approval workflow: field group shown to approvers (none) or one of the table's field groups; asked only when the table has field groups Overview

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape stops the wizard before anything is created.

The wizard checks after prompt 1 that the table exists, belongs to your model and has no canSubmitToWorkflow, and after prompt 4 that the display menu item exists.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The progress notification Creating workflow ContosoExpenseRequestApproval… shows each element. Then the wizard changes the table and the form and shows a summary such as:

Created the ContosoExpenseRequestApproval workflow in ContosoExtensions. ContosoExpenseRequest got the ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus field, canSubmitToWorkflow and setWorkflowStatus. Form ContosoExpenseRequest shows the workflow bar. Add the privileges ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalSubmitter and ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalApprover to duties, build, then configure the workflow in the web client.

Open Workflow Type opens the workflow type in the designer.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
With base name B = ContosoExpenseRequestApproval and table ContosoExpenseRequest (17 elements):

Element Type Purpose BStatus Base enum Draft, Submitted, ChangeRequested, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled; extensible BQuery Query One data source on the table BDocument Class Extends WorkflowDocument; getQueryName returns the query BEventHandler Class Workflow type events: started, canceled, completed BApprovalEventHandler Class Approval outcomes: completed, returned, change requested BSubmit Class main for the Submit and Resubmit buttons BSubmit Action menu item Label @SYS68352, runs BSubmit, linked to form WorkflowSubmitDialog BResubmit Action menu item Label @SYS109048, runs BSubmit BCancel Action menu item Label @SYS323585, runs WorkflowCancelManager, linked to form WorkflowCancelWorkflow BApprove Action menu item Label @SYS105443, runs WorkflowWorkItemActionManager BReject Action menu item Label @SYS105445, runs WorkflowWorkItemActionManager BRequestChange Action menu item Label @SYS105446, runs WorkflowWorkItemActionManager BDelegate Action menu item Label @SYS109047, runs WorkflowWorkItemActionManager, linked to form WorkflowWorkItemActionDialog BCategory Workflow category Label and the module you picked BApproval Workflow approval Document, document menu item, preview field group, Resubmit and Delegate menu items; outcomes Approve (Complete), Reject (Return), RequestChange (RequestChange); Deny disabled BType Workflow type Category, document, document menu item, the three event handlers, Submit and Cancel menu items, the approval as supported element BSubmitter Security privilege Invoke on Submit, Resubmit, Cancel BApprover Security privilege Invoke on Approve, Reject, RequestChange, Delegate

For example BType is ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalType.

docs.title: Changes to your table
docs.text:
The table gets:

  • a field BStatus of the enum BStatus;
  • canSubmitToWorkflow, which allows submitting drafts, documents sent back for changes and rejected documents;
  • a static setWorkflowStatus(RefRecId, BStatus) that the handlers and the submit class call.
public boolean canSubmitToWorkflow(str _workflowType = '')
{
    return this.ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus == ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Draft
        || this.ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus == ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::ChangeRequested
        || this.ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus == ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Rejected;
}

public static void setWorkflowStatus(RefRecId _recId, ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus _status)
{
    ContosoExpenseRequest contosoExpenseRequest;

    ttsbegin;
    update_recordset contosoExpenseRequest
        setting ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus = _status
        where contosoExpenseRequest.RecId == _recId;
    ttscommit;
}

(The generated canSubmitToWorkflow is on one line; it is wrapped here for reading.)

docs.title: Changes to the form
docs.text:
The wizard reads the display menu item's object. When that form is in your model and has a data source on the table, it sets on the form's Design:

Property Value WorkflowEnabled Yes WorkflowDatasource the table's data source WorkflowType BType

Otherwise the summary tells you what to set by hand.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The workflow type's event handler keeps the status in step:

class ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalEventHandler implements WorkflowStartedEventHandler, WorkflowCanceledEventHandler, WorkflowCompletedEventHandler
{
    public void started(WorkflowEventArgs _workflowEventArgs)
    {
        ContosoExpenseRequest::setWorkflowStatus(_workflowEventArgs.parmWorkflowContext().parmRecId(), ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Submitted);
    }

    public void canceled(WorkflowEventArgs _workflowEventArgs)
    {
        ContosoExpenseRequest::setWorkflowStatus(_workflowEventArgs.parmWorkflowContext().parmRecId(), ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Draft);
    }

    public void completed(WorkflowEventArgs _workflowEventArgs)
    {
        ContosoExpenseRequest::setWorkflowStatus(_workflowEventArgs.parmWorkflowContext().parmRecId(), ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Approved);
    }

}

The approval handler sets Rejected on returned and ChangeRequested on changeRequested; its completed is empty because the workflow type's completed approves the document.

The submit class handles both Submit and Resubmit:

public static void main(Args _args)
{
    ContosoExpenseRequest record = _args.record();
    Object caller = _args.caller();

    if (!record || record.TableId != tableNum(ContosoExpenseRequest) || !caller)
    {
        throw error(Error::wrongUseOfFunction(funcName()));
    }

    if (_args.menuItemName() == menuItemActionStr(ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalSubmit))
    {
        WorkflowSubmitDialog submitDialog = WorkflowSubmitDialog::construct(caller.getActiveWorkflowConfiguration());
        submitDialog.run();
        if (submitDialog.parmIsClosedOK())
        {
            Workflow::activateFromWorkflowType(workflowTypeStr(ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalType), record.RecId, submitDialog.parmWorkflowComment(), NoYes::No);
            ContosoExpenseRequest::setWorkflowStatus(record.RecId, ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Submitted);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        WorkflowWorkItemTable workItem = caller.getActiveWorkflowWorkItem();
        WorkflowWorkItemActionDialog actionDialog = WorkflowWorkItemActionDialog::construct(workItem, WorkflowWorkItemActionType::Resubmit, new MenuFunction(menuItemActionStr(ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalResubmit), MenuItemType::Action));
        actionDialog.run();
        if (actionDialog.parmIsClosedOK())
        {
            WorkflowWorkItemActionManager::dispatchWorkItemAction(workItem, actionDialog.parmWorkflowComment(), actionDialog.parmTargetUser(), WorkflowWorkItemActionType::Resubmit, _args.menuItemName());
            ContosoExpenseRequest::setWorkflowStatus(record.RecId, ContosoExpenseRequestApprovalStatus::Submitted);
        }
    }

    FormDataSource dataSource = FormDataUtil::getFormDataSource(record);
    if (dataSource)
    {
        dataSource.research(true);
    }
    caller.updateWorkflowControls();
}

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Add BSubmitter and BApprover to duties, and those to the roles of requesters and approvers.
  2. Build (Build Project and Model), deploy and synchronize the database (the table has a new field) (Deploy to Environment, Synchronize Database).
  3. In the web client, open the workflow configuration of the module you picked, create a workflow from your workflow type, set the approvers and activate it.
  4. Open the form: the workflow bar shows Submit for draft records.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates one label (ID = the base name, text = your label) in the first en-US label file of your model. It is used on the workflow category, type and approval. The enum label is the same label followed by status; the privileges are labelled Submit ... and Approve .... The menu items use standard @SYS labels. Without a label file the plain text is used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts and the table and form changes are in newWorkflow in src/scaffolding/wizards.ts. It uses the bridge actions read_object (table, menu item, the ModuleAxapta enum, the form's data sources) and get_table_fields (field groups).
  2. The elements and the table changes are built in src/scaffolding/workflow.ts. The workflow approval and type are sent as typed metadata to create_object.
  3. All or nothing for the 17 elements: if one fails, the ones created before it are deleted again.
  4. After the elements, update_object adds the field and the methods to your table, and set_element_property sets the three Design properties of the form. These two steps are not rolled back; when one fails, the summary says what to do by hand.
  5. scripts/scaffold-test.js runs the wizard's builders on a scratch table, checks that the type lists the approval and that the table update succeeds, builds the model and deletes everything. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One approval step. Add tasks, conditions or more approvals in the web client's workflow editor or with more workflow elements.
  • Only tables of your project's model. For standard tables, standard workflows already exist or you need a different design.
  • The Deny outcome is disabled.
  • The wizard does not add privileges to duties or configure the workflow in the environment.
  • When the table or form change fails, the elements stay; finish the change by hand.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ... belongs to ...; the workflow wizard changes the table, so pick a table of ... The table is not in your project's model Use a table of your model ... already has canSubmitToWorkflow: it is already used by a workflow. The table already has workflow methods Use another table, or extend the existing workflow Display menu item ... not found. Wrong menu item name Check it with Open Element Form ... is not in ... or Form ... has no ... data source in the summary The form cannot be changed automatically Set WorkflowEnabled, WorkflowDatasource and WorkflowType on the form's Design by hand ... could not be changed (...); add the ...Status field and the two methods by hand. The table update failed Add the field and methods shown above The form shows no workflow bar after deploy No active workflow configuration, or the form settings are missing Configure and activate the workflow in the web client; check the form's Design properties

docs.text:
