  • Element Designer
  • Security View
  • Build Project and Model
  • Scenario: Build a Feature End to End

Source: Wizard-Approval-Workflow on the wiki.

docs.title: Wizard: Batch Job
docs.text: New Batch Job (SysOperation)… creates a complete SysOperation batch job in your model: a data contract, a service class, a controller, an action menu item and a privilege. You enter a name and a caption; the wizard writes the standard pattern, so you only write the job's work in the service's process method. Visual Studio has no equivalent wizard; there you create the five elements by hand.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need a new periodic job that users run from a menu, either at once or scheduled in batch.
  • You want the current SysOperation pattern (contract, service, controller) instead of the older RunBaseBatch.
  • You want the menu item and the privilege created with the code, so security is not forgotten.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects). The wizard creates its elements in the project's model and stops with Open a D365FO project first: the new elements go to its model. when no project is open.
  • The metadata server runs (F&O Studio is connected to an environment, see Connect to Environment).
  • Optional: your model has a label file with an en-US language. The wizard then puts the caption in a label; otherwise it uses the plain text (see Labels).

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Batch Job… New Element Wizards > Batch job (SysOperation) Command Palette F&O Studio: New Batch Job (SysOperation)…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New batch job (SysOperation): name Base name with your prefix. The classes get Contract, Service and Controller appended. Letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, 3 to 61 characters. ContosoPostVendInvoices 2 New batch job: caption What users see on the menu and in the batch job list Post vendor invoices

The grey text in each box (for example ABCPostVendorInvoices) is a placeholder, not a default value. Leave a box empty or press Escape to cancel; nothing is created.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A progress notification Creating ContosoPostVendInvoices… shows each element as it is created. Then a message lists the elements and reminds you to add the privilege to a duty and write the job in the service. Open Service opens the service class.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For base name ContosoPostVendInvoices:

Element Type Content ContosoPostVendInvoicesContract Class [DataContractAttribute] class with one parameter, parmTransDate (TransDate) ContosoPostVendInvoicesService Class Extends SysOperationServiceBase; empty process(ContosoPostVendInvoicesContract _contract) ContosoPostVendInvoicesController Class Extends SysOperationServiceController; main and defaultCaption ContosoPostVendInvoices Action menu item Label = caption, Object type Class, Object = the controller ContosoPostVendInvoicesGenerate Security privilege Label = caption, entry point on the menu item with Invoke access

All five are added to the project.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The contract:

/// <summary>
/// Parameters of Post vendor invoices.
/// </summary>
[DataContractAttribute]
class ContosoPostVendInvoicesContract
{
    TransDate transDate;

    /// <summary>
    /// The date the job works for.
    /// </summary>
    [DataMemberAttribute]
    public TransDate parmTransDate(TransDate _transDate = transDate)
    {
        transDate = _transDate;
        return transDate;
    }

}

The service, where you write the job:

/// <summary>
/// Post vendor invoices: the work, run by ContosoPostVendInvoicesController in batch or interactively.
/// </summary>
class ContosoPostVendInvoicesService extends SysOperationServiceBase
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Runs the job for the contract's parameters.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="_contract">The parameters.</param>
    public void process(ContosoPostVendInvoicesContract _contract)
    {
        // Write the job's work here for _contract.parmTransDate(), in one transaction per unit of work so a restart can continue.
    }

}

The controller:

/// <summary>
/// Starts Post vendor invoices (dialog, batch scheduling) for ContosoPostVendInvoicesService.
/// </summary>
class ContosoPostVendInvoicesController extends SysOperationServiceController
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Entry point of the menu item.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="_args">Menu item arguments.</param>
    public static void main(Args _args)
    {
        ContosoPostVendInvoicesController controller = new ContosoPostVendInvoicesController(classStr(ContosoPostVendInvoicesService), methodStr(ContosoPostVendInvoicesService, process), SysOperationExecutionMode::Synchronous);
        controller.parmArgs(_args);
        controller.startOperation();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The caption of the dialog and the batch job.
    /// </summary>
    /// <returns>The caption.</returns>
    public ClassDescription defaultCaption()
    {
        return "@ContosoLabels:ContosoPostVendInvoices";
    }

}

When the model has no label file, defaultCaption returns the caption text instead, for example "Post vendor invoices".

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Write the work in ContosoPostVendInvoicesService.process. Add parameters to the contract as parm methods with [DataMemberAttribute]; the SysOperation framework puts them on the dialog.
  2. Add the privilege ContosoPostVendInvoicesGenerate to a duty (for example with a duty extension or Add to Privilege), and the menu item to a menu.
  3. Build (Build Project and Model) and deploy (Deploy to Environment).
  4. Open the menu item in the web client (Copy Name and Open in Browser). The dialog shows the date parameter and the batch options.
  5. Write a test (Generate SysTest Class) that calls the service with a contract.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: Before creating the elements, the wizard looks for a label file in your model (a file <LabelFileId>_en-US.xml under the model's AxLabelFile folder). When it finds one, it creates a label with the ID = the base name and the text = the caption, and uses @<LabelFileId>:<base name> in the menu item, the privilege and defaultCaption. When there is no label file, or the label cannot be created (for example the ID exists), the plain caption is used; Best Practice Checks then report the hard-coded text.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The wizard is newSysOperationJob in src/scaffolding/batch.ts. It reads the project's model, asks the two questions, and creates the label with the create_label bridge action (src/scaffolding/common.ts).
  2. Each element is a create_object request to the metadata server, which saves it through Microsoft's metadata API (never by writing XML). Each created element is added to the .rnrproj with add_to_project.
  3. All or nothing: when one element fails (for example a class with that name exists), the wizard deletes the elements it already created, in reverse order, and reports the failure, for example Class ContosoPostVendInvoicesService: ... The elements created before it were removed again.
  4. The generated code is checked by scripts/scaffold-test.js: it creates the elements of every wizard in a test model, builds the model with the X++ compiler, requires no errors in the generated elements, lists any warnings, and deletes everything again. The wizards' output is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The contract has one example parameter (TransDate). Replace or extend it for your job.
  • The controller runs the operation Synchronous; change the execution mode in main if you need another default.
  • The wizard does not add the privilege to a duty, the menu item to a menu, or write the job's logic.
  • A label created before a failure stays in the label file; only the elements are removed.

Invalid characters, or fewer than 3 characters Use a valid X++ name The wizard closes without creating anything A prompt was left empty or cancelled Run it again and fill both prompts Class ...: ... already exists ... and the elements were removed One of the generated names is already used Choose another base name Not removed: ... The rollback could not delete some elements Delete them from the project view (Delete) The caption shows as plain text, not a label The model has no en-US label file, or the label ID exists Create a label file (Label Editor) or rename the existing label

docs.title: Wizard: Business Event
docs.text: New Business Event… creates a business event for a table: the contract class with one data member per field you pick, the event class registered in the business event catalog, and a Chain of Command extension of the table's insert or update that sends the event when it is enabled. It follows the standard pattern (precedent: HireActionBusinessEvent). Visual Studio has no wizard for this.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• An external system (Power Automate, Azure Service Bus, Event Grid, an HTTPS endpoint) must react when records of a table are created or changed.
  • You want the event in the business event catalog with a name, description and category, ready to activate in the web client.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • The table can be a standard or a custom table: the wizard does not change the table itself, it adds a Chain of Command class in your model.
  • Your model references the package of the table.
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the catalog name and description.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Business Event… New Element Wizards > Business event Command Palette F&O Studio: New Business Event…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New business event: table The table whose records the event is about CustGroup 2 New business event: fields of CustGroup the event carries Pick one or more fields (multi-select); the description shows each field's EDT, enum or type CustGroup, Name 3 New business event: when is it sent? When a record is created or When a record is changed When a record is created 4 New business event: name Base name with your prefix; the classes get BusinessEvent and BusinessEventContract appended ContosoCustGroupCreated 5 New business event: name in the catalog What users see in the business event catalog Customer group created 6 New business event: description One sentence for the catalog Sent when a customer group is created. 7 New business event: catalog category (module) A value of the ModuleAxapta enum, listed from the metadata Customer

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box, no picked field or Escape cancels without creating anything. When the table does not exist, the wizard stops with Table ... not found.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The progress notification Creating business event ContosoCustGroupCreated… shows each element. The final message reminds you: After deploying, rebuild the business event catalog (System administration > Business events > Manage > Rebuild business event catalog) and activate the event. Open Event opens the event class.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For base name ContosoCustGroupCreated on table CustGroup:

Element Type Content ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract Class Extends BusinessEventsContract; one private variable and one parm method per field ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent Class Extends BusinessEventsBase; [BusinessEvents(...)] attribute; buildContract CustGroup_ContosoCustGroupCreated_Extension Class [ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustGroup))]; wraps insert (or update) and sends the event

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The contract copies the fields of the record:

/// <summary>
/// Data of the ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent business event.
/// </summary>
[DataContract]
public final class ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract extends BusinessEventsContract
{
    private CustGroupId custGroup;
    private Description name;

    public static ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract newFromCustGroup(CustGroup _custGroupRecord)
    {
        ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract contract = new ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract();
        contract.initialize(_custGroupRecord);
        return contract;
    }

    private void new()
    {
    }

    private void initialize(CustGroup _custGroupRecord)
    {
        custGroup = _custGroupRecord.CustGroup;
        name = _custGroupRecord.Name;
    }

    [DataMember("CustGroup"), BusinessEventsDataMember("CustGroup")]
    public CustGroupId parmCustGroup(CustGroupId _custGroup = custGroup)
    {
        custGroup = _custGroup;
        return custGroup;
    }

    [DataMember("Name"), BusinessEventsDataMember("Name")]
    public Description parmName(Description _name = name)
    {
        name = _name;
        return name;
    }

}

The event class registers the event in the catalog. The attribute takes the label IDs without @:

/// <summary>
/// Business event sent when a CustGroup record is created.
/// </summary>
[BusinessEvents(classStr(ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract), "ContosoLabels:ContosoCustGroupCreatedName", "ContosoLabels:ContosoCustGroupCreatedDescription", ModuleAxapta::Customer)]
public final class ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent extends BusinessEventsBase
{
    private CustGroup custGroupRecord;

    public static ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent newFromCustGroup(CustGroup _custGroupRecord)
    {
        return new ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent(_custGroupRecord);
    }

    private void new(CustGroup _custGroupRecord)
    {
        custGroupRecord = _custGroupRecord;
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public BusinessEventsContract buildContract()
    {
        return ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEventContract::newFromCustGroup(custGroupRecord);
    }

}

The table extension sends the event after the record is written, only when the event is enabled:

/// <summary>
/// Sends ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent after a CustGroup record is inserted.
/// </summary>
[ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustGroup))]
final class CustGroup_ContosoCustGroupCreated_Extension
{
    public void insert()
    {
        next insert();
        if (BusinessEventsConfigurationReader::isBusinessEventEnabled(classStr(ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent)))
        {
            ContosoCustGroupCreatedBusinessEvent::newFromCustGroup(this).send();
        }
    }

}

With When a record is changed, the extension wraps update instead. (Doc comments are generated on every method; some are left out above.)

docs.title: Field types
docs.text: Each member's type is the field's EDT; without an EDT, the enum for enum fields; otherwise the primitive type (str, int, int64, real, date, utcdatetime, guid, TimeOfDay). A field whose type has no mapping (for example a container without an EDT) gets str; leave such fields out.

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Build and deploy (Build Project and Model, Deploy to Environment).
  2. In the web client, open System administration > Business events, then Manage > Rebuild business event catalog. The event appears in the catalog under the category you picked.
  3. Set up an endpoint and activate the event for it.
  4. Create a record (or change one, for an update event) and check that the endpoint receives the payload with your fields.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates two labels in the first en-US label file of your model: <Base>Name with the catalog name and <Base>Description with the description. Without a label file, the attribute gets the plain texts instead of label IDs.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newBusinessEvent in src/scaffolding/lifecycleWizards.ts. It reads the table's fields with get_table_fields and the ModuleAxapta values with read_object.
  2. The three classes are built by businessEventElements in src/scaffolding/lifecycle.ts and created with create_object through the metadata server.
  3. All or nothing: if one class fails, the classes created before it are deleted again.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a business event on a scratch table, builds the model, and deletes everything. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One trigger: insert or update. Events for deletes, or sent from business logic (for example after posting), must be written by hand: call <Base>BusinessEvent::newFrom<Table>(record).send() where the event should fire.
  • The event is sent from the table's insert or update. Code that bypasses those methods (for example set-based operations with skipDataMethods) does not send it.
  • The wizard does not rebuild the catalog or activate the event in the environment.
  • Labels created before a failure stay in the label file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Table ... not found. Wrong table name Check it with Open Element Class ...: ... already exists ... A generated class name is taken, for example the table already has an extension with that name Choose another base name The event is not in the catalog The catalog was not rebuilt after deployment Manage > Rebuild business event catalog The event never fires It is not activated, or records are written set-based Activate it; check how the records are created Build error on a contract member A field type has no X++ mapping Remove that member, or give it a suitable type

docs.title: Wizard: Custom Service
docs.text: New Custom Service… creates a custom service that external systems call over JSON or SOAP: request and response data contracts, the service class with a process operation, the service, a service group that deploys it, and a privilege for the operation. After deployment the operation is at /api/services/<Base>ServiceGroup/<Base>Service/process. In Visual Studio you create these six elements by hand.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• An external application must call X++ logic (create orders, post journals, return a computed value) and data entities do not fit.
  • You want a request/response contract with error handling and a company context from the start.
  • You want the privilege for the operation created with the service, so you can grant it to the calling application's role.

For plain create/read/update/delete of records, a data entity is usually better: see Wizard Data Entity.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the description label.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Custom Service… New Element Wizards > Custom service Command Palette F&O Studio: New Custom Service…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New custom service: name Base name with your prefix; the elements get Service, Request, Response and ServiceGroup appended ContosoOrderImport 2 New custom service: description What the service does Imports orders from the web shop

The grey text is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape cancels without creating anything.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The progress notification Creating service ContosoOrderImport… shows each element. The final message lists the elements and says: After deployment the operation is at /api/services/ContosoOrderImportServiceGroup/ContosoOrderImportService/process; add the privilege ContosoOrderImportInvoke to a role for the calling app. Open Service Class opens the service class.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For base name ContosoOrderImport:

Element Type Content ContosoOrderImportRequest Class Data contract with DataAreaId and Description members ContosoOrderImportResponse Class Data contract with Success and Message members ContosoOrderImportService Class The process operation ContosoOrderImportService Service Class = the service class, External name = the same, Description = the label, operation process ContosoOrderImportServiceGroup Service group Auto deploy = Yes, contains the service ContosoOrderImportInvoke Security privilege Entry point on service operation ContosoOrderImportService.process with Invoke access

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The request contract (the response is built the same way with parmSuccess and parmMessage):

/// <summary>
/// Request of the ContosoOrderImportService.process operation.
/// </summary>
[DataContractAttribute]
class ContosoOrderImportRequest
{
    DataAreaId dataAreaId;
    Description description;

    /// <summary>
    /// The company the request is for.
    /// </summary>
    [DataMemberAttribute('DataAreaId')]
    public DataAreaId parmDataAreaId(DataAreaId _dataAreaId = dataAreaId)
    {
        dataAreaId = _dataAreaId;
        return dataAreaId;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The request data; replace with your fields.
    /// </summary>
    [DataMemberAttribute('Description')]
    public Description parmDescription(Description _description = description)
    {
        description = _description;
        return description;
    }

}

The service class runs the work in the requested company, in a transaction, and turns an error into a response instead of a failed call:

class ContosoOrderImportService
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Handles one request in the request's company.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="_request">The request.</param>
    /// <returns>The result.</returns>
    public ContosoOrderImportResponse process(ContosoOrderImportRequest _request)
    {
        ContosoOrderImportResponse response = new ContosoOrderImportResponse();

        try
        {
            changecompany(_request.parmDataAreaId() ? _request.parmDataAreaId() : curExt())
            {
                ttsbegin;
                // Do the work for _request here.
                ttscommit;
            }
            response.parmSuccess(true);
        }
        catch (Exception::Error)
        {
            response.parmSuccess(false);
            response.parmMessage(infolog.text(infologLine()));
        }
        return response;
    }

}

When DataAreaId is empty, the current company is used.

docs.title: Calling the service
docs.text:
After you build and deploy, the operation is available at:

POST https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com/api/services/ContosoOrderImportServiceGroup/ContosoOrderImportService/process

In D365FO JSON services, the body carries each parameter of the operation by name, so the request contract goes under _request:

{
    "_request": {
        "DataAreaId": "usmf",
        "Description": "Order 1001 from the web shop"
    }
}

The response contains the Success and Message members. The caller needs a Microsoft Entra ID token for the environment, and its application user needs a role that holds the ContosoOrderImportInvoke privilege.

To try the call from VS Code, use Try Service Operation: it builds a request body from the data contract and saves the request as an .http file.

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Replace Description in the request with your fields (parm methods with [DataMemberAttribute('Name')]), and add fields to the response if the caller needs data back.
  2. Write the work inside the ttsbegin/ttscommit block.
  3. Add ContosoOrderImportInvoke to a duty and role for the calling application (Security View).
  4. Build and deploy (Build Project and Model, Deploy to Environment).
  5. Test the call with Try Service Operation.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates one label (ID = the base name, text = the description) in the first en-US label file of your model. It is used as the service and service group description, the privilege label and in the service class's doc comment. Without a label file the plain text is used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newService in src/scaffolding/wizards.ts; the elements are built by serviceElements in src/scaffolding/service.ts.
  2. The service and service group are sent as typed metadata (class, operations, services, auto deploy) to the create_object bridge action; the metadata server saves them through Microsoft's metadata API.
  3. All or nothing: if one element fails, the ones created before it are deleted again, and the error names the failing element.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a service with these builders, builds the model, and deletes the elements. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One operation, process. Add more methods to the class and operations to the service in the Element Designer.
  • The request contract has placeholder members; the wizard does not design your payload.
  • The wizard does not grant the privilege to a role or register the calling application in the environment.
  • Any error is caught as Exception::Error and its last infolog line returned; other exception types are not handled.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Class ContosoOrderImportRequest: ... already exists ... A generated name is taken Choose another base name The wizard closes without creating anything A prompt was empty or cancelled Run it again The call returns 404 after deploy The service group was not deployed, or the URL differs Check the group and service names; they are in the URL as created The call returns 401 or 403 Token or authorization problem Check the token's audience and that the application user's role has the ...Invoke privilege Success is false with a message The X++ code raised an error Read the message; debug with the Debugger

docs.title: Wizard: Data Entity
docs.text: New Data Entity… creates a data entity over one table, enabled for OData and for data management, with its staging table and View and Maintain privileges. You pick the table, the public names and the fields; the wizard finds the entity key from the table's natural key. The result is what Visual Studio's data entity wizard creates, plus the two privileges.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• An integration must read or write the records of a table over OData (/data/<collection>).
  • Users must import or export the table with data management (Data management workspace, packages, recurring integrations).
  • You built a setup table (for example with Wizard Table with Form) and want it in configuration data packages.

For extending a standard entity with new fields, use a data entity extension instead (Create Extension).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • The table exists. Ideally it has a natural key: an alternate key index set as its replacement key, or a primary index on business fields. Otherwise the wizard asks which fields form the key.
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the entity label.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Data Entity… New Element Wizards > Data entity Command Palette F&O Studio: New Data Entity…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New data entity: table The table the entity reads and writes ContosoVehicleGroup 2 New data entity: name Entity name with your prefix ContosoVehicleGroupEntity 3 New data entity: label What users see in data management Vehicle groups 4 New data entity: public name (OData, singular) The OData entity name ContosoVehicleGroup 5 New data entity: public collection name (OData, plural) The OData collection name ContosoVehicleGroups 6 New data entity: fields of ContosoVehicleGroup The fields the entity exposes (multi-select; all are selected at first) ContosoVehicleGroupId, Description 7 New data entity: key fields (... has no natural key index) Only when the table has no replacement key or primary index: the key fields

Only fields of these types are offered: string, integer, real, date, date-time, enum, GUID and time. Int64 fields (such as RecId references) and containers are not offered, because they are not staged.

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape cancels without creating anything.

docs.title: The entity key
docs.text: The wizard reads the table's ReplacementKey property, or else its PrimaryIndex, and uses that index's fields as the entity key. Every key field must be among the fields you picked; otherwise the wizard stops with The entity must include the key field(s) .... When there is no key index and you pick no key field, it stops with The entity needs at least one key field.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The progress notification Creating ContosoVehicleGroupEntity… shows each element. The final message says: Add the privileges to duties, build and synchronize the database; the entity is then at /data/ContosoVehicleGroups and in data management. Open Entity opens the entity in the designer.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For entity ContosoVehicleGroupEntity over table ContosoVehicleGroup:

Element Type Content ContosoVehicleGroupEntityStaging Table Staging table: the data management fields plus one field per picked field ContosoVehicleGroupEntity Data entity Public, data management enabled, root data source on the table, one mapped field per picked field, key EntityKey ContosoVehicleGroupEntityView Security privilege Data entity permission Read ContosoVehicleGroupEntityMaintain Security privilege Data entity permission Read,Update,Create,Delete

docs.title: Entity properties
docs.text: Property Value Label Your label PublicEntityName / PublicCollectionName Your OData names IsPublic Yes DataManagementEnabled Yes DataManagementStagingTable The staging table EntityCategory Reference PrimaryKey EntityKey (the key fields) PrimaryCompanyContext DataAreaId, only when the table saves data per company Data source The table as root data source, Dynamic Fields = Yes Fields Mapped fields with the same names as the table fields

docs.title: Staging table
docs.text:
Part Value Fields DefinitionGroup (EDT DMFDefinitionGroupName), ExecutionId (DMFExecutionId), IsSelected (DMFIsSelected), TransferStatus (enum DMFTransferStatus), then the picked fields with their EDT or enum Index StagingIdx: unique alternate key on DefinitionGroup, ExecutionId and the key fields; primary, cluster and replacement key Properties TableGroup = Staging, TableType = Regular, SaveDataPerCompany = No, TitleField1 = the first key field, Developer documentation @DMF:StagingDeveloperDocumentation

The staging table has the same field names as the entity, which data management needs for its default mapping.

docs.title: Using the entity
docs.text:
After build, database synchronization and deployment:

GET https://yourenv.operations.dynamics.com/data/ContosoVehicleGroups?cross-company=true

returns the records as OData JSON. Use Try Data Entity (OData) to run such queries from VS Code and save them as .http files.

In data management, the entity is listed under its label; it can be added to import and export projects.

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Add the View and Maintain privileges to duties (for example a duty for the integration's application user).
  2. Build (Build Project and Model), synchronize the database (Synchronize Database) and deploy (Deploy to Environment).
  3. In data management, refresh the entity list so the new entity is known.
  4. Test a read with Try Data Entity (OData), and an import with a small file.
  5. Run Analyze Performance, Review My Changes or the Pre-Deploy Checklist: they check data entity readiness (public names, keys, staging fields, mandatory fields).

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates one label (ID = the entity name, text = your label) in the first en-US label file of your model. It is the entity's, the staging table's and the privileges' label. Without a label file the plain text is used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newDataEntity in src/scaffolding/wizards.ts. It reads the table with read_object (properties, indexes) and get_table_fields.
  2. The elements are built by dataEntityElements in src/scaffolding/dataEntity.ts. The entity is sent as typed metadata (view metadata, fields, keys) to create_object and saved by the metadata server through Microsoft's metadata API.
  3. All or nothing: if one element fails, the ones created before it are deleted again.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates an entity over a table built by the table-with-form builder, builds the model and deletes everything. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One table, no joined data sources, no computed or virtual fields. Add them in the Element Designer.
  • RecId references (Int64) and containers are not offered; entities usually expose the referenced record's natural key instead, which needs a joined data source.
  • The entity category is always Reference.
  • The wizard does not add the privileges to duties, synchronize the database or refresh the data management entity list.

docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Table ... not found. Wrong table name Check it with Open Element The entity must include the key field(s) ... You unselected a key field Run again and keep the key fields selected The entity needs at least one key field. The table has no key index and you picked none Pick key fields, or add an alternate key to the table first Table ...Staging: ... already exists ... The entity or staging name is taken Choose another entity name /data/... returns 404 after deploy Not synchronized or not deployed, or the collection name differs Synchronize and deploy; use the public collection name The entity is not in data management The entity list was not refreshed Refresh the entity list in the Data management workspace

docs.title: Wizard: Feature Management
docs.text: New Feature (Feature Management)… creates a feature class that appears in the Feature management workspace: a class implementing IFeatureMetadata, with its name, summary, module and default, and a static isEnabled() you use to guard new behaviour. Show Feature Usage then lists where a feature class is checked in code. The pattern follows standard features such as QMSApprovedCustomerListFeature. Visual Studio has no wizard for this.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• A change in behaviour must be switched on by an administrator per environment, instead of being active as soon as it is deployed.
  • You want to ship code that stays off until a customer is ready, or that can be turned off again if it causes trouble.
  • You want to find all places that check a feature before you remove the flag.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the feature name and summary.
  • For Show Feature Usage: the cross-reference database is built for the code that checks the feature (see Find All References).

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Feature… New Element Wizards > Feature (Feature management) Command Palette F&O Studio: New Feature (Feature Management)…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New feature: class name Class name with your prefix, ending with Feature ContosoFastInvoicingFeature 2 New feature: name in Feature management What administrators see Fast invoicing 3 New feature: summary What turning it on changes Posts invoices in one step. 4 New feature: module A value of the FeatureModuleV0 enum, listed from the metadata AccountsReceivable 5 New feature: default Off by default or On by default Off by default

The name check accepts any valid class name; ending it with Feature is the convention, not enforced. The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape cancels without creating anything.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The progress notification Creating feature ContosoFastInvoicingFeature… runs, then the message says: Created ContosoFastInvoicingFeature. Guard new behaviour with if (ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::isEnabled()) { ... }; after deploying, Feature management > Check for updates lists it.

Copy Check copies this snippet to the clipboard:

if (ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::isEnabled())
{
}

docs.title: Element created
docs.text:
One class, <class name>, added to the project.

using System.ComponentModel.Composition;
using Microsoft.Dynamics.ApplicationPlatform.FeatureExposure;

/// <summary>
/// Feature management: ContosoFastInvoicingFeature. Check it with ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::isEnabled().
/// </summary>
[ExportAttribute(identifierStr(Microsoft.Dynamics.ApplicationPlatform.FeatureExposure.IFeatureMetadata))]
public final class ContosoFastInvoicingFeature implements IFeatureMetadata
{
    private static ContosoFastInvoicingFeature instance = new ContosoFastInvoicingFeature();

    private void new()
    {
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public static ContosoFastInvoicingFeature instance()
    {
        return ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::instance;
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public static boolean isEnabled()
    {
        return Microsoft.Dynamics.ApplicationPlatform.FeatureExposure.FeatureStateProvider::isFeatureEnabled(ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::instance());
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public FeatureLabelId label()
    {
        return literalStr("@ContosoLabels:ContosoFastInvoicingFeature");
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public int module()
    {
        return FeatureModuleV0::AccountsReceivable;
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public FeatureLabelId summary()
    {
        return literalStr("@ContosoLabels:ContosoFastInvoicingFeatureSummary");
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public WebSiteURL learnMoreUrl()
    {
        return '';
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public boolean isEnabledByDefault()
    {
        return false;
    }

    [Hookable(false)]
    public boolean canDisable()
    {
        return true;
    }

}

(Doc comments are generated on every method; they are left out above.) When the model has no label file, label() and summary() return the plain texts and the class comment shows the name text instead of the class name.

Method Returns instance() The single instance Feature management knows isEnabled() Whether the feature is on in this environment label() The name in Feature management module() The module it is listed under summary() What the feature does learnMoreUrl() Documentation link; empty isEnabledByDefault() true for On by default, else false canDisable() true: administrators can turn it off again

docs.title: Using the feature in code
docs.text:
Guard the new behaviour, for example in a Chain of Command wrapper:

[ExtensionOf(classStr(SalesFormLetter))]
final class SalesFormLetter_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    public void run()
    {
        if (ContosoFastInvoicingFeature::isEnabled())
        {
            // new behaviour
        }
        next run();
    }

}

docs.title: Show Feature Usage
docs.text:
Show Feature Usage lists every place that references a feature class, so you can review the gated code or remove the flag cleanly.

  1. Right-click a class in Application Explorer or the project view and choose Show Feature Usage, or run F&O Studio: Show Feature Usage and pick the class.
  2. The Results view opens Feature usage: ContosoFastInvoicingFeature with the summary N place(s) check or use ContosoFastInvoicingFeature and the section Code gated by the feature.
  3. Each finding is Element.method with the line and module. Click it to open the code at that line.
  4. When nothing is found, the section says not used: the feature gates nothing (or the cross references are not built).

The command queries the cross-reference database (where_used, up to 1000 references) and leaves out references inside the feature class itself. Run Again in the Results view runs it again after a build.

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Guard the new code with isEnabled().
  2. Build and deploy (Build Project and Model, Deploy to Environment).
  3. In the web client, open Feature management, select Check for updates, find the feature and enable it.
  4. Test with the feature off and on.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates two labels in the first en-US label file of your model: ID = the class name (feature name) and <class name>Summary (summary). Without a label file the plain texts are used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newFeature in src/scaffolding/lifecycleWizards.ts; it reads the FeatureModuleV0 values with read_object.
  2. The class is built by featureElements in src/scaffolding/lifecycle.ts and created with create_object; on failure nothing is left.
  3. Show Feature Usage is registered in src/extension.ts and uses the where_used bridge action on the cross-reference database.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a feature class with these builders, builds the model and deletes it. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• learnMoreUrl() returns an empty string; fill it if you have documentation.
  • canDisable() returns true; change it if the feature must not be turned off once on.
  • The wizard does not enable the feature in an environment.
  • Show Feature Usage finds only references in the cross-reference database; code not yet built with cross references is missing.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The feature is not in Feature management after deploy The list was not refreshed Select Check for updates in Feature management Class ...: ... already exists ... The class name is taken Choose another name Show Feature Usage finds nothing No code checks the feature yet, or cross references are not built Build with cross references, then Run Again isEnabled() stays false The feature is not enabled in this environment Enable it in Feature management

docs.title: Wizard: Number Sequence
docs.text: Add Number Sequence… sets up a number sequence for a new ID: it creates the extended data type, adds the data type to a module's number sequence references (a Chain of Command extension of the module's loadModule), adds a numRef...() method to the module's parameters table, and can make a field of your table get the next number when a record is created. It follows the standard pattern of NumberSeqModuleCustomer.loadModule. Visual Studio has no wizard for this.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Records of your table need an automatic ID (request number, contract number, batch number) from a number sequence.
  • You want the reference listed in the module's parameters form (Number sequences tab) and created by the Generate wizard of Number sequences.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • Your model references the package of the module class and parameters table you extend (for the listed modules, Application Suite).
  • Optional: the table that gets the number is in your project's model and has no initValue method yet (then the wizard adds it).
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the EDT's label.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > Add Number Sequence… New Element Wizards > Number sequence Command Palette F&O Studio: Add Number Sequence…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 Add number sequence: ID type (EDT) The new extended data type with your prefix ContosoRequestId 2 Add number sequence: label What the ID is called Request number 3 Add number sequence: module whose parameters hold the reference A module from the list, or Other module… Accounts receivable 3a Module class (only for Other module) The NumberSeqModule class NumberSeqModuleCustomer 3b Parameters table (only for Other module) The module's parameters table CustParameters 4 Add number sequence: your table (optional) A table of your model whose field gets the next number in initValue; leave empty for none ContosoServiceRequest 5 Add number sequence: field (only with a table) The field that gets the number; created with the new EDT when it does not exist RequestId

Modules in the list and what the wizard extends:

Module Module class Parameters table Accounts receivable NumberSeqModuleCustomer CustParameters Accounts payable NumberSeqModuleVendor VendParameters Inventory management NumberSeqModuleInventory InventParameters Sales and marketing NumberSeqModuleSalesOrder SalesParameters Procurement and sourcing NumberSeqModulePurchaseOrder PurchParameters Project management NumberSeqModuleProject ProjParameters General ledger NumberSeqModuleLedger LedgerParameters

The wizard checks that the module class and the parameters table exist (... was not found. otherwise) before it asks for your table.

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. Leaving a required box empty or pressing Escape stops the wizard before anything is created.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The progress notification Adding number sequence ContosoRequestId… shows each element. The final message says what was done, for example:

Added ContosoRequestId to NumberSeqModuleCustomer. ContosoServiceRequest.RequestId gets the next number in initValue. After deploying, run Number sequences > Generate (or set up the reference on the CustParameters form's Number sequences tab).

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
The two extension classes are named <Module class>_<Prefix>_Extension and <Parameters table>_<Prefix>_Extension. The prefix is the run of capitals at the start of the EDT name without its last capital (for ABCRequestId it is ABC). When that is empty, as for ContosoRequestId, the prefix is the model name.

For EDT ContosoRequestId in model ContosoExtensions with Accounts receivable:

Element Type Content ContosoRequestId Extended data type String, extends Num, Label and Help text = the label NumberSeqModuleCustomer_ContosoExtensions_Extension Class [ExtensionOf(classStr(NumberSeqModuleCustomer))]; wraps loadModule CustParameters_ContosoExtensions_Extension Class [ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustParameters))]; numRefContosoRequestId()

With a table and field, the wizard also changes your table (see below).

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The module extension registers the data type as a company-specific reference:

/// <summary>
/// Adds the ContosoRequestId number sequence reference to NumberSeqModuleCustomer.
/// </summary>
[ExtensionOf(classStr(NumberSeqModuleCustomer))]
final class NumberSeqModuleCustomer_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Adds ContosoRequestId to the module's references (Number sequences > Generate).
    /// </summary>
    protected void loadModule()
    {
        next loadModule();

        NumberSeqDatatype datatype = NumberSeqDatatype::construct();
        datatype.parmDatatypeId(extendedTypeNum(ContosoRequestId));
        datatype.parmReferenceHelp(literalStr("@ContosoLabels:ContosoRequestId"));
        datatype.parmWizardIsContinuous(false);
        datatype.parmWizardIsManual(NoYes::No);
        datatype.parmWizardIsChangeDownAllowed(NoYes::No);
        datatype.parmWizardIsChangeUpAllowed(NoYes::No);
        datatype.parmWizardHighest(999999);
        datatype.parmSortField(1000);
        datatype.addParameterType(NumberSeqParameterType::DataArea, true, false);
        this.create(datatype);
    }

}

The parameters table extension gives code a way to find the reference:

[ExtensionOf(tableStr(CustParameters))]
final class CustParameters_ContosoExtensions_Extension
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The number sequence reference of ContosoRequestId.
    /// </summary>
    /// <returns>The reference.</returns>
    public static NumberSequenceReference numRefContosoRequestId()
    {
        return NumberSeqReference::findReference(extendedTypeNum(ContosoRequestId));
    }

}

docs.title: Changes to your table
docs.text:
When you name a table of your model without an initValue method, the wizard adds this method (and the field, as a string field with the new EDT, when it does not exist):

/// <summary>
/// Defaults the record; RequestId gets the next number of ContosoRequestId.
/// </summary>
public void initValue()
{
    super();
    this.RequestId = NumberSeq::newGetNum(CustParameters::numRefContosoRequestId()).num();
}

When the table is not in your model or already has initValue, the wizard changes nothing and the message tells you the line to add yourself:

this.RequestId = NumberSeq::newGetNum(CustParameters::numRefContosoRequestId()).num();

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Build and deploy; synchronize the database if a field was added (Build Project and Model, Deploy to Environment, Synchronize Database).
  2. In the web client, run Number sequences > Generate, or open the module's parameters form (for Accounts receivable, Accounts receivable parameters), tab Number sequences, and assign a sequence to the new reference.
  3. Create a record: the field gets the next number.
  4. Make the field read-only on the form if users must not change it.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates one label (ID = the EDT name, text = the label) in the first en-US label file of your model. It is the EDT's label and help text and the reference help in loadModule. Without a label file the plain text is used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts and the table change are in addNumberSequence in src/scaffolding/lifecycleWizards.ts. It checks the module class and parameters table with find_object, and reads your table with read_object and get_table_fields.
  2. The EDT and the two classes are built by numberSequenceElements in src/scaffolding/lifecycle.ts and created with create_object through the metadata server.
  3. All or nothing for the three elements: if one fails, the ones created before it are deleted again.
  4. The table change (update_object with the initValue method and, if needed, the field) runs after the elements and is not rolled back. If it fails, the message says ... could not be changed (...).
  5. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a number sequence for NumberSeqModuleCustomer and CustParameters, builds the model and deletes the elements. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The reference is company-specific (NumberSeqParameterType::DataArea). Shared or other scopes need a code change in loadModule.
  • The wizard writes initValue only when your table has none; otherwise you add one line yourself.
  • It does not create or assign the number sequence in the environment; run Generate or set it up on the parameters form.
  • The extension class names follow the <Element>_<Prefix>_Extension convention. If your model already has a class with that name (for example from Create Code Extension), the wizard fails and removes what it created; add the methods to the existing class by hand.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ... was not found. The module class or parameters table name (Other module) is wrong Check the names with Open Element Class NumberSeqModuleCustomer_..._Extension: ... already exists ... An extension class with that name exists in your model Add the loadModule wrapper and numRef method to the existing classes by hand ... is not a table of ...: set ... yourself. The table is standard or in another model Set the field in your own code or a Chain of Command extension ... already has initValue: add ... to it. The table has initValue Add the shown line to the existing method The reference is not on the parameters form Not deployed, or loadModule not run Deploy, then run Number sequences > Generate NumberSeq::newGetNum fails at runtime No sequence is assigned to the reference in this company Assign one on the parameters form

docs.title: Wizard: Report
docs.text:
New Report… creates a complete SSRS report over one table with the report data provider (RDP) pattern: a TempDB table, an optional date-range contract, the data provider class, the controller, the report with a ready-to-run auto design, an output menu item and a privilege. You pick the table, the fields and an optional date filter; the report runs after a build and deploy. In Visual Studio you create these elements one by one.

This wizard is different from New Element… > Report, which creates an empty report as Visual Studio's Add New Item does.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need a list report of one table, with or without a From/To date filter.
  • You want a starting point with the correct RDP plumbing (data set attribute, contract attribute, system parameters) and then refine the design.
  • You want the menu item and the privilege created with the report.

For reports from a scanned or printed document, see Scenario: Report from a Scanned Document.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects); otherwise the wizard stops with Open a D365FO project first: the new elements go to its model.
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • The source table exists in the metadata (standard or custom).
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the report title label.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Report… New Element Wizards > Report (wizard) Command Palette F&O Studio: New Report…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New report: name Report name with your prefix. The classes and the table get DP, Controller, Contract and Tmp appended. ContosoCustInvoiceList 2 New report: title What users see on the menu and as the report title Customer invoices 3 New report: table The table the report lists CustInvoiceJour 4 New report: fields of CustInvoiceJour Pick one or more fields (multi-select). The description shows each field's EDT, enum or type. InvoiceId, InvoiceDate, InvoiceAmount, InvoiceAccount, CurrencyCode 5 New report: filter by a date? No date range, or one of the table's date fields (shown as From/To date filter). Asked only when the table has date or date-time fields. InvoiceDate

Only fields of these types are offered: string, integer, int64, real, date, date-time, enum, GUID and time. Container fields and other types are left out.

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape cancels without creating anything. When the table does not exist, the wizard stops with Table ... not found.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The progress notification Creating report ContosoCustInvoiceList… shows each element. The final message lists the elements and says: Add the privilege ContosoCustInvoiceListView to a duty and the menu item to a menu, build, then deploy the report. Open Data Provider opens the data provider class.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For base name ContosoCustInvoiceList:

Element Type Content ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp Table TableType = TempDB, TableGroup = Miscellaneous; one field per picked field, same name, same EDT or enum ContosoCustInvoiceListContract Class Only with a date filter: [DataContractAttribute] with parmFromDate and parmToDate ContosoCustInvoiceListDP Class Extends SRSReportDataProviderBase; data set method and processReport ContosoCustInvoiceListController Class Extends SrsReportRunController; main runs the report's Report design ContosoCustInvoiceList Report One data set, the parameters and an auto design named Report ContosoCustInvoiceList Output menu item Label = title, Object type Class, Object = the controller ContosoCustInvoiceListView Security privilege Entry point on the output menu item with Read access

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The data provider fills the temporary table in one set-based statement:

/// <summary>
/// Data of the ContosoCustInvoiceList report: CustInvoiceJour rows in ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp.
/// </summary>
[SRSReportParameterAttribute(classStr(ContosoCustInvoiceListContract))]
class ContosoCustInvoiceListDP extends SRSReportDataProviderBase
{
    ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp contosoCustInvoiceListTmp;

    /// <summary>
    /// The rows of the report.
    /// </summary>
    /// <returns>The report data.</returns>
    [SRSReportDataSetAttribute(tableStr(ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp))]
    public ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp getContosoCustInvoiceListTmp()
    {
        select contosoCustInvoiceListTmp;
        return contosoCustInvoiceListTmp;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Fills the report data in one set-based statement.
    /// </summary>
    public void processReport()
    {
        ContosoCustInvoiceListContract contract = this.parmDataContract() as ContosoCustInvoiceListContract;
        CustInvoiceJour source;

        insert_recordset contosoCustInvoiceListTmp (InvoiceId, InvoiceDate, InvoiceAmount, InvoiceAccount, CurrencyCode)
            select InvoiceId, InvoiceDate, InvoiceAmount, InvoiceAccount, CurrencyCode from source
            where source.InvoiceDate >= contract.parmFromDate() && source.InvoiceDate <= contract.parmToDate();
    }

}

Without a date filter, the class has no SRSReportParameterAttribute, no contract variable and no where clause.

When the date field is a date-time field, the range is converted to the company's time zone and the To date is inclusive:

        where source.CreatedDateTime >= DateTimeUtil::newDateTime(contract.parmFromDate(), 0, DateTimeUtil::getCompanyTimeZone())
           && source.CreatedDateTime < DateTimeUtil::newDateTime(contract.parmToDate() + 1, 0, DateTimeUtil::getCompanyTimeZone());

The contract (with a date filter):

[DataContractAttribute]
class ContosoCustInvoiceListContract
{
    FromDate fromDate;
    ToDate toDate;

    [DataMemberAttribute('FromDate')]
    public FromDate parmFromDate(FromDate _fromDate = fromDate)
    {
        fromDate = _fromDate;
        return fromDate;
    }

    [DataMemberAttribute('ToDate')]
    public ToDate parmToDate(ToDate _toDate = toDate)
    {
        toDate = _toDate;
        return toDate;
    }

}

The controller:

public static void main(Args _args)
{
    ContosoCustInvoiceListController controller = new ContosoCustInvoiceListController();
    controller.parmReportName(ssrsReportStr(ContosoCustInvoiceList, Report));
    controller.parmArgs(_args);
    controller.startOperation();
}

(Doc comments are generated on every class and method; they are left out above for brevity.)

docs.title: The report element
docs.text:
Part Value Data set Named like the Tmp table; Data Source Type ReportDataProvider; Query SELECT * FROM ContosoCustInvoiceListDP.ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp; Dynamic Filters on Data set fields One per picked field. Enum fields are strings showing the enum's label. Dates and date-times are System.DateTime, reals System.Double. Parameters The hidden system parameters AX_PartitionKey, AX_CompanyName, AX_UserContext, AX_RenderingCulture, AX_ReportContext, AX_RdpPreProcessedId; with a date filter also the visible FromDate and ToDate Design Auto design Report: title = the report label, layout template ReportLayoutStyleTemplate, page 8.5 x 11 in, 0.5 in margins Data region A table with style TableStyleTemplate and one column per field (=Fields!<Field>.Value)

Open the report in the Report Element Designer to change the design, or use Create Precision Design… on the auto design to get a precision design for the Report Designer.

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Add the privilege to a duty and the output menu item to a menu.
  2. Build the project and the report (Report Build, Build Project and Model).
  3. Check the layout locally with Report Preview.
  4. Deploy (Deploy to Environment) and run the menu item in the web client.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates one label with ID = the base name and text = the title, in the first en-US label file of your model, and uses it as the report title, menu item label and privilege label. Without a label file the plain title is used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newReport in src/scaffolding/wizards.ts. The table's fields come from the get_table_fields bridge action.
  2. The elements are built in src/scaffolding/report.ts (reportElements). The report is sent as typed metadata (data sets, parameter group, designs) and saved by the metadata server through Microsoft's metadata API.
  3. Elements are created in order with create_object and added to the project. All or nothing: if one fails, the ones created before it are deleted again and the error names the failing element.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a report over CustInvoiceJour with a date filter, checks the saved data set and auto design, builds the model and deletes the elements. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One source table, no joins, no grouping or totals. Extend processReport and the Tmp table for more.
  • The date filter supports one field. Other filters come from the data set's dynamic filters or from new contract members.
  • Fields of unsupported types (for example containers) are not offered.
  • The wizard does not add the privilege to a duty or the menu item to a menu.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Table ... not found. The table name is wrong Check it with Open Element A field is missing from the field list Its type is not supported (for example a container) Add it to the Tmp table and processReport by hand No date question The table has no date or date-time fields of a supported type Add a contract by hand if you need other filters Table ContosoCustInvoiceListTmp: ... already exists ... A generated name is taken Choose another base name The wizard closes without creating anything A prompt was empty or cancelled, or no field was picked Run it again

docs.title: Wizard: Table with Form
docs.text: New Table with Form… creates a setup table with its list form, following the standard "group" pattern of CustGroup: a key EDT, a table with an alternate key, field groups and find/exist methods, a SimpleList form with a quick filter and a grid, a display menu item, and View and Maintain privileges. In Visual Studio you create these six elements by hand and apply the form pattern yourself.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• You need a new setup or reference table (groups, codes, types) that users maintain in a simple list.
  • You want the table, its form, its menu item and its security in one step, consistent with standard setup forms.
  • You plan to expose the table through a data entity afterwards (Wizard Data Entity).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A D365FO project is open (D365FO Projects).
  • The metadata server runs (Connect to Environment).
  • Optional: an en-US label file in your model, for the table and key field labels.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: Place How Dynamics 365 view Create > New Table with Form… New Element Wizards > Table with form Command Palette F&O Studio: New Table with Form…

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
# Prompt (title) What to enter Example 1 New table with form: name Table, form and menu item name with your prefix; the key field gets Id appended ContosoVehicleGroup 2 New table with form: label What users see as the form caption and menu item Vehicle groups 3 New table with form: key field label The label of the key field Vehicle group

The grey text in the boxes is a placeholder, not a default. An empty box or Escape cancels without creating anything.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The progress notification Creating ContosoVehicleGroup… shows each element. The final message says: Add fields to ContosoVehicleGroup and its Overview field group, the menu item to a menu, and the privileges ContosoVehicleGroupView and ContosoVehicleGroupMaintain to duties. Open Table and Open Form open the new elements in the designer.

docs.title: Elements created
docs.text:
For base name ContosoVehicleGroup:

Element Type Content ContosoVehicleGroupId Extended data type Extends SysGroup; label = the key field label ContosoVehicleGroup Table Key field, Description, alternate key index, field groups, find and exist ContosoVehicleGroup Form SimpleList pattern: action pane, quick filter, grid ContosoVehicleGroup Display menu item Opens the form; label = the table label ContosoVehicleGroupView Security privilege Read access to the menu item ContosoVehicleGroupMaintain Security privilege Read, Update, Create and Delete access to the menu item

docs.title: The table
docs.text:
Part Value Fields ContosoVehicleGroupId (EDT ContosoVehicleGroupId, Mandatory = Yes, AllowEdit = No) and Description (EDT Description) Index ContosoVehicleGroupIdIdx on the key field: no duplicates, alternate key Primary index, cluster index, replacement key ContosoVehicleGroupIdIdx Field groups AutoLookup (key, Description), AutoIdentification (key), Overview (key, Description) Properties Label = your label, TableGroup = Group, CacheLookup = Found, TitleField1 = key, TitleField2 = Description

AllowEdit = No on the key means users enter the ID when they create a record and cannot change it afterwards.

docs.text:
Part Value Data source ContosoVehicleGroup on the table, InsertIfEmpty = No, with the two fields Design Caption = your label, Pattern SimpleList 1.1, Style SimpleList, Data source and Title data source = the table ActionPane Empty action pane for your buttons CustomFilterGroup Pattern CustomAndQuickFilters, with a QuickFilter control on the grid, default column the key field Grid Tabular grid with Grid_ContosoVehicleGroupId and Grid_Description

The form opens in the Form Designer and Preview, which shows how the web client will render it.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text:
The table's find and exist methods follow the standard setup table pattern:

/// <summary>
/// Finds a ContosoVehicleGroup record by its key.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="_contosoVehicleGroupId">The key.</param>
/// <param name="_forUpdate">Select for update.</param>
/// <returns>The record; empty when it does not exist.</returns>
public static ContosoVehicleGroup find(ContosoVehicleGroupId _contosoVehicleGroupId, boolean _forUpdate = false)
{
    ContosoVehicleGroup contosoVehicleGroup;

    if (_contosoVehicleGroupId)
    {
        contosoVehicleGroup.selectForUpdate(_forUpdate);
        select firstonly contosoVehicleGroup where contosoVehicleGroup.ContosoVehicleGroupId == _contosoVehicleGroupId;
    }
    return contosoVehicleGroup;
}

/// <summary>
/// Whether a ContosoVehicleGroup record with the key exists.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="_contosoVehicleGroupId">The key.</param>
/// <returns>true when it exists.</returns>
public static boolean exist(ContosoVehicleGroupId _contosoVehicleGroupId)
{
    return _contosoVehicleGroupId && (select firstonly RecId from ContosoVehicleGroup where ContosoVehicleGroup.ContosoVehicleGroupId == _contosoVehicleGroupId).RecId != 0;
}

Use them from other code:

if (!ContosoVehicleGroup::exist(vehicleGroupId))
{
    throw error(strFmt("Vehicle group %1 does not exist.", vehicleGroupId));
}
Description description = ContosoVehicleGroup::find(vehicleGroupId).Description;

docs.title: After the wizard
docs.text:
1. Add more fields to the table in the Element Designer, and add them to the Overview field group and the grid if they should show in the list.
  2. Add the menu item to a menu, for example with a menu extension of the module's setup menu.
  3. Add the privileges to duties: View for users who read the setup, Maintain for those who change it (Add to Privilege, Security View).
  4. Build, synchronize the database and deploy (Build Project and Model, Synchronize Database, Deploy to Environment).
  5. Open the form in the web client with Copy Name and Open in Browser.
  6. Use the key EDT on other tables' fields that refer to this table, and add a relation to the table.
  7. Optional: expose the table with Wizard Data Entity.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The wizard creates two labels in the first en-US label file of your model: ID = the base name with your label (table, form caption, menu item and privileges), and ID = <Base>Id with the key field label (the EDT). Without a label file the plain texts are used.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The prompts are in newTableWithForm in src/scaffolding/wizards.ts; the elements are built by tableFormElements in src/scaffolding/tableForm.ts.
  2. The table is sent with its fields, index, field groups, properties and methods; the form as typed metadata (data source, design and controls, including the quick filter's control extension properties). The metadata server saves both through Microsoft's metadata API.
  3. All or nothing: if one element fails (for example the name is taken), the ones created before it are deleted again, and the error names the failing element.
  4. scripts/scaffold-test.js creates a table with form with these builders, uses the table for the data entity test, builds the model and deletes everything. The generated code is meant to compile without errors or warnings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Two fields only (key and description); you add the rest.
  • The form uses the SimpleList pattern. For tables with many fields, a SimpleListDetails or Details Master form fits better; change the form yourself.
  • The wizard does not add the menu item to a menu or the privileges to duties.
  • Labels created before a failure stay in the label file.

A generated name is taken Choose another base name The wizard closes without creating anything A prompt was empty or cancelled Run it again and fill all three prompts New fields do not show on the form They are not in the grid Add grid controls in the form designer Users cannot open the form The privileges are not in their roles Add the privileges to duties and roles

docs.title: Work Items and Pipelines
docs.text: Three commands connect your X++ work to Azure Boards and to your build pipelines: Link Work Item… puts a work item mention into the commit message, Open Work Item… opens a work item in Azure Boards, and Open Pipelines opens the repository's Azure Pipelines or GitHub Actions. Review My Changes then lists the work items your branch mentions, so the pull request summary names them. None of them needs a token or an API call.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Every commit that belongs to a work item: link it, so the commit and the pull request show up on the work item.
  • When you pick up a work item number from a review comment or a commit and want to read it.
  • After a push, to check the team's build.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A Git repository with an origin remote on Azure DevOps or GitHub (forms in Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration).
  • The workspace folder, or one of your custom models, inside that repository.
  • Work items in Azure Boards. On GitHub, the repository connected to Azure Boards (the Azure Boards app), so AB# mentions link.

docs.title: Link Work Item…
docs.text:
Where: command palette (F&O Studio: Link Work Item…) or the Dynamics 365 view, Deploy group (marked "Azure Boards").

  1. Stage or write your changes as usual.
  2. Run Link Work Item….
  3. In the Link work item box, enter the Azure Boards work item ID (digits only, up to nine). Anything else shows "A work item number."
  4. F&O Studio adds the mention to the commit message box of VS Code's Source Control view and opens that view:
  5. Azure Repos: #123
  6. GitHub: AB#123

If the box is empty, the message becomes #123 (mention and a space) so you can type after it. If it already holds text, the mention is appended after a space: Validate customer group on CustTable #123. If the message already contains the mention, nothing is added. 5. Write or finish the message and commit.

If VS Code's Git extension has no open repository, the mention is copied to the clipboard and you see "#123 is on the clipboard: add it to your commit message."

Example commit messages:

Add ContosoOrderStatus to SalesTable #4711
Wrap SalesFormLetter.run for order status update AB#4711

docs.title: Open Work Item…
docs.text:
Where: command palette (F&O Studio: Open Work Item…).

  1. Run the command and enter the work item ID in the Open work item box.
  2. On Azure Repos, the work item opens in the browser at https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_workitems/edit/<id>.
  3. On GitHub, F&O Studio cannot know the Azure DevOps project, so it shows "The repository is on GitHub: open the work item from Azure Boards (AB# mentions link there)."

docs.title: Open Pipelines
docs.text:
Where: command palette (F&O Studio: Open Pipelines) or the Dynamics 365 view, Deploy group.

  • Azure Repos: opens the project's pipelines, https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_build.
  • GitHub: opens the repository's Actions page filtered on the current branch, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions?query=branch:<branch>. In a detached HEAD the filter is left out.

The command opens a page only. It does not start, queue or watch a run; F&O Studio has no pipeline of its own (see Build Automation and Pipelines).

docs.title: Work items in Review My Changes
docs.text:
Review My Changes asks for the branch to compare with (proposed: xpp.git.baseBranch, else main). With a base branch, it reads the messages of all commits between that branch and HEAD and collects every #<number> and AB#<number>. The report then has a Work items line, for example:

**Work items:** #4711, #4720

When no commit names a work item, the line says "none named in the commit messages (Link Work Item… adds one)." and the finding is a warning in the Results view. With an empty base branch (uncommitted changes only) no work items are listed. Copy the report with Copy Report as Markdown in the Results view and paste it into the pull request description. See Review My Changes.

docs.title: Options and settings
docs.text: Setting Default Effect xpp.git.baseBranch empty Proposed base branch in Review My Changes, whose commits are searched for work item mentions.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
src/devops.ts:

  1. Find the repository. The workspace folders first, then the real folders of your custom models; the first folder where git rev-parse --show-toplevel succeeds is the repository.
  2. Read the host. git remote get-url origin, parsed into Azure DevOps (https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>) or GitHub (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>).
  3. Link Work Item… gets VS Code's Git extension API (vscode.git, version 1), picks the repository with the same root (or the first one) and writes to its commit message box. Then it runs workbench.view.scm.
  4. Open Work Item… and Open Pipelines build the URL and open it with vscode.env.openExternal. Open Pipelines reads the branch with git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD.
  5. Work items for the review: git log --format=%B <base>..HEAD, all mentions collected, duplicates removed, sorted by number.

No Azure DevOps or GitHub API is called and no token is used.

The agent F&O Release Notes uses the same information (changed elements from xpp_diff_changes, commit messages and the work items they name) to write user-facing release notes.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• F&O Studio does not read work item titles or states, and cannot check that a work item exists.
  • Only Azure Boards work items. GitHub issue references (#123 on a GitHub repository) are counted by Review My Changes but Link Work Item… always writes AB# on GitHub.
  • Open Work Item… does not work for GitHub repositories.
  • Open Pipelines opens the Azure Pipelines list unfiltered; filtering by branch is GitHub-only.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix "The workspace is not in a Git repository with an Azure DevOps or GitHub origin." No repository found, or the origin remote is not on dev.azure.com, *.visualstudio.com or github.com. See Azure DevOps and GitHub Integration. "A work item number." The ID contains something other than digits. Enter only the number, without # or AB#. Review My Changes says "none named in the commit messages" No commit on the branch has a mention, or the base branch was left empty. Amend or add a commit with Link Work Item…, or enter a base branch. The commit is not shown on the work item GitHub repository not connected to Azure Boards, or the commit is not pushed yet. Connect the repository to Azure Boards; push the branch.
